**Assumptions**

- A compile function is read as a function from a match predicate and a net to a CompiledNet (Reference/Compiled.lean): place count P, ID lookup placeId, ID-to-place map placeAt, transitions by ID, needs and inhibitor masks as bit functions over (transition ID, place ID), consumption places and reverse index as lists, a cardinality check as an optional list of (place ID, required count), and a match flag. Only membership of the lists is stated: their order and repetitions are not normative (all three collect a transition once per arc and then de-duplicate the reverse index: Rust through a hash set, whose iteration order is not fixed, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:110; Java with distinct(), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java:237-245; TypeScript through a Set, typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:203-207).
- The masks are stated at every number for every transition ID: at a place ID by NeedsMask and InhibitorMask, and at a number at or above P they hold no bit, which is what 'exactly the IDs' says. The runtimes test the masks word by word over all ceil(P/ws) words (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap.rs contains_all; Java and TypeScript compare whole long and Uint32 words), so a stray needs bit at or above P would leave its transition never enabled. A compiler whose needs-masks also set bit P meets line 3 at the place IDs and is killed (CONC_007_mutant_padBit_killed). Bits under a number that is no transition ID belong to no mask and are not stated.
- A net with match specifications is read as its Reference.Net, which holds every arc and output specification of its transitions, together with the match predicate hm: hm t holds exactly when t carries a match specification. The compiled net holds nothing of a match specification but its flag, so lines 1 to 6 state the compiled net of every net, with or without match specifications, and line 7 states both halves of the match-flag sentence. The predicate is over transition values, so two transitions that are equal as values (same name, same arcs) get one flag; a net in which only one of two such transitions carries a match specification is out of scope. That the ν-net model gives hm as the presence of its match specification is NU-020's line (W9), which instantiates this block at that predicate. Rust (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:52 and :120), TypeScript (typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:65 and :138) and Java's PrecompiledNet (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNet.java:96 and :253) store the flag; Java's bitmap CompiledNet stores none and its executor reads the flag as compiled.transition(j).matchSpec() != null (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java:428 and :1381), a value of the compiled net's transition at ID j, which meets line 7 because line 2 fixes that transition. Whether the flag is computed at compile time or read on demand is AC2's question (kind Q) and is not stated. A compiler that sets every flag is killed on a net without match specifications (CONC_007_mutant_noMatchLine_killed), and a compiler that sets no flag, which meets the half 'no flag without a match specification', is killed on a net whose transitions carry one (CONC_007_mutant_noFlagSet_killed).
- 'The places of the net' are read as netPlaceList n. The runtimes compile nets whose declared places include every arc place and every place of an output specification: every net builder output does (CORE-040 line 2). Rust's PetriNet::map_transitions can return a net that breaks this, against its documented unchecked precondition (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:157-174); Rust numbers places from net.places() alone (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:68-75) and panics at compile on an arc place it did not number (:124), so such a net is out of scope. On a net built by the reference net builder these are exactly the built net's places (netPlaceList_built, refCompileWith_placeCount_built in Reference/Compiled.lean), the places the builder collected from the declared places, the arcs and the output specifications. A compiler that leaves out the output specifications gives no ID to a place that is only deposited into and is forbidden (CONC_007_forbids_noOutputPlaces).
- 'Stable' is read as ruling D55 (a): the IDs are fixed for the life of the compiled net. In Lean this holds by type: a compiled net is an immutable value and its IDs are fields of it. The order in which places are numbered is not stated (line 1 fixes a bijection onto 0 to P-1, not which one): Rust sorts the place names, Java and TypeScript number places by first use, and the reference keeps the order List.dedup leaves. Transition numbering is fixed: the ID is the declaration position (line 2), as the EXEC-002 block numbers transitions. A compiler that numbers the transitions in another order, here in reverse, meets every other line and is killed (CONC_007_mutant_permTrans_killed).
- The reset-mask of the original body is replaced by the consumption places (ruling D55 (a)): Rust and TypeScript keep no reset-mask, and the one Java builds is read by no executor (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java resetMask). The consumption places are what the three compilers keep (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs consumption_place_ids, typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts _consumptionPlaceIds, java CompiledNet consumptionPlaceIds). A needs-mask that also holds the reset places (the reset-mask folded into needs) is killed (CONC_007_mutant_resetNeeds_killed): a reset never gates its transition (CORE-034). An inhibitor-mask that also holds the read places is killed (CONC_007_mutant_readInhibitor_killed), and a needs-mask without the read places and consumption places that hold the read places are forbidden (CONC_007_forbids_noReadNeeds, CONC_007_forbids_readConsumption): a read arc gates its transition and never consumes.
- Line 5 is CONC-005's 'affected transitions': a transition that only deposits into a place is not in its reverse index, and an inhibitor arc puts its transition in the index (all three runtimes add it, so that a token landing on an inhibitor place re-checks the transition). The reading without the inhibitor places is killed (CONC_007_mutant_noInhibitorAffected_killed), and so is the reading that also lists a transition under the places it deposits into (CONC_007_mutant_outputAffected_killed).
- Line 6 is the weak form both runtime choices meet: Rust and TypeScript give a cardinality check to a transition with any input that is not One, and list every input; Java gives one only for a required count above 1, All or AtLeast, and lists every input. Both satisfy the block (CONC_007_reference, CONC_007_allows_javaCard). The cardinality bullet ('needed for a transition with an input that requires more than one token') is read with the presence bit: it already shows one token, so an input of required count at most 1 (One, All, Exactly 0 or 1, AtLeast 0 or 1) needs no count check. That phase 2 then answers what the cardinality check of the glossary answers is CONC-008's line, not restated here. A check whose entries carry count 1 meets the first half of line 6 and is killed by the second (CONC_007_mutant_unitCounts_killed); a compiler that builds no cardinality check at all is killed by the first (CONC_007_forbids_noCard).
- The presence check on the compiled masks, over the presence bitmap indexed by place ID, answers what CONC-004's presence check (MaskCheck) answers on the bitmap by name, for every compiler that satisfies the block (conc007_presence_iff). The body's 'This enables array-based access instead of hash map lookups' is the reason for the representation, a quality property, and is not encoded.
- AC1 (places and transitions have stable numeric IDs) is lines 1 and 2, with 'stable' read as above. A compiler that gives two places one ID violates line 1 (CONC_007_forbids_mergedIds), and so does one whose ID range has an ID too many (CONC_007_mutant_noRange_killed).
- AC2 (all masks are precomputed at compilation time, not at each enablement check) is a quality property of when the masks are computed and is not encoded: the block states what the compiled net holds, a function of the net alone. The test derivation (compile a net and verify that the masks match the expected bit patterns) is CONC_007_nonvacuous on a seven-place, two-transition net.

- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_all` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyAll): ✓ **The whole specification has one model.** One build check, one firing relation, one timing contract, one ready order, one timed step, one queue firing, one output validator, one transition builder, one snapshot, one composition, one environment verifier, one split, one exporter, one executor and one executor with events that steps as it meet every area at once: the CORE, IO, TIME, queue, structure, composition, ν, verifier, executor, event and export blocks, and the cross-model lines of wave W11. Over string place names the same witnesses also meet EVT-014, and every marking snapshot the executor reports is CORE-073's snapshot `Snap` of the declared places; CORE-037's warnings wrap the one executor and the one environment verifier, and MOD-051's `verify` runs the one instantiation, build script, entry check and environment verifier. Over flat place identities the one executor's runs are runs of the verifier's in-flight model by their counts (`CountAgrees`), so the split the verifier checks covers them (VER-004, block B).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_008"></a>
## CONC-008: Multi-Phase Enablement

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_008` · Kind **F** · Scope all executors, transitions that build and have no match specification · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 2ed06600a6fb11e9 ai** · Statement hash `2ed06600a6fb11e9`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition that builds has no match specification and has an `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, and its presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking, its cardinality check *shall* pass exactly when every input place holds at least its required count.<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has no match specification and has an `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking and the cardinality check passes.<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has no match specification and no `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the presence check passes on the presence bitmap of the marking.<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has no match specification, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the transition is enabled ([CORE-022]). | 1. For every transition t that builds (Builds t: distinct input places, every input arc requiring at least one token, no place with both an input arc and a read arc, a well-formed output spec; no transition has a match specification here) and every count marking m:<br>2. if t has an input that is not `One` and the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m, the cardinality check of t passes on m exactly when every input place of t holds at least its required count;<br>3. if t has an input that is not `One`, the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m and the cardinality check of t passes on m;<br>4. if t has no input that is not `One` (a transition with no input arc included), the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when the presence check of t passes on the presence bitmap of m;<br>5. the enablement check of t on m passes exactly when t is enabled in m. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] C ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    Builds t →<br>      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>        (¬OnlyOneInputs t →<br>            C.presence t (presenceOf m) = true →<br>              (C.cardinality t m = true ↔ CardinalityOk t m)) ∧<br>          (¬OnlyOneInputs t →<br>              C.check t m = (C.presence t (presenceOf m) &amp;&amp; C.cardinality t m)) ∧<br>            (OnlyOneInputs t → C.check t m = C.presence t (presenceOf m)) ∧<br>              (C.check t m = true ↔ Enabled t m)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A marking is read as its token counts (CountMarking) and its presence bitmap as one bit per place, set exactly when the place is marked (glossary: Presence bitmap). The check is the abstract EnableCheck of CONC-004: its presence phase on a bitmap, its cardinality phase on counts, and the whole check on a marking.
- 'The presence check' in the quoted sentences is the glossary term that CONC-004 pins, so the sentences mean this block and CONC-004 together; the presence phase is constrained there, not here. Read alone, this block accepts a presence phase that ignores the input bits of a transition with an input that is not `One`, since its cardinality phase covers those places (conc008_dropInputs_ok); CONC-004 kills that check (CONC_004_forbids_dropInputs). The two blocks hold together of one check (CONC_004_008_consistent), and together they fix the whole check of every transition that builds to the reference check (conc004_008_pins_check).
- Every line speaks of transitions that build (glossary: Builds), as CORE-022 does: a definition that building rejects is held by no executor, so no check is asked of it. Two build checks matter here. IO-002 and IO-004 reject an `Exactly(0)` or `AtLeast(0)` input, which is enabled on an empty place but fails the presence check: without them the fourth line contradicts the second line together with CONC-004 (conc008_unscoped_conflict). CORE-030 rejects two input arcs on one place, which have no coherent consumption semantics: a cardinality phase that adds up the required counts of all arcs on one place answers what the reference answers on every transition that builds, and the block allows it (CONC_008_allows_sumDup).
- Phase 3 and AC3 (a transition with a match specification needs the ν-match check, which scans its correlated inputs for a shared name, [NU-020]) are the second block of this file, CONC_008_nu: the count-level transition has no match specification, so every quoted sentence here is stated for transitions without one. The lines for a transition with one, and the body item 'This is the only per-token phase; there is no value-predicate phase (guards were removed, [IO-006])', are that block's. At the count level no check sees token values, so a value-predicate phase cannot be expressed; the fourth line already forbids any extra phase that rejects an enabled transition.
- A transition with no `Exactly(n)`, `All` or `AtLeast(m)` input, including one with no input arc at all (a read-only, inhibitor-only or source transition), is checked by phase 1 alone (third line, AC1). 'Fully checked in Phase 1' is read as 'the answer of the check is the answer of phase 1': computing phase 2 anyway is not forbidden, and its cardinality phase is not constrained. Rust and TypeScript skip phase 2 for it (they build no cardinality check unless some input is not `One`); Java also skips it for an `Exactly(1)` input (it builds one only for a required count above 1, `All` or `AtLeast`); the reference runs phase 2 for every transition, where it passes whenever phase 1 does. All three satisfy the block (CONC_008_reference, CONC_008_allows_skipOneOnly, CONC_008_allows_skipJava). For a transition with an input that is not `One`, phase 2 checks every input place, `One` inputs included, as the runtimes do.
- 'Phases 2 and 3 are only reached if Phase 1 passes, minimizing work for most transitions' is not encoded as an order of evaluation. The second line is an equation of Boolean values, whose answer does not depend on the order its parts are evaluated in, so a check that evaluates phase 2 first, or always, satisfies it (CONC_008_allows_cardFirst). What the sentence implies for the answer is encoded: the whole check passes only if phase 1 does (second and third lines), and where phase 1 fails phase 2 is not constrained (the first line is stated only at a marking where phase 1 passes; there a skipped phase 2 passes trivially, and that is the right answer because every input place is marked). The order and the saving of work are quality properties. Phase 1's 'O(W) bitwise check' and 'fast reject for most transitions' are CONC-004's and PERF-002's quality properties.
- Which marking the phases read is not this ID's subject: in the enablement update the presence phase reads the bitmap snapshot and the cardinality phase the live counts, taken at the same instant; in the recheck of a firing pass (EXEC-003) the cardinality phase discounts same-pass deposits. This block is the function of one marking; the pass recheck is EXEC-003's.
- The body names the mask test of CONC-004 the 'Enablement check' and this ID makes it phase 1 (clash conc-a#10). The reading in which CONC-004's formula is the whole enablement check is the mutant CONC_008_mutant_maskOnly, killed by AC2.
- With CONC-004 in force, the fourth line follows from the first three; it is kept because this block alone needs it: it makes phase 1 on the presence bitmap agree with enablement for a transition with only `One` inputs, and CONC_008_forbids_cardOnly uses it.
- AC1 (a transition with only One inputs and no match specification is fully checked in phase 1) is the third line (CONC_008_mutant_noPhase1Only_killed, CONC_008_nonvacuous).
- AC2 (a transition with an Exactly(5) input needs phase 2 to verify the token count) is the first and second lines: with three tokens the presence check passes, the cardinality check fails and so does the enablement check (CONC_008_mutant_maskOnly_killed, CONC_008_nonvacuous). CONC_008_nonvacuous also runs an `All` input and an `AtLeast(3)` input through both phases.
- AC3 is not encoded here: it is the block CONC_008_nu (see above).
- The test derivation's 'correct enablement' is the fourth line; its 'minimal re-evaluation' is CONC-005's subject.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_008_nu"></a>
## CONC-008: Multi-Phase Enablement (ν-match check)

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_008_nu` · Kind **F** · Scope all executors, transitions that build, with and without a match specification · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 e74f39afa3b38f90 ai** · Statement hash `e74f39afa3b38f90`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition that builds has a match specification and phases 1 and 2 pass on the token counts of the marking, its ν-match check *shall* pass exactly when the match specification keys at least one place and there is a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens of that name ([NU-020]).<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has a match specification, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when phases 1 and 2 pass on the token counts of the marking and its ν-match check passes.<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has no match specification, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when phases 1 and 2 pass on the token counts of the marking.<br><br>*When* a transition that builds has a match specification, its enablement check *shall* pass exactly when the transition without its match specification is enabled on the token counts of the marking ([CORE-022]), the match specification keys at least one place and there is a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens of that name. | 1. For every transition t that builds with or without its match (NuBuilds t) and every queue marking M of stamped tokens:<br>2. if t has match specification ms and the count-level check of t without its match passes on the token counts of M, the ν-match check of t on M passes exactly when some name n is eligible on the selection input read off M (the match has a key, and every correlated input holds at least one token of n and at least its required count of them);<br>3. if t has match specification ms, the whole check of t on M is the count-level check of t without its match on the token counts of M, and then the ν-match check of t on M;<br>4. if t has no match specification, the whole check of t on M is the count-level check of t on the token counts of M;<br>5. if t has match specification ms, the whole check of t on M passes exactly when t without its match is enabled on the token counts of M and some name is eligible on the selection input read off M. | <pre>fun {N V Nm} [DecidableEq N] [LinearOrder Nm] C ↦<br>  ∀ (t : NuTrans N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>    NuBuilds t →<br>      ∀ (M : QMarking N (Stamped V)),<br>        (∀ (ms : MatchSpec N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>            t.mspec = some ms →<br>              C.base.check t.base (qCount M) = true →<br>                (C.nuMatch t M = true ↔ ∃ n, eligible (matchIn ms t M) n = true)) ∧<br>          (∀ (ms : MatchSpec N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>              t.mspec = some ms →<br>                C.check t M = (C.base.check t.base (qCount M) &amp;&amp; C.nuMatch t M)) ∧<br>            (t.mspec = none → C.check t M = C.base.check t.base (qCount M)) ∧<br>              ∀ (ms : MatchSpec N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>                t.mspec = some ms →<br>                  (C.check t M = true ↔<br>                    Enabled t.base (qCount M) ∧ ∃ n, eligible (matchIn ms t M) n = true)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a NuEnableCheck: base, the count-level check of CONC-004 and the first CONC-008 block (phases 1 and 2), applied to the transition without its match (t.base) and to the token counts of the marking (qCount); nuMatch, the ν-match check (phase 3), on a ν transition (glossary NuTrans) and a queue marking of stamped tokens; and check, the whole check. 'Phases 1 and 2 pass on the token counts of the marking' is base.check of the transition without its match (t.base) on the token counts (qCount M), which CONC-004 and CONC-008 constrain; for a transition with a match these are the phases of the transition without it, since a match specification adds no arc. This block does not constrain base, so its sentences mean this block and those two together: then the whole check of every transition that builds is the reference check (conc008_nu_pins_check), and it passes exactly when the transition is ν-enabled (conc008_nu_enabled, glossary NuEnabled). The three blocks hold together of one check (CONC_004_008_nu_consistent).
- The scan of phase 3 counts the required count, as every runtime computes it: Rust find_match_binding (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:381-405, and the precompiled backend), Java MatchEngine.findBinding and requiredFor, and TypeScript findBinding and requiredFor (typescript/src/runtime/match-engine.ts:112-140) keep a name only when every correlated input holds at least the required count of its tokens, the count of an Exactly(n) or the minimum of an AtLeast(m) input, and 1 for One and All (glossary reqAt). The reading that asks only for a name with one token in every correlated input is killed (CONC_008_nu_forbids_sharedOnly). 'Tokens of that name' are the tokens of the correlated input whose key gives that name. The Lean name test (eligible) also asks for at least one token of the name in every correlated input; on a transition that builds this adds nothing, since every correlated input is an input place and every input arc requires at least one token (IO-002, IO-004), so the sentences leave it out (conc008_eligible_iff).
- Ruling D37 (a): a token whose key yields no name has no name on that input and is not counted (matchIn keeps only the tokens with a name). 'The match specification keys at least one place' is the first conjunct of eligible: a match without keys has no eligible name, so its ν-match check fails, as in the runtimes (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/match_engine.rs:33-34, select_match_name returns no name for no correlated inputs); a check that passes it is killed (CONC_008_nu_forbids_vacuous). The minimum of two keys is a check of the match builder only (ruling D37 (a), NU_020_build), not a build-time check of the transition: Rust MatchSpec::from_keys (rust/libpetri-core/src/match_spec.rs:82) leaves it to the caller and the transition build checks only a duplicate key (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:514), so a transition that builds (NuBuilds) may carry a match with fewer than two keys, and the sentences say 'keys at least one place'. Which name the firing then joins on is NU-020's and NU-022's subject, not this block's: the check asks only whether some name is eligible. The reference reads that off NU-022's selection, which returns a name exactly when one is eligible (refSelect_isSome_iff), as the runtimes do; the incremental matcher they read on the fast path (cache.best()) answers what the rebuild answers by NU-022's AC2.
- 'Phases 2 and 3 are only reached if Phase 1 passes' is not encoded as an order of evaluation, as in the first CONC-008 block: the second line is an equation of Boolean values. What it implies for the answer is encoded: the first line constrains the ν-match check only where phases 1 and 2 pass, which is where all three runtimes run it (bitmap_backend.rs:329-371, BitmapNetExecutor.java canEnable, bitmap-net-executor.ts canEnable, and the precompiled executors); where they fail, the ν-match check is not constrained and the whole check fails.
- 'This is the only per-token phase; there is no value-predicate phase (guards were removed, [IO-006])' is the type of base, which reads token counts only (EnableCheck on a count marking), together with the second and third lines: a transition without a match is decided by phases 1 and 2 on the token counts, and a transition with one by those phases and the ν-match check, with no further phase. A check that adds a guard on token values is killed (CONC_008_nu_forbids_guard).
- Which marking the phases read is not this ID's subject: a join whose correlated input took a deposit in the same firing pass is deferred to the next pass in every runtime (EXEC-003 AC4), which is RefExec's with the ν kernel. This block is the function of one marking. That an enabled matched transition fires is an offer, not a line: it is the conjunct NuCovers of the ν consistency theorem.
- With CONC-004 and the first CONC-008 block in force, the fourth line follows from the first two (conc008_nu_enabled); it is kept because this block alone leaves base free and needs it: a check whose base stops after phase 1 meets the first three lines and is killed by the fourth (CONC_008_nu_forbids_maskBase).
- AC3 (a transition with a match specification requires phase 3 to scan tokens for a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens of that name) is the first two lines: on a marking where both correlated inputs are marked but share no name, phases 1 and 2 pass, the ν-match check fails and so does the whole check (CONC_008_nu_nonvacuous); the check without phase 3 is killed (CONC_008_nu_mutant_noPhase3_killed). AC1 and AC2 are the first CONC-008 block's.
- The test derivation's 'correct enablement' is the fourth line for a transition with a match and the first block's fourth line for one without; its 'minimal re-evaluation' is CONC-005's subject.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_010"></a>
## CONC-010: Orchestrator Wake-Up

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_010` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0e0f4c602d8b221e ai** · Statement hash `0e0f4c602d8b221e`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| When the orchestrator is idle (no transitions ready, waiting for work), it must be woken by each of these causes:<br><br>**Action completion:** an action returns, or its timeout expires ([EXEC-022]), and its outcome is queued for the orchestrator.<br><br>**External event injection:** `inject()` accepts a token for an environment place ([ENV-003]).<br><br>**Timer expiry:** the timer the wait set for a timing boundary of an armed transition runs out.<br><br>**Lifecycle:** the executor is drained ([ENV-011]), closed ([ENV-013]) or terminated immediately ([ENV-015]).<br><br>**Publication:** an action's flush queues a batch of outputs before the action returns ([IO-015]), in an implementation with mid-action publication.<br><br>A flush that the join-relay check rejects ([NU-054]) queues nothing and is no wake cause; the firing then ends with an error when its action returns.<br><br>A timing boundary of an armed transition is its earliest bound, while its elapsed time has not reached it, and, for a reapable transition, the reading at which it becomes expired ([TIME-013]).<br><br>The orchestrator judges Ready, Expired and the timing boundaries for its wait at the firing-clock reading its deadline step took in the current cycle ([EXEC-001] step 4), which is not earlier than the reading of its enablement update ([TIME-010]).<br><br>*While* the outcome of an action, a flushed publication or an accepted injection is queued and not yet processed, the executor *shall not* block in its wait ([EXEC-001] step 6).<br><br>*While* a transition is Ready or Expired at the reading of the cycle's deadline step, the executor *shall not* block in its wait.<br><br>*When* an action's outcome is queued, an action's flush queues a publication, `inject()` accepts a token, or the executor is drained, closed or terminated immediately, the executor *shall* end any block of its wait at once and be ready to leave the wait for the start of its loop ([EXEC-001] step 1) without waiting for a timer.<br><br>*When* the executor blocks in its wait while an armed transition has a timing boundary ahead, it *shall* set a timer no longer than the time from the reading of the cycle's deadline step to the nearest such boundary, plus the timer resolution.<br><br>*When* an action returns or its timeout expires, the executor *shall* queue the action's outcome for the orchestrator.<br><br>So no queued work waits for a timer or a poll, and a wait with a timing boundary ahead carries a timer that runs out no later than that boundary, within timer resolution, counted from the reading of the cycle's deadline step. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C:<br>2. no park step starts in a state whose completion, publication or event queue is not empty;<br>3. no park step starts in a state in which a transition of the net is Ready or Expired at the cycle reading;<br>4. every arrival step (a return, a budget expiry, a flush that queues a publication, an accepted request, a drain, a close, an immediate termination) ends in a state that is not parked;<br>5. every park step with timer tmr starts in a state where, if a timing boundary is ahead at the cycle reading, tmr is set and is at most the nearest boundary plus the timer resolution C.res;<br>6. every return or budget expiry of firing i ends in a state whose completion queue holds i. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (while fun s ↦ Conc010.WorkQueued s, never fun s s' ↦<br>        ∃ tmr, R C s (XLbl.park tmr) s') ∧<br>      (while fun s ↦ Conc010.DueAtCycle C s, never fun s s' ↦<br>          ∃ tmr, R C s (XLbl.park tmr) s') ∧<br>        (∀ (l : XLbl N T),<br>            on fun s s' ↦ R C s l s' ∧ Conc010.Arrival l s s', shall fun x s' ↦<br>              s'.parked = false) ∧<br>          (∀ (tmr : Option ℕ),<br>              on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.park tmr) s', shall fun s x ↦<br>                Conc010.TimerWithin C s tmr) ∧<br>            (∀ (i : ℕ) (ok : Bool),<br>                on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.ret i ok) s', shall fun x s' ↦ i ∈ s'.cq) ∧<br>              ∀ (i : ℕ) (e : List (N × T)),<br>                on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.expire i e) s', shall fun x s' ↦ i ∈ s'.cq</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The wait is the loop phase await (EXEC-001 step 6); park tmr is the loop blocking in it (XSt.parked becomes true) with a timer tmr (none: no timer), and wake is the end of the wait, by its timer, by an arrival or for no reason, after which the loop runs step 1 again. The outside steps ret, expire, flush, request, drain, close and terminateNow are the arrivals; the loop may also take a queued completion, publication or injection straight from the wait (EXEC-001, ruling D70 (a)). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor, whose wait is a select over its completion, flush and signal channels and a timer from cycle_now.
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Conc010Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The third EARS sentence demands an answer and is quoted whole; its safety half is line 3, and its existence half is that clause. Lines 1, 3 and 5 make up 'no lost wake-up', together with Conc010Covers. Line 1 is the check before the block: the loop blocks only with nothing queued, so an arrival before the block is never slept through (CONC_010_forbids_parkWithCompletion: a check-then-park executor that blocks with a returned action's outcome queued; CONC_010_forbids_parkWithPublication: one that blocks with a flushed publication queued; for the event queue, ENV-005's ENV_005_forbids_parkWithQueued). Line 5 makes line 1 read the right thing: a return or a budget expiry puts the firing's outcome on the completion queue, the queue the park check reads (CONC_010_forbids_outcomeOnRecord: an executor that keeps the outcome on the firing record only, so its park check sees an empty queue and blocks again with the outcome unprocessed). An accepted injection is queued by ENV-003 line 1, and a flush is an arrival only when it queues its batch, by the definition of the arrival. The wake during the block has two parts: line 3, the arrival leaves the state unblocked (CONC_010_forbids_deafCompletion: a return that leaves the wait blocked, noticed only when the timer fires; CONC_010_forbids_deafLifecycle: a drain that leaves it blocked), and Conc010Covers, the way out of the wait, a wake back to step 1, is offered at once after an arrival taken in the wait with no terminal place marked (the reference meets it, conc010_ref_covers; an executor whose arrivals clear the flag but whose wait can be left only when its sleep is over, a poll, meets every line and fails that clause, conc010_covers_sleepyWait). Rust meets line 1 by its select, which returns at once when a channel holds an item, Java by its semaphore permit, TypeScript by its latched wake-up (wakeUpPending) and its queue re-check on entry to the wait.
- Line 2 is the first description sentence's 'no transitions ready' read at the cycle reading (ruling D61 (c)): the loop does not block while a transition it could act on without new work is Ready or Expired at the reading its deadline step took, which is not earlier than its enablement update's (CONC_010_forbids_parkWhileDue: a wait that looks only at the queues and blocks with a transition Ready). The reference meets it by its park guard (nothingDue); on its own runs the guard never bites, since a pass started every Ready transition or took its clock and the deadline step reaped every expired one, but the line constrains every executor. Judging at a later reading of the same cycle is stricter (a transition Ready or Expired at the cycle reading is Ready or Expired later too) and also satisfies the line; judging at the cycle reading is what Rust does (cycle_now), and the reference blocks while a transition is already Ready at the host's present (CONC_010_allows_staleReading). That transition is judged by the next cycle, which the timer starts.
- Line 4 is AC3 under ruling D13 (a) (conc-b clash CB-6): a timing boundary of an armed transition is its earliest bound while not reached and, for a reapable transition, the reading at which it becomes expired (nextBoundary, glossary GlossaryExec.lean); a block with a boundary ahead sets a timer of at most that wait plus the timer resolution C.res, and with none ahead any timer or none (Rust re-checks after 60 s, Java after its poll interval). An executor that blocks without a timer while a Delayed transition is armed breaks it (CONC_010_forbids_untimedPark). The resolution is a configuration value of the model (Cfg.res): Java rounds a wait below one millisecond up to one millisecond, Rust truncates to whole milliseconds, and the runtimes wake at the latest bound of a transition with a deadline, earlier than the expiry boundary, which a shorter timer allows. The timer is a duration counted from the cycle reading: a runtime that starts it at its present reading, as Rust does, may end the wait later than the boundary by the time the cycle took since its update, which ruling D3 allows (the executor may be late by any amount). Java and TypeScript compute the timer from the cycle reading too (Java's nanosUntilNextTimedTransition(cycleNanos), TypeScript's awaitWork(cycleNowMs), which hands that reading to millisUntilNextTimedTransition), so a boundary that falls due while the wait is set up still gets its timer. A timer computed from a reading taken in the wait, after the cycle reading, finds such a boundary passed, sets no timer and blocks while an action is in flight: that is the park CONC_010_forbids_untimedPark models, the behaviour RD-32 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded for TypeScript.
- AC1 and AC2 are line 3 and Conc010Covers for an accepted injection and for an action's return or budget expiry, together with line 1 for the arrival that comes before the block and, for AC2, line 5 for the queueing (CONC_010_nonvacuous part 6 runs an accepted injection that ends a block and is injected from the wait). AC3 is line 4 for its timer, with the readiness it promises left to the cycle the timer starts, and only if the transition is still armed then: there TIME-010 and TIME-014 make a Delayed transition Ready once its earliest bound is reached and TIME-013 reaps an expired one (CONC_010_nonvacuous part 4 runs the timer, the next cycle and the start). AC4 is line 3 and Conc010Covers for a drain, a close and an immediate termination (ruling D13 (a): drain and close are wake causes, and the list is 'must wake on').
- Kind Q, outside the lines: 'immediately' in AC1, 'must be responsive' and 'does not depend on a poll interval', and the latency the test derivation measures, are latencies of the host's wake-up; the model gives steps no duration, so they are tested, not proven. The third cause, the timer running out, and the sentence 'Ending the wait when that timer runs out is the work of the host timer ([TIME-015]).' are Q as well: line 4 bounds the timer the park step sets, and no line makes a wake happen when it runs out, since delay is never restricted (ruling D3). The lines say that nothing in the executor waits between an arrival and its processing: no block with work queued, an outcome always on the queue the check reads, and no block that survives an arrival, and, by Conc010Covers, the way out of the wait offered at once; that the host takes that way promptly is Q.
- Allowed and outside the lines: the wait may end for no reason (a spurious wake-up, or Java's and Rust's periodic re-check behind the direct wake-up, TIME-015's 'the wait MAY complete early'), since wake is offered in every state of the wait and delay is never restricted (ruling D3). A snapshot request (ENV-014) may be answered from the wait without ending it: the model's snapshot step in the wait leaves the state unchanged, the flag included, and ENV-014 states the answer. A flush that the join-relay check of NU-054 rejects queues nothing, so it is no arrival and the reference keeps the block (flushStep); the firing's return then reports the error. Under an injected host clock (TIME-015) the host's wait carries the wake-up; parked stands for it.
- Not covered by the lines, and said so in the markdown: a drain, a close or an immediate termination taken after the termination test and before the loop blocks. The reference park guard reads the queues and the timing state but not the lifecycle mode, so it may still block after such a step although the termination test would now finish the run; the runtimes do not (Rust's select finds the signal on its channel, Java finds the semaphore permit, TypeScript the latched wake-up), and their tests check it. An executor that wakes the wait on a lifecycle signal only when it is already blocked, as TypeScript's wakeUp() did before it latched the signal, meets every line. The same gap covers a block taken again after a drain, a close or an immediate termination arrives in the wait: the arrival clears the flag (line 3), but the reference may block once more without going back to step 1, because its park guard does not read the mode either (conc010_refExec_repark_after_drain). So a lifecycle-deaf wait loop of the form 'while the queues are empty, await a signal', read as clear and block again, also meets every line and Conc010Covers; CONC_010_forbids_deafLifecycle kills only a drain that leaves the wait blocked. A line on this case waits for the model's park guard to read the lifecycle mode.
- Depends on EXEC-001 (the loop, its steps 1 and 6), ENV-003 (an accepted injection is queued), ENV-005 (lines 1 and 3 of ENV-005 are line 1 restricted to the event queue and line 3 restricted to an accepted request, conc010_env005_lines of ConsistencyExec.lean), TIME-010 and TIME-013 (Ready, Expired, the boundaries), and TIME-015 (the host's wait). The test derivation (inject a token while the orchestrator is idle and measure the latency to its processing) is CONC_010_nonvacuous's runs for its order, with the latency left Q.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_021"></a>
## CONC-021: Opcode-Based Consume Operations

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_021` · Kind **F** · Scope the precompiled executor, transitions without a match specification · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 90f801704231c404 ai** · Statement hash `90f801704231c404`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* hand the action from each input place the oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc ([IO-007]) for the number of tokens the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5), in queue order, and nothing from any other place.<br><br>*When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* hand the action for each read arc the head of the read place's queue as it is after the input operations and before the reset operations.<br><br>*When* the precompiled executor fires a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]), its consume operations *shall* remove from each reset place every token the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5), leave each other input place its queue without the tokens handed to the action, leave the queue of every other place unchanged, and hold a queue for every place the token storage held and for no other place. | 1. For a token store S by place id and a consume program X over it, for every store state s and compiled transition t such that S holds a queue for every place t has an arc on, t has no two input arcs on one place, and t is enabled on the queues of s by the reference enablement:<br>2. the inputs X hands the action are the reference's: from each input place the first tokens of its queue, in queue order, as many as the consumption count of the arc on the queue's length (One 1, Exactly n, All and AtLeast every token), and nothing from any other place;<br>3. the read tokens X hands the action are the reference's: for each read arc, in arc order, the head of the read place's queue after the input consumption;<br>4. after X, S holds a queue for exactly the places it held one for in s, and at each of them the queue is the reference's: empty at a reset place, the queue without its consumed prefix at any other input place, unchanged at every other place. | <pre>fun S X ↦<br>  ∀ (s : S.σ) (t : Transition),<br>    (∀ (p : PlaceId), touches t p → S.ok s p) →<br>      DistinctInputPlaces t →<br>        bbCanEnable (S.view s) t = true →<br>          (X s t).inputs = bbInputsBag (S.view s) t ∧<br>            (X s t).reads = bbReadsBag (bbPostInput (S.view s) t) t.reads ∧<br>              ∀ (q : PlaceId),<br>                (S.ok (X s t).store q ↔ S.ok s q) ∧<br>                  (S.ok s q → S.view (X s t).store q = bbConsumeMarking (S.view s) t q)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a token store S (glossary: MarkingOps, at place ids PlaceId and token values Colour), CONC-022's interface: view s p is the queue place p holds in s, oldest first (glossary: Queue order), and S.ok s p says that s is a well-formed store holding a queue for p. The consume program X maps a store state and a compiled transition (Libpetri.Transition of Basic.lean: input arcs with their cardinality, inhibitor, read and reset places, by place id) to a ConsumeOut: the store after the consume phase and the input and read tokens the action receives, by place id. The tokens a reset destroys are not handed to the action, so they are not a field; that they are reported to the event store is EVT's subject. The right-hand sides are the Bitmap reference executor's consume (Refinement/Model.lean: bbInputsBag, bbReadsBag over bbPostInput, bbConsumeMarking), applied to the store's view, and the enablement premise is the reference enablement bbCanEnable on the view, not the program's own enablement check.
- Scope: transitions without a match specification (ruling D30, the consequence of D16 for EXEC-010). A transition with a match specification consumes its correlated inputs by name ([NU-020]) and does not run the input opcodes (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1146, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2332-2335, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1085-1088). The compiled Transition has no match specification, so every transition the statement quantifies over is one the EARS sentences speak of; the ν consume path is NU-020's subject. Each quoted sentence carries the scope in its trigger, and the prose sentence on iterating the opcode array states it as its exception.
- The premises are the build-time guarantees under which the precompiled executor fires: every place a transition has an arc on is a compiled place id (the store holds a queue for it; CompiledNet::compile interns every referenced place), no two input arcs of a transition are on one place (DistinctInputPlaces, CORE-030 AC3, rejected at build time; with duplicate inputs the opcode interpreter is not total, canEnable_insufficient_for_totality in RetrodictExec.lean), and the transition is enabled ('fires' presupposes it). Guards are not modelled: input guards were removed from the spec (IO-006), and the guard field of the Lean InSpec is ignored by both the reference and the interpreter.
- The statement does not assume ruling D15 (no input arc and read arc on one place, EXEC-012): the reference peeks the reads after input consumption whatever the arcs, and so does the precompiled executor. Under D15, which the build enforces, a read place is never an input place, so 'after the input operations' is not observable on a transition that builds: CONC_021_forbids_readsBeforeInputs kills a peek before the input opcodes only on a transition with an input arc and a read arc on one place, so on buildable nets that half of line 2 is stricter than the build needs. 'Before the reset operations' is observable, for a place that is both a read place and a reset place, which EXEC-013 allows and which CONC_021_forbids_readsAfterReset tests.
- Draining opcodes are modelled with no same-pass deposit outstanding (clash conc-b#10, ruling D20). The opcode table and the first and third EARS sentences say 'the tokens the firing may drain ([EXEC-003] AC5)': a draining arc or reset that fires later in a firing pass takes only the tokens present when the pass began, and tokens a same-pass synchronous action deposited survive it (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1276-1279 and :1300, drainable at :690-695; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:791). A consume program here sees one firing and no pass, so every token is one the firing may drain, the available count of line 1 is the queue's length, line 1 reads 'every token' for All and AtLeast, and line 3 reads 'empty' at a reset place (the module header of Conservation.lean states the same limit). The deposited case is the Phase 2 executor model's (RefExec, W5) and EXEC-003's. For the same reason a program that also drains the inhibitor places with the RESET tail meets the lines: an enabled transition's inhibitor places are empty, and only a same-pass deposit between the enablement check and the consume could tell the two apart, which is for that model's mutant list.
- Line 1 is the first EARS sentence. 'The oldest tokens the place holds, as many as the consumption count of the input arc ([IO-007]) for the number of tokens the firing may drain' is the queue's prefix of length consumptionCount(available), with available the queue's length (consumeCountAt). 'Nothing from any other place' is the bag equality off the input places: a reset place that is not an input place hands the action nothing. CONSUME_ATLEAST taking only its minimum is killed (CONC_021_forbids_atLeastMin), the RESET tail run before the input opcodes, which hands an input place that is also a reset place nothing, is killed (CONC_021_forbids_resetFirst), a RESET tail that hands the tokens it drains to the action is killed at the reset-only place 1 (CONC_021_forbids_resetHandsTokens, 'nothing from any other place'), and CONSUME_N taking the newest tokens of its place is killed (CONC_021_forbids_newestFirst, 'the oldest tokens ... in queue order').
- Line 2 is the second EARS sentence: per read arc the head of the read place's queue after the input consumption and before the drain, by bbReadsBag, which adds one head per read arc in arc order. A peek after the RESET tail, the order the Rust precompiled executor had before fix (b) (preFixReads, read_reset_order_diverges in RetrodictExec.lean), hands a read place that is also a reset place nothing and is killed (CONC_021_forbids_readsAfterReset); a peek before the input opcodes is killed as the D15 paragraph says. The sentence presupposes the read place's queue is not empty after the input operations; bbReadsBag hands nothing when it is, which only a read place that is also a draining input place can reach, and D15 rejects that transition at build time.
- Line 3 is the third EARS sentence. Its view half is bbConsumeMarking: a reset place ends empty, any other input place keeps its queue without the consumed prefix, in order, every other place (read places and inhibitor places included) keeps its queue. A read compiled as a consuming opcode (AC2: reads do not consume) removes the read token and is killed (CONC_021_forbids_readConsumes), so is a program without the RESET tail (CONC_021_forbids_noReset), and so is one that hands the right tokens but shrinks the ring from its tail, leaving the input place its newest tokens removed instead of its oldest (CONC_021_forbids_tailShrink, 'its queue without the tokens handed to the action'). Its S.ok half is 'hold a queue for every place the token storage held and for no other place', both directions of the frame condition that lets one firing's store be the next firing's: a program that hands back a store with the right queues but no places is killed (CONC_021_forbids_forgetPlaces), and so is one that hands back a store holding places, with tokens, that the store before did not hold (CONC_021_forbids_seedPlaces, a lazily allocated pool reseeded from a cached template). Token conservation (the queue before is the delivered tokens, then the reset-destroyed tokens, then the queue after) is a consequence on the places the store holds, token_conservation in Conservation.lean.
- Not quoted: the prose sentences 'Each transition's input and reset arcs are compiled into a flat integer array of opcodes.', 'During firing, the executor iterates the opcode array instead of pattern-matching on sealed arc types, except for a transition with a match specification, whose inputs are consumed through the match path (its correlated inputs by name, [NU-020]).' and 'Read arcs are compiled into a separate place-ID array.', and the opcode table. They describe the compiled representation and how firing walks it, which a consume program's observable behaviour does not show: a program that dispatches on arc types and one that runs an opcode array satisfy the lines alike. Only the by-name exception of the second sentence is used, as the scope above. The witness has the structure (compileConsumeOps: the input opcodes in declaration order, then the RESET tail; reads outside it, consumeForFiring_eq_program, cited by conc021_program). The u32 encoding and the pc walk are not modelled (Compile.lean header).
- The witness is the Rust ring pool. The Java precompiled executor keeps rings too; the TypeScript one keeps a plain array per place (clash conc-b#5, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:179). The statement is over CONC-022's store interface and reads the store through its view, so a consume program over an array store is in its domain alike. CONC_021_ringMarking shows the reference over core070_ringMarking, the store of the consistency theorem spec_consistent_queue.
- AC1 (each transition has a precompiled consume operation array) and AC2's first half (read arcs compiled into a separate place-ID array) are the compiled representation, kind Q, not lines; the witness's compileConsumeOps has that shape (conc021_program). AC2's second half (reads do not consume) is line 3 at a read place (CONC_021_forbids_readConsumes).
- AC3 (firing iterates the opcode array without type dispatch, except for a transition with a match specification, whose inputs are consumed through the match path, its correlated inputs by name) is a cost and structure criterion, kind Q, not a line; its by-name exception is the scope assumption above.
- AC4 (all five opcodes produce the same observable behaviour as the corresponding arc types) is the three lines: the right-hand sides are the reference arc semantics, and CONC_021_nonvacuous runs one transition with all five opcodes (One, Exactly 2, All, AtLeast 2, two resets), two read arcs and an inhibitor arc. The test derivation (compile a net with all arc types, fire, compare with the bitmap executor) is the same example; over whole runs on the untimed immediate synchronous fragment the comparison is precompiled_refines_bitmap_immediate (Refinement.lean), which cites CONC-021.
- The Kind line is F, the kind of its one block (ruling D21: one letter); the structure sentences are Q content without a line.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_022"></a>
## CONC-022: Flat-Array Token Storage

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_022` · Kind **F** · Scope the precompiled executor's token storage · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 880805f193ea6fac ai** · Statement hash `880805f193ea6fac`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The precompiled executor's token storage *shall* hold a dedicated queue for each place of the net it is built for.<br><br>*When* a token is added to a place the token storage holds a queue for, the token storage *shall* append it at the tail of the place's queue whatever the capacity of the place's storage, *shall* keep holding a queue for every place it held, and *shall* leave the queue of every other place unchanged.<br><br>*When* the first token of a marked place the token storage holds a queue for is removed, the token storage *shall* return the head of the place's queue, keep the rest of that queue in queue order, keep holding a queue for every place it held, and leave the queue of every other place unchanged.<br><br>*When* the first token of a place the token storage holds a queue for is read without removing it, the token storage *shall* return the head of the place's queue, or nothing when the place is not marked.<br><br>The token storage *shall* report as the token count of a place it holds a queue for the length of the place's queue. | 1. For a token store S by place id:<br>2. for every number n, some state of S holds a queue for each of the place ids below n;<br>3. and for every state s of S and place p for which s is a well-formed store holding a queue for p (S.ok s p):<br>4. adding a token x to p appends x at the tail of p's queue; every place q the store held a queue for still has one, and every such q other than p keeps its queue;<br>5. if p is marked, removing the first token of p returns the head of p's queue and leaves p its queue without the head, in order; every place q the store held a queue for still has one, and every such q other than p keeps its queue;<br>6. peeking p returns the head of p's queue, which is nothing when p's queue is empty;<br>7. the count of p is the length of p's queue. | <pre>fun S ↦<br>  (∀ (n : PlaceId), ∃ s, ∀ p &lt; n, S.ok s p) ∧<br>    (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId) (x : Colour),<br>        S.ok s p →<br>          S.view (S.add s p x) p = S.view s p ++ [x] ∧<br>            ∀ (q : PlaceId),<br>              S.ok s q →<br>                S.ok (S.add s p x) q ∧ (q ≠ p → S.view (S.add s p x) q = S.view s q)) ∧<br>      (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId),<br>          S.ok s p →<br>            Marked (Counts (S.view s)) p →<br>              (S.removeFirst s p).1 = Head (S.view s) p ∧<br>                S.view (S.removeFirst s p).2 p = (S.view s p).tail ∧<br>                  ∀ (q : PlaceId),<br>                    S.ok s q →<br>                      S.ok (S.removeFirst s p).2 q ∧<br>                        (q ≠ p → S.view (S.removeFirst s p).2 q = S.view s q)) ∧<br>        (∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId), S.ok s p → S.peek s p = Head (S.view s) p) ∧<br>          ∀ (s : S.σ) (p : PlaceId), S.ok s p → S.count s p = Counts (S.view s) p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a token store by place id (glossary: MarkingOps, at place ids PlaceId and token values Colour). Its state type is σ; view s p is the queue place p holds in s, oldest token first (glossary: Queue order); ok s p says that s is a well-formed store that holds a queue for p. A store whose places are fixed when the net is compiled (the ring pool sized per place id) holds queues for those places only, so lines 2 to 5 are stated at the places the store holds, as the quoted sentences are ('a place the token storage holds a queue for').
- Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. The interface has no net, so 'each place of the net it is built for' is read on place ids: a compiled net of n places numbers them 0 to n - 1 (CONC-020; which name gets which id, and where tokens on a place outside the net go, are CONC-020's and CORE-072's subject), and line 1 asks for a state holding a queue for each of them, for every n. It rules out a store with no well-formed state (CONC_022_forbids_noPlace) and a store that holds a queue for one place only, which satisfies lines 2 to 5 with their frame halves empty (CONC_022_mutant_heldFree_killed). It does not say that the state is empty, nor that it is the state an executor starts from: the interface has no constructor for the store of a net, so neither can be stated (see the ok assumption below).
- The scope is the precompiled executor's token storage: the section stands under the heading 'Precompiled Flat-Array Executor', and the first quoted sentence names it; the later sentences say 'the token storage' for the same storage. The Bitmap reference executor's marking is CORE-070's subject, over the same interface.
- Which states are ok is the implementation's choice, made by its refinement to its runtime, and the statement only constrains ok states. A store can therefore hide a fault by leaving out of ok every state it fails on, provided the states it keeps are closed under the operations: a ring pool whose growth (new capacity cap + cap / 2) leaves a ring of capacity 1 at capacity 1, with ok asking every ring to have capacity 2 or more, satisfies the block (CONC_022_allows_noGrowCap1) although it loses a token on the capacity-1 ring that the reference grows (conc022_noGrowCap1_wrong). The reference's ok (Pool.WF and a place id below nplaces) is the widest one: it holds every well-formed pool, capacity-1 rings included, and conc022_fullPool shows such a ring grow. The Rust runtime starts every ring at capacity 4 and doubles it (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:34, 162, grow_ring_static at :1412). Closing the gap needs the store an executor starts from in the interface (a constructor of MarkingOps, a glossary change) or in the executor model (CONC-025's Materialiser, RefExec in W5); neither is in this block.
- Token values are Colour (a natural number). No line inspects a value, so the choice of value type does not matter; it is fixed because the witness, the ring pool, stores Colour.
- The two prose sentences of the section ('Token storage uses ring buffers indexed by place ID for O(1) access.' and 'Each place has a dedicated ring buffer that preserves FIFO ordering [CORE-013] and grows dynamically when capacity is exceeded.') are not quoted. Their behaviour is the five shall sentences: 'indexed by place ID' is the store being addressed by place id, 'each place has a dedicated' buffer is line 1 with the frame halves of lines 2 and 3, 'preserves FIFO ordering' is lines 3 and 4 (AC2), 'grows dynamically when capacity is exceeded' is line 2 whatever the capacity. 'Ring buffer', 'grows dynamically' as a mechanism, and 'O(1)' are data structure and cost (kind Q): any unbounded store meets line 2 without growing, and the TypeScript precompiled executor keeps a plain array per place (typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:179) and removes the head with Array.shift, while Rust and Java keep ring buffers. How that wording is migrated is ruling D20 (clash conc-b#5, recommendation CB-4, decided (a)); the block is written against the behaviour, which every runtime has, so the wording edit does not change it. The section's Kind line is F, the kind of its one block, following the one-letter convention of the signed blocks (spec/04-execution-model.md:41, EXEC-002, Kind F with Q content); whether the Kind line changes for Q content is ruling D21, decided (a): one Kind letter per ID, with the matrix showing it.
- Line 2 is the second quoted sentence. 'Whatever the capacity of the place's storage' is the growth of AC3: the store accepts the add at a full place too, and the token lands at the tail with every earlier token in order; the line does not test fullness, it holds at every capacity. 'Keep holding a queue for every place it held' is the S.ok conjunct, which keeps a bounded store from escaping the line by making ok false at a full place. A ring that never grows overwrites its oldest token (CONC_022_forbids_noGrow), and a growth that copies the ring from the start of its block instead of from its head reorders a wrapped ring (CONC_022_forbids_badGrow). The frame half ('leave the queue of every other place unchanged') is the section's 'dedicated' buffer: one queue shared by all places violates it (CONC_022_forbids_shared), and so does a growth in place whose new slots run on into the next place's block (CONC_022_forbids_inPlaceGrow).
- Lines 2 and 3 are stated at a place the store holds, frame half included: an add or a removal at a place id the store does not hold is not constrained, and may change any queue. The quoted sentences say the same ('a place the token storage holds a queue for'). The ring model needs this: its fields are total functions, and Pool.addLast at a place id at or above nplaces grows into a block that may overlap a held place's. No runtime makes that call: Rust routes a token on a place outside the net to extra_marking (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:1331), and ring_add_last indexes place_offset by the place id, which panics out of range. Where such a token goes is CORE-072's subject.
- Line 3 is the third quoted sentence, stated for a marked place (glossary: Marked) on the count of the view. Removing the first token of an unmarked place is not a call the precompiled executor makes (ring_remove_first unwraps the head slot, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:396-403, and the ring pool's well-formedness does not survive a removal at count zero), so it is left out; what a marking does there is CORE-070's subject. A LIFO removal is the mutant CONC_022_mutant_lifo.
- Line 3 is about the storage operation that removes the first token, not about which tokens a firing consumes. Which tokens a firing consumes is EXEC-010's subject (oldest first, except on a correlated ν input, ruling D16); a correlated ν input removes the first matching token through a different operation (ring_remove_matching, Libpetri.Pool.removeMatching in Ring.lean), which this interface does not have. Ruling D30 (a), recommendation CB-3, is decided: AC2's text now carries D16's exclusion ('except on a correlated input of a match specification, [NU-020]'). Line 3 is the storage operation, not the consumption order of a firing, so no formula changes.
- Line 4 is the fourth quoted sentence: the token storage reads a place's first token (the read arc's peek, glossary Queue order 'reads the head') without changing the store; peek takes the state and returns only a token, so it changes nothing by its type. On an unmarked place the head of the queue is nothing (glossary Head), which is the sentence's 'or nothing when the place is not marked'. A peek of the newest token violates the line (CONC_022_forbids_peekNewest), and so does a peek that returns a default token on an empty place (CONC_022_forbids_peekDefault).
- Line 5 is the fifth quoted sentence, on the glossary's Token count of the view. A count that reports only whether the place is marked violates it (CONC_022_forbids_presenceCount).
- AC1 (token access is O(1) by place ID, no hashing or map lookup) is cost, kind Q, and is not encoded: the statement only fixes that the store is addressed by place id. AC1 is false of the TypeScript precompiled executor's removal (Array.shift on a plain array, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1098) and of tokens on places the compiled net does not know, which TypeScript keeps in a map keyed by name (unknownPlaceTokens, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:181-188, CORE-072); the wording is D20's.
- AC2 (FIFO ordering is preserved, oldest token consumed first, except on a correlated input of a match specification, [NU-020]) is lines 3 and 4, together with line 2's tail append: a token added later is removed and read later (CONC_022_nonvacuous). The ν exception is the line 3 assumption above: a correlated input removes through ring_remove_matching, an operation this interface does not have.
- AC3 (ring buffers grow dynamically when capacity is exceeded) is line 2 at a full place (CONC_022_nonvacuous: a full wrapped ring of capacity 2 takes a third token in order; CONC_022_nonvacuous_frame: a full ring grows next to another place's block and that place keeps its queue).
- AC4 (token count per place is available in O(1)) is line 5; the cost is kind Q, not encoded.
- The test derivation (add and consume tokens in various orders, verify FIFO ordering and counts) is CONC_022_nonvacuous and CONC_022_nonvacuous_frame on the ring pool.
- The section depends on CORE-013 (token FIFO ordering). Both blocks use the glossary term Queue order; CORE-013 states it over the queue firing relation, and CONC_022_refQOps shows that the queue marking the EXEC and CORE-013 blocks step (refQOps, view the identity) is itself a store this block accepts. The consistency theorem spec_consistent_queue puts CONC-022 and CORE-070 on one store, the ring pool with its removal guarded by the count (core070_ringMarking, CONC_022_ringMarking).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CONC_023"></a>
## CONC-023: Priority-Partitioned Ready Queues

`Libpetri.Spec.CONC_023` · Kind **F** · Scope the ready order of the precompiled executor, and by AC4 of every backend; on the all-immediate fast path the declaration order (ruling D14 (a)) · Source **verbatim** (spec/05-concurrency.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 814d35b7abaf7bf8 ai** · Statement hash `814d35b7abaf7bf8`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* be the ready transitions grouped by priority level, at most one group per priority level, with the groups in descending order of priority.<br><br>*Where* the net does not take the all-immediate fast path, the ready order *shall* offer the ready transitions of one priority level in ascending order of stamp.<br><br>The ready order *shall* hold every ready transition exactly once and no other transition, on the all-immediate fast path as well.<br><br>The ready order *shall* offer ready transitions of one priority level with equal stamps in ascending declaration order, also when they were armed in different cycles and on the all-immediate fast path.<br><br>Within the same priority, FIFO ordering by enablement time is preserved.<br><br>Feeding a level's queue in declaration order is NOT sufficient: transitions enabled in different cycles must drain in enablement order even when it disagrees with declaration order, and equal enablement timestamps break by ascending declaration order — the identical order [EXEC-002] AC3/AC4 requires of every backend.<br><br>The all-immediate single-priority fast path is exempt: it bypasses the ready queues and fires in declaration order, which [EXEC-002] AC4 requires of every backend alike. | 1. For every input of a pass, fast path included:<br>2. the order holds every ready transition exactly once and no other transition;<br>3. two transitions of equal priority and equal stamp come in ascending declaration order;<br>4. and off the all-immediate fast path there are groups (a priority and a list of transitions each) such that the order is the groups drained one after the other, the groups' priorities are strictly descending, so each priority level has at most one group, and every transition of a group has the group's priority;<br>5. and within each group a transition with an earlier stamp comes first, and of two with equal stamps the earlier-declared one comes first;<br>6. and on the all-immediate fast path the order is the ready transitions in ascending declaration order, whatever their stamps. | <pre>fun O ↦<br>  ∀ (I : ReadyIn),<br>    ((O I).Perm I.readyList ∧<br>        List.Pairwise (fun a c ↦ I.prio a = I.prio c → I.clock a = I.clock c → a &lt; c)<br>          (O I)) ∧<br>      (¬I.FastPath →<br>          ∃ blocks,<br>            O I = List.flatMap (fun x ↦ x.2) blocks ∧<br>              (List.Pairwise (fun x1 x2 ↦ x1 > x2) (List.map (fun x ↦ x.1) blocks) ∧<br>                  ∀ b ∈ blocks, ∀ a ∈ b.2, I.prio a = b.1) ∧<br>                ∀ b ∈ blocks,<br>                  List.Pairwise<br>                    (fun a c ↦ I.clock a &lt; I.clock c ∨ I.clock a = I.clock c ∧ a &lt; c)<br>                    b.2) ∧<br>        (I.FastPath → O I = I.readyList)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is EXEC-002's ordering function O from the inputs of one pass (ReadyIn: the transitions numbered in declaration order, their priorities, timings and stamps, and which are ready) to the list of ready transitions in the order the pass offers them for firing. A group of the formula is the content of one priority level's ready queue when the pass drains it; the formula does not model the queues, only the order they produce. Ready and stamp are the glossary terms (Armed, Ready, [TIME-010]); which transitions are ready and which reading becomes a stamp are EXEC-002's and TIME-010's inputs, free here.
- The first quoted sentence is line 3 ('the ready transitions grouped by priority level' together with line 1: each ready transition in exactly one group, nothing else; 'at most one group per priority level, with the groups in descending order of priority' is the strictly descending group priorities). Levels that hold no ready transition need no group. It restates the body sentence 'Transition selection scans priority levels in descending order and picks the first non-empty queue, giving O(L) selection where L is the number of distinct priority levels (typically 1–3).' as far as the order of one pass shows it: 'picks the first non-empty queue' is read as the selection of the next transition, repeated until every queue is drained, not as a pass that offers the highest level only (conc023_topOnly is forbidden by line 1). Re-selection after a firing of the same pass has changed which transitions are ready is the executor's pass model (EXEC-001, EXEC-003), a Phase 2 behaviour line over RefExec, not this block; the test derivation's 'fire in correct priority order' is likewise checked as offer order. The selection cost O(L) is not encoded.
- The second quoted sentence is line 4, which states it inside one group together with line 2 (equal priority holds inside a group), so that the groups are Sched.lean's LevelBlocks. The third quoted sentence is line 1 and the fourth is line 2, both on every input. 'Also when they were armed in different cycles': the interface has no cycle, the stamp is all a pass reads of the arming, and the firing clock's readings 'never decrease and may repeat' (glossary Firing clock, GlossaryTime ClockReading), so two transitions armed in different cycles can share a stamp, and line 2 then gives declaration order (conc023_Irep_forced).
- AC4's first two sentences (quoted) are line 4 with line 2: within a level, stamp ascending, then declaration order ascending. 'Enablement time' and 'enablement timestamp' are the stamp, and 'enablement order' is stamp order. 'Transitions enabled in different cycles must drain in enablement order even when it disagrees with declaration order' is line 4 on two stamps that differ; on two stamps that are equal although the cycles differ, the clause 'equal enablement timestamps break by ascending declaration order' governs, as the fourth quoted sentence says. Rewording AC4's 'transitions enabled in different cycles' to 'transitions with different stamps' is an editorial edit under ruling D20 (a), not yet made in the markdown. 'Feeding a level's queue in declaration order is NOT sufficient' is the mutant exec002_tidOrder (each level in declaration order), killed by line 4 (CONC_023_mutant_tid_killed). 'The identical order [EXEC-002] AC3/AC4 requires of every backend' is CONC_023_iff_EXEC_002: the block holds exactly when EXEC-002 holds.
- AC4's third sentence (quoted) is line 5 together with the premise 'not the all-immediate fast path' on lines 3 and 4. The fast path is ReadyIn.FastPath, EXEC-002's condition (every transition Immediate, all priorities equal), which is the condition all three runtimes test. 'It bypasses the ready queues' is the premise: no groups are asked of the fast path. 'And fires in declaration order' is line 5: the order is the ready list, whatever the stamps, as EXEC-002's fast-path line says (ruling D14 (a): the fast path is accepted as stated). Lines 1 and 2 hold on the fast path as well and there follow from line 5. The runtimes scan the enablement bitmap in ascending declaration index on the fast path: rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs and bitmap_backend.rs (collect_ready_immediate), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java (fireReadyImmediate), typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts (fireReadyImmediate). A backend without the fast path that sorts by stamp on every input is killed (CONC_023_mutant_fastOpen_killed: on exec002_Ifs, all Immediate and one priority, transition 1 armed before 0, the sort offers [1, 0] where line 5 asks [0, 1]); a fast path that offers only the first ready transition, offers transitions that are not ready, or reverses a tie is killed as well (CONC_023_mutant_generalOnly_killed, CONC_023_forbids_allFast, CONC_023_forbids_revFast).
- AC1 (distinct priority levels precomputed and sorted descending) is a property of the precompiled program's data (the priority-level array built at compile time), kind Q, inspected in the runtimes; its observable consequence is line 3, whose strictly descending group priorities are the sorted distinct levels that hold a ready transition. The body sentence 'Distinct priority values are sorted descending at compile time.' is the same as AC1. 'Each transition maps to a priority index for O(1) ready-queue insertion.' is data layout and cost, kind Q, not encoded.
- AC2 (each priority level has a separate FIFO queue) and AC3 (selection is O(L) in the number of distinct priority levels), and the body sentence 'Each priority level has its own FIFO queue.', are structure and cost, not encoded. As written they disagree with AC4 and with the runtimes (clash conc-b#6): a FIFO queue fed from the enablement bitmap gives declaration order, which AC4 calls not sufficient, so Rust and Java sort each level's queue by stamp and declaration order on every pass and TypeScript sorts one buffer. Their rewording is an editorial edit under ruling D20 (a), not yet made in the markdown, and is out of this block; lines 2 and 4 state the order the queues must deliver whatever their structure, so until that edit the quoted sentences are the binding ones.
- The test derivation (three priority levels; priority order across levels, FIFO within each level) is checked by CONC_023_nonvacuous on conc023_I5: priorities 3, 2 and 1, with two transitions of the lowest level armed in the order opposite to their declaration and two with equal stamps.
- Form: the quoted sentences use 'shall' inside a SHOULD requirement, as IO-016 and TIME-015 do. The SHOULD is the queue structure; the order the sentences state is required of every backend by EXEC-002 (MUST), so 'shall' is true whether or not a backend keeps per-level queues.
- Equivalence: line 1 to line 5 together are the same as EXEC-002's four lines (CONC_023_iff_EXEC_002; on the fast path line 5 is EXEC-002's fourth line; off the fast path, the order is a permutation of the ready transitions strictly sorted by EXEC-002's canonical key, the hard direction being conc023_blocks_of_sorted). That the precompiled backends compute the drain is Q evidence: collect_ready_general_refines (Sched.lean) shows that a drain of level blocks of the ready set equals the reference's sort, and precompiled_refines_bitmap_immediate (Refinement.lean) covers the immediate fragment.
