<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_032"></a>
## CORE-032: Read Arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 114ece4e82239077 ai** · Statement hash `114ece4e82239077`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a read place of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of a transition is marked, the read arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire or the marking its firing leaves.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, each of its read places on which it has neither an input arc nor a reset arc *shall* end the firing with its token count before the firing plus the tokens the firing deposits there. | 1. For every transition t and every read place p of t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;<br>3. from a marking m in which p is marked, t fires to m' exactly when t without its read arcs on p fires from m to m';<br>4. if t has no input arc and no reset arc on p, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) = m(p) + (tokens d puts in p). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    ReadArc t p →<br>      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (m : CountMarking N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            Marked m p → (Fire F t m m' ↔ Fire F (withoutRead t p) m m')) ∧<br>          ((∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →<br>            ¬ResetArc t p →<br>              ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>                F t m d m' → m' p = m p + Deposits d p)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
- AC1 (read place must have tokens for enablement) is the second line.
- AC2 (token remains in place after firing) is the fourth line, for a read place the transition neither consumes from nor resets. A place that is also an input place or a reset place of the same transition loses tokens through those arcs ([CORE-030], [CORE-034], [EXEC-013] AC4); the third line says the read arc adds nothing to that loss.
- AC3 (action receives the read token value) is not encoded: the firing relation works on token counts and has no action or token values. Which token is read is [EXEC-012]'s subject, the context access [CORE-061]'s.
- 'Marked' is read as 'holds at least one token' (glossary: Marked), the spec's 'at least one token for enablement'.
- AC2's 'token remains' is encoded at count level only. A firing that takes the read token out of p and puts it, or another token, back in the same step leaves the same counts and satisfies this statement, but moves the token to the FIFO tail and changes its timestamp. Token identity, FIFO position and timestamp are below the count granularity of the firing relation, as for CORE-030 AC2; they belong to [EXEC-012] ('both A and B remain after firing', the oldest is peeked), and no count-level block can catch the bug.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-032: `Seam.enabledNA` requires every read place to hold a token, so `t` does not fire while `p` is unmarked; the consumption (`Seam.nconsumed`), the deposits and the effect (`Seam.fireNC`) never read the read arcs, so with `p` marked removing them changes nothing; and with no input arc and no reset arc on `p`, `Seam.fireNC` leaves `m p - 0 + Deposits d p` there.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_032 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_ignoresRead` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Ignoring the read arc violates CORE-032 (first clause): `core032_t` fires from the empty marking.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_ignoresReadFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_readAlwaysBlocks` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ A read arc that blocks its transition while its place is marked violates CORE-032 (second clause): `core032_t` cannot fire from the marked marking, but without its read arc it can.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_readConsumes` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Consuming the read token violates CORE-032 (third clause): `core032_t` fires from the marking with one token in every place and leaves place `0` empty, depositing nothing.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_readConsumesFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_forbids_skipReadReset` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): ✗ Skipping the reset of a read place violates CORE-032 (second clause): with one token in place `0`, `core032_tRes` without its read arc fires and drains place `0`, but no firing of `core032_tRes` leaves place `0` empty.
  <pre>¬CORE_032 core032_skipReadResetFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropConserve_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The clearing firing kills the third mutant: it satisfies the mutant (it fires exactly when the reference does, and the reference satisfies the first two clauses) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` fires from the marked marking and leaves place `0` empty, depositing nothing).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropConserve core032_clearsAllFire ∧ ¬CORE_032 core032_clearsAllFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropMarked_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The always-blocking firing kills the second mutant: it satisfies the mutant (a transition with a read arc never fires) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` does not fire from the marked marking although it fires there without its read arc).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropMarked core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire ∧<br>  ¬CORE_032 core032_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_mutant_dropUnmarked_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): The idle firing kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (whether a transition fires does not depend on its arcs, and no firing changes a token count) but not CORE-032 (`core032_t` fires while its read place is unmarked).
  <pre>CORE_032_mutant_dropUnmarked core032_idleFire ∧ ¬CORE_032 core032_idleFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_032_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_032): All three clauses of CORE-032 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core032_t` has a read arc on place `0` and no input or reset arc there; it does not fire from the empty marking, although without its read arc it does (first clause); it fires from the marked marking, as it does without its read arc (second clause); and that firing deposits nothing and leaves place `0` holding its one token (third clause).

The firing relation `F` is the reference firing relation, the build check `Build` is the reference builder `refBuild`, the transition builder `TB` is the reference transition builder (whose build check is `refBuild`), and the instantiation function is the reference instantiation `refInst Nm`. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_033"></a>
## CORE-033: Read arc multi-reader

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 a864c7bea1b325a9 ai** · Statement hash `a864c7bea1b325a9`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a place is marked, a read arc to that place *shall not* stop its transition from firing, so all transitions with read arcs to the place can be enabled simultaneously.<br><br>*When* a transition with a read arc to a marked place fires, and the transition has no input arc and no reset arc to that place, the read arc of any transition to that place *shall not* stop that transition from firing afterwards (no conflict), since read arcs do not consume tokens. | 1. For every transition t and every read place p of t, at every marking m in which p is marked:<br>2. if t without its read arcs on p can fire from m, then t can fire from m;<br>3. for every two transitions t₁, t₂ with read arcs on p, where t₁ has no input arc and no reset arc on p:<br>4. after every firing of t₁ from a marking m in which p is marked to m', if t₂ without its read arcs on p can fire from m', then t₂ can fire from m'. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>      ReadArc t p →<br>        ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>          Marked m p →<br>            (∃ m', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t p) m m') → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧<br>    ∀ (t₁ t₂ : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>      ReadArc t₁ p →<br>        ReadArc t₂ p →<br>          (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t₁ p c) →<br>            ¬ResetArc t₁ p →<br>              on Fire F t₁, shall fun m m' ↦<br>                Marked m p →<br>                  (∃ m'', Fire F (core033_withoutRead t₂ p) m' m'') →<br>                    ∃ m'', Fire F t₂ m' m''</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.
- AC1 (two readers both enabled when the place has tokens) is the first two lines: whether a firing relation lets t fire from m depends on t and m alone, so 'both enabled' is each enabled, and each reader's read arc on a marked p adds no condition. The text does not claim a reader fires with its other arcs unsatisfied, hence the comparison with the reader without its read arcs on p.
- AC2 (both can fire without conflict) is read in the untimed interleaving: firing one reader does not take away, through p, the other reader's ability to fire (last two lines). Conflicts through other places (t₁ consuming an input of t₂, or depositing into an inhibitor place of t₂) are not this block's subject.
- The restriction to a t₁ with no input arc and no reset arc on p is an interpretation choice: such a t₁ removes tokens from p (CORE-030, CORE-034; EXEC-012 allows a read arc and a reset arc on one place), so it can disable the other reader; the text's reason 'read arcs do not consume tokens' covers the read arcs only.
- t₁ and t₂ may be the same transition: a reader firing twice in a row is covered too. In the untimed step model this is no stronger than the case of two transitions with the same arcs.
- The read token's value reaching the action (CORE-032 AC3, EXEC-012) is below the count granularity and not this block's subject.
- Both clauses assume p is marked: a reader firing from an empty read place is CORE-032 AC1 (its first clause), not this block's subject. A firing relation that ignores read arcs satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_ignoresRead).
- Clause 2 asks only that p stay marked for the other reader, which is what 'no conflict' needs. That a read leaves the count of p unchanged (apart from deposits) is CORE-032 AC2 (its third clause); the 'since read arcs do not consume tokens' of this text is that requirement's reason, not a second acceptance criterion here. A read that takes one token whenever two or more are present satisfies this block (CORE_033_allows_readTakesSurplus).
- Each firing is one atomic step, so a read token held or reserved while the reader's action runs (taken at the start and put back at completion, or a per-place lock on read places), which would keep two readers from being in flight together, cannot be expressed here. In-flight concurrency of readers needs a start/complete step model (CONC, EXEC); a take-and-put read that reorders the FIFO queue is below count granularity (EXEC-012).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-033: a read arc on a marked place adds no condition (`core033_ref_fire_of_withoutRead`), and a firing of a reader with no input arc and no reset arc on `p` consumes nothing from `p` and does not reset it (`refFire_apply`), so `p` stays marked for the other reader.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_033 RefFire</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_allows_ignoresRead` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): ✓ CORE-033 allows a firing relation that ignores read arcs, under which `core033_t₁` fires from the empty marking: both clauses assume the read place is marked, so a reader firing from an empty read place is outside this block. CORE-032's first clause rejects it (CORE-032's `CORE_032_forbids_ignoresRead`, for the same relation).
  <pre>CORE_033 core033_ignoresReadFire ∧<br>  Fire core033_ignoresReadFire core033_t₁ core033_empty core033_empty</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_allows_readTakesSurplus` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): ✓ CORE-033 allows a read that takes surplus tokens: the read place never becomes empty, so no reader blocks another ('no conflict' holds), yet `core033_t₁` fires from `core033_two`, deposits nothing and leaves one token in place `0`. CORE-032's third clause (the count after a firing is the count before plus the deposits) rejects it.
  <pre>CORE_033 core033_readTakesSurplusFire ∧<br>  core033_readTakesSurplusFire core033_t₁ core033_two [] fun n ↦ if n = 0 then 1 else 2</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_forbids_readAlwaysBlocks` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): ✗ A read arc that blocks its transition while its place is marked violates CORE-033 (first clause): `core033_t₁` cannot fire from `core033_one`, but without its read arc it can.
  <pre>¬CORE_033 core033_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_forbids_readConsumes` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): ✗ A read that consumes violates CORE-033 (second clause): `core033_t₁` fires from `core033_one` and drains place `0`, after which `core033_t₂` cannot fire although it can without its read arc.
  <pre>¬CORE_033 core033_readConsumesFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_mutant_dropEnabled_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): The always-blocking firing kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (a transition with a read arc never fires, so no reader's firing takes anything away) but not CORE-033 (`core033_t₁` does not fire from `core033_one`).
  <pre>CORE_033_mutant_dropEnabled core033_readAlwaysBlocksFire ∧<br>  ¬CORE_033 core033_readAlwaysBlocksFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_mutant_dropNoConflict_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): The consuming read kills the second mutant: it satisfies the mutant (a `One` input on a marked place adds no condition) but not CORE-033 (`core033_t₁` drains place `0` and blocks `core033_t₂`).
  <pre>CORE_033_mutant_dropNoConflict core033_readConsumesFire ∧<br>  ¬CORE_033 core033_readConsumesFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_033_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_033): Both clauses of CORE-033 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core033_t₁` and `core033_t₂` both read place `0`, which `core033_one` marks; `core033_t₁` without its read arc fires from `core033_one`, and so does `core033_t₁` (first clause); `core033_t₁` fires from `core033_one` back to `core033_one`, from which `core033_t₂` without its read arc and `core033_t₂` both fire (second clause).
  <pre>ReadArc core033_t₁ 0 ∧<br>  ReadArc core033_t₂ 0 ∧<br>    Marked core033_one 0 ∧<br>      Fire RefFire (core033_withoutRead core033_t₁ 0) core033_one core033_one ∧<br>        Fire RefFire core033_t₁ core033_one core033_one ∧<br>          Fire RefFire (core033_withoutRead core033_t₂ 0) core033_one core033_one ∧<br>            Fire RefFire core033_t₂ core033_one core033_one</pre>

The firing relation `F` is the reference firing relation, the build check `Build` is the reference builder `refBuild`, the transition builder `TB` is the reference transition builder (whose build check is `refBuild`), and the instantiation function is the reference instantiation `refInst Nm`. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_034"></a>
## CORE-034: Reset arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 93e6155b06c813c7 ai** · Statement hash `93e6155b06c813c7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, each of its reset places *shall* lose every token it held before the firing and end the firing holding exactly the tokens the firing deposited there.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* affect whether its transition can fire, whether the reset place is marked or not.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* change what its transition can deposit: from every marking, the transition and the same transition without its reset arcs *shall* be able to make exactly the same deposits, so a reset arc neither adds a deposit nor removes one.<br><br>A reset arc *shall not* change the token count of any place other than its own. | 1. For every transition t and every reset place p of t, writing t∖p for t without its reset arcs on p:<br>2. every firing of t that deposits d leaves p with exactly as many tokens as d puts in p, whatever p held before;<br>3. every firing of t∖p from a marking m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place (a reset arc removes no deposit, and t fires wherever t∖p does);<br>4. every firing of t from m that deposits d is matched by a firing of t∖p from m whose deposit puts the same number of tokens in every place and that leaves every place other than p with the same token count (a reset arc adds no deposit, t∖p fires wherever t does, and the arc changes no other place). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    ResetArc t p →<br>      (∀ (d : List N),<br>          on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>        (∀ (d : List N),<br>            on fun m m'' ↦ F (withoutReset t p) m d m'', shall fun m x ↦<br>              ∃ d' m', F t m d' m' ∧ SamePerPlace d d') ∧<br>          ∀ (d : List N),<br>            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>              ∃ d' m'',<br>                F (withoutReset t p) m d' m'' ∧<br>                  SamePerPlace d d' ∧<br>                    ∀ (q : N), q ≠ p → TokenCount m' q = TokenCount m'' q</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking: removing a reset arc changes where a firing leads, so the second sentence compares the existence of a firing, not its target. It is the existence half of the second and third lines taken together (`CORE_034_canFire`), so it has no line of its own.
- Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit, whatever their order (`SamePerPlace`).
- AC1 (fires even if the reset place is empty) is the second line at a marking with p empty: the reset arc on p adds no condition, so t fires there whenever t∖p does. The text does not claim t fires with its other arcs unsatisfied.
- AC2 (all tokens removed on firing) is the first line. A reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there (glossary: Deposit); a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, whatever was consumed from it.
- AC3 (no token requirement, no contribution to enablement) is the second and third lines at every marking, empty or marked.
- AC4 (same deposits with and without the reset arc, compared per place; a reset arc on an output place neither adds nor removes an outcome) is the second line (no outcome removed) and the third line (no outcome added).
- The third line is also the frame of a reset arc: it rules out a reset that also empties a place the transition has no arc to, and a reset whose removed tokens feed a Forward or timeout deposit (they are not consumed; IO-013/IO-014 forward only consumed tokens). It compares against the same transition without the arc rather than spelling out the whole marking change; the effect of the other arcs is CORE-030, CORE-031, CORE-032 and IO-013's subject.
- The comparison is over firing relations, not over which output specs build: a transition and the same transition without its reset arcs have the same output spec, so the build-time checks of IO-011 to IO-014 accept both or neither.
- Token counts only: which tokens are removed, and EXEC-003 AC5 (a reset later in the same firing pass leaves same-pass deposits in place) are below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject, not this block's.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-034: `Seam.fireNC` sets a reset place to the deposit count (`refFire_apply`), neither `Seam.enabledNA` nor the deposit (`Seam.nconsumed`) reads the reset arcs, so a firing of `t` and of `t` without its reset arcs on `p` exist at the same markings with the same deposits, and `Seam.fireNC` reads the reset arcs only at the reset place itself.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_034 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_firstBranch` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc that removes a deposit violates CORE-034 (second clause): without its reset arc `core034_tXor12` deposits in place `2`, with it only in place `1`.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_firstBranchFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_keepsTokens` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc that removes nothing violates CORE-034 (first clause): under the idle firing `core034_t` fires from `core034_full`, deposits nothing, and place `0` keeps its three tokens.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_idleFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetAfterDeposit` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset that also removes the firing's own deposit violates CORE-034 (first clause): `core034_tOut` deposits one token in its reset place `0` and must end holding it, not zero.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_resetAfterDepositFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetForwards` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset whose removed tokens feed a forward violates CORE-034 (third clause): on timeout `core034_tFwd` forwards the three tokens its reset removed from place `0` into place `1`, a deposit no firing of `core034_tFwd` without its reset arc makes, in any order (it consumed nothing from `0`).
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_resetForwardsFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetNeedsToken` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset arc with a token requirement violates CORE-034 (second clause): without its reset arc `core034_t` fires from the empty marking, with it no firing matches.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_resetNeedsTokenFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_forbids_resetsNeighbour` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): ✗ A reset that also empties a place the transition has no arc to violates CORE-034 (third clause): without its reset arc `core034_t` leaves place `1` at three tokens, with it place `1` ends at zero.
  <pre>¬CORE_034 core034_resetsNeighbourFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_mutant_dropEmpties_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The idle firing kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (every transition fires from every marking, whatever its arcs, deposits nothing and changes nothing) but not CORE-034 (place `0` keeps its tokens).
  <pre>CORE_034_mutant_dropEmpties core034_idleFire ∧ ¬CORE_034 core034_idleFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_mutant_dropFrame_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The neighbour-emptying firing kills the third mutant: the reset place itself ends with the deposit and every firing without the arc is matched by one with it (the mutant holds), but place `1` is emptied by a reset on place `0` (CORE-034 fails).
  <pre>CORE_034_mutant_dropFrame core034_resetsNeighbourFire ∧<br>  ¬CORE_034 core034_resetsNeighbourFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_mutant_dropRemoves_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): The first-branch firing kills the second mutant: its firings are reference firings, so they empty every reset place and are matched by the firing without the arc (the mutant holds; a deposit of the first branch stays one when a reset arc is dropped, because the deposit does not read the reset arcs), but `core034_tXor12` cannot deposit in place `2` although it can without its reset arc (CORE-034 fails).
  <pre>CORE_034_mutant_dropRemoves core034_firstBranchFire ∧ ¬CORE_034 core034_firstBranchFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_034_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_034): All three clauses of CORE-034 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core034_t` has a reset arc on place `0`; from `core034_full` it fires and empties place `0` (first clause, three tokens removed, none deposited), where without its reset arc place `0` would keep them, while every other place ends the same with and without the arc (third clause); it fires from the empty marking, as it does without its reset arc (second clause, reset place unmarked); `core034_tOut`, whose reset place is also its output place, ends with place `0` holding the one token it deposited there (first clause with a nonzero deposit); and `core034_tXor` (AC4), with the reset arc on one of its two output places, deposits in place `0` or in place `1` exactly as it does without the arc, and after depositing in place `0` holds that token alone there.

The firing relation `F` is the reference firing relation, the build check `Build` is the reference builder `refBuild`, the transition builder `TB` is the reference transition builder (whose build check is `refBuild`), and the instantiation function is the reference instantiation `refInst Nm`. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_035"></a>
## CORE-035: Output arc

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 7ce7e918319b593c ai** · Statement hash `7ce7e918319b593c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, it *shall* deposit tokens only in its output places, according to its output spec (see [IO-010]–[IO-015]).<br><br>*When* a transition fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold every token the firing deposited.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, every place that is neither an input place nor a reset place of the transition *shall* change by exactly the tokens the firing deposited there. | 1. For every transition t and every deposit d:<br>2. every firing of t that deposits d puts tokens only in places that t's output spec names;<br>3. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a marking in which every place holds at least as many tokens as d put there;<br>4. every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves every place p with no input arc and no reset arc of t holding m p plus what d put in p, no more and no less. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (d : List N),<br>    (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>        ∀ (p : N), Produced d p → OutputArc t p) ∧<br>      (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ m' p) ∧<br>        on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>          ∀ (p : N),<br>            (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) → ¬ResetArc t p → m' p = m p + Deposits d p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. 'When the transition's action completes' is read as 'when the firing deposits', for every outcome: the timeout outcome ([IO-013]) also deposits only in places the output spec names (a Timeout child, a ForwardInput's `to`).
- An output place is a place the transition's output spec names (glossary: Output arc), every Xor branch, Timeout child and ForwardInput `to` included. A transition with no output spec has no output place, so its firings deposit nothing.
- Which output places one firing deposits in, and how many tokens, is the subject of [IO-010]–[IO-016] ('according to its output spec'), not of this block: a firing relation that never deposits satisfies CORE-035 and is ruled out by [IO-016].
- The second line says only that the deposited tokens are in the resulting marking; the exact count of an input place is [CORE-030]'s and of a reset place [CORE-034]'s. A reset place that is also an output place ends holding exactly what was deposited, which satisfies the line.
- The third line is the marking side of 'only in its output places': on every place [CORE-030] and [CORE-034] do not cover (a pure output place, a read-only or inhibitor-only place, a place with no arc), the firing adds exactly its deposit. A place the firing does not deposit in is therefore unchanged, and an output place keeps its earlier tokens (no overwrite, no double or deduplicated deposit). On read places this coincides with [CORE-032]'s third clause.
- AC1 (after the transition fires, produced tokens appear in the output place) is the second line, with the first saying the place is an output place.
- AC2 (output tokens carry the current timestamp): not encoded. The firing relation works on token counts and carries no token timestamps; timestamps are [CORE-011] and the timed semantics' subject.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): The reference semantics satisfies CORE-035: `Reference.deposit` takes its tokens from an output branch (`Out.branches`) or from the first `Timeout` child (`Out.timeoutDeposits`), both of which name only places of the output spec; and `Seam.fireNC` adds the deposit's counts to every place (after consumption, or in place of the old count on a reset place), so a place with no input or reset arc gains exactly the deposit.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_035 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_dedup` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A deduplicating store violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from `core035_one`, and place `0` keeps one token instead of two.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_dedupFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_double` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A double deposit violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from the empty marking and place `0` ends with two tokens for a deposit of one.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_doubleFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_lost` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Losing the deposited tokens violates CORE-035 (second clause): `core035_t` deposits a token in place `0`, but under `core035_lostFire` the marking it leaves is still empty.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_lostFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_overwrite` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Overwriting an output place violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` fires from `core035_one`, and place `0` ends with one token instead of two.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_overwriteFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_phantom` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ A phantom write violates CORE-035 (third clause): `core035_t` deposits only in place `0`, yet place `7` gains a token.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_phantomFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_resetAfter` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Resetting after depositing violates CORE-035 (second clause): `core035_r` deposits a token in its reset place `0`, which `core035_resetAfterFire` then empties.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_resetAfterFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_forbids_stray` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): ✗ Depositing outside the output spec violates CORE-035 (first clause): `core035_silent` has no output spec, yet under `core035_strayFire` it deposits a token in place `0`.
  <pre>¬CORE_035 core035_strayFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_mutant_dropAppear_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): The reset-after firing kills the second mutant: off the reset places it is the reference firing, so it satisfies the mutant, but it empties a reset place the deposit filled.
  <pre>CORE_035_mutant_dropAppear core035_resetAfterFire ∧ ¬CORE_035 core035_resetAfterFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_mutant_dropFrame_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): The double firing kills the third mutant: its deposits are reference deposits and the marking holds them, but it adds each deposit twice.
  <pre>CORE_035_mutant_dropFrame core035_doubleFire ∧ ¬CORE_035 core035_doubleFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_mutant_dropOutputs_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): The stray firing kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (it adds its deposit to the marking) but not CORE-035 (it deposits outside the output spec).
  <pre>CORE_035_mutant_dropOutputs core035_strayFire ∧ ¬CORE_035 core035_strayFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_035_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_035): All three clauses of CORE-035 are exercised by the reference semantics: `core035_t` fires from the empty marking depositing a token in place `0`, which is an output place of `core035_t` (first clause) and holds that token afterwards (second clause); fired again from `core035_one`, place `0`, which has no input or reset arc, ends with its old token plus the new one (third clause).
  <pre>RefFire core035_t core035_empty [0] core035_one ∧<br>  Produced [0] 0 ∧<br>    OutputArc core035_t 0 ∧<br>      Deposits [0] 0 = 1 ∧<br>        core035_one 0 = 1 ∧<br>          RefFire core035_t core035_one [0] core035_two ∧<br>            core035_two 0 = core035_one 0 + 1</pre>

The firing relation `F` is the reference firing relation, the build check `Build` is the reference builder `refBuild`, the transition builder `TB` is the reference transition builder (whose build check is `refBuild`), and the instantiation function is the reference instantiation `refInst Nm`. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_036"></a>
## CORE-036: Arc semantics summary

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_036` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors; the outcome line with output validation enabled (CONC-026, the default) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 153aed3781898e2a ai** · Statement hash `153aed3781898e2a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* an input place of the transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of the transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* an inhibitor place of the transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the transition has no match specification ([NU-020]) and is enabled, it *shall* be able to fire, whatever its output places and reset places hold.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each input place that is not a reset place *shall* lose the consumption count of its input arc, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each place that is neither an input place nor a reset place *shall* lose no tokens, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each reset place *shall* end holding exactly what the firing deposited there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with its action, on an executor with output validation enabled ([CONC-026], the default), the places in which it deposits *shall* be exactly the places of one output branch of its output spec, each receiving one or more tokens.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall* deposit in every place as many tokens as the timeout outcome puts there ([IO-013], [IO-014]).<br><br>Deposits are compared per place: the order in which a firing deposits its tokens is not normative, and two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit.<br><br>As in [CORE-022], the transitions these sentences describe are transitions that build: a definition that building rejects is not a transition of any net and never fires. | 1. For every transition t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which an input place p holds fewer tokens than the required count c of its input arc;<br>3. t does not fire from a marking in which a read place p is unmarked;<br>4. t does not fire from a marking in which an inhibitor place p is marked;<br>5. if t builds (Builds t: it passes every build-time check), then from every marking at which t is enabled some firing of t exists (to some marking);<br>6. every firing of t that deposits d leaves an input place p that is not a reset place with what it held, minus the consumption count of its arc, plus what d puts in p;<br>7. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t with what it held plus what d puts in p;<br>8. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a reset place p with exactly what d puts in p;<br>9. every firing of t from m that deposits d either puts one or more tokens in each place of some output branch b of t and none in any other place, or puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout outcome d₀ of t for what the firing consumed from m. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    (∀ (p : N) (c : Card),<br>        InputArc t p c → while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p &lt; requiredCount c, never Fire F t) ∧<br>      (∀ (p : N), ReadArc t p → while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (p : N), InhibitorArc t p → while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>          (Builds t → ∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧<br>            (∀ (d : List N) (p : N) (c : Card),<br>                InputArc t p c →<br>                  ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                      TokenCount m' p =<br>                        TokenCount m p - consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) +<br>                          Deposits d p) ∧<br>              (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                  (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →<br>                    ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = TokenCount m p + Deposits d p) ∧<br>                (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                    ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>                  ∀ (d : List N),<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m x ↦<br>                      (∃ b, OutputBranch t b ∧ OnPlacesOf d b) ∨<br>                        ∃ d₀, TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d₀ ∧ SamePerPlace d d₀</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part, so 'produced on complete' (Output) and 'consumed / removed on fire' (Input, Reset) both land in the one step. 'Able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.
- Requires token? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as 'holds at least the required count' (glossary: Enabled, Required count), which is one token for One and All; 'Yes' for a read arc as 'marked'; 'No (blocks if present)' for an inhibitor arc as 'marked blocks'. The 'No' entries (output, reset, and the inhibitor arc while its place is unmarked) are read together as the fourth line: the table lists every token requirement, so a transition whose input, read and inhibitor arcs are all satisfied can fire whatever its output and reset places hold.
- Consumes? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as the consumption count of IO-007 (glossary: Consumption count). 'No' for output, inhibitor and read arcs is the sixth line: a place that only those arcs touch loses nothing. 'Yes (all)' for a reset arc is the seventh line (glossary: Deposit): a reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there, and a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, so the fifth line excludes reset places.
- The fifth line uses truncated subtraction, as Seam.fireNC does; under the first line the subtraction never truncates, because a firing only starts when every input place holds at least its required count.
- Effect column, Output ('Token produced on complete') is the outcome line, the last line of the reading, which reads the eighth, ninth and tenth sentences quoted together. A firing relation does not record how a firing ended. As IO-012 says, a firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome, and a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome. So the eighth and ninth sentences are read as one disjunction: the deposit marks exactly the places of an output branch (eighth: the branch fixes which places receive tokens, one or more each, not how many; glossary: Output branch, Produced set), or it equals a timeout outcome per place (ninth: as many tokens in every place). A transition with no output spec has the one empty branch, so it deposits nothing. Read ('Token remains') is the sixth line. Inhibitor ('Disables transition') is the third line.
- Tenth sentence (deposits are compared per place). Every line of the reading reads the deposit d only through Deposits d (the produced set of d is the set of places p with Deposits d p ≠ 0), so two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place satisfy it alike and the order of d plays no part: core036_c8_perPlace shows it for the outcome line, and core036_perPlace_closed shows that closing any firing relation under per-place equal deposits keeps CORE-036. Lines 5 to 7 already compare per place.
- The outcome line is scoped by CONC-026: F is read as the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled, the default. With the CONC-026 skip enabled a firing that ends with its action deposits what the action wrote, as CONC-026 says, and the outcome line is not claimed of it; lines 1 to 7 hold of every executor.
- The eleventh sentence (the transitions described are those that build) is read as CORE-022 reads it: 'transitions that build' is the glossary term Builds. It scopes line 4, the one existence claim: a definition that building rejects never fires (CORE-022, CONC-026), so no firing of it is asked, and an executor that holds only transitions that build satisfies CORE-036 (CORE_036_builtOnly). Lines 1 to 3 and 5 to 8 forbid or constrain firings; a transition that does not build has no firing in any executor, so on it they ask nothing of an executor, and they are stated over every Trans because the reference fires every transition and meets them on all of them. TimeoutOutcome reads the first Timeout node in pre-order. A transition that builds holds at most one Timeout node and no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child (IO-013, IO-014), so that node's outcome is the timeout outcome. That at most one output branch matches a deposit (IO-012) is not part of CORE-036: the outcome line asks for some branch.
- Transitions with a ν match specification (NU-020) are scoped out of the fourth sentence (ruling D30, as in CORE-022): such a transition can be enabled at count level (glossary: Enabled) and still unable to fire, because no single name satisfies every correlated input. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so line 4 quantifies over every transition that builds. On a correlated input the consumption count of the fifth sentence applies to the tokens of the chosen name (glossary: Correlated input), not to the whole place; line 5 reads it over the whole place, which is the same thing for a transition with no match specification. How the correlation condition decides a firing and what it consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here. Lines 1 to 3 need no exclusion, for the reason CORE-022 gives: a correlated input requires at least its required count of tokens of one name, so at least its required count of tokens.
- Which runtime firings are steps of F. A firing whose action fails, or whose completion fails output validation (EXEC-030, IO-015 AC2 and AC3), consumes its inputs and clears its reset places but deposits no outcome; it is not a firing in F (glossary: Fire), as in CORE-050, so the outcome line says nothing of it and line 4 asks only that some firing exists. Tokens an action publishes before the firing ends (ctx.flush(), Rust and Python only; IO-015) are not in the one-step model, as in EXEC-020 and CORE-050: the orchestrator deposits each flushed batch as a step of its own (CONC-001), the firing's deposit d is what the executor deposits when the firing ends, and F is read as the firings whose action publishes nothing mid-action. With a flush, IO-015 counts the flushed places towards the eighth sentence's branch, and a firing that ends with the timeout outcome keeps the flushed tokens besides the timeout outcome (glossary: Action), so on Xor(A, Timeout(B)) an action that flushes A and then times out leaves A and B; that is the ninth sentence read over the deposit at the firing's end, and neither case is encoded.
- What the outcome line loses. A firing relation does not record how a firing ended, so a firing that ended with the timeout outcome but deposits exactly the places of some output branch, with any counts, satisfies the first disjunct. On t: All(2) -> Timeout(ForwardInput(2, 1)), which consumes two tokens from 2, the deposit [1] (forwarding only the first consumed token, which IO-014 forbids) passes, although the timeout outcome is [1, 1] (core036_fwdFirst_accepted): [1] is also the places of the Timeout child read as an output branch. The ninth sentence's full strength, per place for every firing that ends with the timeout outcome, is carried over a relation T of timed-out firings by IO-013's fifth line ('every firing of t in T from m deposits, place by place, exactly the tokens of the timeout outcome') and IO-014's firing line; here the ninth sentence only widens what an action firing may look like.
- The ninth sentence in the runtimes. Every runtime deposits the timeout outcome without validating it against the output spec and on the places the rewritten output spec names, as given: on And(A, Timeout(d, B)) a timed-out firing deposits B (Java BitmapNetExecutor and PrecompiledNetExecutor processCompletedTransitions, and TypeScript bitmap-net-executor.ts and precompiled-net-executor.ts, skip validation when TransitionContext.isDetachedForTimeout(); Rust, and Python on it, skip it on the timeout path), and Java (TransitionContext outputToHarvest and forwardToHarvest, ExecutorSupport produceTimeoutOutputRecursive) and TypeScript (transition-context.ts outputToHarvest and forwardToHarvest) take the actual places without resolving them through the composition correspondence again. Two wrong executors are recorded in spec/runtime-defects.md as history of Java and TypeScript. RD-01: one that validates the timeout outcome against the whole output spec fails every timed-out firing of And(A, Timeout(d, B)); the statement does not catch it, because a failed firing is not in F and line 4 asks only that some firing exists; IO-013's T-lines do (IO_013_forbids_validateTimeout). RD-31: one that resolves the timeout branch's places through the correspondence a second time deposits, on a port collision (port a bound to b, port b bound to c), the timeout token meant for b on c; when c is an output place the deposit can pass the first disjunct of the outcome line, so the statement does not catch it either; IO-013's fifth line and MOD-031 do (mod031ctx_timeout_resolveTwice in MOD_031.lean).
- Read, 'provides value': the value of the read token is not visible at token-count granularity; that the action receives it is CORE-032 AC3, not encoded here.
- Input token order (FIFO, CORE-030 AC2) and output token timestamps (CORE-035 AC2, IO-014 AC5) are below token-count granularity and not encoded here.
- AC1 (each arc type behaves exactly as described in the table) is the whole statement: one line per cell of the 'Requires token?' column (lines 1 to 4) and of the 'Consumes?' and 'Effect' columns (lines 5 to 7 and the outcome line), as laid out in the assumptions above.
- AC2 (an action that writes two tokens into one place of the branch it satisfies fires, and the marking receives all of them) is CORE_036_allows_multi: CORE-036 holds of a firing relation in which t: a → and(b, c) fires with the write b, b, c, and that firing leaves 2 tokens in b and 1 in c. That such a write is deposited at all is IO-015 and IO-016 AC4; CORE-036 only has to allow it.
- AC3 (two firings that deposit the same number of tokens in every place, in different orders, deposit the same outcome) is core036_c8_perPlace and core036_perPlace_closed, and concretely CORE_036_allows_multi: the write c, b, b of the same transition is allowed alike and leaves the same marking.
- InputArc names the first input arc on a place (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a transition with two input arcs on one place at build, so for every well-formed transition it is the only one.

**Evidence**

Without the `Builds t` premise line 4 would demand a firing of an enabled definition the build rejects, which the eleventh sentence says never fires, and would reject this relation.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_037"></a>
## CORE-037: Dead Arc Warning

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_037` · Kind **F** · Scope the dead-arc report of every executor backend and of the SMT verifier; the events and report lines are the second block of this ID · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ebc7c7b7ff9bccba ai** · Statement hash `ebc7c7b7ff9bccba`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The dead-arc report *shall* contain a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition of the net exactly when no transition has an input arc on the arc's place, no transition's output spec names that place anywhere in its tree (every `And` and `Xor` branch, the `Timeout` child and the `ForwardInput` target included), the place is not an environment place and the initial marking holds no token on it, and *shall* contain nothing else.<br><br>The dead-arc report *shall* list each dead arc once, as its own entry (two dead arcs on one place are two entries), in the order the net holds its transitions (the order they were added to the builder) and, within a transition, its read arcs, then its inhibitor arcs, then its reset arcs, each kind in the order the transition declares those arcs.<br><br>The warning text of a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition *shall* be `&lt;kind> arc of '&lt;transition>' on '&lt;place>': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; &lt;effect>.` with `&lt;kind>` the arc's kind (`read`, `inhibitor` or `reset`), `&lt;transition>` the name of the transition that declares the arc, `&lt;place>` the name of its place, and `&lt;effect>` `the transition can never be enabled` for a read arc, `the arc never blocks` for an inhibitor arc and `the arc has no effect` for a reset arc. | 1. For every dead-arc report Rep and warning text Msg on nets whose places are their names:<br>2. for every net X, environment places env and initial marking m0, an entry is in Rep X env m0 exactly when some transition t of X carries the entry's transition name and has an arc of the entry's kind on the entry's place, and that place is dead: no transition of X has an input arc on it or names it anywhere in its output spec (outPlaces: both children of an And, both branches of an Xor, the Timeout child, the target of a ForwardInput), env does not hold it and m0 puts no token on it;<br>3. Rep X env m0 is the list of every read, inhibitor and reset arc of X in report order (deadArcCandidates: the transitions in the order X holds them, within a transition its read, then inhibitor, then reset arcs, each kind in the transition's own order), keeping exactly the entries Rep X env m0 holds, each as often as X lists it;<br>4. the warning text of a read arc entry (t, p) is the template with kind `read`, the transition name t, the place name p and effect `the transition can never be enabled`;<br>5. the warning text of an inhibitor arc entry is the template with kind `inhibitor` and effect `the arc never blocks`;<br>6. the warning text of a reset arc entry is the template with kind `reset` and effect `the arc has no effect`. | <pre>fun Rep Msg ↦<br>  (∀ (X : Reference.Net String) (env : String → Bool) (m0 : String → ℕ)<br>      (a : DeadArc String),<br>      a ∈ Rep X env m0 ↔<br>        ∃ t ∈ X.transitions,<br>          a.transition = t.core.name ∧<br>            (a.kind = DeadArcKind.read ∧ ReadArc t a.place ∨<br>                a.kind = DeadArcKind.inhibitor ∧ InhibitorArc t a.place ∨<br>                  a.kind = DeadArcKind.reset ∧ ResetArc t a.place) ∧<br>              DeadPlace X env m0 a.place) ∧<br>    (∀ (X : Reference.Net String) (env : String → Bool) (m0 : String → ℕ),<br>        Rep X env m0 =<br>          List.filter (fun a ↦ decide (a ∈ Rep X env m0)) (deadArcCandidates X)) ∧<br>      (∀ (t p : String),<br>          Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.read, transition := t, place := p } =<br>            "read arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>              "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the transition can never be enabled.") ∧<br>        (∀ (t p : String),<br>            Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.inhibitor, transition := t, place := p } =<br>              "inhibitor arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>                "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the arc never blocks.") ∧<br>          ∀ (t p : String),<br>            Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.reset, transition := t, place := p } =<br>              "reset arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>                "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the arc has no effect."</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a pair: a dead-arc report Rep from a net (Reference.Net String: its transitions, in order), its environment places (a predicate on places) and its initial marking (token counts) to a list of entries (kind, name of the declaring transition, place), and a warning text Msg of one entry. The environment places and the initial marking are parameters, as in all three runtimes (`dead_arcs` in the dead_arcs module of the Rust core crate, `findDeadArcs` in typescript/src/core/internal/dead-arcs.ts, `ArcDiagnostics.deadArcs` in Java): an executor passes the environment places registered for the run and the initial marking it was given, the verifier its own initial marking and environment places ([VER-001]). 'Starts empty' and 'the initial marking holds no token' are m0 p = 0.
- Places and transitions are identified by name (ruling D10), so a place of the model is its name and `<place>` in the text is that string, written as is. A text that prints some other rendering of the place, such as a Java Place record, is killed (CORE_037_forbids_recordMsg). Java tests whether a place is fed on its Place record (name and token type, the divergence MOD-024 records), Rust and TypeScript on its name; a net with two same-named places of different token types is that divergence and is not encoded. Lines 1 and 2 hold of refDeadArcs at every place type (core037_line1_ref, core037_line2_ref).
- Transition order is the order of the net's transition list. That this list is the order in which the transitions were added to the builder is CORE-040's line under ruling D32 (wave W2, RefNetBuild); the W2 integrator may then add a [CORE-040] link to the second sentence. Within one kind the order is the transition's own arc list (NTransition.reads, inhibitors, resets), which is the order the transition declares the arcs in all three runtimes. A transition that lists one place twice under one arc kind declares two arcs, and line 2 lists both, which is the sentence's 'each dead arc once, as its own entry'; whether a builder accepts such a transition is not this block's subject.
- The text lines fix Msg on every read, inhibitor and reset arc entry, dead or not, as the third sentence says: the text is a pure template of the entry, and an implementation uses it only for the entries of the report.
- The output-spec clause of line 1 is outPlaces: the place of a Place node, both children of an And, both branches of an Xor, the child of a Timeout and the target of a ForwardInput. The source of a ForwardInput is not named by the output spec; IO-014 requires it to be an input place of the transition, so the input-arc clause covers it.
- The section's definition is its bullets (ruling D20, clash core-b#1): the lead-in ends at 'is dead when:', because 'nothing can ever put a token on P' is not equivalent: a place with an input arc but no producer, no initial token and no injection also stays empty for the whole run, yet its read arc is not dead, so the report holds nothing for it (core037_gap_nonvacuous). The sentence 'No firing ever puts a token on such a place, …' is a consequence on the reference firing semantics: a dead place is empty in every reachable marking (core037_dead_stays_empty), so a dead read arc's transition is never enabled (core037_deadRead_never_enabled), a dead inhibitor never blocks (core037_deadInhibitor_never_blocks) and a dead reset clears nothing (core037_deadReset_clears_nothing). Reach has no injection step: an environment place is not dead by line 1, and the sentence's 'a host injects tokens only into environment places' is ENV-001's; that the Rust and Python executors accept an injection into a place that is not registered, under a host assumption (ruling D89, clash env-a), is the environment requirements' subject, not this block's.
- The executor bullet (one log-message event per dead arc when the executor is constructed, through the CORE-072 AC4 mechanism: logger `libpetri.runtime`, level `WARN`, the declaring transition's name, emitted only where events are recorded and never changing execution) and the verifier bullet (one report line per dead arc, the warning text prefixed with `WARNING: `, no result field and no verdict depending on it) are SHOULD sentences over the event model and the verifier pipeline. They are the second part of this ID, kind B, in CORE_037_B.lean: CORE_037_events over the executor event model of Reference/Events.lean, and CORE_037_verifier over an environment-aware verifier (EnvDecider, VER-006); they are not encoded here. Their text 'One message per dead arc, not per place: two dead arcs on one place are two messages.' and 'Arcs are reported in transition order and, within a transition, read, inhibitor, then reset.' is lines 1 and 2 of this block: a report with one entry per place loses an entry line 1 requires (CORE_037_forbids_perPlace), a report in kind order across transitions breaks line 2 (CORE_037_forbids_kindMajor), and so do a report with the kinds in another order within a transition (CORE_037_forbids_resetFirst) and a report with one kind's arcs in reverse order (CORE_037_forbids_reverseWithinKind).
- AC1 (a reset arc on a place no transition consumes from or produces into, not an environment place and empty in the initial marking, gives exactly one warning naming the transition and the place) is line 1 and the reset text; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks the test derivation's net (`hub_kill` resets `answer/IN`) and the message bytes of AC1's example; a report that counts a reset arc as consuming its place drops AC1's arc (CORE_037_forbids_resetConsumes), and a text with another reset effect (CORE_037_forbids_resetMsg) or with the transition and the place swapped (CORE_037_forbids_swapNames) is killed. That the warning is one WARN log-message event and one `WARNING:` report line is CORE_037_events and CORE_037_verifier.
- AC2 (the same for a read arc and an inhibitor arc, with their effects) is line 1 and the read and inhibitor texts, checked by CORE_037_nonvacuous; a text that swaps the read and inhibitor effects is killed (CORE_037_forbids_swapMsg).
- AC3 (no warning when the initial marking puts a token on the place, when it is an environment place, when any transition has an input arc on it, or when any transition's output spec contains it in any branch) is line 1, the clauses of DeadPlace; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks a seeded place, an environment place, a consumed place and a place only a Timeout child inside an Xor names, and core037_outSpec_nonvacuous a place only an And child names and a place only a ForwardInput target names. Reports that ignore the initial marking (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreInit), ignore the environment places (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreEnv), count producers only (CORE_037_forbids_producersOnly), read only a top-level output place (CORE_037_forbids_topOnly), skip the Timeout child (CORE_037_forbids_noTimeout) or skip the ForwardInput target (CORE_037_forbids_noForward) are killed.
- AC4 (the warning never rejects a net and never changes execution, a verdict or a result field): the report is a total function with no failure value, and no line of this block constrains a builder, a firing or a verdict; that a dead arc never makes a builder reject is CORE-040's (W2), and that execution, verdicts and result fields do not depend on the warning is CORE_037_events (lines 4 and 5) and CORE_037_verifier (line 2).
- The SHOULD priority applies to the requirement: an implementation that reports dead arcs follows the three shall sentences.
- The test derivation (a transition `kill` that resets `x`, nothing else touching `x`, one warning naming `kill` and `x` with an empty initial marking and none with `x` seeded; the same with a read and an inhibitor arc, and with `x` produced by another transition's Xor branch) is CORE_037_nonvacuous on the reference report: `kill` with a read, an inhibitor and a reset arc on untouched places, a seeded place, and a place only an Xor branch of `use` names. The event, the report line and their counts are the B block's.

## CORE-037: Dead Arc Warning: verifier report lines

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_037_verifier` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier, all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind a verifier that reports dead arcs) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 16c48ca3f59b7e86 ai** · Statement hash `16c48ca3f59b7e86`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *Where* the SMT verifier reports dead arcs, the lines of a verification's report that are `WARNING: ` followed by the warning text of an arc of the net (its dead-arc lines) *shall* be, in report order, one line per entry of the dead-arc report for the net as the caller passed it, the verification's initial marking and its environment places, each `WARNING: ` followed by the warning text of that arc.<br><br>*Where* the SMT verifier reports dead arcs, its report with the dead-arc lines and the blank line after them left out *shall* be the report of the same verifier that does not report dead arcs, and every other field of its result except the elapsed time *shall* be as it is in that verifier. | 1. For every pair of environment-aware verifiers D (the verifier that reports dead arcs) and D0 (the same verifier that does not report dead arcs), on nets whose places are their names, and for every environment mode, environment places envs, options o, net X, property φ and initial marking m0:<br>2. the notes of D's result that are dead-arc lines (WARNING: followed by refDeadArcMsg of a read, inhibitor or reset arc of X's net) are exactly, in order, one line per entry a of refDeadArcs for X's net as the caller passed it, envs and the counts of m0, the line being WARNING: followed by refDeadArcMsg a;<br>3. D's result with the dead-arc lines left out of its notes (core037bStrip) is D0's result: the same verdict, route, trace, counterexampleConfirmed, counterexampleTiming, invariants and other notes. | <pre>fun D D0 ↦<br>  ∀ (mode : EnvMode) (envs : List String) (o : Verifier.Options) (X : TimedNet String)<br>    (φ : VerProp String) (m0 : Novel.Seam.NMarking String),<br>    List.filter (core037bDeadLine X.net) (D mode envs o X φ m0).notes =<br>        core037bLines X.net envs m0 ∧<br>      core037bStrip X.net (D mode envs o X φ m0) = D0 mode envs o X φ m0</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a pair of environment-aware verifiers (D, D0 : EnvDecider String, the verifier entry point of VER-006: the environment mode, the registered environment places, the options, the user's net, the property and the initial marking to a Result). The report is the result's notes (Result.notes, one note per non-blank line of the report). All three verifiers write a blank line after the dead-arc lines when there is one (SmtVerifier.java 1599-1601, smt-verifier.ts 1322, smt_verifier.rs finish), which is why the second quoted sentence leaves that blank line out with them; the model has no blank notes. The order of the dead-arc lines among the other notes and the line breaks are report wording (kind Q): Rust puts them after the total budget, Arrivals and reaping lines (smt_verifier.rs finish), Java and TypeScript after the reaping and in-flight lines (SmtVerifier.java 1589-1601, smt-verifier.ts 1316-1322). Line 1 fixes the dead-arc lines among themselves only.
- The model's Result holds the verdict, the route, the counterexample's transition labels, counterexampleConfirmed, counterexampleTiming, the P-invariants and the notes (Verifier/Result.lean). The runtime fields it leaves out (Rust counterexample_trace, the sequence of markings, discovered_invariants and statistics of VerificationResult, and their Java and TypeScript counterparts) are bound by the second quoted sentence and checked by no line. The elapsed time (Rust elapsed_ms) is wall-clock time that differs between any two runs, so the sentence excepts it and the model has no such field.
- The report is judged on the net as the caller passed it, before every rewrite of the verified-net function (the Arrivals closure of VER-006, the inert places of VER-001, the in-flight split of VER-004, the terminal rewrite of EXEC-042), whose arcs are the verifier's own: Rust computes the lines first in verify (smt_verifier.rs 772-776), Java and TypeScript on callerNet. 'Its environment places' are the places registered for the verification, envs; under Arrivals all three count them as environment places although the closure clears them (Rust before the closure, Java and TypeScript by adding the arrival places back). 'The verification's initial marking' is m0, the marking passed in, read as counts (NMarking.count; a place starts empty when its count is 0). The statement reads CORE-037's reference report and text, which the F block fixes (CORE_037_unique, core037b_msg_unique).
- Line 1 recognises a dead-arc line by its text alone, so it kills a verifier that writes no line (CORE_037_verifier_forbids_silent), one that leaves out the WARNING: prefix (CORE_037_verifier_forbids_noPrefix) and one that warns about every read, inhibitor and reset arc, dead or not (CORE_037_verifier_forbids_everyArc). Line 2 is 'No result field changes and no verdict depends on it.' and AC4's verifier half: a verifier whose verdict changes when it reports a dead arc breaks it (CORE_037_verifier_forbids_verdict).
- Line 2 compares D with D0, and the block alone does not say which verifier D0 is: taken alone it holds of any D once D0 is chosen as D with its dead-arc lines left out. The forbids evidence of line 2 fixes D0 = refEnvVerify, and so does the reference pair, whose D0 notes hold no dead-arc line (core037b_refEnvVerify_clean). The consistency theorem spec_consistent_all (ConsistencyAll) joins this block with the verifier blocks: there D0 is the shared verifier, of which the verifier blocks are stated, and D is a wrapper of it (the witness is core037bVerify of the shared verifier), so AC4's 'never changes a verdict or a result field' holds of a D0 that meets those blocks. Every result field but the notes is D0's, so a line of another verifier block that reads only those fields holds of D when it holds of D0, and a line that asks for a note in the notes (VER-006's vacuity note) too.
- AC1 and AC2, verifier half (one WARNING: line per dead reset, read or inhibitor arc, with its effect) are line 1 with CORE-037's text lines: CORE_037_verifier_nonvacuous shows the three lines of the test derivation's net, byte for byte, and that seeding the reset arc's place drops its line. AC3 (no line for a seeded place, an environment place, a consumed place or a place an output spec names) is line 1 through refDeadArcs, as in the F block. AC4, verifier half (never changes a verdict or a result field) is line 2. That verification never fails on a dead arc is an offer clause: the model's verifier (EnvDecider) is a total function, so no line can say it, and it belongs in a coverage theorem (an open item). The executor halves of AC1 to AC4 are the block CORE_037_events.
- The test derivation's verifier half (verify any property of the same net and assert the report line) is CORE_037_verifier_nonvacuous, with a PlaceBound property under Ignore. Python runs the Rust verifier and inherits its report.
