## CORE-040: Net Builder

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_040` · Kind **F** · Scope all net builders used without composition or fusion sets · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f3285a7fcfead14f ai** · Statement hash `f3285a7fcfead14f`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The sentences below concern a net builder used without composition ([MOD-020], [MOD-025], [MOD-027]) and without fusion sets ([MOD-060], [MOD-061]), which rewrite arcs, drop places or reject at build under their own requirements.<br><br>*When* a net is built from transitions, each added once, whose names are pairwise distinct ([TIME-010]), the net *shall* hold exactly the added transitions, in the order they were added, which is the declaration order of its transitions.<br><br>*When* a net is built, every declared place, every declared terminal place ([EXEC-042]), every place that an input, inhibitor, read or reset arc of an added transition names and every place in the `allPlaces` set of the output specification of an added transition ([IO-017]) *shall* be a place of the net.<br><br>*When* a net is built, the net *shall not* hold any other place, and *shall not* hold a place twice ([CORE-002]).<br><br>Building a net that declares no terminal place ([EXEC-042]) *shall* succeed.<br><br>Which nets that declare terminal places build, and which terminal places a built net holds, are stated by [EXEC-042]. | 1. For every transition builder B and every net builder NB over B's instances:<br>2. if NB returns the net b for the input inp and the added transitions of inp have pairwise distinct names, the transitions of b are the definitions of the added transitions, in the order added;<br>3. if NB returns b for inp, every declared place of inp, every declared terminal place of inp and every place an added transition has an arc on (an arc place: input, read, inhibitor or reset) or holds in the allPlaces set of its output specification (an output arc, IO-017) is a place of b;<br>4. if NB returns b for inp, every place of b is a declared place, a declared terminal place or a place an added transition has an arc on or holds in the allPlaces set of its output specification, and no place of b appears twice;<br>5. for every input inp that declares no terminal place, NB returns a net. | <pre>fun {N A} [DecidableEq N] B NB ↦<br>  (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>      NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>        (List.map (fun x ↦ (B.defOf x).core.name) inp.trans).Nodup →<br>          b.trans = List.map B.defOf inp.trans) ∧<br>    (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>          ∀ (p : N),<br>            (p ∈ inp.places ∨<br>                p ∈ inp.terminals ∨<br>                  ∃ x ∈ inp.trans,<br>                    ArcPlace (B.defOf x).toTrans p ∨ OutputArc (B.defOf x).toTrans p) →<br>              p ∈ b.places) ∧<br>      (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>          NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>            (∀ p ∈ b.places,<br>                p ∈ inp.places ∨<br>                  p ∈ inp.terminals ∨<br>                    ∃ x ∈ inp.trans,<br>                      ArcPlace (B.defOf x).toTrans p ∨ OutputArc (B.defOf x).toTrans p) ∧<br>              b.places.Nodup) ∧<br>        ∀ (inp : NetIn B), inp.terminals = [] → ∃ b, NB inp = Except.ok b</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A net builder (NetBuilder B) is the build call of one implementation's net builder, read as a function from what the host added (NetIn B: the declared places in the order declared, the added transitions in the order added, as instances of the transition builder B, and the declared terminal places) to a built net (BuiltNet: its places, its transitions' definitions, its terminal places) or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception, read as `.error msg`). A net holds only what a transition builder returned (BuiltNet.FromBuilder; the W2 tracer decision), so the added transitions are instances of B, not bare definitions. Places are the abstract place type N, identity = equality on N; how a host place object maps to N (by name in TypeScript, Rust and Python, by name and token type in Java) is CORE-002's (PlaceKeyed).
- Scope. The block concerns a builder used without composition (MOD-020 instance composition, MOD-025 direct composition, and MOD-027's rejection of an arc on a port place that instance composition bound) and without fusion sets (MOD-060, MOD-061), as its first quoted sentence says. Fusion rewrites the arcs of every transition (rewriter::apply_fusion, called from build_with_fusion in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), which breaks line 1, and removes non-canonical members from the place set (build_with_fusion, its step 4), which breaks line 2; build panics or throws on fusion overlap (build_with_fusion) and on an arc naming a port place that instance composition bound (MOD-027, reject_bound_port_references) with no terminal place declared, which breaks line 4 (Java: java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java, Builder.build, which throws from buildWithFusion and rejectRetired). What a composed or fused net holds is the composition model's (W8), stated over the same net builder extended. Rust's second public constructor PetriNet::map_transitions (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs) is not a net builder: its documented, unchecked precondition is that the mapping introduces no place the net does not already declare, so a net it returns meets line 2 only when the caller keeps that precondition.
- Line 1 is the declaration order of ruling D32 (a): the order the transitions were added is the net's transition order, which EXEC-002 (FIFO among equal priorities) and CORE-037 (the order of the dead-arc report) read. Its premise is the shared unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23 (a) (spec/03-timing.md, TIME-010: the transitions of one net have pairwise distinct names), on the added transitions, read over the list of additions (the quoted 'each added once'), so one transition instance added twice has its name twice and is outside the premise; no builder checks it. Outside it the runtimes differ: given one transition instance twice, Java and TypeScript hold it once (a set) and Rust twice (a Vec, a clone keeps its identity) (clash core-b#5, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:30, rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:32). A builder that reverses the transitions (core040_reverseNB) violates line 1 and meets the order-free reading (CORE_040_mutant_orderFree).
- Line 2 is AC3 made a MUST by ruling D32 (a): the places of every arc of all five kinds are collected, the arc places of the glossary (input, read, inhibitor, reset; ArcPlace in Spec/GlossaryTime.lean) and every place of the output specification (OutputArc; IO-017's AllPlaces, so the target of a ForwardInput and every place of a Timeout child count). All three runtimes do so (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:319-339, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:320-328, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:218-237). A declared terminal place is declared as a place too in all three (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:301-308, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:362-367, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:206-210). A builder that collects only input and output places (core040_inOutOnlyNB, the pre-D32 reading, CORE_040_mutant_inOutOnly) or drops a declared place no arc names (core040_dropDeclaredNB, CORE_040_mutant_arcPlacesOnly) violates line 2, and so does one that collects the source of a ForwardInput instead of its target and nothing from a Timeout child (core040_outSlipNB, CORE_040_forbids_outSlip: place 5 of the example is the target of a ForwardInput inside a Timeout). The quoted sentence collects the allPlaces set of IO-017, which holds a ForwardInput's target only; its source is collected all the same, as an input place: the transition builder rejects a forward from a place that is not an input of the transition (IO-014 AC3, Spec/Glossary.lean WellFormedOut), and the added transitions are its outputs. Line 2 is what discharges the hypothesis hDecl (Novel.Seam.ArcsDeclared) of the postfix soundness theorems for every builder that meets CORE-040 (core040_arcsDeclared), not only for the reference (refNetBuild_arcsDeclared_toNNetB).
- Line 3: the net holds no place other than those of line 2 and no place twice, both on N. Ruling D66 (a) keeps 'no place twice' a MUST, and every runtime meets it under its own identity (CORE-002): Rust and Java keep the places in a set under their place equality, and TypeScript, where place(name) returns a fresh object each call (typescript/src/core/place.ts), keeps the builder's places in a Map from name to place, so two place objects named 'A' give PetriNet.places one entry, the first object added (PetriNetBuilder._places and addPlace, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts), as the compiled net keys places by name (typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts). A builder that keeps two place objects of one name, as a place set keyed by object reference does (the behaviour RD-03 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of TypeScript's builder), holds a place twice under name identity (N := String) and violates line 3. A builder that keeps a place twice (core040_noDedupNB, CORE_040_mutant_dupsAllowed) or adds a place nobody declared or named (core040_extraNB, CORE_040_mutant_extraAllowed) violates line 3. The order of the places is not stated: ruling D32 orders transitions only, and the reference keeps the last occurrence of a place where the runtimes keep the first.
- Line 4: the net builder rejects nothing of its own. Its one rejection in scope is EXEC-042 AC5 (a declared terminal place that an added transition consumes from or reads, NetIn.TerminalClash); on an input with no terminal place it cannot arise. Over an input with terminal places, EXEC-042's build block (EXEC_042_build, kind F, over every abstract net builder, not over the reference only) says both directions: its line 1 rejects a clash, its line 2 builds every input without one, so a builder that also rejects a terminal place on an inhibitor or reset arc violates EXEC_042_build line 2 on exec042_netInh (as EXEC_042_build_mutant_rejectAll_killed shows for the builder that rejects every terminal place). EXEC_042_build's own scope note reads its line 2, with no terminal place declared, as this line 4. A transition definition the transition builder rejects never reaches the net builder: the added transitions are instances, and CORE-020 says which inputs build. Without line 4 a builder that rejects everything meets lines 1 to 3 vacuously; one that rejects an empty net (core040_rejectEmptyNB, CORE_040_mutant_noAccept) violates it. Only success and failure are stated, not a message.
- Terminal places of the built net (BuiltNet.terminals). None of CORE-040's four lines reads them; a declared terminal place enters the net as a place by line 2. That the built net's terminal places are exactly the declared ones is EXEC_042_build line 3, over every abstract net builder; a builder that drops them (exec042_dropTerminalsNB, the TypeScript EMPTY_TERMINALS choice at typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:734-745 made unconditionally) violates it (EXEC_042_build_forbids_dropTerminals). How often a terminal place is listed is stated nowhere: EXEC_042_build line 3 reads the terminal places as a set, all three runtimes keep each once (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:301-308, Java's LinkedHashSet, TypeScript's Map by name) and the reference keeps them once each in declaration order (refNetBuild_terminals); no requirement reads the multiplicity.
- AC1 (the builder can add places and transitions) is lines 1, 2 and 4 together: a declared place and an added transition are in the net, and building succeeds (CORE_040_nonvacuous). The builder pattern as an API shape is a Q-kind test (ruling D99 (a)).
- AC2 (build produces an immutable net) is CORE-041's subject: here a built net is a value (BuiltNet), and that a handle on it shows the same net after later builder calls is CORE-041's line over BuilderApi, whose builder trace (copyBuilder_trace) shows refNetBuild's net. A builder that hands out its live sets (aliasBuilder, the behaviour RD-02 recorded of TypeScript's builder) violates CORE-041's line (ruling D66 (a)); no runtime's built net shares its place or transition set with the builder.
- AC3 (places referenced by transitions are auto-collected) is line 2; its parenthesis ('implementations that auto-collect from arcs SHOULD do so') is replaced by the MUST of ruling D32 (a). The test derivation (build a net with transitions and verify all places from arcs are present) is line 2 on CORE_040_nonvacuous's example, whose transitions have arcs of all five kinds, with an output specification of every node kind but Xor: Place, And, Timeout and a ForwardInput inside the Timeout (a bare ForwardInput does not build, IO-014). The example's second transition has priority 5 and the first priority 0, so the order added (line 1) is not the priority order: a builder that sorts the transitions by priority (core040_prioSortNB, CORE_040_forbids_prioSort) violates line 1 on it.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_041"></a>
## CORE-041: Net Immutability

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041` · Kind **B** · Scope all net builders used without composition or fusion sets · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 b99651775fb321ff ai** · Statement hash `b99651775fb321ff`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| After construction, a Petri net definition is immutable.<br><br>The set of places, transitions, and their connections cannot be modified.<br><br>*When* the build call of a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes is made, the call *shall* give the net that [CORE-040] describes, or report the rejection that [EXEC-042] describes, for all the places, transitions and terminal places added to that builder before the call, including those added before an earlier build call.<br><br>*When* a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes has built a net and is used again, to add places, transitions or terminal places or to build again, the net it built *shall* keep the places, transitions and terminal places it had when it was built. | 1. For every transition builder B, every net builder NB over B's instances and every builder state machine BA:<br>2. for every history of uses of a new builder (calls and builds, in the order made), the handle the next build returns shows, right after that build, NB's result (a built net or a rejection) on every call of the history, in the order made (NetIn.ofOps of the calls; a build adds nothing and resets nothing);<br>3. for every history of uses of a new builder and every later history of uses, the handle the build after the first history returns shows after the later history what it showed right after that build. | <pre>fun {N A} [DecidableEq N] B NB BA ↦<br>  (∀ (pre : List (BUse B)),<br>      BA.view (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2 =<br>        NB (NetIn.ofOps (callsOf pre))) ∧<br>    ∀ (pre post : List (BUse B)),<br>      BA.view (runUses BA (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1 post)<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2 =<br>        BA.view (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A builder state machine (BuilderApi in Reference/Build.lean) is the net builder of one implementation: its calls declare a place, add a built transition or declare a terminal place (BOp), build returns a handle on the built net, and view is what a handle shows (a built net, or the rejection the build reported: a Java exception or a Rust panic is read as a handle that shows the rejection). The net builder NB is the function CORE-040 is stated over. On its own, line 0 pins the handle relative to NB only: the blind builder, whose handle always shows the empty net, meets CORE-041 against the net builder that always returns the empty net (core041_blind_constEmpty). Read together with CORE-040 over the same NB, line 0 says that the handle shows CORE-040's built net (the builder trace, design note 3.8): every NB that meets CORE-040 lines 2 and 4 puts a declared place into the net, and then the blind builder violates line 0 (core041_blind_killed_declared). The joint statement over one shared NB is the integrator's (Spec/ConsistencyStructure.lean).
- Line 0 is the first quoted shall sentence. Without it the block is satisfied by a builder whose handle always shows the empty net (design note S6: core041_blindBuilder satisfies line 1, CORE_041_mutant_stableOnly_killed). Line 0 equates the handle with NB's whole result, so the build rejects exactly when NB rejects; in scope that is the rejection of EXEC-042 AC5 (CORE-040 line 4: the net builder rejects nothing of its own). A history may hold earlier builds; a build adds nothing to what the builder holds and resets nothing, so a second build shows every call made so far, including those made before the first build, as Java, TypeScript and the Python binding do (the Python NetBuilder clones the accumulated builder, PyPetriNetBuilder build in rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs). A builder that empties itself at build meets line 0 on histories without an earlier build and line 1, and violates line 0 at its second build (core041_resetBuilder, CORE_041_mutant_firstBuild_killed). Rust consumes the builder (PetriNetBuilder::build in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), so in Rust no use follows a build and both lines speak of the first build only.
- Line 1 is the second quoted shall sentence and the body's two sentences ('After construction, a Petri net definition is immutable.' and 'The set of places, transitions, and their connections cannot be modified.'): a net's connections are the arcs of its transitions, which the built net carries in its transition definitions (TransDef), so a built net that keeps its places, transitions and terminal places keeps its connections. Later uses are calls and builds alike: a builder that keeps only the last built net, so that a later build changes the net an earlier handle shows, violates it (core041_slotBuilder, CORE_041_mutant_callsOnly_killed, the reading that allows later calls only).
- Ruling D66 (a): the MUST stands, and every runtime's built net keeps its own place and transition sets. Java copies the sets into unmodifiable ones (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:70-71), and TypeScript's build gives the net copies of the builder's place map and transition set (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts build, new Set(this._places.values()) and new Set(this._transitions)), so a place or transition added after build, or a channel composition that removes a caller transition, does not reach a net already built. A builder whose build passes its own live sets to the net (aliasBuilder, the behaviour RD-02 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of TypeScript's builder) shows a transition added after build in the built net and violates line 1 (CORE_041_forbids_alias, and CORE_041_mutant_traceOnly_killed: it meets line 0).
- Scope: a net built without fusion sets, instance composition or retired ports, as in CORE-040, which both quoted shall sentences name ('a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes'); those rewrite arcs and drop places, and belong to the composition model (W8). Nets derived from a built net (binding actions, CORE-042; composition) are new nets built through a builder, not changes to the built net, and are outside this block. What a handle shows is the net's places, transitions with their definitions and terminal places; the net's name and subnet membership are not modelled.
- AC1 (no mutation methods exist on the constructed net) and AC2 (collections returned by the net are unmodifiable or copies) are API shape, tested and not proven (kind Q): the model has no method that changes a built net, and a host that changed a returned collection would be changing the net, which line 1 forbids for the builder's own uses only. In TypeScript the returned sets are read-only by type only. The test derivation ('build a net; verify no mutation API exists') is AC1. As in CORE-040 (ruling D99 (a)), these API-shape criteria stay in the markdown unmarked.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): ✓ The reference builder state machine with the reference net builder satisfies CORE-041: `build` keeps `refNetBuild` of what was added (line 0, with `copyBuilder_view_built`) and later uses never change a kept net (line 1).
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (B : TBuilder N A),<br>  CORE_041 B refNetBuild (copyBuilder B)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_forbids_alias` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): ✗ The aliasing builder (the behaviour RD-02 recorded of TypeScript's builder) violates CORE-041 (line 1): build a new builder, then declare place 0, and the handle the build returned shows place 0.
  <pre>¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (aliasBuilder core041B)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_mutant_callsOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): The slot builder kills the calls-only reading: it shows the reference net builder's result right after a build (line 0) and later calls never change it, but building a new builder, declaring place 0 and building again changes what the first handle shows (line 1).
  <pre>CORE_041_mutant_callsOnly core041B refNetBuild (core041_slotBuilder core041B) ∧<br>  ¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (core041_slotBuilder core041B)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_mutant_firstBuild_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): The reset builder kills the first-build reading: right after a build from a history of calls it shows the reference net builder's result, and later uses never change a handle (line 1), but a new builder that declares place 0, builds and builds again shows the empty net at the second build, where line 0 asks for the net with place 0.
  <pre>CORE_041_mutant_firstBuild core041B refNetBuild (core041_resetBuilder core041B) ∧<br>  ¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (core041_resetBuilder core041B)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_mutant_stableOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): The blind builder kills the stability-only reading: its handle never changes (line 1), but a new builder that declares place 0 and builds shows the empty net (line 0). The kill is relative to the net builder: here `NB` is the reference `refNetBuild`; `core041_blind_killed_declared` gives it for every `NB` that keeps a declared place, and `core041_blind_constEmpty` shows that it fails for the net builder that always returns the empty net.
  <pre>CORE_041_mutant_stableOnly core041B refNetBuild (core041_blindBuilder core041B) ∧<br>  ¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (core041_blindBuilder core041B)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_mutant_traceOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): The aliasing builder kills the trace-only reading: right after a build its handle shows the reference net builder's result on every call made (line 0), but a later call changes it.
  <pre>CORE_041_mutant_traceOnly core041B refNetBuild (aliasBuilder core041B) ∧<br>  ¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (aliasBuilder core041B)</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): ✓ Both lines of CORE-041 are exercised by the reference: a new builder that declares place 0 and builds shows the net with place 0 (line 0), and still shows it after place 1 is declared and the builder builds again, while that second build shows places 0 and 1 (line 1, and line 0 on a history with an earlier build).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_042"></a>
## CORE-042: Action Binding Separation

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042` · Kind **F** · Scope Java, TypeScript, Rust (net-level bindActions, both forms); Python rides on the Rust binding and exposes no net-level binding · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 14c5416ef5b28912 ai** · Statement hash `14c5416ef5b28912`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The net's static structure (places, transitions, arcs, timing, priority) MUST be separable from the runtime behavior (actions).<br><br>A `bindActions()` operation takes a structure and a mapping of transition names to actions, producing a new net with actions bound.<br><br>*When* actions are bound to a net, in either form, the new net *shall* have the name, the places and the terminal places of the original net and, for each transition of the original net, in the same order, a transition with the same name, arcs, output specification, timing and priority.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a resolver that returns an action for a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry that action in the new net.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a resolver that returns no action (`null`/`None`) for a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry in the new net the action it carried before.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a mapping that maps a transition's name to an action, the transition *shall* carry that action in the new net.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a mapping whose values are actions and that does not map a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry in the new net either the passthrough action or the action it carried before, and an implementation makes the same one of these two choices for every transition, every net and every mapping, so a transition that carried passthrough still carries passthrough.<br><br>Binding actions to a net *shall* return a new net for every net and every resolver or mapping, and *shall* leave the original net unchanged.<br><br>Binding is lazy and total: it never rejects, so a partially bound net is a legitimate intermediate value and an action MAY be bound after instantiation ([MOD-031] AC7); the declared structure is reconciled against the bound behaviour at compile time ([CORE-043]).<br><br>**Divergence:** the map form substitutes passthrough for every transition the map omits in Java and TypeScript (so a second call clobbers the first's bindings) but leaves them untouched in Rust; only the resolver form, where a `null`/`None` result defers a transition, binds in stages identically across implementations.<br><br>In Java a mapping may hold a name with a `null` value, and the map form then defers that transition as the resolver form does; TypeScript substitutes passthrough for a `null` or `undefined` value. | 1. For every resolver-form binding Bind and map-form binding BindMap:<br>2. for every built net b and every resolver r, the net Bind b r and the net BindMap b r each have b's places and b's terminal places, and their transition lists match b's position by position (same length, same order), each transition with b's name and arcs (core), output specification, timing and priority;<br>3. for every b and r, the transition at each position of Bind b r carries the action a whenever r answers that position's name in b with a;<br>4. for every b and r, the transition at each position of Bind b r carries the action b's transition there carried whenever r answers that name with none (defers it);<br>5. for every b and every map m, the transition at each position of BindMap b m carries the action a whenever m maps that position's name in b to a;<br>6. either, for every b and m, the transition at each position of BindMap b m carries passthrough whenever m does not map that name, or, for every b and m, it carries the action b's transition there carried whenever m does not map that name. | <pre>fun {N A} Bind BindMap ↦<br>  (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br>      ∀ f ∈ **Assumptions**

- A binding is a function from a built net (BuiltNet: places, transition definitions in declaration order, terminal places; Reference/Build.lean) and a resolver or map to a built net. A resolver and a map are both read as a function from names to an optional action: the resolver's null/None and a name the map does not hold are none. An action is read as its identity tag (Act: the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id); what an action does is CORE-050's and the action model's (W3).
- The lines range over mappings whose values are actions (the body's 'a mapping of transition names to actions', and the quoted line 5 sentence's 'a mapping whose values are actions'). A mapping that holds a name with a null value, which Java's map allows, is outside them and outside every quoted shall sentence: the quoted Java sentence records what the runtimes do with it (Java defers that transition, since getOrDefault returns the held null and the resolver form keeps a transition whose resolver gives null, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:202 and :219; TypeScript substitutes passthrough, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:80-82; a Rust map holds only actions). Read as none, such a mapping would make Java's map form keep some omitted transitions and clobber others within one call, which line 5 forbids; the line 5 sentence names mappings whose values are actions so that it does not.
- The sentence that binding returns a new net for every net and every resolver or mapping and leaves the original net unchanged is not a line: it holds of every binding in the model, where a binding is a function on immutable values, so it returns a net for every net and every resolver or map and cannot change its argument b; in the runtimes it is tested directly. 'Total, it never rejects' is its first half: it includes a resolver or map that leaves some transitions with passthrough or answers a name that is no transition (that name is never asked for, so it is ignored). 'Lazy' is read as: binding checks nothing, neither comparing a bound action with the transition's output specification nor requiring every transition to be bound, so a partially bound net is a legitimate value, and reconciling it with the declared output specifications is the compile-time check of CORE-043. Binding after instantiation (MOD-031 AC7) and per-instance binding, including an override key that names no transition (ruling D87), are MOD-030's and MOD-031's (W8).
- The lines are stated per position, not per name, so they do not need the shared unique-names assumption (NetNamesDistinct, rulings D10 and D23): with two transitions of one name every runtime asks the resolver once per transition and binds both (Java PetriNet.bindActions(Function) in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java, TypeScript bindActionsWithResolver in typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts, Rust bind_actions_with_resolver in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), and so does the statement. Under that assumption binding by position is binding by name.
- Line 1 is the body's first sentence: binding changes no field of the static structure. It names the terminal places (EXEC-042) and the output specification, which the body's list '(places, transitions, arcs, timing, priority)' does not: both are static structure and all three runtimes keep them (the same three methods: Java's and TypeScript's construct the new PetriNet from the net's name, places and terminals, and Rust's goes through PetriNet::map_transitions, which clones them). The quoted sentence asks for a transition with the same fields, not the same transition: all three runtimes rebuild a rebound transition through the transition builder (Java and TypeScript rebuildWithAction; Rust rebuild_with_action in rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs, called from bind_actions_with_resolver, with a fresh TransitionId), so the identity of a rebound transition (CORE-021) is not kept, and the line compares the fields position by position. The net's name, which the quoted sentence also names, is not a field of BuiltNet; every runtime keeps it (the same three places) and a test checks it outside the model. The subnet membership metadata is kept as MOD-026 says (the mapping survives a re-bind unchanged) and the declared-to-actual place correspondence as MOD-031 says (the rebuild that swaps the action carries it forward); neither is modelled here. A binding that rebuilds a transition and drops its read arcs (CORE_042_forbids_dropReads) violates line 1, and so does one that keeps only what firing reads and resets the priority (CORE_042_mutant_firingView_killed).
- The sentence 'When actions are bound to a net, in either form, a transition that has a match specification ([NU-020]) shall have the same match specification in the new net.' is quoted and stated by the companion block CORE_042_nu in this file, over ν nets (NuBuiltNet: the places, the ν definitions NuDef of Reference/Nu.lean, each a TransDef and an optional match, and the terminal places). It is not a line here: the match specification is not a field of TransDef, so no binding on BuiltNet can drop it, and a binding that rebuilds an answered transition without its match has exactly refBind as its shadow on BuiltNet (core042_nuDropBind_shadow) and meets every line here; CORE_042_nu kills it (CORE_042_nu_mutant_deferredOnly_killed). NU-030 states the same for every rebuild through a place rewrite, the identity rewrite of action binding included: its line 3 says that the match of the rebuilt transition is the original one mapped by the rewrite (the original one itself under the identity), and that a transition without a match stays without one.
- Lines 2 and 3 are the resolver form, which all three runtimes share: an answered name gets the action, a null/None result defers the transition, which keeps its action. A binding that ignores the resolver (CORE_042_forbids_ignoreResolver) violates line 2, and so does one that binds only transitions still carrying passthrough (CORE_042_mutant_onlyUnbound_killed). A resolver form that replaces a deferred action by passthrough (the map form's Java reading applied to the resolver) violates line 3 (CORE_042_mutant_deferPassthrough_killed). The model reads a resolver that returns no action (null/None, and in TypeScript also undefined) as one that answers none. TypeScript treats null and undefined alike as no action (bindActionsWithResolver, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:97: action != null, and SubnetDef.bindActionsWithResolver in typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts), so a JavaScript resolver such as name => obj[name], for a name obj does not hold, defers the transition, which keeps its action. Java (null) and Rust (None) defer as line 3 says (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:219, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:196-200). A binding that treats only null as no action rebinds such a transition to undefined and breaks line 3 (the behaviour RD-05 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of TypeScript; the model has no undefined, so this is test evidence: typescript/tests/core/petri-net.test.ts 'bindActionsWithResolver defers a transition when the resolver returns undefined (CORE-042)').
- Lines 4 and 5 are the map form's common part (ruling D20 (a) on clash core-b#4: the common part, and the divergence recorded). Rust keeps an omitted transition's action (mapKeep, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:177-183) and Java and TypeScript substitute passthrough (mapClobber, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:202, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:80-82); both readings satisfy the block (CORE_042_reference_keep, CORE_042_reference_clobber) and they differ on a net whose omitted transition carries another action (CORE_042_mapForms_undecided). Line 5 asks for one reading per map form, as each runtime has: every omitted transition of every net carries passthrough, or every one keeps its action. A map form that keeps some omitted transitions and clobbers others meets the per-transition reading and violates line 5 (CORE_042_mutant_perTransition_killed). A map form that ignores the map (CORE_042_forbids_ignoreMap) violates line 4, and so does one whose map binds only transitions still carrying passthrough (CORE_042_mutant_mapOnlyUnbound_killed). Line 5 is stronger than AC4 alone: a map form that resets an omitted transition's action to a fixed other action meets AC4 and violates line 5 (CORE_042_mutant_ac4Only_killed).
- AC1 (a net can be created with no actions, all transitions using passthrough) is the builder default: a transition built without an action carries passthrough (TransIn.resolve, resolve_action_none in Reference/Build.lean), which is CORE-051's line (W3) and is not restated here; CORE_042_nonvacuous starts from such a net.
- AC2 (bindActions(mapping) produces a new net with actions bound by transition name) is line 4 with line 1.
- AC3 (the original net is not modified) is the second half of the quoted sentence that binding leaves the original net unchanged, which holds of every binding in the model (above) and is not a line.
- AC4 (unbound transitions retain the passthrough action) is line 5 on a transition that carried passthrough, and line 3 for the resolver form. The test derivation (bind 2 of 3 transitions, the third still has passthrough) is CORE_042_nonvacuous, for the resolver form and both map readings.
- The paragraph on SubnetDef.bindActions (the same argument forms, keyed by unprefixed names, a new definition) is the operation on a subnet definition, MOD-051's paragraph 'Binding actions on a definition' with its AC8, and is quoted there (W11). The Python binding exposes binding on instances and subnet definitions only (the bind_actions methods of PyInstance and PySubnetDef in rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs), not on a net; it rides on the Rust binding.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_042_nu"></a>
## CORE-042: Action Binding Separation: the match specification

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_nu` · Kind **F** · Scope Java, TypeScript, Rust (net-level bindActions, both forms, on a net whose transitions may have a match specification); Python rides on the Rust binding · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 3f906fdfcf23b4d9 ai** · Statement hash `3f906fdfcf23b4d9`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* actions are bound to a net, in either form, a transition that has a match specification ([NU-020]) *shall* have the same match specification in the new net. | 1. For every resolver-form binding Bind and map-form binding BindMap on ν nets (built nets whose transition definitions may carry a match specification):<br>2. for every ν net b and every resolver or map r, the transition lists of Bind b r and of BindMap b r match b's position by position, and at each position where b's transition has a match specification ms, the transition of the new net has ms. | <pre>fun {N A K} Bind BindMap ↦<br>  ∀ (b : NuBuiltNet N A K) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br>    ∀ f ∈ [Bind, BindMap],<br>      List.Forall₂<br>        (fun d' d ↦ ∀ (ms : MatchSpec N K), d.mspec = some ms → d'.mspec = some ms)<br>        (f b r).trans b.trans</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A ν net (NuBuiltNet) is a built net (BuiltNet, Reference/Build.lean) whose transition definitions are ν definitions (NuDef, Reference/Nu.lean: a TransDef and an optional match specification). A binding in either form is a function from a ν net and a resolver or map, both read as a function from names to an optional action, to a ν net, as in CORE_042. What binding does to the places, the terminal places and the TransDef part of each transition (its name, arcs, output specification, timing, priority and action) is CORE_042's lines, on the shadow of the ν net (NuBuiltNet.shadow: the match dropped); the reference binding here shadows refBind (core042RefNuBind_shadow). This block adds only the match.
- 'The transition in the new net' is read position by position, as CORE_042 line 1 reads it: the line asks that the transition lists match position by position, which line 1 already asks of the shadow, and compares the match at each position, so it needs no unique-names assumption.
- The sentence speaks of a transition that has a match specification and the line states no more: a transition without one is not constrained here. That it stays without one is NU-030's line 3 under the identity rewrite of action binding (NU-030 names action binding among its rebuilds): that line maps the optional match, so no match stays no match, and with the identity rewrite it also gives the rebuilt transitions of this line. All three runtimes copy the match only when there is one, so a transition without one stays without one.
- All three runtimes keep the match in both forms: a deferred transition is kept as it is (the resolver forms: Rust bind_actions_with_resolver in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs, Java PetriNet.bindActions(Function) in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java, TypeScript bindActionsWithResolver in typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts), and a rebound one is rebuilt with its match carried forward (Rust rebuild_with_action in rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs, Java and TypeScript rebuildWithAction in the same two files), which the runtimes warn would otherwise turn a join correlated by name into a plain join; the map form goes through the resolver form in all three. Pinned by the tests bind_actions_preserves_match_spec in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs and bindActions_preservesMatchSpec in java/src/test/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNetTest.java. Python rides on the Rust binding.
- A binding that rebuilds an answered transition from the fields CORE_042 line 1 lists and drops its match, keeping a deferred transition as it was (the regression the runtime tests pin), has refBind as its shadow (core042_nuDropBind_shadow), so it meets every line of CORE_042, and it violates this line (CORE_042_nu_mutant_deferredOnly_killed). The same binding meets the reading that keeps the match only of a transition the binding leaves deferred, which is the mutant that theorem kills.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_nu_reference_clobber` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✓ The reference binding on ν nets satisfies CORE-042's match sentence with the map read as Java and TypeScript read it.
  <pre>∀ {N A K : Type}, CORE_042_nu core042RefNuBind core042RefNuBindMapClobber</pre>
- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_nu_reference_keep` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✓ The reference binding on ν nets satisfies CORE-042's match sentence with the map read as Rust reads it.
  <pre>∀ {N A K : Type}, CORE_042_nu core042RefNuBind core042RefNuBindMapKeep</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_nu_mutant_deferredOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): The match-dropping binding kills the mutant: it keeps every deferred transition as it was, so it meets the deferred-only reading, but binding the example's matched join `j` with action 1 leaves `j` without its match (the line).
  <pre>CORE_042_nu_mutant_deferredOnly core042NuDropBind core042RefNuBindMapKeep ∧<br>  ¬CORE_042_nu core042NuDropBind core042RefNuBindMapKeep</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_nu_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✓ The match sentence is exercised by the reference: binding the example's matched join `j` with action 1 gives `j` the action and keeps its match, the deferred `t` keeps passthrough and stays without a match, in the resolver form and in both map readings; the match-dropping binding gives `j` the same action and loses its match, while its shadow is the reference binding's.
  <pre>List.map (fun x ↦ x.action) (core042RefNuBind core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>    [Act.other 1, Act.passthrough] ∧<br>  List.map (fun x ↦ x.mspec) (core042RefNuBind core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>      [some core042NuMs, none] ∧<br>    List.map (fun x ↦ x.mspec) (core042RefNuBindMapKeep core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>        [some core042NuMs, none] ∧<br>      List.map (fun x ↦ x.mspec)<br>            (core042RefNuBindMapClobber core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>          [some core042NuMs, none] ∧<br>        List.map (fun x ↦ x.action) (core042NuDropBind core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>            [Act.other 1, Act.passthrough] ∧<br>          List.map (fun x ↦ x.mspec) (core042NuDropBind core042NuEx core042NuR).trans =<br>              [none, none] ∧<br>            (core042NuDropBind core042NuEx core042NuR).shadow =<br>              (core042RefNuBind core042NuEx core042NuR).shadow</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_043"></a>
## CORE-043: Output-Declaring Transitions Must Produce

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043` · Kind **F** · Scope every compile step and every verification entry point (state-class graph and SMT), under every property and option setting the entry point accepts · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 fcb226a000337de7 ai** · Statement hash `fcb226a000337de7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* a net holds a transition that declares an output spec, a `Timeout`-only spec included, and carries the built-in passthrough action ([CORE-051]), whether bound explicitly, carried because a `bindActions` mapping omitted it ([CORE-042]), or left in place as the builder default, *then* compiling the net *shall* fail with an error that names the first such transition in declaration order.<br><br>*If* no transition of a net both declares an output spec and carries the built-in passthrough action, *then* compiling the net *shall not* fail under this requirement.<br><br>*If* a transition declares no output spec, or carries an action other than the built-in passthrough, a `fork()` action ([CORE-052]) or a hand-written action that produces nothing included, *then* compiling the net *shall not* fail under this requirement naming that transition.<br><br>*When* a net is submitted to a verification entry point (state-class graph or SMT), under any property and option the entry point accepts, the entry point *shall* fail under this requirement exactly when compiling the submitted net does, with an error that names the same transition. | 1. For every compile check C and every verification entry check V, each a function from a built net to none (the check passes) or some name (the check fails naming that transition):<br>2. if the transitions of net b, in declaration order, are l1, then d, then l2, d declares an output specification and carries the built-in passthrough, and no transition of l1 does both, then C b fails naming d;<br>3. if no transition of net b both declares an output specification and carries the built-in passthrough, then C b passes;<br>4. for every net b, V b is C b: the verification entry point fails on exactly the nets compiling fails on, naming the same transition. | <pre>fun {N A} C V ↦<br>  (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A) (l₁ : List (TransDef N A)) (d : TransDef N A)<br>      (l₂ : List (TransDef N A)),<br>      b.trans = l₁ ++ d :: l₂ →<br>        d.out ≠ none →<br>          d.action = Act.passthrough →<br>            (∀ e ∈ l₁, e.out ≠ none → e.action ≠ Act.passthrough) →<br>              C b = some d.core.name) ∧<br>    (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        (∀ d ∈ b.trans, d.out ≠ none → d.action ≠ Act.passthrough) → C b = none) ∧<br>      ∀ (b : BuiltNet N A), V b = C b</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A compile check (C) is the CORE-043 check of one implementation's compile step, read as a function of the built net: none when the check passes, some n when it fails (a panic or an exception) with an error naming transition n. A verification entry check (V) is the same check at one verification entry point of that implementation under one property and one option setting the entry point accepts: the state-class-graph entry point and the SMT entry point are each their own V, each setting gives its own V, and the block holds for every such V (CORE_043 C V once per entry point and setting). Other reasons a compile step or a verifier may refuse a net are not this block's subject. The message bytes are not stated: they differ by one word across the runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:792-799 and typescript/src/core/internal/output-action-check.ts:13-19 against java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/OutputActionCheck.java:32-36); only that the error names the transition is stated, read as the returned name.
- An action is read as its identity tag (Act): the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id. That the built-in is one stable instance and that the identity predicate accepts it and rejects every other action is CORE-051's (line 3 of its AC list); this block reads 'carries the built-in passthrough' as action = passthrough. The third quoted sentence is lines 1 and 2 together, under the shared unique-names assumption (ruling D23): a transition that declares no output specification, or carries fork(), a hand-written action that produces nothing or any other action than the built-in, is no offender, so either the net has no offender and line 2 passes it, or line 1 names the first offender, which is another transition with another name (core043_nonOffender_unnamed, through core043_pin: the three lines determine both checks). Without unique names a non-offender that shares the first offender's name gets the same returned name, which no check over names can tell apart; the lines themselves need no unique-names premise. CORE_043_nonvacuous checks a sink, a fork()-bound and a no-op transition together, alone and next to an offender; CORE_043_forbids_extensional kills the check that also refuses the hand-written one.
- 'Declares an output spec' is read as 'has an output specification' (out is not none): an empty And or Xor cannot be built (rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs:47, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Arc.java:274-275, typescript/src/core/out.ts:68-69), so 'non-empty output spec' (AC1) and 'output spec' name the same transitions. A Timeout-only spec, Timeout(d, ForwardInput(P, Q)), is an output specification like any other: the ForwardInput branch is deposited by the executor on the timeout outcome (IO-014), which passthrough never reaches, and line 1 does not exempt it (CORE_043_mutant_timeoutExempt_killed).
- 'The first such transition in declaration order' is the order of the built net's transitions, the order in which they were added (CORE-040, ruling D32). All three runtimes walk the net's transitions and throw on the first offender (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:66, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java:101, typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:80). A check that names another offender violates line 1: the last one (CORE_043_mutant_someOffender_killed), or the one with the least name, as a walk over the transitions sorted by name would (CORE_043_forbids_nameSorted); core043_netTwo declares its offenders b then a, so both are told apart from the first. Every transition is checked, a source with no input arc included: a check placed inside the walk over input arcs skips sources and violates line 1 (CORE_043_forbids_skipSource). Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, with the shared unique-names assumption of ruling D23).
- The lines range over every built net, including one no builder produced; the check reads only each transition's name, output specification and action, so a net a host can submit (one that holds only builder outputs, BuiltNet.FromBuilder) is one case of them. How a transition came to carry passthrough plays no part: the check reads the net handed to the compile step, after the builder default (CORE-051), either bindActions form (CORE-042: refBind with a resolver; mapKeep, where an omitted transition keeps its prior action, which is passthrough when it was never bound; mapClobber, where an omitted transition gets passthrough), binding on a subnet definition (MOD-051), per-instance binding (MOD-030) and channel merge (MOD-021). The first quoted sentence's 'carried because a bindActions mapping omitted it' covers both map forms. The theorems core043_builderDefault and core043_mapOmitted show the builder default and the mapClobber substitution reaching the reference check; subnet binding, per-instance binding and channel merge are the composition model's (W8), which rebuilds through the builder, so the lines already range over the nets it builds and their evidence is W8's.
- The verification entry point is checked against the net submitted to it, under every property and option setting it accepts. A net the verifier derives from it, such as the in-flight split of VER-004 and NU-052 under PrioritySemantics CONFLICT (whose start half keeps a sink's name and action and gains an output place), is not the submitted net and is not checked under this requirement. Every runtime checks the submitted net once, before any rewrite: Rust's SMT entry point checks the net it is given (rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs SmtVerifier::for_net), and the TypeScript and Java SMT entry points check the caller's net before prepare() rewrites it (typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts verify and encodeScripts, requireOutputProducingActions(this.callerNet); java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java pipeline and encodeScripts, requireOutputProducingActions(callerNet)). The in-flight split gives the start half of a sink on the built-in passthrough a placeholder action that is never run (rust/libpetri-verification/src/in_flight.rs halves and placeholder_action; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/InFlight.java START_ACTION; typescript/src/verification/in-flight.ts NEVER_RUN_ACTION), and keeps every other action, so the checks the state-class graph builders make on the derived net (rust/libpetri-verification/src/nu_scg_verifier.rs verify_name_scg and state_class_graph.rs StateClassGraph::build_core, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/StateClassGraph.java initial class) pass on it exactly when compiling the submitted net does; the Python binding rides on Rust. A verifier that runs the check on the derived split net, whose start half keeps a sink's passthrough and gains an output place, refuses under CONFLICT a net that compiles and violates line 3 (the behaviour RD-08 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of all three runtimes and Python); so does a reused verifier that checks the net its previous call left rewritten instead of the one submitted (the behaviour RD-47 recorded of Java's SmtVerifier). The tests: rust smt_verifier.rs core043_conflict_split_of_a_passthrough_sink_is_not_refused; java SplitDemandTest CORE043_aConflictSplitOfAPassthroughSinkIsNotRefused and CORE043_aReusedVerifierChecksTheCallersNet; typescript tests/verification/smt-verifier-core043.test.ts; python tests/test_smoke.py test_core_043_conflict_split_of_a_passthrough_sink_is_not_refused. The environment transitions of a VER-022 contract are not transitions of the submitted net and are not checked (VER-022: 'Their actions never run, so one that declares outputs gets a placeholder action instead of a [CORE-043] refusal'). The verifier pipeline model (Verifier/Pipeline.lean, the block VER_003) does not model the entry check: its decider starts from the property-place refusal, so the reference entry check is refVerifyEntry = refCompile (refVerifyEntry_eq) and line 3's holds evidence is true by definition. That every verifier entry point runs the check is test evidence (kind Q), the runtime sites named above.
- The body's 'compiling or verifying such a net MUST fail' is lines 1 and 3; 'one check there covers the builder default, either bindActions form, binding on a subnet definition, per-instance binding and channel merge alike' is the reading above that the check reads the net, not the binding. 'Such a transition can never fire usefully' is a consequence: an output specification never offers an empty deposit to an action outcome (core043_no_empty_action_deposit, every branch names a place: branches_ne_nil_mem), so under IO-015 the empty output of passthrough fails validation on every firing (IO_015_ac6); on a net that passes the check, a transition carrying passthrough has no output specification and its empty deposit is the one its spec offers (core043_passthrough_sink). 'Verification does not compensate' and 'the rule is unconditional' (it does not depend on the CONC-026 validation opt-out) are why the check exists, not further lines: the check reads no executor option.
- AC1 (compiling errors when a transition with a non-empty output spec carries passthrough, bound explicitly, substituted by a bindActions mapping or left as the builder default, a Timeout-only spec included) is line 1, with the readings above; a compile step that never refuses (a check made at bind time only, which misses the builder default) violates it (CORE_043_forbids_bindTimeOnly), and so does one that exempts a Timeout-only spec (CORE_043_mutant_timeoutExempt_killed) or skips a source transition (CORE_043_forbids_skipSource). CORE_043_nonvacuous computes the four cases of the test derivation on the reference, and a source transition.
- AC2 (the error names the offending transition, the first one in declaration order when there are several) is line 1's 'fails naming d'.
- AC3 (submitting the same net to a verification entry point fails the same way) is line 3, once per entry point and option setting; a verification entry point that never refuses violates it (CORE_043_forbids_verifyNever), and so do the readings 'refuses at least the nets compiling refuses' (CORE_043_mutant_verifyCovers_killed) and 'refuses the same nets, naming any transition' (CORE_043_mutant_sameNets_killed).
- AC4 (a sink may carry passthrough; CORE-042 is untouched) is line 2 on a net whose transitions carrying passthrough have no output specification, and the third quoted sentence on a net that also holds an offender. That binding stays lazy and total is CORE-042's line, not restated here.
- AC5 (the built-in is recognised by identity, so a hand-written action that produces nothing is not claimed) is line 2 and the third quoted sentence read over the identity tag; the extensional reading of the whole check (an output-declaring transition is refused when its action produces nothing) is CORE_043_mutant_extensional, killed by the extensional check. That such an action fails at run time is IO-015's.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_050"></a>
## CORE-050: Transition Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_050` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0e01354c5393cdc4 ai** · Statement hash `0e01354c5393cdc4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive a transition context holding the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read ([EXEC-010], [EXEC-012]).<br><br>*When* a firing ends with the completion of its action, the firing *shall* deposit exactly the output tokens the action completed with, whether the action wrote them through the context or returned them.<br><br>*If* the executor admits the completion of a firing's action ([EXEC-020]), the transition has no match specification ([NU-020]) and the output tokens fill one output branch ([IO-015]), *then* the firing *shall* end with that completion. | 1. Let Q be the queue firings (Q t M δ e M': t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action, emits e and leaves M') and AF the action firings (AF a t M δ e M': such a firing under the action a that ends with the completion of a, which emitted e).<br>2. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: every firing in AF a is a firing in Q with the same delivery, emission and markings, so the action receives exactly what the firing delivers.<br>3. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: if AF a has a firing of t delivering δ and emitting e, then a completes with e on t and δ.<br>4. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e whose places, in emission order, are one output branch of t and that a completes with on t and δ: every firing of t in Q delivering δ and emitting e is a firing in AF a. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q AF ↦<br>  (∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>      on fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M') ∧<br>    (∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>        on fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦ a t δ (Except.ok e)) ∧<br>      ∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>        (e : List (N × T)),<br>        OutputBranch t (List.map Prod.fst e) →<br>          a t δ (Except.ok e) →<br>            on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (Q, AF). Q is the queue firing relation (QFireRel, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean; glossary: Queue order): Q t M δ e M' says that t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action (the tokens it consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read, Delivered), emits e (places and tokens, in emission order) and leaves M'. AF is the action firing relation (ActFireRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): AF a t M δ e M' is a firing of t under the action a that ends with the completion of a, which emitted e. A plain QFireRel cannot carry AF: it does not record how a firing ended, and a firing that ends with the timeout outcome deposits tokens no action produced (IO-013). The witness pair is RefQFire and refActionFire, the reference queue firings whose emission fills one output branch and that the action completes with.
- An action (glossary: Action; ActionRel in Spec/GlossaryAction.lean) is a relation from a transition and the delivery to how the action ends: completing with an emission or failing with a message (EXEC-030). It is a relation, not a function, because an action may read the world. The transition context is read as the delivery δ; its accessors (input, inputs, inputToken, read, output) are CORE-060 to CORE-063's, stated over the same delivery.
- Line 1 reads the first sentence as 'the action receives what the firing delivers': the delivery of a firing in AF is that of a firing in Q. Which tokens Q delivers is EXEC-010's second line (from each input place, its consumed oldest tokens) and EXEC-012 (one head per read arc), stated over the same Q in the joint model; CORE-050 does not restate them. An executor that hands the action every token of each input place violates line 1 against the reference Q (CORE_050_mutant_wholePlaces_killed).
- Line 2 reads the second sentence: the emission of a firing in AF a is one a completes with on that delivery, and the firing in Q (line 1) deposits exactly that emission; 'exactly' is Q's effect rule (EXEC-020: appended at the tail, in emission order; CORE-035). An executor that deposits tokens of its own in the places the action wrote violates it (CORE_050_mutant_placesOnly_killed), and so does one that counts a timed-out firing as a firing that ends with an action that never completes (CORE_050_forbids_timeout). Whether the action wrote its tokens through the context or returned them, they reach the firing as the emission it completes with; the context's output buffer is CORE-062's.
- Line 3 reads the third sentence. The model has no stop, no immediate termination and no Timeout budget, so 'the executor admits the completion' is read as 'the action completes': an admitted completion is never that of a firing that ended with its timeout outcome or that a stop on a terminal place or an immediate termination abandoned (glossary: Admitted completion; EXEC-020), and which completions the executor admits is the executor model's (RefExec). A transition of the model has no match specification (Trans, ruling D16), which is the sentence's scope: on a correlated join the relay check of NU-054 may reject a completion that fills a branch (EXEC-021). An executor whose firings never end with their action violates the line (CORE_050_mutant_soundOnly_killed: the first draft, lines 1 and 2 alone, held of it).
- Line 3 is stated on the granularity of the reference: the places of the emission, in emission order, are one output branch as Out.branches lists it (glossary: Output branch, one token per place, the IO-016 convention). RefQFire compares the emitted places with an offered deposit as a list, so a completion that fills a branch with its places in another order, or that puts more than one token in a place of a branch, is no firing of RefQFire, and line 3 says nothing of it. That such a completion passes validation and deposits in the order the action produced its tokens is IO-015's set comparison and EXEC-020, stated at count level.
- Line 3 is relative to Q, so CORE-050 alone holds of the empty pair. In the joint model Q covers every reference firing (QCovers) and delivers the reference delivery (EXEC-010, EXEC-012), so every completion with an output branch of an enabled transition is a firing in AF (core050_fires), every firing in AF, counted, is a firing of the count semantics (core050_projects), and every firing in Q ends with the completion of an action or with IO-013's timeout outcome (core050_endsBy).
- Ruling D17: 'ends with the completion of its action' is the admitted completion (glossary: Admitted completion). A completion that is not admitted (after the timeout outcome, a stop on a terminal place, an immediate termination) is not one line 2 speaks of. AF a holds a tuple only if a completes with its emission on its delivery (line 2), so an action that fails ends no firing in AF (EXEC-030), and an executor that counts a failed action as completing with no token violates line 2 (CORE_050_forbids_failAsEmpty). A tuple does not record how the firing ended: the child of a Timeout node is also an action branch, so the tuple of a firing that ended with the timeout outcome is in AF a whenever a can complete with the same emission (core050_timeout_overlap), and EndsByActionOrTimeout is a cover, not a partition; CORE_050_forbids_timeout therefore uses an action that never completes. Tokens an action publishes before it completes (the IO-015 flush, Rust and Python) are not in the atomic model, as in EXEC-020. The ν-correlated inputs of NU-020 are not modelled: RefQFire consumes oldest first from every input place (ruling D16).
- Q models an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026), as RefQFire does: a completion whose emission fills no output branch ends no firing (EXEC-021). The deposit of the action's write under the validation skip is CONC-026's.
- A built transition carries its action as an identity tag (Act, CORE-020); the action a tag names is Act.interp I, the passthrough tag naming the action that completes with no token (CORE-051). By line 2 a firing under the passthrough tag deposits nothing (core050_passthrough_nil), the firing-level fact CORE-043 rests on (passthrough_never_offered).
- AC1 (the action receives a context with consumed input tokens and read token values) is line 1 together with EXEC-010 and EXEC-012 on the same Q; the context's accessors are CORE-060 and CORE-061.
- AC2 (the action produces output tokens via the context or a return value) is line 2: through either channel the tokens are the emission the action completes with. That both channels exist is API shape.
- AC3 (the action is asynchronous: it returns a future, a promise or a completion stage) is API shape, a Q-kind test, not encoded. That an action starts at one step and completes at a later one is CONC-002's, over the executor model (RefExec).
- The test derivation (an action that reads its input, transforms it and produces output) is CORE_050_nonvacuous: an action that doubles the value it is handed, fired on a place holding 7 then 8, receives the oldest token 7 and the firing deposits 14.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_050_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_050): ✓ The reference pair satisfies CORE-050: a reference action firing is a reference queue firing whose emission fills an output branch and that the action completes with, and every such queue firing is one.
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_050 RefQFire refActionFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_050_forbids_failAsEmpty` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_050): ✗ It violates line 2: on the sink `s` under an action that only fails, it counts the firing that deposits nothing as one that ends with the action, which never completed.
  <pre>¬CORE_050 RefQFire core050_failAsEmpty</pre>
