<a id="Libpetri-Spec-EXP_007_config"></a>
## EXP-007: Export Configuration

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_007_config` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 af2399c8d9c410dc ai** · Statement hash `af2399c8d9c410dc`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The export supports configuration options:<br><br>**Layout direction**: top-to-bottom, left-to-right, etc.<br><br>The export *shall* lay out the drawing in the layout direction the configuration names.<br><br>The export *shall* draw the same graph, apart from its layout direction and the label drawn inside each transition node, under two configurations that differ only in the layout direction and the show options.<br><br>*Where* a configuration carries a show-types option, the export *shall* draw the same graph whichever value the option has.<br><br>The default configuration names the top-to-bottom layout direction and shows timing and priority. | 1. For the exporter E, every configuration cfg and every net X:<br>2. the drawing E cfg X has the layout direction of cfg;<br>3. for every value b, E draws X under cfg with show-types set to b exactly as under cfg;<br>4. for every configuration cfg' with the environment places and cluster source of cfg, E cfg X and E cfg' X have the same edges, the same clusters, the same compound attribute, and the same nodes once the label inside each transition node is blanked. | <pre>fun E ↦<br>  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),<br>    (E cfg X).dir = cfg.dir ∧<br>      (∀ (b : Bool),<br>          E<br>              { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := b, showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,<br>                showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }<br>              X =<br>            E cfg X) ∧<br>        ∀ (cfg' : ExportCfg),<br>          cfg.env = cfg'.env →<br>            cfg.cluster = cfg'.cluster →<br>              (E cfg X).edges = (E cfg' X).edges ∧<br>                (E cfg X).clusters = (E cfg' X).clusters ∧<br>                  (E cfg X).compound = (E cfg' X).compound ∧<br>                    List.map XNode.eraseTransLabel (E cfg X).nodes =<br>                      List.map XNode.eraseTransLabel (E cfg' X).nodes</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the drawn graph (glossary XGraph: layout direction, compound attribute, nodes, edges and clusters) of a configuration and a net. Line 3 compares two configurations that agree on the environment places and the cluster source, which the configuration also carries (EXP-008 and EXP-016 read them), so they differ only in the layout direction and the three show options; they have the same edges, clusters and compound attribute, and their nodes are compared after XNode.eraseTransLabel, which blanks the inner label of a transition node and keeps every other field (identity, category, external label) and every other node. So the graph is compared field by field except for the layout direction, which line 1 fixes per configuration. Lists are compared with their order: no option changes the order in any runtime. What the transition labels are is the label block, joined to E by the second clause of ExportAgrees.
- Line 2 is the show-types sentence, which is ruling D41 (a): the option stays in the configuration types of all three runtimes (Rust DotConfig.show_types, Java ExportConfig.showTypes, TypeScript DotConfig.showTypes) and no mapper reads it, so the 'Show/hide types' bullet is dropped and the sentence says the option changes nothing. A mapper that lets show-types hide the timing and priority of transition labels meets line 3, which allows label changes, and violates line 2 (EXP_007_forbids_typesHide); a mapper that ignores the direction violates line 1 (EXP_007_forbids_fixedDir); a mapper that also drops the timeout labels of output edges when timing is hidden violates line 3 (EXP_007_forbids_hideTimeoutLabels), and so does one that sets the compound attribute from a show option (EXP_007_forbids_compoundFlag).
- The 'etc.' of the layout direction bullet is the four directions every runtime has (glossary RankDir: TB, LR, BT, RL; Rust graph RankDir, Java export.graph.RankDir, TypeScript RankDir); line 1 holds for each. The DOT text is not modelled: that the rankdir attribute of the DOT text carries the typed graph's direction (the renderers' RankDir tables, TB, LR, BT and RL each to itself) is kind Q, checked by the renderer tests.
- The default sentence states no export behaviour: it describes the configuration type, so an exporter cannot break it and the statement has no line for it. The glossary's default ExportCfg is TB with timing and priority shown (EXP_007_default, which cites the sentence), as are Rust DotConfig::default(), Java ExportConfig.DEFAULT and TypeScript DEFAULT_DOT_CONFIG; that the runtime defaults match the glossary is checked by their tests, not here. What the export does under the default is line 1 and the label block at cfg = {}: the drawing is top to bottom (EXP_007_config_nonvacuous) and transition labels carry the interval and the non-zero priority (EXP_007_label_nonvacuous).
- AC1 (configuration controls what information is displayed) is line 1 for the direction and the label block for the transition labels; line 3 says the show options change nothing else in the drawn graph (edges, clusters, compound attribute and every node field but the inner transition label). AC2 (default configuration shows all information) is the default sentence together with line 1 and the label block's lines 2 and 4 at the default. AC3 (minimal configuration hides timing and priority) is the label block's line 1; the preset name is kind N (Java only). The test derivation is EXP_007_config_nonvacuous: the worked net of EXP-013 under the default configuration and with timing and priority hidden, same edges, transition labels RefreshCache [1, 5]ms prio=3 against RefreshCache.

## EXP-007: Export Configuration, the transition label

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_007_label` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter, the label of a transition node · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 9c513b8ff7802d44 ai** · Statement hash `9c513b8ff7802d44`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| **Show/hide timing**: toggle timing interval display on transitions<br><br>**Show/hide priority**: toggle priority display on transitions<br><br>*Where* the configuration hides timing and priority, the export *shall* label a transition node with the transition's name alone.<br><br>*Where* the configuration shows timing and hides priority, the export *shall* label a transition node with the transition's name, a space and `[e, l]ms`, where e is `earliest()` and l is `latest()` of the transition's timing, in milliseconds and in decimal, and l is written `∞` when `hasDeadline()` is false ([TIME-001]).<br><br>*Where* the configuration shows priority and the transition's priority n is not 0, the export *shall* label the transition's node with the label it would have if the configuration hid priority, followed by a space and `prio=n`, with n in decimal.<br><br>*Where* a transition's priority is 0, the export *shall* label its node with the label it would have if the configuration hid priority. | 1. For the transition labeller TL of an export, every configuration cfg, transition name, timing τ and priority n:<br>2. with timing and priority hidden, the label is the name;<br>3. with timing shown and priority hidden, the label is the name, then ' [e, l]ms' with e = earliest τ, and l = latest τ when τ has a deadline, else ∞;<br>4. when n is 0, the label is the label under cfg with priority hidden;<br>5. with priority shown and n not 0, the label is the label under cfg with priority hidden, then ' prio=n'. | <pre>fun TL ↦<br>  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (name : String) (τ : Novel.TimedScg.Timing) (n : ℤ),<br>    (cfg.showIntervals = false → cfg.showPriority = false → TL cfg name τ n = name) ∧<br>      (cfg.showIntervals = true →<br>          cfg.showPriority = false →<br>            TL cfg name τ n =<br>              (name ++ " [" ++ toString τ.earliest ++ ", " ++<br>                  if τ.hasDeadline = true then toString τ.latest else "∞") ++<br>                "]ms") ∧<br>        (n = 0 →<br>            TL cfg name τ n =<br>              TL<br>                { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,<br>                  showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals, showPriority := false,<br>                  env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }<br>                name τ n) ∧<br>          (cfg.showPriority = true →<br>            n ≠ 0 →<br>              TL cfg name τ n =<br>                TL<br>                      { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,<br>                        showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals, showPriority := false,<br>                        env := cfg.env, cluster := cfg.cluster }<br>                      name τ n ++<br>                    " prio=" ++<br>                  toString n)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a transition labeller TL : TransLabeller (glossary): the label of a transition node from the export configuration (glossary ExportCfg), the transition's name, its timing (the Timing of TIME-001: earliest, latest, hasDeadline, in whole milliseconds) and its priority. That every transition node of a drawn graph carries this label is the second clause of ExportAgrees, which the export consistency theorem takes; that the label starts with the name is EXP-003's line. ExportAgrees constrains only nets with X.Distinct (distinct transition names, at most one input arc per place), so the four sentences reach the drawing of such nets only; on a net with two transitions of one name the label of each node is left open, as in the other export blocks (the W4 shape).
- The four lines determine the label for every configuration: EXP_007_label_determined shows that refTransLabel is the only labeller that meets the block. So the show-types option, the layout direction, the environment places and the cluster source never change a transition label. This is the label half of the show-types sentence of the config block (ruling D41 (a)); a labeller that reads show-types as a master switch for the whole label violates line 2 (EXP_007_forbids_typesMaster).
- Numbers are written as Lean's toString writes Nat and Int: decimal digits, a minus sign before a negative priority (t [7, ∞]ms prio=-1), and ∞ is U+221E. A timing without a deadline is labelled with ∞ and never with its latest() value MAX_DURATION_MS (rulings D2 and D11: the label reads hasDeadline by timing variant); a mapper that prints the maximum is killed (EXP_007_forbids_printsMax). Java's Unconstrained timing, which the Lean Timing lacks, has earliest 0 and no deadline, so the same sentence labels it [0, ∞]ms. Sub-millisecond durations are out of scope: the model's durations are whole milliseconds, Java prints toMillis() and TypeScript the raw number.
- The parts are in the order name, interval, priority, each after one space; a mapper that writes the priority before the interval violates line 4 (EXP_007_forbids_prioFirst). A mapper that ignores the hide-timing option violates line 1 (EXP_007_forbids_alwaysInterval), and one that writes prio=0 violates line 3 (EXP_007_forbids_prioZero).
- AC1 (configuration controls what information is displayed) is these four lines for the transition label, and line 1 and line 3 of the config block for the rest of the drawing. AC2 (default configuration shows all information) is lines 2 and 4 at the default configuration: the interval of every transition, Immediate included as [0, ∞]ms, and the priority when it is not 0 (EXP_007_label_nonvacuous); token types are never drawn (ruling D41 (a)), so they are not part of all information. AC3 (minimal configuration hides timing and priority) is line 1 (export design, skeptic correction S-5): with timing and priority hidden the label is the bare name. The name 'minimal configuration' is kind N: only Java has such a preset (ExportConfig.minimal()), so the block quantifies over configurations instead.
- The test derivation (export with the default and with the minimal configuration, verify the difference) is EXP_007_label_nonvacuous: t [5, 10]ms prio=3 under the default against t when timing and priority are hidden.

## EXP-008: Styling

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_008` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter's mapper, on the place nodes of a net (before a documentation generator restyles interface ports) · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 1e4bf950dfb9a657 ai** · Statement hash `1e4bf950dfb9a657`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The export applies visual styling to distinguish node categories:<br><br>The export *shall* give a terminal place the terminal category.<br><br>The export *shall* give an environment place that is not a terminal place the environment category.<br><br>The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start category exactly when no transition's output spec names it.<br><br>The export *shall* give the end category to an ordinary place that some transition's output spec names and on which no transition has an input arc or a read arc.<br><br>The export *shall not* give the end category to an ordinary place on which some transition has an input arc.<br><br>The export *shall* give an ordinary place the start, the end or the regular place category.<br><br>The export *shall* give the same category to all ordinary places, in one net or in different nets, that some transition's output spec names, on which some transition has a read arc and on which no transition has an input arc. | 1. For the place classifier C, every net X with environment places env and terminal places term, and every place p:<br>2. a terminal place is terminal;<br>3. an environment place that is not terminal is environment;<br>4. for a place that is neither (an ordinary place): it is start exactly when no transition has an output arc on it;<br>5. it is end when some transition has an output arc on it and none has an input arc or a read arc on it;<br>6. it is not end when some transition has an input arc on it;<br>7. it is start, end or the regular place row;<br>8. and if some transition has an output arc on it, some has a read arc on it and none has an input arc on it, then every ordinary place p' of every net X' (with any env' and term') of which the same holds gets the same row as p. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] C ↦<br>  ∀ (X : Reference.Net N) (env term : N → Bool) (p : N),<br>    (term p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.terminal) ∧<br>      (term p = false → env p = true → C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.environment) ∧<br>        (term p = false →<br>          env p = false →<br>            (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ↔ HasOutputArc X p = false) ∧<br> true → C X env term p ≠ Export.NodeCat.end) ∧<br>                  (C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.start ∨<br>                      C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.end ∨<br>                        C X env term p = Export.NodeCat.place) ∧<br>                    (HasOutputArc X p = true →<br>                      HasInputArc X p = false →<br>                        HasReadArc X p = true →<br>                          ∀ (X' : Reference.Net N) (env' term' : N → Bool) (p' : N),<br>                            term' p' = false →<br>                              env' p' = false →<br>                                HasOutputArc X' p' = true →<br>                                  HasInputArc X' p' = false →<br>                                    HasReadArc X' p' = true →<br>                                      C X' env' term' p' = C X env term p))</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a place classifier C : PlaceClassifier N: the node row (glossary of the style table, Libpetri.Export.NodeCat) the export's mapper gives place p of net X, given the environment places env (ENV-001) and the terminal places term (EXEC-042) as predicates. C reads only the arcs of X, as every runtime's analysis does (analyze_places in the Rust crate libpetri-export, PlaceAnalysis.java, analyzePlaces in petri-net-mapper.ts); the marking, the timing and the configuration play no part. Lines 1 to 6 fix C from the arc kinds on p in every case but one, and line 7 makes that one case, too, the same answer for every place and every net, so C reads no more of X than whether p has an output arc, an input arc and a read arc. That the exporter draws each place node with the row C gives is the third clause of the glossary agreement ExportAgrees (each place node has the category C gives its place, with the configuration's environment places and the net's terminal places), which the export consistency theorem carries; that a place row is not the transition row is EXP-002's line 1 and EXP-003's line 3; EXP_002_draws_EXP_008 shows the reference exporter drawing each place node with the row of the reference classifier. This block itself does not see the graph.
- C is the mapper's classification, the one the production export pipeline gives. The three documentation generators (SubnetDotExport.java, subnet-dot-export.ts, and the Rust subnet_dot_export module; compile-time diagrams, EXP-011) afterwards rewrite the DOT of a subnet body and redraw its interface-port places with the interface-port row; that rewrite is a later step on the DOT text, not C's answer, and is out of scope. The markdown says so in the sentence after the bullets. A mapper that gives an ordinary place the interface-port row itself violates line 6 (EXP_008_forbids_otherRow).
- Which places get a node at all is EXP-001's subject (ruling D60): Rust draws every declared place, Java and TypeScript only places some arc touches. Line 3 gives a place that no arc touches the start category, which is what Rust draws; Java and TypeScript draw no node for it, so their answer for it is never seen (PlaceAnalysis.category answers place for an unknown name). The reference classifier answers start, as Rust does.
- The words 'incoming' and 'outgoing' of the body bullets ('no incoming arcs', 'no outgoing arcs') are read as the markdown's sentence after the bullets defines them, which is how all three runtimes count: an incoming arc of a place is an output arc of some transition on it (glossary: Output arc, the target of a ForwardInput included), and an input arc on it is an outgoing arc. Whether a read arc is an outgoing arc is the open case of ruling D51 (next assumption). Inhibitor arcs and reset arcs count as neither, although the glossary draws them from the place to the transition and the reset edge of EXP-004 and EXP-013 is drawn from the transition to the place (clash exp-a#5 and exp-a#9): a classifier that counts them as outgoing violates line 4 (EXP_008_forbids_glossaryDirections), one that counts a reset arc as incoming violates line 3 (EXP_008_forbids_resetIncoming).
- Ruling D51 (a): the common form of 'end place'. A place that an output spec names, on which no transition has an input arc and some transition has a read arc, is regular in Java and TypeScript (a read arc counts as outgoing) and end in Rust (only input arcs count). Lines 4 and 5 hold of both shapes and leave that place open (EXP_008_readOnly_open); the Rust shape is an allowed classifier (EXP_008_allows_inputsOnly). The case is open per classifier, not per place: line 7 says a classifier answers it the same way for every such place of every net, so a mix of the two shapes is rejected, whether the answer hangs on whether the reader writes elsewhere (EXP_008_forbids_readByWriter) or on whether the reader is the place's own writer (EXP_008_forbids_selfReadSkipped). The end state of D51, that a read arc keeps a place from being an end place, is the reference classifier's answer; the later line that makes line 4 an 'exactly when' with read arcs counted waits for the Rust mapper to change and is not encoded. The markdown records the open case and the intended answer in a sentence without shall.
- The precedence terminal, environment, start, end is all three runtimes' (ruling D51) and is lines 1 to 3 and 6: a terminal environment place is terminal (EXP_008_forbids_envFirst), an environment place no output spec names is environment, not start (EXP_008_forbids_startFirst), and a place with no arcs at all is start, not end (EXP_008_forbids_endFirst). EXEC-042 builds reject a terminal place with an input or read arc, which the precedence does not need.
- AC1 (start places are visually distinct from other places) and AC2 (end places are visually distinct from other places) are read on the style table: the start row and the end row each differ from every other place row and from the transition row (EXP_008_rows_distinct, decided on the generated table), and lines 1 to 7 decide which places get the start and the end row. The drawn style is tied to C by the third clause of ExportAgrees, so AC1 and AC2 are EXP_008_rows_distinct together with that clause, carried by the export consistency theorem, and EXP_002_draws_EXP_008 (EXP_002.lean, tagged as citing EXP-008 AC1 and AC2), which proves on the reference exporter, for every cluster stage, that each place node has the reference classifier's row and a style different from every place or transition node of another row. The colours of the body bullets ('e.g., green', 'e.g., blue', 'e.g., yellow') are examples; the values are the table's and are checked by the runtimes' tests, not here. The bullet on transitions (a distinct colour) is the transition row's difference from the place rows in EXP_008_rows_distinct; that transitions are drawn with the transition row is EXP-003's subject.
- The test derivation (a net with start and end places, export, styling applied) is EXP_008_nonvacuous on the reference classifier: a net with a start, a regular, an end, an environment, a terminal and an inhibitor-only place.
- Out of scope: the rows of composition (interface-port, sync-channel), which only the documentation generators' rewrite of a subnet diagram uses (see the second assumption; MOD-040 and EXP-016 add grouping only), and the rows of junctions (EXP-012), which are synthetic nodes, not place nodes; ν correlation (NU-020, EXP-018) changes no place category. Places are compared by identity (DecidableEq N); export IDs and sanitising are EXP-014's (ruling D46).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-EXP_012"></a>
## EXP-012: XOR/AND Junction Nodes

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_012` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter, the output side of one transition · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 058caa2740b22067 ai** · Statement hash `058caa2740b22067`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| For every `Out.Xor` or `Out.And` group with **two or more children**, the mapper MUST insert a synthetic *junction node* between the transition and the children.<br><br>A group with fewer than two children MUST NOT produce a junction (it is a pass-through).<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw one junction node for each `And` or `Xor` group of an output spec that has two or more children, of the group's kind, and no other junction node.<br><br>*Where* an `And` or `Xor` group has fewer than two children, the mapper *shall* draw its child, if it has one, from the group's parent and with the label the edge into the group would carry.<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw exactly one solid output edge into each junction node, into the place of each `Place` leaf and into the target place of each `ForwardInput` leaf, from the nearest junction node above it, or from the transition when there is none, and no other edge for the output spec.<br><br>The edge into a child of an `Xor` junction *shall* carry the child's branch label: the place name of a `Place` child, `⏱&lt;n>ms` for a `Timeout` child of n ms, and no label for an `And` or `Xor` child.<br><br>The edge into a child of an `And` junction, and the edge from the transition into the output spec, *shall* carry no label of their own.<br><br>*Where* a `Timeout` node of n ms is in an output spec, the edge drawn into its child *shall* carry `⏱&lt;n>ms` in place of the label the edge into the `Timeout` would carry.<br><br>*Where* a leaf is a `ForwardInput` from place F to place P, the mapper *shall* draw its edge as the edge of a `Place` leaf for P at the same position, dashed instead of solid, and with `⟵F` after its label and a space, or as its only label when it has none.<br><br>*Where* [EXP-013] combines a leaf edge into a reset place, that edge *shall* take the arc type, label and style [EXP-013] gives it in place of the ones above. | 1. For every transition name t, reset places R and output tree o (any tree, short and empty groups included), there is a one-to-one renumbering ρ of the junction indices the emitter E uses, such that:<br>2. the junctions E draws, renumbered, are the groups of o with two or more children, one junction each, of the group's kind (OutTree.junctions), in any order;<br>3. the edges E draws, renumbered, are the edges of the drawing rule (Drawing t o), one each, in any order: both ends of every edge, and for every edge that does not end in a reset place also its arc type output, style row output, dash and label as the rule gives them. | <pre>fun E ↦<br>  ∀ (t : String) (R : List String) (o : OutTree),<br>    ∃ ρ,<br>      (∀ (i j : ℕ), ρ i = ρ j → i = j) ∧<br>        (List.map (fun kj ↦ (kj.1, ρ kj.2)) (E t R o).junctions).Perm o.junctions.zipIdx ∧<br>          (List.map (XEdge.seen R ρ) (E t R o).edges).Perm<br>            (List.map (DrawnEdge.seen R) (Drawing t o))</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an output emitter E : Emitter (glossary): from a transition name t, its reset places R and its output tree o (glossary OutTree: n-ary And and Xor groups, a Timeout with its duration in ms, Place and ForwardInput leaves), the junctions, as (kind, index), and the edges (glossary XEdge: ends, arc type, style row, dash, label) the exporter draws for the output side of t. The input, inhibitor, read and standalone reset edges and the place and transition nodes are drawn outside the emitter and are other blocks' subject (EXP-001 to EXP-004, EXP-013).
- The drawing rule Drawing t o is the glossary's drawOut from the transition, with no inherited label, junctions numbered from 0, one clause per sentence: a group with two or more children gives one junction of its kind and one solid output edge into it from the parent with the inherited label, then its children below it (the first and third shall sentences); a shorter group gives no junction and draws its children from the parent with the inherited label (the second); a Place leaf gives one solid edge into its place from the parent with the inherited label (the third); below an Xor junction a child inherits its branch label (glossary branchLabel), below an And junction and from the transition nothing (the fourth and fifth); a Timeout hands its child the label ⏱<n>ms in place of the inherited one (the sixth); a ForwardInput leaf from F into P is the Place leaf for P, dashed, labelled forwardLabel (⟵F after the inherited label and a space, or ⟵F alone) (the seventh). The two body sentences that open the section say what the first two shall sentences say.
- Junction indices are compared up to a one-to-one renumbering ρ: which index each junction gets (pre-order from 0) is EXP-014's line, so an emitter that numbers its junctions in post-order still meets this block. The renumbering must be one to one, so an emitter that draws the edge into a junction at one index and the edges out of it at another (two nodes in the graph for one group) violates the block (EXP_012_forbids_split).
- Order is not stated: the junctions and edges are compared as lists up to permutation (List.Perm), membership and multiplicity only. Node and edge order across languages is open ruling R2 (exp-b) and kind Q; the order of an Xor junction's children is EXP-005's line.
- The last shall sentence is the guard of the third line: for an edge that ends in a place of R only its two ends are compared, and its arc type, style row, label and dash are EXP-013's. Its ends and the count, one edge per leaf, still bind, so an emitter that draws a combined edge next to an output edge for one leaf violates this block.
- The block quantifies over every output tree, including a group with fewer than two children (Rust's Out::Xor is a public variant and a TypeScript node a plain object, so a short Xor reaches the mappers' pass-through arm), an empty group (no junction and no edge, as all three mappers draw it) and a ForwardInput below an Xor junction, which no transition that builds has (IO-013, IO-014): the seventh shall sentence draws it as the Place leaf for its target, so its label is the target name, a space and ⟵F, which is what all three mappers draw.
- The junction node attributes (shape diamond, fill, stroke, pen width, size, the glyphs ✕ and ✚, font size, fixed size) and the node categories xor-junction and and-junction belong to the exporter's nodes and the style table (Libpetri.Export.Styles), not to the emitter. The category ('Style category xor-junction', 'Style category and-junction') is EXP-014's eighth line: every junction node of kind k has the row JKind.cat k, which the reference's refJunctionNode draws and an exporter that swaps the two rows violates (EXP_014_forbids_junctionCatSwap). The other attributes are the table's constants, checked by tests (kind Q).
- This block states the third shall sentence ('one junction node for each group ..., and no other junction node') for one output spec, on the emitter. On the graph it is carried by the junction clause of the export agreement (ExportAgrees, glossary: on a net with distinct transition names the junction nodes of each transition of the net are the emitter's for its output spec, up to order), which the export consistency theorem carries, together with EXP-014's seventh line (no junction node for a transition the net does not have): an exporter that adds a junction node for a name no transition of the net has meets the agreement and violates EXP-014 (EXP_014_forbids_strayJunction).
- AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are EXP_012_nonvacuous on the reference emitter: XOR(P_a, P_b) gives one xor junction and the edges junction to P_a and junction to P_b; AND(P_c, P_d) one and junction and two edges; AND(P_a) a direct edge from the transition to P_a and no junction (AC3 is stated with AND by ruling D26 item 1, since IO-012 gives every Xor two or more children); XOR(AND(P_a, P_b), P_c) an and junction nested below the xor junction. Their junction attributes (diamond, ✕, ✚) are the exporter's, as above.
- AC5 (Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers produce byte-identical junction nodes and edges) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4.

## EXP-013: Combined reset+output Edge

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_013` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter, the edges of one transition into one place · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 de8231f060c029c7 ai** · Statement hash `de8231f060c029c7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

| When a transition has both an output arc and a reset arc to the same place P, the mapper MUST draw every output edge to P as a combined edge, styled as the reset-output category (color `#fd7e14`, style `bold`, penwidth `2.0`, arrowhead `normal`) and labelled `"reset+out"`.<br><br>The standalone output edge to P MUST be suppressed in this case.<br><br>The standalone reset edge to P MUST be suppressed in this case.<br><br>When the output spec names P in more than one leaf (for example `Xor(P, And(P, Q))`), each such leaf gives one combined edge.<br><br>If a transition resets place P but does not output to P, the standalone reset edge with label `"reset"` MUST still be emitted (existing behavior preserved).<br><br>If a transition outputs to P but does not reset P, the standalone output edge MUST be emitted (existing behavior preserved).<br><br>The combination applies regardless of whether the output edge originates at the transition directly or at an XOR/AND junction underneath the transition (per EXP-012).<br><br>When the output is a leaf under a junction, the *junction → P* edge is the one that becomes reset-styled with the `"reset+out"` label.<br><br>The combined edge carries the label `"reset+out"` alone and is never dashed: it replaces the branch label, the timeout label and the `ForwardInput` label and dash the leaf edge would carry under X).edges,<br>        e.arc = ArcType.resetOutput →<br>          ∃ t ∈ X.trans,<br>            e.src.owner? = some t.name ∧ ∃ P ∈ t.core.resets, e.dst = NodeRef.place P</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration and the export view of a net (ExportNet: declared places, transitions in declaration order with their input, inhibitor, read and reset arcs and their n-ary output tree), the typed graph a mapper builds before DOT text. The block reads only its edges: the output-side edges and the reset edges of one transition into one place, and the edges of arc type resetOutput of the whole graph. The edges of a transition are found by their ends (the node of t or a junction of t), and the exporter keys transition nodes by name, so the five per-transition lines, like the five EARS sentences they encode, bind only nets whose transition names are pairwise distinct: with two transitions named T, each with Out.Place(P), every mapper draws two edges from t_T into p_P where each transition has one leaf. The sixth line needs no such condition and binds every net. Ghost edges between clusters (EXP-017) have their own arc type and are in none of the three.
- Which leaves end in P is read off the output tree: a Place leaf for P and a ForwardInput leaf into P (t.outLeaves). Which edge belongs to which leaf, where each edge starts (the transition or the nearest junction above the leaf, so the junction edge of the sentence on a leaf under a junction) and the order of the edges are EXP-012's lines, carried to the exporter by the agreement ExportAgrees; this block fixes their number per place and their arc type, style row, dash and label. The combined edge is never dashed and carries reset+out alone, so it replaces the branch label of an Xor child, the timeout label and the ForwardInput label and dash (ruling D26 item 3), which is the last shall sentence of EXP-012. The sixth line keeps the combined style off every other edge: an edge into a junction (the parent edge of a group, an output edge of EXP-012) and an edge from the place back to the transition are never of arc type resetOutput.
- For an edge into a place t does not reset, this block fixes the arc type output and the style row output: that is the black output edge of AC2 and the plain output style of AC4, whose colour is a constant of the style table. Its label and dash (the branch label Q of AC4, a timeout label, the ForwardInput label and dash) are EXP-012's, and that the row of an output edge is output is also EXP-004's output line.
- An output spec may name P in more than one leaf (Xor(P, And(P, Q)) builds: its branches differ). Then all three mappers draw one combined edge per leaf, and the first line and the fifth line say so (ruling D26 item 4: every output edge to P becomes a reset+out edge).
- A transition may hold two reset arcs on one place (the TypeScript and Rust builders append without removing duplicates); the third line then asks for one standalone reset edge per arc, as all three mappers draw them. That a reset arc is drawn transition to place is the drawing convention of all three mappers (EXP-004).
- The style rows name the rows of the style table (Libpetri.Export.Styles, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json): the colour #fd7e14, the bold line, the pen width 2.0 and the arrowhead of the reset-output and reset rows are constants of that table, checked by tests (kind Q). The worked DOT of the section is illustrative: its four edges are among refExportFlat_example_edges (Reference/Export.lean) at the level of IDs, arc types and labels, where the example net has further arcs (two input arcs, an inhibitor arc, a read arc and a reset arc on a second place) and the edges come in declaration order, those of Try before those of RefreshCache.
- AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 are EXP_013_nonvacuous on the reference exporter: Out.Place(P) with reset(P) gives one reset+out edge from the transition and no reset edge; Out.Place(P) without a reset one plain output edge; reset(P) without an output to P one reset edge labelled reset; Out.Xor(P, Q) with reset(P) a combined edge from the junction to P and a plain edge, labelled Q, from the junction to Q.
- AC5 (Java, TypeScript and Rust mappers produce byte-identical edges) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-EXP_014"></a>
## EXP-014: Junction ID Format and Layout Stability

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_014` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter, the DOT IDs, the junction nodes and the junction numbering of the exported graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 93861fe2b59913fc ai** · Statement hash `93861fe2b59913fc`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Synthetic junction nodes MUST use IDs of the form `j_&lt;transitionSanitized>__&lt;kind>_&lt;idx>`, where:<br><br>`transitionSanitized` is the transition's name with non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters replaced by `_` (the same `sanitize` function used for place and transition IDs).<br><br>`&lt;kind>` is `xor` or `and`.<br><br>`&lt;idx>` is a non-negative integer. Junctions in a single transition's `Out` tree are numbered in depth-first pre-order, with the counter starting at `0` and incrementing once per emitted junction. Single-child XOR/AND groups collapse (per EXP-012) and consume no counter slot. Example: `t_Nested` with output `AND(XOR(a,b), XOR(c,d))` produces three junctions in the order `j_Nested__and_0`, `j_Nested__xor_1`, `j_Nested__xor_2`.<br><br>Junction IDs do not collide with place IDs (`p_…`) or transition IDs (`t_…`).<br><br>*Where* a node's name (the place's, the transition's, or for a junction its transition's) holds only ASCII characters, the mapper *shall* give the node the ID `p_&lt;s>`, `t_&lt;s>` or `j_&lt;s>__&lt;kind>_&lt;idx>` according to what it stands for, with `&lt;s>` that name with each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced by `_`, `&lt;kind>` the kind of the junction and `&lt;idx>` its index written in decimal without leading zeros.<br><br>The ID of a node whose name holds a character outside ASCII is implementation-defined, within the rule of the next sentence.<br><br>The mapper *shall* give no junction node the ID of a place node or a transition node, whatever the names.<br><br>*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw for each transition one junction node for each group with two or more children in its output spec, of the kind of that group, and no other junction node for the transition.<br><br>*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* give the junction node of a group with two or more children the index of that group in the depth-first pre-order of such groups in the transition's output spec, counting from 0, with one counter for both kinds.<br><br>*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, the mapper *shall* draw as the output edges of a transition, compared by their ends, exactly the edges [EXP-012] draws for its output spec, each as often as [EXP-012] draws it, with each junction numbered by the index of its group.<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw no edge that starts or ends at a junction node it does not draw.<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw no junction node for a transition the net does not have.<br><br>The mapper *shall* give a junction node of kind `xor` the `xor-junction` category of the node table and a junction node of kind `and` the `and-junction` category.<br><br>*Where* the transition names of a net are pairwise distinct, its place and transition names hold only ASCII characters, and no two different place names, nor two different transition names, become equal when each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` is replaced by `_`, the mapper *shall* give no two nodes of the graph the same ID.<br><br>AC1 covers the junctions of transitions whose name is not empty and holds only ASCII characters. | 1. For every configuration cfg and net X, the graph E cfg X satisfies:<br>2. every node whose name (the place's, the transition's, or for a junction its transition's) is ASCII has the ID nodeId of what junction nodes of each transition t, as (kind, index), are the kinds of the groups of t's output spec with two or more children in depth-first pre-order, numbered 0, 1, 2 in that order, one node per **Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the typed graph (nodes with reference, ID, category and labels; edges; clusters) a configuration and a net are drawn as, before DOT text. The node references (place, transition, junction (t, kind, index)) are the graph's own data; this block constrains the IDs it gives them, the junction indices and kinds it uses, the transition a junction node belongs to, the category of a junction node and the ends of the output edges. Every other attribute of a node or edge is another block's subject (EXP-001 to EXP-013).
- The ID function is the glossary's nodeId over sanitize, which keeps an ASCII letter, digit or underscore and replaces every other character by an underscore, and writes the index with toString (decimal, no leading zeros). By ruling D46 (a) the first line binds only nodes whose name is ASCII: on other names the runtimes differ (Rust keeps every Unicode letter and digit, Java replaces per code point as the model does, TypeScript per UTF-16 code unit, so a character outside the basic plane becomes two underscores) and the spec leaves them implementation-defined, which is the plain sentence quoted after the first shall sentence.
- The sixth line is guarantee 1 and the second shall sentence, for every name: all three runtimes keep the prefixes p_, t_ and j_ for every name, so a junction ID, which starts with j_, is no place or transition ID. Without it a mapper that writes non-ASCII names verbatim, without a prefix, meets every other line and gives the transition Ü and its junction one ID (EXP_014_forbids_rawNonAscii, exp014_rawNonAscii_rest). The reference meets it by EXP_014_guarantee1.
- The second and third lines restate the numbering bullet and the third, fourth and fifth shall sentences: the junction nodes of a transition are one per group with two or more children, of that group's kind (and for And, xor for Xor, which the spec's example implies and the third shall sentence states), the index of a junction is the position of its group in the pre-order of those groups (OutTree.junctions, which skips a short group, so a collapsed group consumes no counter slot), and the output edges are exactly the edges of EXP-012's drawing rule wired to those indices, so an extra, missing or repeated output edge breaks the third line (EXP_014_forbids_dupOutEdge). EXP-012 compares junctions and edges only up to a one-to-one renumbering; these two lines fix the renumbering to the identity. Both lines read a transition by its name, so they are stated on nets with pairwise distinct transition names, which every net that builds has and which the shall sentences state as their condition; the input-arc half of X.Distinct (CORE-030) plays no part here.
- The third line reads the output side by arc type: an output or reset+output edge from the transition or one of its junctions. An edge from a junction drawn with another arc type escapes it but not the fourth line, which still requires its junction end to be drawn; arc types are EXP-012's subject and the export agreement's (ExportAgrees).
- The fourth line is the sixth shall sentence: an edge whose end is a junction no node stands for would make Graphviz invent an unstyled node with a junction ID. Ghost edges (EXP-017) are included.
- The seventh line is the shall sentence on junction nodes for a transition the net does not have, for every net. Lines 2 and 3 read the junctions of each transition of X by its name, so without the seventh line an exporter that adds a junction node for a name no transition of X has (a junction left over from an earlier export, say) meets lines 1 to 6 on every net and draws a junction on a net with no output spec at all (EXP_014_forbids_strayJunction, exp014_strayJunction_rest). With line 2 on nets with distinct transition names, and with the junction clause of the export agreement (ExportAgrees, glossary), it carries EXP-012's 'and no other junction node' from one output spec to the whole graph. All three mappers make a junction node only while walking the output spec of a transition of the net (emit_output in the Rust crate libpetri-export, emitOutput in PetriNetGraphMapper.java and petri-net-mapper.ts), as the reference does.
- The eighth line is the shall sentence on the category of a junction node, and EXP-012's 'Style category xor-junction' and 'Style category and-junction' attributes: a junction node of kind k has the row JKind.cat k of the node table (Libpetri.Export.Styles, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json). Java and TypeScript set the category from the kind (PetriNetGraphMapper.java, petri-net-mapper.ts); Rust draws the XOR_JUNCTION or AND_JUNCTION style by kind (mapper.rs), which is that row. An exporter that swaps the two rows violates it (EXP_014_forbids_junctionCatSwap). The other junction attributes (shape, glyph, size, font) are the table's constants and kind Q, as EXP-012 says.
- The fifth line is the uniqueness shall sentence, the uniqueness that 'uniquely determined' claims, under the name assumption of ruling D46 (a) (kind A, ExportNet.IdNames, on a net with pairwise distinct transition names): ASCII names, and no two place names nor two transition names equal after sanitize. Without it two names such as b1/x and b1_x get one ID in every runtime. A place and a transition never share an ID (prefixes p_ and t_), and a junction ID is no place or transition ID (prefix j_) and determines its transition's sanitised name, kind and index (EXP_014_junctionId_inj, by reading the ID from its end: the index has no underscore, the kind word is three letters after a double underscore). Ruling D46 (a) also names non-empty names; uniqueness does not need that (an empty place name, an empty transition name and their junctions still get the IDs p_, t_ and j___<kind>_<idx>), so ExportNet.IdNames leaves it out and only AC1 is scoped to non-empty names. The assumption's 'no empty / segment' clause is EXP-016's and plays no part here.
- The 'uniquely determined by the depth-first traversal' clause of the flat-counter paragraph is the second and third lines.
- AC1 (all junction IDs match j_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__(xor|and)_[0-9]+) follows from the first line, for every exporter meeting EXP-014, for a junction of a transition whose name is non-empty and ASCII (EXP_014_ac1), which is what the last quoted plain sentence scopes AC1 to. An empty transition name builds in every runtime and gives j___xor_0, which the regex rejects; a non-ASCII name gives an implementation-defined ID, and Rust's j_é__xor_0 does not match the regex either.
- Guarantee 2 and AC2 (two exports of one net are byte-equal) have no content over a Lean function, which is deterministic; across processes they fail today for Java and Rust (HashSet order, ruling R2 (exp-b)); kind Q. Guarantee 3 and AC3 (Java, TypeScript and Rust exports are byte-equal) are a property of three programs and kind Q by ruling D60 (c); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The order of nodes and edges is not stated (List.Perm), only the numbering the spec pins.
- The test derivation (export twice and diff; export in three languages and diff) is AC2 and AC3, kind Q. EXP_014_nonvacuous decides the spec's example AND(XOR(a,b), XOR(c,d)) on t Nested, a deeper tree that separates pre-order from breadth-first numbering, a collapsed group, sanitised place, transition and junction IDs, and a junction ID apart from the transition ID on a non-ASCII name, on the reference.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.EXP_014_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.EXP_014): The clustered reference exporter `refExport` (the witness of the export consistency theorem) meets EXP-014 (`EXP_014_any` at the reference cluster stage).
  <pre>EXP_014 refExport</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.EXP_014_forbids_badWiring` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.EXP_014): ✗ Wiring every edge to index 0 violates EXP-014 on `AND(XOR(a, b), c)` (line 4: the edge from the and junction into the xor junction ends at `j_T__xor_0`, which no node stands for).
  <pre>¬EXP_014 exp014_badWiring</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-EXP_016"></a>
## EXP-016: Subnet Instance Cluster Subgraphs

`Libpetri.Spec.EXP_016` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter, the clusters of the exported graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/09-export.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 2fc6972b040c7f87 ai** · Statement hash `2fc6972b040c7f87`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| DOT export of a net produced by modular composition (per [MOD-020]) SHOULD emit a `subgraph cluster_&lt;sanitizedKey>` block grouping each subnet's nodes.<br><br>**Subnet-membership metadata** ([MOD-026]) carried by a directly-composed net — a node mapped to subnet `S` clusters under `cluster_&lt;sanitize(S)>`; a shared (multi-subnet) place has no entry and is not grouped by metadata.<br><br>**Instance-prefix detection** — a node whose name begins with `&lt;prefix>/` (the separator established by [MOD-010]) clusters under `cluster_&lt;sanitize(prefix)>`. Nested instance prefixes (per [MOD-013]) MUST produce nested cluster subgraphs.<br><br>When the net carries membership metadata the exporter SHOULD prefer it and fall back to instance-prefix detection for any node without an entry, so direct and instance composition coexist.<br><br>The cluster source MAY be caller-selectable (metadata-only, prefix-only, or no clustering); the default SHOULD be metadata-when-present.<br><br>The sanitization function applied to the key MUST match the existing DOT ID sanitization per [EXP-014] (non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters, including `/`, replaced by `_`). The cluster `label` attribute SHOULD carry the original (un-sanitized) key string for human readability.<br><br>This requirement does NOT alter the styling, junction, or arc rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it adds grouping structure only. A net with neither composed instances nor membership metadata (no `/` in any node name) MUST produce no cluster subgraphs.<br><br>The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter draws cluster subgraphs at all. For an exporter that draws them, every MAY, SHOULD and MUST sentence of this requirement reads as *shall*: it lets the caller select each cluster source named above, takes the default source when the caller selects none, and follows the sentences below.<br><br>Under the default cluster source the cluster key of a place or a transition is its membership entry when it has one and otherwise its instance prefix; under the metadata-only source it is the membership entry alone, under the prefix-only source the instance prefix alone, and under no clustering there is none. The instance prefix of a name is the part before its last `/`; a name without `/`, or whose only `/` is its first character, has none. A junction node has the cluster key of its transition. A node without a cluster key is a top-level node. A `/`-prefix of a key is the non-empty beginning of the key up to, and not including, one of its `/` characters.<br><br>These sentences cover nets whose place names and transition names are ASCII, in which no two place names and no two transition names become equal under the sanitization of [EXP-014], and in which every cluster key of a place or transition name is ASCII, non-empty and has no empty `/`-segment: it neither starts nor ends with `/` and holds no `//`. On other nets the clustering, and whether it changes the nodes and edges drawn, is implementation-defined.<br><br>The mapper *shall* make each node that has a cluster key a direct member of the cluster of that key and of no other cluster, and a top-level node a member of no cluster.<br><br>The mapper *shall* list as a member of a cluster only a node it draws, and, on a net whose transition names are pairwise distinct, list each such node at most once.<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw exactly one cluster for each cluster key of a drawn node and for each `/`-prefix of such a key, and no other cluster.<br><br>The mapper *shall* nest each cluster directly in the cluster whose key is the part of its own key before the last `/`, and draw a cluster whose key has no `/` at the top level.<br><br>The mapper *shall* give the cluster of key K the ID `cluster_` followed by K with each character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_]` replaced by `_`, and the label K.<br><br>The mapper *shall* draw, in any order, the same nodes, and the same edges other than the ghost edges of [EXP-017], as it draws for the same net and configuration under no clustering. | 1. For every configuration cfg and net X that meets the name assumption (ExportNet.ClusterNames: EXP-014's ExportNet.IdNames, ASCII place and transition names with no two place names and no two transition names equal after sanitize, and every cluster key of a place or transition name of X under cfg.cluster ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment), with key the glossary's nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member (membership entry, else instancePrefix, per cluster source; a junction takes its transition's key), the graph E cfg X satisfies:<br>2. every drawn node is a direct member of a cluster exactly when the cluster's key is the node's key (so a node with a key is in the cluster of its key and no other, and a node without a key is in no cluster);<br>3. every member of a cluster is the reference of a drawn node, and when the transition names of X are pairwise distinct no cluster lists a member twice;<br>4. a string is the key of a cluster exactly when it is the key of a drawn node or a /-prefix of such a key (IsSlashPrefix: a non-empty initial segment of the key that is followed by / in it);<br>5. no two clusters have the same key;<br>6. the parent of every cluster is the instance prefix of its key (the part before its last /, none without one);<br>7. every cluster has the ID clusterId of its key (cluster_ followed by sanitize of the key) and its key as label;<br>8. the nodes are those E draws for cfg with cluster source none, and the edges other than ghost edges are those E draws for cfg with cluster source none, each up to order (List.Perm: the same multiset, every field of each node and edge included). | <pre>fun E ↦<br>  ∀ (cfg : ExportCfg) (X : ExportNet),<br>    ExportNet.ClusterNames cfg.cluster X →<br>      (∀ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,<br>          ∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters,<br>            n.ref ∈ c.members ↔ nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member n.ref = some c.key) ∧<br>        (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters,<br>            (∀ r ∈ c.members, ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes, n.ref = r) ∧<br>              ((List.map ExportTrans.name X.trans).Nodup → c.members.Nodup)) ∧<br>          (∀ (q : String),<br>              q ∈ List.map XCluster.key (E cfg X).clusters ↔<br>                ∃ n ∈ (E cfg X).nodes,<br>                  ∃ K,<br>                    nodeKey cfg.cluster X.member n.ref = some K ∧<br>                      (q = K ∨ IsSlashPrefix q K)) ∧<br>            (List.map XCluster.key (E cfg X).clusters).Nodup ∧<br>              (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters, c.parent = instancePrefix c.key) ∧<br>                (∀ c ∈ (E cfg X).clusters, c.id = clusterId c.key ∧ c.label = c.key) ∧<br>                  (E cfg X).nodes.Perm<br>                      (E<br>                          { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,<br>                            showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,<br>                            showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env,<br>                            cluster := ClusterSource.none }<br>                          X).nodes ∧<br>                    (List.filter (fun e ↦ e.arc != ArcType.ghost) (E cfg X).edges).Perm<br>                      (List.filter (fun e ↦ e.arc != ArcType.ghost)<br>                        (E<br>                            { dir := cfg.dir, showTypes := cfg.showTypes,<br>                              showIntervals := cfg.showIntervals,<br>                              showPriority := cfg.showPriority, env := cfg.env,<br>                              cluster := ClusterSource.none }<br>                            X).edges)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): the typed graph a configuration and a net are drawn as, before DOT text. Clusters are the graph's XCluster list (key, ID, label, parent key, direct members). Which subgraph block an edge is written in (deepest_common_prefix in the runtimes), cluster styling and the order of sibling clusters are properties of the DOT text, not stated (ruling R2 (exp-b) on order); the block states membership, nesting, IDs and labels.
- The key rule is a fixed glossary definition (clusterKey, nodeKey, instancePrefix in Spec/GlossaryExportCluster.lean), the same three lines in all three mappers (cluster_key_of in Rust, autoClusterKeyOf and its switch in TypeScript, PetriNetGraphMapper in Java), so a mapper with another key rule breaks the first and third lines: the first-/ key (EXP_016_forbids_firstSlash), metadata only under the default source (EXP_016_forbids_metadataDefault), MOD-040's subnetOf walk-up used for clustering (EXP_016_forbids_walkUp; MOD-040 itself says the exporter still clusters s1/obs/TURN under s1/obs) and junctions left at the top level (EXP_016_forbids_junctionTop).
- The membership bullet, the prefix bullet and the fall-back sentence are the key rule under the default source auto. By ruling D26 item 7 a shared place has no membership entry and is therefore not grouped by metadata; under the default source it falls back to its instance prefix like every node without an entry, so it is at the top level only when its name has no instance prefix (the old wording 'stays top-level' contradicted the fall-back sentence). The junction sentence is ruling D26 item 5 (all three mappers put a junction in its transition's cluster).
- The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter clusters at all (ruling D26 item 7: the MUST sentences inside a SHOULD requirement read 'an exporter that clusters shall'). The scoping sentence extends that reading to the MAY and SHOULD sentences: for an exporter that clusters, 'MAY be caller-selectable', 'the default SHOULD be metadata-when-present', 'SHOULD prefer it and fall back' and 'the cluster label attribute SHOULD carry the original key' are obligations, as the block states them (all three runtimes meet them). The model takes the caller's choice as cfg.cluster and the statement quantifies over all four sources, so an exporter that ignores the choice fails the first and third lines; the glossary's ExportCfg defaults cfg.cluster to auto (metadata when present, else the prefix), which is the default-source sentence. An exporter that never draws clusters does not meet the predicate and is outside the requirement.
- Ruling D46 (a) with (x), kind A: the block covers nets that meet ExportNet.ClusterNames. Its first half is EXP-014's name assumption ExportNet.IdNames (ASCII names, no two place names and no two transition names equal after sanitize). The first line depends on it: all three runtimes look a node's key up by its DOT ID (node_id_to_prefix in Rust, nodeIdToPrefix in Java and TypeScript), so on b1/t from b1/x to b1_x the two places are one node p_b1_x, which no exporter can put both in cluster_b1 and at the top level (exp016_collide_outside); under IdNames the ID is one to one on the nodes the reference draws (exp014_nodeId_inj), so looking a key up by ID finds the node's own key. Its second half (ExportNet.ClusterKeysWellFormed, over the declared places, the places the arcs touch and the transition names of X) is that every cluster key is ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment. The ASCII half is needed because a membership key is a subnet name (MOD-026), not a node name, so it can hold other characters while every node name is ASCII; Rust's sanitize keeps Unicode letters (ruling D46 (a) makes them implementation-defined), so for a key Größe Rust draws the cluster ID cluster_Größe where Java and TypeScript draw cluster_Gr__e, and the sixth line, which states the ID through the glossary's ASCII sanitize, would bind Rust on a character D46 leaves open (exp016_nonAsciiKey_outside). On a key with an empty segment (a name such as a//x, /a/x or http://host/x) all three mappers register the glossary's keyChain, every non-empty /-prefix followed by / and then the key itself (register_prefix_chain in Rust, registerPrefixChain in Java and TypeScript), and route an edge by the longest entry of one key's chain that is in the other's, so they draw the clusters the reference draws and neither panic nor throw (exp_016_key_with_empty_segment_registers_its_key_chain in Rust, partitionRegistersTheKeyChainOfAKeyWithAnEmptySegment_EXP016 in Java, the EXP-016 empty-segment test of typescript/tests/export/cluster-builder.test.ts, and python/tests/test_dot_export.py). A Rust chain that skipped the empty segment and never registered the key, the Java failure on a key with a leading or trailing /, and the TypeScript failure on a key with a leading / or the empty key, are the behaviour RD-12 recorded. The empty-segment half of the premise is there because the scope sentence of the requirement excludes such keys. Dropping it needs that sentence reworded in the markdown and the lines checked there, on a key with a leading / (no instance prefix, so a top-level cluster) and on the empty membership key (cluster ID cluster_, outside AC5's pattern). The Unicode cluster ID is implementation-defined under ruling D46 (a), and the lookup by DOT ID is the Known limit sentence of EXP-016. On a net outside the assumption the whole predicate is silent, the seventh line included. The reference model stays total there (the reference builder of Reference/ExportCluster.lean registers the keyChain of Spec/GlossaryExportCluster.lean, which holds the key and its parent).
- Two membership keys whose sanitised forms are equal (a/b and a_b) get one cluster ID; the sixth line states that ID as the runtimes draw it, and no line depends on the keys' sanitised forms being distinct.
- The second line's at-most-once half (EXP_016_forbids_dupJunction) carries the premise that the transition names of X are pairwise distinct, as EXP-014's uniqueness line does: two transitions with one name draw one node reference twice, and the members of a cluster list each drawn reference in node order.
- The sixth line is the sanitisation sentence and the label sentence: sanitize is EXP-014's (each character outside [A-Za-z0-9_], / included, replaced by _). The seventh line is 'does NOT alter the styling, junction, or arc rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it adds grouping structure only' together with the last shall sentence: ghost edges are excluded because EXP-017 adds them only when there are clusters (export design, skeptic correction S-4), and EXP-017 itself keeps the visible edge set. The statement reads ghost edges as the glossary's ArcType.ghost, so the [EXP-017] in the shall sentence is a citation, not a dependency (EXP-017 depends on EXP-016); likewise MOD-040 in the Depends-on line is a spec cross-reference (MOD-040, wave W8, cites this block), not a Lean import. 'MUST produce no cluster subgraphs' on a net without metadata and without / is a consequence of the first and third lines (EXP_016_ac4).
- AC1 (cluster_b1 and cluster_b2 for instances b1 and b2) and AC3 (cluster_outer containing cluster_outer_inner) are decided on the reference in EXP_016_nonvacuous, and follow from the third, fifth and sixth lines for every exporter meeting the block. AC2, restated by ruling D26 item 5 to count nested cluster blocks and the junctions of a cluster's transitions, follows from the first and third lines (EXP_016_ac2): a node is inside the cluster of K, directly or through a nested cluster, exactly when its key is K or has K as a /-prefix.
- AC4 (no / in any node name and no membership metadata gives no cluster) is EXP_016_ac4, for every exporter meeting the block on a net meeting EXP-014's name assumption. AC5: the regex half (cluster_[A-Za-z0-9_]+) is EXP_016_ac5 for every cluster with a non-empty key, and the name assumption makes every key of the net's names non-empty; the determinism half has no content over a Lean function, which is deterministic, and is kind Q. AC6 (Java, TypeScript and Rust produce byte-identical cluster blocks) is a property of three programs and kind Q by ruling D60 (c); the runtimes differ today in the order of sibling clusters (ruling R2 (exp-b)). AC7, restated by ruling D26 item 7 to shared places whose names carry no instance prefix, is the first line under a membership map, decided on a directly composed net in EXP_016_nonvacuous.
- The test derivation (compose two instances, nested instances and a direct composition; assert blocks, members and sanitised IDs) is AC1, AC3, AC2, AC5 and AC7 on composed nets; how compose builds names and the membership map is MOD-010, MOD-013 and MOD-026 on the composition model (W8), and the block quantifies over every net and membership map the mapper can see.

## EXP-017: Compound Cluster Layout Hints

**Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from a configuration (with its cluster source, EXP-016) and the export view of a net (with its membership map, MOD-026), the typed graph a mapper builds before DOT text. The block reads the compound attribute, the nodes in their order and the edges in their order; a ghost edge is an edge of arc type ghost, and of it the block reads its source, target, ltail and lhead.
- The cluster key of a node is EXP-016's (nodeKey: the membership entry, else the part of the name before its last /, per cluster source; a junction has its transition's key). So the key of a node is its deepest cluster: outer/inner/a to an orphan to other/b bridges (outer/inner, other) and not (outer, other), and outer/a to an orphan to outer/inner/b bridges a cluster to its own child (ruling D26 item 6; exp_b probe cases 8 and 9; exp017NetE in EXP_017_nonvacuous, EXP_017_forbids_skipNested). The sentence 'Orphan paths that fall entirely inside a single cluster (X == Y)' compares keys, not the drawn boxes: both ends of outer/a to o to outer/inner/b lie inside the box of outer, yet the keys differ and the pair is bridged, as the quoted sentence on nested clusters says. Graphviz may warn about and ignore ltail and lhead when one cluster contains the other, so such a ghost edge may constrain less than a ghost edge between two sibling clusters; whether to keep drawing it is a feature question outside the migration. A place shared by two subnets of a direct composition has no membership entry and no prefix, so it is an orphan too. Cluster IDs are compared as EXP-016 draws them (clusterId, cluster_ followed by the sanitised key).
- Ruling D46 (a) with (x), kind A: lines 2 to 5 cover the nets EXP-016 covers, as the scope sentence of the requirement says: nets that meet ExportNet.ClusterNames under cfg's cluster source (EXP-014's name assumption, and every cluster key ASCII and non-empty with no empty /-segment). The compound line binds every net, since its sentence says 'in every export'. On other nets the runtimes do not draw what lines 2 to 5 would ask. All three look a node's key up by its DOT ID (node_id_to_prefix in Rust, nodeIdToPrefix in Java and TypeScript), so on a net where b1/t outputs to b1_x, b2/u consumes b1_x and b1/v consumes b1/x, the place b1/x gives the shared ID p_b1_x the key b1, the orphan b1_x is not seen as an orphan, and no runtime draws the ghost edge for (b1, b2) that the bridges keyed by node reference ask for. On a non-ASCII membership key Rust draws a cluster ID that the glossary's clusterId does not give. The Unicode cluster ID is implementation-defined under ruling D46 (a), and the lookup by DOT ID is the Known limit sentence of EXP-016; the block is silent on such nets. A key with an empty segment (a name such as a//x) is outside the premise only because EXP-016's scope sentence excludes it: all three mappers register the key chain the reference draws there (see EXP-016). Inside the premise a cluster key may hold the NUL character (it is ASCII), and the block binds on such nets. All three mappers dedup ghost edges by the ordered pair: Rust keys by the (String, String) pair, Java by List.of(X, Y), and TypeScript by the string of the length of X, a colon, X and Y, which no two pairs share (ghostEdgesDedupByOrderedPair_nulInKeyDoesNotMerge_EXP017 in Java, the EXP-017 ordered-pair test of typescript/tests/export/cluster-builder.test.ts). A dedup by the string X, NUL, Y (the behaviour RD-37 recorded) merges the distinct pairs (a NUL b, c) and (a, b NUL c) and draws one ghost edge where the second line asks for two (EXP_017_forbids_nulDedup on exp017NulNet). The reference meets the block without the premise (EXP_017_reference does not use it), and every mutant below fails it on a net that meets the premise.
- Bridges are read over the drawn edges of every arc type in the direction drawn (ruling D26 item 6), as all three mappers scan them: a reset edge into an orphan place and a read edge out of it bridge two clusters although no token moves between them (exp_b probe case F, EXP_017_forbids_tokenFlow), and an orphan transition whose output spec has a junction bridges nothing through it, since its junction is itself an orphan whose only incoming edge leaves the keyless transition. Whether these should change is a feature question outside the migration. The ghost edges are left out of the scan; they join two nodes with keys, so they would bridge nothing anyway, and the quoted definition of an edge leaves them out, so the definition does not refer to itself.
- The scan order is the graph's own node and edge order, so the first bridge depends on the order the exporter draws its nodes and edges, which differs between the runtimes (ruling R2 (exp-b)) and is stated by no requirement. The block fixes the anchors relative to the drawn order, which is what each mapper computes.
- Order of the ghost edges is not stated: the second and third lines are membership statements and the fourth line counts, so the ghost edges are compared up to order. Order of the other edges is not stated either: the fifth line compares them with the edges drawn under cluster source none up to order (List.Perm), the visible edge set of the body, as EXP-016's seventh line does. The first bridge is read in the order of the graph drawn under cfg, so an exporter that draws its edges in another order when it clusters anchors at the first bridge of that order.
- The style of a ghost edge (style invis, arrowhead none) is a visual constant of the DOT renderer, checked by tests (kind Q); so is the claim that the line is a no-op for flat nets in Graphviz. That ghost edges change no cluster membership is EXP-016's (its members are read off node keys, not edges); the fifth line states that they change no other edge.
- The header says SHOULD and the body MUST; the EARS sentences read an exporter that clusters shall (ruling D26 item 7). The SHOULD priority is whether an exporter clusters at all. The predicate is what an exporter that clusters draws: its bridges are read off the cluster keys (nodeKey under cfg's cluster source and X's membership map), which are the clusters an exporter meeting EXP-016 draws, not off the clusters the exporter happens to draw. An exporter that never draws clusters does not meet it on a net with a bridge and is outside the requirement, as in EXP-016. With cluster source none no node has a key, so there is no bridge and, by the third line, no ghost edge.
- AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC7 are EXP_017_nonvacuous on the reference exporter: every export has compound true, a flat net has no ghost edge (AC1, AC7); the net exp017NetA has three orphan transitions bridging (left, right), one bridging (right, left), one with left on both sides and one with a single clustered neighbour, and gets exactly two ghost edges, one per direction, anchored at the first bridge (AC2 to AC6). AC2's literal net, exp017NetAC2 (left and right bridged by one orphan transition), gets exactly one ghost edge with ltail cluster_left and lhead cluster_right.
- AC8 (anchor selection matches across Java, TypeScript and Rust byte for byte) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (export design P3, ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration. The test derivation is AC2 to AC7.

X).edges,<br>            e.arc ≠ ArcType.ghost →<br>              e.row = Export.EdgeRow.matchInput →<br>                e.arc = ArcType.input ∧<br>                  ∃ t ∈ X.trans,<br>
