**Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (glossary): from an export configuration (glossary ExportCfg) and a net as the exporter reads it (glossary ExportNet), the typed graph the runtimes' mappers build before DOT text (glossary XGraph). An edge (glossary XEdge) carries its ends, its arc type (glossary ArcType), its style row (Libpetri.Export.EdgeRow, generated from spec/petri-net-styles.json) and its label. A transition (glossary ExportTrans) carries in corr the places its ν-net match specification correlates (NU-020), empty without one; NU-020 makes every correlated place an input place of the transition, which is why the lines speak of input arcs only. The DOT text and its attribute syntax are not modelled.
- Relay targets: corr holds the places of match keys only, never the relay targets of NU-054, as in every runtime: each mapper decorates an input when the correlates test of the match specification holds, and that test checks match keys only, never relay keys. So line 4 forbids drawing a relay edge (an output edge to a relay target) with the match-input row, as it forbids any teal output edge (EXP_018_forbids_outTeal); NU-054's API note is reworded to agree (spec edit NU-054-relay-export).
- Colour: the colour bullet (#0d9488, teal, the match-input edge style in spec/petri-net-styles.json, distinguishing the edge from a plain input edge) is read as the match-input style row: an edge names a row of the generated style table and the colour is the row's. EXP_018_nonvacuous decides on the table that the match-input row has colour #0d9488 and that the input row has another colour (#333333). Which hex value the DOT text carries for a row is kind Q (the style generator's gate).
- Arc type: all three mappers keep the arc type of a correlated edge as input and change only its style row, so line 1 asks for an edge of arc type input for every input arc, correlated or not, and a mapper that changes the arc type of a correlated edge (EXP_018_forbids_arcRead) or drops the edge (EXP_018_forbids_dropCorr) violates the block. Line 1 overlaps EXP-001's line on input edges and follows from the first halves of lines 2 and 3; it is kept as the line of the first EARS sentence, which states the arc type apart from the decoration, and the two mutants it names also fail the first half of line 2.
- Labels: the cardinality label is EXP-006's, in the forms ruling D41 (a) pins (×n, *, ≥m, none for One), the function refCardLabel; the correlated label is glossary corrLabel: ⟨n⟩ (U+27E8, n, U+27E9) alone when the cardinality label is none, else ⟨n⟩, one space and the cardinality label. A correlated One edge is therefore labelled ⟨n⟩ and nothing else (EXP_018_forbids_trailingSpace); EXP-006's AC2 ('One cardinality has no cardinality label') names the cardinality label (ruling D41 (a), clash exp-a#6), and ⟨n⟩ is not one, so the ⟨n⟩ label does not contradict it.
- Lines 2 and 3 have two halves each. The first half holds on every net: some input edge from the place of the arc to the transition has the row and the label. The reference meets it on every net, since it draws refInputEdge t s for every input arc s of every transition t. The second half asks the same of every input edge with those ends, and only on nets whose transitions have distinct names and at most one input arc per place (glossary ExportNet.Distinct): the exporter keys transition nodes by name, so with two transitions of one name, or two input arcs of one transition on one place, two arcs would share the ends of one edge and the half could ask two labels of it. Line 4 needs no such condition.
- No builder gives ExportNet.Distinct to every net. Distinct transition names are the reading of CORE-020 (a name identifies the transition, see TIME-010); no runtime's net builder rejects two transitions of one name, and only composition does (MOD-025). One input arc per place is CORE-030's transition builder check, with the implementation's own Place equality (CORE-002), and in Java that equality is name-and-type (the MOD-024 divergence note).
- On a net that is not Distinct the first halves still bind. A mapper that looks up a transition's match specification by its name, last write wins, draws a correlated input plain when a later transition of the same name has no match; the first half of line 2 rejects it (EXP_018_forbids_lastWinsCorr). With the two transitions in the other order it decorates an uncorrelated input; the first half of line 3 rejects it (EXP_018_forbids_lastWinsUncorr). A Java transition with two input arcs on places of one name and different types, only one of them correlated, is modelled as two input arcs on one place, both correlated, because the exporter names a place node by the place name: the first half of line 2 asks for one decorated edge, which Java draws, and Java's second, plain edge is not ruled out.
- The second halves are needed on top of the first: an exporter that draws the decorated edge of a correlated input and also a plain copy of it meets the first half of line 2 and violates the second (EXP_018_forbids_dupPlain).
- 'Non-correlated inputs of the same transition are unaffected' is line 3: the edge keeps the input row and the plain cardinality label, so a mapper that decorates every input of a transition that has a match violates the block (EXP_018_forbids_allInputs), and so does one that keeps the input row of an uncorrelated input but writes ⟨n⟩ before its label (EXP_018_forbids_uncorrPrefix). Line 3 binds every uncorrelated input of every transition, including a transition with no match specification (corr empty), not only the other inputs of a transition with a match. For those it restates the input row of EXP-001 and the cardinality label of EXP-006, so it adds no obligation beyond them; it is what every runtime draws. 'No other edge changes' is line 4 for the style row: no output, inhibitor, read or reset edge, and no input edge of an uncorrelated place, is drawn with the match-input row (EXP_018_forbids_outTeal). Ghost edges (EXP-017) are drawn invisible and their style row is that requirement's, so line 4 excludes them. A label on another edge that happens to start with ⟨n⟩ (an Xor branch label of a place so named) is not ruled out: the label lines speak of input edges only.
- The sentence 'The decoration is a mapper concern: it is emitted into the DOT by every exporter, so the canonical viewer and all three doc generators render it identically with no viewer change.' is a design note on where the decoration is computed: the block is a predicate over the exporter, which is that mapper, and what the viewer and the doc generators render from the DOT is kind Q.
- No configuration option changes the decoration in any runtime, so the lines hold for every configuration.
- AC1 (an input edge to a correlated place has color #0d9488 and a label beginning with ⟨n⟩) is line 2 with the colour reading above; line 2 asks for the whole label, so the literal reading 'begins with ⟨n⟩' is weaker and a mapper that writes ⟨n⟩×2 without the space meets it but not this block (EXP_018_forbids_noSpace). A mapper that writes ⟨n⟩ only when a cardinality label exists draws a correlated One edge with no label and violates line 2 (EXP_018_forbids_optionMap).
- AC2 (a non-correlated input edge on the same transition keeps the default color and no ⟨n⟩ prefix) is line 3.
- AC3 (the label combines with cardinality as ⟨n⟩ ×n, ⟨n⟩ *, ⟨n⟩ ≥m) is line 2 with EXP-006's pinned forms; a mapper that replaces the cardinality label by ⟨n⟩ violates it (EXP_018_forbids_replace).
- AC4 (the emitted DOT for a ν-net is byte-identical across the Java, TypeScript and Rust exporters) is kind Q: a Lean function is deterministic and cross-language equality is a property of three programs (ruling D60 (c)); the export corpus EP-2 replays the reference against the runtimes after the migration.
- The test derivation (a join with match correlating two One inputs, both correlated edges teal and labelled ⟨n⟩, a third non-correlated input unchanged) is EXP_018_nonvacuous on the reference, with a second transition whose correlated Exactly(2), All and AtLeast(3) inputs show ⟨n⟩ ×2, ⟨n⟩ * and ⟨n⟩ ≥3 next to an uncorrelated Exactly(2) input labelled ×2.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_001"></a>
## IO-001: Input One

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_001` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 749a74beaedb4a3d ai** · Statement hash `749a74beaedb4a3d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `One(place)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both 1.<br><br>*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the input place of a `One` input arc is marked and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.<br><br>*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly 1 token from the input place.<br><br>*When* a transition with a `One` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly 1 fewer token than it held before the firing. | 1. For every transition t and place p such that the input arc of t on p is One:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;<br>3. from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire;<br>4. unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + 1 = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly 1 token, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + 1 = m(p): p loses exactly 1 token, whatever deposit the firing reports. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    InputArc t p Card.one →<br>      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>            Marked m p →<br>              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (io001_withoutInput t p) m m')) ∧<br>          (¬ResetArc t p →<br>            ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>              F t m d m' →<br>                m' p + 1 = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + 1 = m p))</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enables' are both read as 'some firing exists'.
- Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the third quoted sentence excludes a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), on which the arc also requires a token of the chosen name. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second line quantifies over every `One` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.
- The first quoted sentence and the bullets (`requiredCount()` returns 1, `consumptionCount(available)` returns 1) are IO-007's contract for `One`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second and third lines, the consumption count the fourth. The bullet values themselves are `io001_counts`.
- AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line (not with 0 tokens) and the third line (with >= 1 token the arc does not stand in the way; whether the other arcs allow the firing is theirs to say, IO-005 and CORE-022).
- AC2 (exactly 1 token consumed on firing) is the fourth line for the count. Which token is consumed (the oldest) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.
- AC3 (remaining tokens stay in the place) is the fourth line: p holds m(p) - 1 tokens plus the firing's deposit there afterwards.
- Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses 1 and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the consumed token is not visible in the marking; the fourth line excludes that case.
- The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed token shows in the marking alone, as exactly 1 token fewer. Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of 1 in the input place would pass the count.
- The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc), and t without its input arc on p drops that arc only; CORE-030 rejects a second input arc on p at build.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_001_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_001): The reference semantics satisfies IO-001: `Seam.enabledNA` requires the `One` place to hold `Card.required .one = 1` token, so `t` does not fire with it unmarked, and with it marked the arc's conjunct of `enabledNA` holds, so dropping the arc changes no enablement (and every output spec offers a deposit); `Seam.nconsumed` takes 1 from it, and `Seam.fireNC` of a non-reset place is "minus consumed, plus deposited", where the deposit is empty outside the output spec's places.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_001 RefFire</pre>

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_001_forbids_idle` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_001): ✗ A firing that consumes nothing violates IO-001 (third clause): `io001_t` fires from the marking with one token in place `0` and leaves that token there.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_002"></a>
## IO-002: Input Exactly

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_002` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 96c1d96e85a20f1e ai** · Statement hash `96c1d96e85a20f1e`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `Exactly(place, n)` is an input arc whose required count and consumption count are both N, where N >= 1.<br><br>*While* the input place of an `Exactly(n)` input arc holds fewer than N tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume exactly N tokens from the input place.<br><br>*When* a transition with an `Exactly(n)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither a reset place nor an output place of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing holding exactly N fewer tokens than it held before the firing. | 1. For every transition t, place p and count N such that the input arc of t on p is Exactly(N):<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than N tokens;<br>3. unless p is also a reset place of t, every firing of t from m that deposits d and leaves m' has m'(p) + N = m(p) + d(p): p loses exactly N tokens, besides what the firing deposits there; and if p is not an output place of t either, m'(p) + N = m(p): p loses exactly N tokens, whatever deposit the firing reports. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),<br>    InputArc t p (Card.exactly n) →<br>      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p &lt; n, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (¬ResetArc t p →<br>          ∀ (m : N → ℕ) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            F t m d m' →<br>              m' p + n = m p + Deposits d p ∧ (¬OutputArc t p → m' p + n = m p))</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking with its deposit (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Enables' is read as 'some firing exists'.
- The first quoted sentence (required count N, consumption count N; the bullets `requiredCount()` returns N and `consumptionCount(available)` returns N) is IO-007's contract for `Exactly(n)`. Here it is observed through firing: the required count is the second line, the consumption count the third. The bullets' qualifier 'when available >= N' is implied: by the second line no firing starts with fewer.
- AC1 (construction with N < 1 rejected, also when the transition is built from a spec written out without the constructor) is a property of construction, not of firing, so this formula does not encode it: its build half is the block IO_002_build in this file (every transition with an Exactly(0) input arc fails to build), and its constructor half is Q-tested there. The formula here quantifies over every N, N = 0 included; for N = 0 both lines hold of the reference semantics trivially, so the restriction N >= 1 neither weakens nor strengthens what is checked about firing.
- AC2 (enables only when the place has >= N tokens) and AC4 (N-1 tokens, not enabled) are the second line. The converse ('enables when the place has >= N tokens', given the other arcs allow it) is the AND-join of IO-005 and CORE-022, not this block's subject.
- AC3 (exactly N consumed on firing, the N oldest, FIFO) is the third line for the count; its second part (the fourth quoted sentence) states it without the deposit for an input place that is neither a reset place nor an output place. Which tokens are consumed (the oldest, FIFO) is below the count granularity of the firing semantics and is the glossary's reading of Consume (CORE-030); it is not encoded here.
- Consumption is observed through the marking: p loses N and gains what the firing deposits there (p may also be an output place). A place that is both the input place and a reset place of t ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), so the N tokens consumed are not visible in the marking; the third line excludes that case, as the fourth quoted sentence does.
- The deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count: on a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so there the consumed tokens show in the marking alone, as exactly N tokens fewer (the fourth quoted sentence, IO-001's guard). Without this a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit of N in the input place would pass the count, and the block would lean on CORE-035 to stand.
- Deposits are counts per place (glossary: Deposit, [CORE-036]): `Deposits d p` counts the tokens d puts in p and ignores their order. The build-time output-spec checks of IO-011 to IO-014 (ambiguity, one Timeout, ForwardInput only under a Timeout) and the validation skip of CONC-026 do not touch input consumption, so the formula quantifies over every transition, built or not, and every executor.
- The input arc of t on p is the first input arc on p (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a second one at build.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_002_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_002): The reference semantics satisfies IO-002: `Seam.enabledNA` requires the input place of an `Exactly(n)` arc to hold `Card.required (.exactly n) = n` tokens, and `Seam.nconsumed` takes `n` from it, so a place that is not a reset place loses `n` and gains the deposit, which is empty outside the output spec's places.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_002 RefFire</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_002_build"></a>
## IO-002: Input Exactly

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_002_build` · Kind **F** · Scope all transition builders · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ff47291b5f476312 ai** · Statement hash `ff47291b5f476312`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Construction with N &lt; 1 is rejected (error or panic). Where the language lets the spec be written out without the constructor (a public enum variant, an object literal), building the transition rejects it. | 1. For the transition builder Build (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg):<br>2. every transition t one of whose input arcs is Exactly(0) fails to build. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, s.card = Card.exactly 0 → Build t ≠ none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Build is the transition builder read as the message it rejects a transition with (none: the transition builds), as in IO-011, IO-013 and EXEC-012; the witness is the reference builder refBuild (glossary: Build-time checks), whose count check (InputCountsPositive, stand-in message msgCount) rejects an input arc that requires fewer than one token. The cardinality of the model (Card) is a value written out directly, so a transition carrying Exactly(0) is the spec written out without the constructor: the second quoted sentence. N ranges over the naturals, so N < 1 is N = 0.
- The first quoted sentence (the constructor rejects N < 1 with an error or a panic) is not encoded: the model has no constructor, only the value. It is Q-tested: Rust exactly() asserts count >= 1 (rust/libpetri-core/src/input.rs:53, test at :174), TypeScript exactly() throws (typescript/src/core/in.ts:47, typescript/tests/core/in.test.ts:33), Java's Exactly record constructor throws IllegalArgumentException (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Arc.java:96), which is also the only way to write the value in Java. Python reaches the Rust constructor.
- The second quoted sentence is the line. The runtimes whose spec can be written out without the constructor check it when the transition is built: Rust for the public In::Exactly variant (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:391-402, tests at :1369 and :1376), TypeScript for an object literal (the input-count check in TransitionBuilder.build in typescript/src/core/transition.ts, test 'build rejects an input that requires no token' in typescript/tests/core/transition.test.ts). A builder without the count check (io002_buildNoCount) builds such a transition and is forbidden (IO_002_build_forbids_noCount).
- Only the failure is stated, not its message: the spec gives the check no message, and the reference fails it with the stand-in msgCount. That a transition whose input arcs all require at least one token, and which passes the other build-time checks, does build is CORE-020's line 4 (Builds includes InputCountsPositive), so a builder that rejects every transition meets this line and breaks that one. The order of the count check against CORE-030's input-arc check is not stated (the reference runs CORE-030's first); EXEC-012's line 5 orders its own check after both.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_002_build_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_002): ✓ The reference builder satisfies the build block: a transition with an `Exactly(0)` input arc fails `InputCountsPositive`, so it does not pass `Builds`, and `refBuild` rejects exactly the transitions that do not (`refBuild_eq_none_iff`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N], IO_002_build refBuild</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_002_build_forbids_noCount` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_002): ✗ A builder without the count check violates the build block: it builds `io002_t0`, whose input arc is `Exactly(0)`.
  <pre>¬IO_002_build io002_buildNoCount</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_002_build_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_002): The build block is exercised by the reference builder: `io002_t0` has an `Exactly(0)` input arc, and building it fails with the count check's stand-in message.
  <pre>(∃ s ∈ io002_t0.core.inputs, s.card = Card.exactly 0) ∧ refBuild io002_t0 = some msgCount</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_003"></a>
## IO-003: Input All

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_003` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f3ab08fa5c1929cf ai** · Statement hash `f3ab08fa5c1929cf`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the place of an `All` input arc of a transition is marked and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the `All` input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, it *shall* consume every token from the place of each of its `All` input arcs that is not a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]).<br><br>*When* a transition fires, the place of each of its `All` input arcs that is neither an output place of the transition nor a correlated input of its match specification *shall* end the firing empty. | 1. For every transition t and every place p on which t has an `All` input arc:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p is unmarked;<br>3. from a marking in which p is marked, t can fire exactly when t without its `All` input arcs on p can fire;<br>4. every firing of t that deposits d leaves p holding exactly the tokens d puts there;<br>5. if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    AllArc t p →<br>      (while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>            Marked m p → ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutAll t p) m m')) ∧<br>          (∀ (d : List N),<br>              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>            (¬OutputArc t p →<br>              ∀ (d : List N), on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ m' p = 0)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing to some marking exists'.
- Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second, third and fourth quoted shall sentences exclude a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), where an `All` arc consumes the tokens of the chosen name only and leaves the others, as the section's last sentence says. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second to fourth lines quantify over every `All` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.
- The first two lines together say that the `All` arc requires exactly one token: `requiredCount()` returns 1 (the first bullet; `Card.required .all = 1`).
- 'Consume every token' is read through the place's count after the firing: p ends holding only what this firing deposited in p, so it kept none of its own tokens. This is the second bullet, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`. A firing that also deposits into p (p is an output place of t) leaves those tokens in p.
- AC1 (enables when the place has >= 1 token) is the second line: with p marked the `All` arc removes no firing. AC3 (0 tokens, not enabled) is the first line. AC2 (all tokens consumed, place empty after) is the third line, with 'empty' read as 'empty apart from this firing's own deposit into p', and the fourth line, where p is not an output place and 'empty' is literal.
- The fourth line is the guard IO-001 also carries: it does not trust the deposit a firing reports. On a place that t's output spec does not name (glossary: Output arc) no firing can deposit (CORE-035, CORE-063), so there the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it, a firing that keeps p's tokens and reports them as its own deposit into p would pass the third line. The fourth line stands alone: it needs neither the third line nor CORE-035.
- A reset arc on p does not weaken the fourth line: the spec sentence has no reset exclusion, and a reset place that is not an output place ends holding what the firing deposited there (CORE-034), which is nothing.
- Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): the lines read the count `Deposits d p` and the marking's count at p, never the order of d.
- Which token is consumed first, and that the consumed tokens reach the action, are below the count granularity of a firing relation; they are not encoded.
- A firing is one step at the count granularity: EXEC-003 AC5 (an `All` or `AtLeast` arc that fires later in a firing pass drains only the tokens the firing may drain, and leaves in place the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass) is below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject and the reference executor's (RefExec, wave W5), not this block's.
- A transition with two input arcs on p is rejected at build by CORE-030. On such a transition the formula reads the first arc on p, as the reference does (`InputArc`); `withoutAll` removes only the `All` arcs on p.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_003_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_003): The reference semantics satisfies IO-003: `Seam.enabledNA` asks `Card.required .all = 1` token of an `All` place, so the transition does not fire while it is unmarked and the arc asks nothing more while it is marked; `Seam.nconsumed` takes every token of an `All` place, so the place ends with only what the firing deposited there (`refFire_apply`); and a reference firing deposits only in output places, so an `All` place that is not one ends empty.

| *While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds fewer than `minimum` tokens, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the input place of an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc holds at least `minimum` tokens and is not a correlated input of the transition's match specification ([NU-020]), the input arc *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire.<br><br>*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, it *shall* consume every token the input place holds, unless the input place is a correlated input of its match specification ([NU-020]).<br><br>*When* a transition with an `AtLeast(place, minimum)` input arc fires, and the input place is neither an output place nor a correlated input of the match specification of the transition, the input place *shall* end the firing empty. | 1. For every transition t, place p and number n such that the input arc of t on p is AtLeast(p, n):<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which p holds fewer than n tokens;<br>3. from a marking m in which p holds at least n tokens, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arc on p can fire from m;<br>4. every firing of t, with whatever deposit d, leaves p holding exactly the tokens d deposited there (every token p held was consumed);<br>5. if p is not an output place of t, every firing of t leaves p empty, whatever deposit the firing reports. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N) (n : ℕ),<br>    InputArc t p (Card.atLeast n) →<br>      (while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p &lt; n, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>            n ≤ TokenCount m p →<br>              ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputArc t p) m m')) ∧<br>          (∀ (d : List N),<br>              on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>            (¬OutputArc t p →<br>              ∀ (d : List N),<br>                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦ TokenCount m' p = 0)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' is read as 'some firing from m exists', whatever marking it leads to: removing the arc changes what the firing consumes from p, so only whether t fires is compared, not where it leads.
- Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second, third and fourth quoted shall sentences exclude a correlated input of a ν-net match specification (NU-020), where an `AtLeast` arc requires and consumes the tokens of the chosen name only, as the section's last sentence says. The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so every input place is one that is not a correlated input, and the second to fourth lines quantify over every `AtLeast` input arc. How a correlated input counts and consumes is NU-020's, not encoded here.
- 'The input arc on p' is the first input arc on p, as the glossary term Input arc reads it; `withoutInputArc` removes that one arc. [CORE-030] allows at most one input arc per place, so on a well-formed transition it is the only one.
- AC1 (construction with minimum < 1 is rejected, also when building a transition from a spec written out without the constructor) is a property of construction, not of firing, so this formula does not encode it: its build half is the block IO_004_build in this file (every transition with an AtLeast(0) input arc fails to build), and its constructor half is Q-tested there. The statement here quantifies over every n, n = 0 included; the reference semantics satisfies it there too (AtLeast(p, 0) never blocks and drains p).
- AC2 (transition enables when the place has >= minimum tokens) is the second line: with p holding at least n tokens the arc does not stop t from firing. Read with [IO-005], the other arcs of t still decide.
- AC3 (all tokens consumed on firing, not just minimum) is the third line, stated on the marking the firing leaves: p ends holding what was deposited there and nothing it held before. A reset arc on p ([CORE-034]) gives the same end count, so neither the third nor the fourth line needs a reset guard.
- The fourth line is the guard IO-001 carries, so the block stands alone: the deposit a firing reports is not trusted for the count. On a place the output spec of t does not name, no firing of t can deposit ([CORE-035]), so the drain shows in the marking alone, as an empty place. Without it a firing that consumes nothing but reports a deposit in p equal to what p held would pass the third line.
- AC4 (place with minimum - 1 tokens, transition not enabled) is the first line, at the count minimum - 1.
- A firing is one step at the count granularity: EXEC-003 AC5 (an `All` or `AtLeast` arc that fires later in a firing pass drains only the tokens the firing may drain, and leaves in place the tokens a synchronous action deposited earlier in the same pass) is below this granularity; that refinement is EXEC-003's subject and the reference executor's (RefExec, wave W5), not this block's.
- The two bullets (`requiredCount()` returns `minimum`, `consumptionCount(available)` returns `available`) are the pure-function contract of [IO-007] and the glossary terms Required count and Consumption count; this block encodes their effect on firing (lines 1 to 4), not the functions themselves.
- The output-spec build checks ([IO-011] to [IO-014]) and the output validation skip ([CONC-026]) do not touch input consumption; the block holds of every firing relation over every transition, built or not.

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_004_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_004): The reference semantics satisfies IO-004: `Seam.enabledNA` requires `requiredCount` = `n` tokens in `p` (first line); with `p` holding that many, the arc's test passes, so removing it leaves enablement unchanged, and whether the output spec offers an outcome does not depend on consumption (second line); `Seam.nconsumed` takes every token of an `AtLeast` place, so `p` ends with its deposit (third line); and a reference firing deposits only in places the output spec names, so outside them that deposit is empty and `p` ends empty (fourth line).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_004_build"></a>
## IO-004: Input AtLeast

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_004_build` · Kind **F** · Scope all transition builders · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 c73d27504afc359b ai** · Statement hash `c73d27504afc359b`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Construction with minimum &lt; 1 is rejected (error or panic), also when building a transition from a spec written out without the constructor, as for [IO-002]. | 1. For the transition builder Build (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg):<br>2. every transition t one of whose input arcs is AtLeast(0) fails to build. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), ∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, s.card = Card.atLeast 0 → Build t ≠ none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Build is the transition builder read as the message it rejects a transition with (none: the transition builds), as in IO-011, IO-013, EXEC-012 and IO_002_build; the witness is the reference builder refBuild (glossary: Build-time checks), whose count check (InputCountsPositive, stand-in message msgCount) rejects an input arc that requires fewer than one token. The cardinality of the model (Card) is a value written out directly, so a transition carrying AtLeast(0) is the spec written out without the constructor. The minimum ranges over the naturals, so minimum < 1 is minimum = 0.
- The quoted sentence has two halves. Its build half ('also when building a transition from a spec written out without the constructor') is the line. Its constructor half ('Construction with minimum < 1 is rejected (error or panic)') is not encoded, as the model has no constructor, only the value; it is Q-tested: Rust at_least() asserts minimum >= 1 (rust/libpetri-core/src/input.rs:71, test at :181), TypeScript atLeast() throws (typescript/src/core/in.ts:60, typescript/tests/core/in.test.ts:71), Java's AtLeast record constructor throws IllegalArgumentException (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Arc.java:114), which is also the only way to write the value in Java. Python reaches the Rust constructor.
- The runtimes whose spec can be written out without the constructor check it when the transition is built: Rust for the public In::AtLeast variant (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:391-402), TypeScript for an object literal (the input-count check in TransitionBuilder.build in typescript/src/core/transition.ts). A builder without the count check (io004_buildNoCount) builds such a transition and is forbidden (IO_004_build_forbids_noCount).
- Only the failure is stated, not its message: the spec gives the check no message, and the reference fails it with the stand-in msgCount. That a transition whose input arcs all require at least one token, and which passes the other build-time checks, does build is CORE-020's line 4 (Builds includes InputCountsPositive), so a builder that rejects every transition meets this line and breaks that one.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_004_build_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_004): ✓ The reference builder satisfies the build block: a transition with an `AtLeast(0)` input arc fails `InputCountsPositive`, so it does not pass `Builds`, and `refBuild` rejects exactly the transitions that do not (`refBuild_eq_none_iff`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N], IO_004_build refBuild</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_004_build_forbids_noCount` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_004): ✗ A builder without the count check violates the build block: it builds `io004_t0`, whose input arc is `AtLeast(0)`.
  <pre>¬IO_004_build io004_buildNoCount</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_004_build_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_004): The build block is exercised by the reference builder: `io004_t0` has an `AtLeast(0)` input arc, and building it fails with the count check's stand-in message.
  <pre>(∃ s ∈ io004_t0.core.inputs, s.card = Card.atLeast 0) ∧ refBuild io004_t0 = some msgCount</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_005"></a>
## IO-005: Input AND-Join Semantics

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_005` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 566c1a17d5cf3f37 ai** · Statement hash `566c1a17d5cf3f37`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* any input place of a transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* every input place of a transition that has no match specification ([NU-020]) holds at least the required count of its input arc, the input arcs *shall not* affect whether the transition can fire. | 1. For every transition t:<br>2. for every input arc s of t, t does not fire from a marking in which the input place of s holds fewer tokens than the required count of s;<br>3. from a marking m in which every input place of t holds at least the required count of its input arc, t can fire from m exactly when t without its input arcs can fire from m. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs,<br>        while fun m ↦ TokenCount m s.place &lt; requiredCount s.card, never Fire F t) ∧<br>      ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>        (∀ s ∈ t.core.inputs, requiredCount s.card ≤ TokenCount m s.place) →<br>          ((∃ m', Fire F t m m') ↔ ∃ m', Fire F (withoutInputs t) m m')</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part. 'Can fire' and 'enabled' are both read as 'some firing exists' (to some marking): the input arcs change what a firing consumes, so the second line compares whether t fires, not where it leads.
- Correlated inputs (ruling D30, extending D16): the second quoted shall sentence is scoped to a transition that has no match specification; a transition with one also needs a name of which every correlated input holds at least its required count of tokens (NU-020). The transitions of the model (Reference.Trans) carry no match specification, so the second line quantifies over every transition. The first quoted shall sentence needs no exclusion: a correlated input that holds fewer tokens than its required count holds fewer tokens of any one name.
- The opening sentence ('All inputs on a transition are AND-joined: every input arc is a precondition, and all of them must hold in the same marking.') is the two lines together: line 1 makes each input arc a precondition (t does not fire while any one of them is unsatisfied), and both lines fix the single marking m the firing starts from, so 'all of them must hold in the same marking' is read as 'every input arc is satisfied in m'.
- Input arcs are read from the transition's list of input arcs, every one of them. A transition with two input arcs on one place, which [CORE-030] rejects at build, is gated by both.
- AC1 (a transition with 3 inputs enables only when all 3 places have sufficient tokens) is the first line, for any number of input arcs, 3 included; the test derivation's 'satisfy all 3; verify enabled' is the second line together with a transition that, without its input arcs, can fire (no read or inhibitor arc blocks it).
- AC2 (any one input unsatisfied disables the transition) is the first line.
- How many tokens an input arc requires (requiredCount) is IO-001 to IO-004 and IO-007, not this block: the statement takes requiredCount as given.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): The reference semantics satisfies IO-005: `Seam.enabledNA` requires every input arc's required count, so an unsatisfied input arc disables the transition; with every input arc satisfied the remaining conditions (read and inhibitor arcs) are those of the transition without its input arcs, and an enabled transition can always fire.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_005 RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_forbids_inputsAlwaysBlock` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): ✗ Input arcs that block their transition although all of them are satisfied violate IO-005 (second clause): `io005_t` cannot fire from `io005_all`, but without its input arcs it can.
  <pre>¬IO_005 io005_inputsAlwaysBlockFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_forbids_orJoin` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): ✗ An OR-join violates IO-005 (first clause): `io005_t` fires with two of its three input arcs satisfied.
  <pre>¬IO_005 io005_orJoinFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_mutant_dropSatisfied_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): The always-blocking input arcs kill the second mutant: they satisfy the mutant (a transition with an input arc never fires) but not IO-005.
  <pre>IO_005_mutant_dropSatisfied io005_inputsAlwaysBlockFire ∧<br>  ¬IO_005 io005_inputsAlwaysBlockFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_mutant_dropUnsatisfied_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): The OR-join kills the first mutant: it satisfies the mutant (with every input arc satisfied, the OR-join's condition holds and the firing is that of the transition without its input arcs) but not IO-005.
  <pre>IO_005_mutant_dropUnsatisfied io005_orJoinFire ∧ ¬IO_005 io005_orJoinFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_005_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_005): Both clauses of IO-005 are exercised by the reference semantics on AC1's transition: with two of its three input arcs satisfied `io005_t` does not fire (first clause, place `2` short of its required count), although without its input arcs it does; with all three satisfied it fires, as it does without its input arcs (second clause).
  <pre>io005_twoOfThree 2 &lt; requiredCount Card.all ∧<br>  (∀ (m' : ℕ → ℕ), ¬Fire RefFire io005_t io005_twoOfThree m') ∧<br>    Fire RefFire (withoutInputs io005_t) io005_twoOfThree<br>        (io005_after (withoutInputs io005_t) io005_twoOfThree) ∧<br>      (∀ s ∈ io005_t.core.inputs, requiredCount s.card ≤ io005_all s.place) ∧<br>        Fire RefFire io005_t io005_all (io005_after io005_t io005_all) ∧<br>          Fire RefFire (withoutInputs io005_t) io005_all<br>            (io005_after (withoutInputs io005_t) io005_all)</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_007"></a>
## IO-007: requiredCount and consumptionCount Contract

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_007` · Kind **F** · Scope all input cardinalities · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 1860eb65b8a890ff ai** · Statement hash `1860eb65b8a890ff`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The required count *shall* be 1 for `One` and `All`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `m` for `AtLeast(m)`.<br><br>*While* `available` is at least the required count, `consumptionCount(available)` *shall* return 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)` and `available` for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.<br><br>*If* `consumptionCount(available)` is called with `available` less than the required count, *then* the call *shall* fail with an error. | 1. requiredCount() is 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), 1 for All and m for AtLeast(m);<br>2. for every cardinality c and every available ≥ requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) returns 1 for One, n for Exactly(n), available for All and available for AtLeast(m);<br>3. for every cardinality c and every available &lt; requiredCount(c), consumptionCount(available) fails (none). | <pre>fun K ↦<br>  (∀ (c : Card),<br>      K.required c =<br>        match c with<br>        \| Card.one => 1<br>        \| Card.exactly n => n<br>        \| Card.all => 1<br>        \| Card.atLeast m => m) ∧<br>    (∀ (c : Card) (a : ℕ),<br>        K.required c ≤ a →<br>          K.consume c a =<br>            some<br>              (match c with<br>              \| Card.one => 1<br>              \| Card.exactly n => n<br>              \| Card.all => a<br>              \| Card.atLeast n => a)) ∧<br>      ∀ (c : Card), ∀ a &lt; K.required c, K.consume c a = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A contract is the pair of functions of one implementation; a call that raises (an exception, a panic, an assertion failure) is read as `none`, a call that returns `k` as `some k`. Which error is raised, and its message, are not part of the statement.
- AC1 (each variant returns the values of the table) is the first two lines: the first line is the requiredCount column, the second the consumptionCount column on every call the third line allows.
- AC2 (calling consumptionCount with insufficient tokens is an error) is the third line.
- The counts n and m range over all naturals. That Exactly(n) and AtLeast(m) are built only with n, m ≥ 1 is IO-002 AC1 and IO-004 AC1, not this block's subject; the table holds for 0 too.
- '(matching) tokens' in the definition of requiredCount() is read at the granularity of a token count: which tokens of a place count as matching (the ν correlation of NU-020) is decided before the count reaches these functions, so `available` is already the matching count.
- That an executor calls consumptionCount only on an enabled transition, where every input place holds its required count, is enablement (CORE-022, IO-005), not this block's subject; that a firing removes exactly consumptionCount(available) tokens is CORE-030's subject (glossary: Consume, bridge lemma `consumes_eq`).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): The reference contract satisfies IO-007: `Card.required` is the requiredCount column, `consumptionCount` (`available` where `Card.consumesAll`, else `Card.required`) is the consumptionCount column, and the guard makes every call below the required count fail.
  <pre>IO_007 ioRefContract</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_forbids_allNeedsNothing` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): ✗ An `All` that needs no token violates IO-007 (first line): its requiredCount is 0, not 1; with it, firing an `All` arc from an empty place would be enabled.
  <pre>¬IO_007 io007_allNeedsNothing</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_mutant_dropConsumption_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): The minimum-taking `AtLeast` kills the second mutant: it meets the mutant (required counts and failures as the table says) but not IO-007 (`AtLeast(1)` with 2 available returns 1, not 2).
  <pre>IO_007_mutant_dropConsumption io007_atLeastTakesMinimum ∧<br>  ¬IO_007 io007_atLeastTakesMinimum</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_mutant_dropError_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): The contract that never fails kills the third mutant: it meets the mutant (both columns are right) but not IO-007 (`One` with 0 available returns 1 instead of failing).
  <pre>IO_007_mutant_dropError io007_neverFails ∧ ¬IO_007 io007_neverFails</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_mutant_dropRequired_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): The contract that requires nothing kills the first mutant: it meets the mutant (the consumption column is right and no call is below a required count of 0) but not IO-007 (`One` requires 0 tokens, not 1).
  <pre>IO_007_mutant_dropRequired io007_requiresNothing ∧ ¬IO_007 io007_requiresNothing</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_007_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_007): Every line of IO-007 is exercised by the reference contract, and the contract is the one the reference firing uses: `AtLeast(2)` requires 2, returns `available` (3) with 3 available and fails with 1; `Exactly(2)` returns 2 with 3 available; and a reference firing of an `AtLeast(2)` arc from a place holding 3 consumes `consumptionCount(3) = 3`, draining it.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_010"></a>
## IO-010: Output place (leaf)

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_010` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with output validation enabled (the default) · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 43da83ca0e74b3ef ai** · Statement hash `43da83ca0e74b3ef`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `Place(place)` is a leaf node of an output spec that names a single output place.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall* deposit one or more tokens in `place`.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, it *shall not* deposit a token in any other place.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `Place(place)` fires, the marking the firing leaves *shall* hold in `place` the tokens the firing deposited there, in addition to the tokens `place` kept through the firing.<br><br>This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]). | 1. For every transition t whose output spec is the leaf Place(p), and every deposit d:<br>2. every firing of t that deposits d puts at least one token in p;<br>3. every firing of t that deposits d puts no token in any place other than p;<br>4. every firing of t that deposits d, from m to m', leaves p holding at least what p kept (nothing if t has a reset arc on p, else m p minus what t consumed from p) plus what d put in p. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (p : N),<br>    OutputSpec t = some (Out.place p) →<br>      ∀ (d : List N),<br>        (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ Produced d p) ∧<br>          (on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ∀ (q : N), Produced d q → q = p) ∧<br>            on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>              (if ResetArc t p then 0 else TokenCount m p - Consumes t m p) +<br>                  Deposits d p ≤<br>                TokenCount m' p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The firing relation F is that of an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026). An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled deposits whatever the action wrote, its Place leaf included, so it may write nothing; CONC-026 lifts IO-010 for it, and the evidence below shows that such an executor's firing relation (io010_skipFire) does not satisfy IO-010 (IO_010_forbids_skip), which is why the scope is stated.
- A transition whose output spec is the leaf Place(p) passes every build-time check of its output spec (IO-011 to IO-014: one place, no Timeout, no ForwardInput, one output branch), so the statement ranges over transitions that build; no well-formedness hypothesis is needed.
- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails, by an action exception or by IO-015 validation, deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.
- The statement covers a transition whose whole output spec is the leaf. A Place leaf inside And, Xor or Timeout contributes its claim {place} to an output branch (IO-015); what that branch must receive is the subject of IO-011, IO-012, IO-013 and IO-015, not of this block.
- 'One or more tokens' is read on the deposit (glossary: Produced set): p is in the produced set. How many tokens beyond one is not constrained: an output branch is a set of places, and several tokens into p conform (IO-015, IO-016 AC4, CORE-036); the reference semantics deposits exactly one (IO-016). Deposits are compared per place (Deposits d p, Produced d p), never by list order (CORE-036).
- The second clause (nothing outside p) reads 'a single output place' together with IO-015's exact-explanation rule: the produced set of a firing of a Place(p) spec is exactly {p}.
- AC1 (output spec declares a single place) is structural and holds by construction: the leaf names one place, outPlaces (Place p) = [p] (checked by example below); the statement's hypothesis selects exactly these transitions.
- AC2 (produced tokens appear in the place) is the first clause on the deposit and the third clause on the marking. The third clause is a lower bound: it rules out a lost write (the firing reports [p] but leaves p as it was) and a misrouted write (the token lands in another place), also when p already holds tokens. The exact count of p (no extra tokens) is [CORE-030]'s on an input place, [CORE-034]'s on a reset place and [CORE-035]'s third line on every other place; tokens appearing in other places are [CORE-035]'s.
- 'The tokens place kept' is the glossary's effect of a firing on one place: a reset place keeps none [CORE-034], an input place keeps its count minus the consumption count [CORE-030], [IO-007], any other place keeps its count. Inhibitor and read arcs consume nothing [CORE-031], [CORE-032].

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): The reference semantics satisfies IO-010: a firing of a transition whose output spec is `Place(p)` deposits `[p]` (`deposit_place_leaf`), one token in `p` and nothing elsewhere, and `Seam.fireNC` adds that token to what `p` kept (`refFire_apply`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], IO_010 RefFire</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_allows_multi` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✓ Several tokens into the leaf's place conform (an output branch is a set of places, IO-015, IO-016 AC4, CORE-036): a firing that deposits `[p, p]` satisfies every clause of IO-010.
  <pre>IO_010 io010_multiFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_forbids_idle` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✗ A firing that deposits nothing violates IO-010 (first clause): `io010_t` fires from the empty marking with an empty deposit, so place `0` receives no token.
  <pre>¬IO_010 io010_idleFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_forbids_lost` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✗ A lost write violates IO-010 (third clause), also when the leaf's place already holds tokens: `io010_t` reports `[0]` from the marking with one token in place `0` and leaves it there, so place `0` holds 1 token where it must hold at least 1 + 1.
  <pre>¬IO_010 io010_lostFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_forbids_misroute` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✗ A misrouted write violates IO-010 (third clause), also when the leaf's place already holds tokens: `io010_t` reports `[0]` from the marking with two tokens in place `0`, but the token lands in place `1`, so place `0` holds 2 tokens where it must hold at least 2 + 1.
  <pre>¬IO_010 io010_misrouteFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_forbids_skip` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✗ The skip executor is outside IO-010's scope (CONC-026): its firing relation lets `io010_t` fire from the empty marking with the empty write, so the first clause fails. This is why IO-010 is scoped to executors with output validation enabled.
  <pre>¬IO_010 io010_skipFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_forbids_spill` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): ✗ A firing that writes a second place violates IO-010 (second clause): `io010_t` deposits `[0, 1]`, and place `1` is not its leaf's place.
  <pre>¬IO_010 io010_spillFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_mutant_dropMarking_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): The lost write kills the third mutant: it reports the deposit `[p]`, so the mutant holds, but it leaves the marking unchanged, so IO-010 does not.
  <pre>IO_010_mutant_dropMarking io010_lostFire ∧ ¬IO_010 io010_lostFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_mutant_dropOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): The spilling firing kills the second mutant: it always writes the leaf's place, so the mutant holds, but it also writes the next place, so IO-010 does not.
  <pre>IO_010_mutant_dropOnly io010_spillFire ∧ ¬IO_010 io010_spillFire</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_mutant_dropProduces_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): The idle firing kills the first mutant: an empty deposit writes nowhere else, so the mutant holds, but it does not put a token in the leaf's place, so IO-010 does not.
  <pre>IO_010_mutant_dropProduces io010_idleFire ∧ ¬IO_010 io010_idleFire</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_010_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_010): All three clauses of IO-010 are exercised by the reference semantics: `io010_t` has the leaf `Place(0)` as its output spec, it fires from the empty marking depositing `[0]` (so the clauses' trigger happens and place `0` receives a token), the deposit names place `0` only, and the marking it leaves holds that token in place `0` (the conclusions are checked on a real firing, not vacuously).
  <pre>OutputSpec io010_t = some (Out.place 0) ∧<br>  RefFire io010_t io010_empty [0] io010_after ∧<br>    Produced [0] 0 ∧<br>      (∀ (q : ℕ), Produced [0] q → q = 0) ∧<br>        TokenCount io010_empty 0 + Deposits [0] 0 ≤ TokenCount io010_after 0</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_011"></a>
## IO-011: Output And

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_011` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026) · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 7b09ae3f76121963 ai** · Statement hash `7b09ae3f76121963`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `And(children)` is a node of an output spec that represents a parallel fork in which all children are active.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `And(children)` fires and its action completes, every child, with nested `And`s flattened, *shall* have received tokens: the produced set contains a place that the child names.<br><br>The same holds for an `And` nested in the alternative that an inner `Xor` chose: the produced set *shall* equal, on the places the output spec names, one output branch of the output spec.<br><br>That output branch is unique, because the output branches of a spec that builds are pairwise distinct sets ([IO-012]).<br><br>This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).<br><br>*If* a single output branch (one choice at every `Xor`, with nested `And`s flattened) names the same place twice, *then* the output spec *shall* be rejected, with<br><br>*If* the output spec names a place twice in one output branch, *then* `&lt;P>` in the message *shall* be the place that the following walk of the spec reports first, so that every implementation names the same place:<br><br>A `Place(P)` node and a `ForwardInput(from, P)` node name `P`.<br><br>A `Timeout` node walks its child and names the places its child names.<br><br>An `Xor` node walks its children left to right.<br><br>*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `Xor` *shall* report that place.<br><br>Otherwise the `Xor` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.<br><br>An `And` node walks its children left to right.<br><br>*If* a child reports a place, *then* the `And` *shall* report that place.<br><br>Otherwise, *if* a place the child names, taken in the order the walk first met them, is already named by an earlier child, *then* the `And` *shall* report the first such place.<br><br>Otherwise the `And` names the places its children name, each once, in the order the walk first meets them.<br><br>The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice, because the alternatives of an `Xor` under an `And` are chosen independently of the `And`'s other children. | 1. Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and F the firings.<br>2. For every transition t whose output spec o names a place twice in one output branch (DupBranch), building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct, it fails with IO-011's message for t and the place p the walk of o reports (firstDup o = some p, msgDup t p).<br>3. For every transition t that builds (Builds) whose output spec is an And node o with no Timeout node in it:<br>4. for every child c of o (nested Ands flattened) and every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d produces some place that c names;<br>5. for every deposit d, every firing of t that deposits d has as its produced set, on the places o names, exactly the places of the output branch at one index of o's branch list, and of no branch at any other index (IO_011_uniqueBranch).<br>6. F is the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build F ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),<br>      OutputSpec t = some o →<br>        DupBranch o →<br>          Build t ≠ none ∧<br>            (PreOutputChecks t →<br>              ∀ (p : N), firstDup o = some p → Build t = some (msgDup t p))) ∧<br>    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),<br>      OutputSpec t = some (l.and r) →<br>        Builds t →<br>          (l.and r).findTimeout = none →<br>            (∀ c ∈ andChildren (l.and r),<br>                ∀ (d : List N),<br>                  on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦ ChildReceived d c) ∧<br>              ∀ (d : List N),<br>                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>                  IO_011_uniqueBranch (l.and r) d</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (Build, F). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the witness is the reference builder refBuild, which runs the build-time checks of the Output Composition preamble in order (glossary: Build-time checks). The build error is msgDup, byte for byte: the message of the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' with <t> the transition's name and <P> the place the walk reports. The preamble does not place the CORE-030 input-arc check among the output-spec checks; refBuild runs it first, so on a transition with two input arcs on one place the build line only requires that building fails.
- The walk is firstDup, through dupScan, clause for clause: steps 1 and 2 are its place, forward and timeout clauses, step 3 its xor clause (xorJoin: the first child's report, else the second's, else the places of both, each once, in first-seen order), step 4 its and clause (andStep at each child: the child's report, else the first place the child names that an earlier child of the And names, else the child's places join the pool). The reference Out is binary: an n-ary And or Xor is right-nested, and dupScan walks a .and met as a child of a .and as part of its parent, so the children of And(c1, ..., cn) are walked as the n-ary node's children. A spec with an And written as a direct child of an And is the one shape the binary Out cannot tell from the flat n-ary node; on it the builders walk the inner And first, the loader's walk (Load.dupWalk, over the spec as written) does the same, and firstDup reads the flat node.
- 'The walk reports a place exactly when some output branch names a place twice' is the theorem firstDup_eq_none_iff, and the place it reports is named twice in some output branch (firstDup_some); the build line therefore names a place exactly when it rejects a duplicate. AC5's And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) names B (IO_011_ac5); naming the first place repeated in the first repeating output branch, in IO-016 order, would name A, and that builder violates the build line (IO_011_forbids_firstBranchName).
- 'Which place the message names' is a constraint on the message only: which transitions build is the first build line together with the other build-time checks, and IO-013's third line ties Builds to the builder.
- Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.
- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails validation (AC3) deposits no outcome and is not a firing here.
- Scope: 'applies to an executor with output validation enabled' is read as a restriction on the model: F is the firing relation of such an executor. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled is not an F this block speaks of; what it does (an And(A, B) firing that deposits only A, CONC-026 AC4) is exactly what io011_leftOnlyFire models, and this block forbids it of a validating executor (IO_011_forbids_leftOnly).
- Scope: the statement quantifies over transitions that build. Building runs the checks of the Output Composition preamble (WellFormedOut: no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every ForwardInput's from an input place, no two output branches at different indices with the same set of places). CORE-022 applies to transitions that build, and a definition the checks reject is not a transition of any net. Build reads one transition definition, so the construction paths that reach the builder are not encoded.
- The reference semantics reads an n-ary And as right-nested binary `Out.and` nodes; `andChildren` flattens them back, so the children of And(A, B, C) are A, B and C. Flattening is the recursive reading of 'ALL child output specs must receive tokens': a nested And has received tokens exactly when each of its own children has.
- 'Received tokens' and 'the produced set' are read on the set of places the deposit touches (Produced, membership in d), and an output branch is read as a set of places (glossary: Output branch): several tokens into one place of the chosen branch conform, and the order of the deposit plays no part (CORE-036). How many tokens is IO-016's subject. Places outside the output spec are not constrained here (CORE-035 ties the marking to the deposit).
- 'Fires and its action completes' is read on output specs with no Timeout node (findTimeout = none), where every firing ends with its action. An output spec with its one Timeout node anywhere in it, such as And(A, Timeout(d, B)), is IO-013's: the deposit alone cannot tell the timeout outcome from the action outcome, so this block does not restate it there.
- The second clause is the recursive reading of 'ALL children receive tokens' below an Xor: an And under the Xor alternative the action chose must give every one of its children tokens, and the Xor itself must take one alternative (IO-012). Without it a deposit [0, 3] for And(Xor(And(0, 1), 2), 3) (a partial write of the chosen alternative) and a deposit [0, 1, 2] for And(0, Xor(1, 2)) (both alternatives) satisfy the first clause.
- 'That output branch is unique' is read by index: one entry of the IO-016 branch list, one per assignment. On a transition that builds it follows from the existence half and the last build check (IO_011_unique_of_wf), so it adds no constraint on F beyond the scope; no weaker mutant can tell it apart, and the evidence for it is that lemma and IO_011_reference_ambiguous, which shows that without the scope the reference fires And(Q, Xor(P, P)) with two exact branches.
- AC1 (requires at least 1 child) is structural and not encoded: the reference output spec has binary And nodes only, so an And with no child cannot be written; an And with one child is that child.
- AC2 (after the action completes, all children have received tokens) is the first clause, and the second at every depth.
- AC3 (validation failure if a child received no tokens) is read on firings: a completion in which a child received no tokens is not a firing, so the marking never shows it. That the failure is reported (an ActionFailed outcome, the error the user sees) is not observable in the firing relation, which has no events or errors; it is EXEC-030's and IO-015's subject and is not encoded here.
- AC4 and the paragraph 'A place at most once per branch' are the build line, and the first build check of WellFormedOut (every output branch Nodup, equivalently no BranchDuplicate, IO_011_noDuplicate_of_wf) for the firing lines' scope: And(P, P), And(P, And(Q, P)) and Xor(A, And(P, P)) are rejected with the message naming P, and Xor(And(P, A), And(P, B)) builds (IO_011_ac4). The construction paths and MOD-020's more specific message are not in the model. The reference semantics still fires And(P, P) depositing two tokens in P (IO_011_reference_fires_duplicate); that transition does not build, so the firing lines do not speak of it.
- AC5 (And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A)) is rejected naming B) is the build line on that spec, checked under the reference builder (IO_011_ac5).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_011_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_011): The reference semantics satisfies IO-011: the reference builder names the walk's place (`IO_011_refBuild_names`), and with no Timeout node the only outcome a reference firing can take is an action branch (`deposit` of a `timedOut` choice needs `findTimeout`), and every action branch of an `And` is the concatenation of one branch per child (`Out.branches`, `cross`), each of which contains a place its child names (`branch_receives_andChildren`); the deposit is itself the branch at its index, so it is exact for itself, and on a transition that builds no other index is (`IO_011_unique_of_wf`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N], IO_011 refBuild RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_011_forbids_bothArms` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_011): ✗ Writing both alternatives of an inner `Xor` violates IO-011: `[0, 1, 2]` matches neither output branch `[0, 1]` nor `[0, 2]` of `And(0, Xor(1, 2))`.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_011_forbids_firstBranchName` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_011): ✗ Naming the first place repeated in the first repeating output branch violates IO-011: the branches of `And(Xor(A, B), Xor(B, A))` are `[A, B]`, `[A, A]`, `[B, B]`, `[B, A]`, so it names `A`, not `B`.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_011_forbids_leftOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_011): ✗ Writing one child of an `And` only violates IO-011: `io011_t` deposits `[0]`, and its child `Place(1)` receives no token.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_011_forbids_partialXorAnd` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_011): ✗ A partial write of the `And` an inner `Xor` chose violates IO-011: `[0, 3]` matches no output branch of `And(Xor(And(0, 1), 2), 3)` on its places (the branches are `[0, 1, 3]` and `[2, 3]`).
