<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_012"></a>
## IO-012: Output Xor

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_012` · Kind **B** · Scope build check: every transition, on every construction path; firing lines: executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026) · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 5d3f24d7a5511c3e ai** · Statement hash `5d3f24d7a5511c3e`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `Xor(children)` is an output spec node with two or more children; it represents a decision point where the action chooses one child.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `Xor(children)` fires and the firing ends with its action, its produced set *shall* equal, on the places the output spec names, one output branch of the output spec.<br><br>*When* a transition whose output spec is `Xor(children)` fires and the firing ends with its action, its produced set *shall not* equal, on the places the output spec names, two output branches that take different children at some `Xor` node.<br><br>This requirement applies to an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]).<br><br>A firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome ([IO-013]).<br><br>Deposits are compared per place ([CORE-036]): a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome, and the two lines above do not constrain it.<br><br>An *assignment* of an output spec chooses one child at each `Xor` node it reaches ([IO-015]).<br><br>`Xor` nodes are told apart by their position in the spec, never by what they contain, so `Xor(P, P)` has two assignments.<br><br>Two assignments are *distinct* when they choose different children at some `Xor` node that both reach.<br><br>*If* two distinct assignments of a transition's output spec claim the same set of places, at any depth of the spec, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with<br><br>Enumerate the output branches of the spec per [IO-016], numbered from 0 in enumeration order (the numbering of the virtual transitions `&lt;t>_b&lt;i>` of [VER-001]).<br><br>The enumeration lists exactly one branch per assignment, so two branches at different indices come from distinct assignments.<br><br>Read each branch as the set of places it names, a `ForwardInput(from, to)` naming `to`.<br><br>Visit the branches in index order.<br><br>The first branch `j` whose set equals the set of an earlier branch fails the check, and `i` is the smallest index of such an earlier branch.<br><br>If no branch fails, the check passes.<br><br>`&lt;places>` lists the places of branch `i` by name, separated by `, `, in the order the spec as written names them (leaves left to right).<br><br>An implementation MAY decide the check without enumerating every branch, provided it reports the same `i`, `j` and `&lt;places>`.<br><br>A transition that builds therefore has pairwise distinct output branches, so at most one output branch equals any produced set, and the second line above holds of every firing of such a transition. | 1. Build check. For every output spec o (the output spec of the transition being built), with bs its output branches (Out.branches, one entry per assignment, numbered from 0):<br>2. the check C passes (C o = none) exactly when no two entries of bs at indices i &lt; j claim the same set of places (IO_012_unambiguous; IO_012_clash compares the entries as sets, SameSet);<br>3. the check fails reporting (i, j, ps) (C o = some (i, j, ps)) exactly when the entries i &lt; j clash, no entry before j clashes with an earlier one, no entry before i clashes with entry j, and ps is entry i as a list (IO_012_reported).<br>4. Building. For every transition t whose output spec o is ambiguous (not IO_012_unambiguous): building t fails (Build t ≠ none); and when every earlier build-time check passes (input places distinct, CORE-030; no output branch naming a place twice, IO-011; at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its child, IO-013; no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child and every forward from an input place, IO-014), building fails with IO-012's message for the pair (i, j) and the places ps the check reports (msgAmbiguous t i j ps).<br>5. Firing. For every transition t whose output spec is Xor(l, r) and passes the check, every deposit d, and every firing of t under F from m to m' that deposits d and whose deposit is not, place by place, a timeout-outcome deposit of t from m (IO_012_timeoutLike): some output branch b of Xor(l, r) is exact for d: on every place q the output spec names, d puts one or more tokens in q exactly when q is in b (ExactOn).<br>6. The second firing line is a consequence, not a clause: on an output spec that passes the check two exact branches would be the same set (both lie within outPlaces), so at most one is exact (theorem IO_012_unique).<br>7. `on R, shall Q` reads: every step from m to m' with R m m' satisfies Q m m'; here Q ignores both markings. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] C Build F ↦<br>  (∀ (o : Out N), C o = none ↔ IO_012_unambiguous o) ∧<br>    (∀ (o : Out N) (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),<br>        C o = some (i, j, ps) ↔ IO_012_reported o i j ps) ∧<br>      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N),<br>          OutputSpec t = some o →<br>            ¬IO_012_unambiguous o →<br>              Build t ≠ none ∧<br>                (PreOutputChecks t →<br>                  ¬DupBranch o →<br>                    timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →<br>                      xorInTimeout o = false →<br>                        forwardOutside o = none →<br>                          (∀ s ∈ forwardSources o, s ∈ inPlaces t) →<br>                            ∀ (i j : ℕ) (ps : List N),<br>                              C o = some (i, j, ps) →<br>                                Build t = some (msgAmbiguous t i j ps))) ∧<br>        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (l r : Out N),<br>          OutputSpec t = some (l.xor r) →<br>            IO_012_unambiguous (l.xor r) →<br>              ∀ (d : List N),<br>                on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m' ∧ ¬IO_012_timeoutLike t m d, shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>                  ∃ b ∈ (l.xor r).branches, ExactOn (l.xor r) d b</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A completion that fails, by an action exception (EXEC-030) or by IO-015 validation, deposits no outcome and is not a firing here: an action failure does not end the firing with its action.
- F models an executor with output validation enabled, the default; an executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled is not constrained by the firing line (scope). The build check is independent of any executor: C is the check itself.
- The check is modelled by what it reports, not by its text: C o = some (i, j, ps) stands for the message `output spec of transition '<t>' is ambiguous: output branches <i> and <j> both claim {<places>}; no write can tell them apart (IO-012)`, with <places> the names of ps joined by ', '. The transition name, the rendering of names, the message text, and the claim that it is byte-identical across implementations are not in the model; the cross-language tests of AC5 pin them.
- The check C is stated for one output spec in isolation; the third line ties it to the builder. In the builder it runs last of the build-time checks (the Output Composition preamble: CORE-030's input check, then IO-011, IO-013's two checks, IO-014 before it), so a spec that an earlier check rejects reports that check's message instead: the third line asks for IO-012's message only when every earlier check passes, and otherwise only that building fails. The message is the glossary's msgAmbiguous, the text the markdown gives. That the check runs on every construction path (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion) and that no executor option skips it is read as: every transition in a net has an output spec C passes. The firing line is stated for such transitions; the model has no construction paths to enumerate.
- 'An implementation MAY decide the check without enumerating every branch' is the extensional reading: the block constrains C only by what it returns, so any algorithm that returns the same (i, j, ps) satisfies it. IO_012_check is one such algorithm, the enumeration of the numbered steps.
- Place identity is equality on N, the implementation's own Place equality (names in TypeScript, Rust and Python, name and token type in Java; CORE-002, MOD-024). A ForwardInput(from, to) claims `to`, a Timeout its child's claim (Out.branches).
- Branches are numbered by the reference enumeration Out.branches over the right-nested binary Out: an n-ary Xor(c₁, …, cₙ) is xor c₁ (xor c₂ … cₙ) and concatenates its children's lists in child order; an n-ary And is the cartesian product with the first child varying slowest. These are IO-016's lists and VER-001's <t>_b<i> numbering, so the binary nesting changes no index.
- 'Receives tokens' is read as IO-015's exact explanation, as AC4 directs: a child whose output branch is a strict subset of the produced set has received tokens but is not satisfied. Read literally, `Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B))` writing {A, B} would have two children receiving tokens; under the exact reading only the second child's branch equals it.
- The produced set is compared on the places the output spec names (outPlaces), as IO-015 compares on declared places: a token in a place the spec never names is CORE-072's business. A token in a named place outside the selected branch still breaks the firing line (IO-015 AC9). A branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many (glossary: Output branch): several tokens into one place of the branch conform.
- A firing ends with its action unless it is the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome, IO-013); the abstract firing relation does not label the outcome, so a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of t from the same marking is not checked (IO-012), whatever the order of its tokens. When the action happens to write such a deposit, that firing is not checked either. An Xor that contains a Timeout node is otherwise covered.
- The firing line covers a transition whose whole output spec is an Xor. An Xor nested inside And or Timeout is covered by IO-015, which validates every Xor an assignment reaches. The build check covers every output spec, an Xor at any depth included: And(Q, Xor(P, P)) is rejected.
- AC1 (at least two children) is structural: the binary xor node has the two children l and r, and an n-ary Xor nests as xor c₁ (xor c₂ … cₙ) (checked by example below); the reference loader rejects an xor with fewer than two children.
- AC2 (exactly one child received tokens) is the firing line (at least one exact branch, so one child of the top Xor) together with its consequence IO_012_unique (not two). An output branch takes exactly one child of the top Xor.
- AC3 (zero branches satisfied → validation error) is the firing line: such a completion is not a firing. The test derivation's 'action produces to both' case is also the firing line under the exact reading: Xor(P1, P2) has no output branch {P1, P2}.
- AC4 (two branches whose claims are the same set never reach a firing) is the build check: such a spec does not pass C, and the firing line is stated only for specs that pass. The strict-subset remark of AC4 is the exact reading above: Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) passes the check (checked by example below).
- AC5 (the rejected and accepted specs and their reported pairs and places) is checked by example on IO_012_check below, with the places A, B, C, P, Q, a named by the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The Timeout duration d is not in the reference Out. The composition case (two output ports in different alternatives bound to one host place) is the check applied to the composed spec; composition itself is MOD-024's model, not this block's.
- The Test derivation's build cases are AC5's; its firing cases are AC3's.
- Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✓ IO-012 holds of the reference: the reference check (`IO_012_check`) reports exactly what the block names, the reference builder (`refBuild`) rejects every ambiguous output spec with IO-012's message once the earlier checks pass, and the reference firings satisfy the firing line.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N],<br>  IO_012 IO_012_check refBuild RefFire</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_allows_permutedTimeout` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✓ IO-012 allows a firing whose deposit is a timeout-outcome deposit in another order ([CORE-036]): `[2, 1]` equals the timeout deposit `[1, 2]` place by place, so the firing may have ended with the timeout outcome and the firing line does not constrain it, although `[2, 1]` matches no output branch (`{0}`, `{1, 2, 3}`).
  <pre>IO_012 IO_012_check refBuild io012_permFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_acceptAll` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A build check that accepts every output spec violates IO-012 (the first build clause, AC4/AC5): it passes `Xor(Place(0), Place(0))`, whose two output branches claim `{0}`.
  <pre>¬IO_012 (fun x ↦ none) refBuild RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_both` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A firing that writes both children violates IO-012 (the firing line; the test derivation's "produces to both"): `Xor(Place(0), Place(1))` has no output branch `{0, 1}`.
  <pre>¬IO_012 IO_012_check refBuild (io012_oneFire ((Out.place 0).xor (Out.place 1)) [0, 1])</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_buildAll` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A builder that builds every transition violates IO-012 (the build line): `io012_dup`, whose output spec `Xor(Place(0), Place(0))` is ambiguous, builds.
  <pre>¬IO_012 IO_012_check (fun x ↦ none) RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_buildVague` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A builder that rejects an ambiguous output spec with another message violates IO-012 (the build line): `Xor(P, P)` passes every earlier check, so building it must fail with IO-012's message for branches 0 and 1 and `{P}`, not with `rejected`.
  <pre>¬IO_012 IO_012_check io012_buildVague RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_iMajor` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A build check that reports the wrong pair violates IO-012 (the second build clause, step 3): on `io012_pqqp` the first clashing `j` is 2 (with `i` = 1), not 3.
  <pre>¬IO_012 io012_iMajor refBuild RefFire</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_silent` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ A firing that writes no child violates IO-012 (the firing line, AC3): `io012_t` fires with an empty deposit, and no output branch of `Xor(Place(0), Place(1))` is empty.
  <pre>¬IO_012 IO_012_check refBuild (io012_oneFire ((Out.place 0).xor (Out.place 1)) [])</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_012_forbids_silentWithTimeout` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_012): ✗ An `Xor` with a `Timeout` child is checked too (the firing line): `Xor(Place(0), Timeout(Place(1)))` firing with an empty deposit is not, place by place, a timeout outcome (that puts a token in `1`) and matches no output branch.
  <pre>¬IO_012 IO_012_check refBuild (io012_oneFire ((Out.place 0).xor (Out.place 1).timeout) [])</pre>

- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_coreIO_time` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyTime): ✓ The CORE and IO requirement blocks, TIME-001, EXEC-002 and the TIME blocks over the timed step relation hold together on one model: one firing relation `F` for the CORE and IO blocks, whose firings are the firings of the timed step relation `R` of the TIME blocks; a timing contract whose bounds are the `Timing` accessors the TIME blocks read; and a ready order for every pass input. ## IO-013: Output timeout

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_013` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 4dd548dd2797bcc8 ai** · Statement hash `4dd548dd2797bcc8`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `Timeout(duration, child)` is a node of an output spec that gives the action of a firing a budget of `duration` to complete.<br><br>*If* the action does not complete within `duration`, the firing *shall* end with the timeout outcome: it is abandoned, and it deposits the tokens of `child`.<br><br>*When* a firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall not* deposit any output of the action, so the marking receives the tokens of `child` and nothing else.<br><br>*If* an output spec holds more than one `Timeout` node, whether one is nested in the child of another or they sit apart, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with<br><br>where `&lt;n>` is the number of `Timeout` nodes in the spec.<br><br>The check runs when the transition is built, on every construction path, as the check of [IO-011] does.<br><br>A transition that builds therefore has at most one timeout outcome, and the `child` of its `Timeout` holds no `Timeout` node.<br><br>The executor, not the action, makes the deposit of the timeout outcome, so nothing chooses among alternatives inside the `Timeout` child.<br><br>*If* the child of an output spec's `Timeout` node holds an `Xor` node at any depth, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with<br><br>The check runs after the `Timeout` count check above, so the spec it sees holds at most one `Timeout` node.<br><br>The timeout outcome of a transition that builds therefore deposits in one fixed set of places: every place the `Timeout` child names. | 1. Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg), F the firings and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome.<br>2. For every transition t whose output spec o holds two or more Timeout nodes, building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct and no output branch of o names a place twice, it fails with the IO-013 message for t and the number of Timeout nodes in o.<br>3. Every transition that passes every build check (distinct input places, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward from an input place, no two output branches claiming one set of places) builds.<br>4. For every transition t that builds: every firing of t in T is a firing in F, with the same deposit and target marking.<br>5. For every transition t that builds: every firing of t in T from m deposits, place by place, exactly the tokens of the timeout outcome of t (for what t consumes at m), and nothing else.<br>6. For every transition t that builds: from every marking m at which t is enabled, every timeout outcome d of t (for what t consumes at m) is the deposit of some firing in T.<br>7. For every transition t that builds and whose output spec has a Timeout node, every firing of t in F is in T, or has as its produced set exactly the places of one output branch of t.<br>8. For every transition t whose output spec o holds at most one Timeout node and an Xor node at any depth of that node's child (xorInTimeout), building t fails; and if t's input places are distinct and **Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (Build, F, T). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the reference builder refBuild runs the checks the model can see in the order of the output composition preamble of spec/02-input-output-specs.md. F is the firing relation and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome), each read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the tokens of one outcome (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A plain FireRel cannot carry T: on Xor(Place 0, Timeout(Place 1)) the timeout deposit [1] is also the action branch {1}, so a timed-out firing that deposits the sibling branch [0] would look like an action firing. The witness triple is refBuild, RefFire and refTimeoutOutcomeFire.
- The build error is msgTimeouts, byte for byte: output spec of transition '<t>' has <n> Timeout nodes; an output spec has at most one, nested or not (IO-013), with <n> the number of Timeout nodes in the spec, nested and sibling ones alike (timeoutCount). The preamble's order puts the IO-011 check (a place twice in one output branch) first, so on such a spec the message is IO-011's and the second line only requires that building fails. The preamble does not place the CORE-030 input-arc check, so on a transition with two input arcs on one place the second line likewise only requires that building fails.
- 'On every construction path' is read as: Build is the one builder every construction path goes through (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion), so a transition that a path yields builds exactly when Build accepts it. Which paths exist is not in the model.
- The third line is the converse that makes 'builds' checkable (AC7's specs that build): a transition passing the checks before the output spec (CORE-030, the IO-002/IO-004 input counts and EXEC-012's input-and-read check, PreOutputChecks) and every build check of the output composition preamble builds. The checks are the glossary terms Builds and WellFormedOut, the build-time checks of IO-011, IO-012, IO-013 and IO-014; checks the model cannot see (AC1's positive duration, a spec that names no place) are outside it.
- A transition that builds has at most one Timeout node, so its timeout outcome is the one Timeout node's child (Out.findTimeout finds it), and that child holds no Timeout node. The firing lines are stated for transitions that build only: a transition building rejects is not a transition of any net (CORE-022) and never fires.
- The duration is not in the model, so whether the budget expires is nondeterministic: from every marking at which t is enabled, the action may overrun it. The sixth line therefore reads 'if the action does not complete within duration, the firing shall end with the timeout outcome' as 'the timeout outcome is always one of the ways a firing of t can end'. That overrunning forces the timeout, and that completing in time rules it out, are statements about time that a model of untimed steps cannot express.
- 'It is abandoned' is the action's output being excluded, which the fifth line states for the deposit. Whether the action is stopped is the side-effect paragraph that follows the first paragraph, not encoded.
- 'The marking receives the tokens of child and nothing else' is read at the deposit (fifth line). Which marking a firing leads to is the effect rule of the glossary term Fire (CORE-030, CORE-034, CORE-035); the fourth line ties every timed-out firing to a firing of F, so that rule applies to it.
- 'The tokens of child' is the glossary term Timeout outcome, as the reference reads it (Out.timeoutDeposits): one token per Place leaf of child, the product at every And, and one token in to per token consumed from from at every ForwardInput (IO-014), counted per place, so the order of the deposit list does not matter (CORE-036). Token values and created_at (the minted tokens of AC3, forwarded values and their stamps, IO-014 AC5) are below the count granularity.
- The eighth line is the paragraph 'One fixed timeout deposit'. Its message is msgXorInTimeout, byte for byte. Any Xor at any depth of the Timeout child counts, under an And or a ForwardInput's sibling included (hasXor). It runs after the Timeout count check, as the premise timeoutCount o ≤ 1 states: with two Timeout nodes the message is the first line's. The preamble's order puts the IO-011 check before it, so on a spec that names a place twice in one output branch the eighth line only requires that building fails, and on a transition with two input arcs on one place likewise (CORE-030). 'The executor, not the action, makes the deposit' is the reason the markdown gives and is not a separate constraint.
- 'The timeout outcome of a transition that builds therefore deposits in one fixed set of places' is a consequence, not a clause: on a transition that builds the Timeout child holds no Xor node, so Out.timeoutDeposits of the child has one entry and the fifth and sixth lines name one deposit (theorem IO_013_one_fixed_deposit, from the glossary's timeoutOutcome_unique). Without the check the reference offers one timeout outcome per alternative of an Xor in the child (IO_013_reference_xorChild_two_outcomes).
- The seventh line is AC5 for a firing that does not report the timeout outcome: it ended with its action, whose produced set is one output branch (IO-015, exact explanation; how many tokens per place is IO-016's). A deposit that merges a timeout outcome with output the action wrote and reports it as an action firing is neither, unless its places happen to form a whole output branch, in which case it is a legal action firing and no observation of the marking can tell the two apart. The line is a requirement on an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026); F models such an executor, as RefFire does. With the skip enabled an action firing deposits the action's write and the line is not claimed of it. The skip changes nothing on the timeout outcome (CONC-026), so the timed-out lines (fourth to sixth) do not depend on it; every runtime holds them (below).
- The timed-out lines in the runtimes. No runtime validates the timeout outcome against the output spec: Rust, and Python on it, skip validation on the timeout path, and Java (BitmapNetExecutor and PrecompiledNetExecutor processCompletedTransitions) and TypeScript (bitmap-net-executor.ts and precompiled-net-executor.ts) skip it, and the IO-016 multiplicity warning, when TransitionContext.isDetachedForTimeout(), running only the NU-054 relay check; so on And(A, Timeout(d, B)), which builds, a timed-out firing deposits B (ruling D24 (a)). An executor that validates the timeout outcome against the whole output spec fails every such timed-out firing and breaks the sixth line, from every enabled marking every timeout outcome is the deposit of some firing in T (io013_validatingFire and io013_validatedTimedOut, IO_013_forbids_validateTimeout; the behaviour RD-01 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of Java and TypeScript).
- Every runtime deposits the timeout outcome on the places the rewritten output spec names, as given: Java (TransitionContext outputToHarvest and forwardToHarvest, and ExecutorSupport produceTimeoutOutputRecursive, which reads a ForwardInput's from place with rawInput) and TypeScript (transition-context.ts outputToHarvest and forwardToHarvest) take those places as the actual places and do not resolve them through the composition correspondence again, and Rust deposits on them directly. An executor that resolves them a second time, on a correspondence collision (port a bound to b, port b bound to c), deposits the timeout token meant for b on c and breaks the fifth line, the deposit equals the timeout outcome place by place (the behaviour RD-31 recorded of Java and TypeScript). The correspondence is not in this model, whose transition is the rewritten one, so the statement cannot see the second resolution; that wrong executor is shown in MOD_031.lean (mod031ctx_timeout_resolveTwice), and the runtimes are tested on it (java AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest OutputTimeoutTests outTimeout_portCollision_depositsOnTheBoundPlace_MOD031_IO013; typescript tests/core/compose-action-place-alias.test.ts 'the timeout branch deposits on the bound place under a port-name collision').
- The sentence 'A firing of a transition with a match specification whose timeout outcome fails the relay check of [NU-054] does not end with the timeout outcome: it fails ([EVT-008]) and deposits none of the tokens of `child`.' is ruling D24 (a) (clash nu-c#8). It narrows the second quote and the sixth line to firings the relay check accepts. Trans carries no match specification, so a transition with one is outside this block, and on every transition here no relay check applies; the exception is stated by NU_054_check (the check) and NU_054_fail (the failed firing deposits nothing of the timeout outcome).
- AC1 (duration must be positive) is a build-time validation of the duration, which the model does not carry; not encoded.
- AC2 (action completes within duration, normal output validation) is the produced-set disjunct of the seventh line; the validation itself is IO-015's subject.
- AC3 (action exceeds duration, every place the timeout child names receives tokens: one minted token for a Place, the forwarded tokens for a ForwardInput) is the fifth and sixth lines, read on token counts.
- AC4 (an ActionTimedOut event is emitted on timeout) is an event obligation (EVT-010, whose lines 1 and 3 state it for both emission variants); the firing relation has no events, so it is not encoded here.
- AC5 (output produced before the budget expired is discarded, the marking receiving the tokens of the timeout child's one fixed set of places and nothing else; a partial write under an Xor sibling is not a second satisfied branch) is the fifth line for a firing in T and the seventh for a firing outside it; 'one fixed set' is IO_013_one_fixed_deposit.
- AC6 (a TimeoutException the action raises is an ordinary action failure, not the timeout branch) is about which trigger ends the firing; an action failure deposits no outcome (EXEC-030) and is not a firing in this model, so it is not encoded.
- AC7 is the second and third lines: its three rejected specs (Timeout(d, Timeout(e, P)), Xor(Timeout(d, A), Timeout(e, B)), And(Timeout(d, A), Xor(B, Timeout(e, C)))) fail with the message for n = 2 and its two accepted specs (Xor(A, Timeout(d, B)), Timeout(d, And(A, B))) build, under the reference builder (IO_013_ac7_rejected, IO_013_ac7_builds).
- AC8 is the eighth and third lines: its two rejected specs (Timeout(d, Xor(A, B)), Xor(C, Timeout(d, And(A, Xor(B, D))))) fail with the Xor message, and its two accepted specs (Xor(A, Timeout(d, B)) and, with i an input place, Timeout(d, And(A, ForwardInput(i, B)))) build, under the reference builder (IO_013_ac8_rejected, IO_013_ac8_builds).
- The test derivation's build cases are AC7's and AC8's; its timing case (an action sleeping past its budget, the event) is outside the model: the duration and the event store are not in it.
- Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.IO_013_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.IO_013): The reference satisfies IO-013: the reference builder rejects a spec with two or more `Timeout` nodes with IO-013's message and accepts every transition that passes every build check; a timed-out reference firing is a reference firing, deposits the timeout outcome and nothing else (`.timedOut j`), is available from every enabled marking, and every other reference firing ends with its action, depositing one output branch (`.action i`).

- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_coreIO_time` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyTime): ✓ The CORE and IO requirement blocks, TIME-001, EXEC-002 and the TIME blocks over the timed step relation hold together on one model: one firing relation `F` for the CORE and IO blocks, whose firings are the firings of the timed step relation `R` of the TIME blocks; a timing contract whose bounds are the `Timing` accessors the TIME blocks read; and a ready order for every pass input. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_014"></a>
## IO-014: Output ForwardInput

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_014` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 73d8a8afcc5b3c0d ai** · Statement hash `73d8a8afcc5b3c0d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| `ForwardInput(from, to)` is a node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed from its input place `from`.<br><br>*If* a `ForwardInput` node of an output spec is not inside the child of a `Timeout` node, *then* building the transition *shall* fail with<br><br>naming the first such node in the order the spec is written (pre-order, children left to right).<br><br>The check runs when the transition is built, on every construction path, as the check of [IO-011] does.<br><br>*When* a firing ends with the timeout outcome, every `ForwardInput(from, to)` in the `Timeout` child *shall* deposit in `to` one token for each token the firing consumed from `from`, carrying the token's value, in consumption order.<br><br>The count *shall* be the consumption count of the input arc on `from` ([IO-007]): 1 for `One`, `n` for `Exactly(n)`, and the whole drained batch for `All` and `AtLeast(m)`.<br><br>*If* a firing consumed more than one token from `from`, *then* the forward *shall not* deposit fewer tokens in `to` than the firing consumed; in particular it *shall not* forward only the first consumed token.<br><br>*If* a firing consumed no token from `from`, which a declared input cannot do but a mis-declared spec can, *then* the forward *shall* deposit no token in `to`. | 1. Let Build be the builder (Build t = none: t builds; Build t = some msg: building t fails with msg) and T the firings that end with the timeout outcome.<br>2. For every transition t whose output spec o has a ForwardInput(from, to) outside the child of a Timeout node, the first in pre-order, building t fails;<br>3. and if t's input places are distinct, no output branch of o names a place twice, o has at most one Timeout node and no Xor node inside its Timeout child, building t fails with the IO-014 message naming t, from and to.<br>4. For every transition t whose output spec has a ForwardInput from a place that is not one of t's input places, building t fails.<br>5. Every transition that passes every build check (distinct input places, no place twice in one output branch, at most one Timeout node, no Xor node inside the Timeout child, no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child, every forward from an input place, no two output branches claiming one set of places) builds.<br>6. For every transition t whose output spec has at most one Timeout node and a ForwardInput(from, to) anywhere in that node's child (also under And or Xor), every deposit d and every firing of t from m in T that deposits d, there is one timeout deposit e of the Timeout child, built with every ForwardInput(a, b) of the child putting in b one token per token the firing consumes from a, such that e puts no more tokens than d in any place (no consumed token is lost, at any forward of the child) and d puts no more tokens than e in any place (one token per consumed token, none extra). | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] Build T ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),<br>      OutputSpec t = some o → forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) → Build t ≠ none) ∧<br>    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src dst : N),<br>        OutputSpec t = some o →<br>          forwardOutside o = some (src, dst) →<br>            PreOutputChecks t →<br>              ¬DupBranch o →<br>                timeoutCount o ≤ 1 →<br>                  xorInTimeout o = false → Build t = some (msgForward t src dst)) ∧<br>      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (o : Out N) (src : N),<br>          OutputSpec t = some o →<br>            src ∈ forwardSources o → src ∉ inPlaces t → Build t ≠ none) ∧<br>        (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N), Builds t → Build t = none) ∧<br>          ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (src dst : N),<br>            (∀ (o : Out N), OutputSpec t = some o → timeoutCount o ≤ 1) →<br>              TimeoutForwards t src dst →<br>                ∀ (d : List N),<br>                  on fun m m' ↦ T t m d m', shall fun m x ↦<br>                    ∃ e,<br>                      TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) e ∧<br>                        (∀ (p : N), Deposits e p ≤ Deposits d p) ∧<br>                          ∀ (p : N), Deposits d p ≤ Deposits e p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (Build, T). Build is the transition builder, read as the message building a transition fails with, none when it builds; the reference builder refBuild runs the CORE-030 input-arc check and then the output-spec checks in the order of the output composition preamble of spec/02-input-output-specs.md (IO-011, IO-013's Timeout count, IO-013's Xor inside the Timeout child, IO-014, IO-014 AC3, IO-012), with each message byte for byte except CORE-030's, which the spec does not give. Place names are rendered with the place type's ToString.
- T is the relation of firings that end with the timeout outcome (glossary: Timeout outcome), read as one step from a marking to a marking that deposits the Timeout child's tokens (glossary: Fire, Deposit); timing and priority play no part. A plain FireRel cannot be used: on Timeout(ForwardInput(from, to)) the action branch [to] and a forward of one token are the same deposit. The witness refTimedOutFire is the part of RefFire whose outcome is a timedOut choice (refTimedOutFire_refFire). That the resulting marking receives d is the effect rule (CORE-030, CORE-034, CORE-035) on the plain firing relation, not restated here.
- The build error is msgForward, byte for byte: output spec of transition '<t>' uses ForwardInput('<from>', '<to>') outside the child of a Timeout node; a forward deposits only on the timeout outcome (IO-014). 'Not inside the child of a Timeout node' and 'the first such node' are forwardOutside: the pre-order walk, children left to right, that does not enter a Timeout node. The preamble's order runs the IO-011 check (a place twice in one output branch) and the IO-013 checks (more than one Timeout node, an Xor node inside the Timeout child) first, so on such a spec the message is theirs, and the second line only requires that building fails; CORE-030's input-arc check is not placed by the preamble and is treated the same way.
- 'On every construction path' is read as: Build is the one builder every construction path goes through (builders, composition, channel merge, fusion), so a transition that a path yields builds exactly when Build accepts it. Which paths exist is not in the model. No executor option reaches Build (CONC-026).
- The fifth line is the converse that makes 'builds' checkable (AC7's specs that build): a transition passing the checks before the output spec (CORE-030, the IO-002/IO-004 input counts and EXEC-012's input-and-read check, PreOutputChecks) and every build check of the output composition preamble builds. The checks are the glossary terms Builds and WellFormedOut, the same checks IO-013 reads.
- The firing line is stated for every transition whose output spec has at most one Timeout node, not only for transitions that build: a transition with two or more Timeout nodes is rejected (IO-013) and has no single Timeout child, so no reading of 'the Timeout child' is claimed there, while a transition with a forward from a non-input place, rejected by the fourth line, is still covered, which is what keeps the fourth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) checkable. A transition with one Timeout node has one Timeout child, the one Out.findTimeout finds.
- 'The `ForwardInput(from, to)` node of an output spec that, on the timeout outcome, deposits in `to` the tokens a firing consumed' (first quote) is the firing line, which says how many.
- 'Every ForwardInput(from, to) in the Timeout child' includes a ForwardInput nested under And or Xor. On a transition that builds the child holds no Xor node (IO-013), so it has one timeout deposit (glossary: timeoutOutcome_unique); the line is also stated for transitions that do not build, where an Xor child has several timeout deposits and which one a firing chose is visible only in the whole deposit, so the statement compares d place by place with one timeout deposit e of the child (glossary: Timeout outcome, TimeoutOutcome); deposits are compared per place, so the order of the deposit list does not matter (CORE-036). This also fixes the tokens the child's Place leaves put in, which is IO-013's subject (AC5); it is restated here only because it is what identifies the chosen alternative. Comparing only the place `to` would let a forward-first firing pass whenever another alternative of the child happens to put the same count in `to`.
- 'The count' (sixth quote) is the firing's consumption from `from`, the glossary term Consume (Consumes t m from), which is IO-007's consumption count of the input arc on `from` (bridge lemma consumes_eq) and 0 for a place with no input arc. The two bounds of the firing line together say d equals e place by place, with one existential e for both; they are split so that losing tokens and inventing tokens are refuted separately.
- The seventh quote (no forward of fewer tokens, not only the first) is the first bound. The eighth quote (no input consumed, nothing forwarded) is the second bound, e having no forwarded token where Consumes t m from = 0.
- The sentence '*When* a `ForwardInput` forwards a consumed token, the token it deposits in `to` *shall* carry the consumed token's `created_at` as well as its value.' is token metadata (a value and a creation stamp) below the count granularity of the firing semantics, which has no token values or stamps; it is not encoded, and neither is the paragraph around it (the TIME-015 exception, the NU-022 tie-break).
- AC1 (from must be a declared input place, validated at build time) and AC3 (an invalid from reference is a build error) are the fourth line. Which forward AC3's existing message names when several are invalid is not said by the text; the reference builder names the first in pre-order, and the statement does not constrain the message.
- AC2 (one token per consumed token, preserving values and consumption order) is the firing line for its count; values and consumption order are below the count granularity and are not encoded.
- AC4 (All or Exactly(n) with N tokens consumed puts exactly N in `to`) is the two bounds together, with Consumes giving N for Exactly(n) and the whole place for All.
- AC5 (a forwarded token's created_at equals the original's and is not re-stamped from the epoch clock, while a minted recovery token is, in every implementation) is token metadata below the count granularity and is not encoded.
- AC6 (every analysis deposits what the executor deposits) is about the verifier's branch expansion (IO-016, VER-001), not about firings or building; Novel/ForwardDeposit.lean proves it for the flattened rows.
- AC7 is the second, third and fifth lines: its three rejected specs (ForwardInput(a, b), Xor(c, ForwardInput(a, b)), And(c, Xor(e, ForwardInput(a, b)))) fail with the message naming a and b, and its two accepted specs (Timeout(d, ForwardInput(a, b)), Xor(c, Timeout(d, And(e, ForwardInput(a, b))))) build, under the reference builder with a an input place (IO_014_ac7_rejected, IO_014_ac7_builds).
- Ruling D15: the premise PreOutputChecks t (glossary) is the checks the reference builder runs before the output-spec checks: distinct input places ([CORE-030]), input arcs that each require at least one token ([IO-002], [IO-004]) and no input arc and read arc on one place ([EXEC-012]). A transition that fails one of them fails with that check's message, so on it the build lines only require that building fails, as for CORE-030 before the ruling.
- Every runtime forwards on the timeout outcome between the places the rewritten output spec names, as given: Java (ExecutorSupport produceTimeoutOutputRecursive reads the from place with rawInput, and TransitionContext.forwardToHarvest deposits in to) and TypeScript (executor-support.ts produceTimeoutOutput and transition-context.ts forwardToHarvest) take those places as the actual places and do not resolve them through the composition correspondence again, and Rust forwards between them directly. An executor that resolves them a second time, on a correspondence collision (port a bound to b, port b bound to c), forwards the token meant for b to c, or reads from the wrong input, so the deposit differs place by place from every timeout deposit of the child and the firing line fails (the behaviour RD-31 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of Java and TypeScript, on both the to and the from side). The correspondence is not in this model, whose transition is the rewritten one, so the statement cannot see the second resolution; that wrong executor is shown in MOD_031.lean (mod031ctx_timeout_resolveTwice), and the runtimes are tested on it (java AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest OutputTimeoutTests outTimeout_forwardInput_portCollision_forwardsFromTheBoundPlace_MOD031_IO014; typescript tests/core/compose-action-place-alias.test.ts 'a timeout ForwardInput reads and deposits on the actual places under a collision').

| An *assignment* selects exactly one child at each `Xor` node it reaches; nodes beneath an unselected `Xor` child are never evaluated.<br><br>Claims are compared with the produced set on the places the output spec names.<br><br>A token in a place the output spec never names takes no part in validation: a transition context never produces to such a place ([CORE-063]), and a token that bypasses the context is [CORE-072]'s subject, not an [IO-015] violation.<br><br>*If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.<br><br>*If* no assignment claims a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because nothing explains what was written.<br><br>*If* two or more assignments claim a set equal to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* fail, because the write is genuinely ambiguous.<br><br>For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set ([IO-012]), so on a firing this third case does not arise.<br><br>The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms. | 1. For every declared output spec o and every deposit d, with assignment i of o claiming the i-th entry of Out.branches o, and an assignment exact for d when its claim equals the produced set of d on every place o names (NamedExact):<br>2. if some assignment i is exact for d and every assignment that is exact for d is i, validation of d against o succeeds;<br>3. if no assignment is exact for d, validation fails;<br>4. if two different assignments i ≠ j are both exact for d, validation fails. | <pre>fun {N} V ↦<br>  (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i : ℕ),<br>      NamedExact o d i → (∀ (j : ℕ), NamedExact o d j → j = i) → V o d = true) ∧<br>    (∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N), (∀ (i : ℕ), ¬NamedExact o d i) → V o d = false) ∧<br>      ∀ (o : Out N) (d : List N) (i j : ℕ),<br>        i ≠ j → NamedExact o d i → NamedExact o d j → V o d = false</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A validator is the verdict function of one implementation: its inputs are the declared output spec and the tokens the completed action produced, as a deposit (a list of places with repetition); its output is success (true) or violation (false). The produced set is the places of the deposit (glossary: Produced set).
- When an action completes, an executor with output validation enabled, which is the default ([CONC-026]), shall validate its produced set against the transition's output spec. This sentence is the trigger and is not encoded: the block fixes the verdict of the check, not when it runs. An executor with the CONC-026 skip enabled runs no check, so the verdict constrains nothing there (CONC-026's subject). A completion that fails validation deposits no outcome and is not a firing (glossary: Fire); a transition with no output spec has nothing to validate; the timeout outcome (IO-013) does not complete the action and is not validated.
- The first two quotes are the comparison: an assignment is exact for d when, on every place o names (outPlaces o), the place is in its claim exactly when d puts a token in it (NamedExact, glossary ExactOn, as IO-011 and IO-012 compare). A place o never names takes no part, so Place(A) with a token in A and one in a place X that o never names succeeds, as with A alone (IO_015_unnamedPlace). The runtimes compare the same way and say why: Rust restricts the produced set to the places the spec names (executor_core/output.rs, ProducedIndex::build, unit test token_in_an_unnamed_place_is_not_an_io_015_violation), Java compares on declaredAndProduced (ExecutorSupport.validateOutSpec), TypeScript counts only the produced places the spec names (executor-support.ts validateOutSpec). Such a token reaches the deposit only through a seam that bypasses the transition context, such as Java's and TypeScript's rawOutput(), and what becomes of it (retained in the marking, the unknown-place diagnostic) is CORE-072's subject (AC3, AC4), not encoded here. A validator that compares on every place rejects that write and breaks the first clause (IO_015_forbids_everyPlace).
- Assignments are counted, not their claims: two assignments that claim the same set are two (Xor(A, A) with A produced has two exact assignments and fails). Out.branches enumerates one claim per assignment, in the claim rules of the bullet list; n-ary And and Xor are read as right-nested binary nodes, which changes neither the number of assignments, their claims nor their IO-016 order.
- The verdict function is total: the three clauses range over every output spec, those IO-012 rejects at build included. The sentence 'For a transition that builds, no two assignments claim the same set' is a consequence, not a clause: the glossary's WellFormedOut is the build-time constraint on an output spec, and on a spec satisfying it no two different assignments are exact for any deposit (theorem IO_015_wf_noAmbiguous), so under IO-015 the verdict is success exactly when some assignment is exact (theorem IO_015_wf_iff). The theorems use only its IO-012 conjunct, pairwise distinct branch sets.
- The set-of-places sentence is a consequence, not a clause: the three clauses fix the verdict from the number of exact assignments (theorem IO_015_determines), and that number reads only the produced set (theorem IO_015_setOnly). Deposits are compared per place (CORE-036): two deposits with the same count in every place, in any order, get the same verdict (theorem IO_015_perPlace).
- AC1 (conforming output → success) is the first clause, 'conforming' read as 'exactly one exact assignment'.
- AC2 (non-conforming output → failure event emitted) and AC3 (consumed input tokens are not restored on failure) are executor behaviour on a failed completion ('Validation failure is treated as a transition failure', EVT-007); the failure is not a firing of the reference semantics, which has no failed completion, so neither is encoded here.
- AC4 (zero exact assignments → violation; two or more → violation) is the second and third clauses.
- AC5 (Xor(And(A, B, C), And(A, B)) with A, B, C produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac5).
- AC6 (output spec declared, action produces nothing → validation failure on every firing) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 and every output spec (theorem IO_015_ac6): every claim names at least one place, so none equals the empty produced set. That the built-in passthrough is rejected before execution is CORE-043's subject.
- AC7 (mid-action publication) fixes which tokens make up the deposit the validator sees (published places count) and that published tokens stay in the marking on a violation; both are executor behaviour outside the verdict function and are not encoded. With the published places in the deposit, the AC7 verdicts (And(A, B) with A, B produced → success; with A only → violation) are checked on the reference validator.
- AC8 (And is unordered) is not a separate clause: a claim is compared as a set, and permuting the children of an And permutes the assignments and the order of places within a claim. It is checked for the AC8 pair And(A, Xor(D, E)) / And(Xor(D, E), A) on every produced set drawn from A, D, E and one foreign place, the empty one included (theorem IO_015_ac8).
- AC9 (Xor(And(A, C), B) with B and C produced → violation) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac9).
- AC10 (Xor(And(A, Xor(D, E)), A) with only A produced → success) is checked for every validator satisfying IO-015 (theorem IO_015_ac10).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_015_firing"></a>
## IO-015: Output validation: a validated write is deposited

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_015_firing` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with output validation enabled (the default, CONC-026) · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 6ce6a995bcfc59ca ai** · Statement hash `6ce6a995bcfc59ca`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* exactly one assignment claims a set *equal* to the produced set, *then* validation *shall* succeed.<br><br>The comparison is over **sets of places**: a spec names places, not counts, so an action that deposits several tokens into one claimed place conforms. | 1. For every transition t that builds, with output spec o, every marking m at which t is enabled and every deposit d such that exactly one assignment of o claims exactly the produced set of d:<br>2. some firing of t from m deposits d. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    Builds t →<br>      ∀ (o : Out N),<br>        OutputSpec t = some o →<br>          ∀ (m : CountMarking N),<br>            Enabled t m →<br>              ∀ (d : List N),<br>                (∃ i, ExactAssignment o d i ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ), ExactAssignment o d j → j = i) →<br>                  ∃ m', F t m d m'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The firing-level reading of the IO-015 sentences quoted: the block IO_015 fixes the validator's verdict; this one ties the verdict to firings. An action may write any tokens (glossary: Deposit), a completion that passes validation deposits what the action wrote, and one that fails is not a firing (glossary: Fire). So every write that validation accepts is the deposit of some firing. 'Conforms' is read as 'passes validation and is deposited', as IO-016 AC4 says of such a write ('the tokens are deposited regardless').
- Timing and priority play no part: whether the action completes within a Timeout budget is nondeterministic (IO-013), so a validated write is always one way a firing can end.
- The block asks firings only of a transition that builds (glossary: Builds): a transition the build-time checks reject (CORE-022, IO-011 to IO-014) is held by no executor, since every runtime rejects its definition when the net is built, so no firing of it is asked. The firing relation itself ranges over every transition, as CORE-036's does: the witness refFireValidated fires unbuilt transitions too, and a validating executor that holds only transitions that build satisfies the block as well (IO_015_firing_builtOnly).
- CORE-036 compares deposits per place and asks only that the places a firing deposits in be the places of one output branch, each receiving one or more tokens, so it allows such a deposit: both blocks hold of the validated-write executor (theorem CORE_036_IO_015_firing_consistent).

**Evidence**

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-IO_016"></a>
## IO-016: Branch Enumeration

`Libpetri.Spec.IO_016` · Kind **F** · Scope all output specs · Source **verbatim** (spec/02-input-output-specs.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 1271111c6f5c5e23 ai** · Statement hash `1271111c6f5c5e23`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The branch enumeration of a `Place` node *shall* be one output branch, holding that place.<br><br>The branch enumeration of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be one output branch, holding `to`.<br><br>The branch enumeration of an `And` node *shall* be the Cartesian product of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each choice of one output branch per child, holding the union of the chosen output branches, with the first child's choice varying slowest.<br><br>The branch enumeration of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's branch enumerations: one output branch for each output branch of each child, the first child's output branches first.<br><br>The branch enumeration of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's branch enumeration. | 1. Place(p) enumerates exactly the one branch {p};<br>2. ForwardInput(from, to) enumerates exactly the one branch {to};<br>3. And(l, r) enumerates, for each branch x of l in order and, within it, each branch y of r in order, the branch x ∪ y, and nothing else;<br>4. Xor(l, r) enumerates the branches of l, in order, then the branches of r, in order, each as often as it occurs there, and nothing else;<br>5. Timeout(c) enumerates exactly the branches of c, in order. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] E ↦<br>  (∀ (p : N), E (Out.place p) = [{p}]) ∧<br>    (∀ (s d : N), E (Out.forward s d) = [{d}]) ∧<br>      (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.and r) = branchCross (E l) (E r)) ∧<br>        (∀ (l r : Out N), E (l.xor r) = E l ++ E r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), E c.timeout = E c</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A branch enumeration is a function from an output spec alone to a list of output branches, so it is static by its type. A branch is a set of places (`Finset`), as the text says ("a set of places: it says which places receive a token when the branch is taken, not how many"). The list keeps multiplicity (`Xor(P, P)` has two branches) and its order: the lines compare lists with equality, so the enumeration is fixed exactly (`IO_016_unique`). The order is normative because the analyses expand a transition into its branches "in the order above" and name the virtual transitions `<t>_b<i>` in enumeration order ([VER-001]), which the byte-identical SMT scripts carry ([VER-013]).
- An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it. List append and the lexicographic Cartesian product are associative and union is associative, so the nesting changes neither the branches nor their order: the n-ary product with the first child slowest is the right-nested product of binary ones.
- A branch read as a set loses a repeated claim: `And(P, P)` enumerates {P}, while the reference `Out.branches` lists [P, P]. IO-011 rejects such a spec when it is built, so on every buildable spec the two agree (`IO_016_card_of_wf`: each set has as many places as the list it reads).
- The list has one entry per assignment (IO-015), counted by position, so on a spec that builds no two entries are the same set: IO-012 rejects at build time any spec with two distinct assignments claiming one set, and its check enumerates per IO-016 and compares the entries as sets in index order (the numbering of VER-001's `<t>_b<i>`). The paragraph saying so is a consequence of IO-012's build check, not a further constraint on the enumeration; it is derived, not stated (`IO_016_nodup_of_wf`). The enumeration itself is defined on every spec, ambiguous ones included, because the build check is computed from it.
- A spec that builds holds at most one `Timeout` node, and a `ForwardInput` only inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014). The `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines still fix the enumeration on every spec: the enumeration is a total function on output specs, and the build checks read it before a spec is known to build.
- AC1 (`And(P1, P2)` → {P1, P2}) follows from lines 1 and 3; AC2 (`Xor(P1, P2)` → {P1}, {P2}) from lines 1 and 4; AC3 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), P3)` → {P1, P2}, {P3}) from lines 1, 3 and 4. The non-vacuity theorem checks all three on the reference enumeration.
- AC4 (the executor's WARN log-message event when a validated firing deposits more than one token in a place its matched branch names, at most once per transition per execution) is an [EVT-013] event of a running executor, and is skipped with the rest of validation by the CONC-026 option. Neither the branch enumeration nor the firing relation has an event store or an execution, and the reference executor does not emit this warning (Reference/Events.lean), so no block states AC4: it is Q-tested, with the test derivation's three cases (two tokens to the one place the spec names, fired three times: every token lands and one warning is emitted; `And(A, B)` with three tokens to A and two to B: one warning naming `(A: 3, B: 2)`; one token per named place: no event) in every runtime, the Rust, Java and TypeScript suites on both backends: Rust `backend_suite_tests` (the libpetri-runtime backend suite) `multiplicity_warns_once_per_transition`, `multiplicity_names_every_repeated_place` and `multiplicity_silent_for_one_token_per_place`; Java `java/src/test/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BackendDivergenceRegressionTest.java` `multiplicity_warnsOncePerTransitionWhenAnActionWritesTwoTokensToAPlaceNamedOnce`, `multiplicity_warnsThroughACompositeSpecNamingEveryRepeatedPlace` and `multiplicity_staysSilentWhenEveryNamedPlaceReceivesExactlyOneToken`; TypeScript `typescript/tests/runtime/executor-shared-semantics.test.ts` (describe 'branch multiplicity diagnostic', three cases); Python `python/tests/test_output_validation.py` `test_multiplicity_warns_once_per_transition`, `test_multiplicity_names_every_repeated_place` and `test_multiplicity_is_silent_for_one_token_per_named_place`. AC4's logger `libpetri.runtime` is omitted where the log-message event carries no logger field, as for the diagnostics of CORE-037 and CORE-072 AC4: EVT-013 gives the event a logger name in Java and TypeScript only, and Rust's `NetEvent::LogMessage` has no logger field (`rust/libpetri-event/src/net_event.rs`), so Rust and Python carry the level, the transition name and the message, and Java (`BitmapNetExecutor.java` and `PrecompiledNetExecutor.java` `warnMultiplicity`) and TypeScript (`bitmap-net-executor.ts` `warnMultiplicity`) carry the logger as well.
- The statement is generic in the place type `N` and its equality, so a branch is a set under the implementation's own place identity (CORE-002: the name, or the name and the token type; glossary: Same set of places). Rust's branches are sets of `PlaceRef`, compared by name (`rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `enumerate_branches`), and Java's are sets of `Place` records, compared by name and token type (MOD-024; `Arc.java` `enumerateBranches`), so both meet the lines under their identity. TypeScript's identity is the name (CORE-002 line 2, ruling D82 (a)), and `enumerateBranches` (`typescript/src/core/out.ts`, its `crossProduct`) keeps one place object per name in a branch, the first met, so `And(place('A'), place('A'))` with two separate objects gives one branch holding one place, as the third line says. A branch built as a JS `Set` of place objects keyed by reference would hold two members there (the behaviour RD-03 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of TypeScript), which the third line rejects under name identity. On a spec that builds the two agree anyway: TypeScript's IO-011 check (`duplicateInBranch`) and IO-012 check (`ambiguousBranches`) compare place names, so no branch of a buildable spec holds two objects of one name, and the analyses key a branch's deposits by name (`typescript/src/verification/analysis/branch-outcomes.ts` `outcomes`).
- A branch fixes which places receive tokens, not how many: with output validation enabled, a firing that ends with its action deposits one or more tokens in each place of one output branch and none in any other (glossary: Output branch, IO-015, CORE-036). The paragraph on what the analyses deposit (one token per place of a branch: VER-010, VER-001, NU-051) describes those analyses, not the enumeration, and is their subject. The reference firing semantics deposits one token per claim of a branch, the case the analyses model; the non-vacuity theorem shows one such firing.
- The paragraph on the timeout outcome says that it is not an output branch (glossary: Timeout outcome), which the `Timeout` line respects by enumerating the child's branches only; the `ForwardInput` line is the branch an action writes, `to` claimed once (glossary: Forward, IO-015), not the timeout outcome's per-consumed-token deposit (IO-014). How the analyses append the timeout outcome after the branches, when it differs place by place from every branch (deposits compared per place, CORE-036), is VER-001's subject.
- The block fixes the enumeration function only. That executors and analyses use it (the executor's validation, the SCG virtual transitions, the flattener) is the subject of IO-015, VER-001 and VER-010.

| The `allPlaces` set of a `Place` node *shall* be the set holding only that place.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of a `ForwardInput(from, to)` node *shall* be the set holding only `to`.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of an `And` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of an `Xor` node *shall* be the union of its children's `allPlaces` sets.<br><br>The `allPlaces` set of a `Timeout` node *shall* be its child's `allPlaces` set. | 1. Place(p) gives exactly the set {p};<br>2. ForwardInput(from, to) gives exactly the set {to};<br>3. And(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;<br>4. Xor(l, r) gives exactly the union of the sets of l and r;<br>5. Timeout(c) gives exactly the set of c. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] A ↦<br>  (∀ (p : N), A (Out.place p) = {p}) ∧<br>    (∀ (s d : N), A (Out.forward s d) = {d}) ∧<br>      (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.and r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧<br>        (∀ (l r : Out N), A (l.xor r) = A l ∪ A r) ∧ ∀ (c : Out N), A c.timeout = A c</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A place-set function is a function from an output spec alone to a finite set of places (`Finset`), so it is static by its type and has no order and no repetition: the text and every runtime return a set (Rust `HashSet<PlaceRef>`, Java `Set<Place<?>>`, TypeScript `Set<Place<any>>`). The lines compare sets with equality, so they fix the function exactly (`IO_017_unique`).
- The lines say "be" and "holding only": the set equals the places the text names, so it is complete (every place, every `Xor` alternative, every `Timeout` child) and exact (nothing else). The markdown's prose ("collect all leaf places") and test derivation ("complete set") state completeness only; the block reads collecting the leaf places as returning them and nothing else, which is what all three runtimes do (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The containment reading is strictly weaker (`IO_017_mutant_superset_killed`), and a `Place` leaf that also names another place is forbidden (`IO_017_forbids_placeExtra`).
- The statement is generic in the place type `N` and its equality, so the set is a set under the implementation's own place identity, which CORE-002 fixes as the name or the name and the token type (line 3, ruling D82 (a)); the glossary entry Same set of places means that identity. Rust's set compares `PlaceRef` by name and Java's set compares `Place` records by name and token type (MOD-024), so both meet the lines under their identity. TypeScript's identity is the name (CORE-002 line 2), and `allPlaces` and `collectPlaces` (`typescript/src/core/out.ts`) collect into a map from name to place, keeping the first object met for each name, so two separate place objects of one name are one member: `Xor(And(A, B), And(A', C))` with `A` and `A'` two `place('A')` objects builds (TypeScript's IO-011 and IO-012 checks compare names) and gives three members, A, B and C, the union the third and fourth lines give. A set of place objects keyed by reference would give four members for those three places (the behaviour RD-03 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded of TypeScript), which the lines reject under name identity.
- An n-ary `And` or `Xor` is read as right-nested binary nodes, as `Reference.Out` writes it and IO-016 does. Union is associative, so the nesting does not change the set. An `And` with one child (the runtimes allow it; an `Xor` needs two) is that child, which the n-ary union also gives.
- The second line strengthens AC2 (`ForwardInput(from, to)` contributes `to`), which does not say that `from` is left out: it reads AC2 as contributing `to` and nothing else. It says "only `to`" rather than "not `from`" because `from` and `to` may be one place, and then the set holds it. The reading follows the text: the prose collects the places the spec writes to, `from` is an input place (IO-014), and all three runtimes add only `to` (Rust `rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs` `collect_places`, Java `Arc.java` `allPlaces`, TypeScript `out.ts` `collectPlaces`). The glossary entries Forward ("In an output branch it claims `to`") and Output arc (a place the output spec names) say the same, so a forward makes `to`, not `from`, an output arc.
- The function is defined on every output spec, ones that fail a build-time check included: the `Timeout` and `ForwardInput` lines fix it whether or not the spec has one `Timeout` node and its forwards inside that node's child (IO-013, IO-014), since the build checks and the glossary read it before a spec is known to build.
- AC1 (`Xor(And(P1, P2), Timeout(5s, P3))` gives {P1, P2, P3}) follows from lines 1, 3, 4 and 5; the timeout's duration does not matter, since `Reference.Out` carries none and the fifth line reads only the child. AC2 is the second line. The non-vacuity theorem checks both on the reference function, and the test derivation (a nested spec gives the complete set) is AC1.
- The relation to IO-016 is derived, not stated: the set is the union of the output branches of the branch enumeration (`IO_017_union_of_branches`, for every pair of functions that satisfy IO-016 and IO-017). So is the relation to the glossary's output arcs (`IO_017_outputArc`).
- The block fixes the function only. That the output specification offers it as a method is an API fact of each runtime and is not encoded. That executors and analyses read output places through it (CORE-035, CORE-062, CORE-072, VER-001) is the subject of those requirements.
