<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_001"></a>
## MOD-001: SubnetDef Definition (open net + interface)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_001` · Kind **F** · Scope every subnet builder · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ae54063c8dcfb969 ai** · Statement hash `ae54063c8dcfb969`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared ports, each with the name, direction and place it was declared with.<br><br>*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its interface *shall* hold exactly the declared channels, each with the name and transition it was declared with.<br><br>*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, its body *shall* hold the places and terminal places of the net that the net builder builds from the declaration, and the declared transitions in the order they were added, none of them renamed.<br><br>*When* building the subnet definition succeeds, the subnet definition *shall* keep the name it was declared with.<br><br>*When* the net builder builds the body and the interface declares no port and no channel, building the subnet definition *shall* succeed. | 1. For every net builder NB of subnet bodies and every subnet builder SB:<br>2. if SB builds S as the definition D, the ports of D are the ports of S (same name, direction and place), each as often as in S, in any order;<br>3. if SB builds S as D, the channels of D are the channels of S (same name and transition name), each as often as in S, in any order;<br>4. if SB builds S as D and NB builds the body of S as b, a place is a place of D exactly when it is a place of b, a place is a terminal place of D exactly when it is a terminal place of b, a transition definition is one of D exactly when it is one of S, and, when the transition names of S are pairwise distinct, the transition definitions of D are those of S, in the same order;<br>5. if SB builds S as D, the name of D is the name of S;<br>6. if NB builds the body of S and S declares no port and no channel, SB succeeds on S. | <pre>fun {N A} NB SB ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (D : SubnetDef N A), SB S = Except.ok D → D.ports.Perm S.ports) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (D : SubnetDef N A),<br>        SB S = Except.ok D → D.chans.Perm S.chans) ∧<br>      (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (D : SubnetDef N A) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>          SB S = Except.ok D →<br>            NB S.body = Except.ok b →<br>              (∀ (p : N), p ∈ D.places ↔ p ∈ b.places) ∧<br>                (∀ (p : N), p ∈ D.terminals ↔ p ∈ b.terminals) ∧<br>                  (∀ (d : CDef N A), d ∈ D.defs ↔ d ∈ S.defs) ∧<br>                    ((List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) S.defs).Nodup → D.defs = S.defs)) ∧<br>        (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (D : SubnetDef N A), SB S = Except.ok D → D.name = S.name) ∧<br>          ∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>            NB S.body = Except.ok b →<br>              S.ports = [] → S.chans = [] → ∃ D, SB S = Except.ok D</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A subnet builder (SubnetMake) and the body net builder NB are read as in MOD-006: SB is the build call of one implementation's subnet-definition builder, NB the net builder it builds the body with, typed as a CORE-040 net builder over defsTB so that CORE-040, EXEC-042, MOD-006 and this block speak of the same function. All three runtimes return the declared name, the built body itself and an interface made of the declared ports and channels (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:378-430, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:624-662, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:539-580); Python rides on Rust. The holds theorem holds for every NB.
- Lines 1 and 2 compare ports and channels as permutations (List.Perm), not as lists: Rust keeps the interface in hash maps (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:104-107), so its iteration order is not the declaration order (MOD_001_allows_portOrder), while Java and TypeScript copy the declared lists. A permutation keeps the count of each entry, so a definition that lists a declared port or channel twice violates line 1 or 2 (MOD_001_forbids_dupChans), which a comparison of sets would let through; no runtime duplicates an entry, since a success has pairwise distinct port names and channel names (MOD-006 lines 3 and 4) and the Rust maps are keyed by those names. A port is its name, direction and place, so a builder that forgets a direction violates line 1. A channel is its name and the name of its transition (ruling D23, settled by D10); Java and TypeScript keep the transition object, which under the unique-names assumption is the same thing. Duplicate names never reach a success (MOD-006 lines 3 and 4), so a declaration S never lists one port or channel twice on a success either.
- Line 3 states the body against the net b that NB builds; that a success comes with a body NB builds at all is MOD-006 line 5, not repeated here. The places include every place an arc of a body transition names (CORE-040), so a port on such a place exposes a place of the definition. Places and terminal places are compared as sets (CORE-040 fixes their collection, not their order). The transition definitions are stated against the declaration in two parts. Unconditionally, as a set: a transition definition is one of D exactly when it was declared, so no declared transition is dropped and none is added, even when two share a name (MOD_001_forbids_dropDupNamed). As a list in the order added, under the premise that their names are pairwise distinct, the unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23 (TIME-010; no builder checks names): without it Java and TypeScript keep a transition object added twice once (an insertion-ordered set, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:286, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:159), Rust twice (a vector, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:337), and all three meet the set part. A definition carries its correspondence (MOD-031) unchanged, because the line equates the whole definitions. Jointly with CORE-040 the definitions are the built body's transitions (mod001_instantiable).
- Line 4 keeps the definition's name, which the runtimes use in their messages (MOD-006) and which direct composition records as the subnet a node belongs to (MOD-026).
- Line 5 is AC3's 'possibly empty' set of ports and channels: an empty interface is no reason to reject. Jointly with MOD-006 line 6 it is implied there, but this block states it of its own.
- AC1 (a subnet definition can be constructed with a body net and an interface) is line 5 together with MOD-006 line 6 (the acceptance line) and the nonvacuity example. AC2 (the body follows all CORE construction rules and is itself immutable per CORE-041): the construction rules are the net builder's (CORE-040, EXEC-042) and MOD-006 line 5 rejects a body they refuse; immutability is a quality property of host values (Lean values are immutable; builder stability is CORE-041's line), tested and not proven. AC3 (the interface enumerates a possibly empty set of ports and a possibly empty set of channels) is lines 1, 2 and 5 for what a built interface holds and for the empty interface, and MOD-006 line 6 for a non-empty interface that builds. AC4 (the definition exposes body() and iface()) is lines 1 to 3: what they hold; the accessor names are API surface, tested and not proven. AC5 (immutable after construction) is a quality property, as for AC2.
- The MAY sentence on a typed Params value and the sentence 'When unparameterised, the parameter type is the implementation's unit/void type' are not modelled: the parameter type is compile-time typing (MOD-010 AC4), and Python offers unparameterised definitions only (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:626, :907), which the MAY allows. The test derivation (two places, one transition, one port; body, interface, port set and channel set accessible and unmodifiable) is the nonvacuity example for the accessible part and AC2/AC5 for the unmodifiable part.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_001_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_001): ✓ The reference subnet builder satisfies MOD-001 for every net builder: what it returns is the declared name, the declared ports and channels, and the body the net builder built, with the declared transitions in the order added; and a subnet with no port and no channel builds whenever its body does.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N]<br>  (NB : NetBuilder (defsTB N A)), MOD_001 NB (refSubnetBuild NB)</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_001_allows_portOrder` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_001): ✓ MOD-001 does not fix the order of the ports. A builder that returns them in reverse order, as Rust's hash map may, meets it: for `buf` it lists the ports `out`, `in` where the reference lists `in`, `out`, and both hold the same two ports.
  <pre>MOD_001 refNetBuild (postSB refNetBuild revPorts) ∧<br>  (∃ D,<br>      postSB refNetBuild revPorts mod006_exS = Except.ok D ∧<br>        List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) D.ports = ["out", "in"]) ∧<br>    ∃ D,<br>      refSubnetBuild refNetBuild mod006_exS = Except.ok D ∧<br>        List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) D.ports = ["in", "out"]</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_001_forbids_dropDupNamed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_001): ✗ A builder that drops every transition whose name occurs more than once violates MOD-001 (line 3): `buf` with `take` added twice builds, and its definition holds no transition at all, although `take` was declared. With distinct names it keeps every transition, so the in-order part of line 3 alone does not reject it. No runtime drops a transition: Rust keeps both copies, Java and TypeScript one.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_003"></a>
## MOD-003: Port Declaration (name + direction + place)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_003` · Kind **B** · Scope every subnet builder · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 bf78e1b0f9221c62 ai** · Statement hash `bf78e1b0f9221c62`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* two ports of one interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.<br><br>*If* the net builder builds the body and a port exposes a place that is not a place of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* building a subnet definition succeeds, building it with one more port, whose name no port of the interface has and which exposes the place of one of its ports, *shall* also succeed, whatever the directions of the two ports. | 1. For every net builder NB of subnet bodies and every subnet builder SB:<br>2. if two ports of S have the same name, SB fails on S;<br>3. if NB builds the body of S as the net b and some port of S exposes a place that is not a place of b, SB fails on S;<br>4. if SB builds S, q is a port of S, n is the name of no port of S and d is any direction, SB builds S with the port (n, d, place of q) appended to its ports. | <pre>fun {N A} NB SB ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A),<br>      ¬(List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.ports).Nodup → ∃ msg, SB S = Except.error msg) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        NB S.body = Except.ok b →<br>          ∀ q ∈ S.ports, q.place ∉ b.places → ∃ msg, SB S = Except.error msg) ∧<br>      ∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (D : SubnetDef N A),<br>        SB S = Except.ok D →<br>          ∀ q ∈ S.ports,<br>            ∀ (n : String) (d : Dir),<br>              n ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.ports →<br>                ∃ D',<br>                  SB<br>                      { name := S.name, places := S.places, defs := S.defs,<br>                        terminals := S.terminals,<br>                        ports := S.ports ++ [{ name := n, dir := d, place := q.place }],<br>                        chans := S.chans } =<br>                    Except.ok D'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A subnet builder (SubnetMake) and the body net builder NB are those of MOD-006 (Spec/Req/MOD_006.lean): the build call of one implementation's subnet-definition builder, read as a function from what the host declared to a subnet definition or a rejection with a message, and the net builder that builds the body first (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:378-430, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:624-662, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:539-580). Line 1 is MOD-006's line 3 and line 2 is MOD-006's line 1, quoted here because the markdown states them under the port declaration too; which offender a failure names is MOD-006's line 7.
- Ruling D35 (a): two distinct ports may expose one body place, whatever their directions, as in every runtime (the subnet builders rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:388-404, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:630-643, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:549-563 check only the port name and the place). Line 3 states the permission as acceptance: adding a port of a new name over the place of an existing port never turns a successful build into a failure. It is relative and appends the new port at the end of the ports; the quote names no position. On its own the block therefore lets a builder reject every subnet that has a port (line 3 is then never triggered); the absolute 'they build' of AC5 and of the MAY sentence 'Two distinct ports MAY expose the same body place', and the insertion of the new port at any other position, are MOD-006 line 6, from which line 3 follows (mod003_of_mod006). The prose sentence 'When two ports expose one body place, a caller binds both to one caller place' is MOD-020's coherent-call precondition (mod020_coherent in Spec/Req/MOD_020.lean): MOD-020 states its binding lines on coherent calls only. Which binding a composition keeps when the two ports are bound to two different caller places is not defined (MOD-020); Rust and Java keep one binding in the iteration order of the caller's map (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1050-1068, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:718). D35 (b), rejecting a shared place at subnet build, is a later runtime change that would replace line 3.
- Line 2 compares a port's place with the places of the built body by equality on the place type N, as MOD-006 line 1 does (CORE-002: by name in TypeScript, Rust and Python, by name and token type in Java, rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:396, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:637, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:556). So a port over a place of name p and token type Integer, on a body that holds p of token type String, is rejected in Java only. The prose MUST sentence 'The exposed place MUST be a place of the subnet's body' is line 2 (and AC4) when the body builds; when it does not, MOD-006 line 5 makes the build fail. That a port on any place of the built body is accepted, including a place only an arc of a body transition names, is MOD-006 line 6: a builder that checks a port's place against the declared places instead of the built body meets MOD-003 and violates MOD-006 (mod003_declPlaces).
- Line 1 reads 'unique within the interface' over the ports alone: port names and channel names are two namespaces (MOD-006). Java refuses a blank port name when the port value is constructed (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:122-144), before any subnet builder sees it, so line 3's new name n ranges over the names Java can construct; TypeScript and Rust accept a blank name. On the interface-builder route of MOD-014 (fromNet) a duplicate port name is rejected even earlier, at the port() call (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:164-170, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:183-190, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:107-113), which meets AC2's 'at build' since it is not later.
- AC1 (a port can be declared with name, direction and a body place) is the Port record of Spec/GlossaryCompose.lean (name, dir, place; Dir has exactly the three directions input, output and in-out); that a built subnet definition keeps every declared port with its name, direction and place is MOD-001's line. AC2 (the port name is unique, duplicates rejected at build) is line 1, stated of the subnet builder itself. AC3 (the exposed place's token type is preserved in the port's typed handle) is MOD_011_typed's, scoped by ruling D36 (a) to the implementations that keep a run-time token type for each port, Java and Rust; its compile-time reading is withdrawn (MOD-011, ruling D36 (a)). TypeScript's port<T>(name) takes T as an annotation it does not check (typescript/src/core/instance.ts:79-85) and Python's lookup takes no type, so for them AC3 is out of scope by the same ruling and no block states it. AC4 (a port whose place is not in the body is rejected at build) is line 2. AC5 (two ports of different names over one body place build, whatever their directions) is line 3 relative to a build, and MOD-006 line 6 for the build itself, with MOD_003_nonvacuous as the worked case.

So a subnet instantiated under `p1`, bound to the caller and built, is read by every block in the same way: the same renamed places, the same transitions, the same build check, the same correspondences and the same firings.

## MOD-004: Port Direction Semantics (advisory; arcs govern flow)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_004` · Kind **B** · Scope every subnet builder and every instantiation of a subnet definition · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 64f5c60f41ba81c3 ai** · Statement hash `64f5c60f41ba81c3`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|

**Assumptions**

- Kind B at MUST, rulings D20 and R-MA7 (2): the requirement was SHOULD, but its normative sentence is the MUST NOT on rejecting a subnet for a direction-versus-arc mismatch, so its priority is raised to MUST. No runtime changes: Rust, Java and TypeScript read a port's direction only in the doc generators (rust/libpetri-docgen/src/subnet_header.rs:98-100, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/doclet/SubnetHeader.java:89-91) and in the verification harness of MOD-051 (rust/libpetri-verification/src/harness.rs:380-407, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:290-320, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:273-284). In rust/libpetri-core/src the only uses of PortDirection are the declaration and the three port constructors (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:350-362, rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:172-184); Java encodes the direction as the record class of the port (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:113-143), and no class of java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core switches on it outside verify. Python rides on Rust.
- Line 1 is the MUST NOT ('MUST NOT reject the subnet on direction-versus-arc mismatch') and AC2 and AC3 read for every builder: a subnet that builds with some directions builds with every other choice of directions, so no arc structure under a port can make its direction a reason to reject. It states acceptance only, not the message of a failure nor the built value: Rust keeps the ports of an interface in a hash map (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:104-107), so two builds need not list ports in one order, and which offender a message names is MOD-006's line 7. Line 1 depends on ruling D35 (a), which dropped MOD-003's sentence that two ports of one direction over one body place are rejected: no runtime implements that check (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:388-404, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:630-643, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:549-562), and a builder that does violates line 1 (MOD_004_forbids_sameDirCheck). Jointly with MOD-006 line 1 follows (mod004_line1_of_mod006), since MOD-006 decides acceptance from the body and the names and places of the ports; the line is kept so that MOD-004 says it on its own.
- Line 2 states for instantiate what line 1 states for the subnet builder, and adds what an instance holds: its places as a set (Rust collects them through a hash map, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:84-96), its transition definitions in order and whole (arcs, timing, priority, action and the declared-to-actual correspondence of MOD-031; no runtime's rewriter reads a direction, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:180-181 and :277-310, so an instantiation that builds a correspondence from the directions is rejected, MOD_004_forbids_inputCorr), its port and channel handles name by name (MOD-011), and its interface ports as a set of names and places. It does not compare the prefix nor the messages of failures. The instance's interface ports carry the definition's directions in the reference (refInst keeps the ports); that the instance keeps them is not stated, since MOD-004 AC1 asks only that the direction be queryable on the definition's port and the instance handle of MOD-011 returns a place without a direction (rust/libpetri-core/src/instance.rs:109).
- Line 3 is AC1 (direction metadata is preserved and queryable via the port handle): the port handle is the interface's port, looked up by name (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:247-257 tests exactly this). The line asks that a port of every declared name exists and carries the declared direction, which the lookup by name then returns. It compares ports by name and not as a list, since Rust's interface is a hash map. A declaration with two ports of one name never builds (MOD-006 line 3), so line 3 asks nothing contradictory of a builder that meets MOD-006. That the definition holds exactly the declared ports, channels and body is MOD-001's line; a builder that stores every port as InOut meets lines 1 and 2 and is killed by line 3 alone (MOD_004_mutant_noDirection_killed).
- AC2 (a subnet whose Output port place is also written internally by transitions is accepted at build) and AC3 (a subnet whose Input port place is also read internally by transitions is accepted at build) are exercised on the reference by MOD_004_nonvacuous: the subnet relay, whose Output port place out is written by take and consumed by drain and whose Input port place in is read by peek and consumed by take, builds, and so does the same subnet with the two directions swapped. For every builder that meets MOD-006 over the reference net builder, relay builds with every choice of directions (mod004_relay_builds). The block alone does not force a build: a builder that rejects everything meets lines 1 to 3, and acceptance is MOD-006's line 6.
- AC4 (where a warning channel exists, an obvious mismatch MAY emit a warning but MUST NOT raise an error) is line 1 for the error half: MOD_004_nonvacuous builds watch, an Input port whose place no transition consumes from, and the same subnet with an Output port that no transition produces into. The warning half is not stated: no runtime emits such a warning (no warn call in the subnet or interface sources of any language), and a warning channel is not modelled. The sentence 'Implementations MAY emit a build-time warning when declared direction conflicts with the arc structure' is a MAY with no runtime witness, recorded as kind N in the plan.
- The sentence that direction does not constrain arc flow at run time ('Actual token flow at run time is governed exclusively by arcs declared per CORE-030..CORE-035') is line 2's 'the same transitions': an instance's transitions, and so its firing (MOD-010's mod010_firesAsBody), do not depend on any direction. That composition does not read direction either (prose of the reworded first sentence) is a property of the composition functions of MOD-020 to MOD-025 and is not stated here; the composition wave states their lines on names and places only.

So the subnet `relay` builds whether its port `in` is an `Input` or an `Output` port, and instantiating it under `r1` gives the same renamed places and transitions either way.

## MOD-005: Channel Declaration (interface transitions for synchronous fusion)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_005` · Kind **B** · Scope every subnet builder · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0fc847fd04bda40d ai** · Statement hash `0fc847fd04bda40d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* two channels of the interface have the same name, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.<br><br>*If* a channel of the interface exposes a transition whose name is not the name of a transition of the built body, *then* building the subnet definition *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* the net builder builds the body, the subnet definition builds without its channels, every channel exposes a transition of the built body, no two channels have the same name, and no channel has the name of a port, building the subnet definition with its channels *shall* succeed. | 1. For every net builder NB of subnet bodies and every subnet builder SB:<br>2. if two channels of S have the same name, SB fails on S;<br>3. if NB builds the body of S as the net b and some channel of S names a transition that is not the name of a transition of b, SB fails on S;<br>4. if NB builds the body of S as b, SB succeeds on S without its channels, every channel of S names a transition of b, the channel names of S are pairwise distinct and no channel of S has the name of a port of S, then SB succeeds on S. | <pre>fun {N A} NB SB ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A),<br>      ¬(List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.chans).Nodup → ∃ msg, SB S = Except.error msg) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        NB S.body = Except.ok b →<br>          ∀ c ∈ S.chans,<br>            c.trans ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) b.trans →<br>              ∃ msg, SB S = Except.error msg) ∧<br>      ∀ (S : SubnetIn N A) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        NB S.body = Except.ok b →<br>          (∃ D, SB S.withoutChans = Except.ok D) →<br>            (∀ c ∈ S.chans, c.trans ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) b.trans) →<br>              (List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.chans).Nodup →<br>                (∀ c ∈ S.chans, c.name ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.ports) →<br>                  ∃ D, SB S = Except.ok D</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The subnet builder SB (SubnetMake) and the body net builder NB are MOD-006's: SB is the build call of one implementation's subnet-definition builder, read as a function from what the host declared (SubnetIn: name, declared places, transition definitions, declared terminal places, ports, channels) to a subnet definition or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception, read as .error msg); NB is a parameter typed as a CORE-040 net builder over defsTB, and the holds theorem holds for every NB. Every runtime builds the body first and checks the channels against the built net after the ports (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:406-423, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:645-658, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:563-575).
- Line 1 is AC2 and the channel half of item 1 ('A name unique within the interface'); it is MOD-006 line 4. The three runtimes also reject a second channel of one name when an interface is assembled by hand for fromNet (MOD-014), at the channel() call itself (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:191-194, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:205-210, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:134-140), which is earlier than the subnet build and meets AC4's 'at build' as well.
- Line 2 is AC4 and item 2 read under rulings D10 and D23 and the R-MA3 (a) reading of the mod-a map, as in MOD-006 line 2: the model's channel carries the name of the transition it exposes, and a channel whose transition's name is the name of no body transition fails in every runtime. Rust and Python store and compare names (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:75-80, rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:415); Java and TypeScript compare transition objects (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:652, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:570), so a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is rejected there and accepted in Rust. That case is implementation-defined in the markdown and outside the block: under the unique-names assumption of D10 and D23 two transitions of one name are one transition (no builder checks names).
- Line 3 is the acceptance line for channels (skeptic correction S2 of the composition design), and the behaviour half of AC1 ('A channel can be declared with a name and a body transition'): channels that meet lines 1 and 2 add no reason to reject. It is relative to the same subnet without its channels, so that the ports and the body stay MOD-006's matter; a builder that rejects every subnet therefore meets this block, and MOD-006 line 6 rules it out. Every builder that meets MOD-006 meets line 3 (mod005_of_mod006).
- Item 1 leaves to the implementation whether port names and channel names share one namespace, and asks that a collision be rejected when they do. Line 3 therefore asks nothing when a channel has the name of a port, and a builder with one shared namespace meets the block (MOD_005_allows_sharedNamespace). No runtime shares the namespace: each keeps two maps or lists (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:105-106 and :151-152, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:178-179, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:103-104), and MOD-006's markdown fixes two namespaces for subnet definitions, so that MOD-006 line 6 rejects the shared-namespace builder. The conditional MUST of item 1 has no case in libpetri and is not a line.
- AC1's existence half (an implementation offers a way to declare a channel with a name and a body transition) is an offer clause, not a safety line: every runtime offers it (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:366, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:617, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:532), and MOD_005_nonvacuous builds a subnet with a declared channel. That the built definition keeps the declared channels, each once, is MOD-001 line 2 (the built channels are a permutation of the declared ones): a builder that validates as the reference and then registers every channel twice fails and succeeds exactly where the reference does, so it meets this block, whose lines speak of failure and success only, and it violates MOD-001 (MOD_001_forbids_dupChans), so the name stays unique within the built interface as item 1 asks. AC3 (the exposed transition's identity is preserved through the channel handle) is MOD-011's line: the handle of channel n of an instance under prefix p names the renamed transition p/x. The paragraph 'A channel MAY be bound at composition time' is MOD-020's and MOD-021's (binding and the merged transition). Java refuses a blank channel name when the channel value is constructed (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:167), before any subnet builder sees it; TypeScript and Rust accept a blank name.
- Error messages are MOD-006 line 7's matter; this block asks only that the build fail or succeed. The test derivation's first half (the handle resolves to the renamed transition) is MOD-011's; its second half (two channels of one name are rejected) is line 1.

**Assumptions**

- A subnet builder (SubnetMake) is the build call of one implementation's subnet-definition builder, read as a function from what the host declared (SubnetIn: the definition's name, the declared places, the transition definitions in the order added, the declared terminal places, the ports and the channels) to a subnet definition or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception, read as .error msg). The body net builder NB is a parameter: every runtime builds the body with its net builder first and checks the interface against the built net (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:379-423, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:624-658, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:539-575). NB is typed as a CORE-040 net builder over defsTB (instances are the body's definitions), so CORE-040, EXEC-042's build block and this block speak of the same function; the holds theorem holds for every NB.
- Line 1 and line 6 compare a port's place with the places of the built body by equality on the place type N (CORE-002: by name in TypeScript, Rust and Python, by name and token type in Java, rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:395, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:637, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:556). The built body holds the declared places and every place an arc of a body transition names (CORE-040 line 2 and line 3), so under any net builder that meets CORE-040 a port on a place that only an arc names is accepted and a port on a place nobody declared or named fails (mod006_core040).
- Line 2 and line 6 match a channel to a body transition by name (ruling D23, settled by D10, and the R-MA3 (a) reading of the mod-a map): the model's channel carries the transition's name, so line 6's 'every channel exposes a transition of the built body' reads as 'the name of every channel's transition is the name of a transition of the built body'. Rust and Python store and compare names (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:75-80, rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:415); Java and TypeScript compare transition objects (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:652, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:570), so a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a body transition is rejected there and accepted in Rust. Under the shared unique-names assumption (D10, D23; no builder checks names) two transitions of one name are one transition, and that case is outside the block. The markdown calls it implementation-defined and keeps line 6 on transitions, not names, so that the English line does not decide it: a channel whose transition's name is no body transition's name fails everywhere (line 2), a channel over a body transition builds everywhere (line 6). The markdown cites TIME-010 for the unique-names assumption, where ruling D10 put it (spec/03-timing.md:276).
- Lines 3, 4 and 6 treat port names and channel names as two namespaces, as all three runtimes do: a port and a channel may share a name, and line 6 then asks the build to succeed. MOD-005 item 1 leaves a shared namespace implementation-defined; MOD-006's markdown fixes the two namespaces for subnet definitions ('Port names and channel names are two namespaces'), so an implementation with one shared namespace violates line 6. Java refuses a blank port or channel name when the port or channel value is constructed (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:122-170, :244-247), before any subnet builder sees it, so line 6 speaks of the ports and channels Java can construct; TypeScript and Rust accept a blank name. On the interface-builder route of MOD-014 (fromNet) a duplicate name is rejected even earlier, at the port() or channel() call (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:164-170, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:183-190, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:107-113), which meets AC1's 'not later'.
- Line 5 is item 5 as reworded under rulings D20 and R-MA7 (3): a body the net builder rejects yields no subnet definition. The CORE-041 reference of the old item is dropped (CORE-041 is immutability and names no check). Through the subnet builders of the runtimes the case cannot arise: they take places, transitions, ports and channels only, transition checks run when a transition is built (CORE-020), and without composition and fusion the net builder rejects only a terminal place that a transition consumes from or reads (EXEC-042 AC5), which no subnet builder can declare. The model's input carries terminal places (for fromNet, MOD-014), so under the reference net builder the line has an instance: a body whose terminal place a transition consumes from (MOD_006_nonvacuous). A body that declares a terminal place and no such clash builds under every net builder that meets EXEC-042's build block, and then line 6 asks the subnet build to succeed when the interface is fine (mod006_exec042; MOD_006_nonvacuous builds buf with the terminal place done); instantiate and composition refuse such a body (EXEC-042 AC6; MOD-010 line 4, MOD-025 line 7).
- Line 6 is implied by line 7 (mod006_line6_of_line7): when the body builds and no port or channel offends, line 7 leaves no message a failure could carry, so the build succeeds. Line 6 is kept as the acceptance line the composition design asks of every partial builder (skeptic correction S2) and has no mutant of its own (as for MOD-010 AC2, skeptic correction S4).
- Line 7 is AC2 and the sentence 'Each failure MUST produce an error identifying the offending element by name.': to name an element is for the message to contain its name as a substring (List.IsInfix on the characters). A duplicate port or channel name (cases 3 and 4) does not depend on the body, so a message naming it meets the line whether or not the net builder builds the body, and a builder may check the names before it builds the body (MOD_006_allows_namesFirst; the markdown's 'may be checked before the body is built'); a port or channel offends against case 1 or 2 only when the body builds. The three runtimes build the body first. The line is existential over the offenders: the runtimes walk the ports in declaration order (duplicate name, then place), then the channels (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:388-423, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:630-658, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:549-575), and Rust's from_net walks a hash set, so which offender is named when there are several is not stated. All three runtimes name the port or channel and also its place or transition; the line asks for the port or channel only. A body rejection passes the net builder's message through unchanged in all three (a panic or exception from the body build); the line allows a message that wraps it.
- Naming by substring is weaker than 'identifying', taken as the modelling choice. A message names every port or channel whose name it happens to contain: the message 'Subnet buf is invalid' names a port called in or a. A port or channel with a blank name, which TypeScript and Rust accept, is named by every message, so line 7 asks nothing of a failure that such a port or channel offends. A message that lists the name of every port and channel meets the line, so the line does not rule out a message that names innocent ports or channels next to the offender (open item: a clause that the message names no port or channel that does not offend is hard to state soundly, because one name can be a substring of another, as in is of input).
- For case 5 line 7 asks only that the message contain the net builder's message. That this message names the offending place or transition is the net builder's matter (CORE-040, EXEC-042), not this block's: when the net builder rejects with a message that names nothing, or with the empty message, line 7 asks nothing more of the subnet builder. For cases 1 to 4 the line asks for the port or channel's name, which is one reading of AC2's 'the offending port, channel, place, or transition'.
- AC1(each rejection case produces an error at subnet build, not later at instantiation or composition) is lines 1 to 5: they are stated of the subnet builder itself. A builder that accepts everything and leaves the checks to instantiation violates line 1 (MOD_006_forbids_lazy). AC2 (error messages name the offending port, channel, place or transition) is line 7. AC3 (a valid subnet definition is immutable after build) is a quality property of the host values (Lean values are immutable; builder stability is CORE-041's line), tested and not proven. What a built definition holds (its ports, channels and body) is MOD-001's line. The test derivation covers rejection cases 1 to 4; case 5 has no runtime input, since the subnet-definition builder takes places, transitions, ports and channels only and fromNet (MOD-014) takes a net that is already built (above).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_010"></a>
## MOD-010: Instance Creation via instantiate(prefix, params)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_010` · Kind **F** · Scope every instantiation of a subnet definition · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 016d6819870b4bff ai** · Statement hash `016d6819870b4bff`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* the prefix given to `instantiate` is empty or contains `/`, *then* `instantiate` *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* `instantiate` is given a non-empty prefix that contains no `/` and the body of the subnet definition declares no terminal place ([EXEC-042]), `instantiate` *shall* succeed.<br><br>*When* `instantiate` succeeds with prefix `p`, the renamed body *shall* hold exactly the body's places and, in the body's order, the body's transitions, each renamed from `x` to `p/x`, with every arc and output specification of a transition naming the renamed places and its timing, priority and action unchanged.<br><br>*If* the prefix given to `instantiate` is non-empty and contains no `/` and the body of the subnet definition declares a terminal place ([EXEC-042]), *then* `instantiate` *shall* fail with an error that names one of those terminal places. | 1. For every naming model Nm (how a prefix renames a place) and every instantiation function Inst:<br>2. if the prefix p is not valid (empty, or containing '/'), Inst fails on every subnet definition;<br>3. if p is valid and the definition's body declares no terminal place (and every port exposes a body place and every channel a body transition), Inst succeeds;<br>4. if Inst returns an instance I under p, the places of I are, as a set, the body's places each renamed by Nm.pre p, and the definitions of I, as transition definitions, are the body's definitions in order, each mapped by TransDef.map (Nm.pre p) (preS p): every input, inhibitor, read, reset and output-specification place renamed by Nm.pre p, the name x renamed to p/x, timing, priority and action unchanged;<br>5. if p is valid and the definition's body declares a terminal place, Inst fails with a message that names (contains, MsgNames) the name of one of the body's terminal places. | <pre>fun {N A} Nm Inst ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String),<br>      ¬ValidPrefix p → ∃ msg, Inst S p = Except.error msg) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String),<br>        ValidPrefix p →<br>          S.terminals = [] →<br>            (∀ q ∈ S.ports, q.place ∈ S.places) →<br>              (∀ c ∈ S.chans, c.trans ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) S.defs) →<br>                ∃ I, Inst S p = Except.ok I) ∧<br>      (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>          Inst S p = Except.ok I →<br>            (∀ (x : N), x ∈ I.places ↔ x ∈ List.map (Nm.pre p) S.places) ∧<br>              List.map CDef.toTransDef I.defs =<br>                List.map (fun d ↦ TransDef.map (Nm.pre p) (preS p) d.toTransDef) S.defs) ∧<br>        ∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String),<br>          ValidPrefix p →<br>            S.terminals ≠ [] →<br>              ∃ msg,<br>                Inst S p = Except.error msg ∧ ∃ x ∈ S.terminals, MsgNames msg (Nm.name x)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D25 (a): a prefix is valid when it is non-empty and contains no '/' (ValidPrefix), as Rust, Java and TypeScript check before renaming (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:90-101, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:450-461, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:595-605; Python calls the Rust check). The separator sentence ('Implementations MUST use exactly "/"') is preS: the renamed name of x under p is p ++ "/" ++ x, for transition names directly and for place names through the naming model's law pre_name. The order of the prefix check and the terminal-place check is not stated, which is why line 4 has the premise that the prefix is valid; the message of line 1 is not stated. Lines 3 and 4 are the markdown's fourth and third shall sentences: the block states what a success returns before the terminal-place rejection, the order the other blocks cite (MOD-010 line 3 for the shape, line 4 for EXEC-042 AC6).
- Places are the abstract N, the key type of the place model (PlaceKeyed.K, CORE-002), and the naming model Nm says how a prefix renames a key. Its law pre_name (the renamed place's name is p/name, item 2) pins the rename at every naming model, so a model that renames x to x/p is not a naming model; its law pre_inj (valid prefixes rename injectively and to disjoint sets) is what the prefix check buys. strNaming (TypeScript, Rust, Python: a place is its name, renamed to p/name) and typedNaming (Java: the name renamed, the token type kept) are the runtime naming models; the holds theorem holds for every naming model. Transition names are strings and are renamed by preS under every naming model.
- Line 4 is EXEC-042 AC6 for instantiate (a subnet body that declares terminal places is rejected with an error that names the place), the composition MUST that EXEC-042's block leaves to the composition model; its direct-composition half is MOD-025 line 7. To name is to contain as a substring (MsgNames, as in MOD-006). Every runtime rejects the body before renaming and names its first terminal place (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:103-104 through reject_subnet_terminals, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:91 and :130-135, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:106-107; Python calls the Rust check); the line asks for one of them. An instantiation without the terminal check meets lines 1 to 3 (MOD_010_mutant_noTerminalCheck_killed), and one that rejects without naming the place breaks line 4 (MOD_010_forbids_unnamedTerminal). Line 2's premises that every port exposes a body place and every channel a body transition hold of every subnet definition the subnet builder accepts (MOD-006). All three runtimes fail instantiate on a port whose place or a channel whose transition is missing from the renamed body (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:124-153, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:117-141, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:129-153), which is unreachable from a built definition; the premises keep line 2 true of those runtimes on the definitions the Lean type allows beyond the built ones.
- Line 3 compares the places as a set: Rust collects the renamed places through a hash map (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:84-96), and the order of places is not normative (ruling D32). It compares the transitions as a list: every runtime rewrites them in the body's order (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:98-102). It states the definitions' TransDef part only: the declared-to-actual correspondence a rewrite pass records (CDef.corr) is MOD-031's, and the instance's handles, prefix and interface (port, chan, pfx, iface) are MOD-011's and MOD-024's.
- Item 4 (arcs reference the renamed places, the arc topology identical modulo the rename) is line 3: TransDef.map renames every arc place of all five arc kinds and every output-specification place, and keeps the arc lists' order, repetitions and cardinalities. Its consequence for firing is mod010_firesAsBody: under the reference firing relation a renamed transition fires exactly as the body transition at the marking pulled back through the rename, and leaves every place outside the rename's image unchanged (fires_mapT, Spec/GlossaryCompose.lean).
- Item 5 (timing, priority and action preserved) is line 3's 'unchanged': the action is read as its identity tag (Act), so 'shared by reference' is MOD-030's line. Item 3 (the renamed body is a structurally valid PetriNet per CORE-040) is not stated here: that every renamed definition passes the build check, which holds since an injective rename keeps every build-time check, is the line 'every definition of a built net passes Build' of MOD-023 (composition wave W8). Every runtime also renames the body net itself to prefix/bodyName (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:90, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:112, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:119), which the spec does not state.
- Item 1 and AC4 (a params value of the wrong type is rejected) are API shape: the parameters value is not modelled, its type is checked by the host language at compile time where it has generics and at construction otherwise, tested and not proven. AC3 (the renamed body is immutable) is a quality property of the host values (Lean values are immutable; CORE-041 states builder stability), tested and not proven.
- AC1 (instantiate("buf1", params) over a body containing place slots produces buf1/slots) is MOD_010_nonvacuous on the reference, by decide; so is line 4 on a body with the terminal place done.
- AC2 (two instantiations of one definition under different prefixes have disjoint place and transition name sets) follows from lines 1 and 3 and the naming model's laws (mod010_disjoint, for every model of the block, on place names and transition names; AC1 at every naming model is mod010_placeName), so it has no mutant of its own (skeptic correction S4 of the composition design). The nested form outer/inner/originalName is MOD-013's (preS_assoc).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_011"></a>
## MOD-011: Instance Handle Map (typed port + channel handles)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011` · Kind **F** · Scope every module instance (Java, TypeScript, Rust, Python) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 7b4595c6b793ff8b ai** · Statement hash `7b4595c6b793ff8b`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* `instantiate` succeeds with prefix `p` and the interface declares a port named `n` that exposes the body place `x`, the instance's port lookup for `n` *shall* return the place `x` renamed under `p`, the place `p/x`.<br><br>*When* `instantiate` succeeds with prefix `p` and the interface declares a channel named `n` that exposes the body transition `t`, the instance's channel lookup for `n` *shall* return the renamed transition `p/t`.<br><br>*If* the port lookup of an instance is given a name that is not a port of the interface, *then* the lookup *shall* fail.<br><br>*If* the channel lookup of an instance is given a name that is not a channel of the interface, *then* the lookup *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* `instantiate` succeeds with prefix `p`, the instance's `prefix()` *shall* return `p`. | 1. For every naming model Nm (how a prefix renames a place) and every instantiation function Inst, whenever Inst returns an instance I for the subnet definition S under the prefix p:<br>2. if the port names of S are distinct, then for every port q of S, I.port q.name is some (Nm.pre p q.place): the place the port exposes, renamed under p;<br>3. if the channel names of S are distinct, then for every channel c of S, I.chan c.name is some (p/c.trans): the name of the transition the channel exposes, renamed under p;<br>4. for every name n that is no port name of S, I.port n is none (the lookup fails);<br>5. for every name n that is no channel name of S, I.chan n is none (the lookup fails);<br>6. I.pfx is p. | <pre>fun {N A} Nm Inst ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>      Inst S p = Except.ok I →<br>        (List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.ports).Nodup →<br>          ∀ q ∈ S.ports, I.port q.name = some (Nm.pre p q.place)) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>        Inst S p = Except.ok I →<br>          (List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.chans).Nodup →<br>            ∀ c ∈ S.chans, I.chan c.name = some (preS p c.trans)) ∧<br>      (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>          Inst S p = Except.ok I →<br>            ∀ n ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.ports, I.port n = none) ∧<br>        (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>            Inst S p = Except.ok I →<br>              ∀ n ∉ List.map (fun x ↦ x.name) S.chans, I.chan n = none) ∧<br>          ∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (p : String) (I : Instance N A),<br>            Inst S p = Except.ok I → I.pfx = p</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The handles are the Instance fields port (a port name to the renamed place, none for an unknown name) and chan (a channel name to the renamed transition's name, none for an unknown name), and pfx. 'Fails' is none: Rust panics (instance.rs port and channel), Java throws IllegalArgumentException (Instance.java port and channel), TypeScript throws an Error (instance.ts port and channel), Python raises (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs port_place_name and channel, through the Rust panic). The messages are not stated.
- The channel handle is the renamed transition's name. Java and TypeScript return the renamed Transition object and Rust and Python its name; under ruling D10 a transition of a net is identified by its name, so the two are one handle. Port places are the abstract N of the naming model, as in MOD-010: a place by name (TypeScript, Rust, Python: strNaming) or by name and token type (Java: typedNaming).
- Lines 1 and 2 are premised on distinct port names and distinct channel names. Every subnet definition the subnet builder accepts has them (MOD-006 lines 3 and 4); the Lean type SubnetDef allows definitions beyond the built ones, on which the reference answers with the first port or channel of the name and the runtimes' maps keep the last one. The handle answers whether or not the port's place was later bound by a composition: it is fixed at instantiation (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:703-705).
- That the handles name nodes of the renamed body (the port's place is a renamed body place, the channel's transition a renamed body transition) is a joint consequence with MOD-010, for every model of both blocks (mod011_handles_resolve): MOD-010 line 3 gives the renamed body and its line 2 the success on a built definition.
- Item 3 and AC5 (params() returns the parameter value supplied at instantiation): the parameters value is not modelled (InstFn, Spec/GlossaryCompose.lean); Java, TypeScript and Rust return the value they were given, and Python's definitions take no parameters, so its Instance has no params(). Tested, not proven.
- Item 1's type parameter, the MUST sentence on the token type and AC2 (port("input", Integer) is rejected) are the second block, MOD_011_typed, scoped to the implementations that keep a run-time token type for each port (ruling D36 (a)). The requirement makes no compile-time claim: no runtime reports a mismatched port type when compiling.
- AC1 (port("input", String) returns the renamed Place<String>) is line 1 (MOD_011_nonvacuous on the reference: port input on place slots under r1 gives r1/slots) and, with its type, mod011_typed_declared. AC3 (channel("attempt") returns the renamed transition whose original name was attempt) is line 2 (MOD_011_nonvacuous: r1/attempt). AC4 (an unknown port or channel name produces an error) is lines 3 and 4.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_011): ✓ The reference instantiation satisfies MOD-011 for every naming model: its port handle looks the port up by name and renames the place the port exposes, its channel handle looks the channel up by name and renames the transition's name, both answer nothing for a name the interface does not declare, and the instance keeps the prefix it was given.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type} (Nm : Naming N), MOD_011 Nm (refInst Nm)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_forbids_noHandles` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_011): ✗ An instantiation whose handles answer nothing violates MOD-011 (line 1): the example's port `input` must give `r1/slots`.
  <pre>¬MOD_011 strNaming (noHandlesInst strNaming)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_forbids_portByPortName` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_011): ✗ A port handle built as `p/portName` violates MOD-011 (line 1): the example's port `input` gives `r1/input`, but the port exposes the place `slots`, so the handle must give `r1/slots`.
  <pre>¬MOD_011 strNaming portByPortNameInst</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_mutant_noChanRename_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_011): The channel handle that returns the unrenamed transition name kills the mutant: it meets lines 1, 3, 4 and 5, but the example's channel `attempt` under `r1` gives `attempt` instead of `r1/attempt` (line 2).
  <pre>MOD_011_mutant_noChanRename strNaming (origChanInst strNaming) ∧<br>  ¬MOD_011 strNaming (origChanInst strNaming)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_mutant_noPortRename_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_011): The port handle that returns the unrenamed place kills the mutant: it meets lines 2 to 5, but the example's port `input` under `r1` gives `slots` instead of `r1/slots` (line 1).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_011_typed"></a>
## MOD-011: Instance Handle Map, the typed port lookup

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_011_typed` · Kind **F** · Scope implementations that keep a run-time token type for each port (Java, Rust) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 c66a65952dec31b4 ai** · Statement hash `c66a65952dec31b4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *Where* an implementation keeps a run-time token type for each port (Java, Rust), *when* a port lookup names a port of the interface and requests the token type the port was declared with, the lookup *shall* return the port's renamed place.<br><br>*Where* an implementation keeps a run-time token type for each port (Java, Rust), *if* a port lookup names a port of the interface and requests a token type other than the one the port was declared with, *then* the lookup *shall* fail.<br><br>*Where* an implementation keeps a run-time token type for each port (Java, Rust), *if* a port lookup names no port of the interface, *then* the lookup *shall* fail, whatever type it requests. | 1. For every reader tyOf of the token type a place handle carries and every typed port lookup PortAs, for every instance I, name n and requested type ty:<br>2. if the port handle I.port n gives the place x (the port's renamed place, MOD_011 line 1) and ty is tyOf x, the type x carries (on typedNaming the type the port was declared with, mod011_typed_declared), PortAs I n ty returns x;<br>3. if I.port n gives the place x and ty is not tyOf x (on typedNaming a type other than the one the port was declared with), PortAs I n ty fails;<br>4. if I.port n gives nothing, PortAs I n ty fails. | <pre>fun {N A T} tyOf PortAs ↦<br>  (∀ (I : Instance N A) (n : String) (x : N) (ty : T),<br>      I.port n = some x → tyOf x = ty → PortAs I n ty = Except.ok x) ∧<br>    (∀ (I : Instance N A) (n : String) (x : N) (ty : T),<br>        I.port n = some x → tyOf x ≠ ty → ∃ msg, PortAs I n ty = Except.error msg) ∧<br>      ∀ (I : Instance N A) (n : String) (ty : T),<br>        I.port n = none → ∃ msg, PortAs I n ty = Except.error msg</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D36 (a): the type check is scoped to the implementations that keep a run-time token type for each port. Java's Instance.port(name, tokenType) compares the requested class with the token type of the renamed place it returns, which keeps the token type of the body place the port was declared on, and throws IllegalArgumentException on a difference (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:98-110). Rust's Instance::port::<T>(name) compares TypeId::of::<T>() with port_types[name], the TypeId that Port::new captured from the Place<T> handle the port was declared with (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:53-64), copied per port name at instantiation (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:122-139); it panics on a difference and otherwise returns Place::<T>::new on the renamed name (rust/libpetri-core/src/instance.rs:109-131). TypeScript's port<T>(name) takes T as an annotation it does not check (typescript/src/core/instance.ts:79-85) and Python's port_place_name(name) takes no type; neither is in scope. The messages are not stated.
- Both runtimes are read at the typed naming model typedNaming, a place handle being its name and its token type, and tyOf is Prod.snd. For Java the handle is the place record (name, tokenType). For Rust it is the pair of the renamed name (port_handles[name]) and the captured TypeId (port_types[name]); on success the Place<T> Rust returns has the requested T, equal to the captured one, so it is that pair. The type is the port's, not a function of the place's name: Rust identifies places by name (MOD-024, strNaming in MOD_011), and one place name can carry two token types, for two definitions instantiated under one prefix whose ports declare the body place slots as Place<String> and as Place<i32>, or for two ports over one body place (MOD-003 AC5) that captured different TypeIds. A lookup that reads the type off the place's name is forbidden (MOD_011_typed_forbids_byPlaceName). On typedNaming the rename keeps the type, so the type the handle carries is the type the port was declared with, the spec's wording: every model of MOD-011 and of this block accepts exactly the declared type of the port's body place (mod011_typed_declared).
- The block is stated for every instance, not only for one instantiate returns: Java and Rust check the type on whatever instance the lookup is called on. Which place the port lookup returns, the port's renamed place, and that it fails on an unknown name, is the handle block MOD_011 (lines 1 and 3).
- The requirement makes no compile-time claim (ruling D36 (a)): no runtime reports a mismatched port type when compiling, since an instance's handle map is not typed by its interface.
- AC1 with its type (port("input", String) on an instance whose interface declared input: Input<String> returns the renamed Place<String>) is line 1, and AC2 (port("input", Integer) on the same instance is rejected) is line 2: MOD_011_typed_nonvacuous on the reference at typedNaming, and mod011_typed_declared for every model of both blocks.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_012"></a>
## MOD-012: Per-Instance State Isolation

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_012` · Kind **B** · Scope every net built by composition · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 17f4a1e737af4dc8 ai** · Statement hash `17f4a1e737af4dc8`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A place of an instance is **private** to it when no port binding names it, as the caller place or as the port place the binding replaces ([MOD-020]), no fusion set lists it ([MOD-060]), no transition of the instance that a channel binding merges names it ([MOD-021]), and no transition outside the instance names it: no hand-added transition, no caller-side definition of a channel binding, no transition of another instance and no directly composed subnet ([MOD-025]).<br><br>An auto-composition ([MOD-024]) of an instance under prefix `q` counts as binding a place `x` when `x` is the unrenamed place of one of that instance's ports or when `q/x` is a place of that instance, whether or not the call binds it.<br><br>Port bindings, channels and fusion sets are how instances share state on purpose, so isolation covers private places only.<br><br>After composition into a flat net, private places of two distinct instances MUST occupy distinct slots in the compiled net's place index, hold disjoint token bags, and evolve independently under the executor.<br><br>This isolation is a structural consequence of name-prefixing per [MOD-010] (distinct prefixed names → distinct place identities → distinct slots).<br><br>No additional runtime mechanism is required.<br><br>In the sentences below, `a` and `b` are single-segment prefixes: non-empty and without `/` **Assumptions**

- Ruling D79 (a): isolation covers private places only. PrivateTo reads privacy off the script of calls, before build, one call at a time (OpLeaves): a hand-added transition does not name the place; a fusion set does not list it; a compose call binds no port to it as the caller place, its caller-side channel definitions do not name it, and an instance definition that names it belongs to an instance under pb, is named pb/x and is bound by no channel; an auto-composition binds no port to it as the caller place, through the interface or by inference (the markdown's sentence on auto-composition: the place is not the unrenamed place of an interface port, and its renamed copy is not a place of the instance, whether or not the inference runs); a directly composed body does not name it. Auto-composition with channels is rejected (MOD-024), so it has no channel clause. These are the sharing paths the runtimes offer: a compose call takes any caller place (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1050-1069), fusion sets list places of the composed net by name (MOD-060), a channel merge gives the caller's transition the instance transition's arcs (MOD-021), and direct composition is unrenamed (MOD-025). A hand-added transition named pb/x counts as outside the instance.
- PrivateTo is broader than the markdown definition in two ways, both harmless. It has no membership condition: a place no call names is private to every prefix, which only widens lines 1 and 2 (safety lines), while line 3 asks for a definition of the instance that names the place. And it does not exclude the instance's own bound port places, which a compose call replaces by their caller places (MOD-020 item 2, retired per MOD-027) so that no transition names them after build: lines 1 and 2 hold of them vacuously, and line 3 states the exclusion as its premise. The condition that an instance definition naming the place is named pb/x holds for every instance made by instantiate (MOD-010 AC1); for an abstract Instance it is part of being the instance's transition.
- A transition of the instance under a is a transition of the flat net whose name has the form a/x (transitions are identified by name, rulings D10 and D23); a channel-merged transition carries the caller's name (MOD-021 clause 5) and belongs to the caller. The prefixes are valid, that is single segments (MOD-010 line 1: instantiate refuses any other), and two valid and different prefixes never give one name (preS_inj), which is what line 2 uses. Two sibling instances nested in one outer instance lie under one valid prefix of the flat net, so line 2 and the clock block say nothing between them there; the markdown sends them to the build of the outer subnet's body, where their prefixes are single segments and both blocks apply. Line 1 does not need the place to be named pb/y: for instances made by instantiate it is (MOD-010 AC1), and another instance's definitions never name it (mod012_inst_leaves).
- Line 3 assumes that the definitions of the call's instance and the caller-side definitions of its channel bindings have pairwise distinct names: the caller obligation MOD-020 takes (mod020_fresh) under the unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23, as MOD-024 lines 3 and 4 do. Transition names are assumed distinct (ruling D23) and no builder rejects a subnet body with two transitions of one name, and every runtime stages one call's rewritten instance transitions in a map keyed by name (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs apply_composition, staged.insert; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:825-828, rewrittenByName.put; typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:580-583, rewrittenByName.set), so of two body transitions of one name only the later reaches the built net: a body with work: IN -> OUT and work: OTHER -> OUT composed under b yields b/work on b/OTHER alone, and the b/work that named the private b/IN is gone. Rust also stages a channel merge under the caller's name in that map, so a caller-side definition named like an unbound instance definition replaces it. The block claims nothing about such a call, which leaves a builder free to reject it. Composing one instance twice, or two instances under one prefix, is not excluded: every runtime appends the second call's transitions after the first.
- 'Distinct slots in the compiled net's place index' and 'hold disjoint token bags' are line 3 with MOD-010 AC2: the build merges no private place into another place, since a definition of the instance that names its private place still names it, under its own name, in the built net (buildScript_keeps: a compose call adds the definition through its binding, which leaves the place, no channel merges it, and fusion moves only listed places); two instances under different prefixes share no place name (mod010_disjoint), and the place index is keyed by place identity (Novel.Seam.PlaceIndex.idx_inj). Line 3 covers compose(instance, bindings) calls; the definitions an auto-composition adds are bound by inference against the builder's places at the time of the call, which the call alone does not show, so they are not covered here. 'No additional runtime mechanism is required' is the holds theorem: the plain reference firing relation RefFire and the reference build script satisfy all three lines (MOD_012_reference, and mod012_buildScript for every transition check and every channel merge that names only its two sides' places).
- 'Evolve independently under the executor' is read as non-interference of the marking (line 2), and of enablement and clocks (the companion block MOD_012_clock). The order in which a firing pass picks ready transitions (EXEC-002; ruling D14: the all-immediate fast path is not preserved by composition), actions shared by reference between instances (MOD-010 item 5, MOD-030), a blocking Java action that stalls the whole net, and per-instance ν name pools (NU-030) are not part of this block. Tokens injected through environment places are ENV's (ENV-003).
- AC1 (tokens added to instance A's private place do not appear in instance B's corresponding private place): tokens a firing of A's transitions adds are line 2 (MOD_012_nonvacuous fires a/work and leaves b/IN as it was); tokens the caller adds to the initial marking land in one named place, and A's and B's places have different names (MOD-010 AC2) that the build keeps (line 3). AC4 (a fusion with a place of a third instance C leaves each transition of A and B naming its own private place) is line 3 (MOD_012_mutant_noKeep_killed: a fusion keyed by local names also fuses a/IN and b/IN into the caller place). AC2 and AC3 are the companion block MOD_012_clock.

## MOD-012: Per-Instance State Isolation (clocks)

**Assumptions**

- A step of R relates two states of the timed executor, each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name (TSt); a step is a delay, a firing or a reap (TRel, the Phase 1 timed step whose witness is RefTStep). 'Timing clock' is the stamp of TIME-010, Armed and Enabled are the glossary terms; 'enablement state' is Enabled at the marking. The composed net is run as BuiltNet.toTimed: the transitions of the built net, each with the timing of its definition.
- Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10): u is the net's transition of its name (InNet), which holds of every transition when the names are distinct (NamesDistinct, inNet_iff_mem). Neither builder checks transition names (composition design, skeptic S8), so the premise is stated, not proved; t and u carry different names because they lie under different valid prefixes.
- Line 1 needs every arc place of u (input, read, inhibitor, reset) private: u's enablement reads only those places, and the firing of t writes none of them (line 1 of MOD_012), so no firing of t restarts u's clock through TIME-012. A transition of b with an arc on a bound caller place or a fused place may be disabled or restarted by a's firing, as it shares that place on purpose. A transition armed with a stale stamp while disabled is not a reachable state of RefTStep and is not claimed: line 1 keeps the stamp of an armed u only.
- Line 2 needs no privacy: a reap removes only the reaped transition's stamp (TIME-013) and a delay keeps every stamp (TIME-010); together with line 1 the clocks of b's transitions never depend on a's steps. Under a delay the clocks of all transitions advance together, so 'independent' means that no step of a changes a stamp of b.
- Line 2 is stated for a net that holds a transition t named pa/x, as the markdown sentence says ('in a net that holds such a transition'); a delay keeping every stamp in any net is TIME-010's own content. Its delay half has its own mutant (MOD_012_clock_mutant_noDelayFrame_killed: a delay that clears every stamp).
- The block takes the build's structure as given and states steps only. A build that merged a private place of b into a shared place leaves b's transitions with an arc place that is not private, outside line 1's premise, so this block alone does not reject it; MOD_012 line 3 does (MOD_012_mutant_noKeep_killed). The prefixes are single segments, as the markdown says; sibling instances nested in one outer instance are covered in the build of the outer subnet's body.
- AC2 (firing a transition in instance A does not affect the enablement of a transition in instance B whose arc places are all private to B) is line 1's first conjunct. AC3 has two parts: firing a transition of A keeps the timing clock of a transition of B whose arc places are all private to B (line 1's second and third conjuncts; MOD_012_clock_nonvacuous fires a/work and b/work keeps its stamp 0), and reaping a transition of A or advancing the clock keeps every timing clock of B (line 2). TIME-011 is cited for the per-instance clocks; its own lines are TIME-011's block. TIME-013 (a reap removes only the reaped transition's stamp) carries the reap half of line 2.
