<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_013"></a>
## MOD-013: Nested Instantiation (prefix concatenation associative)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_013` · Kind **F** · Scope every instantiation of a subnet definition whose body holds places or transitions of a composed instance · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 eeef7dafaeee4204 ai** · Statement hash `eeef7dafaeee4204`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the body of a subnet definition `S` holds the place `i/x` of an instance under prefix `i` of a subnet definition `T`, for a place `x` of `T`, and `S` is instantiated with prefix `o`, the instance *shall* hold the place `o/i/x`.<br><br>*When* the body of a subnet definition `S` holds the transition `i/t` of an instance under prefix `i` of a subnet definition `T`, for a transition `t` of `T`, and `S` is instantiated with prefix `o`, the instance *shall* hold the transition `o/i/t`.<br><br>*When* `instantiate` is given a non-empty prefix that contains no `/` and the body of the subnet definition declares no terminal place, `instantiate` *shall* succeed, also when names of the body contain `/` because the body holds a composed instance. | 1. For every naming model Nm (how a prefix renames a place) and every instantiation function Inst:<br>2. if Inst instantiates T under i to J and S under o to I, then for every place x of T whose renamed place Nm.pre i x is a place of J and a place of the body of S, the place Nm.pre o (Nm.pre i x) is a place of I (its name is o/i/x, by the naming law pre_name);<br>3. if Inst instantiates T under i to J and S under o to I, then for every transition of T named t such that i/t names a transition of J and a transition of the body of S, o/i/t names a transition of I;<br>4. if o is valid and the body of S declares no terminal place (and every port exposes a body place and every channel a body transition), Inst succeeds on S under o, whatever the names of the body of S contain. The lines do not trace the body of S back to J: S only has to hold a place equal to Nm.pre i x or a transition named i/t. | <pre>fun {N A} Nm Inst ↦<br>  (∀ (T S : SubnetDef N A) (i o : String) (J I : Instance N A),<br>      Inst T i = Except.ok J →<br>        Inst S o = Except.ok I →<br>          ∀ x ∈ T.places,<br>            Nm.pre i x ∈ J.places →<br>              Nm.pre i x ∈ S.places → Nm.pre o (Nm.pre i x) ∈ I.places) ∧<br>    (∀ (T S : SubnetDef N A) (i o : String) (J I : Instance N A),<br>        Inst T i = Except.ok J →<br>          Inst S o = Except.ok I →<br>            ∀ d ∈ T.defs,<br>              preS i d.core.name ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) J.defs →<br>                preS i d.core.name ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) S.defs →<br>                  preS o (preS i d.core.name) ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) I.defs) ∧<br>      ∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (o : String),<br>        ValidPrefix o →<br>          S.terminals = [] →<br>            (∀ q ∈ S.ports, q.place ∈ S.places) →<br>              (∀ c ∈ S.chans, c.trans ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) S.defs) →<br>                ∃ I, Inst S o = Except.ok I</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The body of S is any subnet definition whose body holds the renamed place or transition: the runtimes build it with fromNet ([MOD-014], raised to MUST by ruling D57 (a)) over a net that composed the instance of T under i ([MOD-020]), as the nested tests of every language do (rust/libpetri-core/tests/mod031_place_resolution.rs:84-121, java/src/test/java/org/libpetri/core/AutoComposeTest.java:284-320, python/tests/test_subnet_local_names.py:597). mod013_viaFromNet gives line 1 through every fromNet that meets MOD-014 line 6, and MOD_013_nonvacuous runs that pipeline on the reference models.
- Which places of T reach the body of S is composition's, and the lines take it as a premise: a port place of T that S binds to a place of its own is replaced by that place ([MOD-020] item 2) and does not become o/i/x; an internal place of T that no arc names is not added by the composition ([MOD-020] clause 3); a transition of T merged with a caller transition through a channel takes the caller's name ([MOD-021]). The sentence that a subnet composing other subnets can be instantiated like any other is line 3, and the sentence on the separator at every level is lines 1 and 2. That the names i/x and i/t of the body of S are the ones the instance of T under i gave, and not places or transitions S declares itself under those names, is composition's too (MOD-020): the lines take the body of S as given and the instance J only bounds which x and t they range over.
- Places are the abstract N, the key type of the place model (CORE-002), renamed by the naming model Nm as in MOD-010: by name in TypeScript, Rust and Python (strNaming), by name with the token type kept in Java (typedNaming). The place Nm.pre o (Nm.pre i x) is named o/i/x at every naming model by its law pre_name (mod013_name). Transition names are strings renamed by preS.
- The associativity sentence ('Prefix concatenation is associative on names: ...') carries no MUST and is no line: it is mod013_flat, a fact about names that holds for every instantiation function, the nested name o/(i/x) being the name (o/i)/x, x renamed under the concatenated prefix o/i (preS_assoc), at every naming model. Ruling D25 (a) makes o/i an invalid prefix, so no single instantiation produces it: every model of MOD-010 rejects the prefix o/i (mod013_concat_rejected), and the markdown no longer compares with an instantiation under outer/inner.
- MOD-013 adds no constraint beyond MOD-010: every model of MOD-010 meets all three lines (mod013_of_mod010). Lines 1 and 2 are MOD-010 line 3 read for the places and transitions a body took over from an instance, and line 3 is MOD-010 line 2 word for word; the clause 'also when names of the body contain /' explains that the formula has no premise on names. The block states the nested reading of MOD-010 that AC1 asks for and gives each nested line a mutant that is a plausible slip. Line 3 is a line of MOD-013 because AC1 says that the nested instantiation produces names, which needs it to succeed; its mutant is an instantiation that refuses a body whose names contain the separator, which the prefix check of D25 makes a plausible mistake. All three runtimes check only the prefix and the terminal places before renaming (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:88-104, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:450-461, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts:595-605).
- The third quoted sentence leaves out line 3's premises that every port exposes a body place and every channel a body transition, for the reason MOD-010 gives for its line 2: they hold of every subnet definition the subnet builder accepts (MOD-006) and of every definition fromNet accepts (MOD-014), so a nested definition built either way meets them.
- The correspondence of a nested transition (its declared places resolving to o/i/x) is MOD-031's, which cites this ID; the lines state names only.
- AC1 (S composing T under inner, instantiated under outer, produces names of the form outer/inner/<original>) is lines 1 and 2 with line 3 for the success, and MOD_013_nonvacuous on the reference: outer/inner/x and outer/inner/t, with the bound port of T replaced by the place outer/src. That the nested items appear in that form only (no outer/x or inner/x next to outer/inner/x) is MOD-010 line 3's 'exactly': in every model of MOD-010 every place of the instance is a body place renamed under o and every transition name a body transition name renamed under o (mod013_ofTheForm).
- AC2 (the names of the form outer/inner/x are exactly the names inner/x the body of S holds, renamed under outer, which is x under the concatenated prefix outer/inner) has two directions. Line 1 gives the inclusion (mod013_nestedName, with mod013_flat for the concatenated reading). The converse, that the instance holds no other place named outer/inner/x, is MOD-010 line 3, not a line of this block: in every model of MOD-010, o/i/x is a place of the instance exactly when i/x is a place of the body (mod013_nestedSet). MOD-013 alone does not give it: the instantiation that keeps the body places next to the renamed ones meets all three lines and violates MOD-010 (mod013_keepBody_accepted, mod013_keepBody_not_mod010). So AC2 is MOD-013 line 1 with MOD-010 line 3 and has no mutant of its own here (skeptic correction S4 of the composition design); the rejection of a single instantiation under outer/inner is mod013_concat_rejected, from MOD-010 line 1.
- AC3 (per-instance state isolation holds at every nesting level) is not a line of this block; it is delegated. It is MOD-012 applied to the nested definition: MOD-012 ranges over every subnet definition, nested or not, and its runtime-state half is MOD-012's: its isolation line over the firing relation (MOD_012) and its clock line over the timed relation (MOD_012_clock), both stated over every build script, so over a net that composes a nested definition too. Its naming half holds for every model of MOD-010, not of MOD-013 alone: two nested places o/i1/x and o/i2/y are one place only when i1 = i2 and x = y (mod013_nested_inj, a fact of the naming laws), and two outer instances of one definition share no name (mod010_disjoint). The instantiation that keeps the body places meets MOD-013 and gives two outer instances o1 and o2 of the nested S the shared place inner/x (mod013_keepBody_shares).
- The test derivation (T with an internal place x, S composing T under inner, S instantiated under outer, outer/inner/x among the renamed places) is MOD_013_nonvacuous.

**Evidence**

## MOD-014: SubnetDef.fromNet retrofit utility

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_014` · Kind **B** · Scope every retrofit utility fromNet · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 9f29ec20e2b63a3f ai** · Statement hash `9f29ec20e2b63a3f`

**Assumptions**

- A retrofit utility (FromNetFn) is the fromNet call of one implementation (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:232-293, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:507-552, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts fromNet; Python's SubnetDef.from_net calls the Rust function, rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:880-883), read as a function from a built net (ClosedNet: its name, places, transition definitions in declaration order and terminal places) and an interface (the ports and the channels) to a subnet definition or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception, read as .error msg). The sentence 'Implementations MUST provide a utility' (raised from MAY by ruling D57 (a)) is the existence of the model: the block's argument is the implementation's fromNet, and all four implementations provide one. It is no block line.
- The net is already built, so no net builder runs and MOD-006's case 5 (a body the net builder rejects) does not arise. The reference refFromNet is MOD-006's reference subnet builder over a net builder that returns the net unchanged (refFromNet_eq), which is the design's 'the same check applied to an already built net'. A net that declares terminal places is accepted (line 5, MOD_014_nonvacuous) and refused when the definition is instantiated (EXEC-042 AC6, MOD-010 line 2's premise); all three runtimes keep the net, terminal places included, as the body.
- Line 1 and line 5 compare a port's place with the net's places by equality on the place type N (CORE-002: by name in TypeScript, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts placeNames, and in Rust and Python, whose Place equality is name-only; by name and token type in Java, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:527).
- Line 2 and line 5 match a channel to a net transition by name (ruling D23, settled by D10, and R-MA3 (a)), as MOD-006 lines 2 and 6 do: the model's channel carries the transition's name. Rust and Python compare names (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:236-240, :272); Java and TypeScript compare transition objects (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:543, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts bodyTransitions.has), so a channel over a second transition object that has the name of a net transition is rejected there and accepted in Rust. The model's channel carries only the transition's name, not a transition object, so it cannot tell that second object from the net's own transition: the case is outside what the block can state, the formula (lines 2 and 5) reads it as Rust does, and the markdown calls it implementation-defined. The shared unique-names assumption (D10, D23; no builder checks names) concerns the transitions inside one net and does not settle this case, since the second object is not in the net. After a composition the net holds rewritten transition objects, so in Java and TypeScript a caller exposes the transition it fetches from the net.
- Lines 3 and 4 are reached only by the model. An interface value of every runtime holds at most one port and one channel of each name: Rust and TypeScript key them by name in a map (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:104-107, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:57-59), Java keeps sets built only by its interface builder (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:29-37), and every interface builder rejects a second declaration of a name at the port() or channel() call (rust/libpetri-core/src/interface.rs:164-170, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Interface.java:183-190, typescript/src/core/interface.ts:107-113). The model's interface is two lists, which can carry a repeated name, and all three runtimes' fromNet check the names again (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:243-251, :264-270, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:520-525, :537-542); the lines state that check. Port names and channel names are two namespaces, as in MOD-006.
- Line 5 is implied by line 7 (mod014_line5_of_line7): when no port or channel offends, line 7 leaves no message a failure could carry. It is kept as the acceptance line (skeptic correction S2 of the composition design) and has no mutant of its own, as MOD-006 line 6. Lines 1 to 5 together fix exactly when fromNet succeeds, and line 6 fixes what it returns, so two models of the block agree on every input up to the message (mod014_determined).
- Line 6 is AC1: 'body equals the supplied net (modulo immutability semantics)' reads as the definition holding the net's places, its transition definitions as a list in the net's order (correspondence included) and its terminal places; Lean values are immutable. The name is the net's name in all three runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:285, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:551, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts new SubnetDef(SUBNET_DEF_KEY, net.name, ...)), which the markdown now states. The interface is the given one: Rust and Java keep the interface value, and the model's lists stand for it; the runtimes' interface has no order to keep, so line 6 returning the lists as given asks nothing of an order.
- The markdown's sentences 'This allows pre-existing nets to be wrapped as reusable subnet fragments without rebuilding them.' and 'It is also how a subnet definition whose body holds a composed instance is built, which nested instantiation needs ([MOD-013]).' are motivation with no shall or MUST: the first is line 6 (the body is the net, not a rebuild), and the second is covered by line 6 with the CDef correspondence the ClosedNet keeps ([MOD-031]); nested instantiation itself is stated by MOD-013's block.
- Line 7 is the sentence of MOD-006 'Each failure MUST produce an error identifying the offending element by name.', which AC2 brings in: to name a port or channel is for the message to contain its name as a substring (List.IsInfix on the characters), with the weakness MOD-006 records (a blank name is named by every message). All three runtimes name the port or channel and also its place or transition and the net (subnet_def.rs:246-280, SubnetDef.java:522-547, subnet-def.ts fromNet). The line is existential over the offenders: Rust walks the interface's hash maps (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:244, :264), so which offender is named when there are several is not stated, nor whether ports are checked before channels.
- AC2 (the interface validation rules of MOD-006 apply) is lines 1 to 4 and 7, MOD-006's cases 1 to 4 and its message rule stated of fromNet; case 5 does not arise (above). AC3 (the result is unparameterised, its parameter type the unit or void type) is API typing, kind Q: the model's SubnetDef carries no parameter type, and the runtimes' result types are SubnetDef<()> (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:232), SubnetDef<Void> (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:507) and SubnetDef<void> (typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts fromNet); tested, not proven. The test derivation (a net with places a and b, the port in on a) is MOD_014_nonvacuous.

**Assumptions**

- Model scope. Bld (Reference/ComposeBind.lean) is what the enclosing builder holds: its places and transition definitions (CDef) in the order added, and what composition leaves for build() (retired ports, contributions, fusion sets). The composition rejects by failing; Rust panics, Java throws IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException, TypeScript throws an Error, Python raises through the Rust panic. The runtimes compose in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs (compose_internal, apply_composition, reject_port_collision) with compose.rs (bind_port, bind_channel), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java (composeInternal, rejectPortCollisions, applyComposition) with ComposeBindings.java, and typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts (applyComposition, rejectPortBindingCollision) with compose-bindings.ts. Item 1 (each binding maps a port name, resolved on the instance, to a caller place) is the binding list ports and bindEntries. A script ends at its first rejected call. A caller that catches a failed compose and goes on with the same builder is out of scope: Rust consumes the builder (compose takes self by value, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:374) and Python makes it unusable (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs, PyPetriNetBuilder::take_builder), while Java (composeInternal records the retired ports before applyComposition runs, and applyComposition adds each channel merge as it goes, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java) and TypeScript (applyComposition records the retired ports and adds each channel merge as it goes, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts) may keep the retired-port records and merged transitions of the failed call.
- Ruling D35 (a): two ports may expose one body place (MOD-003). A call that binds two such ports to different caller places has no defined outcome: Rust keeps one binding in hash order and Java the last one put (compose_internal in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs, composeInternal in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java), and the reference keeps the first. Lines 1 and 4 to 9 are stated on coherent calls only (mod020_coherent); lines 2, 3 and 10 hold of every call. The prose of the spec says so in the definition of a coherent call.
- The caller obligations (mod020_fresh), assumed by line 1 and line 9. Ruling D72 (ii)(b): binding one caller-side transition to two channels of one instance in one call is a compose-time error naming the transition and both channels (AC6). Every runtime rejects it when it records the second channel binding, with the message Transition '<t>' is already bound to channel '<c1>'; it cannot also be bound to channel '<c2>' (MOD-020) (rust/libpetri-core/src/compose.rs bind_channel, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java bindChannel, typescript/src/core/compose-bindings.ts bindChannel; Python raises it through the Rust panic). The runtimes compare the caller transition by identity (Rust by its id, Java by ==, TypeScript by ===); the block reads one transition as one name (ruling D23). The reference composition refCompose (Reference/ComposeBind.lean) does not reject such a call, so no line states the rejection; lines 1 and 9 treat it as a caller obligation: the instance's transitions and the caller-side transitions of the channel bindings have pairwise distinct names, and the block claims nothing about the outcome of a call that breaks it. That premise is the part of ruling D10 (transition names are assumed distinct, ruling D23; no builder checks them) that the name-keyed staging maps of one call need; it does not exclude an instance transition whose name the builder already holds, so composing one instance twice is covered, and every runtime then appends the second copy (Java holds transitions in a LinkedHashSet of objects without a structural equals, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:286). Ruling D42 (m): a caller-side transition already in the builder is replaced by the merge in Java and TypeScript and kept beside it in Rust, so the caller obligations also exclude it. Rust rewrites the caller-side transition through the binding before the merge (petri_net.rs apply_composition, substitute_places) and Java and TypeScript merge it as given, so the caller obligations also exclude a caller-side transition that names a bound port place of the instance.
- Ruling D72 (i)(a): a port re-bound in one call fails with an error naming the port. Every runtime rejects at the second binding with the message Port '<name>' is already bound (rust/libpetri-core/src/compose.rs bind_port, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java bindPort, typescript/src/core/compose-bindings.ts bindPort); Java's Map overload cannot name a port twice. Line 2 reads 'naming' as 'the message contains the text of the port name' (MsgNames, as in MOD-006); so a message that happens to contain a short port name meets it, and an empty port name is contained in every message. MOD_020_forbids_genericDup shows the line rejects a message that does not contain the port. With several re-bound ports the runtimes name the first one re-bound, and line 2 asks for one of them. The sentence and line 2 are premised on no channel being bound twice: a call is a list of bindings that every runtime records through one binding builder in the caller's order (bind_port and bind_channel in rust/libpetri-core/src/compose.rs, bindPort and bindChannel in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java and typescript/src/core/compose-bindings.ts), so when a channel is also bound twice and its duplicate comes first, the call fails with Channel '<name>' is already bound, which names no port. A call that binds a channel twice fails by line 10. For the same reason the sentence and line 2 are premised on no caller-side transition being bound to more than one channel: the binding builder rejects the second channel binding of one caller transition when it records it (bind_channel, bindChannel), so when that binding comes before the re-bound port the call fails with a message that names the transition and two channels and no port. Line 2 reads that premise as pairwise distinct names of the caller-side definitions, the block's reading of one transition (ruling D23).
- Line 3 (an unknown port fails) is the new EARS sentence for what every runtime does (Rust compose_internal panics with the known ports, Java and TypeScript resolve the port through instance.port, which fails, MOD-011 AC4). Line 10 (ill-formed channel bindings fail) is what every runtime does: a channel bound twice fails in bind_channel / bindChannel (rust/libpetri-core/src/compose.rs, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java, typescript/src/core/compose-bindings.ts); an unknown channel fails in apply_composition with the known channels (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs) and through instance.channel in Java and TypeScript; a second channel on one instance transition finds that transition already merged away and fails (the internal-invariant panic of Rust apply_composition, the IllegalStateException of Java applyComposition, the Error of TypeScript applyComposition in typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts); a channel whose transition is missing cannot come from a built subnet definition. The messages are not stated. Line 9 assumes the binding checks pass (mod020_checks): a caller place of another token type than its port's is MOD-022's line.
- Clauses 2 to 5 and the reworded clauses 3 and 4 (ruling D20, clashes mod-b#7 and mod-b#9) are line 1. Clause 2 is the rewrite TransDef.map (bindSubst bm) id, which renames every input, inhibitor, read and reset place and every output-specification place, and keeps the name, the timing, the priority and the action. Clause 3: every runtime adds the places the arcs of the new transitions name (builder auto-collection: the transition() calls that end apply_composition in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs and applyComposition in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java and typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts), so an internal place no arc names is not added. The place clause compares places by the place model's equality; TypeScript keys its builder's places by name and keeps the first Place object of a name (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:161 and addPlace at :191-193), so a caller Place object that has the name of a place the builder holds adds no second place. Clause 4: a transition a channel binding names is replaced by its merge with the caller-side transition; line 1 says the merge Mg of the caller side with the rewritten instance transition is among the new transitions, and fixes the number of new transitions and the order of the unmerged ones. The slot of a merge differs (Rust the instance transition's slot, Java and TypeScript the merges first, ruling D42 (3) unspecified) and is not stated; what the merge holds is MOD-021's (over Mg). Line 1 compares TransDef, not CDef: the declared-to-actual correspondence is MOD-031's. The MOD-021 rules (c) and (d) that a merge MUST be rejected at compose time are line 1 with MOD-021's Mg: a call whose merge fails cannot succeed (mod020_mergeFails).
- Clause 5 (eager) is line 1: the state the call returns already holds the rewritten transitions. Its consequence mod020_eager states that no unmerged new transition names a bound port place when no caller place is itself a bound port place; that build() rejects an arc on a retired port place is MOD-027's. The sentence 'The result of composition over the enclosing builder MUST be observationally indistinguishable from a hand-written flat net' and AC4 are MOD-023's (composition wave W8).
- The input and output collision lines (4 to 7) are stated for two different bound port places sent to one caller place (InCollision, OutCollision), as Rust and Java check (reject_port_collision in rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs, rejectPortCollisions in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java). An output collision is taken inside one AND branch of Out.branches, which flattens nested Ands (the sentence 'A branch is taken after flattening nested `And`s, as in [IO-011].'), and two places in different Xor alternatives are in different branches, so they are no collision (the sentence 'Two ports that land in **different** `Xor` alternatives are not a port-binding collision, because each alternative still names the place once.'). TypeScript compares every input place after the substitution (rejectPortBindingCollision in typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts), so it also prints the collision message for a caller place that an instance transition already names under its own name, or for two input arcs on one unbound place; Rust and Java skip a pair of one place named twice in one AND branch and can then miss a collision in that branch. Lines 5, 7 and 8 assume a plain call (mod020_plain), where the three checks agree and which every built body meets but for the caller places. Lines 4 and 6 claim rejection only: the accepted set is the same in every runtime, since a collision makes the rewritten transition fail CORE-030 or IO-011 when the rebuild meets it.
- Lines 5, 7 and 8 state a message only when every other transition is fine (skeptic correction S3 of the composition design). Rust and TypeScript check transition by transition, collision first and then the rebuild (the loop over the renamed body in apply_composition, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs, and in applyComposition, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts); Java checks every port pair for collisions before any rebuild (composeInternal calls rejectPortCollisions before applyComposition, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java). So the lines assume every transition before t passes, every transition after t has no collision, and t has a collision of one kind only. When several pairs of t collide, the runtimes name different pairs (Rust and TypeScript the first input arc whose caller place repeats, Java the first port pair in code-point order of the port names), so the lines ask for some colliding pair of t; MOD_020_forbids_threePortToBuild shows they reject a check that only reports a pair of two ports and sends three to the rebuild. Rust and TypeScript name the two ports in input-arc order, Java in code-point order of the port names (clash mod-b#15), so the lines accept either order. Where two ports expose one place, TypeScript names the last port of the instance on that place, which need not be a bound one, so the lines name some port exposing each place (mod020_portsOf), and the spec's MUST says the same.
- Line 8 delegates the message to Build (skeptic correction S6): the block holds for every Build. With the reference builder refBuild, Xor(a, b) bound to Xor(X, X) fails with the IO-012 ambiguity message and an input arc and a read arc bound to one place with the EXEC-012 message; those messages are IO-012's and EXEC-012's lines. So the sentence 'If the substitution makes two distinct alternatives claim the same set of places, such as `Xor(a, b)` becoming `Xor(X, X)`, then rebuilding the transition shall fail with the [IO-012] ambiguity message, which names the transition, the two output branches and the places.' is line 8 with IO-012, shown on the reference by MOD_020_nonvacuous (bindEx_xorAmbiguous). The sentence 'Other effects of binding two ports to one place (an input and an output, an input and an inhibitor) are unchanged: they are legal arcs with their usual semantics.' is line 9 where Build accepts the rewritten transition, and line 8 where it does not: whether such arcs are legal is Build's (CORE-030, IO-011, EXEC-012). The sentence 'The checks apply wherever [MOD-020] bindings are processed, so the auto-bound form of [MOD-024] is covered too.' is MOD-024's (its lines over refAuto). The sentence 'Without this check the rebuild would fail on [CORE-030] AC3 with a message that names only the rewritten transition, not the binding that caused it.' is informative.
- AC1 (every arc that referenced the port's renamed place now references P) is line 1 and mod020_eager; MOD_020_nonvacuous shows it on the reference (Join under s with a, b and out bound to X, Y and P gives s/join over X, Y and P). AC2 (internal places that an arc names appear under their renamed names) is line 1's place clause. AC3 (transition count after a call without channel bindings is the prior count plus the instance's) is line 1's length clause (mod020_count). AC5 (a port bound twice is rejected with an error naming the port) is line 2 (MOD_020_nonvacuous: Port 'a' is already bound). AC6 (one caller transition bound to two channels is rejected) is what every runtime does (the caller obligations above) and is not stated: the reference composition accepts such a call, so a line for it needs refCompose to reject it first. AC7 (ports a and b of s bound to X with join consuming from both is rejected with the collision message; with no transition consuming from both it is accepted) is lines 4, 5 and 9 (MOD_020_nonvacuous). AC8 (And(a, b) rejected with the output collision message; Xor(a, b) rejected with the IO-012 message) is lines 6, 7 and 8 (MOD_020_nonvacuous). The channel merge of clause 4 is line 1 (MOD_020_nonvacuous: channel go of C bound to host leaves the one transition host).

## MOD-021: Channel Composition, the transition merge

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_021` · Kind **B** · Scope channel composition in every implementation: the merge of a caller-side transition with the instance-side channel transition it is bound to · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 30c6b6651b9c75fc ai** · Statement hash `30c6b6651b9c75fc`

transition *shall* have the caller-side transition's name and priority.<br><br>**Priority**: the merged transition has the caller-side transition's priority; the instance-side priority is **Assumptions**

- Model scope. A merge function takes the caller-side definition c and the instance-side channel definition i (CDef: name, input, inhibitor, read and reset arcs, output specification, timing, priority, action and the declared-place correspondence of MOD-031) and gives the merged definition or a rejection message, as Rust merge_transitions (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:611-698), Java SubnetRewriter.mergeTransitions (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:529-598) and TypeScript mergeTransitions (typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:483-555) do; Python uses the Rust code. The witness is refMerge (Reference/ComposeMerge.lean) with the reference's timing rendering timingStr, and the block holds for every Build, sq and cm (MOD_021_reference). Rewriting i through the port bindings before the merge, putting the merged definition into the composed net and not adding the instance-side channel transition separately (clause 5) are MOD-020's (refCompose, Reference/ComposeBind.lean). The merged definition's declared-place correspondence is MOD-031's and no line here constrains it.
- Ruling D42 (m), clash mod-b#8: the caller-side transition is assumed not to be in the builder already and to have no arc on a port bound in the same compose call; the markdown now scopes the sentences to that case. Java and TypeScript then have nothing to replace and Rust has nothing to rewrite, so the three runtimes merge the same two definitions. Outside that case they differ (Java and TypeScript replace a caller already in the builder, Rust keeps it beside the merged one; Rust rewrites the caller's arcs through the port map, Java and TypeScript do not), and the outcome there is an open item of D42. The caller-side name: every runtime refuses a merge under an empty merged name, which is the caller-side name, before any other check (Rust assert!(!merged_name.is_empty()), rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:615-618, a panic whose message names neither timing; TypeScript mergedName.length === 0, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:488; Java mergedName.isBlank(), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:536, which also refuses a name of white space only), while no transition builder refuses such a name (CORE-020). The markdown therefore scopes the sentences to a caller-side transition whose name is neither empty nor white space only, and lines 8 to 11, whose messages and acceptance that refusal would break, carry the premise mod021_named c (some character of the name is not white space in the sense of Java's Character.isWhitespace, mod021_javaSpace). Lines 1 to 7 speak only of a success and need no premise; the first half of line 9 holds for every name, since the refusal is a failure. A merge under a name of white space only is outside the sentences: Java refuses it and Rust and TypeScript merge it. The example merge with that refusal in front, mod021_emptyGuard, meets the block (mod021_emptyGuard_holds). Where the merged transition sits in declaration order (Rust: the slot of the channel transition; Java and TypeScript: before the surviving instance transitions) is not stated, and neither is the firing order that slot breaks ties in (EXEC-002).
- Ruling D77 (a), clashes mod-b#1 and mod-b#2: the merged timing follows the rule all three runtimes share (rtMergeTiming: Immediate yields to the other side, two equal timings collapse, every other pair is rejected; rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:831-844, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:717-734, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:641-653), not the intersection of firing intervals the markdown stated before; clause 2, AC2, AC3 and the test derivation are reworded to it. The interval rule is the wrong model of MOD_021_forbids_intervalTiming: it merges Deadline(100) with Delayed(50) to Window(50, 100), which every runtime rejects. The merged timing is always one of the two sides' timings (rtMergeTiming_side), so it is valid when both are (rtMergeTiming_valid, TIME-001) and it is reaped exactly when one of the sides is (rtMergeTiming_reapable, TIME-006). Java's deprecated Unconstrained timing (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Timing.java:138) is not Immediate to mergeTimings, so Unconstrained with Delayed(50) is rejected; it is out of scope here as in TIME-001.
- Actions. sq stands for the runtimes' composed action, which runs the caller-side action and then the instance-side action against one context within one firing (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:866-883, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:765, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:683). Line 6 pins the merged action to sq applied to the two sides' actions in that order; at a non-commutative sq such as list append the instance-first order is killed (MOD_021_mutant_instanceActionFirst_killed). That the composed action runs within one firing, as clause 4 and AC4 say, is not a line: one merged definition is one transition, and its firing is EXEC-001's and CORE-021's. The witness sq is seqAct f, which also drops the built-in passthrough on either side, an elision nothing can observe. Priority: no runtime offers an override (pick_priority, pickPriority return the caller's), so clause 3 is reworded to the caller's priority without the former MAY, and line 1 states it.
- Input arcs. Line 2 and lines 10 and 11 assume that neither side has two input arcs on one place, which every built transition satisfies (CORE-030). On each place the table decides (MOD_021_table, every model of which is mergeCard). The position of a merged arc among the input arcs (the runtimes fold the caller's arcs and then the instance's, keeping the first-seen position: rewriter.rs:949, SubnetRewriter.java:845, subnet-rewriter.ts:846) is not normative (ruling D32) and not stated. Line 10's diagnostic names a real offending pair, the caller-side arc first, which is what that fold reports in all three runtimes; with one offending place the pair is fixed (mod021_offTable_sole).
- Other arcs and the output. Line 3 compares the inhibitor, read and reset arcs as sets without repetition: the runtimes unite them caller first, keeping the first occurrence (rewriter.rs:906, SubnetRewriter.java:800, subnet-rewriter.ts:725), and that order is not stated. Rule (a), reworded under ruling D20 (clash mod-b#3), covers these three arc types only. Line 4: the merged output specification is And(caller, instance), caller first, in all three runtimes (rewriter.rs:888, SubnetRewriter.java:782, subnet-rewriter.ts:707). When both sides produce into one place, And(Q, Q) names Q twice in one AND branch and the transition builder rejects the merge (IO-011, mergeEx_buildFails, mod021_buildFails): clause 1's union is read with line 7, so such a channel merge fails in every runtime and is no defect; the markdown says so under rule (b).
- Rule (d) is read as all three runtimes read it, by sets of arc types (ruling D20, clash mod-b#4; rewriter.rs:1063-1065, SubnetRewriter.java:884-886, subnet-rewriter.ts:907-909): Read + Reset on one side against Read alone on the other is a conflict, although pairing same-type arcs off first would leave no conflicting pair. That pair-off reading is the wrong model of MOD_021_forbids_pairOff. An output is not counted, as in every runtime: an input arc on one side and an output into the same place on the other is the usual channel wiring, which is why the premises of the markdown sentences speak of places on which both sides have an input, inhibitor, read or reset arc.
- Messages. Line 10 states the rule (c) diagnostic byte for byte as the three runtimes write it; Java and TypeScript spell atLeast(n), Rust and Python at_least(n) in the cardinality and in the closing hint (rewriter.rs:643-650, :1002-1009), and the line accepts both. The timing and arc-type messages are stated by what they name. Line 8: every runtime passes the caller-side name as the channel name and names it in the timing message and in the arc-type message. The two timings are named in each runtime's own rendering (Rust Debug, rewriter.rs:840; Java the record's toString, SubnetRewriter.java:731; TypeScript describeTiming, subnet-rewriter.ts:650), so line 8 states them through the parameter tstr; the witness is the reference's timingStr, and MOD_021_mutant_timingNameOnly_killed kills a message that names the caller only. Line 9: the caller-side name, an offending place and both sides' sets of arc types on it in the sorted rendering [inhibitor, input, read, reset] that the three runtimes share (describe_kinds rewriter.rs:1080-1084, the TreeSet toString of SubnetRewriter.java:900, describeKinds subnet-rewriter.ts:938-940); rule (d) of the markdown now states that rendering.
- Order of the checks, composition design skeptic correction S3. Rust and TypeScript check the timing, the ν-net match, the correspondence, the arc types, the input arcs and then the builder; Java checks the arc types first, then the timing, the match and the correspondence (rewriter.rs:624-651, SubnetRewriter.java:544-548, subnet-rewriter.ts:496-517). Line 8 therefore claims the two timings only when the arc types agree (Java's arc-type message names the caller but not the timings; clause 2 lets an implementation report the rule (d) error instead), and lines 9 and 10 claim a message only when the earlier checks of every order pass. Line 9 claims that some offending place is named, not which one: Rust takes the first in its sorted map of the instance's places, TypeScript the first in the instance's arc order and Java the first its HashMap yields.
- The declared-place correspondence merge cm is MOD-031's: its content and its rejection are that block's, and this block reads it only in the premises of lines 9 to 11. The ν-net match a transition may carry (NU-060) is not modelled here: CDef has no match field. The markdown sentences carry the premise that at most one side carries a match, since Rust and TypeScript reject two matches before the arc types and the input arcs (merge_match_specs, rewriter.rs:708-724); lines 9 to 11 hold over CDef, where no side carries one. NU-060 (wave W9) adds the field, its check and that premise to the Lean lines.
- AC1 is MOD_021_nonvacuous on the reference: caller T with input P and output Q merged with channel transition C with input R and output S gives one transition T with inputs P and R, output And(Q, S) and Immediate timing. AC2 is line 8: Delayed(100) against Deadline(50) is rejected with the timing message naming T, Delayed(100) and Deadline(50) (MOD_021_nonvacuous). AC3, reworded under ruling D77 (a), is lines 5 and 8 on its three cases (MOD_021_nonvacuous). AC4's order is line 6; that both actions run within one firing and that token movement is atomic is EXEC-001's and CORE-021's, since one merged definition is one transition. AC5 (one invocation per fire) follows for the same reason and is EXEC-001's. AC6 is line 2 with the table block on its rows (MOD_021_nonvacuous). AC7, reworded to the set reading, is line 9: input against reset on P is rejected naming T, P, [input] and [reset] (MOD_021_nonvacuous). AC8 is line 10: one() against all() on P gives the exact diagnostic (MOD_021_nonvacuous). AC9 is reworded under ruling D48 (a) to cite CORE-011, CONC-003 and EXEC-020, which own the stamp of a produced token and the order of deposited tokens; its one TokenAdded event per produced token is EVT-011's. The Depends on line now lists the requirements the reworded text cites.
- Mutants: line 1 kills MOD_021_mutant_instanceName and MOD_021_mutant_instancePriority, line 2 MOD_021_mutant_concatInputs, line 3 MOD_021_mutant_appendReads, line 4 MOD_021_mutant_callerOutput, line 5 MOD_021_mutant_callerTiming, line 6 MOD_021_mutant_instanceActionFirst, line 7 MOD_021_mutant_skipBuild, line 8 MOD_021_mutant_acceptTimingConflict and MOD_021_mutant_timingNameOnly, line 9 MOD_021_mutant_noKindCheck, line 10 MOD_021_mutant_instanceSeam, line 11 MOD_021_mutant_conservative. A merge that rejects everything violates line 11 (MOD_021_forbids_rejectAll).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_021_table"></a>
## MOD-021: Channel Composition, the input-arc merge table

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_021_table` · Kind **F** · Scope the input-arc merge table of every implementation, used by channel composition and by fusion (MOD-061) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0a4cf69a5fd0c3a6 ai** · Statement hash `0a4cf69a5fd0c3a6`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* two input arcs on one place are merged and each of them is `one` or `exactly`, the merged arc *shall* be `exactly` of the sum of their counts, where `one` counts 1.<br><br>*When* two `all` input arcs on one place are merged, the merged arc *shall* be `all`.<br><br>*When* two `atLeast` input arcs on one place are merged, the merged arc *shall* be `atLeast` of the larger of their two minimums.<br><br>*If* two input arcs on one place are merged and the pair is none of these three cases (each side `one` or `exactly`, both `all`, both `atLeast`), *then* the merge *shall* be rejected (rule (c)). | 1. For every merge table mg (two input-arc cardinalities on one place give the merged cardinality, or none for a rejection):<br>2. if each side draws a fixed count (one draws 1, exactly n draws n), mg merges them to exactly of the sum: one with one gives exactly 2, one with exactly n (either order) gives exactly (n + 1), exactly n with exactly m gives exactly (n + m);<br>3. mg merges all with all to all;<br>4. mg merges atLeast n with atLeast m to atLeast (max n m);<br>5. mg rejects (none) every pair the table does not list (mod021_listed: not both one or exactly, not both all, not both atLeast), for example one with all, exactly 2 with atLeast 2, all with atLeast 1. | <pre>fun mg ↦<br>  (∀ (a b : Card) (n m : ℕ),<br>      mod021_draw a = some n →<br>        mod021_draw b = some m → mg a b = some (Card.exactly (n + m))) ∧<br>    mg Card.all Card.all = some Card.all ∧<br>      (∀ (n m : ℕ),<br>          mg (Card.atLeast n) (Card.atLeast m) = some (Card.atLeast (max n m))) ∧<br>        ∀ (a b : Card), mod021_listed a b = false → mg a b = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A merge table is read as a function on the cardinalities of two input arcs that meet on one place (Card, Basic.lean: one, exactly n, all, atLeast n), giving the merged cardinality or a rejection. Only the cardinality is stated; the place of the merged arc, its slot among the transition's arcs, a guard on either side and the case of more than two arcs on one place (the runtimes fold the arcs left to right, first-seen slot) are the merge block's (MOD_021, kind B) and MOD-061's. All three runtimes implement exactly this table: Rust merge_in_pair (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:979-999), Java mergeInPair (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:845-860), TypeScript mergeInPair with summableCount (typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:846-873); Python uses the Rust code. The witness mergeCard (Spec/GlossaryCompose.lean) is that table.
- Counts are unbounded naturals. A sum past a machine integer (Java int, Rust usize) is out of scope, and so is a count the arc builder rejects (exactly 0, atLeast 0): the merged arc is rebuilt through the transition builder, whose checks are CORE-030's and IO-002's, and that rebuild is the merge block's line.
- The table is complete: every model of the block is mergeCard (mod021_table_unique). So 'The table is symmetric' holds of every model (mod021_table_symm) and needs no line of its own, and the explanatory sentence on why one and exactly sum while atLeast keeps the stricter minimum is mod021_table_required: a merged arc requires the sum of the two sides' required counts, or for two atLeast arcs the larger one, or for two all arcs is all.
- Rule (a) as first written ('Same arc type with same cardinality/weight: collapse to a single arc') would merge one with one to one, against the table, AC6 and every runtime (clash mod-b#3). Under ruling D20 (MB-6) rule (a) is reworded to cover read, inhibitor and reset arcs only, leaving input arcs to the table. The literal reading is the mutant MOD_021_table_mutant_ruleA, killed by mod021_collapse (equal cardinalities collapse, the table otherwise).
- Line 1 kills mod021_firstWins (keeps the first side's arc) and MOD_021_table_mutant_ruleA; line 2 kills MOD_021_table_mutant_noAllRow (two all arcs read as a conflict); line 3 kills MOD_021_table_mutant_atLeastSummed (atLeast minimums summed, AC6's 'not AtLeast(4)'); line 4 kills MOD_021_table_mutant_rowsOnly (an off-table pair merged to atLeast of the summed requirements instead of rejected). A table that rejects everything violates line 1 (MOD_021_table_forbids_rejectAll).
- AC6 (One with One gives a single Exactly(2) arc, All with All gives All, AtLeast(1) with AtLeast(3) gives AtLeast(3), not AtLeast(4)) is lines 1 to 3 on those rows (MOD_021_table_nonvacuous, by decide); that the merged transition carries a single input arc on the place is the merge block's line. AC8 (One with All rejected) is line 4 on that pair (MOD_021_table_nonvacuous); the shape of the rejection message (seam, both cardinalities, place) is the merge block's line for channel composition and MOD-061's for fusion, each with a sole-offender premise (composition design, skeptic correction S3).
- AC1 (arc union), AC2 (disjoint timings rejected), AC3 (overlapping timings), AC4 (the action order), AC5 (one firing per fire) and AC7 (different arc types rejected) are the merge block's (MOD_021, kind B, composition wave W8, over refMerge). AC9 (token timestamp and FIFO order of tokens produced by merged firings) is CONC-003 and EXEC-020 under ruling D48 (a), which rewords AC9 to cite them; its one TokenAdded event per produced token is EVT-011's.

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D36 (a): the type check is scoped to the implementations whose place identity carries the token type, which is Java. Java's compose(instance, map) and compose(instance, bindings) both run composeInternal, which for every port binding first fails on an unknown port and then compares the token type of the renamed port place (Instance.port(name, tokenType)) with the caller place's token type, throwing IllegalArgumentException with a message that names the port, the subnet, both types and the caller place (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java), before the collision check, the rewrite and the channel merges. tyOf is the place record's tokenType (typedNaming's second component, Prod.snd), and the text of a type is its Class.getName().
- Rust, TypeScript and Python are out of scope: their place identity does not carry the token type, and their compose checks no type. Rust's bind_port::<T> and TypeScript's bindPort<T> take T from the caller place they are given and record the place without its type (rust/libpetri-core/src/compose.rs, typescript/src/core/compose-bindings.ts), Rust's compose_internal resolves a port through port_handles and never reads the port's recorded TypeId (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), and Python's compose passes names. The composition that never checks (mod022NeverCheck) violates line 1 on the typed example (MOD_022_forbids_neverCheck). The withdrawn compile-time claim (old items 1 and 2: no binding API relates the port's type to the caller place's type, since ports are bound by name) and the per-language note are the markdown's prose; the typing invariant of CORE-003 is premised on compatible emissions in every language.
- A composition function is one implementation's compose(instance, bindings) read as a function from the builder, the instance, the port bindings as a list of (port name, caller place) and the channel bindings as a list of (channel name, caller-side definition) to the builder after the call or a rejection with a message (an exception, read as .error msg), as in MOD-020. Java's port bindings are a map, so no port is bound twice through compose(instance, map), and ComposeBindings.bindPort rejects a second binding of a port (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java); lines 1 to 3 are premised on distinct port names, which is MOD-020's matter (D72 (i)(a): a port bound twice fails, MOD-020 line 2).
- Line 2 is the markdown's 'with a message naming the port, the token type of the port's place and the token type of the caller place': to name is to contain as a substring (MsgNames, as in MOD-006 line 7). It is existential over the offending bindings: Java walks the map in hash order and reports the first offender it meets, so which offender is named when there are several is not stated. The markdown sentence and the line are premised on every bound port being known and bound once, because an unknown port met first in Java's walk reports the unknown-port message instead, and on no channel being bound twice, because Java's binding builder rejects a second binding of a channel while the caller records the bindings (ComposeBindings.bindChannel, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/ComposeBindings.java), before composeInternal checks any type, with the message Channel '<name>' is already bound, which names no type. For the same reason the sentence and the line are premised on no caller-side transition being bound to two channels: bindChannel rejects the second channel binding of one caller transition with a message that names the transition and two channels and no type. The line reads that premise as pairwise distinct names of the caller-side definitions (ruling D23). It is not premised on the absence of collisions: a composition that runs MOD-020's collision check before the type check fails with the collision message, which names no type (MOD_022_forbids_collisionFirst). Java's message also names the subnet and the caller place; the line asks for the port and the two types only.
- Line 2 does not say which of the two named types is the port's and which is the caller place's: a message that gives the two types the wrong way round meets it, as the substring reading of MOD-006 line 7 does not fix the order of words either. Substring containment is weak for a short name: the port name in occurs inside the words instance and String of any such message, so the example checks the quoted form port 'in' (MOD_022_nonvacuous), and the composition whose type message leaves out the port name is killed with a port q, whose letter occurs nowhere else in that message (MOD_022_forbids_anonPort).
- Line 3 is the acceptance half ('well-typed' bindings are not rejected for their type), stated for coherent calls without channel bindings and premised on everything else MOD-020 rejects being absent. Coherence (mod020_coherent, ruling D35 (a), as in MOD-020 lines 1, 4 to 9) is the premise because two ports may expose one body place (MOD-003) and a call that binds them to different caller places has no defined outcome: the reference rewrites through the first such binding (bindLookup), Java's composeInternal puts every binding into mergeMap in the caller's order so the last one wins, and its rejectPortCollisions pairs the ports, not the places (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java), so Java can reject such a call with a collision or a transition-builder message that the first-binding rewrite does not meet. The rest of the premises: a port bound twice, an unknown port, an input collision or output collision (two different bound ports sent to one caller place, consumed by one transition or named in one AND branch) and a rewritten transition that the transition builder Build rejects. It asks nothing of the ports the call leaves unbound: a call may bind only some of the interface's ports. The ports of the interface are read through the instance's port lookup (I.port), which on every instance that instantiate produces agrees with the interface (MOD-011). Java's builder transition() rejects nothing (Builder.transition, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java), so the builder b is arbitrary. Java's compose also refuses an instance whose definition's body declares a terminal place (composeInternal calls SubnetRewriter.rejectTerminals first, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java), which instantiate already refuses (EXEC-042 AC6), so no instance that compose is given has one. A call with channel bindings succeeds or fails by MOD-020 and MOD-021 (the channel merge); channel bindings carry no token-type check, since transitions are not typed, and arc-level type compatibility is CORE-003's.
- The type a binding is checked against is the type of the renamed port place that the instance's port lookup returns. On Java's naming model the rename keeps the token type, so jointly with MOD-011's two blocks this is the type the port was declared with, and a binding of a port to a caller place of another type than its declared type fails (mod022_declared).
- AC1 (port("in", String) -> Place<String> composes successfully) is line 3 in Java (MOD_022_nonvacuous: binding the String port in of the example instance r1 to the String place X composes, and r1/work then takes from X); in the other implementations it is MOD-020's acceptance. AC2 (in Java, a binding of the String port in to an Integer place is rejected at compose, through the typed overload and the map overload alike, with a message containing port 'in', String and Integer) is lines 1 and 2 (MOD_022_nonvacuous: the reference rejects that binding with a message containing port 'in', String and Integer). The test derivation is the two ACs.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_022_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_022): ✓ The reference composition satisfies MOD-022 for every token-type reader and transition builder: it checks every port binding's type before anything else, rejects a binding of another type with a message that names the port and both types (Java: port `in` has type String, caller place `X` has type Integer), and composes a well-typed call that nothing else rejects.
  <pre>∀ {N A T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N] [inst_2 : DecidableEq T]<br>  [inst_3 : ToString T] (tyOf : N → T) (Build : Reference.Trans N → Option String),<br>  MOD_022 tyOf Build (refCompose tyOf Build mod022Merge)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_022_forbids_anonPort` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_022): ✗ A composition whose type message leaves out the port name violates MOD-022 (line 2). It checks the bindings in Java's order and rejects every binding of another type, but when the `String` port `q` of `Worker` under `r1` is bound to the `Integer` place `X`, its message says only that "a port" of `r1` has type `String` and "its caller place" has type `Integer`: the letter `q` occurs nowhere in it, so the user cannot tell which binding is wrong.
  <pre>¬MOD_022 Prod.snd refBuild (mod022AnonCompose Prod.snd refBuild mod022Merge)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_022_forbids_collisionFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_022): ✗ A composition that runs the collision check of MOD-020 before the type check violates MOD-022 (line 2). Ports `a` (`String`) and `b` (`Integer`) both feed the transition `r1/t`, and the call binds both to the `String` place `X`: port `b` has the wrong type, but the call fails with the message about two ports sent to one place, which never says `Integer`.
  <pre>¬MOD_022 mod022CpTy refBuild (mod022CollFirst mod022CpTy refBuild mod022Merge)</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_023"></a>
## MOD-023: Composition Produces Flat Net

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_023` · Kind **B** · Scope build() of every enclosing builder, whatever compose(...), fuse(...) and other builder calls were made on it (Java, TypeScript, Rust, Python) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 5cbec5570ebe1e37 ai** · Statement hash `5cbec5570ebe1e37`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* `build()` succeeds, every transition of the built net *shall* pass the checks of the transition builder ([CORE-030], [IO-002], [IO-004], [EXEC-012], [IO-011] to [IO-014]), whichever `compose(...)`, `fuse(...)` or other builder calls produced it.<br><br>*When* `build()` succeeds, a new builder on which the places of the built net are declared, its transitions are added by hand in the same order with the same name, arcs, output specification, timing, priority and action and no correspondence ([MOD-031]), and its terminal places ([EXEC-042]) are declared *shall* build a net with the same transitions in the same order, the same places, each listed as often, in any order, and the same set of terminal places.<br><br>*When* `build()` succeeds, no `compose(...)` call binds a channel ([MOD-021]) and no composed instance has two transitions of one name, the built net *shall* hold one transition for each transition added by hand and for each transition of a composed instance or of a directly composed subnet, in the order of the calls and, within one call, in the order of the subnet, each with the name, timing, priority and action it was added with. | 1. **Assumptions**

- Model scope. A build-script function (ScriptFn, Reference/ComposeBuild.lean) is one implementation's enclosing builder read as a function of the calls made on it, from a new builder, up to build(): Rust's PetriNet builder and its build (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), Java's PetriNet.Builder (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java) and TypeScript's builder (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts); Python rides on Rust. A panic or exception, at a call or at build(), is a rejection (.error msg). The calls are Op: place, transition (a Transition exists only once built, so a hand-added definition has passed Build), terminal place, fusion set (MOD-060), compose with bindings (MOD-020), auto-compose (MOD-024) and direct composition (MOD-025). Each transition call adds one built transition: adding one Transition object twice, which Java and TypeScript keep once in an identity-keyed set (CORE-021), is not a script this block reads. The witness buildScript folds those calls over the builder record of the reference net builder (CORE-040: buildScript_core) and finishes with fusion (MOD-061), the terminal check of EXEC-042 and the retired-port check of MOD-027. The naming model Nm is the place naming the composition calls rename under, a model parameter of every composition block (MOD-010, MOD-024, MOD-025). No line reads it; the block keeps it because the holds theorem may bind only the model parameters it passes to the block, and the witness buildScript renames auto- and direct composition through a naming model, which exists at no type uniformly (Unit has none: two valid prefixes must rename its one place apart). So MOD_023_reference passes its Nm through this binder, and all three lines hold for every naming.
- Line 1 holds for every Build: the specific rejection messages belong to CORE-030, IO-002, IO-004, EXEC-012 and IO-011 to IO-014 (the list of CORE-022's note), and line 1 is what lets their 'every construction path' notes reach a composed net. Build reads the firing view of a definition only (TransDef.toTrans: arcs, output specification and the reapable bit of the timing), so the checks line 1 reaches are the arc and output-specification checks. A check that reads timing values (the timing check of TIME-001 that EXEC-012's note places in the transition builder, the maximum-duration rejection of 03-timing.md) is not in Build and is out of line 1: every transition was built when it was added, so its timing passed that check then, and line 3 says that composition and fusion keep the timing a transition was added with; the timing of a channel merge is MOD-021's (line 5) and its result is a built transition (MOD-021 line 7). Line 1 is met by construction in the runtimes: a hand-added transition is built, composition rebuilds every rewritten transition through the transition builder (MOD-020), a channel merge returns a built transition (MOD-021), fusion rebuilds every rewritten transition (MOD-061 line 2), and direct composition adds a body's built transitions unchanged (MOD-025). The mutant mod023_noCheckScript, which never runs the checks, builds a fused transition that consumes from and reads one place, which EXEC-012 rejects; mod023_handCheckScript, which checks hand-added transitions and never a rewritten one, does the same and is forbidden.
- Line 2 compares the structure only. Transitions are compared as a list of TransDef, so name, arcs, output specification, timing, priority, action and declaration order are equal (declaration order is the last tie-break of the ready order, EXEC-002, ruling D32). Places are compared up to order (List.Perm, each place as often) and terminal places as a set: the order of places is not normative (ruling D32), and the reference net builder lists a place once, at its last occurrence. The two records a composed net may carry beside that structure are not compared: the MOD-031 correspondence (a hand-written definition has none, and an action of a composed transition resolves its subnet's declared places through it, where a hand-written action names the actual places) and the MOD-026 membership map (only direct composition records one; the hand-written net has none). That is the sentence of the markdown's first paragraph that the two records 'sit beside that structure and are not part of it', and the reading of 'indistinguishable' and 'same actions' the block takes. The mutant mod023_dupScript, which lists a declared place a second time when an arc also names it (a slip from the set the builders keep their places in to a plain list), meets lines 1 and 3 and breaks line 2: the hand-written copy of a composed net declares every place, so A_IN, answer/OUT and go come out twice. mod023_canonScript, which stores the timing of a hand-added transition in canonical form (Window(0, d) as Deadline(d)) and keeps a composed transition's timing as it comes, breaks lines 2 and 3 and is forbidden: a composed Window(0, 5) transition, written by hand, builds as Deadline(5).
- Line 3 ties the build to the calls, which line 2 cannot do: line 2 compares a built net with the net its own hand-written copy builds, so a loss that a second build repeats passes it. Line 3 compares the built transitions with the transitions the calls added: the hand-added one, the instance's transitions in the instance's order for compose and auto-compose (MOD-020 line 1, MOD-024), the body's transitions in the body's order for direct composition (MOD-025 line 1), in the order of the calls; fusion rewrites each transition in place and keeps the order (MOD-061 line 1). It compares name, timing, priority and action only: the arcs and the output specification are rewritten by the bindings (MOD-020) and by fusion (MOD-061), whose blocks state the rewrite. Line 3 is premised on distinct names within each composed instance (rulings D10 and D23, the unique-names assumption), because no builder rejects a subnet body with two transitions of one name and every runtime then stages the instance's rewritten transitions in a map keyed by name, so only one of the two reaches the built net (Rust staged.insert and order in apply_composition, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1132-1137 and :1215-1219; Java rewrittenByName, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:825-828; TypeScript rewrittenByName, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:580-583), where the reference keeps both. MOD-020 (mod020_fresh) and MOD-024 take the same premise. Direct composition adds a body's transitions one by one (MOD-025) and needs no such premise. A script with a channel binding is out of line 3, since a merged transition takes its name, priority, timing and action from the MOD-021 merge (MOD-021 lines 1, 5 and 6). In the runtimes, Java's SubnetRewriter.rebuildWithName copies timing, priority and action onto every rewritten transition (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:202-210) and applyFusion collects the rewritten transitions in an insertion-ordered set (SubnetRewriter.java:941-958). The mutant mod023_dropPriScript, a composition that rebuilds every rewritten transition at the default priority 0 (CORE-020), meets lines 1 and 2 and breaks line 3: composing a subnet whose transition has priority 5 builds it at priority 0, and the hand-written copy of that net, written from the built net, builds it at 0 too. mod023_nameOrderScript, a fusion that returns the transitions in name order (a slip from an insertion-ordered set to a hash set in applyFusion, or to a name-keyed map in Rust's build_with_fusion), is forbidden by line 3 for the same reason.
- The paragraph on downstream consumers, reworded under ruling D20 (clash mod-b#11, recommendation MB-6 of the composition map): the executor and the event subsystem run the firing relations, which read a built net through BuiltNet.toNet and BuiltNet.toTimed only, and mod023_sameView shows that for every model of line 2 a net and its hand-written equivalent have the same transitions in the untimed view, the same timing of every transition in the timed view and the same places up to order. The verifier reads the same structure (MOD-050, whose block carries AC4). The exporter MAY read the MOD-026 membership to draw subnet clusters (MOD-040); that is the one stated exception, since every exporter reads it (rust/libpetri-export/src/mapper.rs:131-136, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/export/PetriNetGraphMapper.java:74, typescript/src/export/petri-net-mapper.ts:94). The sentence that compiled representations (CONC-007, CONC-020) are constructed identically, provided the hand-written net declares its places in the order the composed net holds them, follows from line 2 because a compiled net is computed from the built net alone; it is not restated here, as no compiled-net model is in scope. The first paragraph's MUST and the two MUST sentences of the consumer paragraph stay in the markdown as prose; lines 2 and 3, mod023_sameView and the blocks named here are what state them.
- AC1 (identical place index, transition count, arc topology, bitmap masks and timing arrays of the compiled representations, for a hand-written net that declares its places in the composed net's order) follows from line 2 for the transitions, their arcs and their timing; the place index also depends on place order, which line 2 leaves free: Rust sorts the place names before indexing (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:68-75), Java and TypeScript index the places arcs name in transition order and then the declared ones (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java:102-113, typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:82-99), so a hand-written net that declares its places in the composed net's order gets the same index, which is the premise AC1 now states. That part is tested, not proven. AC2 (identical event sequences and final markings, with the hand-written actions naming the actual places) follows from line 2 for every firing semantics that reads only the structure (mod023_sameView); the net of line 2 keeps the composed actions with no correspondence, so it is the structure AC2 compares, not the hand-written net AC2 runs; equality of a run's event sequence, timestamps included, is tested, not proven. AC3 is reworded under ruling D20 (clash mod-b#11): byte-equal DOT when the composed net carries no membership, and the subnet clusters drawn from membership as the allowed difference of a directly composed net; DOT bytes are EXP's and MOD-040's, not this block's. AC4 (identical verification results) is MOD-050's line, which takes MOD-023 line 2 as its premise.
- No acceptance line. The block is three safety lines on a successful build: a builder that rejects every script meets it. When a script builds is stated by the blocks that own each call: CORE-040 for a hand-written script (buildScript_core), MOD-020 line 9, MOD-021, MOD-024 line 4, MOD-025 line 5 and MOD-061 line 6; that the builder offers build() at all is an existence clause for a coverage theorem, not a line of this block. The test derivation (a composed net N1 and a hand-written equivalent N2 run alike) is MOD_023_nonvacuous on the reference for the structure, and a test for the runs.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_023_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_023): ✓ The reference build script satisfies MOD-023 for every naming model and every transition-builder check. Compose the instance `answer` into a builder that already has a hand added transition, and build: every transition of the net passes the transition builder's checks. Write the built net out by hand (its places, its transitions in the same order, its terminal places) and build that: the same transitions come out in the same order, with the same places and terminal places. With no channel bound, the transitions are the hand added one and then the instance's, each with the name, timing, priority and action it was added with.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N] (Nm : Naming N)<br>  (Build : Reference.Trans N → Option String),<br>  MOD_023 Nm Build<br>    (buildScript Nm (fun x ↦ ()) Build<br>      (refMerge Build (seqAct fun a x ↦ a) fun x x_1 ↦ Except.ok none))</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_023_forbids_canonTiming` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_023): ✗ The builder that stores a hand-added timing in canonical form, and a composed one as it comes, is forbidden: composing instance `answer` of a subnet whose transition `work` has timing `Window(0, 5)` builds `answer/work` with `Window(0, 5)`, while writing the same net by hand builds it with `Deadline(5)`, so the composed net is not the net its hand-written equivalent builds.
  <pre>¬MOD_023 strNaming refBuild mod023_canonScript</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_023_forbids_fuseNameOrder` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_023): ✗ The builder whose fusion returns the transitions in name order is forbidden: adding `t2` and then `t1` and fusing their input places builds `t1` before `t2`, so the built transitions are not in the order the calls added them, and the ready order, whose last tie-break is declaration order ([EXEC-002]), changes.
  <pre>¬MOD_023 strNaming refBuild mod023_nameOrderScript</pre>
