<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_024"></a>
## MOD-024: Identity-Default Port Inference (auto-compose)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_024` · Kind **B** · Scope every enclosing-net builder that offers the single-argument compose(instance) (Java, TypeScript, Rust); lines 3 and 4 for those with the inference path (all three) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 68382e84d6e6ea1a ai** · Statement hash `68382e84d6e6ea1a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* `compose(instance)` is called on an instance whose subnet declares at least one port and no channel, the builder *shall* give the same result as `compose(instance, bindings)` with each declared port bound to the place on that port's declaration, the same rejection included.<br><br>*If* the subnet of an instance passed to `compose(instance)` declares a channel, *then* `compose(instance)` *shall* fail with an error that names every channel the subnet declares.<br><br>*Where* the builder infers bindings for a subnet without ports, *when* `compose(instance)` succeeds on an instance whose subnet declares no port and no channel and whose transitions have pairwise distinct names, the builder *shall* keep its transitions and add the instance's transitions in order, each with every arc and output place on a renamed body place `p/x` moved to `x` when the builder held `x` at the call, by the implementation's `Place` equality, every other place kept, its name, timing, priority and action unchanged and its declared-to-actual place correspondence ([MOD-031]) moved the same way or, when every entry of it then maps a place to itself, dropped as a whole as [MOD-031] allows, *shall* add to its places exactly the places those transitions name, and *shall* leave its terminal places, retired ports, subnet membership and fusion sets as they were.<br><br>*Where* the builder infers bindings for a subnet without ports, *when* `compose(instance)` is called on an instance whose subnet declares no port and no channel and whose transitions have pairwise distinct names, `compose(instance)` *shall* succeed exactly when every instance transition, with each renamed body place `p/x` moved to `x` when the builder holds `x`, passes the transition builder's checks. | 1. For every naming model Nm, transition builder check Build, composition function C and auto-composition function Au (whose third argument is the names of the channels the instance's subnet declares):<br>2. for every builder b and instance I with at least one port, Au b I [] equals C b I ports [], where ports binds each port's name to the place on its declaration (I.iface), in declaration order, and no channel is bound;<br>3. for every builder b, instance I and non-empty list cs of declared channel names, Au b I cs fails with a message that contains every name in cs;<br>4. for every builder b and instance I without ports whose definitions have pairwise distinct names, if Au b I [] returns b', then the definitions of b' are those of b followed by one definition per definition of I, in order, each I's definition rewritten by autoDef (every place q goes to the first builder place h with Nm.pre (prefix of I) h = q, when q is a place of I, and stays otherwise; name, timing, priority and action kept, the MOD-031 correspondence chained through the same map) or that rewrite with its correspondence dropped as a whole when every entry of it maps a place to itself (mod024_autoOk, corrDropPass of MOD-031), a place is in b' exactly when it is in b or a rewritten definition names it, and the terminal places, retired ports, subnet contributions and fusion sets of b' are those of b;<br>5. for every builder b and instance I without ports whose definitions have pairwise distinct names, Au b I [] succeeds exactly when Build accepts every rewritten definition. | <pre>fun {N A} x Nm Build C Au ↦<br>  (∀ (b : Bld N A) (I : Instance N A),<br>      I.iface ≠ [] →<br>        Au b I [] = C b I (List.map (fun pt ↦ (pt.name, pt.place)) I.iface) []) ∧<br>    (∀ (b : Bld N A) (I : Instance N A) (cs : List String),<br>        cs ≠ [] → ∃ msg, Au b I cs = Except.error msg ∧ ∀ c ∈ cs, MsgNames msg c) ∧<br>      (∀ (b b' : Bld N A) (I : Instance N A),<br>          I.iface = [] →<br>            (List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) I.defs).Nodup →<br>              Au b I [] = Except.ok b' →<br>                (∃ ms,<br>                    b'.defs = b.defs ++ ms ∧<br>                      List.Forall₂ (mod024_autoOk Nm b I) ms I.defs) ∧<br>                  (∀ (x_1 : N),<br>                      x_1 ∈ b'.places ↔<br>                        x_1 ∈ b.places ∨<br>                          ∃ d ∈ I.defs, x_1 ∈ (autoDef Nm b I d).namedPlaces) ∧<br>                    b'.terminals = b.terminals ∧<br>                      b'.retired = b.retired ∧<br>                        b'.contrib = b.contrib ∧ b'.fusions = b.fusions) ∧<br>        ∀ (b : Bld N A) (I : Instance N A),<br>          I.iface = [] →<br>            (List.map (fun x ↦ x.core.name) I.defs).Nodup →<br>              ((∃ b', Au b I [] = Except.ok b') ↔<br>                ∀ d ∈ I.defs, Build (autoDef Nm b I d).toTrans = none)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The single-argument form is a SHOULD. Java (PetriNet.java compose(Instance), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:409-453), Rust (compose_auto, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:440-501) and TypeScript (composeAuto behind compose(instance), typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:437-489) offer it. Python offers only the explicit forms (NetBuilder.compose and compose_instance take a port_bindings mapping, rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs), which the SHOULD allows; the block's scope leaves it out.
- The model passes the names of the channels the instance's subnet declares as the argument cs, since Instance holds no channel list; that cs is the declared list is the caller's premise, not a line. Lines 1, 3 and 4 are stated at cs = [], the subnet declaring no channel. Line 2 holds whatever the ports are: Rust and TypeScript check channels first, Java checks for terminal places first, which instantiate already refuses (EXEC-042 AC6), so the check is unreachable from an instance and not stated here.
- Line 1 is the sentence 'the resulting binding map MUST be processed identically to an explicit compose(instance, map) call per [MOD-020]' as an equation of results: the same builder or the same rejection message. Rust and TypeScript bind a port to the builder's equal-named place object when the builder holds one (petri_net.rs:472-476, petri-net.ts:458-469); under name-only place equality that object is the declared place, so the binding is the one line 1 names. In TypeScript the explicit form keeps the caller's own Place object in the rewritten arcs (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:551), and the builder keys its places by name and keeps the first object of a name (petri-net.ts:161 and addPlace at :191-193), so both forms leave one place of that name in the builder; the line compares places by name, the TypeScript place equality of CORE-002. Two ports over one body place (ruling D35 (a)) are bound to one declared place, so their bindings agree. AC1 (structurally equal to the explicit form) and AC5 (auto-compose then build() is indistinguishable from the explicit form then build()) are line 1, build() being a function of the builder. AC2 (the declared place P arrives in the net through the rewritten port arcs when the builder lacked it) is line 1 with MOD-020's success shape, which adds every place an arc of an added definition names; MOD_024_nonvacuous shows it on the reference. The result satisfying MOD-023 is MOD-023's line applied to the explicit form.
- Line 2 is AC4 and the sentence 'If the subnet's interface declares any channel, compose(instance) MUST raise an error naming the channels'. To name a channel is for the message to contain its name as a substring (MsgNames, MOD-006). All three runtimes name every declared channel and point at their explicit overload (compose_with in Rust, compose(instance, Consumer) in Java, compose(instance, bind => ...) in TypeScript); the pointer is API-specific text and is tested, not proven.
- Lines 3 and 4 are the MAY paragraph on body inference and AC3, scoped to implementations with the inference path: all three runtimes walk the renamed body's places, strip the prefix and probe the builder's place set with the original identity (Java by name and token type, Place.of(originalName, renamed.tokenType()); Rust and TypeScript by name), and bind each match through the same composition step as the explicit form (applyComposition / apply_composition) with no port, so no MOD-020 collision can arise (two different places never rename to one) and no port is retired (MOD-027). The naming model Nm is the implementation's place equality (strNaming or typedNaming, CORE-002), so the probe is Nm.pre (prefix) h = q. The two equalities give different bindings when the builder holds a place of the body place's name and another token type: Java keeps the body place private, the name-only runtimes bind it (mod024_placeEquality_divergence). An implementation without the inference path is out of the scope of lines 3 and 4: line 1's sentence then applies with no bindings. The inference reads the builder's places at the call, so it is order-sensitive by design (MOD-025 contrasts this); MOD_024_nonvacuous shows a builder that does not hold the place at the call keeping the renamed place private.
- Line 3 states the definitions, the place set and the builder's other records; the order of the places is not normative (ruling D32). An instance place that no arc names is not added, as for the explicit form (ruling D20, mod-b item 9). Line 3's rewrite is CDef.map, so the MOD-031 correspondence is chained through the inferred map; what the correspondence then resolves is MOD-031's line. A rewritten definition may instead carry no correspondence when the chained one maps every place to itself (mod024_autoOk, MOD-031's corrDropPass): that is the MAY of MOD-031 (AC9), and all three runtimes take it on every rewrite pass (Rust wholesale_drop_if_all_identity, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs; Java compactIdentityAlias, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java, by name and token type; TypeScript dropIfAllIdentity, which returns EMPTY_ALIAS, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts). On the inference path a body place s/P moved back to P chains the entry (P, P), so a definition whose places the builder all holds ends with an all-identity correspondence, which the runtimes drop and the reference keeps; mod024_dropAu_holds shows that the model that drops it meets the block. The identity test is decided by the naming model's place equality (decide on N), which is the one the correspondence lookup uses (MOD-031). The builder's terminal places, retired ports (MOD-027: body places merged by inference are not ports and are not retired), subnet contributions (MOD-026 item 4: instance composition records no membership) and fusion sets (MOD-060) stay as they were: Rust apply_composition retires only merge entries that are port places (its MOD-027 retire step, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs), TypeScript applyComposition walks the instance's port handles and Java composeInternal its interface's ports, which an instance without ports has none of, and none of the three records membership or a fusion set on this path.
- Line 4 is the acceptance line skeptic correction S2 of the composition design asks for, with its converse: a transition that fails the transition builder's checks after the rewrite fails the call, as in MOD-020, since all three runtimes rebuild every rewritten transition through the transition builder (Rust substitute_places, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:142-146). The message is the builder's, as in MOD-020, and line 4 does not state it. With line 3 this is AC5 for a subnet without ports: the explicit form with the inferred wiring succeeds and fails on the same calls and gives the same builder.
- The sentence that name-only implementations MUST document the more permissive matching contract in their API surface is a documentation duty (Rust compose_auto's doc comment and TypeScript composeAuto's comment state it), reviewed, not proven. The SHOULD that the probe uses the implementation's own Place equality is the parameter Nm. The SHOULD on when callers use the explicit overloads is guidance to callers, not a duty of the builder.
- AC6 (an empty subnet composes as a no-op on the builder's place and transition sets) follows from lines 3 and 4 for every model of the block (mod024_empty), so it has no mutant of its own.
- Lines 3 and 4 assume that the instance's transitions have pairwise distinct names, the premise MOD-020 takes (mod020_fresh) under the unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23. Transition names are assumed distinct (ruling D23) and no builder rejects a subnet body with two transitions of one name, and Rust's apply_composition stages the rewritten transitions in a map keyed by name (its staged map, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs) and drains it through the insertion order (its order vector), so the second transition of a name replaces the first and the builder gains one transition fewer than line 3 says. The block claims nothing about such a call, which leaves a builder free to reject it. Composing one instance twice, or two instances under one prefix, is not excluded: every runtime appends the second instance's transitions after the first (Java and TypeScript hold transitions in sets keyed by object identity, Rust in its builder's transition list), as line 3 says.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_024_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_024): ✓ The reference auto-composition satisfies MOD-024 for every naming model and transition builder. An instance `w1` with a port `in` on its place `in` is composed exactly as if `in` were bound by hand to the caller place `in`. An instance whose definition declares the channel `go` is refused, with a message that names `go`. An instance with no ports moves its place `w1/x` onto the builder's place `x` when the builder has one, and keeps it as `w1/x` otherwise.

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_024_mutant_noAcceptance_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_024): The auto-composition that rejects every subnet without ports kills the mutant: it meets lines 1, 2 and 3 (line 3 speaks of successes only), but rejects the empty instance, whose transitions all pass the transition builder (line 4).

## MOD-025: Direct Composition (compose a subnet without instantiation)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_025` · Kind **B** · Scope every direct composition of a subnet definition into an enclosing builder (Java, TypeScript, Rust, Python); the token-type line where place identity carries the token type (Java) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 b94fd7c7b25294f2 ai** · Statement hash `b94fd7c7b25294f2`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* direct composition of a subnet definition into an enclosing builder succeeds, the builder *shall* hold its earlier transitions followed by the body's transitions in the body's order, each unchanged and under its original name, and its earlier places together with every body place and every place a body transition names, a body place equal to a place it already holds being that place, **Assumptions**

- The builder is the composition model's Bld (Reference/ComposeBind.lean): its places, its transition definitions in the order added, its declared terminal places, retired ports (MOD-027), direct-composition contributions (MOD-026) and fusion sets (MOD-060). A direct-composition function (DirectFn) is one implementation's compose(SubnetDef) call read as a function of the builder at the call and the definition: Rust compose_direct (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:536-607), Java Builder.compose(SubnetDef) (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:576-650), TypeScript composeDirect (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:348-407), Python through the Rust call. A panic or exception is a rejection (.error msg); 'at the call' is that D b S itself fails, which is 'at compose time' and item 4 (composition is eager, MOD-020): nothing waits for build(). That the builder offers a direct-composition operation at all is an existence clause, not a safety line: it belongs in a coverage theorem (as ExecCoversW5 does for the execution blocks), not in this block.
- Places are the abstract N, the key type of the place model (CORE-002), so 'merge purely by name equality' is equality of keys: a body place equal to a place the builder holds is that place. Under strNaming (TypeScript, Rust, Python) a key is the name; under typedNaming (Java) it is the name and the token type, and a same-named place of another type is the type line's rejection, so no two places of one name arise either way. Line 4 is the token-type sentence for the implementations whose place identity carries the token type (Java, ruling D36 (a)): tyOf is the token type there (Prod.snd on typedNaming keys). Rust and TypeScript compare places by name and document the name-only merge (petri_net.rs:525-527, petri-net.ts:341-343), the MAY carve-out of the markdown: for them tyOf is constant and line 4 asks nothing. The markdown's MUST that such implementations document the name-only merge contract in their API surface is a documentation obligation, not behaviour, and no line states it; those doc comments are where it is met. The compile-time half of a token type is not modelled.
- Line 1 is items 1 to 3. 'Unchanged' is equality of the definition values (CDef), so arcs, output specification, timing, priority and action tag are those of the body; that the action is shared by reference is MOD-030's line, and that a directly-composed definition carries no correspondence is MOD-031's. The order of places is not normative (ruling D32), so the places are compared up to order: 'no place added twice' is that the places after the call are the earlier ones, each as often as before, and some new ones, each once and none held before (AC1's single output place). The definitions are compared as a list: the body's transitions follow the builder's in the body's order in all three runtimes, which is the declaration order EXEC-002 uses as its last tie-break. The subnet membership a direct composition records (the contrib field) is MOD-026's line, not this block's. The places a body arc names are added too: every runtime's transition() collects them (petri_net.rs:597-599, PetriNet.java:644-645, petri-net.ts:402-403), and every built body already holds them (DirectClosed).
- Line 2 is the paragraph on transition name collisions. The check is against the transitions the builder holds at the call (petri_net.rs:559-575, PetriNet.java:595-606, petri-net.ts:370-381): a host transition of the same name added after the call is not rejected by direct composition. That case falls under the shared unique-names assumption (ruling D10; no builder checks transition names, ruling D23). For the same reason no line asks anything of two body transitions of one name, or of two transitions of one name the builder already holds: line 5 accepts such a call and line 1 adds both, as all three runtimes do, since they take the host's names once before the loop; such nets are outside the unique-names assumption. The message part has a sole-offender premise (skeptic correction S3 of the composition design): all three runtimes check terminal places, then channels, then transition names, then (Java) token types, and stop at the first failure, so with several offending names the message names one of them, and with a terminal place or a channel it is that check's message. To name is to contain as a substring (MsgNames, as in MOD-006), so a message that lists every body transition, the offending one among them, also meets the message part; that the message names the offending transition and no innocent one is tested, not proven. The markdown asks the message to name both nets and to point at instantiate(prefix); the model's builder carries no net name, so the line asks for the transition and the subnet definition only, and the enclosing net's name and the pointer, which all three runtimes write, are tested, not proven.
- Line 3 is the channel paragraph's rejection (all three runtimes: petri_net.rs:542-553, PetriNet.java:582-589, petri-net.ts:355-364). That the message names the channels and points at instantiation with explicit binding is tested, not proven: the reference's stand-in text does not list the channels. Line 4 is the token-type paragraph's rejection (PetriNet.java:608-627); that the message names the place and both token types is likewise tested, not proven. Java compares each body place with every host place of its name (a name-keyed map of lists, PetriNet.java:613-616), so when the builder already holds two places of one name with different token types it rejects a body place of that name whichever type it has, as line 4 does, and names the first host place of another type in the order the builder added them.
- Line 5 is the acceptance line every partial composition function needs (skeptic correction S2: a function that rejects everything meets lines 2 to 4). Its premise on terminal places is line 7. Interface ports are advisory (MOD-004): no line reads the ports, so a port's place merges by equality like any other body place, and a model that consulted the ports could not meet line 1 and line 5 at once on a definition whose port places are its body places.
- Line 6 is the order-independence paragraph as reworded under ruling D20 (clash mod-b#12): the two builders hold the same places, transitions and arcs, while the declaration order of the places and of the transitions follows the order of the calls (line 1). It is stated for two definitions (AC3); the body's 'any order' of any number of definitions follows for every model of the block (mod025_perm: a sequence of direct compositions that succeeds in one order succeeds in every reordering with the same flat net), since by lines 1 to 5 a later call depends on the builder only through its places and transition names as sets (mod025_congr). Its premises hold of every built subnet definition (DirectClosed, above) except the terminal places, which line 7 rejects in every order. Line 6 follows from lines 1 to 5 for every model (mod025_line6_of): a successful first call shows the second definition clashes with neither the builder nor the first definition, and the clash checks read only set membership. So it has no mutant of its own (as for MOD-010 AC2, skeptic correction S4); without its premise on body places it would not follow, since the type check reads the body places only (Reference/ComposeBind.lean, notes of the model step).
- Line 7 is EXEC-042 AC6 for direct composition, which EXEC-042's block leaves to the composition model: a subnet body that declares terminal places is rejected by compose. All three runtimes reject it before any other check (petri_net.rs:539, PetriNet.java:578, petri-net.ts:352), so the body's terminal declarations are never dropped without a word. That the message names the place is tested, not proven: the reference's stand-in text names the subnet only (all three runtimes name the first terminal place through the helper instantiate uses). The same rejection by instantiate, with the message naming the place, is MOD-010 line 4.
- AC1 (one output place, the body arc on the host place) is line 1 and MOD_025_nonvacuous. AC2 (body transitions under their original names, no prefix/ separator introduced) is line 1: the definitions are the body's own values; MOD_025_forbids_prefixes kills a composition that prefixes them. AC3 (two subnets in opposite orders give the same place set, transition set and arc topology) is line 6, with its example in MOD_025_nonvacuous. AC4 (a transition name collision is rejected at compose time, naming the transition and pointing at instantiation) is line 2. AC5 (a declared channel is rejected) is line 3. AC6 (token-typed implementations reject a same-named body place of another type) is line 4. AC7 (an empty subnet is a no-op) follows from lines 1 and 5 (mod025_empty), up to the order of the places and the membership records of MOD-026. AC8 (direct and instance composition may be mixed, un-prefixed and prefix/ names coexist) is line 5: a direct composition is rejected only for a name the builder holds, and a renamed name p/x is not the body's name x; that instance composition then accepts the result is MOD-020's. AC9 (direct composition then build() is indistinguishable from a hand-written net) and the sentence 'The result MUST satisfy [MOD-023]' are MOD-023's line that a built net passes the build checks and is flat (composition wave W8), with its DOT clause reworded under ruling D20 (clash mod-b#11). The sentences on when to use direct composition and that it is additive are guidance, not behaviour.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_026"></a>
## MOD-026: Subnet-Membership Metadata for Direct Composition

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_026` · Kind **B** · Scope every build of a net through an enclosing builder (Java, TypeScript, Rust, Python) and every action binding of a built net · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 d56ae3d51d7883ae ai** · Statement hash `d56ae3d51d7883ae`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a `compose(SubnetDef)` call succeeds, the builder *shall* record each body place and each body transition of the subnet definition, by name, as contributed by that subnet under the definition's name with each `/` replaced by `_`.<br><br>The builder *shall* record contributions only in `compose(SubnetDef)` calls.<br><br>*When* a build succeeds, the membership mapping of the built net *shall* be the resolution of the contributions the build recorded, except for the names of the places that fusion ([MOD-061]) removed.<br><br>*If* fusion removes a member place other than the first member of its fusion set, *then* the membership mapping of the built net *shall* have no entry for that member's name.<br><br>*When* a build succeeds, a build that differs from it only in the names of the subnet definitions it composes directly *shall* also succeed and give the same places, transitions, terminal places and transition correspondences ([MOD-031]).<br><br>*When* actions are bound to a built net ([CORE-042]), the net that binding returns *shall* carry the same membership mapping. | 1. For every naming model Nm, every build-script function S and every action-binding function Rb on composed nets, where the records of a script are, in the order of its calls, for each direct composition of a subnet definition D one record (name of p, slashFree D.name) per body place p and one record (name of t, slashFree D.name) per body transition t, and nothing for any other call, and a name n is fused away in a script when some fusion set the script declares has a member other than its first member whose name is n:<br>2. if S ops returns the composed net c and n is not fused away in ops, then c.member n is s exactly when the records of ops resolve n to s (MemberOf: (n, s) is a record and every record for n names s);<br>3. if S ops returns c and n is fused away in ops, then c.member n is absent;<br>4. if S ops returns c and ops' is ops with the subnet definition of each direct composition renamed, each call on its own, and every other call unchanged (RenamesDirect), then S ops' returns some c' with the same places, transitions, terminal places and correspondences as c;<br>5. for every composed net c and every resolver r, Rb c r has the membership map of c. | <pre>fun {N A} Nm S Rb ↦<br>  (∀ (ops : List (Op N A)) (c : ComposedNet N A) (n s : String),<br>      S ops = Except.ok c →<br>        ¬FusedAway Nm ops n →<br>          (c.member n = some s ↔ MemberOf (scriptRecords Nm ops) n s)) ∧<br>    (∀ (ops : List (Op N A)) (c : ComposedNet N A) (n : String),<br>        S ops = Except.ok c → FusedAway Nm ops n → c.member n = none) ∧<br>      (∀ (ops ops' : List (Op N A)) (c : ComposedNet N A),<br>          S ops = Except.ok c →<br>            RenamesDirect ops ops' →<br>              ∃ c',<br>                S ops' = Except.ok c' ∧<br>                  c'.toBuiltNet = c.toBuiltNet ∧ c'.corrs = c.corrs) ∧<br>        ∀ (c : ComposedNet N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)), (Rb c r).member = c.member</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a triple. Nm is the naming model of places (strNaming, names as keys, for TypeScript, Rust and Python; typedNaming, name and token type, for Java), whose name function gives the name a record carries. S is a build-script function (ScriptFn, Reference/ComposeBuild.lean): a script of builder calls (declare a place, add a transition, declare a terminal place, declare a fusion set, compose an instance with explicit bindings or by auto-binding, compose a subnet definition directly) folded over a new builder, then build(), giving the composed net or a rejection. A composed net is core's built net (places, transitions, terminal places), the MOD-031 correspondences and the membership map, a function from node name to an optional subnet name (none: no entry): Rust PetriNet::subnet_membership, Java subnetMembership(), TypeScript subnetMembership, Python Net.subnet_membership. Rb is an action-binding function on composed nets. The witnesses are buildScript (for every naming model, token type map, transition check and channel merge) and composedRebind, core's refBind with the map carried along.
- Line 1 is rule 1, the recording sentences and the sentence that the mapping is the resolution: the records are read off the script (scriptRecords), the resolution is MOD_026_resolve's rule written as MemberOf. All three runtimes record exactly a direct composition's body places and body transitions under the definition's name with each / replaced by _ (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:586-604, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:638-648, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:393-405), and only after every check of the call passed. A body place the builder already held is recorded too, so a place the host declares and one subnet contributes maps to that subnet: host declarations record nothing (wrong models hostSkip, placesOnly and hostRecords). Instance composition by compose and compose_auto records nothing (rule 4, MOD-020 and MOD-024 as reworded under ruling D20; wrong model instanceRecords). That a compose(SubnetDef) call which fails records nothing (rule 1's last sentence) is not a line: in the model a failed call fails the whole script, so a host that catches the rejection and goes on with the builder (Java and TypeScript throw, Rust compose_direct panics) is outside the model. All three runtimes run every check of the call before the first record (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:539-604, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:578-648, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:352-405); that part is checked by reading the cited code.
- Places and transitions share one mapping keyed by name, in the model and in all three runtimes. A place and a transition of one name would share an entry; the shared unique-names assumption (rulings D10 and D23; no builder checks names) rules that net out, and the lines need no premise for it because they speak of names, as the runtimes do. That a transition is never recorded by two subnets is MOD-025's transition-name rejection, not a line here.
- Line 2 is the fusion sentence. A name is fused away when it is the name of a member place of a declared fusion set other than the set's first member (FusionSet.canonical, ruling D54), compared as a place, not as a position in the list of members. The runtimes drop entries by the names of the non-canonical members (the membership filter of build_with_fusion, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:967-980; filterFusedMembership in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java and typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts), so a transition with the name of a removed place loses its entry too; line 2 is stated by name for that reason. Overlapping fusion sets fail the build (MOD-061), so on a built net each member lies in one set. A set may list its first member again (members [a, b, a]): every runtime skips a later member equal to the canonical member when it collects the removed names (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:907-914, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:1141-1147, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:817-825), so the canonical member keeps its entry, as lines 1 and 2 (mod026_dupCanonical_kept), AC5 and the sentence that the surviving canonical place keeps its own entry say.
- Line 3 is the sentence that the mapping is observability-only. Every runtime reads a subnet definition's name only to record it (and to name it in rejection messages, which the line does not compare), so renaming the definitions changes the mapping freely (two definitions renamed to one name merge their entries, one name split into two splits them) while the built net and the MOD-031 correspondences stay the same, compared as lists. The renaming is per call: one renaming function for every call can merge two definition names but never split one, so that reading would accept a build that rejects a place shared by two definitions of different names, which AC1 and AC2 need to build (mod026_mutant_uniformRename_killed). Execution, marking and the properties of MOD-023 read the built net (places, transitions, terminal places) and the correspondences, never the mapping, in the model, whose executors take only the built net; for the runtimes this part of the sentence (it does not affect execution or marking) rests on that modelling argument, not on a line. That the verifier reads none of it is MOD-050's line. That the mapping is immutable is a property of the value (Java unmodifiableMap, TypeScript ReadonlyMap, Rust no mutator), tested, not proven; in the model the map is a field of an immutable value.
- Line 4 is the action-binding sentence: Rust bind_actions_with_resolver through map_transitions (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:165-202), Java bindActions (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:216-229) and TypeScript bindActionsWithResolver (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:93-107) pass the map through. What binding does to the transitions is CORE-042's block; composedRebind does it with core's refBind.
- Priority SHOULD with shall sentences, in the form ruling D22 gives the SHOULD requirements of VER: recording the mapping is optional, and an implementation that records it follows the lines. All three runtimes record the mapping, so the lines bind every implementation. The opening sentence (cluster-aware export relies on the mapping), the clause that a shared place renders outside any cluster, the purpose clause that the mapping names only nodes that still exist, and rule 4's sentence on subnetOf are motivation and the export side, stated by MOD-040 and EXP-016, not lines of this block.
- AC1 (a private node of A maps to A) is line 1 with MOD_026_nonvacuous (composing s/one and two directly, a and t1 map to s_one, b and t2 to two). AC2 (a place named in both subnets whose recorded names differ is absent) is line 1 with the resolution's line 2 (pipe has no entry in MOD_026_nonvacuous); two definitions with one recorded name are one subnet, so their shared place maps to that name (mod026_sameName_shared), and line 3 makes the AC2 build succeed whenever the build with one name does. AC3 (a flat or instance-composed net has an empty mapping) is mod026_noDirect, for every model, with a flat net and an instance-composed net in MOD_026_nonvacuous. AC4 (opposite orders give equal mappings) is mod026_perm, for every model: two scripts that are reorderings of each other and both build have equal mappings; MOD_026_nonvacuous decides both orders. AC5 (fusing away a non-canonical place removes its entry, the canonical place keeps its own) is lines 2 and 1, with the fusion of a into b in MOD_026_nonvacuous. AC6 (a name with / is recorded with / replaced) is line 1 through slashFree and mod026_slashFree (no entry of any model contains /), with s/one recorded as s_one in MOD_026_nonvacuous.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_026_resolve"></a>
## MOD-026: Subnet-Membership Metadata for Direct Composition (resolution of the recorded contributions)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_026_resolve` · Kind **F** · Scope the resolution of the subnet contributions recorded by direct composition into the membership mapping (Java, TypeScript, Rust, Python) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f8bec762e8af2ade ai** · Statement hash `f8bec762e8af2ade`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a node name is recorded as contributed by exactly one subnet, the resolution of the recorded contributions *shall* map that node name to that subnet.<br><br>*If* a node name is recorded as contributed by two or more different subnets, *then* the resolution *shall* have no entry for that node name.<br><br>*If* a node name is recorded as contributed by no subnet, *then* the resolution *shall* have no entry for that node name. | 1. For every resolution function res, which maps a list c of records (node name, subnet name) and a node name n to an optional subnet name:<br>2. if (n, s) is a record of c and every record of c for n names s, res c n is s;<br>3. if (n, s₁) and (n, s₂) are records of c and s₁ differs from s₂, res c n is absent;<br>4. if c has no record for n, res c n is absent. | <pre>fun res ↦<br>  (∀ (c : List (String × String)) (n s : String),<br>      (n, s) ∈ c → (∀ (s' : String), (n, s') ∈ c → s' = s) → res c n = some s) ∧<br>    (∀ (c : List (String × String)) (n s₁ s₂ : String),<br>        (n, s₁) ∈ c → (n, s₂) ∈ c → s₁ ≠ s₂ → res c n = none) ∧<br>      ∀ (c : List (String × String)) (n : String),<br>        (∀ (s : String), (n, s) ∉ c) → res c n = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the resolution step of build(): Rust resolve_subnet_membership (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:810-821), Java Builder.resolveSubnetMembership (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:1078-1090) and TypeScript resolveSubnetMembership (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:757-765), Python through Rust. Each keeps a set of subnet names per node name and keeps a node exactly when its set has one element; the model takes the records as a list, so a subnet recorded twice for one node (possible only for a place, since MOD-025 rejects a second transition of one name) counts once, as it does in the sets. The witness is memberOf (Reference/ComposeBuild.lean), the function the reference build script uses.
- Node names are strings and subnets are told apart by their recorded names (MOD-026 rule 1, reworded under ruling D20): two subnet definitions whose recorded names coincide are one subnet here, in the model and in the runtimes. Which records a build makes, and that the built net's mapping is this resolution minus the names fusion removed, is the builder block MOD_026. The three lines fix the resolution (mod026_resolve_unique: every model is memberOf), and the builder's line 1 is exactly the statement that, off the fused-away names, the map of a built net is this resolution applied to the build's records (mod026_line1_iff_resolve, for every model of this block).
- The three lines determine res c n from the set of records of c alone, so for every model the resolution does not depend on the order of the records or on repeated records (mod026_resolve_congr): the order-independence of AC4 at the level of the resolution.

For example, with the records `(pipe, A)`, `(pipe, B)` and `(a, A)`, the node `a` resolves to `A`, and `pipe` and `z` resolve to nothing.

**Assumptions**

- Model scope. A build script is one implementation's net builder driven through its calls and then built, read as a function from the list of calls to the net or a rejection (ScriptFn, Reference/ComposeBuild.lean); a panic or exception at a call or at build() is a rejection. The runtimes record retired ports in compose and check them in build(): Rust PetriNetBuilder (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs, recording at :1109-1130, build at :678-700, the check reject_bound_port_references at :711-731), Java PetriNet.Builder (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java, recording at :721-731, build at :1000-1006, checkRetiredPorts at :1016-1038, after fusion at :1186), TypeScript PetriNetBuilder (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts, recording at :586-592, build at :732-739, rejectBoundPortReferences at :932-950, after fusion at :834). Python builds its Net through the Rust builder, so the Rust panic surfaces as StructureError, as the implementation notes say. tyOf is the token type MOD-022 checks at compose (a constant where no type is kept). The witness is the reference script buildScript; mod027_ref shows the block for every naming, token-type check, transition-builder check and channel merge (MOD-021). A script ends at its first rejected call. A caller that catches a failed compose and goes on with the same builder is out of scope: Rust consumes the builder (compose takes self by value, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:374) and Python makes it unusable (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs, PyPetriNetBuilder::take_builder), while Java (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:729-734, :894-895) and TypeScript (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:591, :645-646) may keep the retired-port records and merged transitions of the failed call. So a retired place is one that a composition the script completed bound.
- What is retired. RetiresPort is the paragraph 'The builder MUST remember every port place a composition retired this way' and the sentence after it: a binding of an explicit compose call, or of MOD-024's auto-bound form (every declared port bound to its own unrenamed body place, which always differs from the renamed place, pre_ne_self), whose caller place differs from the port's renamed place under the implementation's Place equality (CORE-002: the place type N, by name in Rust, TypeScript and Python, by name and token type in Java). A port bound to its own renamed place, a port that is not bound, a place that direct composition (MOD-025) merges by name, a body place that MOD-024's inference merges and a fusion member (MOD-061) are no retirements. What the builder remembers is not observable through a build script; the lines state what build() does with it, and the reference keeps exactly these records, the first one per place first (mod027Inv).
- Ruling D35 (a): what a composition does when it binds one renamed place to two different caller places is not defined. Rust keeps the binding that comes last in the iteration order of its std HashMap of bindings, whose hasher is seeded at random (RandomState; rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:377, :1050-1068), and retires the renamed place only when the binding it kept is to another place (:1113-1124). So the same calls may build in one run and fail in the next: a subnet whose ports in1 and in2 both expose IN, composed as answer with in1 bound to answer/IN and in2 to A_IN, then a host transition resetting answer/IN, builds when answer/IN wins and fails with the MOD-027 message when A_IN wins, so the same script with one more place declared, or one more transition that names no retired place, may fail where the script without it built. Java and TypeScript fill their binding maps differently (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:718, :720-731, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:549, :587-592). A build script is then not a function of its calls, so every line leaves such scripts out (OneCallerPerPort): lines 1 to 4 ask it of the script without the inserted call, which the inserted transition or place does not change, and line 5 of the compose call and of the calls around it. OneCallerPerPort also leaves out one port bound twice to two places, which the Map-based binding APIs cannot express and MOD-020 rejects. With two ports bound to one caller place, the message may name either port: Java the first in interface order (putIfAbsent over iface.ports(), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:722-731), Rust and TypeScript the one their map from renamed place to port name keeps (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1103-1107, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:578-579). So line 2 names some binding by which the first retiring call retired the place.
- Line 1 and the built net. The second half of line 1 reads the calls: a transition added by a call of the script (Op.trans) is in every builder after it, since in the reference and in Rust a call only appends (step_prefix), so after fusion it is a transition of the net build() checks; a builder that dropped it, or rewrote its arc onto the caller place, and built would break line 1. The first half reads the built net, and covers the transitions a composition added. Ruling D42 (m): the caller-side definition of a channel binding is not already in the builder and has no arc on a port bound in the same call (MOD-021). Rust rewrites such a caller arc through the binding and builds, Java and TypeScript keep it and fail at build() (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1188, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:881-882, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:634); the caller-side definition is part of the compose call, not an added transition, so both meet line 1, and the difference is MOD-021's. A caller-side transition already added stays beside the merged one in Rust (transition() appends, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:319-338); Java and TypeScript replace it by the merge (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:894-895, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:645-646), which is built from the caller side as given, with the union of the arcs and And(caller, instance) as output, so it names every place the replaced transition named, and the second half of line 1 holds in all three. Transition names are unique where a name keys something (rulings D10 and D23).
- What a transition names. namedPlaces holds the input, inhibitor, read and reset places and the places of every branch of the output specification, XOR branches included (outPlaces). The source of a forward output is not among them, but IO-014 requires every forward source to be an input place of the transition (WellFormedOut), so the input arc names it and the transition builder's check rejects a forward from a place with no input arc.
- Messages (skeptic correction S3 of the composition design). Line 2 states the message of a sole offender only. Rust and Java run the EXEC-042 terminal check before the retired check (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:693-698, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:1003-1004), TypeScript runs it after (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:735-739), and with several retired places named the runtimes report different ones (Rust sorts the output places, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:718-719). So line 2 asks that the rest of the net builds and that the transition after fusion consume from or read no terminal place and name exactly one retired place; which offender a failure names otherwise is not fixed. The message text is the same in the three runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:725-729, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:1032-1036, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:937-942) and the markdown; names are printed through the naming Nm. 'When two compositions retire the same place, the first record is kept' is line 2's first retiring call: every runtime records a place once (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:1126-1129, Java putIfAbsent, TypeScript a has-check before set).
- Order and fusion. The check runs at build(), so line 1 holds for every script, whatever the order of the arc and the compose call, and lines 2 to 5 insert the transition, the place or the compose call at any position after which only blind calls follow, which covers 'before or after the compose(...) call'. An auto-composition reads the builder's places (MOD-024's inference is order-sensitive by design) and a direct composition reads its transition names and places (MOD-025), so a call inserted before one of them may change what that call does; those positions are outside lines 2 to 5. For an auto-bound composition the message of line 2 is therefore claimed only for a transition added after it, while the failure of line 1 holds in either order. A transition after fusion is d rewritten by fuseDef under the substitution of the declared sets (MOD-061 line 1); without a fusion set it is d itself (fuseDef_id). Lines 2 and 3 take the declared fusion sets pairwise disjoint and the inserted transition fused without an input-arc collision (fuseDef succeeds), as the sentences say; a builder whose net builds has disjoint sets in every runtime (Rust build() panics on an overlap, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:673). That the check sees the net after fusion is line 1 on the fused transitions and line 3 on a transition whose arc fusion moved off the retired place.
- The rule rejects nothing else. Lines 3, 4 and 5 are frame lines, stated more generally than the markdown, whose matching sentences are 'A net that merely declares the retired place, without any arc naming it, is not rejected by this rule' and AC4 to AC7: no other build-time rejection of such a transition, place or compose call is allowed. This is an intended addition. It matches the runtimes: Rust build() rejects only a fusion overlap, a terminal clash and a retired reference (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:673-700). Line 5 says that a retirement by itself rejects nothing: the twin of a compose call adds the same transitions and places and retires nothing, so the two builders differ only in the records. Whether a net without retired places builds is the business of other blocks (CORE-040, EXEC-042, MOD-020, MOD-022, MOD-025, MOD-061); line 5 ties the net with the retirement to it. Its hypotheses are MOD-020's acceptance conditions without channel bindings, the transition builder's check on the rewritten transitions coming from the twin's direct composition, which runs it.
- Per builder. 'A retired place is recorded per builder' and 'The record is not carried on the built net' hold by construction: a ComposedNet has no field for retired ports, and the script of a new builder that re-declares a built net (MOD-023) holds no compose call, so it retires nothing.
- Acceptance criteria. AC1 is line 2 with the transition added last, and line 1; MOD_027_nonvacuous shows it (answer composed with in bound to A_IN, then hub_kill resetting answer/IN, fails with the message). AC2 is line 2 with the transition added before the compose call (a compose call is blind) and the second example. AC3 is lines 1 and 2, since namedPlaces holds every arc place and every place of the output specification; the examples show a read arc and an XOR branch on answer/IN failing with the message. AC4 is line 3 with the example in which hub_kill resets A_IN and the net builds (that the instance's transition now takes from A_IN is MOD-020's rewrite); the base script, answer composed with in bound to A_IN, builds by line 5 wherever its twin builds. AC5 and AC6 are line 3, since a port bound to its own renamed place and a port that is not bound are no retirements; the examples show both. AC7 is line 3 for its first half (after fusion the transition names the canonical member X, which is not retired; its base builds by line 5 as in AC4) and line 1 for its second half (after fusion the arc on the other member names the retired canonical member), with both outcomes on the reference. The test derivation is AC1, AC2 and AC4.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_027_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_027): ✓ The reference build script satisfies MOD-027 for every naming, every token-type check and every transition-builder check. Compose the instance `answer` with its port `in` bound to the caller place `A_IN`. A host transition that names `answer/IN`, added before or after the compose call, makes `build()` fail with the message that points at `A_IN`; one that names `A_IN` instead builds; declaring `answer/IN` without naming it builds; and the compose call builds wherever the same instance transitions, composed directly with their arcs already on `A_IN`, build.

## MOD-030: Action Binding Per Instance (share-by-default, override via bindActions)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_030` · Kind **F** · Scope every per-instance action binding (Instance.bindActions in Java, TypeScript and Rust; Python's Instance.bind_actions rides on the Rust binding) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ea726ec7985c3c23 ai** · Statement hash `ea726ec7985c3c23`

**Assumptions**

- A per-instance binding is a function from a module instance (Instance: prefix, renamed places, renamed transition definitions in order, port and channel handles, interface; Spec/GlossaryCompose.lean) and an override mapping to a derived instance or a rejection (InstBindFn). The mapping is a list of (original name, action) pairs, read through ovr: a key's action is its first entry's, and a runtime map holds one entry per key. An action is read as its identity tag (Act: the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id), so 'shared by reference, not by copy' and 'the same action object' are 'the same tag'; what an action does when the net fires is CORE-050's. The block is stated over every Instance record, which is stronger than 'a module instance': it also covers records no instantiate call makes (a transition name not of the form p/x, places that do not match the definitions). Both models bind every record the same way, so the stronger scope excludes no runtime behaviour on instances made by instantiate (MOD-010) whose transition names are distinct. An instantiated body can hold two transitions of one name, since no builder and no instantiation checks transition names (ruling D23 assumes them distinct and requires no check; refInst does not check either); such an instance is outside the shared unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23, and the block still states it. On such an instance every runtime keeps the own action of a transition the mapping does not name: the resolver defers it (none, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:187-202; null, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:220-226 and typescript/src/core/instance.ts:155-157), and the net's resolver binding keeps a deferred transition as it is. MOD_030_forbids_firstOfName kills a binding that gives such a transition the action of the first transition of its name, the behaviour RD-41 recorded. Line 2 compares the places as a list, so their order and multiplicity are kept too; every runtime keeps the receiver's place collection as it is.
- Ruling D87 (a): a key that names no transition of the instance is out of scope. Rust and Python ignore it (rust/libpetri-core/src/instance.rs:188-221 translates every key to p/k and binds through the resolver form, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:187-202, which asks only for the names of the body's transitions; rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:667-680), Java and TypeScript reject the call (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:207-214, typescript/src/core/instance.ts:137-148). Line 1 is therefore stated for mappings whose every key names a transition, and lines 2 to 4 for calls that return; the reference refBindInst (Rust) and strictBindInst (Java, TypeScript) both satisfy the block and differ on such a key (MOD_030_unknownKey_undecided). The quoted sentence that leaves the case unspecified records the ruling. Java checks the keys against the definition's body and TypeScript against the renamed body; for an instance made by instantiate these are the same set (MOD-010 line 3).
- All three runtimes bind an instance through the resolver form of CORE-042, the transition the call does not name being deferred (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:187-202, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:220-226, typescript/src/core/instance.ts:155-157), so CORE-042's map-form divergence (Java and TypeScript give an omitted transition passthrough) does not reach per-instance binding; a binding that does is killed by line 4 (MOD_030_mutant_clobber_killed).
- Line 2 is what 'a derived instance whose specified transitions carry the supplied actions instead' leaves unchanged. All three runtimes keep the prefix, the definition, the port and channel handles and the parameters (rust/libpetri-core/src/instance.rs:211-220, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:228; TypeScript rebuilds its channel handles against the rebound body by name, typescript/src/core/instance.ts:169-190, which the model's name-valued handles read as unchanged) and rebuild a rebound transition through the transition builder, keeping its name, arcs, output specification, timing and priority (CORE-042 line 1) and its declared-to-actual correspondence (MOD-031: 'Binding or rebinding a transition's action ([CORE-042], [MOD-030]) MUST preserve this correspondence', rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:614-643). A binding that rebuilds and drops the correspondence violates line 2 (MOD_030_mutant_dropCorr_killed). The parameters value is not modelled (MOD-010 AC4). By line 2 binding never changes how a transition fires (mod030_toTrans).
- AC1 (by default two instances of one subnet definition reference the same action object per transition) is MOD-010's line 3 (instantiation keeps every action), not a line here: mod030_shared derives, for every model of MOD-010, that two instances of one definition carry the same actions position by position. Their per-instance override is AC2 and the test derivation: MOD_030_nonvacuous binds produce on p1 and leaves p2 with the default.
- AC2 (bindActions({"produce": newAction}) gives an instance whose produce transition uses newAction, the original unchanged) is lines 1 and 3; 'the original instance is unchanged' holds of every binding in the model, a function on immutable values, and is tested in the runtimes, not proven. A binding that never accepts meets lines 2 to 4 and violates line 1 (MOD_030_mutant_noAcceptance_killed).
- AC3 (the override map keys use original, un-prefixed transition names) is line 3's reading of a key k as the transition p/k: a binding that looks a key up as the transition's full name binds nothing under the original names and violates line 3 (MOD_030_forbids_prefixedKeys).
- AC4 (transitions not named in the override map retain their shared default action) and AC7 (a call that overrides t leaves the action of every u != t exactly as inherited from the receiver) are line 4: the receiver's action, which is the shared default unless an earlier call rebound it.
- AC5 (the override is purely structural, established before the subnet is composed and fixed for the lifetime of the resulting net) is not a line: binding is a function on instance values with no runtime state, and a composed net is an immutable value whose transitions carry the actions of the instances composed into it (MOD-020, MOD-021); tested, not proven.
- AC6 (successive calls compose as last-wins replacement; A is not invoked for t) follows from lines 2 and 3 for every model of the block (mod030_lastWins): after two calls the transition carries the second call's action. That A is not invoked at run time is that line with CORE-050 (a firing runs the transition's bound action). A binding that keeps an earlier override (first wins) violates line 3 (MOD_030_mutant_firstWins_killed). A sequential composition of A and B is not expressible over identity tags and is excluded by line 3, which gives the transition exactly the supplied tag.
- AC8 (bindActions is non-mutating; the receiver stays usable for independent derivations) and the body's 'MUST NOT mutate the receiver' hold of every binding in the model, a function on values, and are tested in the runtimes, not proven. Java returns the receiver itself for an empty mapping (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Instance.java:196-198), which satisfies lines 2 to 4, the receiver being immutable. 'Overriding actions on instance A does NOT affect instance B' holds for the same reason: binding takes one instance and returns another, and MOD_030_nonvacuous shows p2 unchanged after binding p1.
- The sentence that MOD-030 extends CORE-042 into the composition layer is the reading above that per-instance binding is the resolver form of CORE-042 applied to the renamed body. Binding on a subnet definition (SubnetDef.bindActions) is MOD-051's (W11).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_031"></a>
## MOD-031: Action Place Resolution under Composition (declared → actual correspondence)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_031` · Kind **F** · Scope the declared-to-actual place correspondence of every composed transition, through rewrite passes, channel merges and action binding · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 3cc284663f97c8d1 ai** · Statement hash `3cc284663f97c8d1`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition that carries no correspondence goes through a sequence of rewrite passes (instantiation, port binding, fusion) with no channel merge among them, the resulting correspondence *shall* resolve every place that the transition's arcs and output specification named before the passes to the place that the same sequence of place maps sends it to, which is the place that the same arc or output now names, and *shall* resolve every other place to itself.<br><br>*When* a rewrite pass rewrites a transition, the places that the transition's input, inhibitor, read and reset arcs and its output specification name, and in particular its input places and its output places, *shall* be the places they named before the pass, each sent through the pass's place map, so that place-set discovery returns the actual composed places.<br><br>A transition that carries no correspondence *shall* resolve every place to itself.<br><br>*If* the two correspondences that a channel merge joins for one transition resolve one place to two different places, neither of them that place itself, *then* the merge of the two correspondences *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* the two correspondences that a channel merge joins for one transition have no such conflict, the merge of the two correspondences *shall* succeed.<br><br>*When* a merge of two correspondences succeeds, the merged correspondence *shall* resolve each place to the place the caller side resolves it to when that differs from the place itself, and otherwise to the place the instance side resolves it to.<br><br>*When* an action is bound or rebound to a transition, before or after instantiation, the transition's correspondence, arcs and output specification *shall* stay unchanged. | 1. For every set of correspondence operations O (a rewrite pass, a lookup, a channel merge, an action binding):<br>2. for every transition definition d that carries no correspondence and every sequence of passes ss (each a place map and a name map), every place p that d names resolves, through the correspondence of d after the passes, to the place the passes' place maps send p to, and every place x that d does not name resolves to x;<br>3. for every pass (place map σ, name map g) and every d, the passed definition's input places are, as a set, d's input places mapped by σ, and, each kind on its own and in order, its inhibitor places, read places, reset places and output places are d's places of that kind mapped by σ;<br>4. the lookup resolves every place to itself through no correspondence;<br>5. for every caller definition c and instance definition i: if some place x resolves, through c's and through i's correspondence, to places other than x that differ, the merge **Assumptions**

- The model (ruling D69 (a)). A correspondence is a list of (declared place, actual place) pairs, looked up first entry first; every runtime keeps it in a hash map keyed by the declared place, so a key has one entry (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs build_local_name_map, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java buildPlaceAlias). A rewrite pass is any place map: instantiation (MOD-010), port binding (MOD-020) and fusion (MOD-061), which all three runtimes run through the same rebuild (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs rebuild_with_name, which apply_fusion calls directly or through substitute_places). The lookup is the correspondence's own lookup, correspondence first and the place itself when it has no entry, as Java and TypeScript resolve (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java and typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts, resolve in each). How the context operations input, inputs, read and output use it, the Rust native context that does not resolve (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs, TransitionContext::input, the binding-hosted MAY) and the Python binding adapter, which resolves through the correspondence first (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs resolve), are line 6, the block MOD_031_ctx in this file.
- Ruling D69 (a), single-valued and not 1:1: the correspondence maps each declared place to one actual place, and two declared places may map to one actual place when two ports are bound to one caller place (MOD-020) or two places are fused (MOD-061); MOD_031_allows_shared shows the reference doing so. The body sentence that calls the correspondence 1:1 is reworded to single-valued.
- Ruling D69 (a), scope: line 1 covers transitions that no channel merge has joined, and so do the body's MUSTs on nested instantiation and on key-set completeness through every rewrite pass; for a transition that a channel merge joined no line states them. Rust, Java and TypeScript read a side of a channel merge that carries no correspondence as an identity entry for every place it names, take the union of the keys of both sides and drop the result as a whole when every entry is the identity (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs merge_local_name_maps and side_map, called from merge_transitions; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java mergeTransitions with sideAlias and mergePlaceAlias; typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts mergeTransitions with sideAlias and mergePlaceAlias). The Python binding builds its nets through the Rust rewriter. That is the reference's key-complete merge (corrMergeVia corrSideFull), with AC9's drop, so the caller's declared places stay keys and a later pass that renames one of them (fusion at build, or instantiating the retrofitted net, MOD-014) moves it. A wrong merge that keeps the instance side's correspondence whole when the caller side carries none (carriedCorrOps, the behaviour RD-23 recorded) also satisfies the block, and the two differ after one more pass (MOD_031_mergeThenPass_undecided). The block does not kill carriedCorrOps: that needs a sentence on key-set completeness for a transition a channel merge joined, which the spec does not state (ruling D69 (a)), so MOD_031_mergeThenPass_undecided stays undecided although no runtime merges that way.
- Line 1 has two halves. The first resolves every place the transition names before the passes; the second is the body's key-set MUST read from above: the chained pass does not re-derive keys from the arcs, whose names are intermediate-pass names the author never declared, so a place the transition did not name resolves to itself. A chained pass that carries the declared entries and also records each intermediate arc name behind them meets the first half and fails the second (MOD_031_mutant_lowerOnly_killed): a port-agnostic action that asks for an output place it discovered would be sent to an input place. The second half holds of the reference, of carriedCorrOps and of the pass that drops an all-identity correspondence (AC9).
- Line 2 names the places of every arc kind, not only the input and output places that discovery returns, and states each kind on its own: the relative clause of the line 1 sentence ('which is the place that the same arc or output now names') is line 1 with line 2 (mod031_resolves_to_named, through mod031_line2_namedPlaces), and the context operation read resolves through the correspondence (line 6, MOD_031_ctx). A pass that maps the input arcs and the output specification and leaves the inhibitor, read and reset arcs on their old places meets discovery and fails line 2 (MOD_031_mutant_discoveryOnly_killed). A pass that maps every place and then rebuilds each inhibitor arc as a read arc keeps the list of all named places and fails line 2, since an inhibitor turned into a read arc is an enabling condition (MOD_031_mutant_namedOnly_killed). Every runtime rebuilds each arc kind from the same kind, in order (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs rebuild_with_name). Line 2 reads the input places as a set, as the sentence's 'place-set discovery' does, because of fusion: when a fusion (MOD-061) sends two input arcs of one transition onto one place, every runtime merges them into one arc by the merge table of MOD-021 (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs apply_fusion with merge_input_arcs, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java applyFusion with mergeInputArcs, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts applyFusion with normalizeInputArcs), so the input list holds that place once where the mapped list holds it twice, and the set of input places is still the mapped set, which is what discovery returns. So line 2 holds of that merge with no premise (MOD_031_allows_mergeInputs: a pass that keeps one input arc for each place after the place map satisfies the block, and on a fusion of two input places it leaves one input arc where the mapped list holds the place twice); the merged arc, its cardinality and its position are MOD-061's lines. Read, inhibitor and reset arcs that land on one place are kept as they are (MOD-061), so those kinds and the output specification are mapped as lists, in order. The reference pass maps the input list in order (TransDef.map), which meets the set reading; a pass that drops an input place or adds one fails it (MOD_031_forbids_extraInput: a pass that adds an input arc on a fresh place). The derived consequences (mod031_resolves_to_named, mod031_lateBind, mod031ctx_inputs_after_passes) need only membership and hold with no premise. The shape of the output specification and the input cardinalities are not places: the rewrite keeps them as MOD-010 line 3 and MOD-020 line 1 state (TransDef.map).
- Line 4 states the merge rule of the body (identity carries no assertion) as resolution: an entry that resolves a place to itself, and an absent entry, are both the identity, so the line quantifies over every place and a place that neither side holds as a key is one that both sides resolve to itself. After a channel merge one correspondence serves the actions of two authors: when the caller's hand-written transition and the instance's channel transition both declare one place name for two different places, the merged correspondence resolves it as the instance side does, and no single correspondence is right for both (clash mod-c#6); the block states the body's rule and no line claims more. The merge here is the correspondence part of a channel merge: the channel merge's other rejections (timing, match specification, arc kinds, the input-arc table) are MOD-021's, so line 4's success is the success of the correspondence part. Only failure is stated, not the message (Rust panics listing every conflict sorted by declared name, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs merge_local_name_maps; Java and TypeScript throw). A merge that writes the instance side's entries last, so that an identity entry overwrites the caller's move, meets the rejection and success halves and fails the result half (MOD_031_mutant_noMergeResult_killed).
- Line 3 follows from line 1 at zero passes (mod031_line3_of_line1), so no model kills line 3 alone; it is kept as the line of AC4 and is a restatement, not an independent check. The 'directly-composed transition carries the identity correspondence' half of AC4 is direct composition adding a definition unchanged (MOD-025, not modelled here): such a definition carries no correspondence and line 3 applies.
- AC1 (instance plus port binding, then ctx.input(declaredIn) and ctx.output(declaredOut) work) is line 1 at two passes, an instantiation and a port binding; that the context operation then passes its declared-place check and answers on the actual places is line 6 (MOD_031_ctx with mod031ctx_inputs_after_passes and mod031ctx_output_after_passes); that the transition then fires and deposits is EXEC's and CORE-062's. AC2 (Out.xor(aDecl, bDecl), the action selects aDecl, exactly one token on the actual a) is line 1 on the output place aDecl; the exactly-one-production check is EXEC's, and that output(aDecl, v) writes on the actual a is line 6 (mod031ctx_output_after_passes). AC3 (nested instantiation resolves to outer/inner/x) is line 1 at three passes; MOD_031_nonvacuous resolves the declared y to b/a/y; that the action's calls answer there is line 6 (mod031ctx_after_passes). AC5's first half (discovery returns the actual composed places) is line 2; its second half (port-agnostic actions written against discovery continue to work) is a claim about running actions and is line 6: a call on a discovered place that the correspondence resolves to itself answers for that place (mod031ctx_fixed), and a discovered place that is also a declared place the correspondence moved is resolved too (mod031ctx_collision).
- AC6 (structural equivalence per MOD-023: place index, transition count, arc topology, bitmap masks, timing arrays, without the correspondence) and the sentence that the correspondence is not consulted by enablement, firing, the verifier, the exporter or the event subsystem are MOD-050's line (wave W8) and MOD-023's: the firing view TransDef.toTrans and the structure read none of corr. 'Purely structural, fixed for the lifetime of the composed net' holds of the model's immutable values.
- AC7 (an action bound after instantiation resolves as a baked-in action does) is line 5; mod031_lateBind derives, for every model of the block, that after a late bind every declared place resolves where the passes sent it and that place is still named by the transition's arcs or output specification. Line 5 keeps the arcs and the output specification as CORE-042's line 1 does on built nets. Rust rebuild_with_action carries local_name_map forward (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs rebuild_with_action), and Java and TypeScript rebuildWithAction carry placeAlias (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts rebuildWithAction). What the binding does to the action is CORE-042's and MOD-030's; that the late-bound action's calls answer on the places the passes sent its declared places to is line 6 (mod031ctx_lateBind). A binding that keeps the correspondence and drops the read arcs fails line 5 (MOD_031_mutant_corrOnlyRebind_killed).
- AC8 (identity round-trip across three passes) is line 1 at three passes: MOD_031_nonvacuous binds the port x to a caller place of its own name while y is prefixed, then instantiates again and resolves both; a pass that drops identity entries one by one violates it (MOD_031_forbids_entryDrop). The third pass is the instantiation of the retrofitted net (MOD-014). That the failure would be consume-then-throw, so the tokens are lost (EXEC-031), is the reason for the requirement, not a line.
- AC9 (an implementation that drops an all-identity correspondence wholesale still satisfies AC8) is MOD_031_allows_dropAllIdentity: the pass that drops it, as Rust, Java and TypeScript do (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs wholesale_drop_if_all_identity, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java compactIdentityAlias, typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts dropIfAllIdentity), satisfies the block. The reference pass does not take this MAY.
- AC10 (identity never conflicts on merge) is line 4: X to X against X to Y succeeds and yields X to Y, two differing non-identity mappings fail (MOD_031_nonvacuous); a merge that rejects any two differing entries is the mutant MOD_031_mutant_anyDifference.
- AC11 (the identity test agrees with the lookup) holds by construction: the identity test and the lookup both use the equality of the place type N. Under name-only places (TypeScript, Rust, Python: N = String, strNaming) X to X is the identity whatever the token types; under places by name and token type (Java: N = String × Ty, typedNaming) a mapping from X of one token type to X of another is a retained entry. This is the MOD-024 divergence, carried by CORE-002.
