## MOD-040: Export Grouping (subgraph cluster_* per instance prefix)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_040` · Kind **F** · Scope the subnetOf accessor of every built net, and the instance-prefix helper · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 4d2b7ff86e4cf6fc ai** · Statement hash `4d2b7ff86e4cf6fc`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| For `subnetOf` and the instance-prefix helper, the SHOULD priority is whether an implementation offers them at all; an implementation that offers them answers as the next six sentences say.<br><br>In the four sentences on `subnetOf` that follow, a `/`-prefix of a name is a non-empty beginning of the name that is immediately followed by a `/`, and a `/`-prefix `P` heads a transition of the net when the name of some transition of the net begins with `P/`.<br><br>*If* `name` is neither a place nor a transition of the net, *then* `subnetOf(name)` *shall* be absent.<br><br>*When* `name` is a place or a transition of the net and the net's membership mapping ([MOD-026]) has an entry for `name`, `subnetOf(name)` *shall* return that entry.<br><br>*When* `name` is a place or a transition of the net with no membership entry and some `/`-prefix of `name` heads a transition of the net, `subnetOf(name)` *shall* return the longest such `/`-prefix.<br><br>*When* `name` is a place or a transition of the net with no membership entry and no `/`-prefix of `name` heads a transition of the net, `subnetOf(name)` *shall* be absent.<br><br>The instance-prefix helper (`instancePrefixOf`) *shall* return the part of a name before its last `/` when that part is not empty, and be absent otherwise. | 1. For the pair M of an accessor M.subnetOf and an instance-prefix helper M.prefixOf, with a net X given by its place names, its transition names and its membership mapping X.member, a name n of X a node when it is one of those place or transition names, and a /-prefix P heading a transition of X (X.Heads P) when IsSlashPrefix P t for some transition name t of X (P is not empty and t begins with P followed by /):<br>2. a name that is no node of X is absent;<br>3. a node with a membership entry s gets s;<br>4. a node without a membership entry, and a /-prefix P of it that heads a transition of X and is at least as long as every /-prefix of it that heads a transition of X, gets P;<br>5. a node without a membership entry none of whose /-prefixes heads a transition of X is absent;<br>6. the helper gives q for n exactly when q is not empty and n is q, a /, and a rest without / (the part before the last /). | <pre>fun M ↦<br>  (∀ (X : SubnetNet) (n : String), ¬X.IsNode n → M.subnetOf X n = none) ∧<br>    (∀ (X : SubnetNet) (n s : String),<br>        X.IsNode n → X.member n = some s → M.subnetOf X n = some s) ∧<br>      (∀ (X : SubnetNet) (n P : String),<br>          X.IsNode n →<br>            X.member n = none →<br>              IsSlashPrefix P n →<br>                X.Heads P →<br>                  (∀ (Q : String),<br>                      IsSlashPrefix Q n → X.Heads Q → Q.toList.length ≤ P.toList.length) →<br>                    M.subnetOf X n = some P) ∧<br>        (∀ (X : SubnetNet) (n : String),<br>            X.IsNode n →<br>              X.member n = none →<br>                (∀ (P : String), IsSlashPrefix P n → ¬X.Heads P) →<br>                  M.subnetOf X n = none) ∧<br>          ∀ (n q : String),<br>            M.prefixOf n = some q ↔<br>              q.toList ≠ [] ∧ ∃ r, n.toList = q.toList ++ '/' :: r ∧ '/' ∉ r</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a pair: the accessor subnetOf over the names of a net (SubnetNet: place names, transition names, the MOD-026 membership mapping as a function, none for no entry) and the instance-prefix helper. Names are strings read as their characters (String.toList), as in the export glossary (IsSlashPrefix, instancePrefix, cutsAux in Spec/GlossaryExportCluster.lean), so the cluster key of EXP-016 and this accessor share one notion of prefix. The accessor reads names only: Java compares place names, not (name, token type) records, and Rust and TypeScript key nodes by name.
- The SHOULD priority of subnetOf and the helper is read by the scoping sentence: it is whether an implementation offers them, not how they answer; the SHOULD sentences of the export half are slice (b). Java (PetriNet.subnetOf, SubnetPrefixes.instancePrefixOf), TypeScript (PetriNet.subnetOf, instancePrefixOf from libpetri/export) and Rust (PetriNet::subnet_of in libpetri-core petri_net.rs, instance_prefix_of in libpetri-core subnet_prefixes.rs, re-exported by libpetri_export::subnet_prefixes) offer both; Python offers Net.subnet_of, which calls the Rust accessor, and no helper. That an implementation offers them is an existence clause, not a line, and it needs no coverage clause: a model is a pair of total functions, so every model answers every name, absent being the answer none. The coverage convention of GlossaryExec.lean is for relations, where a sub-relation can drop a step; a function cannot drop an answer. Which language offers which of the two is the list above, a fact about the code bases that no Lean statement carries.
- Lines 1 to 4 are steps 1 to 4 of the rule as an accessor. Step 3 says 'the longest /-prefix of name that some transition of the net lives under' and gives its test (some transition's name begins with P/); it is not a fact about instances: when a subnet uses / for a transition of its own namespace (a transition s1/obs/tick), the place s1/obs/TURN answers s1/obs, which is no instance (mod040_ownNamespaceTransition). Line 3 states the longest qualifying prefix declaratively; the reference finds it by walking from the longest (subnetWalk), as the runtimes do. An index that keeps only the part before the last / of each transition name loses the outer prefixes of a nested transition and breaks line 3 (MOD_040_forbids_immediateIndex). The five lines fix both functions on every input: every model is the reference pair (mod040_unique).
- The sentence 'For a transition name step 3 returns its own instance prefix (the transition itself begins with it), so transitions are attributed as by the part before the last /' is mod040_transition_eq_instancePrefix, for every model: a transition without a membership entry answers its instance prefix. The phrase that subnetOf 'follows the default (AUTO) cluster rule above without its nesting, except that the prefix it falls back to is one some transition lives under' is mod040_agrees_auto: on a node whose part before the last / heads a transition, or that has none, subnetOf equals the AUTO cluster key of EXP-016; the exception is mod040_differs_from_clusterKey.
- A /-prefix is non-empty in line 3. The step-3 prose 'the prefixes of name ending before one of its / characters' also covered the empty prefix of a name that starts with /; no runtime answers it (the walks stop at position 0: Rust instance_prefix_of returns none for idx 0, Java and TypeScript loop while the position is greater than 0, and the transition-prefix sets skip position 0), so the markdown now says 'the first non-empty P'. The runtimes agree on every name, empty segments included: Rust collects a transition's prefixes by walking instance_prefix_of up (stopping early at a prefix already collected, whose own prefixes are then collected too), Java and TypeScript by scanning every / after position 0; both give the non-empty prefixes followed by /. The block needs no assumption on names (no D46 name assumption).
- Line 5 is the instance-prefix helper, the 'instance-prefix detection' bullet's prefix: Java, TypeScript and Rust return the substring before the last / and none when there is no / or the last / is at position 0 (instancePrefix_eq_some). The default (AUTO) cluster key of EXP-016 is the membership entry, else this helper (mod040_clusterKey_auto, for every model of the block), so the exporter clusters s1/obs/TURN under s1/obs while subnetOf answers s1 (mod040_differs_from_clusterKey): the sentence that subnetOf differs from the DOT AUTO cluster rule is a consequence of lines 3 and 5.
- The export half of MOD-040 is slice (b), the block MOD_040_b (MOD_040_b.lean) over the exporter of EXP-016: the opening sentence (a subgraph cluster per subnet), the membership and instance-prefix bullets, the preference and fall-back sentence, the caller-selectable cluster source (kind N), the sanitisation sentence, the label sentence and the sentence that the requirement changes no styling, junction or arc rule. EXP-016's block states the same rule for every exporter today (EXP_016, Spec/Req/EXP_016.lean), and its forbids theorem EXP_016_forbids_walkUp kills an exporter that clusters by subnetOf.
- Quality, kind Q and tested, not proven: 'The set of prefixes that head a transition SHOULD be computed once per net, lazily, so subnetOf costs O(depth of the name)' (all three runtimes build the index on the first call, Rust subnet_index OnceLock, Java volatile subnetIndex, TypeScript _nameIndex), and 'subnetOf is additive: no export output, membership mapping or event changes' together with 'The exporter's instance-prefix helper and its clustering are unchanged by this rule' (a property of a change to the code, which a statement about the accessor cannot carry).
- AC1 (two instances b1 and b2 give subgraph cluster_b1 and subgraph cluster_b2), AC2 (each cluster block holds exactly the nodes under its prefix), AC3 (nested prefixes give nested subgraphs), AC4 (no composed instance, no metadata and no / gives no cluster subgraph), AC5 (cluster IDs match cluster_[A-Za-z0-9_]+), AC6 (one cluster block per subnet of the membership metadata, a shared place at the top level) and AC7 (metadata nodes cluster by subnet name, prefix-named nodes by prefix) are the export half, slice (b), the block MOD_040_b; EXP-016 states them for every exporter too (EXP_016_nonvacuous for AC1 and AC3, EXP_016_ac2, EXP_016_ac4, EXP_016_ac5, and its first line under a membership map for AC6 and AC7).
- AC8 is decided on the reference in MOD_040_nonvacuous: a directly composed node answers its subnet name (line 2), the instance-composed node b1/inner/p answers b1/inner (line 3, the net having the transition b1/inner/t; an instance composed from a subnet with no transition has no transition under its prefix, and its nodes answer an outer prefix or are absent), and a shared rendezvous place without /, a flat node without / and a name the net does not declare are absent (lines 1, 2 and 4: a shared place has no entry, by MOD-026 rule 3, and without / it has no /-prefix). A shared place whose /-prefix heads a transition answers that prefix by line 3 (mod040_sharedPlaceUnderPrefix), which is why AC8 says 'without /'.
- On a net a MOD-026 builder produces, every membership key is a node, so line 1 is binding only in the abstract model, whose mapping may have an entry for a name that is no node; there it also rules out an accessor that looks the entry up before the node test. No runtime does: Java (PetriNet.java subnetOf, the nodes test on line 118), TypeScript (petri-net.ts line 123) and Rust (petri_net.rs line 143, index.nodes.get(name)?) test the node first. The statement is stronger than the observable contract here, not weaker.
- AC9 is decided on the reference in MOD_040_nonvacuous: with a transition s1/t the place s1/obs/TURN answers s1 (line 3, walking up past s1/obs to a prefix some transition lives under), x/y with no transition under x/ is absent (line 4), with a transition outer/inner/t the place outer/inner/p answers outer/inner, and a membership entry wins over each (line 2). Its last sentence, that the DOT export of the same nets is byte-identical to before, is the export half (slice (b), the block MOD_040_b) and kind Q for the bytes.
- The test derivation (a composed net with two instances, and a directly composed net of two subnets, exported and checked for cluster blocks) is the export half, slice (b), the block MOD_040_b.

## MOD-040: Export Grouping (subgraph cluster_* per instance prefix): the export half

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_040_b` · Kind **F** · Scope every exporter that draws cluster subgraphs, the clusters of the exported graph of a composed net · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 e97ee6b07645e9c5 ai** · Statement hash `e97ee6b07645e9c5`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| DOT export per [EXP-001] of a composed net SHOULD emit a `subgraph cluster_&lt;sanitizedKey>` block grouping the nodes of each subnet.<br><br>The sanitization function applied to the key MUST match the existing DOT ID sanitization per [EXP-014] (non-`[A-Za-z0-9_]` characters, including `/`, replaced by `_`).<br><br>This requirement does NOT change the styling, junction, or arc-rendering rules of EXP-002..EXP-015; it only adds grouping structure.<br><br>For the export half of this requirement (the sentences on DOT export: the opening sentence and its two bullets, the preference and cluster-source sentences, the sanitization and label sentences and the sentence on EXP-002..EXP-015), the SHOULD priority is whether an exporter draws cluster subgraphs at all; an exporter that draws them reads every MAY, SHOULD and MUST sentence of the export half as *shall*, lets the caller select the metadata-only, prefix-only and no-clustering sources, uses the default source when the caller selects none, takes the cluster key of a node and the covered nets as [EXP-016] defines them, and follows the next three sentences, which restate shall sentences of [EXP-016].<br><br>The exporter *shall* make each node that has a cluster key a direct member of the cluster of that key and of no other cluster, make a node without a cluster key a member of no cluster, and list as a member of a cluster only a node it draws.<br><br>The exporter *shall* draw exactly one cluster for each cluster key of a drawn node and for each `/`-prefix of such a key and no other cluster, nest each cluster directly in the cluster whose key is the part of its own key before the last `/` and draw a cluster whose key has no `/` at the top level, and give the cluster of key K the ID `cluster_` followed by K sanitized per [EXP-014] and the label K.<br><br>The exporter *shall* draw, in any order, the same nodes, and the same edges other than the ghost edges of [EXP-017], as it draws for the same net and configuration under no clustering. | 1. **Assumptions**

- The model is an exporter E : Exporter (Spec/GlossaryExport.lean), the typed graph a configuration and a net are drawn as, before DOT text, and the words are EXP-016's (nodeKey, clusterKey, instancePrefix, IsSlashPrefix, clusterId, ExportNet.ClusterNames). A composed net reaches the exporter as its names and its MOD-026 membership map, so the block quantifies over every net and membership map the exporter can see, as EXP-016 does: which names composition builds is MOD-010 and MOD-013, and which membership map it records is MOD-026, on the composition model. Which subgraph block an edge is written in, cluster styling and the order of sibling clusters are properties of the DOT text, not stated (ruling R2 (exp-b)).
- Ruling D26 (a) item 7: one statement of the clustering rule. The scoping sentence names the sentences of the export half and reads its SHOULD, MAY and MUST sentences as an exporter that clusters shall, as EXP-016's scoping sentence does: the opening sentence (a cluster block per subnet), the membership bullet, the instance-prefix bullet with its nesting clause, the preference and fall-back sentence, the caller-selectable cluster source with its default, the sanitisation sentence, the label sentence and the sentence that the requirement changes no styling, junction or arc rule are the seven lines through EXP-016's definition of the cluster key (clusterKey under cfg.cluster). That the caller may select the metadata-only, prefix-only and no-clustering sources is the shape of the model: an exporter is a total function of the configuration, so it accepts every cluster source, and the statement quantifies over all four; an exporter that ignores the caller's choice fails the first and third lines (MOD_040_b_forbids_fixedSource draws the default clusters under no clustering). All three runtimes offer the four sources. The opening sentence asks for a cluster block 'grouping the nodes of each subnet'; it is weaker than the third line and shaped differently (the third line draws a cluster for s1/obs, which is no subnet, and none for a subnet of the membership map with no drawn node), and the scoping sentence ties it to the next three sentences, which the lines state. The phrase 'the exporter still clusters s1/obs/TURN under s1/obs' is the first line with the key rule (mod040b_walkNet on the reference; MOD_040_b_forbids_walkUp kills an exporter that clusters by subnetOf), and the bridge to slice (a) is mod040b_inside_subnetOf.
- The seventh line reads the ghost edges of EXP-017 as the edges of arc type ghost (the glossary's ArcType.ghost), as EXP-016 does, so it sets aside every ghost edge, also one EXP-017 does not ask for: an exporter whose ghost-edge loop lacks the check that the two clusters differ draws a ghost edge from cluster_left to itself and still meets this block, and drawing no ghost edge other than those EXP-017 asks for is EXP-017's obligation (EXP_017_forbids_sameCluster kills that exporter). Likewise a rule of EXP-002..EXP-015 that holds of the whole drawing rather than of its nodes and edges, such as the direction of EXP-007, is that block's obligation: a drawing that turns top to bottom once it has clusters meets the seven lines and fails EXP_007_config.
- MOD_040_b_of_EXP_016: every exporter meeting EXP-016 meets this block, so the consistency theorem gets the block from EXP_016. The converse fails only by the at-most-once half of EXP-016's second line (no cluster lists a member twice, on a net with distinct transition names), which MOD-040's sentences do not state; it is EXP-016's obligation, not repeated here.
- Ruling D46 (a) with (x), kind A: the block covers the nets of EXP-016's name assumption (ExportNet.ClusterNames); on other nets the clustering is implementation-defined. On a cluster key with an empty /-segment every exporter registers the glossary's keyChain and draws the clusters the reference draws, without a panic or an exception (register_prefix_chain in Rust, registerPrefixChain in Java and TypeScript); such keys stay outside the block only because EXP-016's name assumption still leaves them out, following the scope sentence of EXP-016. A non-ASCII membership key gets a Unicode cluster ID in Rust (implementation-defined under ruling D46 (a)), and the runtimes look a node's key up by its DOT ID, so two names that sanitize to one ID become one node (a known limit of EXP-016); all three cases are outside the block, as they are outside EXP-016.
- Quality, kind Q: the sentence of slice (a) that the exporter's instance-prefix helper and its clustering are unchanged by the subnetOf rule, and the last sentence of AC9 (the DOT export of the same nets is byte-identical to before), are properties of a change to the code and of DOT bytes, tested, not stated.
- AC1 (instances b1 and b2 give subgraph cluster_b1 and subgraph cluster_b2) and AC3 (nested prefixes give nested subgraphs) are decided on the reference in MOD_040_b_nonvacuous and follow from the third, fifth and sixth lines for every exporter meeting the block. AC2 (each cluster block contains, directly or through the cluster blocks nested in it, exactly the places and transitions whose cluster key is the cluster's key or begins with it followed by /, and the junction nodes of those transitions) is mod040b_ac2; it is worded as EXP-016's AC2, which ruling D26 item 5 reads the same way. AC4 (no composed instance, no metadata and no / gives no cluster) is mod040b_ac4. AC5 (cluster IDs match cluster_[A-Za-z0-9_]+) is mod040b_ac5 for every cluster with a non-empty key.
- AC6 (one cluster block per subnet of the membership metadata, a shared place whose name has no instance prefix at the top level) and AC7 (metadata nodes cluster by subnet name, prefix-named nodes by prefix) are the first line under a membership map, decided on the reference in MOD_040_b_nonvacuous; by ruling D26 item 7 a shared place has no membership entry and falls back to its instance prefix, so it is at the top level when its name has no / (hub), and in the cluster of its prefix otherwise (rv/x in cluster_rv), which is why AC6 and the test derivation name the shared place without /. AC8 and AC9 are slice (a) (MOD_040_nonvacuous).
- The test derivation (a composed net with two top-level instances and a directly composed net of two subnets whose shared place is named without /, exported and checked for cluster blocks, members and IDs) is AC1, AC2, AC5 and AC6 on composed nets.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_041"></a>
## MOD-041: Debug Protocol Subnet Instances

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_041` · Kind **F** · Scope every debug protocol implementation (Java, TypeScript, Rust; Python has none) · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 a25051467e9f467a ai** · Statement hash `a25051467e9f467a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a debug session subscribed to a live net answers `Subscribed`, its subnet instance list *shall* hold exactly one descriptor for each distinct instance prefix that the name of some transition or listed place of the net carries, and no other descriptor.<br><br>*When* a debug session subscribed to a live net answers `Subscribed`, each subnet instance descriptor *shall* list as its transitions exactly the transitions of the net whose instance prefix is the descriptor's prefix, and as its places exactly the listed places of the net whose instance prefix is the descriptor's prefix.<br><br>*When* a debug session subscribed to a live net answers `Subscribed`, each subnet instance descriptor *shall* carry as its parent prefix the instance prefix of its own prefix, and no parent prefix when its own prefix has none.<br><br>*When* a debug session subscribed to a live net answers `Subscribed`, the `instancePrefix` field of the `PlaceInfo` or `TransitionInfo` of every node *shall* be the instance prefix of the node's name, and *shall* be absent when the name has none. | 1. For every debug view V and every net X (its transition names and its listed place names, the places that some arc or output specification of a transition names; instancePrefix n is the part of n before its last '/', none when n has no '/' or that part is empty):<br>2. the prefixes of the descriptors V.descs X are pairwise distinct, and a string P is the prefix of some descriptor exactly when P is the instance prefix of some transition or listed place of X;<br>3. for every descriptor d of V.descs X and every name n, n is among d's transitions exactly when n is a transition of X with instance prefix d.pfx, and n is among d's places exactly when n is a place of X with instance prefix d.pfx;<br>4. for every descriptor d of V.descs X, d's parent is the instance prefix of d.pfx;<br>5. for every place or transition n of X, the instancePrefix field V.nodePrefix X n is the instance prefix of n (none when n has none). | <pre>fun V ↦<br>  (∀ (X : Mod041.NameNet),<br>      (List.map (fun x ↦ x.pfx) (V.descs X)).Nodup ∧<br>        ∀ (P : String),<br>          P ∈ List.map (fun x ↦ x.pfx) (V.descs X) ↔<br>            ∃ n ∈ X.nodes, instancePrefix n = some P) ∧<br>    (∀ (X : Mod041.NameNet),<br>        ∀ d ∈ V.descs X,<br>          ∀ (n : String),<br>            (n ∈ d.transitions ↔ n ∈ X.transitions ∧ instancePrefix n = some d.pfx) ∧<br>              (n ∈ d.places ↔ n ∈ X.places ∧ instancePrefix n = some d.pfx)) ∧<br>      (∀ (X : Mod041.NameNet), ∀ d ∈ V.descs X, d.parent = instancePrefix d.pfx) ∧<br>        ∀ (X : Mod041.NameNet), ∀ n ∈ X.nodes, V.nodePrefix X n = instancePrefix n</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D71 (a): the descriptors are a function of the names of the flat net, which carries no instance provenance (MOD-023). A descriptor exists for each distinct last-slash prefix of a node name, its place set is every listed place under that prefix, its parent is the prefix's own prefix. This is what all three debug protocol implementations do: rust/libpetri-debug/src/debug_session_registry.rs:91-134 (and its test :961-992, which asserts the internal place p1/nextItem in exposed_place_names), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/debug/DebugSessionRegistry.java:583-632, typescript/src/debug/debug-session-registry.ts:86-161. After composition the places under a prefix are the instance's internal places and its unbound ports: a bound port takes the caller place's name and has no prefix.
- The places of X are the listed places (the markdown's term): the places that some input, inhibitor, read or reset arc or some output specification of a transition names. Every runtime builds the session's place list, which gives both the PlaceInfo entries and the places the descriptors group, from the arcs and output specifications alone (rust/libpetri-debug/src/place_analysis.rs:39-65, used at debug_session_registry.rs:206 and read by build_subnet_instances at :105-114; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/export/PlaceAnalysis.java:47-73, used at DebugSessionRegistry.java:145 and read by buildSubnetInstances at :600-604; typescript/src/debug/place-analysis.ts:37-80, used at debug-session-registry.ts:193 and read at :142). A place the builder holds that no arc or output names (an explicit place, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:274, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:315, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:177, or a terminal place no arc names, petri_net.rs:296) has no PlaceInfo and is in no descriptor in all three runtimes. The runtimes agree and the debug protocol describes no other place, so the markdown sentences say listed places and the block states them; such a place is not in X.
- Names are strings, read as their characters, and the instance prefix is the export glossary's instancePrefix (Spec/GlossaryExportCluster.lean), the helper of MOD-040 line 5 and the AUTO cluster key of EXP-016: the part of a name before its last '/', none for a name without '/' and for a name whose only '/' is its first character, as instancePrefixOf and parentOf do in every runtime (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_prefixes.rs:22-40, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/export/SubnetPrefixes.java:41-65, typescript/src/export/subnet-prefixes.ts:33-72); parentOf is instancePrefixOf applied to the prefix, so line 3 uses instancePrefix for both. So the instancePrefix field and MOD-040's helper agree on every node (mod041_nodePrefix_eq_helper), and the debug descriptors, the helper and the export clusters speak about one prefix.
- Lines 1 and 2 compare sets: the order of the descriptor list and of the names in a descriptor is not stated (Rust sorts the prefixes through a BTreeMap, debug_session_registry.rs:102-103; Java and TypeScript keep discovery order, transitions first), nor are repetitions within a descriptor's name lists (a net holds each name once).
- Items 2 and 3 (the subnet definition's name and the parameter value, 'where available') are not stated: the markdown records that current runtimes keep neither after composition, and every runtime leaves the definition name absent (debug_session_registry.rs:128, DebugSessionRegistry.java:625) and carries no parameter value.
- That the Subscribed response carries the descriptor list beside the place and transition descriptors, and the field names (subnetInstances, prefix, parentPrefix, transitionNames, exposedPlaceNames, instancePrefix), are wire shape, tested and not proven. The sentence that the requirement is observability-only is true of any function of the net's names and has no line. The instancePrefix the event converter adds to events (netEventConverter_emitsInstancePrefixForPrefixedEvents) is not stated here.
- Scope: a session over a live net, as each sentence says. A session over an imported archive carries no net topology, and the markdown leaves its list unspecified: Java and TypeScript return an empty list, Rust groups the transition names it holds (debug_session_registry.rs:104-124); not stated. Python has no debug protocol (spec/coverage-matrix.md, the MOD-041 row).
- AC1 (one descriptor per distinct instance prefix that some transition or listed place name carries) is line 1; its 'one' is the no-repeat half (MOD_041_mutant_dupPrefix_killed). AC2 (the transition and exposed-place sets of a descriptor enumerate exactly the transitions and listed places under its prefix) is line 2. AC3 (a node whose name has an instance prefix carries it as instancePrefix, one whose name has none carries none) is line 4; the bound port src of the pipeline carries none (MOD_041_nonvacuous). AC4 (a nested instance reports its parent prefix) is line 3; the reference example outer/inner with parent outer is MOD_041_nonvacuous. AC5 (a net with no '/' in any name gives an empty list and no instancePrefix field) follows from lines 1 and 4 for every model of the block (mod041_flat).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_050"></a>
## MOD-050: Verification Pass-Through on Composed Flat Net

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_050` · Kind **B** · Scope every verification facility of section 07, on every net build() returns · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 03e6a8a2873ef5fc ai** · Statement hash `03e6a8a2873ef5fc`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a verification facility specified in section 07 (VER) runs on a net that `build()` returned, it *shall* give the result that section 07 specifies for the hand-written net with the same name, the same places in the same order, the same transitions in the same order with the same names, arcs, output specifications, timing, priorities and actions, and the same terminal places in the same order.<br><br>The result of a verification facility specified in section 07 (VER) *shall not* depend on which subnet a place or transition belongs to ([MOD-026]) or on the place correspondence of a transition ([MOD-031]). | 1. For every result type R, every facility F on built nets (the facility as section 07 specifies it) and every facility V on the nets build() returns:<br>2. on the hand-written net of every built net b (no correspondence, no membership), V gives what F gives on b;<br>3. on two nets c and c' with the same built net (the same places, transitions and terminal places, in the same order), V gives the same result, whatever correspondence and membership each carries. | <pre>fun {N A R} F V ↦<br>  (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A), V (handWritten b) = F b) ∧<br>    ∀ (c c' : ComposedNet N A), c.toBuiltNet = c'.toBuiltNet → V c = V c'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A net that build() returned is a ComposedNet (Reference/ComposeBuild.lean): core's BuiltNet (places, transition definitions in order, each with its name, arcs, output specification, timing, priority and action, terminal places) and the two things composition leaves on a net, the place correspondence of each transition (MOD-031: Rust local_name_map, Java and TypeScript placeAlias) and the membership map (MOD-026: Rust subnet_membership, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:40). A hand-written net is a ComposedNet with neither (handWritten), as buildScript builds it from place, trans and terminal calls (Op.ofBOp gives every transition the correspondence none; only direct composition records membership). A facility is a function of the net it runs on; its inputs other than the net (the property, the initial marking, the environment mode, the options) are part of the facility, so each choice of them is one F.
- The net's name is not modelled. The first quoted sentence names it ('the same name') only so that the hand-written net it speaks of is one net; a facility whose result shows the name (a report title) gets the composed net's name on both sides. The model therefore covers the facilities whose result does not show the name, which are the ones items 1 to 5 list.
- The statement is stronger than the sentences in one respect: it ranges over every ComposedNet value, not only the nets build() returns. Line 1 also speaks of hand-written nets the net builder would reject (two places with one name, a terminal clash of EXEC-042 AC5), and line 2 of values no script builds (a correspondence list whose length differs from the transitions', membership of a name the net does not hold). A verifier is only ever handed a built net, so the strengthening excludes only a verifier that is right on every buildable net and inconsistent on a value no runtime constructs; the reference meets the stronger form (MOD_050_reference).
- The first quoted sentence is lines 1 and 2 together: V c = F c.toBuiltNet for every net c (mod050_iff_factor), since c and handWritten c.toBuiltNet have the same built net. The places, the transitions and the terminal places are lists, and two built nets are equal when the three lists are, so the sentence says 'in the same order' of each. The line does not claim that a facility ignores the order: place order is non-normative (ruling D32), and composition does not fix it (Rust adds an instance's renamed places in hash-map order, rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:84-96). The runtimes' verifiers do not see that order, because every flat net indexes its places sorted by name (rust/libpetri-verification/src/net_flattener.rs:101-104, typescript/src/verification/encoding/net-flattener.ts:82, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/encoding/NetFlattener.java:104), and the incidence matrix of the P-invariant computation and the SMT encodings are built from the flat net (IncidenceMatrix.from(FlatNet) in all three); such a facility is order-free (mod050_sortIdx_orderFree).
- The second quoted sentence is line 2: two nets that differ only in correspondence and membership get one result. It is about the result, not about which fields a facility touches. No verifier result depends on either. A grep of rust/libpetri-verification/src, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis and typescript/src/verification finds no read of subnet membership or subnetOf. The correspondence is read only where a verifier pass rebuilds a transition and copies it through unchanged: rust/libpetri-verification/src/reaping.rs:122-123, rust/libpetri-verification/src/in_flight.rs:404-405, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/Reaping.java:116, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/InFlight.java:434, typescript/src/verification/reaping.ts:86, typescript/src/verification/in-flight.ts:370 and typescript/src/verification/terminal-places.ts:57. Such a pass meets the line (MOD_050_allows_copyThrough). The same line carries MOD-031's sentence that the correspondence is not consulted by the verifier (mod050_sameStructure cites it).
- A helper whose result is the rebuilt net itself (TypeScript relaxLate, exported at typescript/src/verification/index.ts:20; Java Reaping.relaxLate, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/Reaping.java:90; Rust relax_late, rust/libpetri-verification/src/reaping.rs:84) is not a facility of section 07, which names no such helper. Its result keeps the correspondence, so it would fail line 2 if it were one; the block does not range over it, and the verdicts computed on its net are facilities of the lines.
- The prose sentence 'All verification facilities specified in section 07 (VER) MUST operate on a composed flat net per [MOD-023] without any composition-aware adaptation' is the two lines on its safety side: a verifier that adapts to composition by reading the leftovers breaks line 2 (MOD_050_forbids_readsMembership, MOD_050_forbids_readsCorr), and one that adapts by recognising subnet transitions in the names of the flat net breaks line 1 (MOD_050_mutant_structureOnly_killed). Its offer side, that the verifier runs on a composed net at all and does not refuse it, is a coverage theorem and no line: Mod050Covers asks that a composed net is accepted whenever section 07's facility accepts its built net, every model of the block meets it (mod050_accepts, the reference included), and a verifier that refuses every net carrying a correspondence is killed (MOD_050_forbids_refusesComposed). 'The verifier sees the composed net as a normal PetriNet' is lines 1 and 2; 'no modular extension to the verifier API is required' is API shape, not modelled: V and F take the same arguments by typing.
- Items 1 to 5 name the facilities F the lines range over; each is specified by its own block on flat nets, and line 1 hands it the built net. Item 1 (VER-002) is instantiated at the reference verdict (mod050_proven_iff, cited for VER-002) and item 2 (VER-005) at the place index the incidence matrix is built over (mod050_pinvColumns, cited for VER-005). Items 3 to 5 (VER-020, VER-021, VER-004, VER-010) are linked through the free F only: no theorem here instantiates F with their blocks (open item). 'Where supported' in item 5 is configuration (kind N): an implementation without a state class graph has no such F.
- AC1 (verification of a composed pipeline completes with a result of the same shape as for a hand-written net) is covered in part. 'The same shape' is the type of the lines: V and F have one result type R. 'Completes' is not modelled (a Lean function is total), and neither is the SMT route: AC1 is reached at the reference verdict only (Reference.verdict of Reference/Decide.lean over the flat net's toNet), where mod050_proven_iff reads the result on a composed net: Proven exactly when the search completed and no reachable marking violates the property (verdict_proven_iff).
- AC2 is reworded in the markdown to agree with the first quoted sentence: the results match on the hand-written equivalent that lists its places in the composed net's order, and a result that does not depend on the order of places matches on every hand-written equivalent per MOD-023. The first half is lines 1 and 2: on the test derivation's pipeline (a producer, a buffer instance with its input port bound to the host place, a consumer) the composed and the hand-written scripts build the same built net and different correspondences, and every model of the block gives them one result (mod050_ac2). The second half is mod050_handWritten: MOD-023 line 2 (buildScript_redeclare) gives the hand re-declaration the same transitions in order, the same places in some order and the same terminal places, so every model gives it the same result from every OrderFree facility. The runtimes' P-invariant computation and SMT encodings are OrderFree (above); mod050_pinvColumns shows the composed pipeline with its places in another order, as a Rust build may return it, and the hand-written pipeline getting one result. A facility that reports over the raw place order (mod050_placeIndex) is not OrderFree, and AC2 does not claim it matches a hand-written equivalent that lists its places in another order.
- MOD-023 AC4 is the second half of AC2: MOD-023's block says its AC4 is MOD-050's line, which takes MOD-023 line 2 as its premise, and the link is the cites tag on mod050_handWritten. MOD-023's block is not imported here; its line 2 holds of the reference build script (mod023_buildScript), and spec_consistent_compose conjoins MOD_023 with this block on one model.
- AC3 (P-invariant computation on a composed net succeeds and is over the composed, prefixed place names) is covered in part. By line 1 the computation runs on the built net, whose places carry the prefixed names (MOD-010, mod010_placeName; MOD-020 for bound ports). MOD_050_nonvacuous shows the place index on the composed pipeline (answer/OUT, not OUT), and mod050_pinvColumns the sorted index the incidence matrix is built over (A_IN, answer/OUT, done, src); a verifier that reports places under the names the subnet declared is killed (MOD_050_forbids_readsCorr). 'Succeeds' is not modelled, and these are stand-in facilities: VER-005's computation is over the numbered rows of the flat net (its InvFn), and no theorem here plugs that function into F (open item).
- The tests listed for MOD-050 in spec/00-index.md (Java SubnetVerifyTest, TypeScript subnet-verify.test.ts, Rust subnet_verify) verify subnets through MOD-051's harness, which composes a synthetic net and runs the standard verifier on it; they exercise line 1, not the comparison of AC2. No test in any language cites MOD-050 (spec/coverage-matrix.md:276, every language column empty), and none compares a composed net with its hand-written equivalent.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_050_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_050): ✓ The pass-through meets MOD-050 for every facility. A net composed from the subnet `answer` and the same net written by hand build the same places and transitions; the verifier is handed that built net in both cases, so it gives one answer, whatever correspondence and membership records the composed net carries beside it.
  <pre>∀ {N A R : Type} (F : BuiltNet N A → R), MOD_050 F (refPassThrough F)</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_050_allows_copyThrough` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_050): ✓ MOD-050 allows a pass that copies the correspondence through: it reads the correspondence of `answer/work` on the composed pipeline (`IN` to `A_IN`, `OUT` to `answer/OUT`) and puts it on the rebuilt net, but the facility's result depends only on the places, transitions and terminal places, so the block holds for every facility.
  <pre>∀ {R : Type} (F : BuiltNet String Unit → R),<br>  MOD_050 F (mod050_copyThroughV F) ∧<br>    (mod050_copyThrough (mod050_build mod050_pipeOps)).corrs =<br>      [none, some [("IN", "A_IN"), ("OUT", "answer/OUT")], none]</pre>

  <pre>¬MOD_050 mod050_placeIndex (mod050_readsCorr mod050_placeIndex)</pre>

  <pre>¬MOD_050 mod050_placeIndex (mod050_readsMembership mod050_placeIndex)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_050_forbids_refusesComposed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_050): ✗ A verifier that refuses composed nets violates MOD-050 (the offer of the prose, through line 2): it verifies the hand-written pipeline and lists `src`, `A_IN`, `answer/OUT`, `done`, but gives no result on the composed pipeline, whose `answer/work` carries the correspondence `IN` to `A_IN`, `OUT` to `answer/OUT`.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_051"></a>
## MOD-051: SubnetDef.verify(harness) for local property verification

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_051` · Kind **B** · Scope verify on a subnet definition in Java, TypeScript and Rust, and verify_subnet in Python (on the Rust one); SHOULD, so the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers it · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 c442a9bd4be9999a ai** · Statement hash `c442a9bd4be9999a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* `verify` returns a result, the synthetic net it verified *shall* be the net that a new enclosing builder builds from one call that composes the subnet's instance under the prefix `sut`, binds each port to its harness place (`harness_in_&lt;port>` for an input port, `harness_out_&lt;port>` for an output port, `harness_io_&lt;port>` for an in-out port), binds no channel and declares nothing else.<br><br>*If* instantiating the subnet under the prefix `sut` fails or building the synthetic net fails, *then* `verify` *shall* fail.<br><br>*If* the harness supplies no token source for an input or in-out port of the subnet, *then* `verify` *shall* fail and *shall* return no verification result.<br><br>*If* the harness supplies a token source for every input and in-out port and the [CORE-043] check fails on the synthetic net, *then* `verify` *shall* fail with an error that names the transition the check names, also when the harness lists no property.<br><br>*When* `verify` returns a result, the result *shall* hold an entry for each property of the harness and no entry for another property, and each entry for a property *shall* be the result of the standard verifier ([VER-003], [VER-006]) on the synthetic net, set up with that property, the harness places of the input and in-out ports as environment places, the selected environment mode, the verifier's default options and the empty initial marking, and then passed, together with the synthetic net, through the configure hook, whose changes override that setup.<br><br>*When* `verify` is called without options, it *shall* verify under the environment mode `AlwaysAvailable` with no configure hook. | 1. For every instantiation function Inst, build-script function BS, CORE-043 compile check C, environment-aware decider D and verification operation SV, over every definition S, harness h and options:<br>2. if some input or in-out port of S has no token source in h, SV fails;<br>3. if SV returns a report r, then Inst instantiates S under the prefix sut as some instance I, and BS builds r's synthetic net from the one call that composes I with every port bound to its harness place and no channel bound (so SV fails when Inst or BS fails);<br>4. if every input and in-out port has a token source, Inst instantiates S under sut as I, BS builds the synthetic script of I as c and C refuses c naming n, then SV fails with a message that names n, whatever properties h lists;<br>5. if SV with options o returns a report r, then for one list envs that is a permutation of the harness places of the input and in-out ports, every entry of r is (φ, verifyOne D o r.synth envs φ) for a property φ of h, and every property of h has an entry;<br>6. SV without options is SV with the options AlwaysAvailable and the hook that changes nothing. | <pre>fun {A} Inst BS C D SV ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetDef String A) (h : SubnetHarness) (o : Option (SubnetVerifyOpts A)),<br>      sourcesOk S h = false → ∃ msg, SV S h o = Except.error msg) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetDef String A) (h : SubnetHarness) (o : Option (SubnetVerifyOpts A))<br>        (r : SubnetReport A),<br>        SV S h o = Except.ok r →<br>          ∃ I, Inst S "sut" = Except.ok I ∧ BS (synthScript S I) = Except.ok r.synth) ∧<br>      (∀ (S : SubnetDef String A) (h : SubnetHarness) (o : Option (SubnetVerifyOpts A))<br>          (I : Instance String A) (c : ComposedNet String A) (n : String),<br>          sourcesOk S h = true →<br>            Inst S "sut" = Except.ok I →<br>              BS (synthScript S I) = Except.ok c →<br>                C c.toBuiltNet = some n →<br>                  ∃ msg, SV S h o = Except.error msg ∧ MsgNames msg n) ∧<br>        (∀ (S : SubnetDef String A) (h : SubnetHarness) (o : SubnetVerifyOpts A)<br>            (r : SubnetReport A),<br>            SV S h (some o) = Except.ok r →<br>              ∃ envs,<br>                envs.Perm (harnessEnvs S) ∧<br>                  (∀ e ∈ r.results,<br>                      e.1 ∈ h.props ∧ e.2 = verifyOne D o r.synth envs e.1) ∧<br>                    ∀ φ ∈ h.props, ∃ e ∈ r.results, e.1 = φ) ∧<br>          ∀ (S : SubnetDef String A) (h : SubnetHarness),<br>            SV S h none = SV S h (some defaultVerifyOpts)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- SV is the subnet verification of one implementation, read as a function: Rust verify_subnet_with_options (rust/libpetri-verification/src/harness.rs:356-447), Java SubnetDef.verify (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:282-380), TypeScript SubnetDef.verify (in typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts), Python verify_subnet (py_verify_subnet in rust/libpetri-py/src/verification.rs, on the Rust one). Failing is a panic or an exception, read as an error; the shorter signatures (verify(harness), verify(harness, mode)) are SV with no options and with the options of that mode and no hook. Places are names (String). The parameter value (item 1) is type-checked by the host language and not modelled (MOD-010 AC4), and neither are token types: Java gives each harness place its port place's token type (SubnetDef.java newSyntheticPlace), Rust and TypeScript key places by name, and no MOD-022 type check can fire on a fresh harness place.
- Line 1 is item 2 and AC3 as reworded under ruling R-MC9 (a), carried by D20: the environment mode of item 4 bounds the input, not the token source. Every runtime calls the source once while it builds the synthetic net and discards the token (harness.rs:39-48, :389-393 and :416, SubnetDef.java:311-313 and :332-334, subnet-def.ts:295-301 and :320-326), so a source carries no count the verifier reads and does not set the harness place's token type either (Java takes it from the port's own place, TypeScript makes an untyped place, Rust keys the place by name); what the line keeps is that a missing source for an input or in-out port is an error. The harness models a source by its port name only, so item 2's 'a source that fails or returns no token makes verify fail' (a panic in Rust, an exception or a null or undefined check in Java and TypeScript) is the host language's and not modelled (harness.rs:380-388 and :407-415, SubnetDef.java:302-309 and :325-331, subnet-def.ts:284-292 and :312-319). A source for an output port or for a name no port has is ignored by every runtime and by the lines. Rust instantiates before it checks the sources; the line claims only the refusal, not which check reports it.
- Line 2 is the first two quoted sentences. It constrains only a call that returns a result, as the first sentence's trigger says, and claims nothing about a call that is refused for another reason. The second sentence is its contrapositive: a report requires the instance under sut and the synthetic net, so a call whose instantiation or build fails fails too (mod051_fails_of_build). The runtimes instantiate under sut (harness.rs:369, SubnetDef.java:288, subnet-def.ts:266), bind every port to its harness place and compose once on a new builder, then build (harness.rs:430-432, SubnetDef.java:347-349, subnet-def.ts:340-342); channels are not bound and flow through as renamed transitions (MOD-021). The enclosing net's name (verify_<definition>) is not modelled, as no net name is (MOD-050). The harness place names are what a property, a sink place or a carrier place set through the hook names, so they are part of the contract; the subnet's own places are named sut/<place> by MOD-010. A wrong synthetic net that adds a generator transition feeding the input place is killed (MOD_051_forbids_generator). The prose sentence that an implementation MAY wrap the subnet in such a net and invoke the standard verifier per MOD-050 is reworded under D20 to say that it does, as every runtime does; MOD-050 then makes the verifier see the synthetic net as a hand-written net.
- Line 3 is the fourth quoted sentence and the bindActions paragraph's 'The [CORE-043] check in `verify` applies to the bound definition as to any other.' Every runtime runs the check on the synthetic net before any property (harness.rs:436, SubnetDef.java:351-353, subnet-def.ts:344-346), so it fails also with no property. C is CORE-043's compile check, which names the first output-declaring transition that carries passthrough (CORE_043 line 1); the line asks that the message names it (MsgNames), not its bytes. CORE-043 line 3 already binds each per-property SMT entry point; this line binds verify's own check, which also runs when there is no property. A verify without the check is killed (MOD_051_forbids_noCore043).
- Line 4 is the fifth quoted sentence, item 4 (the mode is supplied in the options of verify or defaulted, not carried by the harness: Java's VerificationHarness record holds the parameters, the generators and the properties only, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/verification/VerificationHarness.java:60-64), the option bullet 'a configure hook, called once per property with the per-property verifier after the implementation's own setup (property, environment places, environment mode) and with the synthetic net, returning the verifier to run', and the hook's override semantics (run_per_property in harness.rs, the per-property loop of SubnetDef.verify in SubnetDef.java and in subnet-def.ts). The setup is a value (VerifySetup) and the hook a function on it that also receives the synthetic net; a hook that returns a verifier for another net is outside the model. The default options and the empty initial marking are the verifier's defaults (SmtVerifier::for_net in rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java:126, typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts:141); the verifier reads no deadline tolerance, so the synthetic net is handed with tolerance 0. D is VER-006's environment-aware decider (EnvDecider): the standard verifier with the mode and the registered environment places, whose verdict lines then apply to every entry. Wrong setups are killed: no environment place registered (MOD_051_forbids_noEnvs, under which the forwarder proves PlaceBound(harness_out_out, 0)), the output ports registered too (MOD_051_forbids_outputsAsEnv, under which Bounded(0) refuses every subnet that writes its output port) and the setup applied after the hook, so that the hook cannot change the mode (MOD_051_forbids_hookFirst).
- A Rust build without the z3 feature has no standard verifier: every entry is Unknown with route Unavailable and the configure hook is not called (rust/libpetri-verification/src/harness.rs:478-500; the feature is off by default, rust/libpetri-verification/Cargo.toml). That build is line 4 with D the constant Unknown decider, and AC6 holds only of a build with the solver (VER-013).
- Line 4 claims no order. Rust keeps the harness's property order and its duplicates; Java's VerificationHarness record copies the properties with Set.copyOf (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/verification/VerificationHarness.java:73), which keeps no order although its comment says it does, and Java and TypeScript return a map keyed by property. The environment places are a permutation of the harness places of the input and in-out ports, in the order the interface yields its ports, one list for the whole call. Several entries for one property are allowed, as the quoted 'each entry for a property' says. Every runtime sets the environment places and the selected mode on every per-property call, also for a subnet without an input or in-out port: Rust (harness.rs:465-468), Java (SubnetDef.java:368-371) and TypeScript (subnet-def.ts:359-361), and Python rides on Rust. So a hook that registers an environment place itself runs under the selected mode. The line keeps the spec's 'the selected environment mode' and kills a verify that hands over the selected mode only when the harness has an environment place and leaves the verifier on its default mode AlwaysAvailable otherwise (MOD_051_forbids_modeOnlyWithEnvs, the behaviour RD-29 recorded).
- Line 5 is the sixth quoted sentence and 'verify therefore SHOULD default to AlwaysAvailable, under which a Proven holds for every environment, and SHOULD let the caller pass a mode instead' (harness.rs:217-221 and :336-338, SubnetDef.java:213-215, subnet-def.ts:261, verification.rs:1062-1066). AC4 (the mode is selectable per verification and defaults to one that models injection, so a subnet with an input port is not refused a Proven by default) is lines 4 and 5 with VER-006: by default every entry is D under AlwaysAvailable with the input places registered (mod051_default), and only Ignore refuses every Proven (VER_006_verdict line 1). On the forwarder the reference proves TerminatesAtSink(harness_out_out) by default and answers Unknown for PlaceBound(harness_out_out, 0) under Ignore (MOD_051_nonvacuous). A verify whose default is Ignore is killed (MOD_051_forbids_defaultIgnore).
- The paragraph on what a verdict is worth under each mode (Ignore refuses every Proven, a Violated still comes back; Bounded(k) caps the resident tokens; Arrivals(k) bounds the total; Arrivals(k, k) delivers exactly k) restates VER-006 on the synthetic net and is reworded under ruling D49 (a), VB2: a Violated under Ignore is a counterexample with injection for a reachability-safety property only, and a rest of the subnet while the environment stays silent for a quiescence property (VER_006_verdict line 3, VER_006_frozen_in_injected). AC5 (a forwarding subnet proves PlaceBound of its output at k under Arrivals(k) and violates it under Bounded(k)) is line 4 handing D the mode Arrivals(0, k) or Bounded(k) on the synthetic net, which for the forwarder is VER-006's env IN → T → OUT renamed (mod051_fwd_synth); the verdicts are VER-006's AC9 and are delegated to it, not computed here, since the reference decider steps aside under Arrivals. The Proven under Arrivals(k) is VER_006_arrivals line 1 (OUT holds at most the arrivals so far; a closure without the optional source is killed by VER_006_arrivals_forbids_noOpt). The Violated under Bounded(k) is a completeness claim, which VER-006 leaves to the runtimes' env IN → T → OUT tests: its lines, the Bounded(k) reachable set of VER_006 line 3 among them, rule out a wrong Proven only.
- AC1 (a result of the same shape as VER-003's) is the type of the entries, D's Result. AC2 (no enclosing net needed) is the type of SV, which takes a definition. AC6 (the hook, or Python's keywords, reaches every per-property verifier, and a setting made there is visible) is line 4: every entry runs the setup the hook returns. Python's keywords are such a hook (the with_configure closure of py_verify_subnet, verification.rs:1081-1134). That a total budget too small to finish gives its exhaustion reason, and a sink place named there changes a quiescence verdict, is VER-013's and VER-014's over that setup; the setup's Options carry neither field, so those halves are tested, not stated here (open item). AC7 (ν options reach the verifier and change the model) and the paragraph 'ν subnets need the ν options' rest on NU-051 and NU-052; the setup here carries no ν option (open item). The Python keyword list, the unknown-name behaviour of sink and carrier places and the implementation notes are kind N. Cancellation through the thread interrupt is VER-013's.
- That verify returns a report whenever nothing is refused is the existence half of the requirement ('A subnet definition SHOULD support a local verification operation'), the coverage condition Mod051Covers, not a line: a verify that refuses every call meets lines 1 to 5 (mod051_rejectAll_meets) and is killed by the coverage condition (mod051_rejectAll_not_covers), which every runtime and the reference meet (mod051_ref_covers).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_051_bind"></a>
## MOD-051: Binding actions on a subnet definition

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_051_bind` · Kind **F** · Scope bindActions (both forms) on a subnet definition in Java, TypeScript and Rust; Python's bind_actions on a definition rides on the Rust one · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 6a9324aa9087148c ai** · Statement hash `6a9324aa9087148c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* actions are bound on a subnet definition, in either form, the new definition *shall* have the name, the ports and the channels of the original definition and the place correspondence ([MOD-031]) of each of its transitions, in the same order.<br><br>*When* actions are bound on a subnet definition with a resolver or a mapping, the body of the new definition *shall* be the net that binding the same resolver or mapping on the original body gives at net level ([CORE-042]), so the resolver or the mapping is keyed by the definition's own, unprefixed transition names. | 1. For every net-level resolver binding Bind and map binding BindMap of CORE-042, and every definition-level resolver binding DBind and map binding DBindMap:<br>2. for every definition S and resolver or map r, both DBind S r and DBindMap S r have S's name, ports and channels, and the place correspondences of S's definitions, position by position;<br>3. for every S and resolver r, the body of DBind S r is Bind applied to the body of S with r;<br>4. for every S and map m, the body of DBindMap S m is BindMap applied to the body of S with m. | <pre>fun {N A} Bind BindMap DBind DBindMap ↦<br>  (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br>      ∀ f ∈ [DBind, DBindMap],<br>        (f S r).name = S.name ∧<br>          (f S r).ports = S.ports ∧<br>            (f S r).chans = S.chans ∧<br>              List.map (fun x ↦ x.corr) (f S r).defs = List.map (fun x ↦ x.corr) S.defs) ∧<br>    (∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br>        subnetBody (DBind S r) = Bind (subnetBody S) r) ∧<br>      ∀ (S : SubnetDef N A) (m : String → Option (Act A)),<br>        subnetBody (DBindMap S m) = BindMap (subnetBody S) m</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A definition-level binding is a function from a subnet definition (SubnetDef: name, places, transition definitions with their place correspondence, terminal places, ports, channels) and a resolver or map to a definition; its body (subnetBody) is the built net of its places, transition definitions and terminal places. Every runtime binds a definition by binding its body at net level and keeping the interface (rust/libpetri-core/src/subnet_def.rs:181-204, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/SubnetDef.java:399-436, typescript/src/core/subnet-def.ts SubnetDef.bindActions, bindActionsWithResolver and withBody); Python binds through the Rust one (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs, PySubnetDef::bind_actions). Java and TypeScript re-point each channel at the rebuilt transition of the same name; a channel is its transition's name here, so it is kept unchanged. The parameter type is not modelled (Rust copies param_type).
- Lines 2 and 3 are 'mirroring the net-level operation of [CORE-042] with the same argument forms (mapping and resolver) and, per form, the same treatment of transitions it does not name, divergence included' and 'It is keyed by the definition's own, unprefixed transition names': Bind and BindMap are the implementation's own net-level bindings, which CORE-042 constrains (its line 5 carries the divergence: Rust keeps an omitted transition's action, Java and TypeScript substitute passthrough), and the body holds the definition's own names. Both readings meet the block (MOD_051_bind_reference_keep, MOD_051_bind_reference_clobber). A binding keyed by prefixed names is killed (MOD_051_bind_forbids_prefixedKeys), and so is a map form that ignores the map (MOD_051_bind_forbids_ignoreMap).
- Line 1 is 'returns a **new** definition whose ports, channels and parameters are unchanged'; the name, the places and the terminal places are kept through line 2, since CORE-042 keeps a net's places and terminal places. The place correspondence of MOD-031 is carried forward by the net-level rebuild in every runtime (CORE-042's assumes); a binding that drops the ports is killed (MOD_051_bind_forbids_dropPorts). 'The receiver is not modified' holds of every binding in the model, a function on immutable values, as in CORE-042.
- 'Instances created from the new definition carry the bound actions as their shared defaults ([MOD-030])' is a consequence: instantiation renames and keeps every action (TransDef.map_kept), so an instance of the bound definition carries the bound actions (mod051_bind_inst). 'The [CORE-043] check in `verify` applies to the bound definition as to any other' is line 3 of MOD_051, which ranges over every definition: binding a hand-written action to the forwarder's passthrough transition lets verify run (MOD_051_bind_nonvacuous).
- AC8 (bindActions on a definition returns a new definition whose instances carry the bound actions, keyed by unprefixed names; the receiver's instances keep the old ones; ports and parameters are unchanged) is lines 1 to 3 with mod051_bind_inst; the receiver's instances keep the old actions because the receiver is unchanged.
- The block is relative to Bind and BindMap and does not require them to meet CORE-042: on its own it is met by a definition binding that changes nothing, paired with a Bind that changes nothing. Its force comes from reading Bind and BindMap as the implementation's own net-level bindings, which CORE_042 constrains; that conjunction is made where the two blocks are read together, at consistency level, and the forbids evidence here fixes Bind to the reference refBind.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_051_bind_reference_clobber` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_051): ✓ **The reference meets the binding block with the map read as Java and TypeScript read it.** Example: binding the forwarder with a map that omits `work` leaves `work` on passthrough, as the same map does on a net.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type}, MOD_051_bind refBind refBindMapClobber refDefBind refDefBindMapClobber</pre>
- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_051_bind_reference_keep` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_051): ✓ **The reference meets the binding block with the map read as Rust reads it.** Example: binding a hand-written action to `work` on the forwarder binds `work` in the body, by that unprefixed name, and keeps the ports `in` and `out`; a name the map omits keeps its action.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type}, MOD_051_bind refBind refBindMapKeep refDefBind refDefBindMapKeep</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-MOD_060"></a>
## MOD-060: Fusion Set Declaration (orthogonal to composition)

`Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060` · Kind **F** · Scope every fusion-set declaration check · Source **verbatim** (spec/11-modular-composition.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 46e5399ec3b0b6e0 ai** · Statement hash `46e5399ec3b0b6e0`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* a fusion set is declared with no member, *then* declaring it *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* a fusion set is declared with a non-empty name and at least one member and no two of its members have different run-time token types, declaring it *shall* succeed and *shall* return the set with its name and with its members in the order they were declared.<br><br>*Where* an implementation keeps a run-time token type for places (Java and Rust), *if* two members of a fusion set have different token types, *then* declaring the set *shall* fail. | 1. A fusion-set declaration check D meets MOD-060 under a token-type reading tyOf of places when:<br>2. for every name n, D rejects the set named n with no member;<br>3. for every set s with a non-empty name and at least one member whose members all have the same token type under tyOf, D returns s itself: its name and its members in declaration order;<br>4. for every set s two of whose members have different token types under tyOf, D rejects s. | <pre>fun {N _T} tyOf D ↦<br>  (∀ (n : String), ∃ m, D { name := n, members := [] } = Except.error m) ∧<br>    (∀ (s : FusionSet N),<br>        s.name ≠ "" → s.members ≠ [] → TypesAgree tyOf s → D s = Except.ok s) ∧<br>      ∀ (s : FusionSet N), ¬TypesAgree tyOf s → ∃ m, D s = Except.error m</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an abstract declaration check D : DeclFn N (Reference/Fuse.lean): a set (FusionSet, glossary GlossaryCompose.lean: a name and the member places in declaration order) is accepted, returning a set, or rejected with a message. The token type is a model parameter tyOf: Java reads Place.tokenType (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/FusionSet.java Builder.build) and Rust the run-time TypeId of each member (rust/libpetri-core/src/fusion.rs FusionSetBuilder.member, which rejects a member of another type as it is added); TypeScript (typescript/src/core/fusion-set.ts FusionSetBuilder.build) keeps no run-time token type and is the case tyOf := fun _ => (), under which line 3 never applies. The Python binding (rust/libpetri-py) exposes no fusion-set declaration, so no line reaches it. The witness is refDeclFusion tyOf, which is what every runtime does on a set with a non-empty name: an empty member list is rejected with 'must have at least one member (MOD-060)', a member whose type differs from the first member's is rejected, and otherwise the set is kept as declared.
- Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and AC4's malformed case: a check that accepts an empty set is killed (MOD_060_mutant_acceptEmpty_killed). Line 2 is the second quoted sentence, AC1 and the body's item 2: a set with one member is accepted (ruling D54 (a): every runtime accepts it, and it fuses nothing, since its canonical member maps to itself); a check that rejects a one-member set as malformed, the earlier SHOULD of AC4, is killed (MOD_060_mutant_rejectSingleton_killed). 'Returns the set as declared' fixes the member order, so the canonical member, the first declared (FusionSet.canonical, which MOD-061's substitution reads), is the one the caller wrote first; a check that reorders the members breaks line 2 (MOD_060_forbids_reorder).
- Line 3 is the third quoted sentence and AC3, under ruling D36 (a): the token-type check is stated where an implementation keeps a run-time token type. A check that compares no token type is killed (MOD_060_mutant_noTypeCheck_killed). Compatibility per CORE-003 is equality of the run-time token type in Java and Rust; a compile-time check (TypeScript's generic FusionSet.of, Rust's typed member) is typing, not modelled.
- AC2 (fusion is independent of port bindings; the canonical fused place is the substitution target of every arc that referenced a port-substituted place or a non-canonical member) and the paragraph on the order of operations, including its sentence that the canonical member is the place of every arc that was on the substituted caller place or on another member, so that their token flows meet, are MOD-061's: that sentence is about arcs, and MOD-061 lines 1, 3 and 4 state where every arc lands; the paragraph's last sentence, that a token put on a non-canonical member at initial-marking time stays on that undeclared name, is ruling D54 (a) and MOD-061 AC2 (CORE-072). Fusion runs at build(), after every compose call (Reference/ComposeBuild.lean finish and fuseStage), and its substitution sends every member to the first declared member (MOD-061 lines 1, 3 and 4 through SubstSpec). The name of a fusion set is used in diagnostics only (MOD-061 step 1). An empty name is out of scope, as body item 1 says it is implementation-defined: line 2 asks for acceptance only of a set with a non-empty name, because Rust rejects an empty name (FusionSetBuilder::new asserts it, rust/libpetri-core/src/fusion.rs:150-156, and FusionSet::of goes through the builder), TypeScript rejects it on the builder (typescript/src/core/fusion-set.ts:126-129) and accepts it in FusionSet.of (fusion-set.ts:107-110), and Java accepts it (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/FusionSet.java:158-160). Line 1 keeps every name, the empty one included, since every runtime rejects a set with no member whatever its name. A check that rejects every empty name and is the reference otherwise meets MOD-060 (mod060_rejectEmptyName_meets), and so does the reference, which accepts it. The test derivation (three members of one type accepted; one member accepted and fusing nothing; no member rejected; mixed types rejected in Java and Rust; the compose-then-fuse case) is MOD_060_nonvacuous for the declarations and MOD-061 for the build.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): ✓ The reference declaration check satisfies MOD-060 for every token-type reading: it rejects a set with no member, rejects a set two of whose members have different token types, and otherwise returns the set exactly as it was declared, a set with one member included.
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : ToString N] [inst_1 : DecidableEq T] (tyOf : N → T),<br>  MOD_060 tyOf (refDeclFusion tyOf)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_forbids_reorder` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): ✗ A check that returns the members in another order violates MOD-060 (line 2): for the set `permits` declared with members 0, 2 and 4 it returns 4, 2, 0, so the canonical member, the first declared, would be 4 instead of 0.
  <pre>¬MOD_060 mod060_ty reorderDecl</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_mutant_acceptEmpty_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): The mutant without line 1 is killed by the check that accepts an empty set: it meets the other two lines, since a set with a member goes to the reference and a set with no member has one token type, but it accepts the set `empty` with no member.
  <pre>MOD_060_mutant_acceptEmpty mod060_ty acceptEmptyDecl ∧ ¬MOD_060 mod060_ty acceptEmptyDecl</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_mutant_noTypeCheck_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): The mutant without line 3 is killed by the check that compares no token type: it meets the other two lines, but accepts the set `mixed` whose members 0 and 1 have two token types.
  <pre>MOD_060_mutant_noTypeCheck mod060_ty (refDeclFusion fun x ↦ ()) ∧<br>  ¬MOD_060 mod060_ty (refDeclFusion fun x ↦ ())</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_mutant_rejectSingleton_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): The mutant without line 2 is killed by the check that rejects a set with fewer than two members, the earlier SHOULD of AC4: it meets the other two lines, but rejects the set `one` with the single member 3, which every runtime accepts.
  <pre>MOD_060_mutant_rejectSingleton mod060_ty rejectSingletonDecl ∧<br>  ¬MOD_060 mod060_ty rejectSingletonDecl</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): ✓ Every line of MOD-060 is exercised by the reference. With places numbered and typed by parity: the set `permits` with members 0, 2 and 4 (one type) is accepted as declared; the set `one` with the single member 3 is accepted too and fuses nothing; the set `empty` with no member is rejected; the set `mixed` with members 0 and 1 (two types) is rejected. The same check without run-time token types, as in TypeScript, accepts `mixed`.
  <pre>refDeclFusion mod060_ty { name := "permits", members := [0, 2, 4] } =<br>    Except.ok { name := "permits", members := [0, 2, 4] } ∧<br>  refDeclFusion mod060_ty { name := "one", members := [3] } =<br>      Except.ok { name := "one", members := [3] } ∧<br>    (∃ m, refDeclFusion mod060_ty { name := "empty", members := [] } = Except.error m) ∧<br>      (∃ m,<br>          refDeclFusion mod060_ty { name := "mixed", members := [0, 1] } =<br>            Except.error m) ∧<br>        refDeclFusion (fun x ↦ ()) { name := "mixed", members := [0, 1] } =<br>          Except.ok { name := "mixed", members := [0, 1] }</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.MOD_060_joint` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.MOD_060): ✓ **The declaration and the fusion of a set fit together.** For every naming, token-type reading and channel merge, there is one declaration check that meets MOD-060 and one fusion that meets MOD-061, and the reference build script records a fusion set through that very check: declaring `fuse s` adds `s` to the builder's fusion sets exactly when the check accepts it, and fails with the check's message otherwise. So a set `{P, Q}` declared on the builder is fused at `build()` as it was declared, `P` first.
  <pre>∀ {N A T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N] [inst_2 : DecidableEq T]<br>  [inst_3 : ToString T] (Nm : Naming N) (tyOf : N → T) (Mg : MergeFn N A),<br>  ∃ Dc Fz,<br>    MOD_060 tyOf Dc ∧<br>      MOD_061 refBuild Fz ∧<br>        ∀ (b : Bld N A) (s : FusionSet N),<br>          scriptStep Nm tyOf refBuild Mg b (Op.fuse s) =<br>            Except.map<br>              (fun s' ↦<br>                { places := b.places, defs := b.defs, terminals := b.terminals,<br>                  retired := b.retired, contrib := b.contrib,<br>                  fusions := b.fusions ++ [s'] })<br>              (Dc s)</pre>
