- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_jodl_forbids_strict` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: a reapable dead-letter (a Deadline or Window transition, [TIME-013]) is enabled on a group with a token in each branch and a `pending` token; a late executor reaps it and rests with it enabled. The first line makes that rest a violation; the strict reading sees no quiescence there.
  <pre>¬NU_040_jodl nu040_strict</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_jodl_mutant_mayMiss_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: the count-level reading reports only markings that rest and hold a `pending` token (count-level rest implies the ν rest), so it meets the second line; it misses the stranded group, so it is not NU_040_jodl. The first line is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_040_jodl_mutant_mayMiss nu040_countLevel ∧ ¬NU_040_jodl nu040_countLevel</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_jodl_mutant_mayOverReport_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: the reading that ignores quiescence reports every rest with a `pending` token, so it meets the first line; it also reports a group the dead-letter is still handling, so it is not NU_040_jodl. The second line is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_040_jodl_mutant_mayOverReport nu040_pendingOnly ∧ ¬NU_040_jodl nu040_pendingOnly</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_jodl_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✓ Worked example. Fork `mA` takes the one budget token and mints name 0 into branch `a` with a `pending` token; fork `mB` mints name 1 into branch `b`. Each fork keeps the mint contract, yet the join is enabled on its token counts and no name is in both branches. The marking rests, `pending` holds a token, and `JoinedOrDeadLettered(pending)` is violated there, also when `done` is declared a sink. On the scatter-gather net with a dead-letter transition, no reachable marking violates the property.

- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.clashNu_countRest` (Libpetri.Spec.ClashesNu): ✓ **nu-b#8 (D20): quiescence reads enablement name-aware.** Worked example: AC2's marking holds X in branch A and Y in branch B. The join is enabled on its counts (both places are marked), but no name is in both branches, so it is not ν-enabled, and the net of that one join rests there although the join is not reapable. With branch A as the pending place, the token X waits there while the net rests: NU-040's joined-or-dead-lettered predicate, which reads the name-aware rest and holds of the reference, calls the marking a violation. The count reading would call the join enabled and the marking not quiescent.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_040_mint"></a>
## NU-040: Bounded Budget and Decidability (budget places declare mints)

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint` · Kind **F** · Scope the mint declaration every verifier route reads (declared_mints / declaredMints), Route A and Route B of NU-050 · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 a3b78a673e9e14f2 ai** · Statement hash `a3b78a673e9e14f2`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *Where* a place is declared to the verifier as a budget place, the ν routes *shall* read every transition that has an input arc on that place as a declared mint ([NU-010]).<br><br>The ν routes *shall* read a transition named as a mint transition on the verifier (`mintTransitions` / `mint_transitions`) as a declared mint, whatever budget places are declared.<br><br>The ν routes *shall* read a transition as a declared mint only when it is named as a mint transition on the verifier or has an input arc on a place declared to the verifier as a budget place. | 1. Let DM B E t say whether the transition t is a declared mint, when B are the places declared to the verifier as budget places and E the names declared to it as mint transitions.<br>2. For all B, E and t: if some input arc of t is on a place of B, then DM B E t is true.<br>3. For all B, E and t: if the name of t is in E, then DM B E t is true, whatever B is.<br>4. For all B, E and t: if DM B E t is true, then the name of t is in E or some input arc of t is on a place of B. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] DM ↦<br>  (∀ (budgets : List N) (explicit : List String) (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>      (∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs, s.place ∈ budgets) → DM budgets explicit t = true) ∧<br>    (∀ (budgets : List N) (explicit : List String) (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>        t.core.name ∈ explicit → DM budgets explicit t = true) ∧<br>      ∀ (budgets : List N) (explicit : List String) (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>        DM budgets explicit t = true →<br>          t.core.name ∈ explicit ∨ ∃ s ∈ t.core.inputs, s.place ∈ budgets</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is one declaration function DM: from the declared budget places, the names declared as mints on the verifier (mintTransitions / mint_transitions) and a transition, whether the transition is a declared mint. The three runtimes compute it once per net as a set of names, seeded with the named mints and extended by every transition with an input arc on a budget place (rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_fragment.rs:140-152, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/NameFragment.java:105-114, typescript/src/verification/analysis/name-fragment.ts:79-89); read per transition it is nu040DeclaredMint, the only model of the three lines (NU_040_mint_unique).
- An input arc is one of the transition's input specifications (input_specs / inputSpecs), whatever its cardinality: a read, inhibitor or reset arc on a budget place declares nothing (the third line, NU_040_mint_mutant_noOnlyWhen_killed). The second line is the word 'also' of the sentence before the first quote: the budget declaration adds to the named one and never replaces it (NU_040_mint_mutant_noAlso_killed). The three lines are the rule of NU-010's sentence 'the ν routes of [NU-050] read a transition as a mint ... only when the net declares it, in one of two ways', stated here once for both.
- What a declared mint must write (one fresh name into every coloured place it writes without consuming one) is the mint contract of NU-010, and how the routes read the write is NU-010's and NU-051's classification; neither is a line here. A named mint that is not a transition of the net is NU-010 AC6 (the declaration fails and names it); per transition, as here, it marks no transition.
- How a budget place is declared (budgetPlace / budget_place / budget_places on the verifier) is configuration, kind N. A declared budget place that is not a place of the net declares no mint, since no transition has an input arc on it.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✓ The reference declaration satisfies NU_040_mint: a transition with an input arc on a declared budget place is a declared mint, a named transition is one whatever the budget places, and no other transition is.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], NU_040_mint nu040DeclaredMint</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_forbids_everyMint` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: with place 0 declared and no mint named, the join only returns a budget token, so the third line keeps it from being a declared mint; the every-mint declaration makes it one, and a route would read its writes as fresh names.
  <pre>¬NU_040_mint nu040_everyMint</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_forbids_explicitOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: with place 0 declared as a budget place and no mint named, the fork takes a budget token, so the first line makes it a declared mint; the explicit-only declaration does not.
  <pre>¬NU_040_mint nu040_explicitOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_forbids_firstArcOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: a fork whose budget arc is its second input (after a request place 9) takes a budget token, so the first line makes it a declared mint; reading only the first arc misses it.
  <pre>¬NU_040_mint nu040_firstArcOnly</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_mutant_noAlso_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: the replacing declaration marks a budget consumer as a mint and marks nothing else, so it meets the first and third lines. With budget place 0 declared and fork `mB` named as a mint, `mB` takes no budget token and the replacing declaration drops it, so a route would read its fresh name as a copy. The second line forbids it, so the second line is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_040_mint_mutant_noAlso nu040_replacing ∧ ¬NU_040_mint nu040_replacing</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_mutant_noOnlyWhen_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✗ Worked example: the reverse-index declaration makes every named transition and every budget consumer a mint, so it meets the first two lines. It also makes the read-only gate a mint: with place 0 declared and no mint named, the gate copies whatever its request carries into `a`, and a route would trust that copy as a fresh name. The third line forbids it, so the third line is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_040_mint_mutant_noOnlyWhen nu040_anyArc ∧ ¬NU_040_mint nu040_anyArc</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_040_mint_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_040): ✓ Worked example. With budget place 0 declared, the fork, which takes a budget token, is a declared mint although no mint is named; the join, which only returns a budget token, is not; a gate that only reads the budget place is not; without the budget declaration the fork is not a mint either; and a named fork is a mint whatever budget places are declared.
  <pre>nu040DeclaredMint [0] [] nu040_fork.base = true ∧<br>  nu040DeclaredMint [0] [] nu040_join.base = false ∧<br>    nu040DeclaredMint [0] [] nu040_gate = false ∧<br>      nu040DeclaredMint [] [] nu040_fork.base = false ∧<br>        nu040DeclaredMint [0] ["mB"] nu040_mB.base = true</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_050_prefix"></a>
## NU-050: Exact Verification of Matched Transitions: the verdict on a built graph

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_prefix` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers the Route B name-partition graph (MAY); the verdict it reads off a built graph, for every property · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 81584bea75537de2 ai** · Statement hash `81584bea75537de2`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* the build of the Route B graph is stopped, because it runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`, whatever classes the build stored.<br><br>*If* the build is not stopped and a stored class violates a safety property, or an expanded class at which the net rests violates a quiescence property, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Violated`, also when the graph does not close.<br><br>*If* Route B answers `Violated`, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property: a stored class for a safety property, an expanded class at which the net rests for a quiescence property.<br><br>*If* the build is not stopped and no class violates the property, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` when the graph closes and `Unknown` when it does not. | 1. For every explorer E over classes, every build outcome o (the stored classes in discovery order, the number expanded, whether the build closed and whether it stopped) and every property p, where a class violates p as Decide.violatesAt reads it (for a safety property a stored class at which the predicate holds; for a quiescence property an expanded class at which the predicate holds and every successor is a firing of a reapable transition):<br>2. if the build stopped, V answers Unknown;<br>3. if the build did not stop and some class violates p, V answers Violated (at some class);<br>4. if V answers Violated at the class index i, class i violates p;<br>5. if the build did not stop and no class violates p, V answers Proven when the graph closed and Unknown when it did not. | <pre>fun V ↦<br>  ∀ (S K L : Type) (E : Explorer S K L) (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S)<br>    (p : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Prop' S L),<br>    (o.stopped = true → V S K L E o p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.unknown) ∧<br>      (o.stopped = false →<br>          (∃ i, Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = true) →<br>            ∃ i, V S K L E o p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.violated i) ∧<br>        (∀ (i : ℕ),<br>            V S K L E o p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.violated i →<br>              Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = true) ∧<br>          (o.stopped = false →<br>            (∀ (i : ℕ), Novel.RouteB.Decide.violatesAt E o p i = false) →<br>              V S K L E o p =<br>                if o.complete = true then Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.proven<br>                else Novel.RouteB.Decide.Verdict.unknown)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a verdict function on a built graph (ClassVerdict, the model of NU_055_truncation, shared so that one verdict function serves NU-050 and NU-055): from the explorer, the build's outcome (Decide.Out: the stored classes, the number expanded, complete, stopped) and the property (Decide.Prop': a safety predicate on classes, or a quiescence predicate with its reapable set), the verdict. How the build stores and expands classes, and that a stored class is reachable in the graph (Decide.prefix_safety_sound, Decide.prefix_quiescence_sound), is Decide.build's and VER-012's; the graph itself (its key, the name-permutation quotient) is VER-012's block. 'Does not close' is o.complete = false: the class bound reached (truncated, o.stopped = false), or the total budget or a cancellation (o.stopped = true), or the fuel of the Lean model run out (also a stop).
- Ruling D59 (a) (clashes nu-b#1, ver-d#1): a truncated graph answers Violated when a stored class violates (the prefix rule of VER-012 AC3), as Rust, Java and TypeScript do (nu_scg_verifier.rs:343-376, NuScgVerifier.java:224-246, nu-scg-verifier.ts:184-204). AC2 is reworded accordingly (NUB-1 (a)); the old 'not Proven/Violated' reading is NU_050_prefix_mutant_unknownOnTruncation, met by nu050_unknownOnTruncation and killed by line 2. A build stopped by the total budget or a cancellation answers Unknown whatever its prefix holds (nu_scg_verifier.rs:333-341, VER-013's rule): line 1, killed in nu050_stoppedPrefix.
- The sentence 'If the Route B graph does not close, then Route B shall not answer `Proven`.' is a consequence of the lines, not a line, so it is not quoted here: a stopped build answers Unknown (line 1), and a build that was not stopped answers Violated (line 2) or, with no violating class, Proven only on a closed graph (line 4). NU_050_prefix_open_never_proven carries it as cited evidence (the same fact as Decide.truncated_never_proven for the shipped verdict). The paragraph on an unbounded name pool ('the verifier MUST NOT return an unsound verdict', reworded under ruling D59 (a) from 'MUST return Unknown rather than an unsound verdict') is this rule together with the soundness blocks NU_050_soundB and NU_050_soundA: a graph that does not close never answers Proven, and a Violated names a class the graph reaches. AC2 is that paragraph's criterion #2 (NUB-1 (a)); its sentence '(NU-050 #2) An unbounded-fresh-name net without a budget place never yields Proven' is not quoted either, since it also says that the graph of every such net does not close, which no line states: the lines give that a graph that does not close answers Unknown or, by the prefix rule, Violated, never Proven, and NU_050_soundB_nonvacuous shows a graph that does not close on one such net at one class bound.
- Line 3 does not say which violating class a Violated names. The shipped verdict names the first in discovery order, which the spec calls the shortest witness; that and the report line naming the truncation are VER-003's and VER-012's report shape (ruling D40, clash ver-a#11), kind Q here. A Violated is sound for the graph: the class it names is reachable in the graph, not necessarily in the executor, since the graph lets a join fire on any shared name and a consumer take any resident one (clash nu-b#3); completeness against that free-choice name semantics is VER-012's (VD-1 (a)). AC1 (a counterexample that needs two different names to be equal is not reported on the exact path) is this: the graph's classes keep names apart, so a Violated names a class whose names are those of a graph path (line 3 and Decide.prefix_safety_sound); its run against the value-blind encoding is a fixture test (kind Q).
- The exactness paragraph's Route B sentence is reworded under ruling D59 (a) and VD-1 (a) from 'exact (sound and complete) whenever the symbolic graph closes' to 'sound for every executor run, and complete for the free-choice name semantics the graph explores': soundness is NU_050_soundB, completeness VER-012's block. Under modelled injection ([VER-006]) Route B declines when a verdict would depend on an environment place: VER-006 AC8 (VER_006_routeB_env, cited by VER-006's block: env_count_frozen and the decline cases of route_b_env_observation), not this block.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_prefix_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): The shipped verdict function satisfies the four lines: a stopped build gives `Unknown` before any class is read; otherwise the search for the first violating class decides, and with none the build's `complete` flag chooses between `Proven` and `Unknown` (`Decide.verdict`).
  <pre>NU_050_prefix refClassVerdict</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_prefix_forbids_closedReading` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): ✗ Reading a truncated graph as closed violates NU-050 (line 4): the build that expanded the good class `0` and then reached the class bound is answered `Proven`, although the classes it never stored may violate the property.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_prefix_forbids_stoppedPrefix` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): ✗ Reading a stopped build violates NU-050 (line 1): the build that ran out of budget with the bad class `2` stored is answered `Violated`, where a stopped build must answer `Unknown`, whatever it stored (VER-013).

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_prefix_mutant_unknownOnTruncation_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): The verdict function that answers `Unknown` on every truncated graph kills the reading of ruling D59 (b): it meets that reading, but NU-050's prefix rule (line 2) rejects it on a truncated build that stored a violating class (clash nu-b#1).

The shipped verdict answers: `Unknown` for a build that ran out of budget, although it stored class `2`; `Violated` at class `2` for a build that reached the class bound with class `2` stored, under the safety reading (the prefix rule), and `Unknown` under the quiescence reading, since class `2` was never expanded; `Unknown` for a cut build of good classes and `Proven` for a closed one; and `Violated` at class `2` for a closed build that expanded class `2`, under both readings.

For the safety property 'class 1 is bad' Route B answers Violated at class 1; for 'class 2 is bad', which no stored class is, it answers Unknown. **Assumptions**

- The model is the plan builder P (build_plan: the coloured set, the classification of every flat row, the checked colour-slot bound of NU-053, the refusals), with the shipped coloured encoding (Novel.RouteA.Enc.shipped, encode_coloured) fixed: a Proven of the encoding is read as its meaning, that no state the encoding's Reachable relation holds is bad (the solver is outside Lean), as in Novel.RouteA.routeA_safety_sound_plan. The executor is the reference ν firing RefNuFire, untimed and environment-free; a run is NuLinkA.RefNuRunA, a sequence of firings each of whose actions keeps the contract of the class build_plan's classification rule gives its source row (NuLinkA.srcClass: classifyRowG under the shipped gates; NuLinkA.NuContract; NU-010's mint contract under ruling D78 (a), NU-051's consumer contract), the premise 'while the declared mints and the coloured consumers keep their contracts' of the quoted sentence. That NuLinkA.NuContract at a mint class is NU-010's contract is NuLinkA.nuContract_mint_iff: it is Reference.MintContract, the contract nu010_contract_fresh derives from NU_010_contract with the reference minter, and Route B's mint contract is the same (nu050_mintContracts_agree). A source row the rule refuses carries no contract, since no declared mint or coloured consumer is read there; the shipped build_plan then refuses the plan.
- Ruling D59 (a) and NUB-2 (a) (clash nu-b#2): the fragment of Route A is 'a colour-slot bound exists' ([NU-053]), not budget conservation; the bullet is reworded so, and 'the initial budget k' and the refund example are dropped. The budget count is not a sound bound (Novel.RouteA.Retro.budget_k_false_proven): a planner with a fixed bound of one slot, the bound a budget of one would give, is killed here (NU_050_soundA_forbids_slotOne) on a mint drawing on a budget of two, which reaches two live names.
- The premises are hypotheses, and none reads the plan P returns. The rows premise (SrcCovers: every firing of the run has a source row) stands for the computation of the flat rows and the coloured set from the net (net_flattener, the coloured-set computation), which the Lean model takes as given, as Novel/RouteA/Plan.lean does; the guard, invariant and coloured-set premises are what the verifier checks before the encoding (buildPlan_premisesS). That the plan carries a classified row for every source row, with the class the rule gives, is a property of the shipped build_plan (NuLinkA.buildPlan_src), not a premise: a planner that leaves out a row (for instance an undeclared mint skipped where build_plan refuses the plan) still faces that row's firings in the premises and the run, and its Proven of the encoding without the row is unsound there (NU_050_soundA_forbids_dropRow). The projection premise is the paragraph on the one name of a coloured token, which the quoted paragraph on coloured writes applies to both routes.
- The quiescence line is stated for a net with no reapable transition, the strict quiescence DeadE of the shipped build_plan path (Novel.RouteA.routeA_quiescence_sound_plan). The reaping-aware form (DeadER over the reapable rows, NuLinkA.refNu_routeA_quiescence_sound_reaping) reads the reapable rows by transition, where the shipped encoder reads them by name (DeadERs, NU-053 line 6); the tie between the two waits for row names (open item of bridge B2) and is not a line here.
- The lines are soundness only: a planner that never answers meets them (the fallback to the over-approximation is the pipeline's: NU_053_dispatch says that without the coloured plan a quiescence property is never Proven, and no block states the rest of the fallback). That a plan is built whenever a colour-slot bound exists is NU-053 line 2. Completeness of Route A (NU-053 AC3, agreement with Route B on the fixtures) is kind Q.
- AC1 (a counterexample that needs two different names to be equal is not reported on the exact path) is the colour discipline of the encoding: a join consumes the same colour from every correlated input (sJoin), so the coloured encoding has no step that equates two names; NU_053 line 5 and the join rule of Novel.RouteA.ColourStep. Its run against the value-blind encoding is a fixture test (kind Q).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_soundA_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): The reference plan builder satisfies NU-050's Route A soundness lines: B2 on contract-keeping runs (`NuLinkA.refNuRunA_routeA_reach`) makes every run read off the source rows a Route A ν run over the rows of the shipped plan, which carries a classified row for every source row (`NuLinkA.buildPlan_src`), and Route A's soundness from the shipped `build_plan` carries a `Proven` of the encoding to every marking that run reaches (and, for quiescence, rests at).

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_soundA_forbids_dropRow` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): ✗ A planner that leaves an undeclared mint's row out of its plan, where `build_plan` refuses the plan, violates NU-050's Route A safety line. The transition writes a name into place `0` without being declared a mint. The slipped planner builds a plan with no row, whose encoding proves "place `0` never holds a name", yet the reference fires the transition once and place `0` holds the name `10`. The rows premise and the run read the source rows, so the left-out row's firing is still judged.

The coloured encoding with one slot proves "where the net rests, place `0` holds fewer than two names", yet after the two mints the budget is spent, the net rests, and place `0` holds two names.

- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_soundA_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050): ✓ Worked example. On a mint that draws on a budget of two, the shipped plan builder builds the plan with two colour slots: the weighting one on both places covers the coloured place and gives `⌊y·M0⌋ = 2`. The safety line then rules out a `Proven` of "place `0` never holds two names" for that plan: the reference runs the mint twice, each time writing a fresh name, and place `0` ends with the names `10` and `11`.

A firing whose action breaks the contract is not a step of the run; the spec makes no claim about it (copyingMint_breaks_simulation, cited by NU-010). The projection premise is the paragraph on the one name of a coloured token, read at every marking the run reaches. The timed lines (the join clock, the name-layer restart, the latest-bound relaxation of TIME-013) are the block NU_050_timed, over the timed semantics the graph's classes stand for (RefRouteBT); that the shipped timed graph is sound against it, and so the name x time claim, is still gap R6 of Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean. The routing order and part of the guard are the block NU_053_dispatch (no Route B after the colour-slot bound; no Proven of a quiescence property on a ν-net without the coloured plan); the Route B decline under environment injection is cited by VER_006 (VER_006_routeB_env) and test evidence; the refusal order of the name-alignment properties is NU_055_refusal; the rest of the guard (Unknown without a declared budget place) is stated by no block. Conflict-only priority (NU-052) is off: the priority pass is the executor's (RefExec), not one firing's, so the translated net is explored with conflict false (nu.md 1.5).

## NU-050: Exact Verification of Matched Transitions: a join's clock on a timed net

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_timed` · Kind **T** · Scope every verifier that offers the Route B name-partition graph (MAY) on a timed net; the timed semantics its classes stand for · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f39e225292e8140c ai** · Statement hash `f39e225292e8140c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition is not enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]), Route B *shall* hold no clock for it, even when its inputs hold the tokens its arcs require but no name is present in every correlated input.<br><br>*When* a transition fires and another transition `j` holds a clock and is not enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) in the intermediate marking ([TIME-012]), Route B *shall* take `j`'s clock away, even when `j`'s inputs still hold tokens, and *shall* give `j` a fresh clock if the firing leaves `j` enabled with an eligible name.<br><br>*When* a transition fires and another transition `j` holds a clock and is enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) before the firing, in the intermediate marking and after the firing, Route B *shall* keep `j`'s clock.<br><br>*When* a firing leaves a transition `j` enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]) and `j` held no clock before it, Route B *shall* start `j`'s clock at that firing.<br><br>*When* a transition fires, Route B *shall* take its clock away and *shall* give it a fresh clock if the firing leaves it enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]).<br><br>*While* time passes, Route B *shall* keep the marking and the start of the clock of every transition enabled with an eligible name ([NU-020], [NU-022]), and *shall* advance the clock reading by the time that passed.<br><br>Route B *shall* fire a transition only when it holds a clock that has run for at least the transition's earliest bound ([TIME-001]), and *shall* leave the clock reading unchanged at a firing.<br><br>This holds with and without the latest-bound relaxation for a late executor ([TIME-013]). | 1. **Assumptions**

- The model is the timed semantics the classes of the Route B graph stand for (RBTRel): a state holds the queue marking of stamped tokens, the clock reading and a stamp per transition name, none for no clock; a step is a delay or an atomic firing naming the fired ν transition, its chosen name and its emission. A class of the graph stands for the states with its marking, its name layer and clock values in its firing domain; the zones (DBM), the name-symbol quotient and the canonical key are not modelled (gap R6 of Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean: the gated successor compute_successor_gated is the shipped code, its Lean model is open). Names are the values the key projections read (NU-001), not abstract symbols; that the quotient keeps the gate is Novel.RouteB.nameEnabled_comp. The witness RefRouteBT is that semantics: strong urgency on delays (a delay may not take a clocked, ν-enabled transition past its latest bound), clocks only on ν-enabled transitions, a clock kept across a firing only when its transition is ν-enabled before, in the intermediate marking and after and is not named as the fired one, and a fresh clock for every other transition ν-enabled after the firing, which is compute_successor_gated with is_enabled and name_enabled as the gates (state_class_graph.rs, name_state_class_graph.rs). A firing of the model is a reference ν firing RefNuFire (the selected name, FIFO takes elsewhere); the graph's free choice of a shared name and of a consumer's resident name (clash nu-b#3) are VER-012's, and every line is stated for the label's own chosen name and intermediate marking. Time is in whole milliseconds, as the executor's clock (TSt.now).
- 'Enabled with an eligible name' in the quoted sentences is NuEnabled ([NU-020], [NU-022]): enabled on the counts and some name eligible, which for a transition without a match is enabled on the counts. 'No name present in every correlated input at the count its arc requires' is ¬NuShared, one way of not being ν-enabled; a matched join whose names are shared but whose counts fail (an empty non-correlated input, a marked inhibitor) is not enabled with an eligible name either, so it holds no clock (line 1) and a clock judged in such an intermediate marking restarts (line 2). 'Another transition' is a transition with a different name, as compute_successor_gated tells the fired transition apart. The intermediate marking is rbtMid: the correlated takes of the chosen name and the drained reset places for a matched transition, the queue consume otherwise, as TIME_012_nu's NuMid on the executor side. Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. Line 2 is the second: its fresh clock is line 2 and its taking away, when the firing leaves j not enabled, is line 1. Line 3 is the third, line 4 the fourth. Line 5 is the fifth, again with the taking away carried by line 1. Line 6 is the sixth, line 7 the seventh. A clock that held a stamp before a firing and is enabled after it is fixed by lines 2, 3 and 5; one that held none by line 4; one not enabled after by line 1; so every firing fixes every stamp.
- The lines speak of every transition of the net, matched or not. For a transition without a match they are the clock rules of TIME-012 read on Route B's relation; they are stated here because the TIME_012 block constrains the executor relation, not RBTRel, and the graph-side persistence rule of VER-010 (Novel/TimedScg/Run.lean) speaks of the un-named graph.
- The body's 'a firing after which no name is present in every correlated input restarts the join's clock' is read on the intermediate marking (line 2), as compute_successor_gated judges it (the intermediate name layer as the gate between) and the executor does (TIME_012_nu, flag_clock_restarts on the live marking): a deposit only adds tokens, so a firing after which no name is shared left none shared in its intermediate marking either, and line 2 then restarts the clock (or, with line 1, leaves none); line 2 also restarts a clock when the firing takes the shared name out and puts it back. The lines speak of steps; the initial class is not gated in the shipped graph (initial_state_class), which is harmless because Route B starts with every coloured place empty (refusal step 7 of NU-055), so no join is enabled on its counts there.
- The eighth quoted sentence is the quantification over every timed ν net: the relaxed net of TIME-013 (Timing.relaxLate, the graph built by reaping::relax_late when the caller does not assume an on-time executor) is one, so the lines hold of it too; NU_050_timed_ac3 runs one net both ways.
- The body sentences 'On a timed net Route B gives a matched join a clock only while one name-symbol is present in every correlated input, because the executor enables the join only then ([NU-020]).' and 'The clock-restart rule of [TIME-012] reads the name layer too: a firing after which no name is present in every correlated input restarts the join's clock, even when the inputs still hold tokens, and a join whose inputs come to share a name starts a fresh clock then.' are restated by the EARS sentences (lines 1 to 5). The executor half ('because the executor enables the join only then') is NU-020's: every firing of RefRouteBT is a RefNuFire firing from a marking at which its transition is ν-enabled (nu050t_fire_executor), and the executor's own clock rule is the TIME_012_nu block. The sentence 'A join whose inputs hold tokens but share no name has no clock, so its latest bound constrains no other firing.' says what the semantics offers, so it is a coverage predicate (RBTCovers: time may pass while every clocked, ν-enabled transition stays within its latest bound, and every clocked, ν-enabled transition past its earliest bound fires), not a line; RefRouteBT meets it (NU_050_timed_covers_reference) and the empty relation, which meets every line, does not (nu050t_coverage_excludes_empty). Strong urgency itself (a delay never takes a clocked transition past its latest bound) is not a line here: it is the timed semantics of VER-010, which Route B carries unchanged.
- AC3 is NU_050_timed_ac3: on the AC3 net, on time and with the relaxation, the join never holds a clock and the watchdog marks BAD at 10 ms, so a sound Route B reports unreachable(BAD) violated; under the count-gated clock of the graph before the fix the join holds a clock with latest bound 5 and time cannot pass to 10 ms (nu050t_countClock_ac3), the graph-level witness of which is Novel.TimedScg.name_disabled_join_escapes (cited as nu050t_old_graph_escapes). For any relation meeting the lines and RBTCovers the same run exists: the join holds no clock (line 1), the watchdog's clock starts at 0 ms and is kept (lines 3, 4 and 6), RBTCovers offers the 10 ms delay and the watchdog's firing. AC4 is NU_050_timed_ac4: the join is count-enabled from 1 ms, first shares a name at 5 ms, gets its clock then, cannot fire at 14 ms and can at 15 ms; under the count-gated clock it fires at 11 ms (nu050t_countClock_ac4). That the join cannot fire before 15 ms holds of every relation meeting the lines, not only of the reference: nu050t_ac4_of_statement (a 9 ms delay keeps the stamp 5 by line 6, and line 7 refuses the firing at 14 ms). Both ACs are run against the shipped Route B by fixture tests (kind Q), since its timed successor is gap R6.
- Modelled injection, environment places and the deadline reaps of the executor ([TIME-013]) are not steps of the relation: Route B reads environment places as VER-006 AC8 says, and accounts for a late executor by the relaxed net instead of reaps.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_050_timed_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_050_timed): Route B's timed semantics keeps the seven lines. Take a join whose inputs A and B both hold name 1. A step after which the join is not enabled leaves it without a clock, because a clock is only kept or given to an enabled transition. When another transition fires and the join is not enabled in the intermediate marking, it cannot keep its clock, so it gets the current reading if it is enabled after the firing. A join that is enabled before, in the intermediate marking and after keeps its stamp. A join without a clock that is enabled after a firing gets the current reading, and so does the join itself after it fires. Time passing keeps the marking and the stamps and moves the clock on, and the join fires only once its clock has run its earliest bound.
  <pre>∀ {N V Nm : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : LinearOrder Nm],<br>  NU_050_timed RefRouteBT</pre>

## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051` · Kind **F** · Scope the fragment classifier of every ν verifier · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 909c7a7142f57771 ai** · Statement hash `909c7a7142f57771`

**Assumptions**

- The classifier is per transition, as the glossary term Fragment classifier reads it: no role for one transition means the net falls back to the sound over-approximation ([NU-050]); the Rust `classify` (rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_fragment.rs) returns no fragment for the net as soon as one transition is refused. The coloured set is an argument. How a verifier builds it is not a line here: the match keys are the glossary's, the declared carriers under EXTENDED (and their absence from the set under BASE) are the block NU_051_colours, and the relay targets are [NU-054]'s. So every line speaks of the places coloured in the mode at hand: a place coloured only by a declared carrier or a relay target is not coloured under BASE, where the coloured set is the match keys alone.
- The first paragraph of the section is not a line. Its sentence 'Both are decided by the solver-free Route B quotient, and by Route A where [NU-053] is offered' (clash nu-c#1, reworded under ruling D20 (a), item 1 of nu-c NC-8) says which routes decide the two modes: that is the route dispatch, Route B's soundness being the block NU_050_soundB and Route A's EXTENDED admission [NU-053]'s subject (Rust name_coloured_encoder.rs builds the consume rows under EXTENDED). The two-value knob, BASE as the default and its builder option names are configuration (kind N); the key format is [VER-012]'s subject.
- Line 1 is the first quoted sentence. It is the BASE half of AC1 for a fixture whose consumed place is coloured under BASE, that is a match key of the net (the coloured place a mint feeds): a consumer of a place coloured only by an EXTENDED carrier or relay target consumes no coloured place under BASE, gets an ordinary role there, and the net is not refused on its account. Whether a given fixture's place is coloured in each mode is the coloured-set computation (for carriers, the block NU_051_colours). Line 2 is the second quoted sentence (the prose: 'The analyzer' takes such a transition 'only as a drain/relay role and only when it consumes exactly one coloured input at count exactly one'; 'A consumer that consumes more than one coloured place, or consumes at any count other than one (`Exactly(n≥2)`, `AtLeast`, `All`), is rejected') and AC2, and its last conjunct is the third quoted sentence and the Route B half of AC8: a timeout write into a coloured place that is a unit token or a forward of another input leaves the transition with no role. Its first conjunct (SingleColouredWrites: every branch puts exactly one token into each coloured place it writes, and no drained batch, a forward from an `All` or `AtLeast` input whose count is read off the marking ([IO-014]), into one) is the clause 'puts on each branch exactly one token, and never a drained batch' of the second quoted sentence. The markdown gives it only as the reason for refusing higher input counts ('the base marking adds exactly one token per output place, so re-emitting a higher input cardinality into the name layer would over-count'); the shipped classifier refuses on it (`classifyT`, the branch check), and so does the line.
- Line 3 is the fourth quoted sentence and the EXTENDED half of AC1: the role is given, not only allowed (the markdown's 'MAY consume' is a permission to the net author; the classifier that the author relies on then has to give the role). Its premises are the sentence's conditions one for one: one coloured input at count one, no test arc on a coloured place (line 4), one token and no drained batch per coloured place a branch writes (SingleColouredWrites, as in line 2), and only forwards of that input on timeout (ForwardsOnly, as in line 2). A transition that builds has SingleColouredWrites whenever its coloured timeout writes forward its one coloured input: an output branch names a place at most once ([IO-011]), and that input is consumed at count one, so its forward deposits one token. The model takes the branches and the timeout writes as two separate arguments, so the line states the premise.
- The mint declaration plays no part in lines 1 to 3 and 6, which hold for both values of declared; the role sentence says so ('whether or not it is declared a mint'). This agrees with [NU-010], whose mint writes a coloured place without consuming one: a declared transition that consumes a coloured place is a consumer here, and the mint rule (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint) is [NU-010]'s verifier line, not this block's.
- 'Because the consumed count is fixed at one, the role is identified by the input place name alone' is encoded by lines 2 and 3, which fix the role to `consume s.place`: Role.consume carries a place and nothing else.
- Line 4 is the fifth quoted sentence and AC3. The prose says the analyzer rejects a net in which 'any coloured place carries' such an arc 'on any transition'; per transition that is line 4, and the net falls back because one of its transitions gets no role. Its reason ('it never turns a `Proven`/`Violated` into an unsound verdict') is [NU-050]'s soundness, not a line.
- Line 5 is the sixth quoted sentence and the first half of AC7. 'A non-coloured non-key input (a budget or permit) is unaffected' is not a line: line 5 speaks only of coloured inputs, and NU_051_nonvacuous shows a join with an uncoloured budget input that gets its join role. The second half of AC7 ('a stranding such a net can reach is not reported `Proven`') is not a line: it is a consequence of line 5 (the off-key join gets no role, so the net is outside the fragment) and of the soundness of the route the net falls back to (the sound over-approximation, [NU-050]; a Route B `Proven` holds of the executor only inside the fragment, the block NU_050_soundB). Its Route A half ('no coloured plan') is the plan refusal of the Route A encoder, which no Route A classifier here abstracts. The fixtures are Q-tested: Rust nu_scg_verifier.rs join_consuming_a_coloured_place_off_key_is_not_in_fragment (Route B) and name_coloured_encoder.rs join_consuming_a_coloured_place_off_key_is_rejected (Route A).
- Line 6 is the seventh quoted sentence, the converse of lines 1 to 3: the coloured-consumer role exists only under EXTENDED ('BASE reproduces the shipped mint → matched-join fragment exactly'), only for 'a transition with **no** match spec' (a matched transition takes a name by its match test, [NU-020], not by the consumer step), and only for a transition that consumes a coloured place (the relay step removes the name 'from its coloured input'). With line 2 it pins down every transition the role is given to.
- The relay and drain semantics ('A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch ... or drains it ... on a branch that produces no coloured output') is the block NU_051_relay. AC6 (MAY: one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is permitted by lines 2 and 3, which do not depend on the branches: the fixture of NU_051_nonvacuous is such a consumer, and NU_051_relay_nonvacuous relays on one branch and drains on the other.
- The relay/drain action precondition is an assumption on the net author (kind A), not a line: the action threads the consumed name into its coloured outputs, or into none, and never mints a fresh name while consuming a coloured token. No analysis can check it. It enters Route B as the consumer contract of the name step (`Novel.RouteB.Contract`, under which `name_step_simulates_exec` holds), the premise of [NU-050]'s soundness (the block NU_050_soundB). 'MUST be documented as such' is a documentation duty (kind Q). 'the report of a verdict names the consumers whose action writes it assumes' is a report line (kind N, Q-tested): every runtime writes 'Relay contract (NU-051) assumed for' followed by the coloured consumers into the report of a call that uses the fragment (Rust name_fragment.rs contract_note, Java NameFragment.java, TypeScript name-fragment.ts), and a coloured Route A verdict ends with 'The verdict assumes the mint and relay contracts named above' (Rust smt_verifier.rs apply_nu_guard).
- The carrier bullet is two other blocks of this ID (NU_051_carrier.lean). That under EXTENDED the coloured set roles are given against is the set with no carrier declared plus the declared carriers, nothing more, and that under BASE the carriers leave it unchanged, is the block NU_051_colours. A declared carrier that is not a place of the net fails loudly in both modes and for every query, naming only missing carriers (ruling D95 (a), clash nu-c#2), which is AC4 and the block NU_051_carrier; Every runtime refuses an absent carrier in both modes and for every query: Rust judges the declaration on the caller's net in SmtVerifier::verify (unknown_declaration_reason, which calls name_fragment::unknown_carrier_reason) and answers that refusal before any route runs, verify_open_net refuses it before either route, and Python answers as Rust and raises from script encoding. A check only under EXTENDED inside Route B, which loses the refusal when Route B defers to Route A, is the behaviour RD-27 recorded, and NU_051_carrier forbids it. That a declaration of places the net has is accepted in either mode is the coverage clause Nu051CarrierCovers next to that block.
- The diagnosability bullet (the 'EXTENDED declined' note: a report line saying that the exact ν path was not taken and why, in words the implementation chooses) is a report line (kind N, Q-tested). Clash nu-c#10 is settled by ruling D20 (a), item 4 of nu-c NC-8, which pins no fixed string. Rust (rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs) asks Route B for a name-alignment property and for a net with a matched transition whose property is a quiescence property or that declares no budget place. When the classifier declines there under EXTENDED, the report carries the EXTENDED_DECLINE note ('ν-net Route B (EXTENDED) declined: net outside coloured-consumer fragment (...)') followed by 'verified via sound over-approximation instead', or, when an undeclared mint is what keeps the net out, 'ν-net Route B declined:' naming the undeclared mints ([NU-010]); for a name-alignment property the note is the reason of the Unknown verdict (name_alignment_decline). A Route B truncation that defers to Route A is not a decline: the report says 'ν-net Route B inconclusive (name-partition truncated); deferring to Route A' and prints no EXTENDED note. On a net with a budget place and a reachability-safety property Route B is not asked: Route A builds its name-coloured plan only inside the fragment (coloured_attempt), and outside it the report carries no EXTENDED note, only the ν guard's note that matched transitions are over-approximated pending the exact ν-analysis (apply_nu_guard), which says the exact path was not taken but not why. The tests: Rust tests/nu_join_relay chain_without_the_declaration_falls_back and a_join_timeout_write_into_a_relay_target_must_forward_a_key, tests/nu_name_alignment nu055_outside_the_extended_fragment_the_verdict_is_unknown_and_no_other_route_is_named, Java JoinRelayTest fig12c_withoutTheRelay_extendedDeclines and aJoinTimeoutWriteIntoARelayTargetMustForwardAKey, Python tests/test_nu_join_relay.py test_a_join_timeout_writing_a_relay_target_without_a_key_is_declined; each is a quiescence query.
- AC5 (SHOULD: an end-to-end quiescence verdict on a carrier fixture, Proven with the drain and Violated without it, attributable to Route B) is a verdict and report line, kind Q: Rust nu_scg_verifier.rs extended_carrier_comint_drain_in_fragment and smt_verifier.rs extended_deadlock_free_proven_with_drain_via_route_b and extended_deadlock_free_violated_without_drain_via_route_b over comint_carrier_drain_net, and Java FragmentExtensionTest. The carrier set it relies on is the block NU_051_colours, the fragment it relies on lines 3 and 6, and the soundness of its Proven the block NU_050_soundB.
- AC8's executor half (with the minting forks m1, m2, the consumers r1, r2 and a join on KA and KB, the executor reaches done and `placeBound(done, 0)` is not `Proven`) is not a line: it is a consequence of line 2's last conjunct (a consumer whose timeout forwards another input into a coloured place gets no role, so the net is outside the fragment) and of the soundness of the route the net falls back to ([NU-050], the block NU_050_soundB for Route B). The fixture is Q-tested: Rust rust/libpetri/tests/nu_mint_contract a_consumer_timeout_forwarding_another_input_is_not_a_relay (the executor reaches done, neither route proves placeBound(done, 0), Route B does not answer), Java NuMintContractTest aConsumerTimeoutForwardingAnotherInputIsNotARelay_routeB and _routeA, TypeScript typescript/tests/verification/nu-mint-contract.test.ts. Its Route A half ('rejected on both routes') is Novel.RouteA.shipped_consume, cited by NU_051_routeA_consume (Route A builds no consume row for such a consumer, Rust name_coloured_encoder.rs), and is not a line: the timeout sentence speaks of the fragment classifier, which is the Route B classifier this block abstracts, and Route A's admission of the EXTENDED fragment is [NU-053]'s subject. Its last sentence ('A consumer whose timeout forwards its coloured input is still a relay') is line 3 with a forward of the consumed input, shown in NU_051_nonvacuous.
- AC2's 'no false `Proven` from an over-counted name layer, no dropped base-enabled firing' is the soundness the refusal buys ([NU-050], the block NU_050_soundB); the block states the refusal.
- Whether a transition is a mint (declared, and writing no coloured place on timeout) is [NU-010]'s verifier line (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint), not this block's.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_051_carrier"></a>
## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier` · Kind **F** · Scope every ν verifier entry point that takes carrier declarations · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 7a1b1a4383e15a26 ai** · Statement hash `7a1b1a4383e15a26`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A refusal that does not depend on the carrier declaration, such as a stop before the call starts ([VER-013]), an unresolved property place ([VER-003]) or a declared mint that is not a transition of the net ([NU-010]), may come first, and that refusal is then the answer.<br><br>*If* a declared carrier place is not a place of the net, *then* the verifier *shall* either reject the declaration, naming such a place, or answer `Unknown` with a reason that names at least one such place and no other place, in both BASE and EXTENDED and whatever the query, unless the same request with no carrier place declared gets the same refusal. | 1. For every query type Q, routes D, ν configuration cfg, net and query q: if some declared carrier of cfg is not a place of the net, the verifier built on D either rejects the declaration naming a declared carrier that is not a place of the net, or answers Unknown with a reason that names at least one place, every place it names being a declared carrier that is not a place of the net; or its answer is a refusal (a rejection or an Unknown, CarrierRefusal) and the same call with no carrier declared gets that same answer (CarrierEscape). | <pre>fun {Q} P ↦<br>  ∀ (D : CarrierVerifier Q) (cfg : NuConfig) (net : CarrierNet) (q : Q),<br>    (∃ p, AbsentCarrier cfg net p) →<br>      LoudRefusal cfg net (P D cfg net q) ∨ CarrierEscape P D cfg net q</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D95 (a) decides the mode question of clash nu-c#2: an absent carrier fails in every mode, not only when a query reaches Route B. AC4 had no mode and the body said carriers are ignored under BASE; the markdown now says 'in either fragment mode and whatever the query', and the BASE sentence speaks of the fragment classifier only (NU_051_colours, line 2). D95 (a) reads 'at configuration, in every mode'; only its 'in every mode' half is a line. The line also accepts `Unknown` from verify, which the markdown has always allowed ('reject at the builder, or surface `Unknown`'), so the 'at configuration' half is deliberately not enforced: where the refusal is made is configuration (kind N, below), and Rust's verify-time `Unknown` meets it.
- Java (SmtVerifier.carrierPlaces) and TypeScript (SmtVerifier.carrierPlaces) reject the declaration where it is made, in both modes, naming the place (NU_051_carrier_builder). Rust and Python answer `Unknown` in both modes and for every query: SmtVerifier::verify judges the declaration on the caller's net before with_arrivals (unknown_declaration_reason in rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs) and verify_net answers that refusal before any route, and verify_open_net refuses a configure_smt hook's absent carrier before either route (open_net/verify_open_net.rs); the reason names every absent carrier once, in code-point order (unknown_carrier_reason in name_fragment.rs; NU_051_carrier_allAbsent). Route B keeps its own check for direct callers (nu_scg_verifier.rs verify_name_scg). A wrong shape that checks only under EXTENDED and only inside Route B ignores an absent carrier under BASE, under EXTENDED on a call that does not reach Route B, and under EXTENDED on a bounded quiescence query that Route B defers to Route A, whose build_plan skips a carrier it cannot resolve; that is the behaviour RD-27 recorded, and NU_051_carrier_forbids_routeBOnly (BASE) and NU_051_carrier_forbids_routeADeferral (EXTENDED) forbid it.
- Order of refusals: the line does not fix which refusal wins when the carrier refusal meets one that does not depend on the carrier declaration; it asks only that such a refusal be the answer the same call gets with no carrier declared (CarrierEscape). Rust's verify_net polls the stop on entry ('net preparation'), then refuses an unresolved property place ([VER-003]), and only then answers the declaration refusal, in which unknown_declaration_reason tries the mint reason of [NU-010] before the carrier reason; verify_open_net and Python's py_encode_smt_scripts also put the mint reason first, and SmtVerifier::encode_scripts panics for a name-alignment property ([NU-055]) before it reads the declarations. On such a call the answer names no absent carrier. Java and TypeScript throw where the declaration is made, so a carrier rejection comes before any verification runs, and a mint rejection comes first only when the mint was declared first. CarrierPipeline does not model the stop, the property or the mints; they are part of the query q and of the net. preCarrierVerify takes the refusals that do not read the carrier declaration as a parameter pre and answers them first, naming no place, then answers as the Rust form: it meets the line through the escape (NU_051_carrier_preRefusal), and the line without the escape rejects it (NU_051_carrier_escape_needed), which is why the markdown carries the clause. The order inside pre, and so which of several such refusals wins, is not modelled.
- What the escape lets through: any refusal the same call with no carrier declared also gets, so a verifier whose routes answer Unknown to every call meets the line. What the line forbids is a Proven or a Violated while a declared carrier is absent, and a refusal that the carrier declaration changes but that does not name an absent carrier alone (NU_051_carrier_forbids_unnamed, NU_051_carrier_forbids_firstDeclared, NU_051_carrier_forbids_namesAll).
- A verifier is modelled as a function of its routes (CarrierPipeline): the line quantifies over the routes D, which is the reading of 'MUST NOT be silently ignored' and of 'whatever the query': no Proven and no Violated while a declared carrier is absent, whatever a route would answer. A verifier that hands the call to its routes unchanged answers what they answer (NU_051_carrier_forbids_ignore). A route that refuses by itself, as Rust's Route B does, is part of the verifier here, so the Route-B-only shape is the pipeline routeBOnlyCarrierVerify, with the queries that reach Route B and the ones deferred from it to Route A as its parameters.
- The answer is abstract: the verdict ([VER-003]) and the places its reason names, or a rejection naming a place. Which form an entry point takes (an exception where the declaration is made, Unknown from verify, Python's keyword path through Rust) is configuration (kind N), as for the declared mints of [NU-010]. The reason text ('declared carrier place 'x' not in the net (NU-051)' in Rust, 'declared carrier place 'x' not in the net' in TypeScript, 'declared carrier place 'x' is not in the net' in Java) is kind Q, and so is the tie between that text and the places the answer says it names. 'naming the offending place' is read as: the reason names at least one absent carrier and no other place. Java and TypeScript throw at the first absent carrier, and Rust names every absent one; when several are absent, which of them are named is not fixed (one, as Java and TypeScript do, or several, as Rust does and as [NU-010] names every unknown mint). Naming a declared carrier that is a place of the net is wrong, alone (NU_051_carrier_forbids_firstDeclared) or beside an absent one (NU_051_carrier_forbids_namesAll).
- The first sentence of the bullet ('Under EXTENDED, an author MAY declare intermediate **carrier** places (`carrierPlaces` / `carrier_place(s)`) that carry a fresh name from the minting fork ([NU-010]) onward to a ν-join input.') is an offer, and the API names in it are kind N. Offers are coverage clauses, never block lines (the convention of GlossaryExec.lean): the clause is Nu051CarrierCovers, defined next to this block, which the added sentence 'In either fragment mode, a declaration whose carrier places are all places of the net is accepted.' states: when every declared carrier is a place of the net, the carrier guard hands the call to its routes unchanged. The reference and the builder form meet it (nu051c_ref_covers, nu051c_builder_covers); a guard that refuses a present carrier under BASE, or in every mode, meets the line and fails the clause (nu051c_covers_baseRefuses, nu051c_covers_refusesAll). The clause speaks of the guard, not of the whole verifier, since under BASE the in-flight split of [VER-004] still reads the carriers (NU_051_colours assumes). The MAY sentence says 'Under EXTENDED', but declaring under BASE is allowed too: the declaration is a no-op for the classifier there (NU_051_colours, line 2), the clause covers it, and the line checks it.
- The reason the sentence gives ('a mistyped carrier would let two fork branches mint independent names and produce a confident, spurious deadlock verdict') is the co-mint fixture of NU_051_colours_nonvacuous, where the carrier is what makes the fork and the relay share one name.
- The open-net entry points ([VER-022], [MOD-051]) take the carriers through the configure hook on the synthetic net: the line applies to that call with the synthetic net as its net. Script encoding ([VER-013]) refuses an absent carrier too: Rust panics with the reason (SmtVerifier::encode_scripts), Python raises ValueError (py_encode_smt_scripts in rust/libpetri-py/src/verification.rs), and Java and TypeScript reject at the declaration. Its answer is scripts or a failure, not a verdict, so it is not one of the pipelines here; a line over it would take NU_010_ac6's MintAnswer form (an open item). AC4 is this line: its builder rejection names the place, as its `Unknown` does, and its 'unless a refusal that does not depend on the declaration is the answer' is the escape.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): The carrier guard satisfies the carrier line in front of any routes: when a declared carrier is missing it answers `Unknown` naming the first missing one, and only that one, whatever the routes would say.
  <pre>∀ {Q : Type}, NU_051_carrier refCarrierVerify</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_allAbsent` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✓ Naming every absent carrier meets the carrier line: the reason names at least one place, and every place it names is an absent carrier.
  <pre>∀ {Q : Type}, NU_051_carrier allAbsentCarrierVerify</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_builder` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✓ The builder rejection of Java and TypeScript meets the carrier line too: declaring a place the net does not have throws, naming it, in either mode.
  <pre>∀ {Q : Type}, NU_051_carrier builderCarrierVerify</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_preRefusal` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✓ Rust's order meets the carrier line: an earlier refusal that does not read the carrier declaration is the answer the same call with no carrier declared gets (the escape), and otherwise the Rust form names every absent carrier.
  <pre>∀ {Q : Type} (pre : CarrierNet → Q → Option String), NU_051_carrier (preCarrierVerify pre)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_forbids_firstDeclared` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: with carriers `2` and `7` declared on the co-mint net, naming `2`, which is a place of the net, points the author at the wrong declaration.
  <pre>¬NU_051_carrier nu051c_firstDeclared</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_forbids_ignore` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: a verifier that ignores a carrier declaration it cannot resolve answers `Proven` on the co-mint net with the mistyped carrier `7` when its routes do, a confident verdict about a net in which the declaration did nothing.
  <pre>¬NU_051_carrier nu051c_ignore</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_carrier_forbids_namesAll` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: with carriers `2` and `7` declared on the co-mint net, a reason that lists both, "declared carrier places 2, 7 not all in the net", does name the missing `7`, but it also names `2`, which is a place of the net, and leaves the author to find which of the two is wrong.
  <pre>¬NU_051_carrier nu051c_namesAll</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_051_colours"></a>
## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours` · Kind **F** · Scope the coloured set every ν verifier computes for a call · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 c7e191c148c2ba43 ai** · Statement hash `c7e191c148c2ba43`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the fragment mode is EXTENDED, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles against the coloured set it uses with no carrier declared, with every declared carrier place added and no other place.<br><br>*While* the fragment mode is BASE, the fragment classifier *shall* give roles against the same coloured set whatever carrier places are declared. | 1. For every list of declared carriers cs, net and place p:<br>2. under EXTENDED, p is coloured with cs declared exactly when p is coloured with no carrier declared or p is in cs;<br>3. under BASE, the coloured set with cs declared is the coloured set with no carrier declared. | <pre>fun C ↦<br>  (∀ (cs : List PlaceId) (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (p : PlaceId),<br>      C Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended cs net p =<br>        (C Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [] net p \|\| cs.contains p)) ∧<br>    ∀ (cs : List PlaceId) (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans),<br>      C Novel.RouteB.Mode.base cs net = C Novel.RouteB.Mode.base [] net</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The coloured set is per call, as the glossary term Coloured place reads it ('The classifier computes the coloured set for each call'); the role each transition then gets from it is the block NU_051 (refClassify takes the coloured set as its argument). 'The analyzer unions the declared carriers into the coloured set before role assignment' is line 1 with that composition: line 1 says the EXTENDED set is the union of the set without carriers and the carriers, nothing more and nothing less, and the classifier reads that set. A set that colours a further place once a carrier is declared breaks line 1 (NU_051_colours_forbids_footprint). 'so the existing mint co-mints one fresh name into all of them' is shown, not stated: NU_051_colours_nonvacuous classifies a fork that writes a key and a declared carrier as a mint of both under EXTENDED, while under BASE the consumer of the carrier writes the key without consuming a coloured place, the shape of a second, independent mint.
- Line 2 speaks of the classifier's coloured set only. The in-flight split of [VER-004] reads the declared carriers in both modes (it refuses to split a transition that writes one: in_flight.rs first_unsplittable, InFlight.firstUnsplittable in Java, firstUnsplittable in TypeScript, each called without the mode), which the edited sentence 'Under BASE, the fragment classifier ignores declared carriers (a documented no-op); the in-flight split of [VER-004] reads them in both modes.' says, and which VER-004 states ('a match key, a relay target or a declared carrier'). So no line says a whole verifier answers the same with and without carriers under BASE: the split can refuse where it would not without them.
- The match keys and the relay targets in the set are the glossary's (Coloured place; [NU-020], [NU-054]), not lines here: the lines fix what the carriers add and take away, relative to the set with no carrier declared, and say nothing of that set itself. So a set that colours every place in both modes, or one that under EXTENDED colours the declared carriers alone and drops every match key, meets both lines; they break the glossary's coloured set (the match keys, and under EXTENDED the relay targets), which no block states as a line: the verifier pipeline model (Verifier/Pipeline.lean, the block VER_003) does not model how a ν verifier builds the coloured set. That set is Q-tested: Rust name_fragment.rs extended_colours_relay_targets_and_the_join_carries_them and a_relay_target_no_join_consumes_is_coloured_and_its_read_arc_rejects (under EXTENDED a relay target is coloured, also one no join consumes), name_coloured_encoder.rs extended_carrier_relay_admitted_only_under_extended and a_relay_target_no_join_consumes_is_coloured_and_produced_by_the_join (the same set in Route A's plan), and Java NuNameAlignmentTest nu055_ac5_theBugVariantClassifiesOnlyWithTheMatchlessGateLifted (under EXTENDED every declared carrier is coloured and an undeclared place is not). refColourSet reads a relay target only on a matched transition, as Rust does (relays come from the match spec). A declared carrier that is not a place of the net joins the set as a name no transition touches; what the verifier does about it is the block NU_051_carrier.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): The coloured set `classify` builds is, under EXTENDED, the set it builds with no carrier declared plus the declared carriers, and under BASE it does not read the carriers.
  <pre>NU_051_colours refColourSet</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_forbids_carriersAlways` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: a verifier that colours a declared carrier under BASE changes the BASE fragment, which is the shipped mint → matched-join fragment, by a declaration BASE ignores (line 2): with `2` declared, `2` becomes coloured under BASE.
  <pre>¬NU_051_colours nu051c_carriersAlways</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_forbids_footprint` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: on the co-mint net with the carrier `2` declared under EXTENDED, a set that also colours what the fork consumes colours the budget `5`, which is neither a declared carrier nor coloured without the declaration. The budget would then be read as a name-carrying place, and the fork as a consumer of it rather than a mint (line 1: the carriers are added, nothing else).
  <pre>¬NU_051_colours nu051c_footprint</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_forbids_keysOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): ✗ Worked example: a verifier that drops the carrier declarations under EXTENDED leaves the declared carrier `2` uncoloured, so the fork and the relay of the co-mint fixture would each mint their own name (line 1).
  <pre>¬NU_051_colours nu051c_keysOnly</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_mutant_holdsOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): The footprint set kills the weakened reading: it holds every declared carrier and leaves BASE alone (the mutant holds), but colours the budget `5` once the carrier `2` is declared.
  <pre>NU_051_colours_mutant_holdsOnly nu051c_footprint ∧ ¬NU_051_colours nu051c_footprint</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_mutant_noBase_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): Reading the carriers in both modes kills the second mutant: EXTENDED is the shipped set (the mutant holds), but BASE changes with the declaration.
  <pre>NU_051_colours_mutant_noBase nu051c_carriersAlways ∧ ¬NU_051_colours nu051c_carriersAlways</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_mutant_noExtended_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): Ignoring carriers in both modes kills the first mutant: BASE is untouched (the mutant holds), but a declared carrier is uncoloured under EXTENDED.
  <pre>NU_051_colours_mutant_noExtended nu051c_keysOnly ∧ ¬NU_051_colours nu051c_keysOnly</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_colours_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051_carrier): Worked example. A fork `m` writes the join key `0` and the place `2`; `r` moves the token from `2` to the other join key `1`. With `2` declared a carrier under EXTENDED, `2` is coloured, so `m` is one mint writing the same fresh name into `0` and `2`, and `r` relays that name from `2` into `1`: the join sees one name on both keys. Under BASE the declaration changes nothing, `2` is not coloured, and `r` writes the key `1` without consuming a coloured place, which is the shape of a mint of its own (a second, independent name) and gets no role unless declared.
  <pre>refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [2] nu051c_net 2 = true ∧<br>  refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [] nu051c_net 2 = false ∧<br>    refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.base [2] nu051c_net 2 = false ∧<br>      refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.base [2] nu051c_net 0 = true ∧<br>        refClassify (refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [2] nu051c_net)<br>              Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended true [] nu051c_fork =<br>            some Novel.RouteB.Role.mint ∧<br>          refClassify (refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [2] nu051c_net)<br>                Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended false [] nu051c_relay =<br>              some (Novel.RouteB.Role.consume 2) ∧<br>            refClassify (refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended [2] nu051c_net)<br>                  Novel.RouteB.Mode.extended false [] nu051c_join =<br>                some (Novel.RouteB.Role.join [(0, 1), (1, 1)] []) ∧<br>              refClassify (refColourSet Novel.RouteB.Mode.base [2] nu051c_net)<br>                  Novel.RouteB.Mode.base false [] nu051c_relay =<br>                none</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_051_relay"></a>
## NU-051: EXTENDED Coloured-Consumer Fragment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay` · Kind **F** · Scope the name layer of Route B · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 14c65885d2d499bd ai** · Statement hash `14c65885d2d499bd`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a coloured consumer fires on a branch with a name its coloured input holds, the name layer *shall* remove one token of that name from the input, add one token of that name to each coloured output of the branch and change no other count, so a branch with no coloured output drains the name. | 1. For every list co of distinct coloured places, consumed input inp, list outs of distinct coloured outputs of the fired branch, consumed name s resident in inp and name marking M, and for every name u and coloured place i: the step's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is inp, equals M's count of u at i, plus one if u is s and i is in outs. | <pre>fun S ↦<br>  ∀ (co : List PlaceId),<br>    co.Nodup →<br>      ∀ (inp : PlaceId) (outs : List PlaceId) (s : ℕ) (M : Novel.RouteB.NM co),<br>        outs.Nodup →<br>          1 ≤ Novel.RouteB.cnt co M s inp →<br>            ∀ (u : ℕ) (i : Fin co.length),<br>              (S co inp outs s M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] = inp then 1 else 0) =<br>                M u i + if u = s ∧ co[↑i] ∈ outs then 1 else 0</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The step is the name layer of Route B (`Novel.RouteB.NM`: the tokens of each name in each coloured place); which transition gets the coloured-consumer role is the block NU_051. The step is applied to a name resident in the consumed input (Route B's `will_fire` for a consumer), hence the premise that s has a token in inp, which the sentence states as 'with a name its coloured input holds'. Which resident name a consumer takes (any, on Route B; the oldest, FIFO, in the executor) is not this line's: it is the action contract and [NU-050]'s soundness; the outputs are the coloured places of the fired branch, without repetition (`colOut`), hence the premises on co and outs.
- The line is the quoted sentence, which restates 'A coloured consumer relays the consumed name-symbol into each coloured output of the fired branch (threading the same name), or drains it (dead-letters the name) on a branch that produces no coloured output'. A relay back into the consumed input leaves its count as it was, which the equation allows. That the name the action writes is the consumed one is the action contract (kind A, see NU_051): this line says what the name layer does, the contract is why that matches the executor ([NU-050], W9).
- AC6 (one `Xor` consumer relays on one branch and drains on another) is this line with outs the coloured outputs of each branch; NU_051_relay_nonvacuous applies it to one branch with a coloured output and one with none. The other acceptance criteria are the block NU_051's subject, which accounts for each.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The Route B consumer step satisfies the relay line: it removes one token of `s` from the input (`removeAt_apply`, the name is resident) and adds one to each output (`foldl_add_apply`).
  <pre>NU_051_relay refConsumerStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_forbids_keepInput` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): ✗ A consumer step that does not take the name out of its input violates the relay line.
  <pre>¬NU_051_relay nu051_keepInput</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_forbids_remint` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): ✗ A consumer step that re-mints violates the relay line: relaying name `0` from `0` into `1` leaves no token of `0` in `1`.
  <pre>¬NU_051_relay nu051_remint</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_mutant_relayOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The step that leaves the consumed token in its input kills the relay-only mutant: it adds one token of the name to each output (`foldl_add_apply`), so it meets the mutant reading, but the relay line asks the input to lose the token (`NU_051_relay_forbids_keepInput`).
  <pre>NU_051_relay_mutant_relayOnly nu051_keepInput ∧ ¬NU_051_relay nu051_keepInput</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_051_relay_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_051): The relay line bites on the Route B step: name `0` is resident in place `0`; the branch that writes the coloured place `1` moves it there (relay), the branch with no coloured output leaves no token of it (drain), and no other name gains a token.
  <pre>1 ≤ Novel.RouteB.cnt [0, 1] nu051_M 0 0 ∧<br>  refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨0, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>      0 ∧<br>    refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>        1 ∧<br>      refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [] 0 nu051_M 0 ⟨0, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>          0 ∧<br>        refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [] 0 nu051_M 0<br>              ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>            0 ∧<br>          refConsumerStep [0, 1] 0 [1] 0 nu051_M 1<br>              ⟨1, of_decide_eq_true (id (Eq.refl true))⟩ =<br>            0</pre>
