## NU-052: Conflict-Only Priority for the Route B Name-SCG

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_052` · Kind **F** · Scope the Route B successor step, under CONFLICT and NONE · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ce33b84a192a3bb8 ai** · Statement hash `ce33b84a192a3bb8`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* leave a base-enabled transition `L` unexpanded from a class exactly when another transition `H` of the net pre-empts `L` in that class, and *shall* expand every other base-enabled transition of the class as under `NONE`, in the same order.<br><br>*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take two transitions `H` and `L` to compete in a class exactly when some place is a consumed input of both and its token count in the class marking is less than the sum of their demands on it, where a transition's demand on a place is the sum of the required counts ([IO-007]) of its input arcs on that place.<br><br>*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* expand each base-enabled transition of a class, in the class's clock order (the code-point order of the transitions' names, [VER-010] AC1), with the successors the transition has when it is expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer, *shall* expand no other transition, and *shall not* read the readiness, in-flight state or competition of any transition.<br><br>*While* the mode is `NONE`, the Route B graph *shall* give a base-enabled transition at least one successor labelled with its name when the base layer can fire one of its branches in the class and the transition will fire on the name layer (always for an ordinary or minting transition, with an enabling name for a join, with a resident name for a consumer). | 1. Let E be the Route B expansion and C the competition test.<br>2. For every net whose transition names are distinct, every base layer whose competition is C read on the count marking κ of the class, and every class: the CONFLICT successors of the class are its NONE successors, in order, without those labelled with the name of a transition L of the net that some transition H of the net pre-empts in the class (glossary: Pre-empt, read as PreEmpts over the base layer's enabled, readyLe, idle and compete and the will-fire test of H's role).<br>3. For every count marking a and transitions H and L: C a H L holds exactly when some input arc of H is on a place that is also the place of an input arc of L and holds fewer tokens in a than the sum of H's and L's demands on it, a transition's demand on a place being the sum of the required counts of its input arcs there (demandOn over Card.required: 1 for One and All, n for Exactly(n) and AtLeast(n)).<br>4. For every base layer, every class and every net whose transitions are listed in the code-point order of their names: the NONE successors of the class are, in that order, the NONE successors each base-enabled transition T has when the step is given T alone (the net [T]), from the same class and the same base layer.<br>5. For every two base layers that agree on enablement and firing: the NONE successors of every class are the same under both.<br>6. For every base layer, class and transition T that is base-enabled, has a branch the base layer fires in the class, and whose role will fire on the class's name layer (willFire): the NONE successors of the class in the net [T] include one labelled with T's name. | <pre>fun {β} E C ↦<br>  (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β) (κ : β → AMarking)<br>      (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)<br>      (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>      (∀ (b : β), base.compete b = C (κ b)) →<br>        (List.map (fun T ↦ T.base.name) net).Nodup →<br>          E co base net role true c S =<br>            List.filter<br>              (fun x ↦<br>                !decide<br>                    (∃ L ∈ net, L.base.name = x.1 ∧ ∃ H ∈ net, PreEmpts base role S H L))<br>              (E co base net role false c S)) ∧<br>    (∀ (a : AMarking) (H L : Transition),<br>        C a H L = true ↔<br>          ∃ sh ∈ H.inputs,<br>            (∃ sl ∈ L.inputs, sl.place = sh.place) ∧<br>              a sh.place &lt;<br>                Novel.RouteB.demandOn H sh.place + Novel.RouteB.demandOn L sh.place) ∧<br>      (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>          (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)<br>          (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)<br>          (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>          List.Pairwise (fun T U ↦ T.base.name &lt; U.base.name) net →<br>            E co base net role false c S =<br>              List.flatMap (fun T ↦ E co base [T] role false c S)<br>                (List.filter (fun T ↦ base.enabled S.b T.base) net)) ∧<br>        (∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base base' : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>            (net : List Novel.RouteB.NuTrans)<br>            (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role) (c : ℕ)<br>            (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>            base'.enabled = base.enabled →<br>              base'.fire = base.fire →<br>                E co base' net role false c S = E co base net role false c S) ∧<br>          ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (base : Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer β)<br>            (T : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans) (role : Novel.RouteB.NuTrans → Novel.RouteB.Role)<br>            (c : ℕ) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β) (d : Novel.RouteB.Row),<br>            base.enabled S.b T.base = true →<br>              d ∈ T.rows →<br>                (base.fire S.b T.base d).isSome = true →<br>                  Novel.RouteB.willFire co (role T) S.m S.bound = true →<br>                    ∃ x ∈ E co base [T] role false c S, x.1 = T.base.name</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (E, C). E is one expansion of a class of the name-aware state-class graph of Route B ([VER-012]): the coloured set, the base layer (Novel.RouteB.BaseLayer: enabled, fire, readyLe, compete and idle), the net with its roles, the mode (true for CONFLICT, false for NONE), the mint counter and the class give the labelled successors, each labelled with the name of the transition that fired. The witness is refExpand, the shipped step Novel.RouteB.succ (name_state_class_graph.rs build_until). C is the competition test on a class's count marking; the witness is refCompete, Novel.RouteB.sharesConsumed (shares_consumed_input). The step reads competition through the base layer (as in Graph.lean), so line 1 is stated for the base layers whose compete is C read on the class's count marking κ; that is what makes C the graph's competition and not a separate function. The untimed base is such a layer, with κ the identity (nu052_untimedBase_compete). The timed base, whose count marking is the marking of the timed class, is not in the model (gap R6, the open item of VER_012); a base layer whose compete is not of this form is a wrong base layer, not a wrong graph, and is not this requirement's subject: that the base layer of a Route B call reads competition by line 2 is the companion block NU_052_split, line 7, which a base layer reading a demand as the tokens one firing consumes breaks (NU_052_split_forbids_consumedBase). The pruning predicate itself is the glossary term Pre-empt; its shipped form is refPrune (GlossaryNuVer, refPrune_iff).
- The first quoted sentence is line 1. 'Exactly when' restates the body's 'is not expanded from a class when' together with the soundness paragraph's 'The pruning removes only interleavings in which a lower-priority transition fires ahead of a ready, conflicting, strictly-higher-priority one': under CONFLICT the graph prunes and does nothing else. 'Another transition' is read as another name: the line is stated for nets whose transition names are distinct, because the shipped step labels successors with names and compares H and L by name (name_state_class_graph.rs:587, `h.name() != l.name()`). Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, with D23 settling that distinct names are one shared assumption for every name-keyed requirement), so the premise is that assumption and the quoted sentence needs no narrowing. Outside it, on a net where two transitions share a name, the Rust prune never lets one pre-empt the other, while the Java and TypeScript prunes compare by identity (NameStateClassGraph.java:402, name-state-class-graph.ts:336) and do; D10 puts that net out of scope, so the case is not encoded.
- Line 1 reads every bullet of the body through the glossary term Pre-empt: strictly higher priority, competition (the base layer's compete, line 2 on count markings), ready no later than L (the base layer's readyLe), no firing in flight (the base layer's idle) and 'actually fires in this class' (willFire of H's role: a join needs an enabling name, a consumer a resident one, so a name-disabled join pre-empts nothing). H ranges over the base-enabled transitions of the class, as the body's 'another enabled transition H in the same class'. 'Actually fires in this class' is read on the name layer, as the body's own gloss ('a name-disabled join, whose inputs carry no shared name, produces no name-successor') and the shipped prune (dominated reads will_fire and no firing of the base) do; whether H has a branch the base layer can fire is not part of it. On the untimed base every enabled transition fires. On a timed base, H ready no later than L (readyLe) makes H firable whenever L is, and when L is not firable pruning it removes no successor; that this holds of the timed readyLe is the timed base's subject (gap R6).
- The second quoted sentence is line 2, for every cardinality. Ruling D97 (a) (clash nu-c#3) reads a demand as the required count of [IO-007], what all three runtimes compute (consumed_demand over required_count in name_state_class_graph.rs, consumedDemand in NameStateClassGraph.java and name-state-class-graph.ts) and the Lean model's demandOn: 1 for All and n for AtLeast(n), not the tokens one firing consumes. The body's bullet says so too. The tokens-consumed reading competes on more pairs (two All arcs on a place with two tokens), so it would prune more; the required count prunes a subset and stays sound (ClashesNu.clashNu_demand, cited). A test with the tokens-consumed reading breaks line 2 (NU_052_forbids_consumed), as does one that gives up on a pair over an All or AtLeast arc on a place only one of them consumes from (NU_052_forbids_wholePair). 'Read and inhibitor arcs do not count' is line 2's 'consumed input of both': only input arcs occur in it.
- The body's 'becomes ready no later than L by the class-relative residual earliest: the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock captured before time is let to pass (readyEarliest, parallel to the enabled set)', the comparison within a float epsilon, and the sentence '*While* the mode is `CONFLICT`, the Route B graph *shall* take `H` to be ready no later than `L` in a class exactly when `readyEarliest[H] <= readyEarliest[L]` within a float epsilon, where `readyEarliest` is the DBM lower bound of each enabled clock before time is let to pass.' are a timing line over a timed base layer, as are the body's claims that a static H.earliest() <= L.earliest() does not suffice, that the rule subsumes the immediate-H case and that it also prunes sound non-zero-earliest conflicts. The base layer here is abstract (readyLe); its timed instance needs the timed class of RefScg (VER-010), so this sentence is not encoded here; the timed base layer is gap R6 (the open item of VER_012). On the untimed base every transition is ready at once (untimedBase.readyLe is true).
- The third quoted sentence is lines 3 and 4. It restates 'The default mode, NONE, MUST reproduce the prior Route B behaviour byte-for-byte' with the first paragraph's 'it expands every base-enabled transition': line 3 says no transition's NONE successors depend on another transition, that they come in the class's clock order and that a transition not base-enabled adds none, so NONE prunes nothing by priority; line 4 says NONE reads none of the base layer's readyLe, idle and compete, the inputs only the prune reads.
- 'In the class's clock order': the runtimes walk a class's enabled transitions in the class's canonical clock order, ascending transition name in code-point order ([VER-010] AC1; the Rust, Java and TypeScript name-state-class graphs walk the base class's enabled list, which the state-class graph permutes into canonical order when it builds a class). The model's step walks the net list it is given, so line 3 is stated for a net listed in that order (the Pairwise premise), and the model's list order is then the runtimes' order on every class. A net listed in another order is the same net handed to the step in another enumeration; line 1's 'in the same order' compares CONFLICT with NONE on one enumeration and needs no premise.
- 'Expanded alone from the same class and the same base layer' is the net [T] with the class and the base layer unchanged. The base layer is the class's own: the base successor of T is computed over the whole net (its clocks, enabled set and readyEarliest, state_class_graph.rs compute_successor_gated), and in the model that whole-net computation is inside base.fire, which line 3 does not vary, so [T] is not the net holding T alone. The minted symbols are compared up to the canonical key of the class ([VER-012] AC2): the runtimes thread one mint counter across the expansions of a class and across classes (name_state_class_graph.rs next_sym), while line 3 passes the same counter c to every transition, so the raw symbol numbers of the runtimes agree with the model only after interning.
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 5. It is the least that 'expands' says of one transition: a transition that fires on both layers yields a successor labelled with its name, so an expansion that yields nothing is ruled out (NU_052_forbids_empty). The will-fire condition is the body's name-disabled join, which 'produces no name-successor', read the other way. Which successors one transition yields, all of them and byte for byte, is VER-012's subject, so 'the prior Route B behaviour' is not stated as a fixed function here.
- Which mode the verifier hands the step is outside the step, and is the companion block NU_052_split (ruling D97 (a), clash nu-c#4): it says to which calls conflict priority applies (none on a net with a transition read as reapable, [VER-002]; a name-alignment call on a net without a ν-join included), and that every other call is verified as under NONE. The lines here hold for whatever mode the step is given.
- The paragraph 'In-flight actions' (split every pruner and every transition depositing into an input or read place of a pruner, never let H pre-empt while inflight:<H> is marked, the NONE verdict naming the transition when one cannot be split, the pruning kept under assumeAtomicFiring) is the companion block NU_052_split, over the verifier's setup of a call and the in-flight test of the base layer; the split itself is VER_004_split. What this block keeps of it is the in-flight guard as the base layer's idle in line 1; NU_052_split line 6 says that idle is the count of inflight:<H> being 0. 'A direct call to Route B ... applies no split and prunes as before' is this block: the step prunes by line 1 whatever net it is given.
- The paragraph 'Soundness' (the pruned firings are ones the eager, priority-ordered executor never performs; L is re-examined after H fires) relates the graph to the executor. It is descriptive (it carries no shall or MUST) and is not stated as a line: that needs a reference executor with a priority-ordered ν pass and actions in flight, and RefExec has neither priorities nor a ν kernel (a gap of the reference model; VER_004_exec, the executor link of the split, leaves priorities out too). A line would also have to list EXEC-003 AC4 (a ν-join that received a same-pass deposit fires no earlier than the next cycle). Ruling D8 (b) makes re-entrancy implementation-defined, so the Java and TypeScript wording of the in-flight case stays. Its evidence is cited, not stated: the retrodictions Libpetri.willFire_guard_is_necessary and Libpetri.inFlight_guard_is_necessary (Priority.lean) show, on the untimed fragment with a boolean name layer, that the prune without each guard drops a firing the executor performs and the shipped prune keeps it. Libpetri.postFixPrune_agrees_with_executor (Priority.lean) is true by construction and is no evidence for it.
- The option names prioritySemantics / priority_semantics, that CONFLICT is opt-in and that an implementation MAY omit it are configuration, not encoded.
- AC1 (NONE is the default and the only mode an implementation MUST provide; NONE leaves every existing Route B verdict unchanged) is lines 3, 4 and 5 for the step: NONE expands each base-enabled transition on its own, reads nothing the prune reads and gives every transition that fires a successor. The default and the verdicts are configuration and VER-012's graph; not encoded beyond that.
- AC2 (the fork-threaded co-mint plus immediate ν-join plus delayed lower-priority drain fixture: Violated under NONE, Proven under CONFLICT on Route B called directly and under assumeAtomicFiring; through verify() with the split on, the NONE verdict and a report note) needs the timed base (a delayed drain) and the verdict, which are not encoded here; its pipeline half (the join cannot be split, so the call is verified as under NONE and the report names the join) is NU_052_split line 5 (NU_052_split_ac2). Its step-level core, that under CONFLICT the join's competitor is pruned when the join pre-empts it, is line 1 (NU_052_nonvacuous on the untimed base).
- AC3 (no over-pruning: a genuine orphan, whose join is name-disabled, still reaches its drain) is line 1's will-fire condition. The Route B retrodiction of commit c23cd9e (Novel.RouteB.WF: a priority-10 join whose keys hold two different names and a priority-0 drain competing for one token) is the evidence: the pre-fix prune without the will-fire guard stalls the class (NU_052_forbids_preFix), and the shipped step keeps the drain's edge (NU_052_orphan_not_pruned). The verdicts Violated without a drain and Proven with one are VER-012's graph and are not encoded here.
- AC4 (only consumed-input conflicts prune; a read or inhibitor arc on the shared place creates no conflict) is line 2 (NU_052_forbids_reads, NU_052_nonvacuous).
- AC5 (a delayed(100) ν-join still pre-empts a delayed(200) lower-priority drain, so DEADLETTER is unreachable under CONFLICT and reachable under NONE) is the residual-earliest comparison over a timed base and a verdict, not encoded here (gap R6). Line 1 keeps the readiness condition (NU_052_forbids_noReady).

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (M, B). M : NuSetupFn K is with_in_flight with conflict_pruning_applies (rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs, SmtVerifier.applyInFlight and conflictPruningApplies in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java, the same pair in typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts; Python rides Rust). Its result is what the rest of the pipeline should read of the mode: the split configuration handed to the in-flight split of [VER-004], whether Route B prunes, and the transition the conflict-off note names. The runtimes read it so everywhere, the Route B environment check of VER-006 AC8 included: that check is handed CONFLICT only where conflict priority applies and NONE otherwise (smt_verifier.rs:1365-1369 and :4158, SmtVerifier.java:1737 and :3193, smt-verifier.ts:1500 and :3042). A pipeline that handed it the selected mode instead, the behaviour RD-39 recorded in spec/runtime-defects.md, would make Route B decline on a call that conflict priority does not apply to because a transition is read as reapable, when an environment place under AlwaysAvailable or Bounded(k) has two consumers, and answer Unknown where the NONE call gives the Route B verdict, against line 2 and against AC8's 'Otherwise its verdict stands'. NuSetupFn does not model that check, so no Lean model shows it. The witness refNuSetup is the [VER-004] plan refSplitPlan told whether conflict priority applies (nu052sApplies), so VER_004_split decides what the configuration does to the net, and this block decides when conflict priority applies, what the call hands on and what it reports. B : InFlightBase is the untimed base layer of Novel.RouteB with the in-flight place of each name given (ifl); the witness refInFlightBase is untimedBase with idle reading ifl and compete the test refCompete of NU_052.
- The call's shape is NuSplitCall: the four booleans conflict_pruning_applies reads (is_name_alignment, a transition with a match spec, is_reachability_safety, a declared budget place). Read as reapable is nu052sReapable: some transition has a Deadline or Window timing and assumeNoReaping is not set, as Verifier.refNet reads the reapable flags ([VER-002], reapable_set). Two overrides of that set are not modelled: a caller that passes its own reapable set to the Route B reaping entry (verify_via_name_scg_reaping, NuScgVerifier.verifyReaping, verifyViaNameScgReaping), and the verifier-level set the open-net route of [VER-022] names for a net whose timing a rewrite is about to drop (SmtVerifier::reapable_transitions in smt_verifier.rs, set at open_net/smt_route.rs:120; reapableOverride at SmtVerifier.java:905; _reapable at smt-verifier.ts:202). On that route the transitions read as reapable are the named ones, not the Deadline and Window transitions of the net handed on.
- The first quoted sentence is line 1. 'The QuiescentCount demand alone' is what VER_004_split line 5 hands on without conflict priority: cfg with the places of a QuiescentCount property counted as tested, and no pruner forced. A NONE setup that forces the pruners would make the NONE call refuse the split of the AC2 shape and answer Unknown instead of the NONE verdict, against AC1 (NU_052_split_forbids_noneDemand). With line 1, 'what it hands them under NONE' in line 5 is ver004WithCount cfg φ with the pruning off. The second sentence is lines 2 and 4 with 3 and 5: 'exactly when' is line 2 for the calls it does not apply to, which are the NONE call, and lines 3 to 5 for those it applies to. 'Conflict priority applies' is the condition (nu052sApplies), not the outcome: line 5 verifies an applying call as under NONE, as VER-004's 'While conflict priority applies' reads it. Ruling D97 (a) widens the body's 'whenever it applies CONFLICT on a net with a ν-join' to every call conflict priority applies to: a name-alignment call on a net without a ν-join is split too, as all three runtimes do (NU_052_split_forbids_joinOnly). The reapable exception is [VER-002]'s 'It does not prune by priority ([NU-052]) on a net with a reapable transition.', which NU-052 now states as well (clash nu-c#4; NU_052_split_forbids_reapBlind). Route B also turns CONFLICT into NONE itself when it is handed a non-empty reapable set (nu_scg_verifier.rs verify_via_name_scg_reaping, NuScgVerifier.java pruningOff, nu-scg-verifier.ts pruningOff), so the verifier's test and Route B's agree; that inner switch-off is not a separate line. A direct call to Route B passes it an empty set and prunes on any net, which is NU_052 line 1.
- The third quoted sentence is line 3. Which net is verified under assumeAtomicFiring (the net itself) is VER_004_split line 1; the report line stating the atomic assumption (atomic_assumption_note_for) is report text, kind N. Lines 3 and 4 also say that no transition is named: keeping conflict priority on writes no conflict-off note, since the runtimes write it only when they turn the pruning off (conflict_off in smt_verifier.rs with_in_flight, off in SmtVerifier.applyInFlight, conflictOff in smt-verifier.ts applyInFlight).
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 4. 'Split every pruner and every transition that deposits into an input or read place of a pruner' is the configuration handed on: ver004WithConflict forces every pruner (ver004Pruners, conflict_pruners: strictly higher priority than another transition that shares an input place with it) and counts its input and read places as tested, and VER_004_split lines 2 to 4 split exactly the forced transitions and those with an output place that is tested, except the environment steps and the completion steps, which Split.splitB leaves atomic even when forced; that is the sentence's 'except a transition that models an environment or is a completion step'. A pruner is read by input places, whatever the cardinality and the token count, as the body's parenthesis has it; line 7 then decides which pruners compete in a class. 'The net has no pruner' covers a net with no conflict at all, where the demand adds nothing and the pruning stays on (Rust's reasons.conflict is false, so nothing is switched off).
- The fifth quoted sentence is line 5. 'What it hands them under NONE' is the NONE setup N, configuration and mode, so every route reads what it reads under NONE and the verdict is the NONE verdict (nu052s_verdict_none); a setup that hands on the bare configuration instead forgets the QuiescentCount demand (NU_052_split_forbids_bareOff). The note names the first transition, in net order, that the split under the conflict demand refuses (first_unsplittable; conflict_off_note). 'Unless the split under NONE is refused too' is the case where a transition the split under N's configuration splits for another reason is a ν-join or a coloured writer: the call then answers Unknown with the refusal of [VER-004], whose reason opens with the first transition that split refuses, and all three runtimes drop the conflict-off note (smt_verifier.rs with_in_flight, InFlight::Refused calls f(verifier, None); SmtVerifier.java applyInFlight, Outcome.Refused sets only inFlightRefusal; smt-verifier.ts applyInFlight, the refused branch sets only _inFlightRefusal), so line 5 names no transition there (NU_052_split_forbids_noteKept, NU_052_split_ac2). That report is VER_004_split's line 3 and VER-003's line 4. The text of the note is kind N.
- The sixth quoted sentence is line 6, the in-flight bullet of the body's 'MUST NOT let H pre-empt anything while inflight:<H> is marked': with line 1 of NU_052 (Pre-empt reads idle), a transition whose in-flight place holds a token pre-empts nothing (NU_052_split_nonvacuous, the reference keeps L expanded while H is in flight). All three runtimes read it on the class marking (priority_dominated in name_state_class_graph.rs, NameStateClassGraph.java, name-state-class-graph.ts). Line 6 is stated for every naming ifl, so it holds for the naming the split uses: the place inflight:<H> is SplitCfg.inflight of the configuration line 4 hands on (in_flight_place), and that the Route B call is given that naming is how the runtimes build the call, not a further line. On a net without in-flight places the place holds nothing and the guard has no effect, which is the body's last sentence. B is the untimed base; the timed base reads the same count on the timed class's marking, and its readyLe is the open timed base of NU_052 (gap R6).
- The seventh quoted sentence is NU_052's second, read here as line 7 on the base layer of a call. NU_052 line 2 states it of the competition test C, and NU_052 line 1 speaks only of base layers whose compete is C; line 7 says the base layer of a Route B call is such a layer, with C the required-count test, so a base layer whose competition reads a demand as the tokens one firing consumes (consumed_demand through the firing count instead of required_count) breaks this block although it meets NU_052 (NU_052_split_forbids_consumedBase). B is untimed; that the timed base reads the same test on the timed class's marking is gap R6.
- The body's 'A direct call to Route B (Rust verify_via_name_scg, TypeScript verifyViaNameScg) applies no split and prunes as before' is NU_052 line 1: the step prunes by Pre-empt on whatever net and mode it is given. 'Two cases break the pruning' (a feeder of H in flight leaves H disabled; H in flight is not started again by Java and TypeScript) is why the split is needed; that the split net over-approximates the executor with actions in flight is VER-004's block B, VER_004_exec (VER_004_exec.lean), and whether a transition starts again while in flight is ruling D8 (b), implementation-defined, under which the split is sound either way.
- AC1's 'NONE MUST leave every existing Route B verdict unchanged' is, for the setup, line 1: under NONE the split gets what it got before conflict priority existed. AC2's pipeline half (through verify() with the split on, the join cannot be split, the verdict equals the NONE verdict and the report says conflict priority is off) is line 5 (NU_052_split_ac2); its verdicts are Route B's (NU_052, VER-012). AC7's split half (H and its feeder t are split, and under assumeAtomicFiring nothing is and the pruning stays on) is line 4 and line 3 (NU_052_split_ac2, VER_004_split_ac7); a pruner in flight pre-empting nothing is line 6. AC3 to AC6 and the test derivation are NU_052's; AC6 on the base layer of a call is line 7.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_052_split_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_052_split): The reference meets the companion block. Worked example of why: under `NONE`, `refNuSetup` tells the [VER-004] plan that conflict priority does not apply, so the plan hands on the `QuiescentCount` demand alone, prunes nothing and the setup names nothing (line 1); when conflict priority does not apply, `CONFLICT` tells the plan the same thing (line 2); otherwise the plan adds the conflict demand and keeps the pruning on (lines 3 and 4) unless the split under it refuses a transition, when the plan hands on the `NONE` configuration with the pruning off and the setup names that transition, or nothing if the `NONE` split is refused too (line 5). **Assumptions**

- The model is the tuple (B, K, U, V). B is a function of the flat net as the shipped build_plan sees it: the place count, the coloured places (sorted, duplicate-free flat indices below the place count), the flat rows (Transition × Deposit, Novel.ForwardDeposit) and the initial count marking. A weighting is handled scaled to integers, a vector Y and a denominator D standing for y = Y / D, as check_cover takes it (slot_bound_lp.rs; Novel.RouteA.checkCover); 'y_p ≥ 1' is Y_p ≥ D and '⌊y·M0⌋' is ⌊Y·M0 / D⌋. A covering weighting at k is Novel.RouteA.ScaledCover at k. The column C_t of a flat transition is post − pre with pre the required count and a timeout outcome counting its deposit (dotIncD), and a reset or consume-all place may carry weight (no H1; SlotBound.lean, 'No H1'); the token-sum bound holds anyway (coloured_tokens_le). U is a relation between the colour columns before and after one rule, so it carries the rule's guard as well as its update; V is the violation term on one encoding state.
- Line 1 is the first quoted sentence and the body's '`k` is `⌊opt⌋`, where `opt` is the least `y·M0` over all such weightings' (ruling D80 (d)): k is certified by a covering weighting and no smaller bound is. 'The optimum is unique, so every implementation computes the same `k`' is NU_053_unique: two bounds that meet NU-053 agree wherever both answer. 'When no weighting exists (the program is infeasible) ... the plan is refused' is NU_053_infeasible. The simplex itself is not modelled: the witness is the least certified bound by classical choice (refColourSlotBound), not an execution of the solve.
- Line 2 is the second quoted sentence, which this migration adds so that a bound that never answers does not conform: on a net that meets Nu053Fits a bound is set whenever a covering weighting is within the cap, and by line 1 it is then the least one (NU_053_answers_least). The sentence after it in the markdown gives the reason the normative solve meets it: Bland's rule never returns to a basis, so it makes fewer than C(n+m, n) pivots of work at most (2n+1)·(n+m+1) each, and a tableau entry in lowest terms is a ratio of two minors of the initial tableau, each at most (n+1)!·E^(n+1) by the Leibniz expansion; the optimal weighting the solve reads off is an exact optimum, which passes the re-check below the cap. Every case of spec/verification-fixtures/slot-bound-lp.json that meets Nu053Fits is optimal or infeasible, and the coefficient-limit and work-limit cases do not meet it. Line 2 kills a bound that never answers (NU_053_forbids_never), one that treats k = 0 as a fallback (NU_053_forbids_zeroFallback), one with a narrower cap (NU_053_forbids_byteCap) and one that answers only integer optima (NU_053_forbids_integerOnly). On a net that does not meet Nu053Fits, whether the solve reaches a limit is the normative solve's, kind Q. A stopped solve ([VER-013]) ends the query with the stop, so B reads a solve that is not stopped.
- Lines 3 and 4 are the third and fourth quoted sentences and the body's 'uses its weighting only after an exact re-check in arbitrary-precision arithmetic' with ruling D80 (a) (clash nu-c#6): the re-check also refuses a bound above 2^31 − 1 (slotCap), as every runtime does (slot_bound_lp.rs SLOT_CAP, SlotBoundLp.java, slot-bound-lp.ts). 'A weighting that fails the re-check is discarded and the plan is refused; it never sets `k`' is line 3 for the bound: no k is set without a weighting the re-check accepts with that bound. That the accepted weighting is the one the solve returned (the shipped colourSlotBoundLP binds the solve's answer to checkCover) is not stated, because B does not expose the weighting it read: a refusal of the solve's own weighting while another weighting would pass is the normative solve's and the fixture's (kind Q), and on a net that meets Nu053Fits line 2 already forbids refusing the plan. The re-check's shape guard on the length of Y (one entry per place) has no counterpart, Weight being total; it only refuses more. Each condition of line 4 is load-bearing: a re-check without the cap (NU_053_forbids_noCap), without the coloured condition (NU_053_forbids_noColouredCheck), without non-negativity (NU_053_forbids_noNegCheck), without the row condition (NU_053_forbids_noRowCheck), without D > 0 (NU_053_forbids_noPosDCheck) or with the ceiling for the floor (NU_053_forbids_ceilCheck) is killed.
- Line 5 is the fifth quoted sentence and the paragraph on the update of a coloured consumer: the rule for colour c is enabled only with colour c resident in the input (its '>= 1' guard), emits '(- x 1)' for the input column and '(+ x 1)' for each coloured output column, and has no update term for a self-loop column, which keeps its guard and is carried over unchanged, as a join's key that is also a relay target is ([NU-054]). U ranges over the colour columns only: the uncoloured columns of the rule (AC7's tick and tock) are the uncoloured update uFire, not this line. Natural subtraction at a zero column does not arise under the guard. The shipped encoder emits exactly this rule (NU_053_consumer_shipped, Novel.RouteA.colourStep_consume_shipped). The old write order, in which the output's '+ 1' overwrote the input's '− 1' on a self-loop, is killed (NU_053_forbids_oldConsumer) and was a live wrong Proven (Novel.RouteA.self_loop_consume_false_proven); a rule without the guard is killed too (NU_053_forbids_noGuard).
- Line 6 is the sixth quoted sentence and the quiescence bullet as reworded by ruling D80 (a) (clash nu-c#5): the quiescence of [VER-002], read colour-aware, for each quiescence property (DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink, JoinedOrDeadLettered, QuiescentCount), each conjoining its own clause Q over the all-colour counts (agg). Q is a parameter: NU-053 fixes the colour-aware quiescence term and that the clause is read over the all-colour counts, not which clause each property has. The clauses of DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink and QuiescentCount are VER-002's lines 1, 2 and 6 without their quiescence conjunct; JoinedOrDeadLettered and its clause, which has no sink clause ([NU-040] AC4), are NU-040's: the block NU_040_jodl fixes the one predicate every route that decides it reads, with no sink clause (NU_040_jodl_forbids_sinkClause), over queue markings. No line ties the coloured violation of each property here (Q, a parameter) to its clause, so on the coloured encoding 'so `JoinedOrDeadLettered` carries no sink clause' has no Lean line. A transition is reapable when its name is in R, the set the verifier hands the encoders (VER-002's reap-aware reading; empty under assumeNoReaping). Disabled 'for an uncoloured reason' is uDisabled: an uncoloured input below its demand, a marked inhibitor or an empty read place; 'for every colour' is colDisabled: a mint finds no globally-fresh colour, a join no colour on every key, a consumer no colour on its input. A row that touches no coloured place has no colour reason (colDisabled of class untouched is False), so it is disabled only for an uncoloured reason, also at k = 0. A strict quiescence that ignores R (NU_053_forbids_strict; Novel.RouteA.ReapW.reaping_breaks_routeA_quiescence) and a count-level quiescence that reads the all-colour counts instead of the colours (NU_053_forbids_countLevel) are killed.
- The bullet on the EXTENDED fragment ([NU-051]: coloured consumers, relay or drain, and declared carrier places, each consuming exactly one coloured input at count one) is the fragment classifier of NU-051 (refClassify, the NU_051 block). The bullet 'classifies each XOR output branch independently by its own incidence' is build_plan's classification of each flat row (Novel.RouteA.ClassShape, buildPlan in Plan.lean); no block states it as a line, and the Lean fact is buildPlan itself. 'The encoding has no environment-injection rule, so it does not answer when injection is modelled ([VER-006] AC7)' is the pipeline's decline under injection, line 3 of the NU_053_dispatch block.
- The bullet on the structural bound restates line 1 and its soundness: 'every reachable marking has Σ_{coloured} M ≤ y·M ≤ y·M0' is NU_053_tokens_le (Novel.RouteA.coloured_tokens_le), and its dual reading (the largest coloured token count of the state equation M = M0 + C·σ over the reals) is LP duality, not encoded. The examples of the bullet (a budget place that gates minting yields a weighting, a refund to a non-minting place keeps the minting budget covering, a leaky co-mint fan-out yields none) are instances of line 1. 'A relay threads its colour onward and still MUST NOT refund' is not a check of its own: a relay that refunds the minting budget leaves the program infeasible, so by line 1 no plan is built (NU_053_relayRefund, mint: budget → a and relay: a → a2, budget), while a relay that refunds to a place that does not mint keeps the program feasible and the plan built (NU_053_otherRefund, k = 1). '`k = 0` is a bound like any other ... the zero-slot plan is exact rather than a fallback' is NU_053_zero_exact (Novel.RouteA.vacuous_colour_layer_lp) with line 2: a bound of 0 is set, not refused (NU_053_ac6).
- The paragraph 'The solve is normative' (the presolve, the tableau, Bland's rule, the weighting read off the slacks, the limits of 4096 places and 16384 rows, the work limit 'it MUST NOT exceed 4000000', the coefficient limit 'MUST have numerator and denominator in lowest terms at most `2^63 − 1` in absolute value' and the order of each round) fixes which nets every implementation refuses and with which pivots. It is kind Q: the shared fixture spec/verification-fixtures/slot-bound-lp.json pins each case's status, pivots, work, presolved sizes, optimum, k and weighting for every implementation (ruling D80 (d)). Line 2 is the one consequence of it stated here. The six report lines, 'colour-slot bound k=<k>' and the stop that prints no line are report text (kind N).
- The paragraph on the dispatch (Route B first, deferral to the coloured plan on a Route B Unknown, a verdict of the coloured plan not downgraded, its Proven sound while the declared mints and coloured consumers keep their contracts) and the paragraph on the [VER-015] linear bound running before the coloured query are verdict and pipeline lines. The dispatch is the NU_053_dispatch block (Route B never after the colour-slot bound and, on a quiescence query, entered before it, the hand-over of Route B's Unknown, the coloured verdict not downgraded, no Proven from the fallback on a quiescence property), and the order against the linear bound is VER_015_order. The soundness line needs the reference ν executor: it is stated over RefNuReach (design ruling S7 (a)) with NU-050. The current evidence for the soundness is Novel.RouteA.routeA_safety_sound_plan and routeA_quiescence_sound_reaping, relative to the Route A ν step (RouteA.NuStep).
- AC1 (a budget-bounded EXTENDED ν-net whose only quiescent marking holds sink tokens is Proven deadlock-free via the coloured Route A encoding) and AC2 (removing the drain turns it Violated) are verdicts of the coloured plan: the quiescence term they read is line 6, the dispatch that hands a truncated Route B over to the coloured plan and passes its verdict on is the NU_053_dispatch block, and the verdicts come with the soundness line (NU_050_soundA) and the test fixtures (kind Q).
- AC3 (Route A and Route B agree on every small fixture both decide) is differential testing, kind Q.
- AC4 (a net with no covering weighting falls back rather than a false Proven; a refund to a non-minting place stays bounded) and AC5 (a leaky co-mint fan-out falls back) are line 1: with no scaled cover at any k the bound answers nothing (NU_053_infeasible). The relay that refunds the minting budget is NU_053_relayRefund (no plan) and the refund to a place that does not mint is NU_053_otherRefund (lines 1 and 2: every bound that meets NU-053 answers 1). The fallback itself is the pipeline's: without a plan the fixpoint query never proves a quiescence property of a net with a ν-join (NU_053_dispatch line 6).
- AC6 (an optimum below one yields the exact plan with k = 0) is lines 1 and 2: on the fork that consumes exactly(3) budget tokens from one budget token, optimum 2/3, every bound that meets NU-053 answers 0 (NU_053_ac6), and the zero-slot plan is exact (NU_053_zero_exact). That quiescence is then decided, never downgraded to Unknown as a name-blind verdict would be, is NU_053_dispatch line 5 (the coloured verdict is not downgraded); that the emitted encoding is well-formed with zero colour slots is the scripts' (kind Q). The remark that an exactly(2) fork refunded by a join has optimum 1 and that an infeasible program is still refused are instances of line 1.
- AC7 (the self-loop consumer `spin: a, tick → a, tock` lets placeBound(tock, 0) be Violated) is line 5: the consumer's self-loop column is carried over under its guard, so `spin` can fire; the old update that kept only the '+ 1' is killed (NU_053_forbids_oldConsumer). The verdict itself comes with the soundness line (NU_050_soundA).
- AC8 (k is the floor of the optimum, identical in every implementation, never larger than the bound of any covering non-negative P-semiflow) is lines 1 and 2 with NU_053_unique and NU_053_le_semiflow: on the exactly(3) fork with a budget of 7, optimum 14/3, every bound that meets NU-053 answers 4 (NU_053_ac8), where every integer cover gives at least 7 (NU_053_forbids_semiflow, NU_053_forbids_integerOnly). The scatter-gather numbers (k = 4 against 10) and that encodeScripts() emits k without a solver ([VER-013] AC1) are fixture checks, kind Q.
- AC9 (a weighting is used only after the exact re-check; a negative weight, a weight below one on a coloured place, an increasing transition or a bound above 2^31 − 1 refuses the plan with the re-check report line; a reset or consume-all arc on an uncoloured place does not refuse the plan by itself) is lines 3 and 4 with their mutants. Its example (mint: budget → a, b, join: a, b → budget and cancel: r → r2 with a reset arc on budget, from {budget: 2, r: 1}) has k = 4 in every bound that meets NU-053 (NU_053_ac9_reset, lines 1 and 2; the reset place carries weight, no H1). The report line text is kind N.
- The test derivation (a co-mint to join net Proven deadlock-free via Route A while its name-partition graph truncates; an EXTENDED drain-steal net Violated; the routes agreeing on the no-stall net) is AC1 to AC3 with the dispatch (NU_053_dispatch: NU_053_dispatch_nonvacuous shows the hand-over from a truncated Route B to the coloured Proven); its scatter-gather k = 4 is a fixture check (kind Q), its exactly(3) fork with k = 0 is NU_053_ac6 and its reset arc that keeps the plan is NU_053_ac9_reset.

## NU-053: EXTENDED-Coloured Quiescence in the Route A SMT Encoder: Place in the Dispatch

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch` · Kind **B** · Scope the dispatch of the SMT verifier on ν-nets, where the coloured encoding of Route A is offered (MAY; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers it) · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 65c74b30c6cdb983 ai** · Statement hash `65c74b30c6cdb983`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a dispatch D: a list of pipeline steps (GStep of Spec/Verifier/Pipeline.lean) over a NuCall, run by runPipeline, as in the order block of VER-015 (VER_015_order). A step whose guard fails is skipped; an applicable step polls the stop, is entered and logged; an aside goes on to the next step and a decision ends the run. The run semantics are Pipeline.lean's, fixed. The step names are the runtimes' (rtStepNames; refNuDispatch_names pins them): Route B (ν name-partition graph) is Route B, colour-slot bound is the step that solves the colour-slot program of the coloured plan (Rust total_budget::step inside the slot-bound closure, Java and TypeScript enter in colouredAttempt's solve), and IC3/PDR query is the fixpoint query, coloured or flat. To run the colour-slot bound is to enter its step.
- A NuCall carries what the runtimes' guards read of one call: the kind of property (a quiescence property, a name-alignment property of NU-055), whether the net has a ν-join and a declared budget place, whether Route A declines for injection (injection modelled on the flat net, or an arrival into a coloured place, VER-006 AC10), whether Route B declines under environment injection before building its graph (VER-006 AC8), what Route B's graph returns, whether the plan's structural checks pass and whether the colour-slot program sets a bound, the Ignore mode with environment places, the verdicts of the coloured and of the flat fixpoint query, and for every other step whether it runs and what it returns. The reference leaves the other steps free (otherNuStep), so the lines hold whatever they do; their guards and phases are their own blocks' (VER-015, VER-017, VER-018, VER-019, VER-020, VER-025). Which properties the coloured encoding decides, and with which slot count, is the first NU-053 block's; this block reads the plan as given.
- The witness is refNuDispatch: Route B enters when the property is a name-alignment property, or the net has a ν-join and the property is a quiescence property or no budget place is declared (smt_verifier.rs, the Route B trigger; SmtVerifier.java and smt-verifier.ts likewise). Its graph's Unknown hands over exactly when the property is a quiescence property, not a name-alignment one, and a budget place is declared (defer_to_route_a in smt_verifier.rs, deferToRouteA in SmtVerifier.java and smt-verifier.ts); the decline under environment injection comes before the graph and ends the call. The colour-slot bound enters when the net has a ν-join, a budget place is declared, no injection is modelled, no arrival feeds a coloured place and build_plan's structural checks pass (coloured_attempt in smt_verifier.rs, colouredAttempt in SmtVerifier.java and smt-verifier.ts). The fixpoint query decides with the coloured verdict when the plan is built, and otherwise with the flat verdict through the name-blind guard (apply_nu_guard in smt_verifier.rs, applyNuGuard in Java and TypeScript); both pass the Ignore downgrade of VER-006 first.
- Line 1 is 'The verifier shall not run Route B ([VER-012]) after the colour-slot bound in one verification call', killed by NU_053_dispatch_forbids_slotFirst. It is a safety line: it holds of a call that never enters Route B, as a budgeted reachability-safety call of a ν-net does (that property stays on Route A, NU-055). Line 2 is the EARS sentence that a colour-slot bound for a quiescence property needs Route B in the same call. Lines 1 and 2 together are the first half of 'The verifier routes a bounded quiescence query to Route B first', for every call that reaches the colour-slot bound: Route B was entered, and before it. A Route B whose trigger leaves out a bounded quiescence query (the trigger's inner or written as and, so that Route B runs only on an unbudgeted one) is killed (NU_053_dispatch_forbids_skipRouteB). That Route B runs on a bounded quiescence query with a ν-join even when the call never reaches the colour-slot bound is the routing itself, an offer: the coverage condition Nu053DispatchCovers asks for Route B in the log, shown of the reference by nu053DispatchCovers_reference.
- Line 3 is 'The verifier shall not run the colour-slot bound on a net without a ν-join or without a declared budget place, or when environment injection is modelled or an arrival feeds a coloured place ([VER-006])' and the quiescence bullet's 'The encoding has no environment-injection rule, so it does not answer when injection is modelled ([VER-006] AC7)'. Each of its three conditions is killed by its own wrong guard: NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noJoin, NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noBudget and NU_053_dispatch_forbids_injection. That a coloured verdict needs a built plan, and a plan the colour-slot bound, is the call record's shape: planOk includes the guard of the colour-slot bound, and is not tied to the colour-slot step having been entered in the run.
- Line 4 is the EARS sentence on Route B's Unknown and the second half of 'The verifier routes a bounded quiescence query to Route B first; when Route B truncates (Unknown), it defers to this scalable Route A encoding rather than returning Unknown'. The runtimes defer on every Unknown the graph returns, not only on a truncation, so the line reads 'the graph returns Unknown'. A Route B step that returns its truncation as the verdict is killed (NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noDefer). That the hand-over reaches the coloured plan, when the plan is built and no later step decides first, is an offer, not a safety line: it is the coverage condition Nu053DispatchCovers (the convention of GlossaryExec), shown of the reference by nu053DispatchCovers_reference. When the total budget or cancellation of VER-013 fires, the run ends without a next step; that is the stop of runPipeline (VER-013's block), so the hand-over holds of every run that is not stopped.
- Line 5 is 'A verdict from the coloured plan is not downgraded as a name-blind verdict would be (the colour-aware deadlock does not over-fire joins); only the Ignore downgrade of [VER-006] applies to it' and its EARS sentence, with AC6's 'quiescence is decided, never downgraded to Unknown as a name-blind verdict would be' for the zero-slot plan. A fixpoint query that applies the name-blind quiescence downgrade to a coloured verdict is killed (NU_053_dispatch_forbids_downgrade). The Ignore downgrade of VER-006 also applies to a coloured Proven, so the line excludes a call under Ignore with environment places registered; that downgrade is VER-006's. When a stop of VER-013 fires during the query, the finisher replaces an Unknown's reason (finishVerdict); a Proven or Violated stands, as VER-013's block states.
- Line 6 is the EARS sentence on a call without a coloured plan and the body's 'When no weighting exists (the program is infeasible) the coloured tokens are not structurally bounded, a genuine colour leak, so the plan is refused and the query falls back to the sound over-approximation', for a quiescence property: the name-blind encoding over-fires joins, so its quiescence verdict is not believed. A fixpoint query that returns the flat verdict unguarded is killed (NU_053_dispatch_forbids_unguarded). The runtimes return Unknown there, a Violated included; the line asks only for no Proven, which is what NU-053 says, and the full guard (Unknown for every verdict without a declared budget place, the over-approximation note) is NU-050's and NU-040's. For a reachability-safety property the flat Proven is sound (the first NU-053 block's NU_053_tokens_le and NU-050), so a fallback there may prove. A quiescence property of a NuCall is one of the four the sentences of lines 2, 4 and 6 list; QuiescentNameAligned, which NU-055 also calls a quiescence property, is a name-alignment property that Route B alone decides (NU-055). Lines 4 to 6 constrain every step of D with that name, whether or not its guard lets the call in; line 4 does not read whether the net is a ν-net (a NuCall has no such field) and asks for no name-alignment property, which none of the four listed properties is. Each of these makes a line stronger than its sentence, never weaker.
- The paragraph on the linear bound of VER-015 ('For a reachability-safety property the linear state-equation bound of [VER-015] runs before the coloured query (after Route B)', its Proven 'ends the query', 'any other outcome hands over to the coloured query unchanged', 'The coloured plan, and the linear program behind its slot bound, are built only when the bound does not prove') is VER_015_order: lines 1, 2 and 6 there put the bound after Route B and before the colour-slot bound, its line 9 makes the bound only prove or hand over, and a decision ends the run. That the bound's Proven is sound on a ν-net ('written over the flat, name-blind net, which over-approximates the ν semantics') is NU-050's and Novel/RouteA/SlotBound.lean's. 'The colour-slot bound k is often several times the budget, and a trivially true bound that IC3 cannot close over k colours within the timeout is proven by the state equation in milliseconds' is motivation.
- 'Its Proven is sound while the declared mints and the coloured consumers keep their contracts ([NU-010], [NU-051])' is the soundness of the coloured plan, NU-050's Route A line over RefNuReach (wave W9, design ruling S7 (a)); the current evidence is Novel.RouteA.routeA_safety_sound_plan and routeA_quiescence_sound_reaping. The report text (colour-slot bound k=<k>, the deferral line, the transitions whose contracts it assumes) is kind N.
- AC1 (Proven deadlock-free via the coloured Route A encoding) and the test derivation's 'a co-mint→join net is Proven deadlock-free via Route A when Route B is forced to truncate' are lines 2, 4 and 5 with the coverage condition: NU_053_dispatch_nonvacuous shows a bounded DeadlockFree call whose graph truncates enter Route B, then the colour-slot bound, and end with the coloured Proven, route smt. AC2 (removing the drain turns it Violated) is the coloured verdict, which line 5 passes unchanged; the verdict itself is the first block's and the soundness line's. AC4 and AC5 (a net with no covering weighting falls back rather than a false Proven) are line 6 for a quiescence property, with the first block's NU_053_infeasible for 'no plan'. AC3 and AC7 to AC9 are the first block's and kind Q.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): **The runtimes' dispatch meets the block.** Route B is the first step and the colour-slot bound the tenth, so a run never enters them the other way round. A quiescence call that reaches the colour-slot bound has a ν-join, so Route B, the first step, applies to it and was entered on the way. The colour-slot bound is guarded on a ν-join, a budget place and no injection. Route B hands a truncated graph over on a bounded quiescence query. The fixpoint query decides with the coloured verdict when the plan is built, and passes a flat quiescence verdict on a net with a ν-join through the name-blind guard, which never leaves it `Proven`.
  <pre>NU_053_dispatch refNuDispatch</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_downgrade` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **A coloured verdict is not downgraded.** On a bounded `DeadlockFree` call with a built plan whose coloured query proves, a fixpoint query that still applies the name-blind quiescence guard turns the `Proven` into `Unknown`.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuDowngrade</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_injection` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **No coloured plan under injection.** The coloured encoding has no injection rule, so a dispatch that solves the colour-slot program on a call with modelled injection is rejected.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuSlotInjection</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noBudget` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **No coloured plan without a budget place.** A dispatch that solves the colour-slot program on a net with a ν-join but no declared budget place is rejected.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuSlotNoBudget</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noDefer` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **A truncated Route B hands over.** On a bounded `DeadlockFree` call whose graph truncates, a Route B that returns its `Unknown` ends the call before the coloured plan can decide it.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuNoDefer</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_noJoin` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **No coloured plan without a ν-join.** A dispatch that solves the colour-slot program on a budgeted call whose net has no transition with a match specification is rejected.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuSlotNoJoin</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_skipRouteB` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **A bounded quiescence query goes to Route B first.** On a bounded `DeadlockFree` call with a ν-join, a dispatch whose Route B trigger leaves out budgeted quiescence skips Route B and goes straight through flattening, the structural pre-check and the P-invariants to the colour-slot bound, so the exact, timed Route B never sees the query.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuSkipRouteB</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_slotFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **Route B comes first.** On a bounded `DeadlockFree` call where Route B's graph is outside its fragment (so Route B steps aside), a dispatch that solves the colour-slot program and then runs Route B enters them in the wrong order.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuSlotFirst</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_forbids_unguarded` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✗ **No `Proven` from the fallback on a quiescence property.** With no coloured plan, the name-blind flat encoding over-fires joins; a fixpoint query that believes its `Proven` of a `DeadlockFree` property on a net with a ν-join is rejected.
  <pre>¬NU_053_dispatch mutNuUnguarded</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_053_dispatch_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_053_dispatch): ✓ **The coloured plan after Route B, on four calls.** When Route B's graph truncates on a bounded `DeadlockFree` query, the call goes on through flattening, the structural pre-check and the P-invariants to the colour-slot bound, and the fixpoint query ends it with the coloured `Proven`, route `smt`. When Route B's graph decides `Violated` the call ends there. With no plan (the colour-slot program has no covering weighting) the fixpoint query falls back and answers `Unknown`, not `Proven`. Under modelled injection the colour-slot bound is not entered.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_054_build"></a>
## NU-054: Join Relay (build checks)

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_054_build` · Kind **F** · Scope every transition builder, on every construction path · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 83a503773740d307 ai** · Statement hash `83a503773740d307`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* the match specification of a transition declares one place as a relay target twice, *then* building the transition *shall* fail.<br><br>*If* the match specification of a transition declares as a relay target a place that its output spec does not name, *then* building the transition *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* the match specification of a transition declares one of its own match keys as a relay target and the transition passes every other build-time check, building the transition *shall* succeed. | 1. Let NB be the transition builder (NB t = none: t builds).<br>2. For every ν transition t whose match specification lists one place twice among its relay targets, NB fails on t.<br>3. For every ν transition t whose match specification has a relay target p that the output spec of t does not name (no output arc on p, glossary: Output arc), NB fails on t.<br>4. For every ν transition t that builds (NuBuilds) and whose match specification has a relay target that is also one of its match keys, NB succeeds on t.<br>5. For every ν transition t that passes every other build-time check (it builds without its match, and the match keys distinct input places) and whose relay targets fail the relay checks (one is declared twice or is not an output place), NB fails on t with a message that names t and names a relay target that is declared twice or is not an output place. | <pre>fun {N K} [DecidableEq N] [ToString N] NB ↦<br>  (∀ (t : NuTrans N K) (ms : MatchSpec N K),<br>      t.mspec = some ms → ¬ms.relayPlaces.Nodup → NB t ≠ none) ∧<br>    (∀ (t : NuTrans N K) (ms : MatchSpec N K),<br>        t.mspec = some ms → ∀ p ∈ ms.relayPlaces, ¬OutputArc t.base p → NB t ≠ none) ∧<br>      (∀ (t : NuTrans N K) (ms : MatchSpec N K),<br>          t.mspec = some ms →<br>            NuBuilds t → (∃ p ∈ ms.relayPlaces, p ∈ ms.keyPlaces) → NB t = none) ∧<br>        ∀ (t : NuTrans N K) (ms : MatchSpec N K),<br>          t.mspec = some ms →<br>            Builds t.base →<br>              KeysDistinct ms →<br>                KeysOnInputs t ms →<br>                  ¬RelaysOK t ms →<br>                    ∃ m,<br>                      NB t = some m ∧<br>                        MsgNames m t.base.core.name ∧<br>                          ∃ q ∈ ms.relayPlaces,<br>                            (2 ≤ List.count q ms.relayPlaces ∨ ¬OutputArc t.base q) ∧<br>                              MsgNames m (toString q)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the transition builder NB for a transition that may carry a match, read as the message a call fails with, none when the transition builds, as in NU_020_build. The reference is refNuBuild, which checks, per relay target in declaration order, 'declared twice' before 'not an output', after the key checks of NU-020 (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:533-556, typescript/src/core/transition.ts:351-370, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:445-470). A relay target is checked when the transition is built, not when the match is built (rust/libpetri-core/src/match_spec.rs:220-235).
- 'An output of the transition (in at least one branch)' is read as a place the output spec names anywhere, an action branch or the timeout child (glossary: Output arc), as Rust's all_places, TypeScript's and Java's output place sets read it.
- 'Naming the transition and the place' (AC1) is the fourth line, as NU-060's rejection names the caller-side transition: the message contains the transition's name and the name of an offending relay target (MsgNames), whatever else it says. It is stated for a transition that passes every other build-time check, because the checks run in order and a transition that also fails an earlier check gets that check's message (NU_020_build); and it names some offending relay target, the first in declaration order in every runtime, since 'declared twice' and 'not an output' are checked per target in that order. The wording is configuration (kind N); the reference messages (msgRelayTwice, msgRelayNotOutput) are Rust's, as stand-ins, and NU_054_build_mutant_anyMessage_killed shows the line load-bearing. How a path fails (a panic, an exception) is kind N too.
- Place identity. The places one transition names are assumed to have pairwise distinct names, and a relay target names the place object of the transition's own output arc, as TIME-010 and MOD-006 assume for their places. Java breaks the model only outside that assumption: it detects a relay target declared twice by name but checks relay-is-output with structural Place equality, name and token type (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:452-469), so two relay targets on distinct places that share a name are rejected as declared twice, and a relay target whose place has an output's name but another token type is rejected as not an output. Rust (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:533-556), TypeScript (typescript/src/core/transition.ts:351-370) and Python (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:1310-1317) compare by name throughout. This is the Place-equality divergence of MOD-024.
- The converse for relays (a transition whose relay targets are distinct output places builds when it passes every other check) is NU_020_build's last line, whose NuBuilds names every check a matched transition passes. The third line here is its self-loop case, which the spec states as a permission ('A relay target MAY also be one of the join's own match keys'); it is a line so that a builder that refuses a relay target on a key is a forbidden model under this ID (NU_054_build_forbids_noSelfLoop; that builder also breaks NU_020_build). 'Every other build-time check' is the list of the glossary entry Build-time checks, which names the match-key checks of NU-020 and the relay checks here after the output-spec checks (clash nu-a#9, ruling D20 (a)); NuBuilds is that list.
- Under composition the relay targets are remapped with the keys ([NU-030], [NU-060]); a rewrite that maps two relay targets of one join onto one place yields a relay target declared twice, which the first line rejects at rebuild, since NB is the one builder every construction path goes through (NU_020_build's reading of 'on every construction path'). The rewrite itself is NU-030's and the composition model's (wave W8).
- AC1 (a relay target that is not an output of the transition, or is declared twice, is rejected at transition build with an error naming the transition and the place) is the first two lines and the fourth; NU_054_build_nonvacuous shows both rejections, each message naming the transition and the place, and the self-loop accepted.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_054_check"></a>
## NU-054: Join Relay (run-time relay check)

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_054_check` · Kind **B** · Scope every executor, with output validation on; one firing of a transition with a match specification · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 4e6b72f5f96a12fd ai** · Statement hash `4e6b72f5f96a12fd`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* output validation is on, *when* a transition with a match specification fires, no token the firing deposits into one of its relay targets *shall* have a name other than the chosen name under that relay target's key projection, whichever output branch or timeout outcome deposited it.<br><br>*While* output validation is on, *when* a transition with a match specification fires, every token the firing deposits into one of its relay targets *shall* have a name under that relay target's key projection, whichever output branch or timeout outcome deposited it. | 1. For every transition t that builds (NuBuilds) with match specification ms and every firing of t in R (an executor with output validation on) with chosen name n that emits e: for every relay target (p, f) of ms and every token x that e puts on p, if f gives x a name m, then m = n.<br>2. For every such firing: for every relay target (p, f) of ms and every token x that e puts on p, f gives x a name. | <pre>fun {N V Nm} [DecidableEq N] [LinearOrder Nm] R ↦<br>  (∀ (t : NuTrans N (KeyFn V Nm)) (ms : MatchSpec N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>      t.mspec = some ms →<br>        NuBuilds t →<br>          ∀ (n : Nm) (δ : QDelivered N (Stamped V)) (e : List (N × Stamped V)),<br>            on fun M M' ↦ R t M (some n) δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>              ∀ r ∈ ms.relays,<br>                ∀ x ∈ qEmittedTo e r.1, ∀ (m : Nm), r.2 x.val = some m → m = n) ∧<br>    ∀ (t : NuTrans N (KeyFn V Nm)) (ms : MatchSpec N (KeyFn V Nm)),<br>      t.mspec = some ms →<br>        NuBuilds t →<br>          ∀ (n : Nm) (δ : QDelivered N (Stamped V)) (e : List (N × Stamped V)),<br>            on fun M M' ↦ R t M (some n) δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>              ∀ r ∈ ms.relays, ∀ x ∈ qEmittedTo e r.1, r.2 x.val ≠ none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a ν firing relation R over queue markings of stamped tokens (NuFireRel), as for NU_020_enable: R t M c δ e M' says that t fires from M with chosen name c, delivers δ, its action emits e (every token it deposits, whatever wrote it) and the firing leaves M'. The lines speak of firings that complete: a completion whose emission breaks the check is not a firing of R. The lines quantify over firings with a chosen name some n; that every matched firing has one is NU_020_enable's first line (a firing of a transition with a match specification has a chosen name, and it is eligible), so a model that fired a matched transition with no chosen name is forbidden there and cannot satisfy these lines vacuously. The two lines together are the relay check RelayOk of the reference (RefNuFire), split so that each half has its own forbidden model. The reference runs it on every outcome the output spec offers, an action branch or the timeout outcome (ruling D24 (a): the timeout outcome is not validated against the output spec, but the relay check runs on it, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs:1293-1300, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java:1915-1918, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts:1259-1260), so the timeout outcome of an output spec such as And(A, Timeout(d, B)) fires in every runtime. An executor that validated the timeout outcome against the whole output spec, the Java and TypeScript behaviour RD-01 recorded, would never fire it.
- A relay target of the branch the firing produced is a relay target the emission puts a token on; a relay target the branch does not write receives nothing, so the lines quantify over every relay target of the match. The lines speak of transitions that build (NuBuilds), as CONC_008_nu does: the runtimes fire only transitions that built, and a transition that builds declares each relay target once (NU_054_build), so one projection per place is checked, as the runtimes' relay_for lookup does (it reads the first relay entry per place). Without the premise a faithful model of that lookup would be forbidden on a match that declares one relay target twice, which never builds.
- The key projection of a relay target is read as the check reads it (ruling D37 (a): partial). A token whose value is absent (null, undefined, None, the unit token an Out.place leaf deposits in a timeout branch), a value of another type, and a projection that throws or raises all give no name. That the check reports an absent value 'without calling the projection', that a Rust projection is infallible by type, and that a panicking projection propagates like a panic in the action are side effects and failure mechanisms (kind N), not lines: the tests pin them (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/nu_relay_tests.rs:228-255; typescript/src/runtime/executor-support.ts:183-192; java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/ExecutorSupport.java:288-294).
- What a failing firing does is the block NU_054_fail (NU_054_fail.lean), on RefExec's fail label (ruling D17): it 'fails the firing like any other validation failure, with an error naming the transition, the place, the matched name and the name found', deposits none of the checked batch while tokens of a batch published earlier with ctx.flush() stay, emits no IO-016 AC4 multiplicity WARN because the relay check runs first, and in Rust makes a refused ctx.flush() return Err carrying the relay message; a batch published mid-action is checked when it is published. 'The check is on by default and is skipped only where output validation itself is skipped ([CONC-026])' is the precondition 'While output validation is on' of both quoted sentences: R is the firing relation of an executor with output validation on, and the validation skip, under which the relay check accepts everything with the rest of output validation, is NU_054_fail's (Cfg.SkipsValidation). 'The runtime check is independent of the mode' holds because the lines take no fragment mode.
- Clash nu-c#8 (ruling D24 (a)): with the relay check a timed-out firing whose timeout outcome writes a unit token, or a forward of another input, into a relay target deposits nothing, where IO-013's quoted sentence says a timed-out firing deposits the tokens of the child. The exception is in IO-013's text (a firing whose timeout outcome fails the relay check fails and deposits none of the tokens of child), which the block IO_013 accounts for through NU_054_check and NU_054_fail, and in IO-014's paragraph on forwarding (a forward into a relay target is checked like every other token of the timeout outcome); this block states the check.
- AC2 (a join whose action writes into a relay target a token projecting to another name, or to no name, fails that firing; the same net with a conforming action fires normally; both backends in every language agree; a projection that throws fails with the no-name error; no IO-016 AC4 WARN): the refusal is the two lines, worked in NU_054_check_nonvacuous; 'the same net with a conforming action fires normally' is the conjunct NuCovers of the consistency theorem (every enabled matched transition fires with every offered emission that passes the check), shown on the example by NU_054_check_nonvacuous; the failure event is NU_054_fail's, and the error text and the WARN order are test evidence there (kind Q, NU_054_fail's assumes); 'both executor backends in every language agree' is a test obligation (kind Q).

## NU-054: Join Relay (a firing the relay check rejects)
