**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor E : XRel N (Stamped V) (glossary GlossaryExec.lean) over tokens that carry a value and a creation stamp (GlossaryNu.lean, Stamped), the token type of the ν kernel. E C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A firing starts in a firing pass and settles in a later step: commit deposits a returned output, tdeposit a timeout outcome, fail nothing (the settle steps of EXEC-021). The action writes (write), publishes what it wrote (flush, a batch queued in XSt.pq and deposited later by publish, ruling D17) and returns (ret), or its budget runs out (expire). The witness is the reference executor RefExec, checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.
- The ν side is read through the configuration. The executor consults its join-relay check C.relay (Cfg.relay: 'part of output validation'); the lines fix it to NU-054's check: mt gives each transition its match specification and cn the chosen name of a firing from what its start delivered, and relayVerdict mt cn accepts an emission exactly when every token it puts on a relay target projects to that name (relayVerdict_iff; for a firing whose chosen name is n it is NU_054_check's RelayOk, nu054f_relayPass_iff). The lines hold for every mt and cn, so they do not depend on how the start chose the name: RefExec's start delivers the heads of the input queues (qDelivered), not the correlated take of RefNuFire, and the block needs only the name. Nothing yet ties mt and cn to the net: no consistency theorem states C.relay = relayVerdict (the match each transition carries) keyName on the delivery of a correlated take, so until that link exists the block says that the executor respects whatever relay check of the NU-054 shape its configuration carries (an open item: the link C.relay = relayVerdict in a consistency theorem).
- 'While output validation is on' is the premise C.relay = relayVerdict mt cn. 'The check is on by default and is skipped only where output validation itself is skipped ([CONC-026])': under the validation skip the relay check accepts everything (Cfg.SkipsValidation). The premise then still holds, but only with a match assignment that gives no transition a match (the check that accepts everything is relayVerdict (fun _ => none) cn), so every RelayPass conjunct is empty, the trigger of line 5 never fires, and what remains is the frame of the settle, flush and publish steps that EXEC-021, EXEC-022 and CONC-003 state for every executor. NU_054_fail_nonvacuous shows the reference depositing a token of another name into a relay target under the skip. Rust checks no relay when skip_output_validation is set: relay_check accepts every output, and fire_transition_async builds no relay guard for a flush (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs). 'The runtime check is independent of the mode' holds because nothing here reads a fragment mode.
- Lines 1, 2, 4 and 6 bind every transition, not only one with a match specification: for a transition without a match RelayPass holds trivially, and the lines restate what other blocks state for every executor. A commit deposits exactly the returned output at the tails (CONC-003 line 1, EXEC-020), a tdeposit exactly the timeout outcome (EXEC-022), a flush deposits nothing and queues at most the action's buffer ([IO-015] mid-action publication), and a publish deposits a queued batch (CONC-003 line 2, which also fixes that it is the oldest one). These exact deposits are here so that the relay conjunct reads on the tokens actually deposited, and so that each of the three quoted sentences has its own wrong models in this block.
- The first quoted sentence is lines 1 and 2: a returned output or a timeout outcome that fails the check is never the emission of a commit or tdeposit step; the steps in which the action writes or returns deposit nothing (EXEC_021's line 4) and, by line 7, hand nothing to the publication queue, so the output cannot reach the marking through a later publish either (NU_054_fail_forbids_retQueues: a return that queues the output unchecked); and the fail step deposits nothing (line 3). Rust runs the check after the output-spec check of a completion and on the timeout path (relay_check, called from handle_completion in executor_core/executor.rs); Java (BitmapNetExecutor.validateOutput, ExecutorSupport.validateRelays) and TypeScript (processCompletedTransitions in bitmap-net-executor.ts, validateRelays in executor-support.ts) run it inside output validation. 'Shall fail the firing' is an offer: that a firing whose returned output or timeout outcome the check rejects is settled by a fail step is the clause ExecFailCovers of the consistency theorem's ExecCoversW5 (refExec_failCovers), not a line (blocks state safety, offers are coverage). The TransitionFailed event is the event the fail label carries (Reference/Events.lean, EVT-008). Its error, 'naming the transition, the place, the matched name and the name found', and the 'no name' error of a projection that throws or of an absent value checked without calling the projection, are message text and failure mechanism (kind N). They are built by relay_check in executor_core/executor.rs and by validateRelays in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/ExecutorSupport.java and typescript/src/runtime/executor-support.ts, and pinned by the runtimes' tests: token_of_another_name_fails_the_firing, token_projecting_to_no_name_fails_the_firing and absent_value_has_no_name_and_the_projection_is_not_called in rust/libpetri-runtime/src/nu_relay_tests.rs; nuRelay_wrongNameFailsTheFiring, nuRelay_noNameFailsTheFiring and nuRelay_throwingKeyFunctionIsNoName in AbstractNetExecutorEngineTest; and 'a token of another name fails the firing, naming transition, place and both names', 'a token projecting to no name fails the firing', 'an absent value has no name, and the projection is not called on it' and 'a key function that throws projects no name: the firing fails with the relay error' in typescript/tests/runtime/nu-join-relay.test.ts.
- The timeout outcome is checked and not validated against the output spec (ruling D24 (a)): line 2 reads the check on every tdeposit step and EXEC_021 forbids validating the outcome. Every runtime runs only the relay check on a timeout outcome (processCompletedTransitions in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java, processCompletedTransitions in typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts, handle_completion in rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs), so a relay violation of a timeout outcome fails the firing in every runtime and And(A, Timeout(d, B)) deposits B on a timeout. An executor that also validated the timeout outcome against the whole output spec, the Java and TypeScript behaviour RD-01 recorded, would fail that firing on every timeout. Clash nu-c#8: a timed-out firing whose timeout outcome writes a unit token, or a forward of another input, into a relay target deposits nothing, where IO-013's sentence says a timed-out firing deposits the tokens of the child. The spec edits of this block add that exception to the text of IO-013 and IO-014 as sentences without shall, so the quotes of IO_013 and IO_014 stay as they are.
- The second quoted sentence is line 3, read on every fail step whatever its cause ('fails the firing like any other validation failure'; one fail label serves the action's error, the output-spec rejection and the relay rejection). The marking is unchanged, so nothing of the output or outcome is deposited, the consumed tokens stay consumed, and a batch already deposited stays in the marking; the queue of published batches is unchanged, so a batch flushed before the failure and still queued is deposited by its publish step (ruling D17: 'deposits none of the checked batch while tokens of a batch published earlier with ctx.flush() stay'). That no later step withdraws a queued batch either is CONC-003's line 3 (conc003Kept). EXEC_021's line 2 states the same frame for every executor, which the sentence cites; line 3 is here so that the NU-054 reading has its own wrong models: a failure that deposits the conforming part of the output (NU_054_fail_forbids_partialDeposit) and one that withdraws the queued batch (NU_054_fail_forbids_failDropsPub).
- The third quoted sentence is lines 4 to 7. 'Shall not deposit that batch' is lines 4, 6 and 7 together: a flush deposits nothing itself and queues only a batch that passes the check (line 4), no other step adds a batch of i to the queue (line 7, together with line 4 for every other identity), and a publish deposits only a batch of i that is queued (line 6), so a refused batch reaches the marking neither at its flush nor later. The wrong models are a flush that deposits at once (NU_054_fail_forbids_flushDeposits), a flush without the check (NU_054_fail_forbids_flushNoGuard), a publish of a batch that was never queued (NU_054_fail_forbids_publishUnqueued) and a return that queues the output (NU_054_fail_forbids_retQueues). 'A batch published mid-action ([IO-015]) is checked when it is published': Rust's flush callback, built in fire_transition_async, checks the batch before it sends it (executor_core/executor.rs). Rust drops every later batch of a firing once one was refused (the callback keeps the refusal in FlushGate.relay_error and refuses each later batch with it); line 4 allows that (the queue stays as it was) and does not require it, since the markdown does not say what happens to a later batch.
- 'Shall fail the firing, and shall deposit neither the output the action returns nor the timeout outcome' is line 5: 'In Rust, a relay violation found while flushing a mid-action batch makes ctx.flush() return Err carrying the relay message, rather than recording it and returning Ok; the firing then fails as it does for a violation found at completion.' After a refused flush of i, no commit or tdeposit of i follows in the run, so the firing, if it is settled at all, is settled by a fail step; NU_054_fail_forbids_recordOk is the executor that drops the batch and lets the firing complete. The trigger is a flush whose batch fails relayVerdict mt cn, which rejects only on a transition with a match, as the sentence says; in the model the relay check is the only thing that refuses a non-empty batch an open asynchronous firing flushes (flushStep). That the fail step is then offered is coverage, not a line. On the reference it is ExecFailCovers: the reference records an error at the return or expiry of a firing marked relayBad (in Rust the task of fire_transition_async takes FlushGate.relay_error as the firing's error, executor_core/executor.rs), and ExecFailCovers offers fail for an error. ExecFailCovers has no disjunct for a firing whose batch was refused, so for another executor the offer follows only jointly: CONC_010 queues its return, a commit or tdeposit of a passing outcome is what ValidatedBy and Exec022Covers would offer and line 5 forbids, and no clause forces a refusing flush to record the error (an open item: a relayBad disjunct of ExecFailCovers). That ctx.flush() returns Err to the action, with the relay message, is the action-side API of Rust (kind N): the model's flush step hands nothing back to the action. Java and TypeScript have no mid-action publication (IO-015's flush is Rust's and Python's), so lines 4 to 7 hold there with no flush step and no publish step.
- Line 5 identifies the firing by its identity. Identities are drawn once from one supply (XSt.nextId); the premise IdsIssued says every firing in flight at the start of the run has an identity the supply has already handed out, true at the start of every run and kept by every reference step (exec022_idsIssued_step), as in EXEC_022's trace lines. The trigger reads the first firing with identity i, which is the one every reference rule acts on. The block does not require E to draw fresh identities, so line 5 also binds a later firing that reused identity i; no runtime and not the reference reuses one.
- 'The relay check runs before the multiplicity diagnostic of [IO-016] AC4, in both executor backends of every language, so a firing that both violates the relay contract and over-writes a place fails with the relay error and emits no multiplicity WARN': the reference event model emits no multiplicity WARN yet (Reference/Events.lean, 'Not emitted by the reference yet'), so the order is test evidence (kind Q): Rust checks the relay before warn_multiplicity (handle_completion in executor_core/executor.rs), Java inside BitmapNetExecutor.validateOutput before warnMultiplicity, and TypeScript in processCompletedTransitions before warnMultiplicity (bitmap-net-executor.ts). On a fail step the reference emits only TransitionFailed, never a deposit's diagnostics, which is the model's half of it.
- AC2 (a join whose action writes into a relay target a token of another name or of no name fails that firing; the same net with a conforming action fires normally; both backends in every language agree; a throwing projection fails with the 'no name' error; no IO-016 AC4 WARN): the refusal is lines 1 and 3 with the fail offer of ExecFailCovers, worked in NU_054_fail_nonvacuous on AC4's join j1 (a token of another name and a unit token of a timeout branch fail the firing, the conforming output and the timeout forward of a match key are deposited); which firings exist is NU_054_check's; 'both executor backends agree', the error text and the WARN order are kind Q and N as above. AC1 (the build rejections) is NU_054_build's; AC3 to AC7 (verdicts, classifier, report notes, key fixtures) are NU_054_verifier's and the verifier pipeline's; none of them is about a failing firing.

**Assumptions**

- The classifier is per transition, as in NU_051 (glossary: Fragment classifier): no role means the net falls back to the sound over-approximation with an 'EXTENDED declined' note ([NU-050]). The coloured set is an argument; that the relay targets of every join are unioned into it under EXTENDED, before the fragment rules are checked, and that BASE colours the match keys alone, is the coloured-set computation, which no block states: the verifier pipeline model (Verifier/Pipeline.lean, the block VER_003) does not model how a ν verifier builds the coloured set. It is Q-tested: Rust name_fragment.rs extended_colours_relay_targets_and_the_join_carries_them and a_relay_target_no_join_consumes_is_coloured_and_its_read_arc_rejects, and name_coloured_encoder.rs a_relay_target_no_join_consumes_is_coloured_and_produced_by_the_join (under EXTENDED a relay target is coloured, also one no join consumes). 'Under BASE the relay declarations are ignored by the analyzer' is the seventh line for the classifier (a relay declaration changes no BASE role, whatever the coloured set), with the first and sixth lines (the declarations neither let a coloured output in nor reach the role), and the pipeline's BASE coloured set for the rest.
- The outcomes of a transition are Route B's rows (Novel.RouteB.NuTrans.rows: the action branches, then the timeout deposits), the timeout writes are the separate argument tw (Rust timeout_writes), as in NU_051. A unit token is TW.unit; a forward of an input is TW.forward with the input's place. 'No reset, read or inhibitor arc on a coloured place' and 'one token, and never a drained batch' are NU_051's ColouredTestArc and SingleColouredWrites.
- The fourth line is the classification the relay exists for ('Relay targets change the classification only under EXTENDED'): it is the admission, on NU_051's pattern for the consume role, and makes a classifier that never gives a relaying join a role a forbidden model (NU_054_verifier_forbids_never). Its conditions are those of the shipped classifier (Novel.RouteB.classifyT and classifyS, rust/libpetri-verification/src/name_fragment.rs classify): the markdown names the coloured-output, off-key, test-arc and timeout rules; 'consumes each match key at a fixed count' is the key-count rule of the matched-join fragment (keyCount: One gives 1, Exactly(n) gives n, All and AtLeast are refused), which the markdown does not spell out and which the sentence states as the runtimes do. The counted keys (place and count per key) are the join's enabling counts, Route B's subject (NU-055); the line fixes only that their places are the keys, in some order.
- The fourth and fifth lines read the relay targets as a set and the counted keys up to order, as the quotes do ('with the relay targets it declares', 'exactly the relay targets the transition declares'). The runtimes give the counted keys in code-point order of the place names and hold the relay targets as a set: Rust name_fragment.rs classify sorts coloured_in and collects relay_to into a BTreeSet; Java NameFragment.classify sorts colouredIn by CodePointOrder and copies relayTo into a Set (NameFragment.java:394-395); TypeScript name-fragment.ts classify sorts colouredIn by compareCodePoints and builds relayTo as a Set (verification/analysis/name-fragment.ts:251-283). The reference refClassify keeps the declared order of both; nu054_sortedClassify, which sorts both as the runtimes do, meets the block too (NU_054_verifier_sorted). Which order the counted keys take matters only to Route B's enabling test with a zero-count key (Novel.RouteB.joinEnab_perm_of_pos, zeroKey_order_matters), which is NU-055's concern, not the classifier's.
- The fragment rules of the relay that are coloured-place rules of NU-051 are NU_051's lines, which apply to a relay target once it is coloured: 'a relay target that the same join also consumes through an input that is not one of its match keys' is NU_051's fifth line, 'a relay target carrying a read, inhibitor or reset arc on any transition' its fourth. 'A relay target no join consumes is still coloured: its consumers take the [NU-051] consume role and any other producer the mint role, when it is a declared mint ([NU-010])' is NU_051's and NU-010's lines over that coloured set. 'A coloured output of a join that is not a relay target, or a relay target produced with a count other than one, is outside the fragment' is the second line here and the branch rule (Novel.RouteB.classifyT: each coloured place a branch writes takes exactly one token, never a drained batch).
- The name step of a relaying join ('A join firing on symbol s removes s from its keys as before, then adds s once to each relay target in the fired branch'; a branch with no relay target drains s; an Xor join may relay on one branch and drain on another; the step mints nothing and commutes with renaming) is Route B's executable model, not a line: Novel.RouteB.joinStep with relOut (Name.lean, Graph.lean), joinStep_sym, and routeB_equivariant for the relay role. The Route A update of a relaying join (the per-colour guards and update terms, no update term on a key that is also a relay target) and the colour-slot weights are NU-053's encoding and the script goldens (VER-013), test-cited (kind Q). The canonical key format and byte parity are VER-012's subject.
- 'A verifier that meets a relay declaration under BASE MUST say in its report that the declaration was ignored and name EXTENDED' and the 'EXTENDED declined' note are report lines (kind N), which no block states; they are Q-tested (the BASE note: Rust tests/nu_join_relay fig12c_under_base_ignores_the_declaration_and_says_so, Java JoinRelayTest, TypeScript tests/verification/nu-join-relay.test.ts, Python tests/test_nu_join_relay.py test_base_ignores_the_declaration_and_says_so; the 'EXTENDED declined' note: NU_051's assumes); clash nu-c#7 (ruling D20 (a)) made the body's SHOULD the MUST of AC5.
- The timeout rule is stated for the coloured places the timeout writes; under EXTENDED those include the relay targets, so it is the spec's 'a join whose Timeout branch writes a relay target by anything other than a forward of one of its match keys'. The run-time reason ('an Out.place leaf writes a unit token with no name, and a forward of another input carries that input's name, so that firing fails and deposits nothing') is NU_054_check with NU_054_fail.
- AC3 (a relay join chain decided through Route B), AC5 (the BASE verdict unchanged, the report naming the ignored declaration), AC6 (Route A and Route B agree on small relay fixtures) and AC7 (no canonical key changes for a net without relay declarations) are verdict, report and fixture lines, which no block states (kind Q): AC3, AC5 and AC6 are tested in Rust tests/nu_join_relay (chain_reaches_done_and_is_deadlock_free_via_route_b, fig12c_under_base_ignores_the_declaration_and_says_so, routes_agree_on_the_relay_fixtures), with the same queries in Java JoinRelayTest and TypeScript tests/verification/nu-join-relay.test.ts, over spec/verification-fixtures/nu-relay-fixtures.json; AC7 is about VER-012's canonical keys, and no test names it. Their classifier halves are lines here: AC3's 'rather than falling back' for the join is the fourth line, AC5's 'the verdict it got without one' is the seventh (the BASE classification, and so the BASE net the verdict is computed on, does not see the declaration), shown in NU_054_verifier_nonvacuous. AC4's rejections are the second and third lines and NU_051's fourth and fifth (its 'neither Route B nor Route A decides it' has a Route B witness only: Novel.RouteA.shippedGate does not model the join-timeout refusal, Plan.lean:419-425, so the Route A half is test-cited); NU_054_verifier_nonvacuous shows the unit-token timeout refused and the timeout forwarding a match key admitted.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_055"></a>
## NU-055: Name Alignment

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_055` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY); the predicate on a class of the Route B graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 844b7488adecca57 ai** · Statement hash `844b7488adecca57`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| For places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, and the name-symbols `s` and `t`: `s` resident in `p` and `t` resident in `q` imply `s = t`.<br><br>An empty place imposes nothing, but a place holding two names violates it whatever the others hold, so the singleton `NameAligned(p)` says that `p` never holds two names.<br><br>*Where* name alignment is offered, `NameAligned(S)` for a non-empty `S` *shall* hold on a class of the graph exactly when, for places `p` and `q` of `S`, the same place included, every name-symbol resident in `p` equals every name-symbol resident in `q`.<br><br>The predicate compares names only for equality, so it is invariant under any permutation of the name-symbols.<br><br>It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.<br><br>Its places compare by name, and a place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence, so `NameAligned(box, list, box)` is `NameAligned(box, list)`.<br><br>The order of `S` changes no verdict; it fixes the description and which place a reason names. | 1. For every coloured set co, base type β, non-empty list ps and class S of the graph, the check A answers true exactly when any name-symbol s resident in a place p of ps and any name-symbol t resident in a place q of ps, p = q allowed, are equal. | <pre>fun A ↦<br>  ∀ (co : List PlaceId) (β : Type) (ps : List PlaceId) (S : Novel.RouteB.NState co β),<br>    ps ≠ [] →<br>      (A co β ps S = true ↔<br>        ∀ p ∈ ps,<br>          ∀ q ∈ ps,<br>            ∀ (s t : ℕ),<br>              Novel.RouteB.resident co p S.m s = true →<br>                Novel.RouteB.resident co q S.m t = true → s = t)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a class of the Route B graph (NState co β, Graph.lean): a base b, a name layer m giving each name-symbol and each coloured place (a position of co) a count, and a bound above every live symbol. A name-symbol s is resident in p when its count there is not 0 (Name.lean resident). The NameAligned bullet speaks of a marking; its EARS restatement and the line speak of a class of the graph, which is where Route B evaluates the predicate. A marking's names are read on its coloured places through the one projection nameOf: its class is its name view (view co nameOf m), and on that view the line is the statement that all tokens in the places of S carry one name (alignedAll_view_iff, cited). Places are PlaceId, so 'its places compare by name' is equality of ids, and the check takes S as a list.
- The line is the definition of the NameAligned bullet (its second and third sentences, restated by the EARS sentence): self pairs included, so a place holding two names fails whatever the others hold, and an empty place has no resident symbol and imposes nothing. The QuiescentNameAligned bullet reads 'the same predicate'; where it is read is NU_055_sound's subject. The first sentence of the NameAligned bullet ('in every reachable marking') is NU_055_sound's.
- The permutation sentence, the first half of the canonical-key sentence and the S-order sentences ('a place listed twice counts once', 'The order of S changes no verdict', read on the predicate) are consequences of the line, not lines of their own: the line fixes A on every non-empty list, so A is the shipped check there (NU_055_eq_ref), and NU_055_perm, NU_055_key and NU_055_members derive the three invariances. The spec states them with 'so' and 'therefore', and they get no EARS sentence. The models that break one of them (nu055_symZero, nu055_headOnly) are killed by the line itself. The second half of the canonical-key sentence ('deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph') is also a claim about the verdict: the verdict on a closed graph is the predicate's answer over its classes, NU_055_truncation line 3.
- An uncoloured place has no row in the name layer, so nothing is resident there (resident_of_not_mem) and the line holds vacuously for it (alignedAll_uncoloured, cited). That such a place is refused (refusal step 6, 'Coloured places only', AC2) is not a line of this block: it is line 6 of the refusal block NU_055_refusal (NU_055_steps.lean), whose NU_055_refusal_uncoloured_refused shows that such a place never reaches the graph, and whose NU_055_refusal_forbids_noUncoloured kills the design's mutant 'proves on an uncoloured place'.
- 'A place listed twice counts once, at its first occurrence' also fixes the description and which place a reason names, and 'The order of S changes no verdict' also covers the reason of an Unknown. The description (the Property: line) is N (an API note), and which place a reason names is the refusal order's (NU_055_refusal). On the predicate, the only part of the verdict this block models, order and repeats change nothing (NU_055_members).
- 'An empty S MUST be rejected where it is constructed' and 'S is a non-empty list' are the language API (N): each constructor rejects an empty list (Java records, the TypeScript signature, the Rust panic, the Python ValueError). The line is stated for a non-empty S only, so the block fixes no answer for the empty list, which never reaches a verdict.
- AC5 (invariance under name permutation, on a class and that class permuted, and under reordering S) is NU_055_perm and NU_055_members, theorems of the line; its run of the worked example with names minted in another scope ([NU-010]) is a test of the minter (NU-010, NU-011) and of the verdict, not of the predicate, and is not encoded.
- AC7 ('S is a list'; the cross pair of reply and staged without the self pairs would accept a marking with two stale replies in reply) is the line with self pairs: NU_055_forbids_crossOnly kills the check without self pairs. AC7's construction rules are the API (N, above) and NU_055_members; its descriptions are N; its verdicts and witness lengths on the worked example are tests on the fixtures (Q), as the Route B graph of that net is not computed in Lean.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The shipped check satisfies NU-055: `alignedAll` is the pairwise reading with self pairs (`alignedAll_eq_true_iff`, `aligned_eq_true_iff`).
  <pre>NU_055 refAlignCheck</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_crossOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ The cross pairs alone violate NU-055: on the singleton `[0]` the check accepts place `0` holding the names `0` and `1`, which the line refuses (AC7: a place holding two names violates the predicate whatever the others hold).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_crossOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_headOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ Reading only the first place violates NU-055: on `nu055_mixed` the check accepts `[0, 1]` because place `0` holds one name, while place `1` holds two and the line refuses the list. The line kills it directly; the same model also breaks the members consequence (`[1, 0]` is refused).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_headOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_forbids_symZero` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ Comparing names with a fixed name violates NU-055: place `0` holding the one name `1` is aligned on `[0]`, and the check refuses it. The line kills it directly; the same model also breaks the permutation and key consequences (`nu055_zero` is accepted, its swap `nu055_one`, with the same key, is not).
  <pre>¬NU_055 nu055_symZero</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_mutant_crossOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The cross-pairs check kills the mutant reading without self pairs: it is that reading, so it meets it, but NU-055, whose line includes the self pairs, rejects it on a place holding two names (`NU_055_forbids_crossOnly`, AC7).
  <pre>NU_055_mutant_crossOnly nu055_crossOnly ∧ ¬NU_055 nu055_crossOnly</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The line of NU-055 is exercised by the shipped check, on both sides of its `iff`: places `0` and `1` holding the one name `0` are aligned, and so is the singleton `[0]` there (two places and self pairs); place `0` holding two names is not aligned on `[0]` (a place holding two names) nor on `[1, 0]` (whatever the others hold); place `1` empty imposes nothing on `[1]`. The consequences show on the same examples: the class with the names swapped gives the same answer (NU_055_perm, NU_055_key), and `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0, 1]` give the same answer on the mixed class (NU_055_members).
  <pre>refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0, 1] nu055_same = true ∧<br>  refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_same = true ∧<br>    refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_two = false ∧<br>      refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1, 0] nu055_two = false ∧<br>        refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1] nu055_two = true ∧<br>          refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_zero =<br>              refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0] nu055_one ∧<br>            refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [0, 1] nu055_mixed = false ∧<br>              refAlignCheck nu055_co Unit [1, 0, 1] nu055_mixed = false</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_055_refusal"></a>
## NU-055: Name Alignment: the refusal order

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_refusal` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY); the refusals before Route B builds the graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 fdec05e446bbdbbb ai** · Statement hash `fdec05e446bbdbbb`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A call can meet several of these refusals at once.<br><br>Its verdict is `Unknown` with the reason of the first that applies, in this order, so every implementation names the same place:<br><br>The refusals that precede every route for every property, in this order: a call cancelled or out of total budget before it starts ([VER-013]); a place of `S` that the net does not declare and the initial marking does not mark ([VER-003] AC5), naming the first such place of `S`; a `Bounded(k)` environment outside its premises ([VER-006] AC3); the in-flight refusal of [VER-004].<br><br>The net is outside the fragment of the mode even when every transition counts as a mint: the fragment decline of the mode, under EXTENDED the note of **EXTENDED** above, under BASE a decline that names EXTENDED.<br><br>Under `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)`, an arrival into a coloured place ([VER-006] AC10), naming the first such place in the order the environment places were registered.<br><br>The net is outside the fragment only because a transition writes a coloured place without consuming one and is not a declared mint: the decline names those transitions in declaration order ([NU-010]).<br><br>Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, an environment place Route B cannot model ([VER-006] AC8). The rules run in this order, each over the environment places the net declares in code-point order of names: one that is coloured; one that an inhibitor arc tests (naming the first such transition in code-point order); where conflict priority is in effect ([NU-052]), one that two or more transitions consume; then, for `QuiescentNameAligned`, the first of them (**Modelled injection** above), and for `NameAligned`, the first that is in `S`.<br><br>The first place of `S`, in the order of `S`, that is not coloured. **Assumptions**

- The model is a gate R : AlignCall → AlignGate. A call (AlignCall) is read through the facts the refusal order looks at: the places of S in the caller's order (a repeat already dropped, NU_055's assumes), the places the net declares and the places the initial marking marks, the stop, the Bounded(k) and in-flight flags, the fragment mode, whether the net is inside the fragment of the mode when every transition counts as a mint, the transitions of the net in declaration order and those of them that would have to be declared mints, the coloured set the classifier computes, the injection mode with the arrival places in registration order, the registered environment places, and per place the transitions with an inhibitor arc on it and the number of transitions that consume it. Places and transitions are their names (String), as 'Its places compare by name' says; < on String compares code points, so 'the first in code-point order' is cpFirst. A refusal .refuse r is the verdict Unknown with the reason r; .build is the call reaching the graph. The calls are those without the caller's error of a declared mint or carrier that is not in the net: 'A declared mint or carrier that is not in the net is the caller's error and is reported as [NU-010] and [NU-051] say, outside this order.' puts that error outside the order, and the runtimes place it differently (Rust checks an unknown declared mint after the absent place of step 1 and before the Bounded(k) premises), so no line speaks of such a call. The route a refusal reports is not modelled: the runtimes report Unavailable for step 1 and Route B for steps 2 to 7 (Rust verify_net and route_b_declined).
- The step functions step1 to step7 are vocabulary: each is the bullet of the refusal order it is named after, read on the call, and returns the reason of its first refusal that applies. The lines fix the gate on every call (NU_055_refusal_eq_ref): the refusal order is a function of the call, so the block states which refusal comes first and what it names, not how a verifier computes it. Why each refusal exists (VER-003 AC5, VER-006 AC3, AC8 and AC10, VER-004, NU-010, NU-051) is those requirements'; whether a call meets one (the classifier's fragment and coloured set, the Bounded(k) premises, the in-flight split) is a fact of the call here.
- Line 1 is step 1, its four refusals in the order the bullet lists them, the absent place being the first place of S that the net does not declare and the initial marking does not mark, which is VER-003's unresolved check on S (Verifier/Result.lean Unresolved). 'Cancelled or out of total budget before it starts' is a stop the first poll sees; a stop that a later poll sees, on entering Route B, is VER-013's and names the step it was charged to. A gate without the absent check lets an absent place reach step 6, where it is named as uncoloured (NU_055_refusal_forbids_noAbsent).
- Line 2 is step 2, and lines 2 and 6 together are the EXTENDED paragraph's 'Such a call is refused at step 2 or at step 6 of the refusal order below unless an earlier step refuses it, and the reason of either step MUST name EXTENDED.' (clash nu-c#7, the body SHOULD made MUST as AC3 has it, ruling D20, and scoped to the refusal order: under BASE a carrier or relay target of S is uncoloured, so a call that steps 1 and 2 let through and steps 3 to 5 do not refuse meets step 6, whose reason carries the mode as step 2's does; a stop, a coloured arrival, undeclared mints or an environment place come first and name no mode), and 'A net outside the EXTENDED fragment gets the "EXTENDED declined" note of [NU-051] and the verdict `Unknown`.': the decline carries the mode (underBase), and names EXTENDED under BASE; under EXTENDED it is the note of the EXTENDED paragraph, which the mode alone tells apart. That the note never says the property was verified by another route is its text (N): every reason here is a refusal, and no route other than Route B is consulted. A gate that checks the places of S before the fragment names list on AC3's BASE call (NU_055_refusal_forbids_uncolouredFirst).
- Line 3 is step 3, for Arrivals(k) and Arrivals(min, max) alike (VER-006 names both; the runtimes read either through their arrivals injection), and 'Under `Arrivals` the net has no environment places left ([VER-006]); the decline of [VER-006] AC10 for an arrival into a coloured place still applies.' The place named is the first coloured one in the order the environment places were registered, as all three runtimes name it (Rust coloured_arrival_reason, Java colouredArrivalReason, TypeScript colouredArrivalReason over the arrival's injected list). The runtimes read the arrival places on the coloured set of the classifier run with every transition counted a mint; declaring mints changes no coloured place, so that set is the call's coloured set.
- Line 4 is step 4: the fragment would hold if the listed transitions were declared mints, and the decline names them in declaration order, the order the net holds its transitions (CORE-040), as all three runtimes list them (Rust undeclared_mints_for, Java NameFragment.undeclaredMints, TypeScript undeclaredMints: the classifier's mints in net order, less the declared ones). Which transitions they are is a fact of the call (undeclared, in any order); their order is read off the net (undeclaredInOrder). A gate that lists them in the order the classifier holds them names sendA, sendB on a net that declares sendB first (NU_055_refusal_forbids_mintsAnyOrder). The caller's error of a declared mint or carrier missing from the net is not a line: that check is NU-010's and NU-051's, and the first assumes says why no line speaks of it.
- Line 5 is step 5 with its four rules, the Modelled injection paragraph's 'In addition, under these modes QuiescentNameAligned with a registered environment place that the net declares is Unknown, and where no earlier refusal ... applies, nor an earlier rule of its step 5, the reason names the first such place in code-point order ...' (its fourth rule; that such a call is never built is NU_055_refusal_envQuiescent_refused). Under Ignore no environment place is modelled and nothing is refused for one; a registered place the net does not declare is not read (envDeclared) and 'Under `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)` ([VER-006]) the decline rule of [NU-050] and [VER-006] AC8 applies to both properties.' (its first three rules and the NameAligned half of the fourth). The third rule's 'where conflict priority is in effect ([NU-052])' is the fact c.conflict, read as NU-052 states it: the mode is CONFLICT, no transition of the net is read as reapable, and no pruner that cannot be split turned the pruning off for the call. All three runtimes read it so: the check is handed CONFLICT only where conflict priority applies (Rust conflict_pruning_applies() before route_b_env_observation, Java conflictPruningApplies(preSplitNet), TypeScript conflictPruningApplies()), so under CONFLICT on a net with a reapable transition a shared environment input is not refused, as under NONE. Reading the selected mode after the split rule alone, the behaviour RD-39 recorded (spec/runtime-defects.md, against NU-052, VER-006 AC8 and this step), refuses it there, although a net with a reapable transition is explored without the pruning (NU-052, verify_via_name_scg_reaping) and the frozen count of a shared environment input then prunes nothing. The rest of that paragraph explains why (the graph never consumes an environment place, the worked example would truncate); it is not a line.
- 'Steps 3 and 5 apply whether or not the coloured places start empty.' is the order of lines 3, 5 and 7: a marked coloured place is the last refusal. The other properties take a different path in the runtimes (a marked coloured place makes Route B decline and the flat pipeline decide them); a gate that keeps that path for name alignment names the marked place first (NU_055_refusal_forbids_markedBeforeEnv, NU_055_refusal_forbids_arrivalLast).
- Line 6 is step 6, the step-6 half of the EXTENDED sentence (see line 2), 'Every place of S MUST be a coloured place of the fragment Route B classified for the call' and the coloured-only paragraph's 'MUST fail loudly' sentence, reworded under ruling NC-7 (a) and D20 (clash nu-c#9): the reason names a place of S only where no earlier refusal applies; 'absent' is step 1's 'not declared and not marked'. The sentence's 'never Proven' is NU_055_refusal_uncoloured_refused: a call with an absent or uncoloured place of S is refused, so the graph is never built for it. That such a place would make the predicate hold vacuously is NU_055's assumes (alignedAll_uncoloured).
- Line 7 is step 7, 'The coloured places MUST start empty' and the sentence on a restored marking, which like the MUST fail loudly sentence names the place only where no earlier refusal applies (AC8: with box marked, QuiescentNameAligned(box, ready) names ready); that such a call is Unknown whatever comes first is NU_055_refusal_build_premises (no call with a marked coloured place is built). The place named is the first marked coloured place in code-point order, whatever the order of S or of the marking. 'There is no fallback' is the Route B only rule: no other route decides a name-alignment property, which is a pipeline rule and not a line of this block.
- Line 8 is the closing EARS sentence: no refusal of this order fires on a call none of the steps refuse. .build is the gate letting the call through to Route B, not a promise that the graph is finished: a stop that a later poll sees ends the call there, which is VER-013's and NU_055_truncation's (a cancelled build does not close), and the caller's error of a missing mint or carrier is outside the calls this block reads. 'The `Ignore` downgrade of a `Proven` ([VER-006]) and a truncation `Unknown` are not refusals: they follow a graph that was built.' is this line read with NU_055_truncation: they are verdicts read off the graph, after the gate built it. The gate's build is where NU_055_sound's premises hps (every place of S coloured) and hempty (the coloured places start empty) come from (NU_055_refusal_build_premises).
- Left out: 'Route B only' (no other route decides, no NU-053 fallback, the script encoders return none) and the routing rule that sends a name-alignment property to Route B before a budget place; they are dispatch rules of the verifier pipeline, not refusals. The reason texts, the report lines and the Property: description are N.
- AC2 (an uncoloured place, the first in S, and an absent place, Unknown naming it, never Proven) is lines 1 and 6: NU_055_refusal_nonvacuous names ready on QuiescentNameAligned(box, ready) and on (box, ready, clr), and nope on (box, nope). AC3 (under BASE, Unknown naming EXTENDED) is line 2 on the BASE call of the worked example (nu055r_base); the report note naming the ignored relay declarations is NU-054's (AC5). AC2's absent place is anchored to the worked example (box, nope), like its uncoloured one. AC6 (typed registered under AlwaysAvailable, Unknown naming typed; a marked coloured place, Unknown, naming it where no earlier refusal applies: box on (box, list) with box marked) is lines 5 and 7. AC8 (the refusal order on the worked example) is lines 5, 6 and 7, all three of its calls in NU_055_refusal_nonvacuous. AC6's 'on the buggy variant' and AC8's report wording are fixture tests (Q); the gate reads the same facts on both variants.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_055_sound"></a>
## NU-055: Name Alignment: soundness

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_sound` · Kind **B** · Scope every verifier that offers NameAligned or QuiescentNameAligned (MAY), judged against the reference ν executor, untimed and environment-free, with atomic firings · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 d20b41b4b40c0e65 ai** · Statement hash `d20b41b4b40c0e65`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| **NameAligned(S)**, for a non-empty list `S` of places: in every reachable marking, the places of `S` together hold at most one distinct name.<br><br>**QuiescentNameAligned(S)**: the same predicate, read only in the reachable quiescent markings.<br><br>Lean `Novel/RouteB/Aligned.lean` (`routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound`, `routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound`) proves: for the **untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings**, a `Proven` of either property holds in every marking that executor reaches (for the quiescent form, every marking at which it rests): the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name.<br><br>*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches.<br><br>*If* the premises above hold, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` only if the tokens in the places of `S` all carry the same name in every marking that the untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings reaches and rests at, resting being read with the reapable set of the call ([VER-002]). | 1. **Assumptions**

- The executor is the reference ν firing RefNuFire (Reference/Nu.lean), untimed and environment-free, one atomic firing per step: a run is NuLink.RefNuRunB, a sequence of firings of transitions of X each of whose actions keeps the contract of the role Route B gives its transition (NuLink.NuContract): a declared mint writes one name no coloured place holds into every coloured place it writes (NU-010, ruling D78 (a), NuLink.nuContract_mint_iff), a coloured consumer writes only a name it received from a coloured input (NU-051, NU-054). This is design correction S7 (a): the lines are stated over the reference executor, as NU_050_soundB's are. The 'untimed, environment-free executor with atomic firings' of the Soundness paragraph is this run; Novel's NuStepC (Sim.lean), where a coloured consumer takes any resident name (ruling D16 is why that differs from EXEC-010's FIFO), is the graph's semantics the holds proof passes through, not the executor of the lines. A firing whose action breaks its contract is not a step of the run; the spec makes no claim about it.
- The premises are hypotheses (design correction S6), one per premise bullet of the Soundness paragraph: 'the coloured places start empty' (every place of co empty in M0); 'the mints and coloured consumers keep their contracts' (the run, above); 'the projection contract of [NU-050]' (NuProj at every marking a contract-keeping run reaches, one projection nameOf for every key and relay); 'every firing writes one token to each output place its branch names' (built into RefNuFire, IO-016 AC4); 'every place of S coloured' (ps ⊆ co; in the shipped verifier the refusal order enforces it, and the empty start with it: NU_055_refusal_build_premises); 'the conditions the classifier establishes (InFragment)', over the translated net; 'unguarded inputs', which needs no hypothesis since IO-006 removed guards and every translated input is unguarded (NuLink.guardFree_toNuTransB); and, for the quiescent form, PosKeys. B1Shape is the shape the bridge needs, which every transition that builds and that the classifier accepts as a join meets (CORE-030 AC3; Route B accepts only One and Exactly keys), as in NU_050_soundB.
- q.co.Nodup is not a spec premise and gets no premise bullet: it says the list the call holds is a set, as the spec's coloured set is and as the classifier's coloured order (Rust coloured_order, the co of the Lean theorems) lists each place once. It does not narrow the claim about a call the shipped pipeline makes. The Route B call's initial counts are those of M0 (AlignQueryR.call), the marking the runs start from.
- Conflict-only priority (NU-052) is off in the Route B call (AlignQueryR.call sets the conflict flag false), as in NU_050_soundB: the priority pass is the executor's (RefExec), not one firing's, so a reference run takes no priority and the translated net is explored with conflict false. The Soundness paragraph's 'Conflict-only priority ([NU-052]) applies as it does to every Route B property' is not a line here: a Proven under conflict priority is sound for Novel's NuStepC with the same prune (routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound and routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound take the conflict flag, cited), and its tie to RefExec's priority pass is NU-052's, as for every Route B property.
- The lines ask soundness for every coloured set and role assignment that meets InFragment, not only for the classifier's. That is the premise bullet as written ('the conditions the classifier establishes (InFragment)', a condition, not the classifier), and Route B alone takes co and role as inputs; the classifier's own output meets InFragment (classifyS_inFragment, Novel/RouteB/Classify.lean, NU-051). That the coloured set is the one the classifier computes for the call, not one the caller names, is the pipeline's and no block states it; how the set is computed is Q-tested (NU_051_colours' assumes).
- The lines are soundness only: a decider that never answers Proven meets them. Ruling D59 (a) reads VER-012's 'exact (sound and complete)' (clash ver-d#1) as sound against the executor and complete for the free-choice name semantics of the graph: soundness is this block; completeness against the graph is NU_055_truncation line 3 (a closed graph none of whose classes violates answers Proven) and VER-012's block. The holds proof is bridge B1 on contract-keeping runs (NuLink.refNuRunB_names_reach: every contract-keeping reference run is a NuStepC run of the translated net with conflict off) composed with routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound and routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound; for the quiescent form a reference rest is an executor rest of the translated net (nu055_execRests_of_nuRests), resting read with the names of the reapable transitions.
- The deciders are AlignDecider (glossary GlossaryNuVer.lean, witness refNameAligned) and QAlignDecider (here, witness refQuiescentNameAligned), asked on the Route B call of q (AlignQueryR.call; AlignQueryR.qcall adds the reapable set): Route B alone, from the initial class, with no refusal step and no routing. The quiescent line reads resting with the call's reapable set, the names of the reapable transitions of X, as the reap-aware quiescence of VER-002 does on the graph and NuRests does on the reference marking. Every refusal of the refusal order (steps 1 to 7: cancellation and budget, an absent place, Bounded(k) outside its premises, in-flight state, the fragment declines of EXTENDED and BASE, an arrival into a coloured place, a modelled environment place, an uncoloured place of S, a marked coloured place) and the 'Coloured places only' and 'Modelled injection' rules are the block NU_055_refusal (NU_055_steps.lean), worded under ruling D20 (clashes nu-c#7, nu-c#9, NC-7, NC-8).
- Three rules of the section are dispatch and classifier rules of the verifier pipeline, not lines of any NU-055 block: 'Route B only' (no other route decides, no NU-053 fallback, no script); the rule that sends these properties to Route B before a budget place; and 'an implementation MUST lift both gates for the name-alignment properties, and only for them', the classifier's no-fragment for a net without a matched transition (Rust classify, whose matchless flag is set from property.is_name_alignment()) and the dispatcher's flat-phase routing of such a net (the name_alignment trigger of verify_net). NU_053_dispatch models the routing: its routeB guard enters Route B on a name-alignment call whatever the join and budget flags, and on any other call only with a ν-join. The classifier gate is lifted here by construction: the lines take every co and role that meet InFragment, a net without a matched transition included (the nonvacuous example is one).
- Not covered, as the spec itself says: the timed name × time graph the shipped Route B builds (gap R6 of Novel/RouteB/Sound.lean), the all-immediate worked example included; markings with actions in flight (the reference run has none); faithfulness of a carrier's name to what its token is about, which rests on the unchecked contracts of NU-051.
- AC1 (the worked example under EXTENDED: QuiescentNameAligned(box, list) and QuiescentCount Proven, NameAligned(box, list) Violated in 8 firings, the buggy variant Violated in 12, each attributed to Route B) is a fixture test (Q): the graph of that net is not computed in Lean. Its Proven verdicts are the kind lines 1 and 2 make sound; its Violated verdicts and witness lengths are graph facts.
- AC2 (an uncoloured or absent place gives Unknown naming it, the first in S) and AC6 (an environment place under AlwaysAvailable gives Unknown naming it, a marked coloured place gives Unknown naming it) and AC8 (the refusal order on the worked example) are lines 1, 5, 6 and 7 of NU_055_refusal. AC3 (under BASE the net is outside the fragment, the reason names EXTENDED and the report names the ignored relay declarations) is its line 2; the report note naming the ignored relay declarations is NU-054's (AC5). AC4 (no other route decides; the script encoders return none) is the pipeline's 'Route B only' rule, not encoded; its last clause (a truncation stays Unknown unless the prefix rule finds a violation) is NU_055_truncation lines 2 and 5.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_sound_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): The shipped deciders satisfy NU-055's soundness lines: B1 makes every contract-keeping reference run a run of Route B's executor model on the translated net (`NuLink.refNuRunB_names_reach`), and `routeB_untimed_nameAligned_sound` and `routeB_untimed_quiescentNameAligned_sound` carry a `Proven` to every marking that run reaches (and, for the quiescent form, rests at).
  <pre>NU_055_sound refNameAligned refQuiescentNameAligned</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_sound_forbids_alwaysProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ A decider that always proves violates NU-055's soundness (line 1): two contract-keeping mints put the names `10` and `11` in place `0`.
  <pre>¬NU_055_sound nu055_alwaysProven refQuiescentNameAligned</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_055_sound_forbids_qAlwaysProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_055): ✗ A quiescent decider that always proves violates NU-055's soundness (line 2): after the two mints the budget is spent, the net rests, and place `0` holds the names `10` and `11`.
  <pre>¬NU_055_sound refNameAligned nu055_qAlwaysProven</pre>

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| It is therefore a function of the canonical key of a class ([VER-012] AC2), and deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph.<br><br>*When* the graph closes, Route B *shall* answer `Proven` for `NameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph is name-aligned on `S`, and for `QuiescentNameAligned(S)` exactly when every class of the graph at which the net rests is.<br><br>A graph that does not close within the class bound never yields `Proven` (Lean `Decide.truncated_never_proven`).<br><br>*If* the graph does not close, because the build reaches the class bound, runs out of total budget or is cancelled ([VER-013]), *then* Route B *shall not* answer `Proven` for either property.<br><br>*If* the graph does not close and the prefix rule finds no violation, *then* Route B *shall* answer `Unknown`.<br><br>*If* Route B answers `Violated` for either property, *then* the class its counterexample ends at *shall* violate the property.<br><br>The prefix rule of [VER-012] AC3 applies: a `NameAligned` violated by a stored class, or a `QuiescentNameAligned` violated by an expanded class at which the net rests (every firing out of it is of a reapable transition; with nothing reapable, an expanded class with no successor, Lean `Decide.quiescentAt`), is `Violated` with the shortest witness in the explored graph and a report line naming the truncation; otherwise the verdict is `Unknown`. | 1. **Assumptions**

- The model is a verdict function on a built graph (Decide.Out: the stored classes in discovery order, the number expanded, whether the build closed and whether it stopped) and a property (Decide.Prop'), restricted to the two name-alignment properties (AlignProp) on a non-empty S, the only S that reaches a verdict (NU_055's assumes). How the build stores and expands classes is Decide.build's, cited by NU_055_sound through the soundness theorems; it is not a line here.
- 'Does not close' is o.complete = false: in the shipped build that is the class bound reached, the early stop (for NameAligned, a build that stops at its first violating class, VER-012 AC5), the total budget or a cancellation (cut). In the Lean model the fuel running out is a stopped build, as a cut is (Decide.loop with fuel 0 gives stopped = true). The quoted Truncation sentence names the class bound only; its EARS restatement names the budget and the cancellation as well, as VER-013 does for every route and refusal step 1 does for a call cancelled or out of budget before it starts. Lines 1 and 2 hold for each cause.
- Line 3 is 'deciding it on the name-permutation quotient decides it on the graph', read on the verdict, and its EARS restatement: on a closed graph, Proven exactly when no class violates the property. Under ruling D59 (a) (clash ver-d#1, VD-1 (a)), 'exact (sound and complete)' is sound against the executor (NU_055_sound) and complete for the free-choice name semantics of the graph, which is this line: a closed graph with no violating class answers Proven. Line 3 says that a closed graph with a violating class does not answer Proven; that it answers Violated is the prefix rule on a graph that was not stopped (NU_050_prefix line 2, on the same ClassVerdict), which line 5 states for a graph that did not close. Its premise o.stopped = false rules out only an outcome the build never makes (Decide.loop: a closed build is never stopped).
- Line 4 is the EARS restatement of the Violated paragraph's 'to a violating class': the class a Violated names violates the property, for NameAligned a stored class and for QuiescentNameAligned an expanded resting class. The paragraph's first sentence is not quoted, because the line encodes only its 'to a violating class': the rest of it (the shortest path, the attribution to Route B, counterexampleConfirmed absent, counterexampleTiming) is VER-003's and VER-012's report shape under ruling D40 (a) (clash ver-a#11): a trace carries a guarantee against the executor only when counterexampleConfirmed is true, and Route B leaves it absent, so a Violated is sound for the graph only; the report fields are kind N and the trace on the fixtures kind Q. The line does not model the counterexample path: it reads 'the class its counterexample ends at' as the class index the Violated verdict carries (Decide.verdict), the class the reported shortest path ends at; that identification is assumed here, not stated, and the path's shape is VER-003's under D40 (a). For QuiescentNameAligned the line is stronger than the sentence's 'violate the property': the class is an expanded one at which the net rests, as the prefix rule of the Truncation paragraph reads it. The line has no closure premise, so it holds on a truncated graph too, matching the prefix rule's 'violated by a stored class' and 'violated by an expanded class at which the net rests'.
- Line 5 is the prefix rule of the Truncation paragraph under ruling D59 (a) (clash nu-b#1): a graph that did not close answers Violated when a stored class violates NameAligned, or an expanded class at which the net rests violates QuiescentNameAligned, as Rust, Java and TypeScript do (nu_scg_verifier.rs, NuScgVerifier.java, nu-scg-verifier.ts; NU_050_prefix line 2 states it for every property on the same ClassVerdict). 'Does not close within the class bound' is o.complete = false with o.stopped = false: a build that reached the class bound, or one that ended at the early stop (for NameAligned, a build that stops at its first violating class, VER-012 AC5), which holds a violating class, so Violated is the right answer there. A build stopped by the total budget or a cancellation answers Unknown whatever its prefix holds (VER-013, NU_050_prefix line 1), and the Lean fuel running out is such a stopped build, so line 5 reads o.stopped = false. Its 'otherwise the verdict is Unknown' is line 2. The verdict that answers Unknown on every graph that did not close (D59 (b)) meets lines 1 to 4 and is killed by line 5 (NU_055_truncation_forbids_unknownWhenCut, NU_055_truncation_mutant_noPrefix_killed). The 'shortest witness in the explored graph' and the 'report line naming the truncation' are the report shape (VER-003, kind N) and the witness lengths on the fixtures are Q; line 5 asks only for a Violated, whose class line 4 fixes.
- AC4's last clause ('a Route B truncation stays Unknown unless the prefix rule finds a violation') is lines 1, 2 and 5; the rest of AC4 is accounted for in NU_055_sound's assumes.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-NU_060"></a>
## NU-060: Match-Arc Composition

`Libpetri.Spec.NU_060` · Kind **F** · Scope channel composition in every implementation: the merge of a caller-side transition with the instance-side channel transition it is bound to, when either carries a ν-net match · Source **verbatim** (spec/12-nu-nets.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 616cb528cb206c85 ai** · Statement hash `616cb528cb206c85`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A correlated input behaves, under channel composition ([MOD-021]), as the input arc it layers on: its arc dedup/conflict rules are unchanged.<br><br>A merge MUST NOT silently drop a match, and no implementation fuses two matches into one: when both merged sides carry a match, whatever places the two matches correlate, the merge MUST be rejected with an error naming the caller-side transition.<br><br>*When* at most one side of a channel merge carries a match, the channel merge *shall* reject with the same error when the same merge of the two transitions without their matches rejects, and otherwise *shall* give the merged transition of that merge with that side's match unchanged, or with no match when neither side carries one.<br><br>*If* both sides of a channel merge carry a match, *then* the channel merge *shall* be rejected with an error that names the caller-side transition. | 1. For every plain channel merge Mg (MOD-021's, on definitions without a match) and every ν channel merge NMg of the same implementation (on definitions c, i that may carry a match):<br>2. line 1: if c or i carries no match, NMg c i is Mg applied to c and i without their matches, with every success given the match c.mspec.or i.mspec (c's when c has one, i's when i has one, none when neither has one), and every rejection the same rejection;<br>3. line 2: if c and i both carry a match, NMg c i fails with a message that contains c's name. | <pre>fun {N A K} Mg NMg ↦<br>  (∀ (c i : NuCDef N A K),<br>      c.mspec = none ∨ i.mspec = none →<br>        NMg c i =<br>          Except.map (fun x ↦ NuCDef.ofCDef x (c.mspec.or i.mspec))<br>            (Mg c.toCDef i.toCDef)) ∧<br>    ∀ (c i : NuCDef N A K) (ms ms' : MatchSpec N K),<br>      c.mspec = some ms →<br>        i.mspec = some ms' → ∃ m, NMg c i = Except.error m ∧ mod021_names m c.core.name</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Model scope. A ν merge takes the caller-side definition c and the instance-side channel definition i, each a CDef (MOD-021's definition with the MOD-031 declared-place correspondence) with an optional match specification (NuCDef), and gives the merged definition or a rejection message, as Rust merge_transitions (rust/libpetri-core/src/rewriter.rs:611-698, with merge_match_specs at :708-727), Java SubnetRewriter.mergeTransitions (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/SubnetRewriter.java:529-598, mergeMatchSpecs at :616-624) and TypeScript mergeTransitions (typescript/src/core/internal/subnet-rewriter.ts:483-555, mergeMatchSpecs at :566-577) do; Python uses the Rust code. The block relates the ν merge to the plain merge Mg of the same implementation, whose lines are MOD-021's; the witness is refNuMerge Mg for every Mg (NU_060_reference), and refNuMerge (refMerge Build sq cm) satisfies both blocks (NU_060_with_MOD_021). The scope of MOD-021 (ruling D42 (m): a caller-side transition not yet in the builder and with no arc on a port bound in the same call) applies here too.
- Ruling D81 (a), clash nu-b#7: every runtime rejects a merge in which both sides carry a match, whatever places the two matches key, and none fuses two matches (merge_match_specs and mergeMatchSpecs compare no places). The markdown said 'on the same place' and allowed 'fuse to a single coherent correlation or reject'; it now states the runtime rule. The literal old reading, rejecting only matches that share a place and fusing the others, is the wrong model of NU_060_forbids_fuseDisjoint; keeping the caller's match is NU_060_forbids_callerWins.
- Line 1 says that a match changes nothing else about the merge: timing, priority, action, the output specification, the inhibitor, read and reset arcs and the input arcs are merged as MOD-021 merges them, and the same pairs are rejected with the same messages (NU_060_forbids_ownError: a merge that reports its own message for a pair with one match that the plain merge rejects; NU_060_forbids_rejectShared: a merge that rejects a pair with one match that the plain merge accepts). The definitions that enter a merge are built transitions, so each side's match already passes NU-020's and NU-054's build checks on its own side; line 1 is also stated for definitions whose match would fail them, which no runtime hands to the merge. In the runtimes the one match passes merge_match_specs unchanged, and the merged transition goes through the transition builder with the match, whose NU-020 checks pass again for such a match: the keys of the surviving match are still input places of the merged transition and its relay targets still output places (refNuMerge_keysOnInputs, refNuMerge_relaysOK, shown on the reference; the builder's own checks are MOD-021's line 7). A merged transition carries the surviving match unchanged, key projections and relay targets included; no place remap happens at the merge, since both sides already name host places (the remap is NU-030's, done by the rewrite before the merge).
- Consequence for the correlated input: with MOD-021, a success of the ν merge has the input arcs MOD-021's line 2 gives, correlated or not, and keeps the match (NU_060_table). The sentence 'A correlated input is therefore merged by the canonical input-arc merge table like any other input arc' holds of this block together with MOD-021, not of this block alone, so it is not quoted here: NU_060_table carries it as cited evidence. A correlated one() on P and the other side's one() on P give one exactly(2) arc on P that the match still keys (NU_060_nonvacuous); the other side's uncorrelated one() therefore stops taking the queue head and takes a token of the chosen name, as ruling D16 reads a correlated input. Keeping the match with the correlated arc at its pre-merge count is the wrong model of NU_060_forbids_countStays.
- Line 2 claims a rejection that names the caller-side transition, not which reason the message gives. Rust and TypeScript check the timing before the matches, Java checks the arc kinds and then the timing before the matches (rewriter.rs:624-634, SubnetRewriter.java:544-548, subnet-rewriter.ts:496-511), so a pair that also breaks a rule of MOD-021 is rejected with that rule's message in some runtimes; each of those messages names the caller-side transition too (MOD-021 lines 8 and 9). The markdown sentence 'Which error a merge reports when it also breaks a rule of [MOD-021] is not specified.' says so. The reference checks the matches first; the message text is a stand-in (nuMatchMsg).
- AC1 (composing a transition that carries a match with a side that carries none preserves the match on the flat net) is line 1 with NU_060_neverDrops: a success carries the caller's match when the caller has one and the instance's when the instance has one (NU_060_nonvacuous: a matched join keyed on P and R merged with a passthrough side keeps its keys P and R; a plain caller merged with a matched channel transition keyed on U and V keeps U and V). Putting the merged definition into the composed net is MOD-020's. Dropping the match is NU_060_forbids_dropMatch, keeping the caller's match only NU_060_forbids_callerOnly.
- AC2 (a merge of two transitions that both carry a match is rejected with an error naming the caller-side transition, whatever places the two matches correlate) is line 2 (NU_060_nonvacuous: join T keyed on P and R against a channel transition keyed on U and V is rejected naming T).
- Mutants: line 1 is load-bearing (NU_060_mutant_line2Only_killed: a merge that drops every match but rejects two matches meets line 2 alone); line 2 is load-bearing (NU_060_mutant_line1Only_killed: caller wins meets line 1 alone); the naming in line 2 is load-bearing (NU_060_mutant_anyMessage_killed: a rejection with an empty message).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✓ The reference ν merge satisfies NU-060 over every plain merge: with at most one match it runs the plain merge and attaches that match, and with two matches it rejects with a message that starts `Channel composition '<caller>'`.
  <pre>∀ {N A K : Type} (Mg : MergeFn N A), NU_060 Mg (refNuMerge Mg)</pre>

  <pre>¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_fuseDisjoint mergeEx)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_forbids_ownError` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✗ Worked example: a merge that reports its own error. The join `T` takes one token from `P` by name; the channel transition takes every token from `P`. `one()` and `all()` have no merge, so the plain merge rejects with the message about the two arcs on `P`. This merge rejects with the message about two matches, although only `T` has a match, so line 1 fails: the same pair must be rejected with the same message.
  <pre>¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_ownError mergeEx)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_forbids_rejectShared` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✗ Worked example: a merge that refuses to merge a correlated arc with an uncorrelated one. The join `T` keyed on `P` and `R` merged with a channel transition that also takes one token from `P` must give one `exactly(2)` arc on `P` that the match still keys, as the plain merge does; this merge rejects the pair, so line 1 fails.
  <pre>¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_rejectShared mergeEx)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_mutant_anyMessage_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✗ Worked example: a merge that rejects two matched sides with an empty message meets line 1 and rejects the pair, but the message does not name the caller `T`. The naming in line 2 is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_060_mutant_anyMessage mergeEx (nu060_silent mergeEx) ∧<br>  ¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_silent mergeEx)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_mutant_line1Only_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✗ Worked example: caller wins meets line 1 (with at most one match it is the plain merge with that match), but not NU-060: two matched sides merge. Line 2 is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_060_mutant_line1Only mergeEx (nu060_callerWins mergeEx) ∧<br>  ¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_callerWins mergeEx)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_mutant_line2Only_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✗ Worked example: the merge that drops every match meets line 2 (it rejects two matches, naming the caller), but not NU-060: a matched join merged with a passthrough side loses its match. Line 1 is load-bearing.
  <pre>NU_060_mutant_line2Only mergeEx (nu060_dropMatch mergeEx) ∧<br>  ¬NU_060 mergeEx (nu060_dropMatch mergeEx)</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.NU_060_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.NU_060): ✓ Worked example on the reference merge (the reference builder, list actions). A join `T` that takes one token each from `P` and `R` by name, merged with a passthrough channel transition that takes from `X`, gives one transition taking from `P`, `R` and `X` that still joins on `P` and `R`. If the channel transition instead takes one token from `P` too, the two `one()` arcs on `P` become one `exactly(2)` arc, and the match still keys `P`: the merged join takes two tokens of the chosen name there. A plain caller merged with a matched channel transition keeps the channel transition's match on `U` and `V`. Two matched sides are rejected with the message that starts `Channel composition 'T'`.
  <pre>nu060_view (refNuMerge mergeEx nu060_join nu060_side) =<br>    some ([("P", Card.one), ("R", Card.one), ("X", Card.one)], some ["P", "R"]) ∧<br>  nu060_view (refNuMerge mergeEx nu060_join nu060_sideP) =<br>      some ([("P", Card.exactly 2), ("R", Card.one)], some ["P", "R"]) ∧<br>    nu060_view (refNuMerge mergeEx nu060_plain nu060_joinUV) =<br>        some ([("X", Card.one), ("U", Card.one), ("V", Card.one)], some ["U", "V"]) ∧<br>      nu060_msg (refNuMerge mergeEx nu060_join nu060_joinUV) = some (nuMatchMsg "T")</pre>
