<a id="Libpetri-Spec-PERF_030"></a>
## PERF-030: Bitmap Memory Efficiency

`Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030` · Kind **F** · Scope bitmap executors (the BitmapNetExecutor of Java, TypeScript and Rust; Python through Rust) · Source **verbatim** (spec/10-performance.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 29912da2d6f403c4 ai** · Statement hash `29912da2d6f403c4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| For a net with P places and T transitions, the bitmap executor *shall* keep its presence bitmap in at most ceil(P / word_size) words, each full-width mask of a transition in at most ceil(P / word_size) words of word_size bits, and its dirty set in at most ceil(T / word_size) words.<br><br>The bitmap executor *shall* keep at most k full-width masks per transition, for one number k that the implementation fixes and that does not depend on the net, and no full-width mask words beside those masks.<br><br>Together the three structures take at most (1 + k × T) × ceil(P / word_size) + ceil(T / word_size) words. | 1. At word size ws (ws > 0), for every net n with P places (placeCountOf n) and T transitions:<br>2. the presence bitmap kept for n takes at most ceil(P / ws) words;<br>3. there is one number k, chosen before the net, such that every transition of every net has at most k full-width masks;<br>4. every full-width mask of a transition of n has at most ceil(P / ws) words, each a number below 2^ws;<br>5. the dirty set kept for n takes at most ceil(T / ws) words;<br>6. no mask is kept at an ID j that is no transition's (j ≥ T), so every word the mask structure holds is a word of a transition's mask. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] ws L ↦<br>  0 &lt; ws →<br>    (∀ (n : Reference.Net N), L.presence n ≤ ceilDiv (placeCountOf n) ws) ∧<br>      (∃ k,<br>          ∀ (n : Reference.Net N), ∀ j &lt; n.transitions.length, (L.masks n j).length ≤ k) ∧<br>        (∀ (n : Reference.Net N),<br>            ∀ j &lt; n.transitions.length,<br>              ∀ m ∈ L.masks n j,<br>                m.length ≤ ceilDiv (placeCountOf n) ws ∧ ∀ x ∈ m, x &lt; 2 ^ ws) ∧<br>          (∀ (n : Reference.Net N), L.dirty n ≤ ceilDiv n.transitions.length ws) ∧<br>            ∀ (n : Reference.Net N) (j : ℕ), n.transitions.length ≤ j → L.masks n j = []</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a bitmap layout (BitmapLayout): for a net, the number of words of the presence bitmap, the full-width masks kept at the ID j (the transition with ID j, its declaration position, CONC-007) as lists of words, and the number of words of the dirty set. The presence bitmap and the dirty set are run state whose content depends on the marking, so only their size is modelled; the masks are compiled data and are modelled as their words, so that line 3 can say what a word is. A faithful layout holds every word the mask structure allocates, read or not: a word that lies in no transition's mask (the unread tail of a flat array allocated too large) sits at an ID that is no transition's. P is placeCountOf n, the places of the net each once (declared places and every place an arc or an output specification names), which is the place count of the compiled net (placeCountOf_eq, CONC-007); T is the number of transitions. The word size is 64 in Rust and Java and 32 in TypeScript, as the markdown says.
- The reference layout refBitmapLayout keeps, per transition, the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask of the reference compiled net (refCompileNet) packed into words by packBits, and no mask at an ID that is no transition's, so its masks are RefCompiled's mask words (refBitmapLayout_maskWords) and its total is RefCompiled's layoutWords, (1 + 2 × T) × ceil(P / ws) + ceil(T / ws) (refBitmapLayout_total). Its mask count is refMaskCount = 2: under ruling D55 (a) there is no reset-mask, since Rust and TypeScript keep the consumption places as a list and the reset-mask Java builds is read by no executor.
- Line 2 is the mask count fixed per implementation (ruling D55 (a), PERF-R1 (a)): the number k is chosen before the net, so a layout whose number of masks grows with the net, one mask per arc of the transition (PERF_030_mutant_perArc), has no such k. The block fixes no value of k and sets no absolute memory cap: the markdown gives the values of the current implementations as information, k = 2 in Rust and TypeScript (the reference) and k = 5 in Java (the needs, inhibitor and reset BitSets and long-array copies of the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java:59-65), and a layout with five masks per transition meets the block (PERF_030_allows_five). Which masks must be kept (the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask) is CONC-007's line, not this block's: PERF-030 bounds memory only, so a layout that keeps fewer masks meets it.
- A word of word_size bits is a number below 2^ws. Line 3 states it for the masks, so a layout that counts a wider number as one word is not a smaller layout (PERF_030_forbids_wideWords: masks of two-place numbers counted as 1-bit words). The presence bitmap and the dirty set are modelled by their size only and carry no such clause.
- Line 5 is the quoted words no full-width mask words beside those masks: with it every word the mask structure holds is bounded, wherever a layout places it. Without it, flat mask arrays allocated with T × P words while the stride stays ceil(P / ws) (a hypothetical slip: flat mask arrays sized with the place count instead of the word count; Rust sizes its needs_masks and inhibitor_masks with word_count, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:92-93) would meet lines 1 to 4, since every transition reads a slice of ceil(P / ws) words and the unread tail lies past the last slice (PERF_030_mutant_flatTail: on AC2's net 10003 words, perf030_flatTail_ac2). Placing the same tail inside a transition's masks is killed by line 3 or line 2, and spreading it over many IDs past T is killed by line 5, so the verdict no longer depends on where a model puts the words.
- One wrong layout per line, each meeting the other four: a presence bitmap with one word per place (PERF_030_mutant_presencePerPlace, line 1), one mask per arc (PERF_030_mutant_perArc, line 2), masks with one word per place (PERF_030_mutant_wordPerPlace, line 3: on the AC2 net one word per place-transition pair and mask, 10003 words, perf030_wordPerPlace_ac2), a dirty set with one word per transition (PERF_030_mutant_dirtyPerTransition, line 4) and flat mask arrays with an unread tail past the last transition (PERF_030_mutant_flatTail, line 5).
- The third quoted sentence is a consequence of the five lines, not a line of its own: a layout that meets PERF-030 keeps at most (1 + k × T) × ceil(P / ws) + ceil(T / ws) words for every net, with the k of line 2 (PERF_030_total), and by line 5 the bound holds for the mask words at every ID, not only at the transitions' (PERF_030_held).
- The block counts words, not bytes: the heap cost of a mask object (a Java BitSet or long array, a TypeScript typed array, a Rust Vec) is not counted, which is why ruling D55 (a) states AC2 in words; a byte number would be false of Java. Further bitmaps an executor keeps beside the three structures (a copy of the presence bitmap or of the dirty set taken for one pass, the sets of enabled, in-flight, restart-pending or timed transitions, such as Java's timedMask, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java:195-196) are outside the count, as the markdown says. A set of transitions is indexed by transition ID and is not a full-width mask: line 5 constrains only the mask words at transition IDs, which a set of transitions is not.
- AC1 (the three structures take at most (1 + k × T) × ceil(P / word_size) + ceil(T / word_size) words, which grows with T × ceil(P / word_size), not with P × T) is PERF_030_total and PERF_030_held. A layout with one word per place in each mask grows with P × T and breaks it (PERF_030_mutant_wordPerPlace, perf030_wordPerPlace_ac2), as does a flat mask array of T × P words (PERF_030_mutant_flatTail, perf030_flatTail_ac2).
- AC2 (for 100 places and 50 transitions, at most (1 + 50 × k) × 2 + 1 words at 64-bit words, 203 for k = 2 and 503 for k = 5, and at most (1 + 50 × k) × 4 + 2 words at 32-bit words, 406 for k = 2) is PERF_030_ac2 and PERF_030_ac2_32: the reference on perf030Net, a net with 100 places and 50 transitions, keeps 203 words at 64 bits and 406 at 32 bits, and perf030_ac2_bound and perf030_ac2_bound_32 give the bounds for every k. The former wording ('< 1KB') was false of the reference: 203 words of 8 bytes are 1624 bytes (perf030_old_ac2_bytes).
- The test derivation (compile a 100-place, 50-transition net, sum the words that the presence bitmap, the mask arrays and the dirty set hold and compare the sum with AC2) is PERF_030_ac2 and PERF_030_ac2_32 on the reference. A runtime test that sums the allocated lengths of those arrays in an implementation is a quality test (kind Q); no test cites PERF-030 today.
- The block is about the bitmap executor's three structures. The sparse masks of the precompiled executor are PERF-042's; its flat arrays are PERF-040's (kind Q).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_030): ✓ The reference bitmap layout satisfies PERF-030 at every word size, with `k = 2` (its needs-mask and its inhibitor-mask), each packed into `⌈P / ws⌉` words of `ws` bits.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (ws : ℕ), PERF_030 ws (refBitmapLayout ws)</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030_allows_five` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_030): ✓ A layout with five masks per transition, as Java keeps, meets PERF-030 with `k = 5`: the requirement fixes the mask count per implementation, not at the reference's 2.
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (ws : ℕ), PERF_030 ws (perf030JavaLayout ws)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030_forbids_wideWords` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_030): ✗ Counting a mask packed into numbers of twice the word size as that many words violates PERF-030 through the word-size clause of line 3: at 1-bit words, transition `a` of the small net has the needs-mask packed into the one number `3`, which is no 1-bit word.
  <pre>¬PERF_030 1 (perf030WideWords 1)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030_mutant_dirtyPerTransition` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_030): ✗ A dirty set with one word per transition meets lines 1 to 3 and violates PERF-030 through line 4: the small net's two transitions take 2 words where `⌈2 / 64⌉ = 1`.

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_030_mutant_flatTail` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_030): ✗ Flat mask arrays of `T × P` words with the stride of `⌈P / ws⌉` meet lines 1 to 4 (every transition reads the reference's masks) and violate PERF-030 through line 5: on the small net the unread tails of the two arrays, 2 words each, lie at the ID 2, which is no transition's.

- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_all` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyAll): ✓ **The whole specification has one model.** One build check, one firing relation, one timing contract, one ready order, one timed step, one queue firing, one output validator, one transition builder, one snapshot, one composition, one environment verifier, one split, one exporter, one executor and one executor with events that steps as it meet every area at once: the CORE, IO, TIME, queue, structure, composition, ν, verifier, executor, event and export blocks, and the cross-model lines of wave W11. Over string place names the same witnesses also meet EVT-014, and every marking snapshot the executor reports is CORE-073's snapshot `Snap` of the declared places; CORE-037's warnings wrap the one executor and the one environment verifier, and MOD-051's `verify` runs the one instantiation, build script, entry check and environment verifier. Over flat place identities the one executor's runs are runs of the verifier's in-flight model by their counts (`CountAgrees`), so the split the verifier checks covers them (VER-004, block B).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-PERF_042"></a>
## PERF-042: Sparse Enablement Masks

`Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042` · Kind **F** · Scope executors that use sparse enablement masks (the precompiled executors) · Source **verbatim** (spec/10-performance.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 37bebb0ba41d2afe ai** · Statement hash `37bebb0ba41d2afe`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, it *shall* compile a needs-mask or an inhibitor-mask to the empty sentinel exactly when all its words are zero and a mask with exactly one non-zero word to the single-word form holding that word's index and value, and it *shall* put only non-zero words of the mask, each with its index, into a multi-word form.<br><br>*Where* an executor uses sparse enablement masks, its presence check on the sparse forms compiled from a transition's needs-mask and inhibitor-mask *shall* return, for every presence bitmap, the result of the presence check of [CONC-004] computed over every word of both masks.<br><br>These two sentences hold for masks and presence bitmaps of the same number of words, each word within the executor's word size.<br><br>Enablement results are identical to full-width bitmap checks. | 1. At word size w, for every mask m whose words are below 2^w:<br>2. C compiles m to the empty sentinel exactly when m has no non-zero word;<br>3. when m has exactly one non-zero word, x at index i, C compiles m to the single-word form (i, x);<br>4. when C compiles m to a multi-word form, every entry (i, x) of it has x non-zero and x the word of m at index i.<br>5. For every needs-mask, inhibitor-mask and presence bitmap of the same number of words, each below 2^w, C's presence check on the compiled forms of the two masks returns what the full-width presence check returns: every word of the needs-mask is contained in the bitmap's word of the same index, and no word of the inhibitor-mask shares a bit with it. | <pre>fun w C ↦<br>  (∀ (m : Words), FitsIn w m → (C.compile m = SparseMask.empty ↔ nonZeroOf m = [])) ∧<br>    (∀ (m : Words) (i x : ℕ),<br>        FitsIn w m → nonZeroOf m = [(i, x)] → C.compile m = SparseMask.single i x) ∧<br>      (∀ (m : Words) (es : List (ℕ × ℕ)),<br>          FitsIn w m →<br>            C.compile m = SparseMask.multi es → ∀ p ∈ es, p.2 ≠ 0 ∧ wordAt m p.1 = p.2) ∧<br>        ∀ (needs inhib snap : Words),<br>          FitsIn w needs →<br>            FitsIn w inhib →<br>              FitsIn w snap →<br>                List.length needs = List.length snap →<br>                  List.length inhib = List.length snap →<br>                    C.check (C.compile needs) (C.compile inhib) snap =<br>                      denseEnable needs inhib snap</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A bitmap is a list of words, each a natural number, and a word past the end of a bitmap reads as zero (glossary: Word). Every line is stated at a word size w for masks whose words are below 2^w (FitsIn), and line 4 for a needs-mask, an inhibitor-mask and a presence bitmap of the same number of words, as the runtimes build them (W words of 64 bits in Rust and Java, of 32 bits in TypeScript). So a check that reads its words at its own word size meets the line at that size (PERF_042_accepts_trunc); the reference reads unbounded naturals and meets it at every size.
- The model is a sparse check (SparseCheck): a compile step from a full-width mask to one of the body's three forms (SparseMask: the empty sentinel, one word with its index, a list of words with their indices) and a presence check on the sparse forms of the needs-mask and the inhibitor-mask. The runtimes compile the forms when the precompiled net is built (Rust from_arc and compile_sparse in precompiled_net.rs, Java PrecompiledNet, TypeScript precompiled-net.ts); a runtime's own encoding of the three cases is read through SparseMask. Line 4 constrains compile and check together, since the check only ever sees compiled forms; a compile slip (the signed 8-bit word index) breaks it as much as a check slip.
- Which place sits at which bit of which word is the compiled net's business ([CONC-007]); the join lemma denseEnable_maskCheck shows that, for any injective placement, the full-width check passes exactly when the glossary presence check (MaskCheck, [CONC-004]) passes, so the block needs no placement. [CONC-020] (a dependency) puts the sparse masks into the precompiled net's flat arrays; it bears on the scope only (the precompiled executors), so no line refers to it.
- The priority SHOULD is about whether an executor uses a sparse representation at all; the lines bind an executor that does (the Where clause of both sentences, and the spec sentence that says so in words), so for such an executor they are mandatory.
- The body sentence 'Enablement masks SHOULD use a sparse representation to avoid scanning zero words in large nets.', the cost halves of its three cases ('skip the check entirely', 'one AND + one compare operation', 'iterate only non-zero entries') and 'This avoids scanning W words when most are zero (common in large, sparse nets).' are about how the check is computed and what it costs, which a pure function cannot show; they are quality properties (kind Q) and are not encoded. The representation halves of the three cases ('Empty (sentinel value)', 'store word index + mask value', 'store only non-zero word indices and their mask values') are lines 1 to 3.
- AC1 (empty masks are detected and skipped with no computation) is line 1 for 'detected' (the sentinel stands for exactly the masks with no non-zero word; PERF_042_mutant_listOnly kills a compile step that never emits it) and line 4 for its result (an empty needs form passes and an empty inhibitor form blocks nothing; PERF_042_forbids_emptyBlocks kills a check that reads an empty inhibitor form as blocked). 'Skipped with no computation' is cost (kind Q), not encoded.
- AC2 (a single-word mask uses one AND and one compare, no loop) is line 2 for the form (a mask with one non-zero word compiles to its index and value; PERF_042_mutant_noSingle kills, through line 2 alone, a compile step that keeps the sentinel and puts such a mask in a one-entry list). 'One AND and one compare, no loop' is cost (kind Q), not encoded; PERF_042_forbids_signed kills the shipped slip in that compare.
- AC3 (a multi-word sparse mask iterates only non-zero words) is line 3 for the form (the multi-word form lists non-zero words of the mask only; PERF_042_mutant_allWords kills a compile step that keeps the zero words) and line 4 for its result (every non-zero word is checked; PERF_042_forbids_firstWord kills a check that reads the first only). That the check's loop walks the listed entries and nothing else is cost (kind Q), not encoded: a check that scans every word of the bitmap on correct forms meets the line.
- AC4 (enablement results identical to full-width bitmap checks) is line 4. The test derivation's net with 200 places whose transitions touch 2 or 3 places is line 4 on one net, exercised by the reference in PERF_042_twoHundredPlaces; its 'is faster' is a cost criterion (kind Q).
- The check is the presence phase only. The cardinality check and the ν-match check ([CONC-008]) are later phases and are not part of it; reset arcs and output arcs play no part (glossary: Presence check).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): The reference sparse check satisfies PERF-042 at every word size: it compiles to the empty sentinel exactly the masks with no non-zero word and a one-word mask to that word, its multi-word form is the list of non-zero words, and dropping zero words leaves the check unchanged, since a zero word is contained in every snapshot word and meets none (`compileSparse_containsAll`, `compileSparse_intersects`).
  <pre>∀ (w : ℕ), PERF_042 w refSparse</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_forbids_emptyBlocks` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ Reading an empty inhibitor mask as blocked violates PERF-042 (AC1's 'skipped'): a transition without inhibitor arcs whose input place is marked is never enabled.
  <pre>¬PERF_042 32 emptyBlocksSparse</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_forbids_firstWord` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ Reading the first non-zero word only violates PERF-042 (AC3's 'iterate only non-zero words' still means every non-zero word): a transition needing places in words 0 and 1 is enabled with the word-1 place empty.
  <pre>¬PERF_042 32 firstWordSparse</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_forbids_int8` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ The signed 8-bit word index violates PERF-042 at 32-bit words: a transition whose only input place sits in word 128 (place index 4096 and above) is enabled with that place empty.
  <pre>¬PERF_042 32 int8Sparse</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_forbids_signed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ The signed compare violates PERF-042 at 32-bit words: a transition whose input place is place 31 (bit 31 of word 0) is never enabled, also with the place marked.
  <pre>¬PERF_042 32 signedSparse</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_mutant_allWords` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ Keeping the zero words in the multi-word form meets line 4 (its results are right) and violates PERF-042 (AC3's 'only non-zero words', line 3): the mask `[0, 1]` is compiled to a list with the zero word 0 in it.
  <pre>ResultLineOnly 32 allWordsSparse ∧ ¬PERF_042 32 allWordsSparse</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_mutant_listOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ Never emitting the empty sentinel or the single-word form meets line 4 and violates PERF-042 (AC1's 'detected', line 1, and AC2's form, line 2): the empty mask `[]` is not compiled to the sentinel, and `[0, 5]` is compiled to a one-entry list instead of the single word 5 at index 1.
  <pre>ResultLineOnly 32 listOnlySparse ∧ ¬PERF_042 32 listOnlySparse</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_mutant_noSingle` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): ✗ A compile step with no single-word form meets lines 1, 3 and 4 (the sentinel is kept, the list holds only non-zero words, and every result is right) and violates PERF-042 through line 2 alone (AC2's form): the mask `[0, 5]` has the one non-zero word 5 at index 1 and is compiled to the one-entry list, not to the single-word form.
  <pre>PERF_042_withoutLine2 32 noSingleSparse ∧ ¬PERF_042 32 noSingleSparse</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): The line is exercised by the reference in each of the three sparse cases, for the needs-mask and for the inhibitor-mask, with both answers: the compiled forms are empty (`[]`, and `[0, 0]` whose words are all zero), single (`[0, 5]`, word 1) and multi (`[1, 0, 2]`, words 0 and 2); an empty needs-mask and an empty inhibitor-mask pass; a single-word needs-mask passes when its word is contained and fails when it is not; a multi-word needs-mask fails when its second non-zero word is missing; a single-word and a multi-word inhibitor-mask block when met and pass when not.
  <pre>refSparse.compile [] = SparseMask.empty ∧<br>  refSparse.compile [0, 0] = SparseMask.empty ∧<br>    refSparse.compile [0, 5] = SparseMask.single 1 5 ∧<br>      refSparse.compile [1, 0, 2] = SparseMask.multi [(0, 1), (2, 2)] ∧<br>        refSparse.check (refSparse.compile []) (refSparse.compile []) [] = true ∧<br>          refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [0, 0]) (refSparse.compile [0, 0]) [0, 0] =<br>              true ∧<br>            refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [0, 5]) (refSparse.compile [0, 0]) [0, 7] =<br>                true ∧<br>              refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [0, 5]) (refSparse.compile [0, 0])<br>                    [7, 1] =<br>                  false ∧<br>                refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0, 2])<br>                      (refSparse.compile [0, 0, 0]) [1, 0, 2] =<br>                    true ∧<br>                  refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0, 2])<br>                        (refSparse.compile [0, 0, 0]) [1, 9, 0] =<br>                      false ∧<br>                    refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0]) (refSparse.compile [0, 4])<br>                          [1, 4] =<br>                        false ∧<br>                      refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0])<br>                            (refSparse.compile [0, 4]) [1, 0] =<br>                          true ∧<br>                        refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0])<br>                              (refSparse.compile [2, 4]) [1, 0] =<br>                            true ∧<br>                          refSparse.check (refSparse.compile [1, 0])<br>                              (refSparse.compile [2, 4]) [1, 4] =<br>                            false</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.PERF_042_twoHundredPlaces` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.PERF_042): The test derivation's net: 200 places in 32-bit words (W = 7). Transition A needs places 5 and 70 (word 0 bit 5, word 2 bit 6) and is inhibited by place 199 (word 6 bit 7); transition B needs places 33 and 40 (word 1, bits 1 and 8) and has no inhibitor. **Assumptions**

- A contract is the accessors, the factories and the transition builder of one implementation over the five variants of the Rust enum (Novel.TimedScg.Timing), with bounds in milliseconds; a call that fails is read as `.error msg` with its message, a call that returns as `.ok`. `factory tm` is the factory of tm's variant called with tm's bounds; `build tm` builds a transition with tm written out directly (a Rust enum variant, a TypeScript object literal, a Java record constructor).
- Bounds are naturals, as Rust's `u64` arguments are, so the rows of the message table that check for a negative bound (TypeScript and Java only) and the `0 <=` halves of the validity table are not encoded. The messages are the Rust, TypeScript and Python form, with the argument printed in decimal milliseconds; Java's form (`MAX_DURATION (PT876000H)`, `Duration.toString()`) is the same table in another notation and is not encoded.
- 'The first rule the bounds break' together with 'The checks run in the order of the table' is encoded by the premises of lines 5 to 11: each line assumes the bounds pass every earlier rule of the variant (only `window` has rules the same bounds can break together; `deadline(0)` and `deadline(by > maximum)` exclude each other). Lines 4 to 11 fix the factory on every timing: a valid one is returned as written, an invalid one fails with exactly one message.
- AC1 (each transition has a timing, Immediate by default) is line 13: `defaultTiming` is the timing the builder gives a transition built without one. The default Delayed(0), which has the same interval [0, maximum] as Immediate, is killed as TIME_001_mutant_sameInterval.
- AC2 (earliest() and latest() are queryable) is lines 1 and 2; the value table of the accessors is the first two shall sentences.
- AC3 (hasDeadline() by variant whatever the bounds, so a Window whose latest bound equals the maximum still has a deadline) is line 3 (ruling D2). The older literal reading 'hasDeadline() is latest below the maximum' is killed as TIME_001_mutant_latestBelowMax, on window(0, maximum). That a transition SHOULD be disabled after its latest bound is keyed on Reapable (Deadline, Window), not on hasDeadline: Exact has a deadline but is enforced softly (TIME-006, TIME-013).
- The validity table of line 4 is Timing.Valid, the predicate the timed step, the state-class graph and the TIME-002 to TIME-006 blocks read (time001_valid_iff, cited).
- AC4 (the validity table is canonical; the boundary at the maximum duration for every bound, including deadline's by and window's latest, with the table's messages) is lines 4 to 11 (ruling D11). The nonvacuous example TIME_001_nonvacuous checks each boundary named in AC4 and in the test derivation, window(maximum + 1, maximum + 2) included. The old checks (Timing.ValidPre: deadline only 0 < by, window only earliest <= latest, delayed and exact nothing) are killed as TIME_001_mutant_validPre.
- AC5 (a timing written out without a factory is held to AC4 and to the factories' other checks, and a valid one builds unchanged) is line 12; TIME_001_forbids_uncheckedBuild is the builder that skips the check and passes delayed(maximum + 1) on to the verifier. Java's records check in their constructors, which the contract reads as a factory and a builder that agree.
- A factory returns the timing as written (line 4): a valid window(earliest, maximum) stays a Window and keeps its deadline (AC3); it is not normalised to delayed(earliest).
- The two body bullets are the rules of other blocks and are not encoded again: no firing before the earliest bound since the transition was armed is TIME-010 (cited by time001_fire_after_earliest), and reaping a reapable transition once its elapsed time exceeds latest plus the deadline tolerance is TIME-013 (cited by time001_reap_past_latest). That Immediate and Delayed have no finite latest bound and their latest() reports the maximum duration is line 2; reading the maximum as no bound at all is not proven (Novel.TimedScg.Timing, module docstring).
- The maximum-duration constant is maxDurationMs = 3153600000000 (time001_maxDuration); Java's MAX_DURATION is Duration.ofDays(36500), the same duration. Java's sixth variant `Unconstrained` is not in the spec and not modelled.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_002"></a>
## TIME-002: Immediate Timing

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 dd46f1ae494fe220 ai** · Statement hash `dd46f1ae494fe220`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition with `Immediate` timing is armed, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready ([TIME-010]).<br><br>The executor *shall not* reap a transition with `Immediate` timing ([TIME-013]). | 1. For every timed net X and every transition u the net holds under its name, with timing Immediate:<br>2. while u is armed, the step relation has every firing of u that the reference semantics has, with the same successor marking;<br>3. no step disarms u while it stays enabled (StaysArmed): when the net's names are distinct, every step other than a reap of u, a firing of u itself included, leaves u armed if u was armed before it and is enabled after it;<br>4. the step relation has no reap of u. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N),<br>    InNet X u →<br>      TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.immediate →<br>        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            Armed s u → RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧<br>          StaysArmed R X u ∧ ∀ (s s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.reap u) s'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt); a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic, and the relation may be late: a delay may pass any bound. Armed, Elapsed time, Ready and Reapable are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean).
- Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. Readiness is read through the step relation: a transition whose timing does not stop it is one the relation may fire. Immediate has earliest bound 0 and is not reapable, so it is ready whenever it is armed, at every elapsed time, also past its finite latest() (the maximum duration). The firing order among ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is EXEC-002 and is not part of an atomic step.
- Line 2 is the same sentence for steps that would make u not ready by disarming it while it stays enabled, whatever the label of the step; TIME_002_forbids_drop shows a firing of another transition that drops u's stamp, and TIME_002_forbids_selfDrop a firing of u itself that leaves u enabled and unarmed. It is the frame StaysArmed shared with TIME-003 to TIME-006 (GlossaryTime.lean); its exception for the reap of u is empty here, by line 3. Distinct names (NamesDistinct, ruling D10) are needed because stamps are kept per name, so the reap of another transition of the same name would drop u's stamp. A firing that leaves u enabled re-arms it, possibly with a fresh stamp (TIME-012); this line says only that u stays armed.
- Line 3 is the second 'shall' sentence: no reap step of u exists at all. Together with line 2 it excludes a reap under another label.
- The interval [0, ∞), earliest() = 0, latest() = maximum duration and hasDeadline() = false are the Timing accessors (time002_interval, cited); the reading of the maximum duration as no bound (ruling D11) is what line 1 and line 3 state for the executor.
- AC1 (fires immediately when enabled) is read as readiness, line 1, exercised in TIME_002_nonvacuous at elapsed time 0. Line 1 speaks of an armed transition; 'when enabled' becomes 'when armed' only through TIME-010 (a transition enabled in the initial marking or after a firing that writes one of its arc places is newly armed) and TIME-012, which ConsistencyTime conjoins: an executor that never arms a newly enabled Immediate transition meets this block on its own. That it fires on the next cycle, before any other ready transition, is the eager Phase 2 executor's and EXEC-002's, not an atomic step's (ruling D3). AC2 (no deadline enforcement) is lines 2 and 3, exercised in TIME_002_nonvacuous past the maximum duration plus the tolerance, where u is still armed, still fires and has no reap.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): The timed reference step satisfies TIME-002: an `Immediate` transition has earliest bound 0 and is never expired under `refPolicy` (it is not reapable), so an armed one fires with every reference firing (line 1), no reap of it exists (line 3), and every other step leaves it armed if it is enabled after (line 2, `staysArmed_of`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], TIME_002 RefTStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_forbids_drop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): ✗ An executor whose firing disarms a still-enabled armed `Immediate` transition violates TIME-002 (line 2): at `T = 0` `v` fires, writing none of `u`'s arc places, `u` stays enabled, and the step drops `u`'s stamp, so `u` is no longer ready.
  <pre>¬TIME_002 (RefTStepW time002_dropPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_forbids_idle` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): ✗ An executor that does not fire an armed `Immediate` transition violates TIME-002 (line 1): at `T = 0` the transition `u` is armed and has a reference firing, which the idle relation does not take.
  <pre>¬TIME_002 time002_idle</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_forbids_selfDrop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): ✗ An executor whose firing of `u` itself leaves `u` enabled but unarmed violates TIME-002 (line 2): with two tokens in `u`'s input place at `T = 0`, `u` fires and stays enabled, and the self-drop policy gives it no clock, a reap hidden in its own firing.
  <pre>¬TIME_002 (RefTStepW selfDropPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_mutant_reapMax_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): The step that reaps `Immediate` at the maximum duration kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-002, since at `T = MAX_DURATION_MS + 6` it reaps `u`, armed since `0` (line 3).
  <pre>TIME_002_mutant_reapMax (RefTStepW time002_reapMaxPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_002 (RefTStepW time002_reapMaxPolicy)</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_002_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_002): Every line of TIME-002 is exercised by the reference step, with tolerance 5 ms. AC1: armed at `T = 0` (elapsed 0), `u` fires (line 1). AC2: a delay to `T = MAX_DURATION_MS + 6` keeps `u` armed (line 2); there its elapsed time is past its finite `latest()` plus the tolerance, yet it still fires (line 1) and has no reap (line 3), where the mutant reading reaps it.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_003"></a>
## TIME-003: Deadline Timing

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_003` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 d4286d66f31f5dbe ai** · Statement hash `d4286d66f31f5dbe`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition with `Deadline(by)` timing is armed, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready until it is expired.<br><br>*If* a transition with `Deadline(by)` timing is armed and its elapsed time exceeds `by` plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it ([TIME-013]). | 1. For every timed net X and every transition u the net holds under its name, with timing Deadline(by):<br>2. while u is armed and its elapsed time is not greater than by plus the tolerance, the step relation has every firing of u that the reference semantics has, with the same successor marking;<br>3. no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance;<br>4. from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance, the step relation has a reap of u;<br>5. a reap of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than by plus the tolerance, and leaves u not armed;<br>6. u's clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but the reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (b : ℕ),<br>    InNet X u →<br>      TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.deadline b →<br>        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            Armed s u →<br>              ¬b + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u →<br>                RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧<br>          (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ b + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u, never fun s s' ↦<br>              ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>            (∀ (s : TSt N),<br>                Armed s u →<br>                  b + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧<br>              (on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>                  Armed s u ∧ b + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u ∧ ¬Armed s' u) ∧<br>                ClockFrame R X u</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt); a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic, and the relation may be late: a delay may pass any bound. Armed, Elapsed time, Expired, Reaped and Deadline tolerance are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean). For a Deadline(by) transition, expired is exactly armed with an elapsed time strictly greater than by plus the tolerance, since Deadline is reapable and its latest bound is by.
- Line 1 is the first 'shall' sentence. Readiness is read through the step relation: a transition whose timing does not stop it is one the relation may fire. Its earliest bound is 0, so the only timing obstacle is expiry, and line 1 asks for every reference firing up to and including the bound, so an executor that refuses to fire at the bound is excluded; one that reaps early is excluded by line 4. The firing order among ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is EXEC-002 and is not part of an atomic step.
- Lines 2 to 4 are the second 'shall' sentence (ruling D4: strictly past by plus the tolerance, and the tolerance is MUST). An atomic relation cannot say that a reap happens, only that it is available and is the only way out: line 3 is the reap step being available (TIME-013 states the same for every expired transition, its last line), line 2 that the expired transition does not fire instead, and line 4 that a reap happens only when it is expired and disarms it. That the reap happens in the deadline step of the very cycle in which the bound is passed ([EXEC-001] step 4) and emits TransitionTimedOut ([EVT-009]) is the Phase 2 executor's, not this block's. Rust and Java (one reading per cycle, shared by the deadline step and the firing pass: cycle_now, cycleNanos) and TypeScript (the deadline step and the pass share cycleNowMs) conform to line 2. A firing pass that takes a clock reading of its own, later than the deadline step's, and checks only the earliest bound there breaks it: a Deadline transition whose elapsed time passes by plus the tolerance between the two readings is not reaped and fires. That is the behaviour RD-16 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded for Java's fireReadyGeneral.
- Line 5 is the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-004 to TIME-006 (GlossaryTime.lean). Its first part is the first 'shall' sentence for steps that would make u not ready by disarming it: the only step that may take the clock from an enabled Deadline transition is its reap, and a firing of u itself that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_003_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts read 'elapsed time' in the second 'shall' sentence through the glossary (Elapsed: the clock reading minus the stamp taken when the transition was most recently newly armed): a delay, the reap of another transition and a firing of another transition that leaves u enabled throughout newly arm nothing, so they keep u's stamp. Without them an executor that restamps every armed transition on each delay (TIME_003_mutant_anyStamp_killed), or restarts every armed clock on every firing (TIME_003_mutant_restart_killed), keeps the elapsed time of u from growing in a busy net and never reaps it. That a delay advances the clock by its length is TIME-015 line 2, conjoined in ConsistencyTime. Distinct names (NamesDistinct, ruling D10) are needed because stamps are kept per name. Under ruling D6 an injected token also writes arc places, but injection is not a step of the Phase 1 relation.
- The body sentence that the transition must fire within by (plus the tolerance) is not a property of the executor, which may be late (ruling D3): the executor reaps instead. The strongly urgent reading, under which time cannot pass beyond the latest bound of an enabled transition, is the verification semantics (Novel.TimedScg.TStep, timed_run_sound) and is not encoded here.
- Construction (0 < by <= maximum duration) is TIME-001 AC4 (ruling D11), a property of Timing.Valid, not of the step relation (time003_construction, cited); the interval, earliest() = 0, latest() = by and hasDeadline() = true are the Timing accessors (time003_interval, cited).
- AC1 (fires immediately after enablement) is line 1 at elapsed time 0, exercised in TIME_003_nonvacuous. AC2 (a transition still armed past by plus the deadline tolerance does not fire after that bound; if it is still armed on the first cycle whose elapsed time is strictly greater than the bound, it is reaped in that cycle) is lines 2 to 4, exercised in TIME_003_nonvacuous with Deadline(5000 ms) and tolerance 5 ms: u fires at elapsed 5005 and cannot be reaped there, and at 5006 it cannot fire, is reaped and is no longer armed. Its first sentence is the safety line 2 (no firing past the bound). Its second sentence is conditional on u still being armed, so a competitor that disables u before its bound does not falsify it ([TIME-011]); on the step relation it is lines 3 and 4, the reap offered in every state strictly past the bound and in no other. That the reap happens in the first such cycle is a property of the cycle loop ([EXEC-001] step 4), which the atomic Phase 1 relation does not have, and is deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec). The test derivation's 'verify transition disabled' after the reap is the reaped transition staying unarmed: across delays and other reaps by line 5, across a firing that writes none of its arc places by TIME-010 line 1 and TIME-013, so it is covered only jointly, in ConsistencyTime. The TransitionTimedOut event of AC2 is EVT-009, deferred to Phase 2.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_004"></a>
## TIME-004: Delayed Timing

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 105e54b6ff04bba2 ai** · Statement hash `105e54b6ff04bba2`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition with `Delayed(after)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is less than `after`, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a transition with `Delayed(after)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is at least `after`, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready.<br><br>The executor *shall not* reap a transition with `Delayed` timing ([TIME-013]). | 1. For every timed net X, every transition u and every bound a such that u's timing is Delayed(a):<br>2. no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is below a (this restates [TIME-010] line 4 for this timing);<br>3. from every state in which u, the net's transition of its name, is armed and its elapsed time is at least a, every reference firing of u is a step, to the marking that firing gives;<br>4. no step reaps u;<br>5. when u is the net's transition of its name, its clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but a reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, a firing of u itself included, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (a : ℕ),<br>    TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.delayed a →<br>      (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ Elapsed s u &lt; a, never fun s s' ↦<br>          ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            InNet X u →<br>              Armed s u →<br>                a ≤ Elapsed s u →<br>                  RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧<br>          (∀ (s s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧ (InNet X u → ClockFrame R X u)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Armed, Elapsed time, Reapable and Reaped are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); bounds are in milliseconds.
- Line 2 reads 'its timing shall not stop it from being ready' on the step relation: a Delayed transition that is armed and past its bound is ready (glossary: Ready; Delayed is not reapable, so it is never expired), and a ready transition can take every reference firing it has, as Covers says for all transitions. Line 2 is that coverage for this timing, so the step relation may not refuse such a firing for a timing reason. Choosing among several ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is [EXEC-002] and [TIME-014]; the atomic step relation of Phase 1 has no such choice.
- Lines 3 and 4 read 'shall not reap' with the glossary meaning of reaping, to disarm without firing: no step labelled as a reap of u (line 3; an executor that reaps a Delayed transition past the maximum duration plus the tolerance breaks it, TIME_004_forbids_reapDelayed), and the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-003, TIME-005 and TIME-006 (line 4, GlossaryTime.lean). Its first part, StaysArmed, says no step leaves u enabled and unarmed (reaped, in the glossary's state reading), a firing of u itself included: a firing of u that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_004_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts keep u's stamp across a delay, a reap of another name and a firing of another name that leaves u enabled throughout; the last is [TIME-012] line 2 specialised to u: without it a firing of an unrelated transition could drop u's clock, a reap hidden in a firing (TIME_004_mutant_dropClean_killed), or restart it, which pushes u's bound back so that its timing stops it from being ready (TIME_004_mutant_restart_killed). A firing that disables u in its intermediate marking or after it drops or restarts u's clock as [TIME-011] and [TIME-012] say, and which stamp a firing of u itself leaves (a fresh one) is [TIME-012] line 4; this block fixes neither. A reap labelled with a transition other than u that carries u's name is not constrained by line 3: it is excluded by [TIME-013] line 1 (only a transition of the net is reaped) together with NamesDistinct (ruling D10). That a delay advances the clock by its length is [TIME-015] line 2.
- The interval bullets (earliest bound after, latest bound the maximum duration, hasDeadline false) are the Timing accessors (time004_interval). The construction bullet is [TIME-001] AC4 (Timing.Valid, ruling D11): Delayed(after) is valid exactly when after is at most the maximum duration.
- AC1 (cannot fire before after has elapsed since enablement) is line 1, with 'since enablement' read as the elapsed time since the stamp ([TIME-010]); measuring from the creation of the consumed tokens is the mutant TIME_004_mutant_tokenAge_killed. AC2 (after after, the transition can fire at any time) is line 2, which holds in every state past the bound, however late, and lines 3 and 4, by which neither a later clock reading nor an unrelated firing takes the transition's clock away or moves it.
- The test derivation (Delayed(3s), enabled at T=0, not ready at T=2s, ready at T=3s) is the nonvacuous example TIME_004_nonvacuous, in milliseconds; it also fires an unrelated transition at T=500 that keeps u's stamp (line 4).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_004): The timed reference step satisfies TIME-004: a firing of a `Delayed(a)` transition passes the spec's gate, so its elapsed time is at least `a` (line 1); an armed transition past `a` is not expired, since `Delayed` is not reapable, so it takes every reference firing it has (line 2); for the same reason it is never reaped (line 3); and the reference step meets the clock frame of every transition of the net (line 4, `clockFrame_refTStep`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], TIME_004 RefTStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004_forbids_reapDelayed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_004): ✗ An executor that reaps a `Delayed` transition once its elapsed time passes the maximum duration plus the tolerance violates TIME-004 (line 3, sentence 3: `Delayed` is never reaped). At `T = MAX_DURATION_MS + 6` `u`, armed since `0`, is reaped. The relation keeps every step of the reference, and its extra steps are reaps that keep the stamp of every other name, so lines 1, 2 and 4 do not reject it: line 4 (`StaysArmed`) excludes a reap of `u` itself, and line 2 is silent once `u` is unarmed.
  <pre>¬TIME_004 time004_reapPastMax</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004_forbids_selfDrop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_004): ✗ An executor whose firing of `u` itself leaves `u` enabled but unarmed violates TIME-004 (line 4, `StaysArmed`): with two tokens in `u`'s input place at `T = 3000`, `u` fires and stays enabled, and the self-drop policy gives it no clock, so it is left reaped, though `Delayed` is never reaped.
  <pre>¬TIME_004 (RefTStepW selfDropPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004_forbids_untimed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_004): A relation that fires every reference firing and ignores the clock (`time010_untimed`) violates TIME-004 (line 1): at `T = 0` it fires `u`, armed with elapsed time `0`, below its bound of 3000 ms.
  <pre>¬TIME_004 time010_untimed</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_004_mutant_dropClean_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_004): The clean-set drop kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-004 (line 4). At `T = 500` the unrelated `v` fires; `u` stays enabled in the intermediate marking and after it, yet loses its clock: it is left reaped, though `Delayed` is never reaped (sentence 3), and no step fires it again (AC2).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_005"></a>
## TIME-005: Window Timing

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0c95b3226f130dae ai** · Statement hash `0c95b3226f130dae`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition with `Window(earliest, latest)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is less than `earliest`, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a transition with `Window(earliest, latest)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is at least `earliest`, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready until it is expired.<br><br>*If* a transition with `Window(earliest, latest)` timing is armed and its elapsed time exceeds `latest` plus the deadline tolerance, *then* the executor *shall* reap it ([TIME-013]). | 1. For every timed net X, every transition u and all bounds e and l such that u's timing is Window(e, l):<br>2. no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is below e (this restates [TIME-010] line 4 for this timing);<br>3. from every state in which u, the net's transition of its name, is armed and its elapsed time is at least e and at most l plus the tolerance, every reference firing of u is a step, to the marking that firing gives;<br>4. no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than l plus the tolerance;<br>5. from every state in which u, the net's transition of its name, is armed and its elapsed time is greater than l plus the tolerance, a reap of u is a step (the 'shall reap' is encoded as the reap being available; that it is taken is deferred, see below);<br>6. a reap of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is greater than l plus the tolerance, and leaves u reaped: enabled and not armed;<br>7. when u is the net's transition of its name, its clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but a reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, a firing of u itself included, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (e l : ℕ),<br>    TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.window e l →<br>      (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ Elapsed s u &lt; e, never fun s s' ↦<br>          ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            InNet X u →<br>              Armed s u →<br>                e ≤ Elapsed s u →<br>                  Elapsed s u ≤ l + Tolerance X →<br>                    RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧<br>          (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ l + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u, never fun s s' ↦<br>              ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>            (∀ (s : TSt N),<br>                InNet X u →<br>                  Armed s u →<br>                    l + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧<br>              (on fun s s' ↦ R X s (TLbl.reap u) s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>                  Armed s u ∧ l + Tolerance X &lt; Elapsed s u ∧ Reaped s' u) ∧<br>                (InNet X u → ClockFrame R X u)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Armed, Elapsed time, Deadline tolerance, Expired, Ready and Reaped are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); bounds are in milliseconds.
- Expired is read with ruling D4: the bound is latest plus the deadline tolerance, and the test is strict, as MUST. A Window transition that is armed is expired exactly when its elapsed time is greater than l plus the tolerance (Window is reapable), which is how lines 2 to 5 spell 'until it is expired' and 'exceeds'.
- Line 2 reads 'its timing shall not stop it from being ready until it is expired' on the step relation: a Window transition that is armed, past e and not expired is ready (glossary: Ready), and a ready transition can take every reference firing it has, as Covers says for all transitions. Choosing among several ready transitions (priority, FIFO) is [EXEC-002] and [TIME-014]; the atomic step relation of Phase 1 has no such choice.
- Lines 3 to 5 are the 'If ... then shall reap' sentence: past the bound u does not fire (line 3), a reap of it is a step (line 4), and a reap of u happens only strictly past the bound and leaves it reaped (line 5). The 'shall' of the sentence is encoded only as the reap being offered (line 4 is existential): a relation that lets the clock run on past the bound without reaping satisfies the block, because the atomic relation of Phase 1 lets a delay pass any bound (the executor may be late). That the reap is taken is the cycle loop's obligation ([EXEC-001], Phase 2), as below. Ignoring the tolerance (bound l instead of l plus the tolerance) is the mutant TIME_005_mutant_noTol_killed, a non-strict bound TIME_005_mutant_reapAt_killed. Rust and Java (one reading per cycle, shared by the deadline step and the firing pass: cycle_now, cycleNanos) and TypeScript (the deadline step and the pass share cycleNowMs) conform to line 3. A firing pass that takes a clock reading of its own, later than the deadline step's, and checks only the earliest bound there breaks it: a Window transition whose elapsed time passes l plus the tolerance between the two readings is not reaped and fires. That is the behaviour RD-16 in spec/runtime-defects.md recorded for Java's fireReadyGeneral.
- Line 6 is the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-003, TIME-004 and TIME-006 (GlossaryTime.lean); it keeps u's clock to the reap step and to the firings that disable u. Its first part, StaysArmed, says no step but a reap of u leaves u enabled and unarmed, a firing of u itself included: a firing of u that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_005_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts keep u's stamp across a delay, a reap of another name and a firing of another name that leaves u enabled throughout; the last is [TIME-012] line 2 specialised to u: without it a firing of an unrelated transition could drop u's clock, a reap hidden in a firing that disarms u before it expires (TIME_005_mutant_dropClean_killed), or restart it, so that a continuously enabled window escapes its bound (TIME_005_mutant_restart_killed). A firing that disables u in its intermediate marking or after it drops or restarts u's clock as [TIME-011] and [TIME-012] say, and which stamp a firing of u itself leaves (a fresh one) is [TIME-012] line 4; this block fixes neither. That a delay advances the clock by its length is [TIME-015] line 2. A reap labelled with a transition other than u that carries u's name is not constrained by line 5: it is excluded by [TIME-013] line 1 (only a transition of the net is reaped) together with NamesDistinct (ruling D10).
- AC2 (a transition still armed past latest plus the deadline tolerance does not fire after that bound; if it is still armed on the first cycle whose elapsed time is strictly greater than the bound, it is reaped in that cycle) is lines 2 to 5 and is not quoted: fireable up to the bound, not fireable past it (the first sentence), the reap offered in every state strictly past it and allowed in no other (the second sentence on the step relation). Both sentences speak of a transition still armed, so a competitor that disables u before its bound falsifies neither ([TIME-011] drops its clock). That the reap happens in the first such cycle is a property of the cycle loop ([EXEC-001] step 4), which the atomic step relation of Phase 1 does not have, and is deferred to Phase 2 (RefExec). Line 4 is the reap of u being available; TIME-013's last line states the same for every expired transition. Which event a reap emits is [TIME-013] and [EVT-009].
- AC1 (cannot fire before earliest) is line 1. AC3 (latest below earliest is rejected) and AC4 (earliest or latest above the maximum duration is rejected) are construction rules over Timing.Valid, the F reading of [TIME-001] AC4 with ruling D11: time005_construction states that Window(e, l) is valid exactly when e and l are at most the maximum duration and e is at most l, and time005_construction_examples checks the boundary cases.
- The interval bullets (earliest bound e, latest bound l, hasDeadline true) are the Timing accessors (time005_interval); Window is reapable, unlike Exact ([TIME-006]).
- The test derivation (Window(1s, 5s): not ready at 0.5s, ready at 2s, expired at 6s) is the nonvacuous example TIME_005_nonvacuous, in milliseconds with the default tolerance of 5 ms, which also checks both sides of the bound 5005, and fires an unrelated transition at T=500 that keeps u's stamp (line 6).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): The timed reference step satisfies TIME-005: a firing of a `Window(e, l)` transition passes the spec's gate, so its elapsed time is at least `e` (line 1), and is not expired, so its elapsed time is at most `l` plus the tolerance (line 3); an armed transition between the two bounds takes every reference firing it has (line 2); past the upper bound it is expired, so a reap is a step (line 4), and a reap needs it expired and drops its stamp only (line 5); the reference step meets the clock frame of every transition of the net (line 6, `clockFrame_refTStep`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], TIME_005 RefTStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_forbids_selfDrop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): ✗ An executor whose firing of `u` itself leaves `u` enabled but unarmed violates TIME-005 (line 6, `StaysArmed`): with two tokens in `u`'s input place at `T = 2000`, inside the window, `u` fires and stays enabled, and the self-drop policy gives it no clock, a reap before the window's bound hidden in its own firing.
  <pre>¬TIME_005 (RefTStepW selfDropPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_forbids_untimed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): A relation that fires every reference firing and ignores the clock (`time010_untimed`) violates TIME-005 (line 1): at `T = 0` it fires `u`, armed with elapsed time `0`, below its earliest bound of 1000 ms.
  <pre>¬TIME_005 time010_untimed</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_mutant_dropClean_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): The clean-set drop kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-005 (line 6). At `T = 500` the unrelated `v` fires; the window `u` stays enabled in the intermediate marking and after it, yet loses its clock long before it expires: a reap hidden in a firing.
  <pre>TIME_005_mutant_noKeep (RefTStepW time005_dropCleanPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_005 (RefTStepW time005_dropCleanPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_mutant_noTol_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): The step that ignores the tolerance kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-005, since at `T = 5003`, with elapsed time `5003`, past `5000` but within the tolerance of 5 ms, `u` cannot fire (sentence 2: ready until it is expired, expired only past latest plus the deadline tolerance).
  <pre>TIME_005_mutant_noTol (RefTStepW time005_noTolPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_005 (RefTStepW time005_noTolPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_mutant_reapAt_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): The step that reaps at the bound kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-005, since at `T = 5005`, with elapsed time exactly `5000 + 5`, it reaps `u` (AC2: "strictly greater than that bound").
  <pre>TIME_005_mutant_reapAt (RefTStepW time005_reapAtPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_005 (RefTStepW time005_reapAtPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_005_mutant_restart_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_005): The restart on every firing kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-005 (line 6). At `T = 500` the unrelated `v` fires and the window `u`, enabled throughout, is restamped `500` instead of keeping `0`, so a continuously enabled window is pushed past its bound by every firing of a busy net and escapes the reap.
  <pre>TIME_005_mutant_noKeep (RefTStepW time005_restartPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_005 (RefTStepW time005_restartPolicy)</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-TIME_006"></a>
## TIME-006: Exact Timing

`Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/03-timing.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 9a5e081db9a5fa53 ai** · Statement hash `9a5e081db9a5fa53`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* a transition with `Exact(at)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is less than `at`, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a transition with `Exact(at)` timing is armed and its elapsed time is at least `at`, its timing *shall not* stop it from being ready.<br><br>The executor *shall not* reap a transition with `Exact` timing, however late it observes it ([TIME-013]). | 1. For every timed net X, every transition u and every bound a such that u's timing is Exact(a):<br>2. no firing of u starts from a state in which u is armed and its elapsed time is below a (this restates [TIME-010] line 4 for this timing);<br>3. from every state in which u, the net's transition of its name, is armed and its elapsed time is at least a, every reference firing of u is a step, to the marking that firing gives;<br>4. no step reaps u;<br>5. when u is the net's transition of its name, its clock is framed (ClockFrame): when the net's names are distinct, no step but a reap of u disarms u while it stays enabled, a firing of u itself included, and a delay, the reap of a transition of another name, and a firing of a transition of another name that leaves u enabled in its intermediate marking and after it keep u's stamp. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (X : TimedNet N) (u : Reference.Trans N) (a : ℕ),<br>    TimingOf X u = Novel.TimedScg.Timing.exact a →<br>      (while fun s ↦ Armed s u ∧ Elapsed s u &lt; a, never fun s s' ↦<br>          ∃ d, R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s') ∧<br>        (∀ (s : TSt N) (d : List N) (m' : N → ℕ),<br>            InNet X u →<br>              Armed s u →<br>                a ≤ Elapsed s u →<br>                  RefFire u s.m d m' → ∃ s', R X s (TLbl.fire u d) s' ∧ s'.m = m') ∧<br>          (∀ (s s' : TSt N), ¬R X s (TLbl.reap u) s') ∧ (InNet X u → ClockFrame R X u)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A step relates two states of the executor (glossary: TSt), each holding a marking, the reading of the firing clock and a stamp per transition name; a step is a delay of the clock, a firing or a reap (TRel). Firings are atomic. Armed, Elapsed time, Reapable and Reaped are the glossary terms (GlossaryTime.lean); bounds are in milliseconds.
- The block describes the executor (ruling D3), as the section says: Exact is enforced softly, gated at a and never force-disabled. The verification reading of [at, at] belongs to [VER-002] and [VER-012] and is only cited here: the state class graph reads Exact(a) as the interval [a, a] (time006_graph_interval), and the late-executor analysis lifts its latest bound (Late.relaxLate). No single step relation satisfies both readings, so this block takes no position on the logical-time one.
- Line 2 reads 'its timing shall not stop it from being ready' on the step relation: an Exact transition that is armed and past its bound is ready (glossary: Ready; Exact is not reapable, so it is never expired, though hasDeadline is true), and a ready transition can take every reference firing it has, as Covers says for all transitions. Line 2 holds however late the state is, which is 'never force-disabled for overrunning at'.
- Lines 3 and 4 read 'shall not reap' with the glossary meaning of reaping, to disarm without firing: no step labelled as a reap of u (line 3), and the frame ClockFrame shared with TIME-003 to TIME-005 (line 4, GlossaryTime.lean). Its first part, StaysArmed, says no step leaves u enabled and unarmed (reaped, in the glossary's state reading), a firing of u itself included: a firing of u that leaves u enabled re-arms it (TIME_006_forbids_selfDrop). Its other parts keep u's stamp across a delay, a reap of another name and a firing of another name that leaves u enabled throughout; the last is [TIME-012] line 2 specialised to u: without it a firing of an unrelated transition could drop u's clock, a reap hidden in a firing that force-disables u (TIME_006_mutant_dropClean_killed), or restart it, which pushes at back so that its timing stops it from being ready (TIME_006_mutant_restart_killed). A firing that disables u in its intermediate marking or after it drops or restarts u's clock as [TIME-011] and [TIME-012] say, and which stamp a firing of u itself leaves (a fresh one) is [TIME-012] line 4; this block fixes neither. That a delay advances the clock by its length is [TIME-015] line 2. A reap labelled with a transition other than u that carries u's name is not constrained by line 3: it is excluded by [TIME-013] line 1 (only a transition of the net is reaped) together with NamesDistinct (ruling D10).
- AC1 (cannot fire before at) is line 1. AC2's 'not force-disabled for being observed late' is lines 2, 3 and 4. AC2's 'fires at the first opportunity at or after at' is liveness of the cycle loop ([EXEC-001], [EXEC-002]), which the atomic step relation of Phase 1 does not state; line 2 makes every such firing available from the bound on. 'Exactness is observable from the firing event' is the event log ([EVT-006], [EVT-007]), not this block; that a late Exact transition emits no TransitionTimedOut ([EVT-009]) follows from line 3, as only a reap emits it.
- The interval bullets (earliest and latest bound at, hasDeadline true) are the Timing accessors (time006_interval). The construction bullet is [TIME-001] AC4 (Timing.Valid, ruling D11): Exact(at) is valid exactly when at is at most the maximum duration. The advice to use Delayed(at) or Window(at, at + slack) instead is not a requirement on the executor.
- The test derivation (Exact(50ms) under a busy executor that cannot run a cycle until well past 50ms: it still fires and is not timed out) is the nonvacuous example TIME_006_nonvacuous: at 1000 ms, far past 50 plus the tolerance, the transition can fire and no reap of it is a step; at 10 ms an unrelated transition fires and the transition keeps its stamp (line 4).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): The timed reference step satisfies TIME-006: a firing of an `Exact(a)` transition passes the spec's gate, so its elapsed time is at least `a` (line 1); an armed transition past `a` is never expired, since `Exact` is not reapable, so it takes every reference firing it has however late (line 2), and it is never reaped (line 3); the reference step meets the clock frame of every transition of the net (line 4, `clockFrame_refTStep`).
  <pre>∀ {N : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], TIME_006 RefTStep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_forbids_selfDrop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): ✗ An executor whose firing of `u` itself leaves `u` enabled but unarmed violates TIME-006 (line 4, `StaysArmed`): with two tokens in `u`'s input place at `T = 50`, `u` fires and stays enabled, and the self-drop policy gives it no clock, so it is left reaped, though `Exact` is never reaped.
  <pre>¬TIME_006 (RefTStepW selfDropPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_forbids_untimed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): A relation that fires every reference firing and ignores the clock (`time010_untimed`) violates TIME-006 (line 1): at `T = 0` it fires `u`, armed with elapsed time `0`, below `at` of 50 ms.
  <pre>¬TIME_006 time010_untimed</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_mutant_dropClean_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): The clean-set drop kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-006 (line 4). At `T = 10` the unrelated `v` fires; `u` stays enabled in the intermediate marking and after it, yet loses its clock: it is left reaped, force-disabled with no reap step and no `TransitionTimedOut` (sentence 3).
  <pre>TIME_006_mutant_noKeep (RefTStepW time006_dropCleanPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_006 (RefTStepW time006_dropCleanPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_mutant_hard_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): The hard step kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-006. Under a busy executor that first looks at `T = 1000`, far past `50 + 5`, it reaps `u` (test derivation: "verify it still fires and emits no `TransitionTimedOut`").
  <pre>TIME_006_mutant_hard (RefTStepW time006_hardPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_006 (RefTStepW time006_hardPolicy)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_mutant_restart_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): The restart on every firing kills the mutant: it satisfies the mutant reading, but not TIME-006 (line 4). At `T = 10` the unrelated `v` fires and `u`, enabled throughout, is restamped `10` instead of keeping `0`, so `at` is pushed back by every firing of a busy net (sentence 2).
  <pre>TIME_006_mutant_noKeep (RefTStepW time006_restartPolicy) ∧<br>  ¬TIME_006 (RefTStepW time006_restartPolicy)</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.TIME_006_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.TIME_006): Every line of TIME-006 is exercised by the reference step, on the test derivation in milliseconds with a tolerance of 5 ms. `u` is `Exact(50)` and armed at `T = 0`. At `T = 49` it cannot fire (line 1); at `T = 50` it can (line 2); under a busy executor that first looks at `T = 1000`, far past `50 + 5`, it still can, and no reap of it is a step (lines 2 and 3). The delays keep its stamp `0` (line 4). At `T = 1000` the deadline transition `v` is expired and reaped, and `u` keeps its stamp (line 4). At `T = 10` `v` fires instead; `u`, armed, is enabled in the intermediate marking and after the firing, and keeps its stamp `0` (line 4).
