**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (S, P). S : SplitFn K has the shape of Split.refSplit, the reference of in_flight.rs split_in_flight_for (Java InFlightSplit, TypeScript in-flight.ts): the configuration SplitCfg carries what the split reads besides the net (the in-flight place of a name and how a place is rendered, the terminal places, the coloured places with the match keys and relay targets already added, the ν-joins, the environment steps of VER-006 and VER-022, and the demand: tested places and forced transitions). P : SplitPlanFn K is with_in_flight's choice of demand: it adds quiescent_count_demand always and conflict_demand when conflict priority applies, and switches conflict priority off when the split under it is refused. The witness pair is Split.refSplit and refSplitPlan (VER_004_split_reference). The verified net of VER-003's abs is S at P's configuration, and a refusal of S is an error of abs, so VER-003's line 4 makes the verdict Unknown whatever a route would answer: that is the 'answer Unknown on every route' of the eighth EARS sentence.
- The first EARS sentence defines the tested places (nonMonotone plus the demand's tested places, Split.splitB). The second is P's QuiescentCount demand (ver004CountDemand) in lines 5 to 7, and the third is the tested half of P's conflict demand (ver004Pruners, the tested field of ver004WithConflict) in line 6. The fourth is splits in lines 2 to 4: an output place in any branch, the Timeout branch included, is Split.outs (outPlaces); 'are not a completion step' is Split.isCompletion, whose definition the parenthesis gives; 'pruning transitions while conflict priority applies' is the forced field of ver004WithConflict, which P hands on exactly when conflict priority stays on (line 6) and drops when it turns conflict priority off (line 7); 'While assumeAtomicFiring is not set' is line 1, under which nothing is split. The fifth and the sixth are splitTimed in line 4 (Split.startHalf; Split.endHalf, whose one input is one(inflight:<t>) and which has no inhibitor, read or reset arc; Split.completionOut; Split.splitNet). The seventh is line 2. The eighth is line 3 with VER-003 line 4: 'a transition to split' is one S splits under the configuration P hands on, so under conflict priority it is read after the switch-off of the ninth sentence, which is why the eighth needs no condition on conflict priority (a net with conflict priority, no pruning transition and a ν-join that deposits into an inhibited place keeps conflict priority on by line 6 and is refused by line 3). The ninth is line 7: the split under the conflict demand is refused, so P hands on the QuiescentCount demand alone with conflict priority off, and S then splits as it does without conflict priority (VER_004_split_fallback), refusing only what the split without conflict priority refuses; its 'While assumeAtomicFiring is not set' is line 7's hypothesis, since under the opt-out line 6 keeps conflict priority on. The tenth is line 1 for the net and line 6 for conflict priority.
- Not in the model, and why. Reference.Trans has no priority and no match spec, so the priorities are P's argument by name, the ν-joins and the coloured places are SplitCfg fields, and the halves' priority and match spec (the start half keeps both; the completion step takes t's priority in all three runtimes, halves in rust/libpetri-verification/src/in_flight.rs, completion in java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/InFlight.java and halves in typescript/src/verification/in-flight.ts, as the body's second bullet says) are kind N. Whether conflict priority applies to a call (conflict_pruning_applies: CONFLICT selected, a ν-join with a property Route B takes, no reapable transition) is P's argument, decided by NU-052 and VER-012. The terminal rewrite of EXEC-042 that runs after the split, so a terminal also inhibits each completion step and excuses each in-flight place, is EXEC-042's (Novel.TerminalRewrite); Reference.Net carries no terminal list, so the split net's terminals are cfg's. The body sentences 'A marked in-flight place never rests: its completion step is enabled, immediate and not reapable.' and 'The completion step is itself one deposit and is never split again.' are consequences: Split.quiescent_no_inflight, and Split.isCompletion in line 2, cited. The refusal text is Rust's heads (Split.refusalHead). Line 3 asks that it open with transition '<t>', the opening all three runtimes share (refusal_head and demand_refusal_head in in_flight.rs, refusalHead and demandRefusalHead in InFlight.java and in-flight.ts; Python rides Rust); the rest of the wording is kind N. A text that only contains the name would be too weak: a split that blames the last refused transition, with the split list in front, still contains the first one's name, and a one-letter name such as a occurs in the word transition itself (VER_004_split_forbids_lastCulprit). The body's 'An implementation MUST offer the opt-out assumeAtomicFiring (assume_atomic_firing)' is an offer, so it is the coverage condition Ver004OptOutCovers (blocks state safety, offers are coverage: the convention of GlossaryExec.lean), not a line: Options carries the field in every runtime, the reference makes the offer (refSplit_optOut_covers), and every split that meets this block makes it too (VER_004_split_optOut). Ruling D20: the refusal reads the body's 'forwards an exactly(n), all or atLeast input', every cardinality that is not one, and AC6 now says so (clash ver-a#10).
- The paragraph 'Atomic firings and in-flight actions' says why the split is needed and is cited: InFlight.inflight_witness (the atomic net proves Unreachable(bad) while the executor marks bad) and InFlight.split_covers_executor. That the split net over-approximates the executor's runs with actions in flight, and so that a Proven holds for them, is block B (VER_004_exec, on RefExec): AC4's first sentence and the sentence 'That is a sound over-approximation for all three.' Ruling D28 (a) scopes it to actions that publish no output before they complete: tokens an action publishes with ctx.flush() (Rust, Python) enter the marking before its completion step, which the split net never reaches, and the report of every split verdict says so (FLUSH_NOTE, kind N). That the split only adds runs (every atomic run is a run of the split net with each split label followed by its completion) is Split.run_splitNet, cited.
- Ruling D8 (b): whether an executor starts a transition again while an earlier firing of it is in flight is implementation-defined (Rust and Python do, Java and TypeScript do not). The split allows it, which over-approximates both. The report note of a Violated whose trace restarts a transition in flight ('NOTE (CONC-002): ...', restart_note) and AC8 are report text, kind Q, not encoded here: which trace restarts is a function of the trace's markings (restarted_transitions), an open item for a later line.
- AC4's examples (the inhibitor net from {p, q, go} with t asynchronous, and reset(p), all(p) or atLeast(2, p) instead) are, on the split side, VER_004_split_nonvacuous (t is split, complete:t follows it, inflight:t follows the places) and Split's worked examples through refVerify (Violated with the split, Proven under assumeAtomicFiring); that the executors reach the same markings is block B's. AC5 (byte-identical scripts with or without assumeAtomicFiring when nothing is split) is lines 1 and 2: the verified net is X itself, so every route reads the same net; the scripts are VER-013's. AC6 is lines 3 and 7 and the tenth EARS sentence (line 1, line 6); its report texts are kind N. AC7 is VER_004_split_ac7: t and H are split under conflict priority, and under assumeAtomicFiring nothing is split and conflict priority is kept; the verdicts Violated and Proven are Route B's (VER-012, with a declared ν pair) and the executors marking bad is block B's. The test derivation's AC4 clause is block B's.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_004_timed"></a>
## VER-004: Untimed Over-Approximation (timing only removes firings)

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_004_timed` · Kind **A** · Scope the executor's timed runs, as every verifier route reads them (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers verification) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 1efbac2ac1dfbce0 ai** · Statement hash `1efbac2ac1dfbce0`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Each firing the executor takes under its timing *shall* be a firing of a transition of the untimed net, from the same marking to the same marking.<br><br>A reap ([TIME-013]) and the passing of time *shall* change no marking.<br><br>*Where* the transitions of a net have distinct names, a marking at which a timed run from the initial marking ([TIME-010]) rests, with no transition it enables armed, *shall* be quiescent as [VER-002] reads quiescence by default: every transition it enables is reapable.<br><br>*Where* the transitions of a net have distinct names, a marking at which an on-time run from the initial marking ([TIME-010]) rests, one that reaps no transition and lets no armed transition pass its latest bound, *shall* enable no transition. | 1. For every timed step relation R and firing relation F:<br>2. every firing step of R, of transition t with deposit d, fires a transition of the net, and is a firing of t under F from the step's marking to its successor's;<br>3. a delay or a reap step of R leaves the marking as it is (FramesMarking R);<br>4. on a net whose transition names are distinct, at every state an R run reaches from the reference initial state where no enabled transition is armed (RefRests), every enabled transition is reapable (VerQuiescent false);<br>5. on a net whose transition names are distinct, at every state an on-time R run (OnTimeStep R: no reap, no delay that carries an armed transition past its latest bound) reaches from the reference initial state where no enabled transition is armed, no transition is enabled (VerQuiescent true). | <pre>fun {K} [DecidableEq K] R F ↦<br>  (∀ (X : TimedNet K) (s : TSt K) (t : Reference.Trans K) (d : List K) (s' : TSt K),<br>      R X s (TLbl.fire t d) s' → t ∈ X.net.transitions ∧ F t s.m d s'.m) ∧<br>    FramesMarking R ∧<br>      (∀ (X : TimedNet K) (m0 : K → ℕ) (now0 : ℕ) (s : TSt K),<br>          NamesDistinct X →<br>            TimedReach R X m0 now0 s →<br>              Verifier.Bridges.RefRests X s → VerQuiescent false X s.m) ∧<br>        ∀ (X : TimedNet K) (m0 : K → ℕ) (now0 : ℕ) (s : TSt K),<br>          NamesDistinct X →<br>            OnTimeReachR R X m0 now0 s →<br>              Verifier.Bridges.RefRests X s → VerQuiescent true X s.m</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (R, F). R : TRel K is the timed step relation the TIME blocks constrain (Reference/Timed.lean: a delay of the firing clock, an atomic firing, or a reap, each one step), and F : FireRel K is the firing relation the CORE and IO blocks constrain, through which VER-003 reads reachability (ReachF F). The witness pair is RefTStep and RefFire (VER_004_timed_reference). Runs start at the reference initialiser TSt.init, which arms every transition enabled in the initial marking (TIME-010), the start state of every RefTStep run; that is the 'from the initial marking ([TIME-010])' of the third and the fourth EARS sentences, without which a run could start at a state with an enabled, unarmed transition that is not reapable and rest there. The block constrains R against F and leaves F to the CORE and IO blocks: a lax F that also lets a firing keep the marking would let through an R that loses a deposit, and the consistency theorem rules it out through those blocks, not through this one. Lines 1 and 2 give ProjectsTo R F and are FramesMarking R, the two conjuncts spec_consistent_coreIO_time already joins, so the consistency theorem can take one R and one F for the TIME, CORE and VER blocks.
- Kind A: the block states what every verifier route assumes of the executor's timing, that timing only removes firings and adds rests; it constrains the executor relation of the TIME blocks, not the verifier. The first two EARS sentences are lines 1 and 2. The body's 'every marking a timed run visits is reachable in the untimed net' follows from them alone (VER_004_timed_reach), and with VER-003's Proven line so does 'A proof of a property of the marking alone on the untimed net therefore holds for the timed net' (marking_properties_transfer and marking_ac3, cited).
- Lines 3 and 4 are the third and the fourth EARS sentences. A run rests where no enabled transition is armed (RefRests): the run loop stops on enabled_count() == 0 with nothing in flight (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor_core/executor.rs, ReapAware.lean). A timed run is any run of R, late delays, late firings within the tolerance and reaps included; an on-time run is a run of the filter OnTimeStep R (ruling D3: strong urgency filters runs and never restricts R, so the TIME blocks' CoversDelay stays true of the same R). Distinct names are ruling D10 with D23: a stamp is kept per name, so with two transitions of one name a transition can be enabled and unarmed without a reap. Transition names are assumed distinct (ruling D23); no builder and no compose checks them, so the body's 'With that reading, a proof on the untimed net is sound for every timed run, a late one included.' holds on a net whose transition names are distinct, the nets that assumption covers. The body sentence 'The untimed abstraction MUST include this, so every quiescence property reads quiescence reap-aware ([VER-002]): a marking where every enabled transition is reapable counts as quiescent.' is VER-002's VerQuiescent; line 3 is what makes that reading sound for a late executor, and line 4 is why the plain reading of assumeNoReaping is sound for an on-time one. That a rest is a reachable marking at all is line 1 and line 2 (VER_004_timed_reach).
- The step relation is atomic: a firing consumes and deposits in one step. An action in flight, whose firing consumes at its start and deposits at its completion with other firings between ([EXEC-001], [CONC-002], [EXEC-003] AC5), is the subject of the in-flight split (VER_004_split) and of block B (VER_004_exec), which covers the executor's runs with actions in flight by the split net through RefExec. The body's paragraph 'Atomic firings and in-flight actions' and the paragraph on restarting a transition in flight (ruling D8: implementation-defined; the split allows a restart, which over-approximates both answers) belong there.
- AC1, rewritten under ruling D28 (a), says what the routes read of timing: the flat routes read no timing bound, only whether a transition is reapable, and Route B keeps each earliest bound and each latest bound only under assumeNoReaping. It is not a line here: what a flat route reads of timing is VER-002's VerQuiescent (TimingOf only through Reapable) and VER-003's yardstick ReachF F (no timing at all), and the graph Route B reads is VER-012's and VER-010's subject.
- AC2 (value-blind; the NU-020 name-equality carve-out of NU-050 when implemented) is the shape of the model rather than a line: a marking is a count per place, and F lets every branch of an output spec happen (Reference.Fires: any outcome the spec offers), so a value-dependent choice is free; Soundness.proposition_one and the carve-out's NU-050 block are cited for it. The body's sentence that there is no value predicate left (guards were removed in IO-006) is IO-006's.
- AC3 is lines 3 and 4 with VER-003's Proven line: a Proven of a quiescence property on the untimed net, read reap-aware, holds at every rest of a late run, and read plainly at every rest of an on-time run. AC3 and the body's second paragraph define the on-time executor as the fourth EARS sentence does, one that reaps no transition and lets no armed transition pass its latest bound (OnTimeStep, ruling D3), which is stronger than firing none late: a delay that carries a transition past its latest bound is not on time even when that transition never fires. Its Route B clause (under assumeNoReaping a firing is one instant step, so a closed graph is exact only for an executor whose actions take no time; the deadline(20) and delayed(60) net with a 150 ms action) needs action duration, which no atomic step relation has (TimedScg.Retrodict.action_duration_escapes); it is VER-012's and VER-023's subject, and the report text that states the assumption is kind N. The test derivation's AC3 clause, the VER-002 AC11 witness, is VER_004_timed_nonvacuous: on p0 to t to p1 with t at window(3, 5), the late run delays past the latest bound, reaps t and rests at the initial marking with t enabled, so DeadlockFree is Violated there in the reap-aware reading and that rest is not quiescent in the plain one.
- Completeness (a counterexample of the untimed abstraction may be a run the timing forbids; such a Violated stands, and counterexampleTiming and the opt-in check of VER-023 say what it means) is VER-003's and VER-023's subject; this block states only the direction from the timed runs to the untimed net. AC4 to AC8 are VER_004_split's, and AC4's coverage of the executor's runs with actions in flight is block B's (VER_004_exec).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_004_timed_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_004): The timed reference satisfies the timed block of VER-004: a firing step is a reference firing of a transition of the net (`refTStep_projects`), a delay or a reap leaves the marking (`refTStep_framesMarking`), every rest of a run has only reapable transitions enabled (`ver004_unarmed_reach`: a transition loses its stamp while enabled only by a reap), and every rest of an on-time run has none enabled (`ver004_allArmed_reach`: an on-time run reaps nothing, so every enabled transition stays armed).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_005"></a>
## VER-005: P-Invariant Computation

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_005` · Kind **F** · Scope the SMT pipeline's invariant phase, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 31974fa0fc93c0df ai** · Statement hash `31974fa0fc93c0df`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the SMT pipeline ([VER-003]) builds its CHC encoding, the verifier *shall* compute the P-invariants of the verified net from the net's incidence matrix, with one injector column for each environment place into which it models injection ([VER-006]).<br><br>The verifier *shall* report a nonzero weight vector `w` with a constant `c` as a P-invariant only when the product of `w` with every column of that incidence matrix is zero and `w · M = c` holds on every marking `M` reachable in the untimed abstraction of the verified net ([VER-004]), injections included.<br><br>*When* the verifier computes the P-invariants of a net that has a transition and in which no transition has a reset arc, an `All` input or an `AtLeast` input, it *shall* report P-invariants such that every weight vector of zeros and ones over the net's places whose product with every column of that incidence matrix is zero is a rational linear combination of their weight vectors. | 1. For every invariant computation I, all deposit rows rows, environment places envs, place counts n and initial markings a0:<br>2. every pair (w, c) in I rows envs n a0 has a nonzero weight below n, and the product of w with the incidence column of every row is zero (dotIncD);<br>3. every pair (w, c) in I rows envs n a0 has w · a = c for every marking a reachable from a0 over rows with injection into envs (ReachADInj);<br>4. if rows is not empty and no row has a reset or consume-all place below n, then every vector w with weights 0 and 1, zero from n on, zero on the incidence column of every row and zero on every place in envs, is, scaled by some nonzero integer k, an integer combination of weight vectors reported in I rows envs n a0. | <pre>fun I ↦<br>  (∀ (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (envs : List PlaceId)<br>      (n : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking),<br>      ∀ yc ∈ I rows envs n a0,<br>        (∃ p &lt; n, yc.1 p ≠ 0) ∧ ∀ tr ∈ rows, Novel.LinearBound.dotIncD yc.1 tr n = 0) ∧<br>    (∀ (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (envs : List PlaceId)<br>        (n : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking),<br>        ∀ yc ∈ I rows envs n a0,<br>          ∀ (a : AMarking),<br>            Novel.ForwardDeposit.ReachADInj rows envs a0 a → dot yc.1 a n = yc.2) ∧<br>      ∀ (rows : List (Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)) (envs : List PlaceId)<br>        (n : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking),<br>        rows ≠ [] →<br>          (∀ tr ∈ rows,<br>              ∀ p &lt; n, tr.1.resets.contains p = false ∧ consumeAllAt tr.1 p = false) →<br>            ∀ (w : Weight),<br>              (∀ (p : PlaceId), w p = 0 ∨ w p = 1) →<br>                SupportBelow n w →<br>                  (∀ tr ∈ rows, Novel.LinearBound.dotIncD w tr n = 0) →<br>                    (∀ p ∈ envs, w p = 0) →<br>                      ∃ k,<br>                        k ≠ 0 ∧<br>                          ∃ cs,<br>                            (∀ x ∈ cs, x.2 ∈ I rows envs n a0) ∧<br>                              ∀ p &lt; n, k * w p = (List.map (fun x ↦ x.1 * x.2.1 p) cs).sum</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The verified net is its flat rows: one deposit row per flat transition and outcome, with the integer post vector the encoder writes (ForwardDeposit.flatRows, fireAD), after the in-flight split of VER-004 and after the Arrivals rewrite of VER-006, so `rows` is the net the matrix is built from and `n` its place count. A forward that drains its source (VER-001 F3) has no row; the computation is not run on such a net, and the statement says nothing about it. Reachability is the untimed atomic abstraction (ReachADInj): firings fire atomically, so the markings of an executor with an action in flight, whose consumed tokens are in no place, are not among them (clash ver-a#9, the D20 wording 'reachable in the untimed abstraction of the verified net', which the spec edit also applies to the prose definition and to AC2). The executor's own reachable markings are tied to this abstraction by VER-004 (Proposition 1, forward_reachability_simulated) and, for the named reference, by Reference.Link.reach_iff_reachAD.
- Injection is unbounded in ReachADInj. Under Bounded(k) the verifier caps it, so the capped markings are a subset and line 2 holds on them; under AlwaysAvailable the injection is the uncapped one; under Ignore and Arrivals `envs` is empty (VER-006). The injector columns are not a separate line: line 2 alone forces zero weight on every place in envs below n, because one injection from a0 is a reachable step (ver005_conserves_env). They appear in line 3 as the premise that w is zero on every place in envs. 'Conservation laws (P-invariants) derived from the closed net MUST NOT be applied to injected environment places' is VER-006's sentence; here a computation without the injector columns is killed by line 2 (VER_005_forbids_noInjector), and one that avoids that by reporting nothing once a place is injected is killed by line 3 (VER_005_forbids_noEnvColumns).
- The first quoted sentence (AC1, 'P-invariants are computed from the incidence matrix') is lines 1 and 3, and the third quoted sentence is line 3. Line 1 is the reporting side: each reported vector is zero on every column of the matrix. Line 3 is the computing side, stated where every runtime meets it: on a net with a transition and without reset, All or AtLeast arcs the gate drops nothing, so the reported vectors are the whole null-space basis the elimination returns, and every 0/1 vector of the null space is a rational combination of them. On a net with such an arc the gate may drop basis vectors whose combinations it would accept, so no completeness is claimed there, and reporting nothing is allowed. A net with no transition and no injected place has an empty matrix and every runtime returns no invariant (`rows == 0 || cols == 0`, `P == 0 || T == 0`), hence the premise that rows is not empty, which is stricter than needed when a place is injected. Line 3 claims the 0/1 vectors only, the conservation of a set of places such as the test derivation's token conservation; the runtimes span the whole null space on such nets, but this block's witness enumerates 0/1 vectors and has no verified elimination, so the wider claim is not a line. Arithmetic is exact in the model; a runtime row whose elimination overflows is dropped by the gate's overflow check, an implementation limit outside the statement. A vector that is constant on the reachable markings without being zero on the columns (the reading of the prose definition 'w · M = constant' alone) satisfies line 2 and is killed by line 1 (VER_005_mutant_reachOnly). The computation that reports nothing satisfies lines 1 and 2 and is killed by line 3 (VER_005_mutant_none). The trigger 'builds its CHC encoding' is the pipeline's (VER-001, VER-003): a route that builds no encoding computes none, and the result says so (VER-003 AC4).
- The second quoted sentence (AC2, 'Each invariant satisfies sum(weights[i] * marking[i]) = constant') is lines 1 and 2. Line 2 at the initial marking gives c = w · M0, the constant the runtimes recompute; a computation that reports another constant is killed (VER_005_forbids_constZero). 'Nonzero' is the elimination's skip of the all-zero row in all three runtimes; the trivial law 0 · M = 0 satisfies lines 2 and 3 and is killed by line 1 (VER_005_mutant_zero). Line 1 alone is not enough for line 2: a vector with weight on a consume-all, AtLeast or reset place can be zero on every column and still change along a firing, because the fire relation is not linear there (Strengthening.lean H1). The gate that drops such vectors is VER-007's ([VER-007] 'exact gate'); here the computations without it are killed by line 2 (VER_005_forbids_noH1, VER_005_forbids_noReset).
- AC3 ('Invariants are reported in the verification result') is the sentence '*When* the verifier computes P-invariants, it *shall* list each one it reports in the verification result, with its weights and its constant.' It is about the result record, kind N, and is not a line of this kind F block: the result's invariant list holds the pairs this computation reports, after the semiflow union of VER-007, in the canonical order of VER-013. That an empty list off the SMT route means 'not computed' is VER-003 AC4. VER-003's line 8 (the block VER_003) says that every P-invariant a result reports, on any route, is conserved on every marking reachable in the verified net; it reads the result's list and not this computation, so that the list holds exactly the pairs this computation reports is carried by this assumes sentence only.
- The test derivation ('Net with known invariant (e.g., token conservation); verify invariant is discovered') is line 3 on the net t: one(p0) -> p1, where p0 + p1 is a 0/1 vector of the null space: a computation that does not report it, or a multiple of it, is killed (VER_005_mutant_none). On the reference the witness reports p0 + p1 = 1 (VER_005_nonvacuous).
- The prose 'P-invariants provide structural proofs that do not require state enumeration' is a motivation, not a requirement; the use of the laws in the encoding is VER-007's strengthening (invariant_strengthening_sound).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_006"></a>
## VER-006: Environment Analysis Mode

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_006` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier and every route it dispatches to, AlwaysAvailable and Bounded(k), all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers environment analysis) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 a83eba97a52d71f7 ai** · Statement hash `a83eba97a52d71f7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| In `AlwaysAvailable` and `Bounded(k)` the verifier MUST **model external injection**: a transition gated on an environment place becomes reachable (the SMT encoding emits an injection rule that produces tokens into each environment place; under `Bounded(k)` injection is capped).<br><br>Equivalently, the environment place is treated as an inexhaustible (or k-capped) external source rather than a column that starts empty and can only be consumed.<br><br>Conservation laws (P-invariants) derived from the closed net MUST NOT be applied to injected environment places, since injection breaks closed-net conservation.<br><br>*While* the mode is `AlwaysAvailable`, the verifier *shall* treat as reachable every marking the executor reaches while the environment injects tokens into the environment places.<br><br>*While* the mode is `Bounded(k)` and the two premises of AC3 hold, the verifier *shall* treat as reachable every marking the executor reaches while the environment keeps at most `k` tokens resident in each environment place.<br><br>*While* the mode is `Bounded(k)`, the verifier *shall* not treat as reachable a marking that holds more than `k` tokens on an environment place, from an initial marking that holds at most `k` on each one. | 1. For every reachable-set function R of the open system, all flat nets given as rows, environment places envs, caps k and markings:<br>2. under AlwaysAvailable, when no consume-all arc carries a guard, every marking the executor reaches with injection (ReachCE, the counts of its coloured marking) is in R from the initial counts;<br>3. under Bounded(k), when no consume-all arc carries a guard and the premise check passes (boundedPremiseOK: at most k on each environment place initially, no row deposits into one), the same holds;<br>4. under Bounded(k), from an initial marking with at most k on each environment place, every marking in R holds at most k on each environment place. | <pre>fun R ↦<br>  (∀ (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (envs : List PlaceId) (m0 m : CMarking),<br>      (∀ tr ∈ rows, GuardFreeConsumeAll tr.1) →<br>        Novel.EnvSemantics.ReachCE rows envs Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.always m0 m →<br>          R rows envs Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.always (alpha m0) (alpha m)) ∧<br>    (∀ (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (envs : List PlaceId) (k : ℕ) (m0 m : CMarking),<br>        (∀ tr ∈ rows, GuardFreeConsumeAll tr.1) →<br>          Novel.EnvSemantics.boundedPremiseOK k envs rows m0 = true →<br>            Novel.EnvSemantics.ReachCE rows envs (Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.bounded k) m0<br>                m →<br>              R rows envs (Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.bounded k) (alpha m0) (alpha m)) ∧<br>      ∀ (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (envs : List PlaceId) (k : ℕ) (a0 a : AMarking),<br>        (∀ e ∈ envs, a0 e ≤ k) →<br>          R rows envs (Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.bounded k) a0 a → ∀ e ∈ envs, a e ≤ k</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the flat open system of Novel/EnvSemantics: place ids, the flat rows of the verified net (one deposit row per way a firing can end), untimed, every row read as not reapable, counts only. The executor side is ReachCE (StepCE: a row fires on the coloured marking, or one token is injected into an environment place, always under AlwaysAvailable and while fewer than k are resident under Bounded(k)); its counts are alpha. Lines 1 and 2 carry the hypothesis of Proposition 1 that no consume-all arc has a guard (GuardFreeConsumeAll). It holds of every net the spec allows, since IO-006 removed input guards: the flat Transition type keeps the guard field of the older model, and the rows of every reference net carry none (guardFree_toTransition, Reference/Link.lean). The reachable set may be larger than the executor's: the lines are inclusions, which is what a Proven needs; that a Violated replays is VER-003's line 5 on the verified net, whose injection steps the runtimes label inject(p) (abstract_replay.rs).
- The third quoted sentence (no conservation law of the closed net on an injected place) is line 1 read on the strengthened set: the conjuncts the encoders add to every rule (P-invariants of VER-005 and VER-007, the counters of VER-016) are part of R, so a law that cuts off a marking the executor reaches breaks line 1. A closed-net law applied to an injected place is killed (VER_006_forbids_closedLaw: env IN → T → OUT conserves IN + OUT without injection, and injection breaks it). That the shipped conjuncts remove no reachable marking is Strengthening.lean, StateEquation.lean and Novel/Certificate.lean, with VER-007's gate H3' (zero weight on an injected place) and VER-005's injector columns (incidence_matrix.rs) as the clauses that keep it true with injection; VER-005 cites this block for the sentence.
- AC2 (AlwaysAvailable: for env IN → T → OUT, PlaceBound(OUT, k) is Violated for every k) is VER_006_ac2: OUT holds more than k in the reference reachable set, for every k (VER_006_nonvacuous at k = 2); a set without injection is killed (VER_006_forbids_frozen), and so is a Bounded(k) set without the injection rule (VER_006_forbids_boundedFrozen). The Violated verdicts that AC2 and the Bounded(k) half of AC9 name are completeness claims, not lines: the lines are inclusions, which rule out a wrong Proven, and VER-003 allows Unknown on every input (the reference decider refEnvVerify answers Unknown there). They are checked by the runtimes' tests (the env IN → T → OUT regression of smt_verifier.rs), since the conformance corpus covers closed nets only; VER_006_ac2 shows that the violating marking is in the reference reachable set. AC3's first sentence (Bounded(k) limits the state space: a transition requiring more than k tokens from an environment place per firing is never enabled) is the third line, read through VER_006_demand_gate, which derives it for every R meeting the block; a cap read as AlwaysAvailable is killed (VER_006_forbids_uncapped). AC3's premises are VER_006_premise and line 2 of VER_006_verdict; its Route B and state-class wording ('the state-class graphs enable an environment input exactly when it demands at most k whatever the place holds') is Novel/EnvSemantics/Supplied.lean (supplied_safety_exact). No block states it for the shipped graphs: the VER-012 blocks (VER_012, VER_012_build) and the VER-010 blocks say nothing of environment places.
- AC1 (each mode is selectable via the verifier configuration) is kind N, an offer of configuration: the mode type EnvMode carries the four modes (VER_006_verdict), and no line states the offer. The default mode (AlwaysAvailable for the SMT verifier, Ignore for the state-class graph API, which refuses Arrivals) is kind N (ruling D49 (a), VB3). AC4 to AC6 are VER_006_verdict's; AC9 and AC11 are VER_006_arrivals'; AC10 and the ν paragraph are accounted in VER_006_arrivals' assumes. AC7: line 3 of NU_053_dispatch (no colour-slot bound when injection is modelled on the flat net or an arrival feeds a coloured place) is the part that the name-coloured encoding does not answer there; that the query then takes the flat encoding, the report line and the witness (env source → fork (mint) → join → merged, Unreachable(merged) Violated) are kind Q (Rust smt_verifier.rs nu_route_a_declines_under_environment_injection, Java SmtVerifierTest.nuRouteA_declinesUnderEnvironmentInjection, TypeScript smt-verifier.test.ts 'Route A declines under environment injection (VER-006)'). AC8 is cited (VER_006_routeB_env, over the Route B model of Novel/RouteB/Retrodict.lean): the graph's base under AlwaysAvailable consumes and injects nothing on an environment place, so when no row deposits into an environment place, every class it reaches holds the initial count there (env_count_frozen); the decline route_b_env_observation (rules 1 to 4) names a place exactly in AC8's four cases, the property reading one (a quiescence property reads nothing when no marking can rest), an inhibitor arc testing one, a coloured one, and one two transitions consume under conflict priority (ver006_envObservation_ne_none_iff); and PlaceBound(E, 0) on T : E → P beside an idle ν-join is read off the frozen count and declined (env_count_witness). The model has no Bounded(k) base and no verdict record, so the rest of AC8 is kind Q: that a decline is the call's Unknown naming the place, under AlwaysAvailable and Bounded(k), that a verdict nothing declines stands, with the AC6 note on a quiescence verdict, and the witness net (PlaceBound(IN, 0) Unknown, Unreachable(accepted) Violated). Tests: Rust smt_verifier.rs ver006_route_b_declines_a_property_reading_an_env_place (both modes), ver006_route_b_declines_an_inhibitor_on_an_env_place, ver006_route_b_declines_a_coloured_env_place, ver006_route_b_still_answers_when_no_env_count_is_read, ver006_route_b_quiescence_vacuity_note_and_decline; Java SmtVerifierTest ver006ac8_routeB_propertyReadingEnvironmentPlace_isUnknown, _inhibitorOnEnvironmentPlace_isUnknown, _colouredEnvironmentPlace_isUnknown, _verdictsNotObservingTheEnvironment_stand, _vacuousQuiescence_carriesTheAc6Note; TypeScript smt-verifier.test.ts 'SmtVerifier Route B under environment injection (VER-006)' (five cases). In the conflict case every runtime reads whether conflict priority applies, not the selected mode, so on a net with a reapable transition the verdict stands as under NONE: Rust smt_verifier.rs nu_052_env_decline_only_where_conflict_priority_applies, Java SmtVerifierTest envDeclineReadsWhetherConflictPriorityApplies_NU052_VER006_AC8, TypeScript smt-verifier.test.ts 'NU-052 / VER-006 AC8: the env decline applies only where conflict priority is in effect', Python test_nu_verification.py test_nu_052_env_decline_only_where_conflict_priority_applies. Reading the selected mode there, which declines where AC8 lets the verdict stand, is the behaviour RD-39 recorded (spec/runtime-defects.md). Steps 3 and 5 of NU_055_refusal (an arrival that feeds a coloured place; an environment place Route B cannot model, under AlwaysAvailable or Bounded(k)) are AC10 and AC8 for the name-alignment properties.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The encoded open system meets the block.** Example: on `env IN → T → OUT`, the executor injects one token into `IN` and fires `T`; the encoding has the injection rule, so it reaches `OUT = 1` too, and under `Bounded(1)` it never holds two tokens on `IN`.
  <pre>VER_006 refOpenReach</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_forbids_boundedFrozen` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **Bounded(k) injects too** (line 2). Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` under `Bounded(1)` the premises hold (nothing deposits into `IN`, which starts empty), and the executor injects one token and fires `T`; a `Bounded(k)` encoding without the injection rule never reaches `OUT = 1`.
  <pre>¬VER_006 ver006BoundedFrozen</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_forbids_closedLaw` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **No closed-net law on an injected place** (line 1, the third quoted sentence). Example: without injection `env IN → T → OUT` keeps `IN + OUT` constant, 0 from the empty marking. The executor injects one token into `IN` and fires `T`, reaching `OUT = 1`; a reachable set cut down by the closed-net law misses that marking and would prove `PlaceBound(OUT, 0)`.
  <pre>¬VER_006 ver006ClosedLaw</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_forbids_frozen` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **A frozen environment is not modelled injection** (line 1). Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` the executor injects one token and fires `T`, reaching `OUT = 1`; without an injection rule the encoding reaches only the empty marking, so it would prove `PlaceBound(OUT, 0)`.
  <pre>¬VER_006 ver006Frozen</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_forbids_uncapped` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **The cap is part of the mode** (line 3). Example: with one environment place and `Bounded(0)`, an uncapped encoding injects one token, a marking the cap forbids.
  <pre>¬VER_006 ver006Uncapped</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **AC2 at `k = 2`.** Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` from the empty marking, three arrivals, each consumed by `T`, put three tokens on `OUT`: `PlaceBound(OUT, 2)` is violated in the reference reachable set.
  <pre>∃ a,<br>  refOpenReach netEnv [envPlace] Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode.always m0A a ∧ 2 &lt; a outPlace</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_006_arrivals"></a>
## VER-006: Environment Analysis Mode: Arrivals(min, max) is a net rewrite

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_arrivals` · Kind **F** · Scope the SMT verifier under Arrivals(min, max), before any route, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f562c16d7d447f94 ai** · Statement hash `f562c16d7d447f94`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the mode is `Arrivals(min, max)`, the verifier *shall* verify the net closed with a mandatory source holding `min` tokens and an optional source holding `max − min` tokens for each environment place, so that a marking of the net is reachable in the closed net exactly when the environment reaches it with at most `max` arrivals on each environment place, and is a dead marking of the closed net exactly when it is reached with at least `min` arrivals on each environment place and enables no transition of the net. | 1. For every Arrivals rewrite C, all flat nets given as rows, environment places envs (distinct, below the fresh place id base), min ≤ max, and markings a0, a of the net (zero from base on), with every arc, reset and deposit of the rows below base:<br>2. some marking reachable in the closed net (C's rows from C's seed) agrees with a below base exactly when the open system, in which a row fires or one token arrives on an environment place that has seen fewer than max, reaches a from a0 with some arrival counts;<br>3. some dead marking reachable in the closed net agrees with a below base exactly when the open system reaches a with at least min arrivals on every environment place and no row of the net is enabled at a. | <pre>fun C ↦<br>  ∀ (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (envs : List PlaceId) (base lo hi : ℕ)<br>    (a0 a : AMarking),<br>    Novel.EnvSemantics.RowsBelow base rows →<br>      (∀ p ∈ envs, p &lt; base) →<br>        envs.Nodup →<br>          lo ≤ hi →<br>            Novel.EnvSemantics.ZeroAbove base a0 →<br>              Novel.EnvSemantics.ZeroAbove base a →<br>                ((∃ x,<br>                      Novel.ForwardDeposit.ReachAD (C.rows rows envs base lo hi)<br>                          (C.seed a0 envs base lo hi) x ∧<br>                        Novel.EnvSemantics.AgreeBelow base x a) ↔<br>                    ∃ c,<br>                      Novel.EnvSemantics.ReachArr rows envs hi (a0, fun x ↦ 0) (a, c)) ∧<br>                  ((∃ x,<br>                      Novel.ForwardDeposit.ReachAD (C.rows rows envs base lo hi)<br>                          (C.seed a0 envs base lo hi) x ∧<br>                        Novel.EnvSemantics.Dead (C.rows rows envs base lo hi) x ∧<br>                          Novel.EnvSemantics.AgreeBelow base x a) ↔<br>                    ∃ c,<br>                      Novel.EnvSemantics.ReachArr rows envs hi (a0, fun x ↦ 0) (a, c) ∧<br>                        (∀ p ∈ envs, lo ≤ c p) ∧ Novel.EnvSemantics.Dead rows a)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the flat open system of Novel/EnvSemantics (Arrivals.lean), untimed, counts only; the fresh places of the closure are the ids from base on, which stands for the name-freshness check of VER-022 ('A name the rewrite would add that the net already declares is rejected, as in [VER-022].', kind B of that block). The closure omits a source whose count is 0 with its transitions (groupRows), so Arrivals(k) has no mandatory source and Arrivals(k, k) no optional one; the line states the rows' effect, not their names. The names env:arrivals[i], env:arrive[i]:P, env:optional[i], env:arrive?[i]:P and env:decline[i], the report form arrivals(k) / arrivals(min..max), and that the rewritten net is verified with no environment place left (so every route, P-invariants and quiescence apply to it as to a closed net) are kind Q and N; that P-invariants range over the rewritten net is VER-005 on the closed net.
- AC9 (Arrivals(k) bounds the total: for env IN → T → OUT, PlaceBound(OUT, k) Proven and PlaceBound(OUT, k − 1) Violated with k arrivals, while Bounded(k) gives Violated for both; DeadlockFree with OUT a sink decided without the AC6 note) is line 1, with OUT holding at most the arrivals so far (a closure without the optional source, which would prove PlaceBound(OUT, 0) under Arrivals(1), is killed: VER_006_arrivals_forbids_noOpt), and line 4 of VER_006_verdict, which allows the note only when some transition has no reason left: on the closed net T keeps its input on IN, an ordinary place there. arrivals_enumeration_sound composes line 1 with the closed enumeration: its Proven holds for every executor run under the environment. The trace wording is kind Q.
- AC11 (Arrivals(min, max) requires the mandatory arrivals: QuiescentCount({OUT}, 2, 2) Proven under Arrivals(2, 2) and Violated under Arrivals(2) with a trace through env:decline[0]; Arrivals(k) and Arrivals(0, k) give the same verdicts, traces and scripts; min < 0 and max < min are rejected) is line 2 for the mandatory arrivals: a rewrite that drops the mandatory source is killed (VER_006_arrivals_forbids_noMin) on that net, where it lets a run rest with no arrival. Arrivals(k) = Arrivals(0, k) holds by construction (the mode has one form, arrivals 0 k). The rejection of min < 0 or max < min when the mode is built, and before any route runs for a mode value written directly (a Rust enum variant), is kind N (ruling D49 (a), VB3): the model's counts are natural numbers and the lines assume min ≤ max.
- AC10 (under Arrivals(k) with a coloured environment place no ν route treats the injection transition as a mint; the ν routes decline naming the place) and the ν paragraph ('An injection transition producing into a coloured place ([NU-051]) is **not** a mint: the ν routes ([NU-050] Route A, [VER-012] Route B) MUST NOT classify it as one', and 'When an injected place is coloured, the ν routes decline with `Unknown` naming the place, exactly as AC8 does under `AlwaysAvailable`.') are not a line here: ArrClosure is the closure of the flat net and carries no ν layer. Step 3 of NU_055_refusal refuses a name-alignment call in which an arrival feeds a coloured place, and line 3 of NU_053_dispatch runs no colour-slot bound (Route A declines) when an arrival feeds a coloured place. For the other properties it is kind Q. All three runtimes decline on both ν routes before any mint is read, whatever the caller declares: the check colours every producer only to find which places are coloured (coloured_arrival_reason, smt_verifier.rs; colouredArrivalReason in SmtVerifier.java and smt-verifier.ts). A decline is the route's answer, and the call's verdict is what the pipeline gives after it: on Route B the Unknown naming the place, as AC8's; on Route A, and on Route B when a marked coloured place keeps Route B from building its graph, the flat encoding, which reads no names, with a report line naming the place (AC7's form). Tests: Rust smt_verifier.rs arrivals_into_a_coloured_place_is_declined_by_route_b and arrivals_into_a_coloured_place_is_not_coloured_by_route_a; Java EnvironmentArrivalsTest anArrivalIntoAColouredPlace_routeBDeclinesNamingThePlace, anArrivalIntoAColouredPlace_quiescenceDeclinesToo and anArrivalIntoAColouredPlace_routeADeclinesToTheFlatEncoding_namingThePlace; TypeScript arrivals-mode.test.ts 'no ν route treats an arrival as a mint: Route B declines naming the place'. A mint declaration naming an injection transition env:arrive[i]:P is refused in every runtime, since the declaration is judged on the caller's net (NU-010); the decline does not read the declarations either way.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_arrivals_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The VER-022 closure is exact.** Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` under `Arrivals(2, 2)` the closed net has a mandatory source of two tokens; it rests only after both have arrived and `T` has fired twice, with `OUT = 2`, which is exactly the open system's rest with two arrivals.
  <pre>VER_006_arrivals refArrivals</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_arrivals_forbids_noMin` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **A run rests only after the mandatory arrivals** (line 2). Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` under `Arrivals(2, 2)`, `QuiescentCount({OUT}, 2, 2)` holds: the closed net rests only with `OUT = 2`. A closure without the mandatory source lets both optional arrivals be declined, and the empty marking becomes a rest, although the open system never rests there with two arrivals.
  <pre>¬VER_006_arrivals ver006ArrNoMin</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_arrivals_forbids_noOpt` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **Every arrival up to `max` is possible** (line 1). <a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_006_premise"></a>
## VER-006: Environment Analysis Mode: the Bounded(k) premises

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_premise` · Kind **F** · Scope the SMT verifier under Bounded(k), before any route, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 7355f61d98d77bbb ai** · Statement hash `7355f61d98d77bbb`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the mode is `Bounded(k)`, the premise check *shall* pass exactly when the initial marking holds at most `k` tokens on each registered environment place and no transition deposits into one. | 1. For every premise check P, cap k, environment places envs, flat rows and initial marking m0: P passes exactly when m0 holds at most k tokens on each place of envs (EnvCappedC) and no row deposits a token into a place of envs (NoEnvDeposit). | <pre>fun P ↦<br>  ∀ (k : ℕ) (envs : List PlaceId) (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (m0 : CMarking),<br>    P k envs rows m0 = true ↔<br>      Novel.EnvSemantics.EnvCappedC k envs m0 ∧ Novel.EnvSemantics.NoEnvDeposit rows envs</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The flat rows stand for the verified net's transitions: a transition deposits into a place exactly when one of its rows does, since the flattener writes one row per branch of the output spec, and the runtimes read the output places of the spec (Rust t.output_places() in bounded_premise_violation, environment.rs), which are the places of its branches. The check is sufficient, not exact: a deposit that could never push the place above k is refused too. Untimed, counts only.
- What the verifier does when the check fails (Unknown, naming the place and the broken premise, and no route runs) is line 2 of VER_006_verdict, whose check envPremiseOK reads the places each output spec names; on every net at flat place ids it is the check of every P meeting this block, applied to the net's flat rows (envPremiseOK_eq_premise). The order of the check (environment places in code-point order, the initial marking first, the first depositing transition in code-point order, a completion step complete:<t> of VER-004 named t) is the reason text, kind Q. Why the premises are needed is Novel/EnvSemantics: without them the encoding's post-cap blocks firings the executor makes (bounded_initial_overflow_wrong_proven, bounded_producer_overflow_wrong_proven) and the state-class graphs miss firings (supplied_bounded_deposit_wrong_proven, supplied_bounded_initial_wrong_proven, quiescence_bounded_initial_spurious); behind the check the reachable set, the supplied successor and the quiescence clause cover the executor (bounded_checked_sound, bounded_checked_supplied_sound, bounded_checked_quiescence_sound). AC3 is this block, line 2 of VER_006_verdict and line 3 of VER_006.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_premise_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The shipped check is the two premises.** Example: under `Bounded(1)` a net whose initial marking holds one token on the environment place and in which no transition deposits into it passes; two tokens there, or a transition that deposits into it, fail.
  <pre>VER_006_premise refPremise</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_premise_forbids_depOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **An overfull initial marking fails the check** (the initial-count premise). Example: `t1` alone from `{E: 2}` under `Bounded(1)`: nothing deposits into `E`, but it starts above the cap; a check of the deposits alone passes.
  <pre>¬VER_006_premise ver006PremiseDepOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_premise_forbids_initOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **A depositing transition fails the check** (the deposit premise). Example: on the AC3 net from `{a: 2}`, the initial marking holds nothing on `E`, but `t0` deposits into it; a check of the initial marking alone passes, and the post-cap then blocks `t0`'s second firing, which the executor makes.
  <pre>¬VER_006_premise ver006PremiseInitOnly</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_premise_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The AC3 nets.** Example: under `Bounded(1)` with `E` registered, `t0 : a → E`, `t1 : exactly(2, E) → out` from `{a: 2}` fails the check (`t0` deposits into `E`); `t1` alone from `{E: 2}` fails it too (the initial count); `t1` alone from `{E: 1}` passes.
  <pre>refPremise 1 [1] ver006RowsAC3 ver006M0A2 = false ∧<br>  refPremise 1 [1] [(ver006T1, [2])] ver006M0E2 = false ∧<br>    refPremise 1 [1] [(ver006T1, [2])] ver006M0E1 = true</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.joint_core_ver_sketch` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyVer): ✓ The CORE firing requirement CORE-022 and the VER requirements hold together. Example: the reference firing relation; one rest set for VER-014 and VER-002 with the reference violations; the reference verified net and expansion of VER-001, the verified-net function that builds that net, and the reference verifier over it (VER-003), the reference environment verifier (VER-006), the reference timed step (VER-004) and the reference XOR analysis on that expansion (VER-021); the bounded witness phase of VER-025 with its pipeline; the reference P-invariant finder, semiflow encoder, zone library, bound phase, counter rules, firing-bound phase and siphon search; the reference `QuiescentCount` constructor; the reference colour-slot bound of NU-053; and the witnesses of the W10 pipeline blocks. The skeleton of `spec_consistent_ver`.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_006_quiescent"></a>
## VER-006: Environment Analysis Mode: quiescence under modelled injection

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_quiescent` · Kind **F** · Scope the quiescence clause of DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink, QuiescentCount and JoinedOrDeadLettered on every route, AlwaysAvailable and Bounded(k), all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ecbb8aec3d9d76e6 ai** · Statement hash `ecbb8aec3d9d76e6`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the mode is `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, an input or read arc on an environment place *shall* not count as a reason a transition is disabled, unless the mode is `Bounded(k)` and the arc demands more than `k` tokens, in which case the transition *shall* count as permanently disabled.<br><br>*While* the mode is `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)`, the verifier *shall* treat a marking as quiescent exactly when every transition that is not reapable is permanently disabled or has a disabling reason that holds at the marking.<br><br>A marking quiescent in this sense that is reachable with injection, from an initial marking that holds at most `k` tokens on each environment place under `Bounded(k)`, enables no transition, and no sequence of injections makes it enable one. | 1. For every quiescence test Q, place count np, flat rows, environment places envs, mode and marking a: Q calls a quiescent exactly when every row is permanently disabled (permDisabled: an input on an environment place demanding more than the cap, or a read on one under Bounded(0)) or has a disabling reason that holds at a (disableReasonsE: an input on a place that is not an environment place below its demand, any inhibitor arc whose place is marked, a read on a place that is not an environment place and is empty). | <pre>fun Q ↦<br>  ∀ (np : ℕ) (rows : Novel.EnvSemantics.Rows) (envs : List PlaceId)<br>    (mode : Novel.EnvSemantics.InjMode) (a : AMarking),<br>    Q np rows envs mode a = true ↔<br>      ∀ ft ∈ rows,<br>        Novel.EnvSemantics.permDisabled np envs mode ft.1 = true ∨<br>          ((Novel.EnvSemantics.disableReasonsE np envs ft.1).any fun r ↦ r a) = true</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the flat open system of Novel/EnvSemantics, untimed: every row is read as not reapable, which is every row of an untimed net and of a net under assumeNoReaping. The shipped encode_quiescent skips a reapable row (smt_encoder.rs), so 'every transition that is not reapable' is the rows here; the reap-aware reading without injection is VER-002's and ReapAware.lean's. The combination of the skip with injection is not proved: the reapable half of the two quiescence sentences has no evidence here, an open item. An inhibitor arc is a reason whatever its place, since it reads the current count. A place with two input arcs on one transition is outside the model (FlatOK, InputsDistinctPlaces).
- The third quoted sentence is the meaning of the reasons form, derived for every Q meeting the block, and it speaks only of reachable markings from a capped initial marking (which the Bounded(k) premises give): pointwise it is false, since under Bounded(1) a transition whose only input is exactly(2, E) on the environment place E is permanently disabled, so {E: 2} counts as quiescent although that transition is enabled there. VER_006_quiescent_stuck (a reachable capped marking Q calls quiescent is dead and stays dead under every injection, relaxed_violation_real), and VER_006_quiescent_exact for the other direction over reachable markings (a reachable marking stuck under every injection future has a reachable saturation Q calls quiescent, so a quiescence property loses no violation; relaxed_quiescence_exact, under a demand bound and for an injection-stable side condition). The two forms agree on reachable markings, not pointwise, which is why the block quotes the reasons form (ruling D49 (a), VB1).
- AC6 (when injection makes some transition enabled in every marking a quiescence property is vacuously true and the report names the reason) is VER_006_verdict's lines 4 and 5 over the same reasons; quiescence_vacuity_sound proves the note true here: when some row has no reason left and is not permanently disabled, no capped marking is stuck under injection. The body sentence 'Under a mode that models injection an environment place is an ordinary place for the rest set of [VER-014]: a token left on it is stranded unless the caller declares the place a sink, as the closure of [VER-022] does.' is an explanatory consequence, not a line of this block or of VER-014: VER-014's rest set reads every place that is not a sink and sets no environment place apart, so with injection modelled a token on an environment place is stranded like any other. Here InjStable covers the stranded-token disjunct over places that are not sinks, environment places included, which the runtimes treat so (stranding_excuses, rest_set.rs).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_quiescent_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The shipped conjunct is the reasons form.** Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` under `AlwaysAvailable`, `T`'s only input is on `IN`, so it has no reason left and no marking is quiescent; under `Bounded(0)` the same input demands more than the cap, `T` is permanently disabled, and every marking is.
  <pre>VER_006_quiescent refOpenQuiescent</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_quiescent_forbids_plain` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **Waiting for input is not quiescence** (the first quoted sentence). Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` from the empty marking under `AlwaysAvailable`, the plain test calls the marking quiescent because `IN` is empty, and would report a deadlock on a net that is merely waiting for its input; with injection `T` has no reason left.
  <pre>¬VER_006_quiescent ver006PlainQuiescent</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_quiescent_forbids_uncapped` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✗ **A demand above the cap is permanently disabled** (the `unless` clause). Example: with only `t1 : exactly(2, E) → out` and `E` registered under `Bounded(1)`, the environment can never supply two tokens, so every marking is quiescent; a test that ignores the cap sees no reason left for `t1` and calls no marking quiescent.
  <pre>¬VER_006_quiescent ver006UncappedQuiescent</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_quiescent_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_006): ✓ **The reasons on small nets.** Example: on `env IN → T → OUT` the empty marking is not quiescent under `AlwaysAvailable` (the environment can enable `T`); with `t1 : exactly(2, E)` under `Bounded(1)` it is (the demand is above the cap); and with `E` not registered, `t1` waits on an ordinary place, so the empty marking is quiescent and `{E: 2}` is not.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_006_verdict"></a>
## VER-006: Environment Analysis Mode: verdicts

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_006_verdict` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier and every route it dispatches to, all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers environment analysis) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 3fa0ed8c4eabc4cf ai** · Statement hash `3fa0ed8c4eabc4cf`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* environment places are registered and the mode is `Ignore`, *then* the verifier *shall* not return `Proven`, on any route.<br><br>*If* the mode is `Bounded(k)` and the premise check fails, *then* the verifier *shall* return `Unknown` naming the environment place and the broken premise, and *shall* run no route.<br><br>*When* the mode is `Ignore` and the verdict is `Violated` with `counterexampleConfirmed` `true`, the trace *shall* be a firing sequence of the verified net without injection to a marking that violates the property.<br><br>The verifier *shall* report the vacuity note only for a quiescence property, and only when some transition of the verified net that is not reapable is neither permanently disabled nor has a disabling reason left under the mode, an input or read arc on an environment place being a reason under `Ignore` and `Arrivals`, which model no injection, and an inhibitor arc that the terminal rewrite of [EXEC-042] adds being a reason in every mode.<br><br>*While* the mode is `AlwaysAvailable` or `Bounded(k)` and environment places are registered, *when* the property is a quiescence property and some transition of the verified net that is not reapable is neither permanently disabled nor has a disabling reason left (an inhibitor arc that the terminal rewrite of [EXEC-042] adds is a reason), the verifier *shall* report the vacuity note with a `Proven` or `Violated` verdict. | 1. For every firing relation F, violation reading V, verified-net function abs of the net without injection, and environment-aware decider D, and all registered environment places envs, options o, timed nets X, properties φ and initial markings m0:<br>2. if envs is not empty, D under Ignore does not return Proven;<br>3. if the Bounded(k) premise check fails (envPremiseOK: some environment place holds more than k initially, or some transition's output spec names one), D under Bounded(k) returns Unknown with the route Unavailable;<br>4. if D under Ignore returns Violated with counterexampleConfirmed true, then for every query q that abs returns, its trace is a firing sequence under F of q's net from q's initial marking to a marking that violates q's property under V;<br>5. under every mode, if D reports the vacuity note, φ is a quiescence property and some transition has no reason left under the mode (NoRest);<br>6. under AlwaysAvailable or Bounded(k), with envs not empty, φ a quiescence property and some transition with no reason left, if D returns Proven or Violated, it reports the vacuity note. | <pre>fun {K} [LinearOrder K] F V abs D ↦<br>  ∀ (envs : List K) (o : Verifier.Options) (X : TimedNet K) (φ : VerProp K)<br>    (m0 : Novel.Seam.NMarking K),<br>    (envs ≠ [] →<br>        ∀ (meth : String),<br>          (D EnvMode.ignore envs o X φ m0).verdict ≠ Verifier.Verdict.proven meth) ∧<br>      (∀ (k : ℕ),<br>          envPremiseOK k envs X m0 = false →<br>            (∃ why,<br>                (D (EnvMode.bounded k) envs o X φ m0).verdict =<br>                  Verifier.Verdict.unknown why) ∧<br>              (D (EnvMode.bounded k) envs o X φ m0).route = Verifier.Route.unavailable) ∧<br>        ((D EnvMode.ignore envs o X φ m0).verdict = Verifier.Verdict.violated →<br>            (D EnvMode.ignore envs o X φ m0).confirmed = some true →<br>              ∀ (q : Verifier.Query K),<br>                abs o X φ m0 = Except.ok q →<br>                  ∃ f,<br>                    RunF F q.net.net (D EnvMode.ignore envs o X φ m0).trace q.init f ∧<br>                      V o.assumeNoReaping q.net q.prop f) ∧<br>          (∀ (mode : EnvMode),<br>              vacuityNote ∈ (D mode envs o X φ m0).notes →<br>                quiescenceProp φ = true ∧ NoRest o mode envs X = true) ∧<br>            ∀ (mode : EnvMode),<br>              mode.injects = true →<br>                envs ≠ [] →<br>                  quiescenceProp φ = true →<br>                    NoRest o mode envs X = true →<br>                      ((D mode envs o X φ m0).verdict = Verifier.Verdict.violated ∨<br>                          ∃ meth,<br>                            (D mode envs o X φ m0).verdict =<br>                              Verifier.Verdict.proven meth) →<br>                        vacuityNote ∈ (D mode envs o X φ m0).notes</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The decider is VER-003's with two more arguments, the mode and the registered environment places, so every VER-003 line applies to D mode envs for the verified-net function of that mode; for Ignore that function is abs, the verified net without injection, which line 3 reads (ruling D49 (a), VB2). Line 3 is that a quiescence Violated under Ignore is a rest of the net with a silent environment, which need not be a rest under injection: on env IN → T → OUT the empty marking violates TerminatesAtSink({OUT}) under Ignore and no marking can be quiescent under AlwaysAvailable (VER_006_verdict_nonvacuous). A reachability-safety Violated under Ignore is a counterexample under injection too, since a run without injection is a run with it (VER_006_frozen_in_injected).
- 'On any route' and 'run no route' are read on the result: the lines hold whatever route the decider dispatches to, and a refusal placed inside one route after another route proved the property is killed (VER_006_verdict_forbids_noDowngrade). Run no route is the route Unavailable, as Rust, Java and TypeScript report it; the reason text naming the place and the premise, and the code-point order of the check, are kind Q. The premises themselves are VER_006_premise over the flat rows; envPremiseOK is the same check by name, reading the places of each output spec (outPlaces), as Rust's t.output_places() does, and on a net at flat place ids it equals every check meeting VER_006_premise on the net's flat rows (envPremiseOK_flat, envPremiseOK_eq_premise). Line 2 binds the refusal when the check fails, not its converse: a decider whose own check also refuses a place holding exactly k tokens (held >= k where the runtimes write held > k, environment.rs bounded_premise_violation) meets the five lines, because its answer (Unknown, route Unavailable, no note) is one VER-003 allows on every input and the runtimes give after a passed check too (Rust's in-flight refusal of VER-004 and the budget cut of VER-013, smt_verifier.rs). The 'exactly when' half is VER_006_premise's, over the check itself.
- The vacuity condition is read on the verified net. The runtimes evaluate it after the terminal rewrite of EXEC-042, which gives every transition an inhibitor arc on each terminal place (terminal_places.rs, inhibit_on_terminals, applied before verify_net in smt_verifier.rs; TypeScript swaps the rewritten net in, Java does the same in prepare()), so on a net with a terminal place every transition keeps a reason and no note is reported. The nets X here are Reference nets, which have no terminal place, so NoRest reads the user's transitions and the two readings agree; nets with terminal places are outside X, and the terminal rewrite is EXEC-042's.
- Lines 4 and 5 are AC6 and the reworded vacuity paragraph (ruling D49 (a), VB1). The note's presence is the line, its wording kind Q. Line 4 holds under every mode: under Ignore and Arrivals no injection is modelled, so an input or read arc on an environment place is an ordinary reason (EnvMode.supplies is false there), and the closure of Arrivals adds only transitions with an input arc; so under Ignore and Arrivals the note is allowed only for a net with a transition that needs no token at all, as on a closed net; under Arrivals the runtimes compute the condition on the closed net, which has the same transitions with no reason left as the net. Line 5 is scoped to a mode that models injection with environment places registered: there no enumeration or structural route runs (VER-017, VER-020 skip a net with environment places), and Route B and the flat encoding both append the note (smt_verifier.rs, quiescence_vacuous). Without environment places the enumeration route can decide a quiescence property on a net with an input-free transition and does not append the note in Rust; that corner is outside line 5. That the note is true (no capped marking is stuck under injection) is quiescence_vacuity_sound, cited by VER_006_quiescent. 'The verdict stands' is the absence of a refusal: no line forbids the Proven, and VER-003's soundness line holds of it on the verified net with injection.
- AC4 (Ignore with registered environment places never returns Proven) and AC5 (on every route, including any structural or state-class route) are line 1, read at the decider (VER_006_verdict_forbids_noDowngrade). The body's 'a safety property that holds only because environment-gated transitions never fire' is the reason; the line refuses every Proven, as all runtimes do (ignores_environment, smt_verifier.rs; ruling D49 (a), VB3).
- The quiescence properties here are VER-002's three (quiescenceProp: DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink, QuiescentCount), the ones the property type VerProp carries. JoinedOrDeadLettered, which the vacuity paragraph also names, is NU-040's property and is not in VerProp, so lines 4 and 5 say nothing about it, and no block states its vacuity note: NU-040's block NU_040_jodl fixes which markings violate it and reads no environment mode. The runtimes report the note for it as for the other quiescence properties, since they test for a quiescence property as 'not reachability-safety' (Rust quiescence_vacuous and is_reachability_safety in smt_verifier.rs, Java isReachabilitySafety in SmtVerifier.java), and JoinedOrDeadLettered is not reachability-safety. The note is test evidence only for DeadlockFree (Rust ver006_route_b_quiescence_vacuity_note_and_decline); no test checks it for JoinedOrDeadLettered. AC6's QuiescentNameAligned exception (Unknown where no marking can rest) is step 5 of NU_055_refusal, over the call type of NU-055, which this decider does not carry. AC1 is the mode type EnvMode, an offer of configuration, kind N, which no line states; the defaults and the state-class API scope are kind N.

## VER-007: Invariant Strengthening from P-Semiflows

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_007` · Kind **F** · Scope the SMT pipeline's Phase 3 and every encoder it feeds (flat and name-coloured), all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 096f0196831dd00a ai** · Statement hash `096f0196831dd00a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

| The verifier's encoders conjoin every accepted conservation law `y·M = y·M0` into the transition-rule bodies of the CHC/IC3 encoding ([VER-004], [VER-005]).<br><br>A law is accepted only by the **exact gate**: `y·C = 0` against the incidence matrix and `y·M0 = c` are re-checked in exact (overflow-checked) integer arithmetic, and `y` MUST carry zero weight on every place a transition consumes with `all()` / `atLeast(n)` or clears with a reset arc, because the encoder's fire relation is not linear there (Lean `Strengthening.lean`, hypotheses H1/H2; injected environment places are covered by [VER-006], H3').<br><br>A law that fails the gate is dropped from the encoding and listed in the report.<br><br>The encoders *shall* receive a conservation law only when the law passed the exact gate: `y·C = 0` against every column of the incidence matrix, each column counting every token its flat transition deposits and the injector columns of [VER-006] included, and `y·M0` equal to the law's constant, both in exact integer arithmetic, and zero weight on every place a transition consumes with `all()` / `atLeast(n)` or clears with a reset arc.<br><br>The encoders *shall* receive every basis row of [VER-005] that passed the gate, whatever the option's setting.<br><br>A law whose weights or exact sums leave the implementation's integer range fails the gate with a weight-overflow reason.<br><br>Every implementation's range holds a law whose weights, and the sum of the absolute values of the terms of each of its sums `y·C` and `y·M0`, are at most `2^31 − 1`.<br><br>An implementation SHOULD therefore offer an option that unions the gate-validated semiflows into the invariant list the encoders receive, and SHOULD offer an **`auto`** setting that applies the condition above on the caller's behalf: compute and union the semiflows exactly when the basis lost a law to the H1 guard, and skip them otherwise.<br><br>*While* the option is off, the encoders *shall* receive exactly the basis rows that passed the gate.<br><br>*While* the option is on, the encoders *shall* receive exactly the basis rows and the enumerated semiflows that passed the gate.<br><br>*While* the option is `auto`, the encoders *shall* receive what they receive with the option on when the gate dropped a basis row for its weight on a consume-all or reset place, and what they receive with the option off otherwise.<br><br>Semiflows are re-validated by the same exact gate as the basis rows before use;
