**Assumptions**

- The verified net is its flat rows: one deposit row per flat transition and outcome, with the integer post vector the encoder writes (ForwardDeposit.flatRows, fireAD), so a timeout row that forwards two tokens is the row [b, b] and its column counts both (dotIncD; net_flattener.rs `post[..] += n`, as in VER-005). A gate that reads a row as one token per claimed place, the reading before the IO-014 fix, is killed (VER_007_forbids_unitColumn): it accepts a law that a reachable firing breaks (ver007_yBad_not_conserved). A forward that drains its source (VER-001 F3, refused by branch_outcomes::drained_forward before any flat route) has no row; Phase 3 is not run on such a net, and the statement says nothing about it.
- The gate is LawGate: H1 and H2 of Strengthening.lean over deposit rows, plus H3' on the injected places below n; with no injected place (envs = []) H3' is empty. The runtime forces H3' through `y·C = 0` on the injector columns of the incidence matrix ([VER-006], incidence_matrix.rs); LawGate states the consequence, zero weight on each injected place. The constant check `y·M0 = c` is not a clause: a law here is a weight vector and its equation is `y·M = y·M0` with the constant read off M0 (ReachADInjStrs), so a law with a wrong constant does not exist in the model; only the overflow of y·M0 is, through LawFits. The weights are unbounded integers. The runtimes' checked arithmetic drops a law whose exact value leaves their integer range with a weight-overflow reason (the sixth quoted sentence): Java keeps weights and the constant in int and sums y·C in checked long (PInvariantComputer.validateExact), Rust extracts i64 weights and sums in checked i128 (validate_invariants_exact, p_invariant.rs), and TypeScript keeps weights, incidence entries and counts safe integers and sums in BigInt (p-invariant-computer.ts). So lines 2 and 3 are split: a law in a list passes LawGate, whatever its size; a law that passes LawGate is in the list when it fits the range 2^31 − 1 of the seventh quoted sentence (LawFits lawRange), under which no operand, product or partial sum of any runtime's gate leaves its range, whatever the order of the terms. A law outside the range may be dropped, which only shrinks the list, and VER_007_preserves_reach holds for every list a VER-007 encoding hands over. The model's encoding takes the initial marking a0 for this reason alone: the reference ignores it, and the gate's y·M0 = c is not a clause (the constant is read off a0).
- The statement fixes the list the encoders receive, not what an encoder does with it. That each encoder conjoins every received law, and only those, into its rule bodies is the encoder's obligation (VER-004 for the flat encoder, NU-050 for the name-coloured one) and out of scope here; the first quoted sentence and the 'receive' wording of the fourth and fifth are read through it. The reach corollary VER_007_preserves_reach models that conjoining (ReachADInjStrs: every handed law conjoined into the firing rules, the injection rules carrying none).
- The lists are read as sets (lines 2 and 3 are membership statements): the encoder conjoins each law, so the order (the canonical order of VER-013) and a semiflow equal to a basis row (deduplicated by strengthen_with_semiflows) do not change the rule bodies' meaning. Malformed rows (a weight vector of the wrong length, a support inconsistent with the weights) do not exist in the model: a weight is a total function on place indices, read below the place count n.
- 'The basis lost a law to the H1 guard' and 'the gate dropped a basis row for its weight on a consume-all or reset place' are read through the drop reason the runtimes key auto on, the one that names Strengthening.lean H1 (smt_verifier.rs union_wanted, smt-verifier.ts basisLostALaw, SmtVerifier.java basisLostALaw). Which reason a row gets depends on the order of the gate's checks. Inside the range 2^31 − 1 of LawFits every runtime records H1 for a basis row that fails it: Rust checks H1 after shape and support only, Java after the length check (its int narrowing in PInvariantComputer.computeChecked and its int constant pass every row in range), and TypeScript after its safe-integer checks of the weights and of the constant (exactCheckFailure, p-invariant-computer.ts), which every row in range passes. Outside the range the recorded reason, and so auto's choice, is the runtime's: TypeScript and Java drop a row whose weights or constant leave their range for overflow first and do not union on it, while Rust checks H1 on its i64 weights and unions. Both meet the quoted sentence, whose trigger is the reason the gate recorded, so neither is a defect. Line 4 is split accordingly: auto's list is the option-on list or the option-off list in every case, so every law it hands over passes the gate; it is the option-on list when a basis row that fits the range fails H1 (BasisLostH1Fits) and the option-off list when no basis row fails H1 (BasisLostH1 false); when the only basis rows failing H1 leave the range the statement leaves the choice open. The overflow-first gate of TypeScript and Java meets the statement (VER_007_allows_overflowFirst, on a basis row of weight 2^60 on a reset place), and an auto list that is neither the option-on nor the option-off list is killed (VER_007_forbids_autoUngated). A row dropped for y·C alone does not switch auto on (killed: VER_007_forbids_autoAnyDrop), and a basis row inside the range lost to H1 does (killed: VER_007_forbids_autoNever).
- The basis rows and the semiflows are inputs: their computation is VER-005's (the null-space basis) and the Farkas enumeration's, which may truncate the minimal set, so sfs is any list. The statement holds for every list, which is the 'arbitrary truncation' paragraph: a law the enumeration never returns is a proof the encoder does not get, never a proof it gets wrong. 'Implementations SHOULD report the truncation when it binds' is a report line (kind Q).
- 'If the option is off, or it is `auto` and the gate dropped no basis row for its weight on a consume-all or reset place, then the verifier shall not compute the semiflows.' is kind Q: a pure function cannot tell a computed and discarded list from one never computed, and the sentence is about cost (the enumeration's run time and heap). Line 2 and line 4 state what the model can see: in those cases no semiflow that is not a validated basis row reaches the encoders. 'The enumeration is expensive and MUST be skipped when nothing will read it.' and 'An implementation MUST compute semiflows only when the option is on, or is `auto` and the gate dropped a basis row for its weight on a consume-all or reset place.' are the same obligation, kind Q, and 'Such a caller MUST request the union explicitly.' is the caller's, not the verifier's: auto's choice is line 4, which says nothing about the form of the invariant list a caller inspects.
- The third quoted sentence has two halves. 'Dropped from the encoding' is lines 2 and 3 (a basis row that fails the gate is in no list: VER_007_forbids_offNoGate; one that passes is in every list: VER_007_forbids_offEmpty, VER_007_forbids_onSfsOnly). 'Listed in the report' is a report line for each dropped basis row, kind Q, as the `Dropped semiflow:` line of AC1 is for each dropped semiflow.
- AC1 is quoted and is lines 2 and 3 for the semiflows: a semiflow that fails the gate is in no list. A gate that checks only y·C = 0 is killed (VER_007_forbids_gateCOnly, the Farkas row yUnit of semiflow_gate_is_necessary), and so are a gate without H3' (VER_007_forbids_noEnvZero, the law of injection_hypothesis_is_necessary), a gate whose H1 forgets reset arcs (VER_007_forbids_resetBlind) and a gate that reads a deposit row as one token per place (VER_007_forbids_unitColumn). The `Dropped semiflow:` report line is kind Q.
- AC2 (with the option off the semiflows do not reach the encoders, are not computed, and the report is byte-identical to a build without the feature) is line 2 for the first clause, killed by an off that lets the semiflows through (VER_007_forbids_offLeaks); not computing them and the byte-identical report are kind Q, and off as the default is kind N.
- AC3 (under auto the report says which way it went and why, the union happens exactly when the gate dropped a basis row for its weight on a consume-all or reset place, the verdict equals that of the explicit setting auto chose, and the report's off wording says the skipped semiflows add no constraint) is line 4 for the union and the verdict: the list auto hands the encoders equals the list of the setting it chose, so every phase reading the list answers alike. An auto that always unions, one that never unions, one that unions on any dropped row and one whose list is neither the on nor the off list are killed (VER_007_forbids_autoAlways, VER_007_forbids_autoNever, VER_007_forbids_autoAnyDrop, VER_007_forbids_autoUngated). The report lines and their wording are kind Q.
- AC4 (the report line `  Semiflows encoded as invariants: N`, N counting the semiflows added after deduplication, and the result's invariant count and list including them) is line 3 for the list; the report line and the count are kind Q. An on that drops the semiflows is killed (VER_007_forbids_onOmits).
- AC5 (the certificate check receives the strengthened list and re-proves every law against the unstrengthened step relation on the flat encoding) is not a line here: the certificate check is a step of the verifier pipeline that the pipeline model names (certificate check, in rtStepNames of Verifier/Pipeline.lean) and does not enter, so no block states what it receives; its soundness is Novel/Certificate.lean (vc_sound). This block fixes the list the check receives.
- AC6 (a genuine violation stays Violated with the option enabled) follows from lines 2 to 4: every law in every list passes the gate, so the strengthened relation reaches exactly the abstract reachable set over the deposit rows with injection (VER_007_preserves_reach: ReachADInj equals ReachADInjStrs). This is also the paragraph sentence that the option is pure strengthening and can never turn a `Violated` into a `Proven`.
- AC7 (the strengthened list reaches the name-coloured encoder of NU-050 as well as the flat one, witnessed by a coloured net whose script differs between the option's two states) is not a line here: E is the list Phase 3 hands to whichever encoder runs, and that the coloured encoder conjoins a coloured place's term as the sum over its colour slots is stated by no block, since no block models the script of Route A's coloured encoder; the differing script is a test (kind Q: Rust smt_verifier.rs semiflows_reach_the_coloured_encoder).
- 'No other phase reads them: the colour-slot bound of [NU-053] is a linear program over the incidence matrix, not a semiflow search.' is kind N, a design fact about another phase: the NU-053 block's model takes the rows and no semiflow list. The rest of the cost paragraph, the 'What auto does not decide' paragraph and the trigger paragraph (one consume-all or reset arc on a busy place loses every basis row whose support touches it) are explanation: the trigger is BasisLostH1 and VER_007_nonvacuous shows it on a net with one consume-all arc. The Implementation notes name the per-language entry points (kind N); the test derivation is AC1 to AC7 on a budgeted work loop, as above.

## VER-010: State Class Graph Analysis

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_010` · Kind **B** · Scope the timed state class graph builder (StateClassGraph.build), Java, TypeScript and Rust (MAY; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers it) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 e8ab985ddefc931d ai** · Statement hash `e8ab985ddefc931d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| In them a timed run of the net starts at an initial marking with every clock at zero, on a net in which no transition's earliest firing time is below zero or above its latest, and follows the Time Petri net semantics: time may pass only as far as no enabled transition goes past its latest firing time, a transition fires no earlier than its earliest firing time and deposits its outputs at the instant it fires, and a clock is kept or restarted by the persistence rule below.<br><br>A class holds a state when the class's marking is the state's marking and its firing domain holds every combination of firing times the state allows the class's clocks.<br><br>A class is well formed when its clocks are the transitions enabled in its marking and its firing domain has the form letting time pass leaves: the closure of a matrix with a finite reference bound in which every clock's lower bound is zero.<br><br>*When* a timed run of the net reaches a state, the state class graph *shall* hold a class, reachable from its initial class, that holds the state.<br><br>Every class the state class graph reaches from its initial class *shall* be well formed and *shall* list its clocks once each, in ascending order of transition name compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).<br><br>*When* a transition can fire with one of its outcomes ([VER-001]) from a state in which no enabled **Assumptions**

- The model is the timed state class graph of Novel/TimedScg on index nets: a net (TNet) lists transitions with their structural core, their outcome rows (branch_outcomes::outcomes, one constant deposit each) and their static interval [eft, lft] in seconds; a class (Cls) is a marking, a clock list and a positional firing domain. The step G is abstract (ScgStep). The witness is refScg: initial_state_class and compute_successor with the canonical order coByName and the emptiness check at EPSILON = 1e-9 seconds, its successors listed with their labels (succL, the order of state_class_graph.rs:186-247). It holds the block (VER_010_reference) by init_sound, Progress.graph_classes_ok, Scg.graph_ordered, timed_run_sound and successor_sound.
- A timed run is a run of TStep, the Time Petri net semantics with strong urgency: time passes only while no enabled transition is past its latest bound, a transition fires at or after its earliest bound and deposits at that instant, and a clock is kept by persists, the rule of VER_010_persist. That TStep is what the executor does is premise 9 of TimedScg/Succ.lean, assumed: the on-time bridge from the reference executor's steps to TStep (J7 of this wave) is not proved, and until it is the block speaks of TStep. The executor behaviours outside TStep are the assumptions AC4 now lists (ruling D20, clash ver-d#8): a late executor that reaps or fires past a latest bound ([TIME-013], Retrodict.reaping_escapes_timed_graph), an action that takes time (Retrodict.action_duration_escapes), and the pass recheck of [EXEC-003] AC3, which belongs to atomic firings. The model's latest bound of an immediate or delayed transition is the finite MAX_DURATION_MS read as no bound (Timing.lean, assumed).
- Line 1 binds the shape of every class G reaches: well formed (ClsWF), so a class that holds a state holds every combination of firing times of the state's enabled transitions, which is the markdown's definition of holding, and ordered by name (ClocksOrdered). An initial class whose zone has no bound at all, no lower bound either, is not well formed and is killed (VER_010_forbids_untimedInit). Line 1 does not rule out the untimed reachability graph: a zone in which every clock's lower bound is zero and no clock has an upper bound is well formed (it is closed and is its own let-time-pass form), holds every state with its marking, and a graph that gives every class it reaches that zone, with the clocks and successors lines 1 to 3 ask, meets this block. Ruling out that widening is the exact half (ruling D67, see line 2), not this block. An initial class left in enabling order is killed (VER_010_forbids_initUnordered): a port that reorders only in compute_successor and forgets initial_state_class (state_class_graph.rs:361-381, the regression test canonical_order_applies_to_the_initial_class_too) is this mutant. The reference meets the line by Progress.graph_classes_ok and Scg.graph_ordered.
- Line 2 ranges over well-formed classes and urgent states, the sentence's state in which no enabled transition is past its latest firing time. Without urgency the line would ask too much: a state with an overdue enabled clock is held vacuously by every class with its marking (that clock allows no firing time), and the firing rule TStep.fire does not ask for urgency. Every state of a timed run is urgent (Run.timed_run_sound), so line 2 loses no run. Run coverage in line 1 follows from line 2, the shape of line 1 and an initial class that holds the start state (ver010_covers_of). Line 2 is the sound half of AC2: the successor holds every state the firing rule allows. The exact half, that every state a successor holds is reached by a timed run, is a later block under ruling D67 (Lean proves the sound half only, TimedScg/Succ.lean), so AC2's 'correctly' is covered here for soundness only: the sound half does not forbid a successor that keeps an empty zone or widens a zone, and so adds markings no run reaches.
- AC1, first sentence (the graph enumerates the reachable marking and zone pairs) is line 1, for soundness; a closed build at the class-key explorer of the model holds every state of every timed run (ver010_closed_covers, from Scg.scgGraph_covers). The Rust, Java and TypeScript builds do too, since their class keys tell markings apart (VER_010_key's assumes). A build that dedups classes by a marking string that does not escape place names, the behaviour RD-40 recorded, can give two classes with different markings one key and miss a marking a timed run reaches from a graph reported complete. AC1's canonical order is line 1 at the classes of G and VER_010_key's first line at the order; AC1's key over the full matrix is VER_010_key. An initial class that ignores the transitions enabled at the start loses every run that fires (VER_010_forbids_noClockInit). AC1's 'Two arrivals at the same marking and zone by different interleavings are one class' is not a line of any block: ScgStep stores no classes. It is evidence on the reference build, cited (ver010_key_graph, ver010_stored_one_class); the markdown states it as a remark, not a shall sentence.
- AC2 (successor computation and consumption by consumptionCount(available)) is lines 2 and 3. Line 3's marking is fireAD, the model of consume_marking then produce_marking (state_class_graph.rs:669-700, input_consume_count deferring to input::consumption_count, IO-007): All and AtLeast inputs drain their place (Basic.consumeAllAt), other inputs lose requiredCount, reset places are emptied. A step that removes requiredCount() tokens from an AtLeast(2) input over 5 tokens leaves 3 and is killed (VER_010_forbids_requiredCount); any step that meets the block empties the place (VER_010_atLeast_drains, the second regression of the test derivation). The first regression (an All input followed by a transition inhibited on its place: the inhibited successor must be reachable) is VER_010_all_enables_inhibited: any step that meets the block reaches a class in which the inhibited transition is enabled.
- AC3 (every outcome, each XOR branch and a timeout outcome that deposits differently, is a virtual transition of its own, [VER-001]) is the label of lines 2 and 3: one successor per outcome index of the fired transition, the index counting the outcomes in the order of branch_outcomes::outcomes, the order in which [VER-001] numbers the _b<i> virtual transitions. A step that keeps only the first outcome is killed (VER_010_forbids_firstOutcome). The rows are constant deposits (premise 3 of Succ.lean): a timeout that forwards an input, whose count produce_marking reads from the tokens the firing consumed (state_class_graph.rs:702-705), is outside the model, so AC3 is not covered for such a transition; an action deposits one token per named place of its branch ([IO-016] AC4).
- AC4 (the persistence rule of the intermediate marking) is VER_010_persist; its fresh-interval clause is covered for soundness only: in succWith the newly enabled clocks are those enabled in M' and not kept, and [VER-011]'s successor line holds each of them between its static bounds, held, not exact, so a graph that widens a newly enabled clock's interval meets VER-010 and VER-011. The exact half is VER-011's later D67 block. 'This is the executor's rule' is premise 9, assumed as above. The environment modes of AC4's last sentence are out of scope: the model has no environment places (premise 8 of Succ.lean), and [VER-006] states the modes. A transition outside the in-flight split fires atomically in the model; the split is AC5.
- AC5 (the builder builds the net it is given and does not apply the in-flight split; a caller outside SmtVerifier must apply it; the documentation must say so) is not a line: the model's builder takes the net it is given (Scg.scgGraph), the caller's obligation to split first is kind A ([VER-004], Novel.InFlight.split_covers_executor), and the documentation sentence is kind Q.
- The persistence sentence and the key sentences are lines of VER_010_persist and VER_010_key, over the survival test, the canonical order and the class identity; ScgStep has no survival test and no key, so those lines bind the graph by construction (ver010_succWith_of, VER_010_joint), not as lines of this block. A graph that restarts a clock the rule keeps, when the fresh interval contains the time the clock had left, meets this block: the restart only widens the zone, which is the exact half. The clock order alone is also bound here, at the classes of G (line 1).
- Further premises of Succ.lean: one input arc per place (premise 2, Basic.InputsDistinctPlaces), exact rational arithmetic (premise 4; floating point is not modelled), and well-formed timing (premise 6, TimingWF, the markdown's net in which no transition's earliest firing time is below zero or above its latest; every net built from the shipped Timing constructors meets it, Timing.timingWF_of_valid_timings, and Rust's TransitionBuilder::build validates it again). Unique transition names (premise 1) are the shared assumption of rulings D10 and D23, for the whole block and not only for the key block: Rust's state-class builder looks up the fired transition, and the transitions behind a clock, by name (state_class_graph.rs, compute_successor, which finds a transition by comparing names), so on a net with two transitions of one name its successors (lines 2 and 3) follow the first one's arcs; Java and TypeScript keep the transition objects (StateClassGraph.java, initialStateClass). Python exposes no state class graph, so the block binds Java, TypeScript and Rust. VER-010 is MAY; its shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the graph (ruling D22).

## VER-010: State Class Graph Analysis: canonical class identity

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_010_key` · Kind **F** · Scope the canonical clock order and the class key of the timed state class graph, Java, TypeScript and Rust · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 a4639db8259032ea ai** · Statement hash `a4639db8259032ea`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The canonical order of the state class graph *shall* either keep a list of transitions or return a permutation of its positions, and *shall* leave every list it is given in ascending order of transition name, compared by Unicode code point ([VER-013]).<br><br>*If* the transition names of the net are unique, *then* the class key of the state class graph *shall* give two classes, each with the transitions enabled in its marking as clocks, once each in that order, and a canonical firing domain (closed, zero on the diagonal, every clock with a finite lower bound), the same key exactly when they have the same marking and their firing domains hold the same firing times. | 1. For every canonical order co (from a net and a clock list to no reordering or an order of the positions) and every class identity same (from a net and two classes to whether they share a key):<br>2. for every net N and every list l of transitions, co N either keeps l or returns a permutation of its positions (CoWF), and l reordered by co N is in ascending order of the code points of the transition names;<br>3. for every net N whose transition names are unique and every two classes C, C' whose clocks are the transitions enabled in their marking, listed once each in name order, and whose firing domains are canonical (closed, zero on the diagonal, a finite reference row): same N C C' holds exactly when C and C' have the same marking and their firing domains hold the same valuations. | <pre>fun co same ↦<br>  (∀ (N : Novel.TimedScg.TNet),<br>      Novel.TimedScg.CoWF (co N) ∧<br>        ∀ (l : List ℕ),<br>          List.Pairwise (fun a b ↦ Verifier.Scg.nameKey N a ≤ Verifier.Scg.nameKey N b)<br>            (Novel.TimedScg.reorder (co N) l)) ∧<br>    ∀ (N : Novel.TimedScg.TNet),<br>      Verifier.Scg.NamesUnique N →<br>        ∀ (C C' : Novel.TimedScg.Cls),<br>          GoodCls N C →<br>            GoodCls N C' →<br>              (same N C C' ↔<br>                C.m = C'.m ∧<br>                  ∀ (θ : ℕ → ℚ),<br>                    Novel.TimedScg.SatN (C.cs.length + 1) C.D θ ↔<br>                      Novel.TimedScg.SatN (C'.cs.length + 1) C'.D θ)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The canonical order and the class identity are abstract. The witnesses are coByName (canonical_order, state_class_graph.rs:406-415: none when the names are already in order, otherwise the positions sorted by name with a stable sort, comparing code points as CodePointOrder in Java and compareCodePoints in TypeScript do) and refSameKey (equality of StateClass::canonical_key: the marking, the clock names in clock order and every bound of the firing domain, state_class.rs:59-61). They meet the block (VER_010_key_reference) by Scg.reorder_sorted and Scg.canon_unique, the new lemma that two canonical domains holding the same firing times agree on every bound. The model's key compares the index marking, which is injective, and so do the runtime keys: Rust's canonical_key and zone_key backslash-escape the separators \ , : | # in place and clock names (marking_state.rs:149-166 push_key_name, dbm.rs:289), TypeScript's class key starts with MarkingState.key(), the JSON of the sorted [name, count] entries (marking-state.ts:76), and Java compares markings and zones by structure (StateClass.equals). A key that renders the marking as a string that does not escape place names, the behaviour RD-40 recorded, gives the markings {a:1, b:1} and {'a:1,b':1} one key, and line 2 fails there. VER_010_key_forbids_markingBlind kills a key that gives two markings one key.
- Line 2 speaks of classes shaped as the graph shapes them (GoodCls). Every class the model's successor step builds (initCls and succ with any order that meets line 1) has that shape when the emptiness check is exact (Scg.ExactEps: every bound a whole number of milliseconds at the Rust EPSILON, ruling D58), so two classes of the graph are one exactly when they have the same marking and the same firing domain, whatever interleavings reached them (ver010_key_graph, for any order and identity that meet the block). The model's key compares exact rationals; the runtimes render each bound at three decimals of a second, which is exact on whole-millisecond bounds ([VER-011] line 8). A fractional TypeScript bound is outside both (VER_011_key_submillisecond).
- Unique names are a premise: with a repeated name the stable sort keeps two enabling orders apart (Scg.ex_order_dupNames). The canonical-domain premise needs the zero diagonal (Scg.ex_diag_needed). The model's explorer dedups by the index key, which is the class key on a net with unique names (Scg.idxKey_eq_iff_classKey), and a build stores one class per marking and zone (Scg.stored_one_class, ver010_stored_one_class). That a graph stores one class per key (AC1's 'Two arrivals ... are one class') is not a line: neither ScgStep nor the key block stores classes, so it is evidence on the reference build only (ver010_key_graph, ver010_stored_one_class, cited). The markdown says that a net with a repeated name ([CORE-021] allows one) falls outside the key sentence.
- The key sentence is phrased about the class key, and the line is about the abstract identity same; the graph is tied to it by construction (VER_010_joint), and line 1 of VER_010 binds the clock order at the classes of the graph. A graph that dedups by another identity meets VER_010; the key sentence forbids it through the identity it uses.
- Mutants: a key over the projections alone (the bounds of each clock against the reference clock, not the bounds between two clocks) merges the two classes ver010_C1 and ver010_C2, which differ in one difference bound (VER_010_key_forbids_projections); a key that leaves the marking out merges ver010_C1 and ver010_C1m, which have one zone and two markings (VER_010_key_forbids_markingBlind, the shape of the behaviour RD-40 recorded); an order that keeps the enabling order lists the clocks b, a, Z as they came (VER_010_key_forbids_enablingOrder); an order that returns no position at all leaves every list empty, and so sorted, but is no permutation (VER_010_key_forbids_dropAll). A key without the clock names is not killed: on good classes of a net with unique names the marking fixes the clock list, so the names add nothing to the identity.
- AC1's measurement (the order-sensitive key inflated the class count 1.5 times on an untimed workflow net, one marking held by fourteen classes) is kind Q, and its remark that a projection-only key can lose a reachable marking is the reason for line 2, not a line.

## VER-010: State Class Graph Analysis: clock persistence

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_010_persist` · Kind **F** · Scope the survival test of the timed state class graph successor (compute_successor), Java, TypeScript and Rust · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 9d3d1118dedb2015 ai** · Statement hash `9d3d1118dedb2015`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition `t` fires from marking `M` into marking `M'`, the successor step of the state class graph *shall* keep the clock of a transition `t'` enabled in `M` exactly when `t'` is not `t` and is enabled both in `M'` and in the intermediate marking `M - Pre(t)`, which has the inputs of `t` consumed, its reset places drained and none of its outputs deposited. | 1. For every net N, marking M, fired transition t, outcome row d and transition t' enabled in M, with M' = fireAD M t d (the successor marking) and Mid = inter M t (the intermediate marking: inputs consumed by consumptionCount, reset places drained, nothing deposited): the survival test keeps t' exactly when t' ≠ t, t' is enabled in M' and t' is enabled in Mid. | <pre>fun surv ↦<br>  ∀ (N : Novel.TimedScg.TNet) (m : AMarking) (f : ℕ) (d : Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit)<br>    (c : ℕ),<br>    Novel.TimedScg.en N m c = true →<br>      (surv N f (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD m (Novel.TimedScg.trOf N f) d)<br>            (Novel.TimedScg.inter m (Novel.TimedScg.trOf N f)) c =<br>          true ↔<br>        c ≠ f ∧<br>          Novel.TimedScg.en N (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD m (Novel.TimedScg.trOf N f) d)<br>                c =<br>              true ∧<br>            Novel.TimedScg.en N (Novel.TimedScg.inter m (Novel.TimedScg.trOf N f)) c =<br>              true)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The survival test is abstract (SurvTest): the successor of the graph is succWith (surv N), compute_successor_gated with both gates true (state_class_graph.rs:493-547), and the test is read only at the clocks of the class, the transitions enabled in its marking. The witness is refSurv = survives (since 6.0.0); it meets the line by its definition (persistence_rule). Any test that meets the line gives the reference successor on every class whose clocks are enabled in its marking (ver010_succWith_of), so VER_010 holds of the graph built with it. The line is stronger than the sentence in one way: the fired transition and the outcome row are arbitrary, not only an enabled transition and one of its rows.
- The pre-6.0.0 rule (survivesOld, Rust 5.x and earlier: not the fired transition and enabled after, with no look at the intermediate marking) is killed on the refresh net of the test derivation (VER_010_persist_forbids_old: Retrodict.netRT, where Refresh takes and puts back the timer token that CloseSession waits on). Retrodict.old_rule_loses_run shows what the old rule cost: a timed run whose state no successor of the old graph holds (ver010_old_rule_loses_run).
- AC4's other sentences: 'Every other transition enabled in M' gets a fresh firing interval' is the shape of succWith (newly enabled = enabled in M' and not kept) with [VER-011]'s successor line; 'This is the executor's rule ([TIME-012])' is premise 9 of TimedScg/Succ.lean, assumed (see VER_010); the limits of the graph are VER_010's assumptions. The bullets of [TIME-012] in the graph are Run.fired_never_persists, inhibitor_never_restarts, reset_restarts and surplus_keeps, cited there.
- The test derivation's three cases are VER_010_persist_nonvacuous: on the refresh net with one timer token the delayed transition restarts, with a second token it keeps its clock, and with a reset arc on the timer place it restarts.

## VER-011: DBM Zone Representation

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_011` · Kind **F** · Scope the zone library of every state class graph, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 112209c5b3864d89 ai** · Statement hash `112209c5b3864d89`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

| *When* the zone library creates a zone from one lower and one upper bound per clock, the zone *shall* hold exactly the firing times that lie between the bounds of each clock.<br><br>Canonicalising a zone *shall not* change the firing times it holds.<br><br>*When* a zone holds some firing times, its canonical matrix *shall* be closed: no bound exceeds the sum of the two bounds of a detour through any clock of the matrix, the reference clock included.<br><br>The zone library *shall* report a zone empty only when it holds no firing times.<br><br>*If* every finite bound of a zone is a whole number of milliseconds and every clock, the reference clock included, has a finite lower bound, *then* the zone library *shall* report the zone empty exactly when it holds no firing times.<br><br>*When* a transition fires from a zone, the successor zone, with the persistent clocks first in the order given and the newly enabled clocks after them, *shall* hold every firing time the firing rule allows: the fired clock is not later than any other clock, each persistent clock keeps the time it had left after the fired clock, and each newly enabled clock lies between its static bounds.<br><br>*When* the clocks of a zone that holds some firing times are permuted, the zone library *shall* keep the reference clock first, move every other bound of the matrix with its two clocks, and write zero as the bound of the reference clock against itself.<br><br>*If* two zones each hold some firing times and every finite bound of both is a whole number of milliseconds, *then* their dedup keys *shall* be equal exactly when their matrices are equal entry by entry, the bounds between two clocks included. | 1. create n lb ub (one lower and one upper bound per clock) holds a valuation θ exactly when every clock i &lt; n lies between lb[i] and ub[i], relative to the reference clock.<br>2. canon d D holds exactly the valuations D holds, on every matrix, empty ones included.<br>3. **Assumptions**

- The model is a zone library ZoneLib on positional matrices (TimedScg.NMat, entry D a b bounds θ a - θ b, index 0 the reference clock, clock i at index i + 1), a dimension beside each matrix, and valuations θ : Nat → ℚ. θ a - θ 0 for a clock a is the firing time the body sentence names: the time from entering the class until that transition fires. Bounds are exact rationals in seconds with ⊤ for infinity; floating point is out of the model (Dbm.lean). The model has no emptiness flag beside a matrix: an empty zone is a matrix that holds no valuation (ver011_emptyMat stands for Rust's empty_dbm). The witness is refZoneLib (createPre, canonN, FlaggedN at EPSILON = 1e-9, constrainPre then fireMat behind the three early returns, permMat, and ver011_key with one key for every flagged zone).
- A whole number of milliseconds is WholeMs, which also accepts ⊤: 'every finite bound' in the fifth and eighth sentences, so a zone with an unbounded clock (a transition with no deadline) is covered. Every zone has the reference clock, so its dimension is at least 1 (the 0 < d premise of line 5), and 'every clock, the reference clock included, has a finite lower bound' is the finite reference row D 0 i for every i < d, D 0 0 included.
- AC1 (lower and upper bounds for each transition clock) is line 1 and the first quoted sentence; a create that drops the upper bounds is killed (VER_011_forbids_noUpper).
- AC2 (zone emptiness is detectable) is lines 4 and 5 and the fourth and fifth quoted sentences: the flag is sound on every matrix (line 4, so a flagged zone never drops a reachable class; a flag raised on a zero diagonal is killed, VER_011_forbids_zeroDiag) and exact on whole-millisecond matrices with a finite reference row (line 5; a flag never raised is killed, VER_011_forbids_neverEmpty). The finite reference row is the premise of Dbm.empty_iff_flagged; every matrix create and fire build has one (each clock gets a finite lower bound and the reference entry is 0). The whole-millisecond premise is ruling D58: the Rust flag is the diagonal below -1e-9, exact only when no negative cycle lies in [-1e-9, 0), which Grid.flagged_of_flagged_zero shows for matrices on the millisecond grid.
- Lines 2 and 3 (the second and third quoted sentences) are what canonical means in AC4: canonicalisation keeps the zone (Dbm.sat_canon) and closes a satisfiable matrix (Dbm.closed_canon). Line 3 quantifies over every index of the matrix, the reference index 0 and repeated indices included, which is what the third sentence's detour through any clock of the matrix, the reference clock included, says. A canonicalisation that resets the diagonal hides an empty zone (VER_011_forbids_diagReset); one that returns the matrix unchanged keeps the zone but is not closed, which a detour through the reference clock shows (VER_011_forbids_noClose). Lines 2 and 3 do not fix one canonical matrix per zone: on a clock with no upper bound a closed matrix of the same zone may carry any non-negative diagonal entry. That two matrices of one zone canonicalise to one matrix (closure with a zero diagonal) is out of scope here. Every matrix create and fire build starts from a zero diagonal, which canonicalisation only lowers and which stays non-negative while the zone holds a valuation (canonN_le, Dbm.diag_nonneg_of_sat), and the dedup over canonical matrices is VER-010's key block.
- AC3 (the successor DBM is computed correctly after transition firing) is line 6 and the sixth quoted sentence, its sound half: the successor holds every firing time the Berthomieu-Diaz rule allows (TimedScg.sat_constrainPre, sat_fireMat, satN_canonN). A successor that keeps a persistent clock's old lower bound instead of the time it has left is killed (VER_011_forbids_noShift). The successor's layout (persistent clock p at index p + 1 in the order given, then newly enabled clock j at index |ps| + j + 1) is part of line 6 and of the sixth sentence; VER-010's permutation into the canonical order relies on it. The exact half (the successor holds no other firing time) is a later block under ruling D67: Lean proves the sound half only, and VER-023's TIMED_CONFIRMED block waits on the exact half. Until that block lands AC3 is partly covered, and 'computed correctly' is not discharged: a successor that drops every constraint, or one built without the constraint that the fired clock fires first, meets line 6. The reference models Rust's three early returns (a fired clock out of range, an empty input zone, a constrained matrix flagged empty) by returning an empty zone; under line 6's premises none is taken (k < n, and the input and the constrained matrix hold a valuation, so neither is flagged), so they bear on the exact half only, and VER_011_fire_first shows the reference returns an empty successor when the fired clock cannot fire first.
- AC4, first half (a permutation of the clocks that reorders the matrix with them) is line 7 and the seventh quoted sentence, for a zone that holds a firing time: Rust and TypeScript return an empty zone unchanged (permuted returns self when the zone is flagged), so the line does not speak of empty zones. Every entry moves with its two clocks, the reference row and column stay first, and the reference entry (0, 0) is written as 0 as all three runtimes write it (out[0] = 0); on a zone that holds a firing time D 0 0 is non-negative, so writing 0 keeps the zone. A permutation that does not move the matrix is killed (VER_011_forbids_noMove), and so is one that keeps the old reference entry (VER_011_forbids_keepRef). That a permuted zone holds the permuted valuations is Dbm.sat_permD (cited for VER-011), and that it stays closed is Dbm.closed_permD.
- AC4, second half (a dedup key over the full canonical matrix; equality positional over the canonical order; exact at millisecond resolution) is line 8 and the eighth quoted sentence, for zones that hold some firing time. All three runtimes give every flagged zone the key DBM[empty] and call two empty zones equal, so two different empty matrices share a key (VER_011_empty_one_key on the reference); the line therefore speaks of zones that hold firing times, which are the only zones the state class graph keys (it drops an empty successor before keying, state_class_graph.rs). The key is a relation sameKey, not a string: the rendering (clock names joined by commas, entries row-major joined by bars) is kind N, and the clock names belong to VER-010's class key. The runtimes render each bound at three decimals of a second (format_bound), so the key is exact only on whole-millisecond bounds, which is ruling D58: always in Rust and Python, after truncation in Java's graph, and not for a fractional TypeScript bound, where VER_011_key_submillisecond shows two zones that differ by a tenth of a millisecond with one key. A key over the projections alone merges zones that differ in a difference bound and is killed (VER_011_forbids_projectionKey). That the matrices are canonical and in the canonical order is VER-010's (AC1), which applies canon and perm before it keys.
- let_time_pass (zeroing the lower bounds after the successor) is part of VER-010's successor step and is not listed in VER-011's criteria; TimedScg.sat_ltpPre and sat_ltpPre_shift cover it. The test derivation (three timed clocks, fire one, check the successor's constraints) is line 6 on a concrete zone, VER_011_nonvacuous.

## VER-012: Name-Aware State Class Graph: the graph step

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_012` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers the Route B name-partition graph (MAY); one step of the graph, the untimed base · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ad6f8d75323aaa06 ai** · Statement hash `ad6f8d75323aaa06`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the Route B graph fires a ν-join on a name-symbol, every correlated input *shall* hold at least the required count of that symbol, and the firing *shall* remove the required count of that symbol from each correlated input and add one token of it to each relay target of the fired branch ([NU-054]).<br><br>*If* every correlated input of a ν-join holds at least the required count of a name-symbol, *then* the name successors of a firing of that join *shall* include one with the canonical key of the join fired on that symbol.<br><br>*When* the Route B graph fires a coloured consumer ([NU-051]), it *shall* fire it on a name-symbol its coloured input holds, removing one token of that symbol from the input and adding one token of it to each coloured output of the fired branch.<br><br>*If* the coloured input of a coloured consumer holds a name-symbol, *then* the name successors of a firing of that consumer *shall* include one with the canonical key of the consumer fired on that symbol.<br><br>*When* the Route B graph fires a minting transition, its one name successor *shall* add one token of a name-symbol that no coloured place of the class holds to each coloured output of the fired branch.<br><br>*When* the Route B graph fires a transition that neither mints, joins nor consumes a name-symbol, its one name successor *shall* be the name layer of the class unchanged.<br><br>Two name layers *shall* have the same canonical key exactly when one is the other with its name-symbols renamed by a permutation.<br><br>The Route B graph *shall* identify two classes exactly when they have the same base class and their name layers have the same canonical key.<br><br>*When* the Route B graph fires a transition, the successor *shall* hold on each place the transition does not reset the tokens the place held, less the tokens the transition's input on that place consumes by [IO-007] (all of them for an `All` or `AtLeast` input), plus the tokens the fired branch deposits there. | 1. Let G be the graph step: succs (the name successors of one firing), key (the canonical key of a name layer), ckey (the key of a class) and fire (the base step on the count marking).<br>2. For every coloured set co, correlated inputs cin with their required counts, relay targets rel, name layer M, branch places d, support bound B and mint counter c: every name successor of a join (role join cin rel) is joinStep on some symbol s that joinEnab accepts (a token of s in the first correlated input and the required count of s in every one): the required count of s removed from each correlated input, one token of s added to each relay target of the branch (relOut d rel).<br>3. For the same data, with M supported below B: for every symbol s that joinEnab accepts, some name successor of the join has the key of joinStep on s.<br>4. For every coloured set co, consumed input inp, name layer M, branch places d, bound B and counter c: every name successor of a coloured consumer (role consume inp) is consumeStep on some symbol s resident in inp (a token of s in inp): one token of s removed from inp, one token of s added to each coloured output of the branch (colOut d).<br>5. For the same data, with M supported below B: for every symbol s resident in inp, some name successor of the consumer has the key of consumeStep on s.<br>6. For every coloured set co, name layer M supported below B, branch places d and mint counter c at or above B: the name successors of a mint (role mint) are the one layer mintStep on some symbol s of which no coloured place holds a token in M: one token of s added to each coloured output of the branch.<br>7. For every coloured set co, name layer M, branch places d, bound B and counter c: the name successors of an ordinary transition (role ordinary) are the one layer M.<br>8. For every base type β, coloured set co and two classes S and S': ckey S = ckey S' exactly when S.b = S'.b and key S.m = key S'.m.<br>10. For every count marking a, transition t, branch outcome r and place p that t does not reset: if fire a t r = some a', then a' p = a p - consumedA a t p + the number of tokens the branch, its drained forwards resolved at a, deposits on p; consumedA a t p is what t's input on p takes: a p for an All or AtLeast input, the required count for a One or Exactly input, 0 when t has no input on p. | **Assumptions**

- The model is the graph step NameGraph. succs is name_successors (name_state_class_graph.rs; Novel.RouteB.nameSuccs), key is NameMarking::canonical_key (Novel.CanonicalKey.canonicalKey), ckey is the pair of intern ids the graph dedups by (Novel.RouteB.keyOf), fire is the base successor of the untimed base layer (Novel.RouteB.untimedBase, fireAD over the branch outcome with each drained forward resolved at the marking fired in). The witness refNameGraph is the explorer's own step: the Route B explorer Novel.RouteB.routeB keys its classes with refNameGraph.ckey and fires the untimed base with refNameGraph.fire (ver012_routeB_key, ver012_untimedBase_fire). The build loop and the verdict are VER_012_build's and NU-050's (NU_050_prefix).
- Which role a transition gets (join for a matched transition, consume, mint, ordinary) is an input of succs, as it is of name_successors. It is the fragment classifier's (Novel.RouteB.classifyT and classifyS, name_fragment.rs classify): a matched transition gets only the join role, with its counted keys and relay targets, by NU_054_verifier; the coloured-consumer role is NU_051's; the mint role, given only to a declared mint, is NU-010's (Novel.RouteB.classifyS_mint); a transition the classifier gives no role makes the net fall back to the sound over-approximation (NU-050). The classifier refuses an `All` or `AtLeast` match key (keyCount) and gives the consumer role only at count one (NU_051 line 2), so no coloured place is drained by a batch and line 9 needs no name-layer counterpart.
- AC1 (a ν-join fires only on a name shared by all correlated inputs; a marking reachable only by equating two distinct names is not reachable, with no budget place required) is lines 1 and 2. joinEnab is the shipped enabling_symbols: a token in the first correlated input and the required count in every one. Every correlated input takes at least one token (TransitionBuilder::build rejects a zero count, Classify.builderOK_posKeys), so on a built net joinEnab is the quoted sentences' 'every correlated input holds at least the required count'; a net with a zero-count key cannot be built and is out of scope (Classify.zeroKey_refused). 'With no budget place required' is that lines 1 and 2 have no premise on the base marking: the join's name test reads the name layer alone. VER_012_nonvacuous shows a crossed layer (name 0 in one input, name 1 in the other) with no join successor; VER_012_forbids_firstInput kills a join that reads a name in its first input only. NU-050 AC1 (a counterexample that equates two names is not reported) is the same fact read at the verdict, NU-050's block.
- Lines 2 and 4 are the free-choice half of ruling D59 (a) and VD-1 (a) (clashes ver-d#1, nu-b#3): the graph fires a join on every name that enables it, and a coloured consumer on every name its input holds, up to renaming, where the executor picks one by the NU-020 rule (the oldest token, EXEC-010). The informative sentence of the body ('the graph fires it on each of them, up to renaming, and a coloured consumer on each resident name') is lines 2 and 4. That is why a closed graph is complete for the graph's own semantics and not for the executor. VER_012_forbids_leastName and VER_012_forbids_consumeLeast kill a graph that fires a join, or a consumer, on one name only (the least one, standing for the executor's choice). Lines 3 and 4 constrain only which names the consumer step is applied to; the step's count update on one name is also NU_051_relay's line. The orbit dedup (one successor per distinct signature, the implementation note) is lines 2 and 4's 'up to renaming': Novel.RouteB.dedup_perm shows it keeps the keyed successors of every signature. VER_012_forbids_anySymbol kills a consumer fired on a name its input does not hold, which creates a token from nothing.
- Line 5 is the body's 'a minting fork introduces a globally-fresh symbol': the minted symbol is fresh for the class (no coloured place holds it). The Rust mints next_sym, next_sym + 1, ... across one expansion, the model the counter c; the line allows any fresh symbol, and the key does not depend on which (Novel.RouteB.mint_key). That the symbol is also fresh across the whole run, and differs from every name the executor minted earlier, is NU-010's executor line; on the graph a symbol no place holds is interchangeable with every other such symbol, so freshness for the class is all the quotient can see. VER_012_forbids_mintZero kills a mint that reuses symbol 0, which merges a fresh name with a live one. Line 6 is the ordinary role: a transition that touches no coloured place leaves the name layer as it was; VER_012_forbids_ordinaryDrop kills a step that empties it.
- AC2 (two markings differing only by a permutation of name-symbols are the same state class) is lines 7 and 8: the name key is renaming-invariant and separates layers that are no renaming of each other (Novel.CanonicalKey.canonicalKey_eq_iff_exists_perm). Its parenthesis ('the quotient is finite when the live-name pool is structurally bounded') is not stated: it is the reason the graph can close, and a graph that does not close is truncated (VER_012_build, NU_050_prefix). Open item: a finiteness theorem for a structurally bounded live-name pool. VER_012_forbids_identityKey kills a key that reads a symbol's identity; VER_012_forbids_nameBlind kills a key that forgets the name layer, which merges the aligned and the crossed layer and is the value-blind count abstraction.
- Line 8 says the class key keeps the whole base class. The model's base type is abstract (BaseLayer β), and the only concrete instance is the untimed base (AMarking), which has no zone and no earliest-ready times. So the memory note's two MUST sentences (the base intern key includes the class-relative earliest-ready times alongside marking and zone; two arrivals that disagree on the earliest-ready times stay two classes) and the body's 'for a timed net its marking, zone and earliest-ready times' have no Lean content beyond 'the key keeps the whole base': the timed base class is gap R6 (open item: give the timed base layer its zone and readyEarliest components and state that the key keeps them). VER_012_forbids_baseBlind kills a class key that hides the base. The runtime base intern keys keep the whole base marking: Rust's intern_base keys by the escaped canonical_key (name_state_class_graph.rs:327, marking_state.rs push_key_name), TypeScript's internBase by baseKeyOf over MarkingState.key(), the JSON of the sorted [name, count] entries, and Java by the structured BaseKey. A base intern key that renders the base marking as a string that does not escape place names, the behaviour RD-40 recorded, gives two base classes with different markings and no clocks one intern id, so line 8 fails there: the graph keeps the first arrival's base and loses the other marking, and AC3's completeness of a closed graph fails on such a net. Why the key must keep everything the step reads is Libpetri.equivariance_is_necessary (Interning.lean): a step that reads a datum the key hides loses a reachable class under interning; for the shipped step Novel.RouteB.routeB_equivariant discharges it, and Novel.RouteB.routeB_interned_keys_eq shows the hash-consed graph is the plain quotient graph (interning is semantics-free). That class indices and the reported trace may differ from a build without interning is report shape (kind Q).
- AC4 (All and AtLeast inputs drain their place in the graph as at run time; an inhibitor arc on that place is then satisfied in the successor) and the exactness precondition's first MUST sentence (the successor step derives each input's count from consumptionCount of IO-007, so All and AtLeast consume every available token) are line 9, for every input: All and AtLeast take every token of the place, One and Exactly(n) their required count (consumedA, the IO-007 contract on counts). VER_012_forbids_requiredCount kills a base step that takes requiredCount from an All input: it leaves a phantom residue, which keeps an inhibitor arc on the place unsatisfied; VER_012_forbids_noConsume kills one that takes nothing from a One input. The inhibitor consequence follows from line 9 and the enabling test (enabledA). A place the transition resets is not an input count: its successor count is the base graph's (VER-010), not this line's. The precondition's last MUST sentence ('delegate to the same cardinality contract the executor uses rather than restating it') is a rule on code structure (kind N): the line states the counts, not how the code obtains them.
- AC3 is split under ruling D59 (a) and VD-1 (a). Its closed-graph sentence, reworded to 'sound for every executor run and complete for the free-choice name semantics the graph explores', is: soundness, NU_050_soundB (cited as ver012_sound_executor; a Route B Proven holds of every marking the untimed reference ν executor reaches, under the contracts of NU-010 and NU-051); completeness, VER_012_build lines 2 and 3 with lines 2 and 4 here (ver012_build_complete_violated for reachability-safety, ver012_build_complete_quiescence for quiescence). Line 3 of VER_012_build needs a key-equivariant successor step; ver012_succs_keys shows that the name successors of every graph meeting this block have keys that depend only on the key of the layer fired from, and for the shipped step the whole premise is Novel.RouteB.routeB_equivariant. Its truncation sentences (a stored violating class gives Violated with the shortest witness, a truncated graph never Proven, Unknown otherwise) are NU_050_prefix and VER-017's rule; the shortest witness is Verifier.Graph.trace (trace_spec: a shortest path of the built graph). The sentence on a graph that keeps a latest bound (an on-time executor whose actions take no time, the report says so) and the PNID Fig. 11(b) fixture are the timed graph and a report line: not modelled (gap R6, kind Q).
- AC5 (early stop) is VER_012_build lines 4 and 5. The report note text, 'the parent ... does not count as expanded' and the PNID fixture are report shape and timing (kind Q); the model's build does not count the parent as expanded (Decide.loop). That quiescence properties do not stop early is the decider's choice: the reference Route B decider builds with the early stop for a safety property only (refRouteB, NU-050).
- The body sentence on the timed firing domain is reworded under VD-5 (item 3, ruling D20): the domain of VER-011 is carried beside the name partition, a matched join's clock gated by name-enablement (NU-050) and, unless assumeNoReaping is set, without latest bounds (TIME-013). None of the timed layer is modelled here: the base layer of Novel.RouteB.Graph is abstract and the end-to-end theorems are for the untimed instance. Novel.RouteB.nameEnabled_comp shows the clock gate is renaming-invariant, so the timed step stays key-equivariant; the timed base step itself is not stated. Open items under gap R6: the timed graph (name-gated clocks, dropped latest bounds, the timed base class of line 8), and AC3's soundness for a timed net, since NU_050_soundB is against the untimed reference ν executor only.
- The exactness precondition's phrase 'in the [EXEC-010] FIFO order' is deleted under VD-1 (a): a name layer counts tokens per symbol and holds no queue order, and the graph takes any resident name where the executor takes the oldest. What the graph keeps of the executor is the count per place (line 9) and, for a join or a consumer, the name fired on (lines 1 to 4).
- The implementation notes (the three runtimes and Python, the shared key format, interning as an option, the orbit dedup's measurements, the counterexample path read from per-class labelled successor lists, solver-free, Route A preferred for budget-declared untimed reachability-safety) are configuration and report shape (kinds N and Q), except the memory note's MUST sentences (line 8, open item above) and the orbit dedup's claim that the class set and the (label, key) successor pairs are unchanged (Novel.RouteB.dedup_perm, lines 2 and 4).

## VER-012: Name-Aware State Class Graph: the build

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_012_build` · Kind **F** · Scope every verifier that offers the Route B name-partition graph (MAY); the build loop of the graph · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 550823c0327b11ab ai** · Statement hash `550823c0327b11ab`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|

**Assumptions**

- The model is the build loop RBBuild: from an explorer (Interning.lean's Explorer: the key, the support bound, the successor list under a mint counter), the class bound, the total budget or cancellation as an oracle cut, the early-stop predicate and switch, the Lean fuel and the initial class, the built graph (Decide.Out: the stored classes in discovery order, the number expanded, closed, stopped, stopped early). The witness refRBBuild is Decide.build (name_state_class_graph.rs build_until). The verdict read off a build is NU_050_prefix's (Decide.verdict, the shared predicate of VER-017); line 4 reads it as vocabulary.
- Line 1 is 'every explored class is reachable' of AC5's note and of the implementation note on the early stop (Lean build_reach), for every build. A Violated therefore names a class the graph reaches (Decide.prefix_safety_sound, Decide.prefix_quiescence_sound). VER_012_build_forbids_staleCounter kills a build that mints with a counter that is not fresh: it stores a class the graph does not reach.
- Lines 2 and 3 are AC3's completeness, reworded under ruling D59 (a) and VD-1 (a) to 'complete for the free-choice name semantics the graph explores': on a closed graph every stored class was expanded and every class the graph reaches has a stored twin, so a reachable class that violates a reachability-safety property gives Violated (ver012_build_complete_violated), and so does a reachable class that rests in the graph and violates a quiescence property (ver012_build_complete_quiescence). The free choice is VER_012 lines 2 and 4: the graph fires a join on every enabling name and a consumer on every resident name, up to renaming. Line 3's premise, the key-equivariance of the successor step, is in the quoted sentence: the build alone cannot give it. Route B's explorer Novel.RouteB.routeB is key-equivariant (Novel.RouteB.routeB_equivariant), and for every graph step meeting VER_012 the name successors' keys depend only on the key fired from (ver012_succs_keys); the base step and the NU-052 prune read only what the class key keeps. Soundness against the executor is NU_050_soundB (ver012_sound_executor). VER_012_build_forbids_truncAsClosed kills a build that reports a truncated graph as closed; VER_012_build_forbids_forgetClosed kills a closed build that loses a reachable class.
- Line 4 is AC5: verdict and route identical to a build without the early stop, the witness ending at the same class. The verdict includes the violating class (Violated i), the class the witness ends at; the route is Route B either way. AC5 is reworded so that which of several equally short paths to that class the witness takes may differ: with the early stop the parent of the violating class is opened (Verifier.Graph.opened) and its edge list may break a tie between equal-length paths differently (W10-graph note 1). The test derivation's 'the early-stop witness ends at the class the witness from a build without it ends at' is line 4. 'Unless that build is stopped': a total budget or a cancellation that would cut the full build after the early stop found its class leaves the full build Unknown (NU_050_prefix line 1) while the early stop answers Violated; the line excludes that case. The early-stopped build is not stopped (ver012_build_cmp). BFS order (the lowest-index violating class, the shortest path) is Decide.build's FIFO queue; VER_012_build_forbids_dropBad kills an early stop that ends without storing the violating class. 'When the bound is hit first, criterion 3 applies unchanged' is the case where the two builds are equal (ver012_build_cmp, left disjunct).
- Line 5 is AC5's 'An early-stopped graph is not complete and MUST NOT be treated as closed', as the build's own flag: the state-space cache of VER-017 stores only a closed graph (Verifier.Graph.store), so an early-stopped graph never serves another property. VER_012_build_forbids_earlyClosed kills a build that flags it closed.
- AC5's list of safety properties, its report note, 'the parent ... does not count as expanded', 'Quiescence properties do not stop early' and the PNID fixture are the decider's and the report's: the reference Route B decider builds with the early stop for a safety property and without it for a quiescence property (refRouteB, NU-050); the note text (its 'a shortest one to any violation' included) and the timing are report shape (kind Q). That the early stop is Route B only (the enumeration route of VER-017 and the timed check of VER-023 build in full) is VER-017's and VER-023's. AC1, AC2 and AC4 are VER_012's; AC3's truncation and timed sentences are NU_050_prefix's and VER_012's assumes.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_013_args"></a>
## VER-013: Solver Transport: timeouts of one process

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args` · Kind **F** · Scope every z3 process the verifier starts, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 8c4c5184fbd153a4 ai** · Statement hash `8c4c5184fbd153a4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the verifier starts a `z3` process with a timeout of `t` milliseconds, `t` at least 1, it *shall* pass `-t:t` and, as `-T`, the smallest whole number of seconds that is at least `(t + 1000) / 1000`, and *shall* kill the process at `t + 2000` milliseconds if it has not exited.<br><br>*While* a total budget is set, the verifier *shall* give each `z3` process the smaller of its normal timeout and the whole milliseconds that remain, and *shall* start no process when none remain. | 1. For every timeout formula B and clamp Cl, and every budget t of at least 1 millisecond: the -t value of B t is t;<br>2. the -T value of B t is the smallest number of seconds whose milliseconds reach t + 1000;<br>3. the watchdog of B t is t + 2000;<br>4. and for every normal budget n: without a total budget, Cl gives n;<br>5. with r milliseconds remaining and r at least 1, Cl gives the smaller of n and r;<br>6. with no millisecond remaining, Cl starts no process. | <pre>fun B Cl ↦<br>  (∀ (t : ℕ),<br>      1 ≤ t →<br>        (B t).1 = t ∧<br>          ((B t).2.1 * 1000 ≥ t + 1000 ∧ (B t).2.1 * 1000 &lt; t + 2000) ∧<br>            (B t).2.2 = t + 2000) ∧<br>    (∀ (n : ℕ), Cl n none = some n) ∧<br>      (∀ (n r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → Cl n (some r) = some (min n r)) ∧<br>        ∀ (n : ℕ), Cl n (some 0) = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D90 (a): the formula is stated for a budget of at least 1 ms. At 0 the runtimes differ (Java and TypeScript raise the budget to 1 ms, Z3Solver.java timeoutMs and z3-process.ts timeoutBudget, so that -t:0, no limit to z3, never reaches the solver; Rust passes -t:0, z3_process.rs args_for), and the markdown says so. The -T value is z3_process.rs hard_timeout_secs ((t + 1000) rounded up to seconds, at least 1, which at t >= 1 is never the floor), and the watchdog watchdog_ms; Java and TypeScript have the same functions. Killed: a -t passed in seconds (VER_013_args_forbids_seconds), a -T rounded down (VER_013_args_forbids_floor: at 1 ms it would give -T:1) and a watchdog at one second of grace instead of two (VER_013_args_forbids_oneGrace).
- The clamp is total_budget.rs clamp: the remaining time is whole milliseconds rounded down, and a remainder of 0 (or a cancellation, which the model reads as nothing remaining) starts no process; the stop it records is VER_013_stop's. Every process passes one choke point per implementation (Java Z3Solver.run, TypeScript runZ3Text, Rust Z3Solver::run), which clamps first and then derives -t, -T and the watchdog from the clamped value (Rust: clamp, then args_for and watchdog_ms of its result). Rust, TypeScript and Java start no process when no whole millisecond remains (Java's Z3Solver.run reads remainingMs() once and refuses at 0, and its polls read the same whole-millisecond clock). A clamp that raises the whole milliseconds left to at least 1, which starts a process at -t:1 with less than 1 ms left (the Java behaviour RD-42 recorded), gives min n (max 1 r) and is killed by line 6 (VER_013_args_forbids_javaSubMs). That the clamped value, not the normal one, is what lines 1 to 3 are applied to is kind Q, since B and Cl are separate functions here: the runtimes' AC9 stub tests (Rust stub_z3, a wedged solver under a per-call timeout of a minute and a total budget of 1.5 s, must return within 1.5 s plus the 2 s slack plus 1.5 s) fail when the watchdog keeps the unclamped budget. A clamp that ignores the remaining time, one that starts a process with nothing left, at a budget of 0 or of 1 ms, and one that gives a budget without a total budget set are killed (VER_013_args_forbids_noClamp, VER_013_args_forbids_startAtZero, VER_013_args_forbids_javaSubMs, VER_013_args_forbids_clampUnset). The HORN query, the certificate script and its detail re-run each get the full per-call budget without a total budget: that is the normal budget n, set by the caller (kind N).
- The argument list (-smt2 -in, fp.engine=spacer for the HORN query), the single write of the script on stdin followed by end-of-file, the concurrent draining of both streams, the kill and reap on every exit path, the executable on PATH or LIBPETRI_Z3, the probe of --version against 4.8.0, and the LIBPETRI_SMT_DUMP file names are process handling, kind Q and N, as is AC6 (the report carries '  Solver: z3 <version>' in its solver phase, or '  Solver: z3 unavailable (<reason>)' followed by the UNKNOWN result line naming the same reason), which is report text; the runtimes' stub-solver tests (the stub_z3 tests of libpetri-verification) check them. AC9 (with a total budget of N ms, verify() returns within N ms plus one watchdog slack and one polling interval) is wall-clock time, kind Q; its reason text and 'no z3 process starts once the budget is spent' are VER_013_stop's lines 5 and 3 with line 6 here.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✓ **The reference timeouts.** Example: a budget of 30 000 ms gives `-t:30000`, `-T:31` and a watchdog at 32 000 ms; with a total budget and 200 ms left, a process whose normal budget is 30 000 ms gets 200 ms; with nothing left none starts.
  <pre>VER_013_args Ver013.refBudgets Ver013.refClamp</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_clampUnset` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **Without a total budget, the normal budget.** Example: with no total budget set, a clamp that starts no process would make every verification `Unknown`, against AC8.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args Ver013.refBudgets clampUnset</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_floor` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **`-T` rounds up.** Example: at a budget of 1 ms, rounding `1001 ms` down gives `-T:1`, a backstop that can fire before the soft timeout's second of grace has passed.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args Ver013.floorBudgets Ver013.refClamp</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_javaSubMs` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **No whole millisecond left, no process, not even at 1 ms** (line 6; the behaviour RD-42 recorded). Example: with 0.4 ms of the total budget left, the whole milliseconds remaining are 0; a clamp that raises them to 1 starts `z3` with `-t:1`, `-T:2` and a 2001 ms watchdog, past the spent budget.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args Ver013.refBudgets javaSubMs</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_noClamp` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **A total budget clamps the process.** Example: with 200 ms left, a process that still gets its normal 30 000 ms can run far past the total budget.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args Ver013.refBudgets noClamp</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_oneGrace` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **The watchdog waits two seconds past the budget.** Example: at 30 000 ms the `-T:31` backstop fires at 31 000 ms at the earliest; a watchdog at 31 000 ms kills a solver that is about to print `timeout`, which turns the hard timeout into a kill.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args oneGraceBudgets Ver013.refClamp</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_seconds` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **`-t` is in milliseconds.** Example: a budget of 30 000 ms passed as `-t:30` gives `z3` 30 ms, a thousandth of its budget.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args secondsBudgets Ver013.refClamp</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_forbids_startAtZero` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✗ **Nothing left, no process.** Example: with 0 ms left, a process at budget 0 would be passed `-t:0`, which `z3` reads as no limit.
  <pre>¬VER_013_args Ver013.refBudgets startAtZero</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_args_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_013): ✓ **The worked numbers.** Example: 30 000 ms gives `(30000, 31, 32000)`; 1 ms gives `-T:2`, since 1001 ms round up to 2 s; 200 ms left clamp a normal 30 000 ms to 200 ms.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_013_classify"></a>
## VER-013: Solver Transport: reply classification

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_013_classify` · Kind **F** · Scope every z3 reply the verifier reads, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 f0d294ca752190df ai** · Statement hash `f0d294ca752190df`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The verifier *shall* read the verdict of a reply off the first stdout line that, trimmed, equals `sat`, `unsat` or `unknown`, wherever that line appears.<br><br>*If* no stdout line of a reply is a verdict line, *then* the verifier *shall* give as the reason of the failure the first of these that applies: a `timeout` line on stdout, the watchdog kill, the first `(error …)` line on stdout and then on stderr, any other stderr text, the stdout itself.<br><br>A verdict line decides whatever else the reply carries, an `(error …)` line or a non-zero exit included. | 1. For every classifier C and raw reply r (trimmed stdout lines, trimmed stderr lines, whether the watchdog killed the process, the exit status): if the first verdict line of r's stdout spells a, C r is the answer a, whatever the stderr lines, the kill flag and the exit status;<br>2. otherwise, if some stdout line is timeout, C r is a timeout-line failure;<br>3. otherwise, if the watchdog killed the process, C r is a kill failure;<br>4. otherwise, if some line of stdout and then stderr is an (error …) line, C r is an error-line failure whose reason is the first such line;<br>5. otherwise, if some stderr line has text, C r is a stderr failure whose reason is the stderr text (its trimmed lines joined by line breaks);<br>6. otherwise C r is an unexpected-output failure whose reason is the stdout itself (its trimmed lines joined by line breaks). | <pre>fun C ↦<br>  ∀ (r : Ver013.RawReply),<br>    (∀ (a : Verifier.SolverAnswer),<br>        Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = some a → C r = Verifier.SolverReply.answer a) ∧<br>      (Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = none →<br>          "timeout" ∈ r.out →<br>            ∃ why,<br>              C r = Verifier.SolverReply.failure Verifier.SolverFailure.timeoutLine why) ∧<br>        (Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = none →<br>            "timeout" ∉ r.out →<br>              r.killed = true →<br>                ∃ why,<br>                  C r = Verifier.SolverReply.failure Verifier.SolverFailure.killed why) ∧<br>          (Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = none →<br>              "timeout" ∉ r.out →<br>                r.killed = false →<br>                  ∀ (e : String),<br>                    Ver013.firstError (r.out ++ r.err) = some e →<br>                      C r =<br>                        Verifier.SolverReply.failure Verifier.SolverFailure.errorLine e) ∧<br>            (Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = none →<br>                "timeout" ∉ r.out →<br>                  r.killed = false →<br>                    Ver013.firstError (r.out ++ r.err) = none →<br>                      Ver013.hasText r.err = true →<br>                        C r =<br>                          Verifier.SolverReply.failure Verifier.SolverFailure.stderrText<br>                            ("\n".intercalate r.err)) ∧<br>              (Ver013.firstAnswer r.out = none →<br>                "timeout" ∉ r.out →<br>
