<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_016"></a>
## VER-016: State-Equation Strengthening with Firing Counters

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_016` · Kind **B** · Scope the flat CHC encoding of every implementation, with the state-equation option enabled · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 103d3b889b9f137a ai** · Statement hash `103d3b889b9f137a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the state-equation option is enabled, the initial fact of the flat CHC encoding *shall* set every firing counter to 0.<br><br>*While* the option is enabled, the rule of each transition *shall* fire that transition only where it is enabled, with the effect it has in the untimed abstraction of [VER-004], add one to its firing counter and copy every other counter, each environment-injection rule *shall* add one token to its place and copy every counter, and no rule but these and the initial fact *shall* derive a `Reachable` fact.<br><br>*While* the option is enabled, each transition rule *shall* require of its successor `(M', n')`, for every place that is not injected, the equality `m'_p = M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` where no consume-all or reset arc clears the place, and the upper bound `m'_p ≤ M0_p + Σ_t C[p][t]·n'_t` where one does.<br><br>*While* the option is enabled, apart from the P-invariant conjuncts of [VER-005] and [VER-007] and the environment bounds of [VER-006], the rule of each transition *shall* accept its firing from every state `(M, n)` in which the transition is enabled and whose successor meets the rows above, and each environment-injection rule *shall* accept its injection from every state, so the rows remove no reachable state. | 1. For every initial fact I and rule relation R:<br>2. the initial fact for a0 is (a0, n) with every counter of n equal to 0;<br>3. every rule step is a raw counter step (CntStep): the firing of an enabled row k with its deposit (fireAD: count tokens land in each place) that bumps counter k and copies the rest, or an injection of one token into an injected place that copies every counter;<br>4. whenever a rule takes any augmented state s by the firing of row k to its successor, every place below the place count w that is not injected satisfies its row there (CntRow, over the columns deposit count minus pre: the upper bound where some row clears the place with a reset or consume-all arc, the equality elsewhere);<br>5. from any augmented state s, reachable or not, the firing of an enabled row k whose successor satisfies the row of every place below w that is not injected is a rule step;<br>6. from any augmented state s, the injection of one token into an injected place, with every counter copied, is a rule step. | <pre>fun I R ↦<br>  (∀ (a0 : AMarking), I a0 = (a0, fun x ↦ 0)) ∧<br>    (∀ (rows : CntRows) (envs : List PlaceId) (w : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking)<br>        (s s' : AMarking × Counters), R rows envs w a0 s s' → CntStep rows envs s s') ∧<br>      (∀ (rows : CntRows) (envs : List PlaceId) (w : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking)<br>          (s : AMarking × Counters) (k : ℕ)<br>          (tr : Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit),<br>          rows[k]? = some tr →<br>            enabledA s.1 tr.1 = true →<br>              R rows envs w a0 s (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD s.1 tr.1 tr.2, bump s.2 k) →<br>                ∀ p &lt; w,<br>                  p ∉ envs →<br>                    CntRow rows a0 (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD s.1 tr.1 tr.2)<br>                      (bump s.2 k) p) ∧<br>        (∀ (rows : CntRows) (envs : List PlaceId) (w : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking)<br>            (s : AMarking × Counters) (k : ℕ)<br>            (tr : Transition × Novel.ForwardDeposit.Deposit),<br>            rows[k]? = some tr →<br>              enabledA s.1 tr.1 = true →<br>                (∀ p &lt; w,<br>                    p ∉ envs →<br>                      CntRow rows a0 (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD s.1 tr.1 tr.2)<br>                        (bump s.2 k) p) →<br>                  R rows envs w a0 s<br>                    (Novel.ForwardDeposit.fireAD s.1 tr.1 tr.2, bump s.2 k)) ∧<br>          ∀ (rows : CntRows) (envs : List PlaceId) (w : ℕ) (a0 : AMarking)<br>            (s : AMarking × Counters),<br>            ∀ p ∈ envs,<br>              R rows envs w a0 s<br>                (fun q ↦ if (q == p) = true then s.1 q + 1 else s.1 q, s.2)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (I, R) of CntInit and CntRuleRel over the untimed abstraction of VER-004 with injection: the flat rows (CntRows: one row per way a firing can end, a transition with its deposit, d.count p tokens landing in p; the abstract semantics enabledA and fireAD), the injected places envs, the place count w and the initial marking a0. The column of row k is C[p][k] = d.count p - pre p (cntCol), as flatten writes it (post[p] += n: Rust net_flattener.rs, Java NetFlattener.java, TypeScript net-flattener.ts) and state_equation_conditions reads it (ft.post[p] - ft.pre[p], smt_encoder.rs). So a row that deposits k > 1 tokens in one place, the timeout forward of an exactly(k) input (IO-014, Novel/ForwardDeposit.lean), is covered with its k in both the effect and the column (VER_016_forbids_unitRules, VER_016_forbids_unitColumn). On rows whose deposits list each place at most once (every action branch, IO-011) refRules is StepCntStrRel of StateEquation.lean with no law, which reads a deposit as a set (VER_016_unit_rows). A forward of an all or atLeast input deposits the drained batch, which no row expresses (drained_forward_has_no_row); the verifier refuses such a net before any flat route reads it (branch_outcomes::drained_forward), so that net is outside this block. Augmented states pair a count marking with Counters (Nat-valued, so the conjoined n' >= 0 holds by construction). The witness pair is refCntInit and refRules.
- w stands for the place count P of the flat net, so every place an arc of the net touches lies below it; places at or beyond w are outside the encoding. The statement quantifies over every w, and refRules carries the rows of exactly the places below w.
- R models the counter and row part of the rules. The P-invariant laws the rules also conjoin are VER-005 and VER-007's, and conjoining gate-validated laws together with the rows removes no reachable state (state_equation_reach_eq, on rows that list each place at most once). The environment mode is AlwaysAvailable: the Bounded(k) cap on the injection rule and the environment bounds on the successor of a transition rule are VER-006's, only remove steps, and are not modelled (the capped rules reach a subset, so the rows still hold on them). These are the conjuncts the fourth quoted sentence sets apart.
- Line 2 is the second quoted sentence: the marking half (enabledness, fireAD, one token per injection, no rule but these and the initial fact) is the untimed abstraction of VER-004 over deposit rows with the injection of VER-006, and the counter half is the bump and the copy. Line 3 is the third quoted sentence, stated for every augmented state: the rule carries the row, not only that reachable states satisfy it. Lines 4 and 5 are the fourth quoted sentence: the rule requires of the source nothing beyond enabling and the successor rows, so a guard on the source rows (VER_016_forbids_srcRow), a guard on reachability (VER_016_forbids_reachOnly) or a guarded injection (VER_016_forbids_injEmpty) is ruled out, and the rows remove no reachable state (VER_016_reach_iff).
- Lines 2 to 5 determine R up to logical equivalence: on every pair satisfying VER-016, R is refRules (VER_016_unique). So a row on an injected place and the equality row on a cleared place are ruled out wherever they would refuse a step (VER_016_forbids_injRow, VER_016_forbids_eqRow), as are rows over the source or over the old counters (VER_016_forbids_oldCnt), the upper bound on an exact place (VER_016_forbids_leAll), and the unit column on a row that deposits two tokens in one place (VER_016_forbids_unitColumn). A conjunct that refuses no step is invisible at the level of the relation; that the script emits no such text is script text (AC2, the parity goldens of VER-013).
- The body's description of the rules ('the initial fact has n = 0', the counter update, the injection rule, 'in the same position', 'in transition order') is lines 1 to 5; the position and order of the conjuncts in the script are text and are not modelled. The inductiveness argument ('a clearing step's guard needs m_p >= pre_p') is ver016_row_fire, behind VER_016_reach_iff. 'The error rule quantifies the counters and constrains the marking only' is the violation of VER_016_certificate, which reads the marking only. 'The counterexample decoder reads a fact's marking from its leading P arguments' is the decoder's text and is not modelled.
- The second paragraph (every linear consequence of the marking equation is a fact in every rule body; the 50-place agent-dispatch figures) is a motivation and a performance figure (kind Q); it states no line. The soundness sentence ('the counters are exact bookkeeping, so every row holds on every reachable augmented state and conjoining them removes none') is VER_016_rows_hold and VER_016_reach_iff; the StateEquation.lean lemmas the sentence names (rows_hold, state_equation_reach_eq) are their case on rows that list each place at most once (VER_016_unit_rows). VER_016_markings says the option neither adds nor loses a marking of the deposit-row abstraction with injection (ReachADInj).
- 'The option is off by default' and 'about 1.5x slower' are configuration (kind N) and a performance figure (kind Q). With the option off the encoding is VER-001's and this block says nothing.
- The sentence on the certificate check is VER_016_certificate: a candidate over (M, n) that passes the three verification conditions against the raw counter step relation CntStep from (a0, 0), with a violation that reads the marking only, proves the property for every marking of ReachADInj (by Novel.Certificate.vc_sound_rel; Novel.Certificate.vc_sound_state_equation is the same result with deposits read as sets). The composition of the candidate (the P-invariants, n >= 0 and the marking equation) is not modelled: VER_016_certificate covers any candidate over (M, n), not that the shipped one contains the marking equation; no block states that: the pipeline model names the certificate check (rtStepNames in Verifier/Pipeline.lean) and does not enter it. That the check is on by default and that a caller may disable it, in which case a Proven rests on the solver's answer alone and the report says 'not applicable (disabled)', is configuration and report text (kind N and Q, ruling D52 (a)).
- 'The option does not apply to the name-coloured encoding or to Route B' is the scope of this block (the flat encoding). The report line for the name-coloured path is AC4 below.
- AC1 (byte identity with the option disabled) and AC5 (byte identity of the HORN and certificate scripts across the four implementations) are about the SMT-LIB text, which is not modelled; they are checked by the golden-script parity tests of VER-013 (kind Q).
- AC2 (arity P + T, the initial fact ends in T zeros, the counter equalities of rule t, the marking equation of every exact place over the primed variables, the upper bound on a consume-all or reset place, none on an injected place) is lines 1 to 5 at the constraint level, with VER_016_unique for 'instead' and 'none' as above; the arity and the SMT-LIB spelling are text (kind Q, the parity goldens of VER-013). It is checked on the reference by VER_016_nonvacuous: on a net whose only transition drains place 0 with a consume-all arc, the firing rule exists from the initial fact and its successor meets the upper bound while the equality would fail; an injection rule copies the counters; a firing from a state off the equation is refused; and on the forward row of exactly(2, a) that deposits two tokens in b, the firing from {a: 2} reaches b = 2 with the row 2 = 0 + 2 n.
- AC3 (while the certificate check is enabled, a Proven that the fixpoint query decides passes the check with the equation in the candidate; a genuine violation stays Violated and its counterexample replays) is VER_016_certificate for the soundness of a check over (M, n), and VER_016_reach_iff with VER_016_markings for the violation: the rules remove no reachable marking, so a violating marking stays reachable. The content of the candidate, that the fixpoint query decides, the verdict and the replay are the pipeline's and no block states them: the pipeline model (Verifier/Pipeline.lean) names the fixpoint query and the certificate check and does not enter them, and the verdict contract every route meets is VER_003.
- AC4 (the report lines 'State equation: encoded over T firing counters (VER-016)' when the option applied and 'State equation: not applied (name-coloured encoding)' on the coloured path, no line when a route or phase decides before the fixpoint query) is report text (kind Q), not modelled.
- The Implementation notes name the per-language option, and the body the per-language certificate switch (kind N). The test derivation (the fork-that-may-halt net of VER-015 with the enumeration budget 0, the witness depth 0, the phases of VER-018 and VER-019 off and this option on, and the unreachable{ra, rb, halt} script) is AC2 to AC4 on fixtures, as above.

## VER-017: Bounded State-Space Enumeration Route

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_017` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier, all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the route) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 ac7e37919d5e9b2f ai** · Statement hash `ac7e37919d5e9b2f`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The enumeration route *shall* apply exactly when the net it receives, after the rewrites of [VER-006], [VER-004] and [EXEC-042], declares no match transition, has no environment place registered and has only `immediate` transitions, and the class budget is positive.<br><br>The build *shall* be stopped only when the total budget runs out or the caller cancels ([VER-013]).<br><br>*While* the build is neither stopped by the total budget nor cancelled ([VER-013]), the state-class graph *shall* be closed exactly when it has fewer classes than the class budget.<br><br>The state-class graph *shall* hold the initial class as its first class, and only classes reachable from it.<br><br>*When* the graph is closed, the route *shall* return `Proven` exactly when no marking reachable from the initial marking violates the property, and `Violated` otherwise.<br><br>*While* the build is neither stopped by the total budget nor cancelled ([VER-013]), the route *shall* return `Violated` when a counted class violates the property, where a counted class is any stored class for a safety property and a class the builder expanded for a quiescence property.<br><br>*When* the route returns `Violated`, it *shall* report a counted class that violates the property, and a firing sequence from the initial marking to the marking of that class that is a path, in the graph the route built, from the initial class to that class.<br><br>*When* the route returns `Violated`, the firing sequence it reports *shall* be no longer than any path, in the graph the route built, from the initial class to a counted class that violates the property.<br><br>The route *shall not* return `Proven` from a graph that is not closed, and *shall* read nothing off a graph whose build was stopped by the total budget or cancelled.<br><br>*When* the route returns `Proven` or `Violated`, the verifier *shall* return that verdict and *shall not* run the SMT pipeline.<br><br>*If* the route does not run, or the graph is truncated and no counted class violates the property, *then* the verifier *shall* continue with the rest of the pipeline exactly as it does without the route, except that the time the route took counts against a total budget ([VER-013]).<br><br>*If* the build is stopped by the total budget or cancelled, *then* the verifier *shall* return the `Unknown` of [VER-013]. | 1. **Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (A, G, P). A reads an EnumInput: the timed net the route receives, whether it declares a match transition, and the environment places still registered on it, after the rewrites of VER-006 (Arrivals clears the registration and closes the net, smt_verifier.rs with_arrivals), VER-004 (the in-flight split) and EXEC-042 (terminals); none of these changes timing or adds a match transition, so the guard's answer is the same before and after the split and the terminal rewrite. Reference.TimedNet has no match transition and no environment place of its own, so both are fields of EnumInput. G is a GraphRoute (Spec/Verifier/Graph.lean) at the identity explorer of a successor function succ, with no early stop: the runtimes' enumeration build (StateClassGraph::build) has none. On a reference net succ is Reference.succ, every enabled transition and every way its firing can end (enumE), so the reachable states are the untimed reachable markings of VER-004 and a run is a firing sequence (VER_017_firing_sequence). P maps the guard's answer, the route's outcome (enumOutcome) and the answer of the rest of the pipeline to the verifier's answer.
- The statement constrains A, G and P one at a time. That the verifier hands P the guard's answer A x n on the net it verifies, and the outcome enumOutcome G (Reference.succ x.net) n cut fuel m0 p of that net's initial marking, is the wiring the model assumes and does not state; VER_017_only_adds and VER_017_firing_sequence derive what the statement gives under that wiring.
- The property is a Decide.Prop': a safety predicate bad over states, or a quiescence predicate with the reapable labels reap (the reap-aware reading of VER-002, nothing reapable under assumeNoReaping). A state violates a quiescence property when it is bad and every step out of it is of a reapable transition (EnumViol); with nothing reapable that is the markdown's 'found without successors'. A counted class (EnumCounted) is a stored state that violates the property, expanded if the property is a quiescence property. That bad is VER-002's predicate on the marking, and that every route reads one shared implementation of it ('implementations MUST share one predicate implementation'), is code structure, kind Q; in the model the enumeration route and Route B (VER-012) read the one Decide.verdict.
- Line 2 is 'The build shall be stopped only when the total budget runs out or the caller cancels': the stop oracle cut stands for the total budget and cancellation, and the fuel is the model's bound on loop steps, which the runtimes do not have. Each step expands one class, so with fuel above the class budget the budget ends the build first, and a build that never sees the oracle raised is not stopped (ver017_loop_noStop). A build that stops whatever the oracle says passes every other line, and is killed here (VER_017_forbids_spuriousStop).
- Line 3 is the budget boundary of ruling D20 (ver-c#4): the class budget is tested when a class is taken from the worklist (state_class_graph.rs, while let Some(current_idx) = queue.pop_front() { if graph.classes.len() >= max_classes), so a graph of C classes closes only at a budget above C, and a stored class count may exceed the budget. A build that closes at a budget of C is killed (VER_017_forbids_closeAtBudget). The Lean reference search of the conformance binary (Reference/Search.lean) tests its cap on insertion and closes at cap = C, so it disagrees with line 3 at that one budget; the conformance corpus never reaches that boundary: its 224 complete nets hold at most 133 classes, its 81 incomplete nets stop at the reference cap of 100000, and the four languages replay it at an enumeration budget of 5000 (checked 2026-11-12, risk R5).
- Line 4 is 'Every class it stored is a real reachable class': class 0 is the initial state and every stored state is reachable from it (build_par, Decide.build_reach). A build from the wrong state is killed (VER_017_forbids_wrongStart).
- Lines 5 to 7 are 'What the verdict means' (exact: sound and complete on a closed graph) and 'A hit is Violated, with the shortest path to a violating class inside the explored graph as the witness'. Shortest means shortest in the graph the route built (ruling D20, V5 (4)), over the paths to every counted class, not only to the class reported. The reference meets it because its build is breadth-first: a class stored before the target of an edge from class a has an edge from class a or from an earlier class (ver017_build_bfs), so an earlier class is never farther from class 0 (ver017_walk_mono), and the route reports the first counted class in storage order (ver017_verdict_first). The witness is not claimed to be a shortest run of the net: a run can pass through classes a truncated graph did not store, and under VER-024 the graph is reduced. Killed: a route that reports the last counted class (VER_017_forbids_lastHit), a longer path to its own class (VER_017_forbids_longTrace), a class that does not violate (VER_017_forbids_wrongClass), an empty witness (VER_017_forbids_emptyTrace), and a frontier class as quiescent (VER_017_forbids_frontierQuiescent).
- On a reference net the run of line 7 is a firing sequence of the untimed net from the initial marking (VER_017_firing_sequence), which is why the result reports it confirmed with nothing to replay (AC2) and with counterexampleTiming UNTIMED_NET (the route runs only on untimed nets, line 1); the confirmed field and the timing label are the result record of VER-003.
- Lines 8 to 10 are 'Verdicts from a truncated graph': Proven never comes from a prefix (line 8; VER_017_forbids_eagerProven), a stopped build reads nothing (line 9; VER_017_forbids_readStopped), and a counted class makes the verdict Violated whenever the build was not stopped (line 10): a stored safety hit on the frontier (VER_017_forbids_safetyExpanded) and an expanded quiescent class on a truncated graph (VER_017_forbids_noPrefixQuiescence). 'The same rule applies to Route B and to the timed check' is VER-012's and VER-023's line, each over the same Decide.verdict.
- Lines 11 to 14 are the dispatcher. 'Shall not run the SMT pipeline' is the pipeline's: a step that decides ends the run, so no later step is entered and no solver script starts after it (VER_017_decided_ends, over runPipeline of Spec/Verifier/Pipeline.lean), and the enumeration comes before flattening and the IC3/PDR query (rtStepNames_order). 'A reachability-safety property first tries the linear bound of VER-015, which runs ahead of this route' is VER-015's line: the linear bound is part of what runs before the route, and a Proven it returns ends the call before the route.
- In line 13 the argument rest is the answer the rest of the pipeline gives when it runs after the route. Under a total budget (VER-013) it runs with the time the route left, so it can be Unknown where it would decide without the route: that is the 'except that the time the route took counts against a total budget' of the sentence and the 'Unless the total budget runs out or the caller cancels' of the prose (ruling D20, ver-c#6). 'The route can only add verdicts' is lines 11, 13 and 14 with line 12: the answer is the rest of the pipeline's unless the route decided or a stop ended the build (VER_017_only_adds).
- Line 1 is the guard, the route's applicability, and only that. An applying route still does not run when an earlier step of the pipeline decided or refused the query: the linear bound of VER-015, whose Proven ends the call; Route B for a name-alignment property, which it alone decides, even on an untimed net without match transitions (smt_verifier.rs, the Route B trigger ahead of the enumeration); the refusals of VER-003 (an unresolved place, a verified net that cannot be built), VER-004 (the in-flight split) and NU-010 (a declared mint transition the net does not hold); and a stop of VER-013. The markdown says so in the sentence after the guard ('An applying route runs unless an earlier step of the pipeline decided or refused the query'); the order of those steps is rtStepNames with the order lines of VER-015, VER-018, VER-019 and NU-053, and the refusals are VER-003's and NU-010's lines.
- Condition 3 (untimed) is Untimed X, every transition immediate, the test VER-003's UNTIMED_NET reads. Java tests its deprecated Timing.Unconstrained as timed (ScgVerifier.java), so a net using it skips the route in Java only, with the same verdict from the rest of the pipeline; that is a kind N note (ruling D20, ver-c#8).
- AC1 (decided by the graph, the report names the route and its class count, no solver phase but the bound of VER-015) is lines 5 to 7 with line 12 and VER_017_decided_ends; the report text and the class count line are kind Q, and the route name is VER-003's result record.
- AC2 (a confirmed real firing sequence) is line 7 and VER_017_firing_sequence.
- AC3 (the result names the route and says that P-invariants were not computed) is the result record of VER-003 and report text, kind Q.
- AC4 (exceeding the budget gives a report line naming the budget and, unless the prefix violates, falls through unchanged) is lines 3, 10 and 13; the report line is kind Q.
- AC5 (skipped for a ν-net, a net with environment places after the rewrites of VER-006, a timed net, a budget of 0; the verdict is the rest of the pipeline's) is lines 1 and 11 (ruling D92 (a)); refEnumGate is false on each (VER_017_ac5). 'The report carries no enumeration section' is kind Q.
- AC6 (where both routes answer, they agree) is soundness: a Proven of the route holds on every reachable marking (line 5) and a Violated is a real run (line 7), and every route meets VER-003, so no two routes give Proven and a confirmed Violated for one net and property.
- AC7 to AC10 (the state-space cache) are the second block, VER_017_cache.
- AC11 (truncated prefix) is lines 7 to 10, checked on the test derivation's producer gen: G -> G, A at a class budget of 50 (VER_017_nonvacuous): placeBound(A, 2) is Violated with the trace gen, gen, gen, and deadlockFree on the same truncated graph falls through.
- The test derivation's pipeline p0 -> t0 -> p1 -> t1 -> p2 is VER_017_pipeline on the reference net: deadlockFree with p2 a sink is Proven from 3 classes at a budget of 4, without the sink it is Violated with t0, t1, at a budget of 3 (the graph size) the graph is truncated, and the delayed variant and the budget 0 skip the route. 'With and without the route the same verdict' is AC6.
- The motivation and measurement paragraphs are not requirements.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✓ **The reference guard, graph route and dispatcher meet VER-017.** Example: on a chain of three markings the reference build closes at a class budget of 4 and is cut off at 3; on the closed graph a property is `Proven` exactly when no reachable marking violates it, and a `Violated` names the first violating class the build stored, with a path to it no longer than any path to another violating class; on a truncated graph a bad stored class is still `Violated`, a frontier class never counts as dead, and nothing is `Proven`; without a total budget the build is never stopped; a skipped or truncated route leaves the rest of the pipeline's answer.
  <pre>∀ {K S L : Type} [inst : DecidableEq S],<br>  VER_017 refEnumGate Verifier.Graph.refGraphRoute refEnumDispatch</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_forbids_alwaysProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✗ Proving on every closed graph violates VER-017 (line 5): on the closed chain `0 → 1 → 2`, "never reach 2" is violated by a reachable state.
  <pre>¬VER_017 refEnumGate ver017_alwaysProven refEnumDispatch</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_forbids_closeAtBudget` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✗ Closing a graph at a budget equal to its class count violates VER-017 (line 3): the chain `0 → 1 → 2` has three classes, and at a budget of 3 it must be truncated.
  <pre>¬VER_017 refEnumGate ver017_closeAtBudget refEnumDispatch</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_forbids_dropProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✗ Not returning the route's verdict violates VER-017 (line 12).
  <pre>¬VER_017 refEnumGate ver017_ref ver017_dropProven</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_forbids_eagerProven` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✗ A `Proven` from a prefix violates VER-017 (line 8): the producer's truncated graph at a budget of 6 has no class violating `false`, and that proves nothing.
  <pre>¬VER_017 refEnumGate ver017_eagerProven refEnumDispatch</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_forbids_emptyTrace` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_017): ✗ A witness that is not a run to the reported class violates VER-017 (line 7). Example: on the chain `0 → 1 → 2`, "never reach 2" is violated at class `2`, two steps away, and an empty firing sequence stays at `0`.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_017_cache"></a>
## VER-017: Bounded State-Space Enumeration Route: State-Space Cache

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_017_cache` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier with a state-space cache, all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the cache) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 9bdcdb87984d993b ai** · Statement hash `9bdcdb87984d993b`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a state-space cache is passed, the verifier *shall* key each entry by the caller's net, the transitions the in-flight split of [VER-004] rewrote, the initial marking and whether the graph is reduced ([VER-024]), and a query *shall* read and write only the entry of its own key.<br><br>*When* an entry holds a closed graph of `C` classes, a query at a budget greater than `C` *shall* reuse it, and a query at a budget of `C` or less *shall* read it as an explored prefix, in both cases without building.<br><br>*When* an entry holds a truncation remembered at budget `B`, a query at a budget of `B` or less *shall* read its explored prefix without building.<br><br>*When* an entry is empty, or holds a truncation remembered at a budget smaller than the query's, the query *shall* build at its own budget, and the entry *shall* then hold a closed graph as closed, a truncated graph with the query's budget, and, after a build stopped by the total budget or cancelled, what it held before.<br><br>*If* a build fails, *then* the entry *shall* stay as the build found it, and the failure *shall* reach the query that ran the build.<br><br>A query *shall* read a graph it built or reused as the route reads it without the cache, and a graph it read as an explored prefix as a graph that is not closed. | 1. For every lookup Lk, keyed query Q and reading R: a closed entry o at budget b answers reused o when o holds fewer than b classes and declined o otherwise, and stays as it was, whatever the build would return;<br>2. a truncation remembered at B answers declined, and stays, at every budget b of B or less;<br>3. when the query builds (the entry is empty, or a truncation at B below b) and the build returns o, the answer is built o and the entry becomes closed o if o closed, stays as it was if o was stopped, and becomes the truncation of o at b otherwise;<br>4. when the query builds and the build fails, the answer is none and the entry stays as it was;<br>5. R reads a built or reused graph o with the route's verdict on o, and a declined graph o with the verdict on o marked not closed;<br>6. on a keyed cache c, a query at key k answers what the lookup of c k answers, leaves at k what that lookup leaves, and leaves every other key's entry as it was. | <pre>fun {S L N M} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq M] Lk Q R ↦<br>  (∀ (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S) (b : ℕ) (build : Option (Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S)),<br>      Lk (Verifier.Graph.Slot.closed o) b build =<br>        (some<br>            (if o.cls.length &lt; b then Verifier.Graph.Use.reused o<br>            else Verifier.Graph.Use.declined o),<br>          Verifier.Graph.Slot.closed o)) ∧<br>    (∀ (B : ℕ) (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S) (b : ℕ)<br>        (build : Option (Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S)),<br>        b ≤ B →<br>          Lk (Verifier.Graph.Slot.truncated B o) b build =<br>            (some (Verifier.Graph.Use.declined o), Verifier.Graph.Slot.truncated B o)) ∧<br>      (∀ (slot : Verifier.Graph.Slot S) (b : ℕ) (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S),<br>          CacheBuilds slot b →<br>            Lk slot b (some o) =<br>              (some (Verifier.Graph.Use.built o),<br>                if o.complete = true then Verifier.Graph.Slot.closed o<br>                else<br>                  if o.stopped = true then slot else Verifier.Graph.Slot.truncated b o)) ∧<br>        (∀ (slot : Verifier.Graph.Slot S) (b : ℕ),<br>            CacheBuilds slot b → Lk slot b none = (none, slot)) ∧<br>          (∀ (E : Explorer S S L) (o : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S)<br>              (p : Novel.RouteB.Decide.Prop' S L),<br>              R E (Verifier.Graph.Use.built o) p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.verdict E o p ∧<br>                R E (Verifier.Graph.Use.reused o) p = Novel.RouteB.Decide.verdict E o p ∧<br>                  R E (Verifier.Graph.Use.declined o) p =<br>                    Novel.RouteB.Decide.verdict E<br>                      { cls := o.cls, exp := o.exp, complete := false,<br>                        stopped := o.stopped, early := o.early }<br>                      p) ∧<br>            ∀ (c : Verifier.Graph.Cache (Verifier.Graph.CacheKey N M) S)<br>              (k : Verifier.Graph.CacheKey N M) (b : ℕ)<br>              (build : Option (Novel.RouteB.Decide.Out S)),<br>              (Q c k b build).1 = (Lk (c k) b build).1 ∧<br>                (Q c k b build).2 k = (Lk (c k) b build).2 ∧<br>                  ∀ (k' : Verifier.Graph.CacheKey N M),<br>                    k' ≠ k → (Q c k b build).2 k' = c k'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (Lk, Q, R) of CacheLookupFn, CacheQueryFn and CacheReadFn, with witnesses cacheLookup, cacheQuery and useVerdict (Spec/Verifier/Graph.lean). An entry is a Slot: empty, a closed graph, or a truncation kept with its budget and its explored prefix (the stored classes, from which the successors are re-read, and the expanded count). The build argument is what a build at the query's budget would return, none when it fails (a panic or an exception in the runtimes); a model that reads it only when it builds is what 'without building' means here. That a cached graph is a graph some build returned is cacheLookup_ok in Graph.lean, and that a reused graph is the uncached build at the query's budget is VER_017_cache_reuse below.
- Line 5 fixes the reading R to the reference reading Decide.verdict, not to the route block's G: 'as the route reads it without the cache' holds through the reference, whose graph route reads with Decide.verdict (refGraphRoute), so the two blocks meet at the reference and not at an arbitrary G. Which key a query uses (its net, split, initial marking and whether the graph is reduced), and that the answer it gets is what the route's dispatcher receives, is wiring the model assumes and does not state.
- The key is CacheKey: the net (or a structural fingerprint of it; Rust and Python key on the Debug rendering of the net every route reads, Java and TypeScript on the net instance), the transitions the in-flight split rewrote (a key without them is killed, VER_017_forbids_cacheNoSplit), the initial marking (with the order in which it lists its places where a witness shows it) and whether the graph is reduced (VER-024). That the fingerprint covers everything the graph reads, and never hits where the graphs differ, is the key's job, not the state machine's: here a key is any value with decidable equality, and two different keys never share an entry (line 6).
- Under Arrivals the graph is that of the closed net, which depends on the registered environment places and the mode as well as on the caller's net and marking: on the net tA: A -> OA, tB: B -> OB with an empty marking under Arrivals(1), PlaceBound(OA, 0) is Violated with A registered and Proven with B registered, so a key without the closure would hand one query the other's graph. The EARS sentence '*While* the mode is `Arrivals(k)` or `Arrivals(min, max)` of [VER-006] and environment places are registered, *when* a state-space cache is passed, the verifier *shall* either key each entry also by the closure (the registered environment places in registration order and the mode), or not use the cache for that query and say so in the report.' is again the key's job: CacheKey is abstract here, and a key that covers the closure is one more field of it. Rust and Python key the fingerprint of the closed net (smt_verifier.rs, state_space_cache.rs), which covers the closure; Java and TypeScript do not use the cache when Arrivals closed the net over registered environment places, and say so in the report with one line (SmtVerifier.java and smt-verifier.ts, the enumeration step); Arrivals(0) closes nothing there, and the cache is used. A key of the caller's net with the closed initial marking, whose arrival sources are new Place objects on every call, misses on every such query and adds an entry with no report line (the TypeScript behaviour RD-28 recorded); it returns no wrong verdict, since it never hits.
- 'The graph depends only on the net, the in-flight split, its initial marking and whether it is reduced; the property, the sinks and the conditional sinks only read it' is the key of line 6 with line 5: the property is an argument of R only. The measurement paragraph is not a requirement.
- Line 1 is the closed bullet: a closed graph of C classes is reused above C and answered as truncated at C or less, where it is read as a prefix (line 5), as Rust's StateSpaceLookup::Declined does for a closed graph (state_space_cache.rs, smt_verifier.rs enumerate). Reusing a closed graph at a budget of C is killed (VER_017_forbids_reuseAtBudget).
- Lines 2 to 4 are the truncation and failure bullets; a cache that builds again at a budget a remembered truncation covers (VER_017_forbids_rebuildBelow), one that stores a stopped build as a truncation (VER_017_forbids_storeStopped) and one that empties the entry on a failed build (VER_017_forbids_failClears) are killed. 'The failure reaches the query that ran the build' is the answer none of line 4; how it reaches the caller (an exception, a panic) is per language.
- Line 5 is 'The verdict, the witness and the route are the same with and without the cache, with two exceptions' (ruling D92 (a)): a graph the query built or reused is read as the route reads it (VER_017_cache_reuse: a reused closed graph is the build at the query's budget, so verdict and witness match the uncached query), and a declined graph is read as a prefix, never Proven (VER_017_cache_declined_not_proven), where it can find a violation an uncached query at the smaller budget would not reach. A reading that takes a declined closed graph as closed is killed (VER_017_forbids_declinedClosed). 'The report says when a cached graph, or a cached truncation, was used' is report text, kind Q.
- The concurrency bullets (one build per entry, waiting queries, a budget of B or less declining at once during a larger rebuild, waiters retrying after a failed build) and 'the cache holds its graphs until the caller drops it or clears it' are not modelled: the model is the sequential state machine, kind Q (AC10, the runtimes' concurrency tests). Rust also answers Stopped to a query whose total budget runs out while it waits on another query's build; that is the route's stopped outcome (line 14 of the route block).
- AC7 (a later query with the same key at the same budget builds no graph and answers as without the cache; under Arrivals the key covers the closure, and the claim is for a query the cache serves) is lines 1, 2 and 5 with VER_017_cache_reuse (ruling D92 (a)), the Arrivals half being the key's, as above. AC8 (a cached truncation at B answers a budget of B or less from its prefix, a larger budget builds and replaces it; a cached closed graph of C classes answers a budget of C or less from the whole graph read as a prefix, without building and never Proven) is lines 1, 2, 3 and 5 with VER_017_cache_declined_not_proven. AC9 (a different marking, net or split never hits another entry; with and without assumeAtomicFiring on a net the split rewrites each query builds) is line 6 (VER_017_cache_nonvacuous checks two keys that differ only in the split). AC10 (parallel queries build once) is concurrency, kind Q.

## VER-018: State-Equation Phase with Refinement

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_018` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier's state-equation phase on the flat path, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 142e63675d5af03a ai** · Statement hash `142e63675d5af03a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the state-equation query answers `unsat`, the phase *shall* end with a proof over the refinements it has added so far.<br><br>*If* the state-equation query fails in the transport, answers `unknown`, gives a model that cannot be decoded, or the timeout runs out before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.<br><br>*When* the state-equation query answers `sat`, the phase *shall* first run the witness search on the candidate, and *shall* return `Violated` with the run the search reports before it tries any refinement.<br><br>The witness search *shall* fire each flat transition at most as often as the candidate's counts allow, under the exact abstract semantics of [VER-004] and with no injection step, and *shall* report a run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.<br><br>A run the witness search reports *shall* be no longer than any other run within the counts that ends in a violating marking.<br><br>The witness search *shall* report that no violating run exists only when it has completed, no run within the counts ends in a violating marking, and no environment place is declared for injection.<br><br>*While* environment places are declared for injection, the phase *shall* still run the witness search, and the search *shall* report the same run it reports on the same net without injection.<br><br>*If* a run within the candidate's counts ends in a violating marking, *then* the witness search *shall* report a run whenever its node budget is large enough.<br><br>The trap search *shall* return a set `Q` of places of the flat net only when every flat transition that can take a token from `Q`, through an input arc, a consume-all input or a reset arc, also puts a token into `Q`, some place of `Q` is marked in `M0`, and the candidate leaves every place of `Q` empty.<br><br>The trap search *shall* return a trap whenever some initially marked trap among the places of the flat net is empty in the candidate.<br><br>The exact re-check *shall* accept an inequality `a·M ≤ b` only when it holds at `M0` and every firing and every injection step of the exact step relation keeps it.<br><br>The exact re-check *shall* accept an inequality `a·M ≤ b` that holds at `M0`, gives no injected place a positive weight, and for which every flat transition that can fire, taken from the least marking its guard allows, passes the keep test or the restore test: the keep test, that the firing does not raise `a·M` and every place the firing clears without inhibiting has a weight of at least 0; the restore test, that the marking after the firing meets the bound and every place the firing neither clears nor inhibits has a weight of at most 0.<br><br>*When* the witness search reports no run and the phase has added fewer refinements than the refinement limit, the phase *shall* settle the candidate in this order: with `Σ_{q∈Q} m_q ≥ 1` when the trap search returns a trap `Q`; otherwise with the inequality the `invariant` query returns, marked inductive, when the exact re-check accepts it and the candidate violates it; otherwise, when that query answers `unsat`, with the inequality the same query returns with the marking equation as a premise of every step, marked relative, when the candidate violates it.<br><br>*When* the phase adds a refinement, it *shall* ask the state-equation query again with every refinement added so far.<br><br>*If* no trap and no inequality settles the candidate, an inequality fails the exact re-check or holds at the candidate, or an `invariant` query fails in the transport, answers `unknown`, gives a model that cannot be decoded, or the timeout runs out before its answer, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.<br><br>*If* the witness search reports no run on a candidate after the phase has added as many refinements as the refinement limit, *then* the phase *shall* end inconclusive, and the pipeline *shall* continue.<br><br>*While* the certificate check is enabled, the verifier *shall* return the phase's proof as `Proven` with method `state-equation` and neither a counterexample nor `counterexampleConfirmed` when the certificate check of [VER-016] passes on the invariant `SE(M, n) ∧ ⋀ refinements(M)`, and a failed or inconclusive check *shall* withhold the `Proven` and let the pipeline continue.<br><br>*While* the certificate check is disabled, the verifier *shall* return the phase's proof as `Proven` with method `state-equation` and neither a counterexample nor `counterexampleConfirmed`, and the report *shall* carry `  Certificate check: not applicable (disabled)` in place of the check.<br><br>*When* the phase returns `Violated`, the verifier *shall* return the markings and transitions of the run, in firing order, as the counterexample, with `counterexampleConfirmed` `true`.<br><br>The refinement limit *shall* be 32 in every implementation.<br><br>The node budget of one witness search *shall* be 100 000 in every implementation.<br><br>Each weight of an inductive or relative inequality *shall* have a magnitude of at most the larger of 8 and the number of tokens in `M0`. | 1. **Assumptions**

- The model is the quintuple (S, T, X, P, W) of SESearch, SETrapFn, SEIndCheck, SEPhaseFn and SEWrap over the untimed abstraction of VER-004 with injection: a flat net (FlatNet, the abstract semantics enabledA and fireA, posts read as sets: post puts one token in each place a row lists), its injected places envs, its place count w and M0. So the model covers rows that deposit at most one token per place. VER-016 reads deposits by count (CntRows, fireAD, cntCol) and agrees with the set reading on such rows (VER_016_unit_rows); a row that deposits two tokens in one place (the timeout forward of an exactly(2) input, Novel/ForwardDeposit.lean), which flatten builds and the phase reads, is outside this model. The violation is a Boolean predicate on markings (the error rule of VER-001 as violation_predicate reads it, with the relax-env quiescence of VER-006 under injection); which markings violate is VER-002's and VER-006's subject. The solver is not modelled: the answers of the state-equation query (SEAns, per list of refinements) and of the two invariant queries (SESynAns, per candidate marking) are inputs of P, so every line holds whatever the solver answers. The witness is refSESearch, refSETrap, refSECheckInd, refSEPhase and refSEWrap.
- The environment mode is AlwaysAvailable: the Bounded(k) caps that prune a firing in the witness search and add conjuncts to the scripts only remove steps (VER-006) and are not modelled. A name-alignment property (NU-055) is refused by the phase before any query; that refusal is NU-055's line.
- The first quoted sentence is line 10. 'A proof' is the outcome proven with the refinements; what the verifier returns for it is the hand-over, lines 15 and 16. That the bare unsat is a proof when the solver is right is VER_018_unsat_sound, from the statement alone: every reachable marking satisfies the equation for the counts of its run (rows_hold, counters_exist of VER-016) and every trap and inductive refinement holds on it (VER_018_refinements_hold); a relative refinement needs its premise, since only the certificate check re-proves it.
- The second quoted sentence is line 9: a transport failure, unknown, a model that cannot be decoded and a timeout are one answer each in SEAns.aside (the phase's budget is the verifier's timeout, and each query gets what is left of it). 'The pipeline shall continue' is the hand-over (line 16: an inconclusive outcome is an aside) with VER_018_order and runPipeline, where an aside goes on to the next step. That the pipeline's state-equation step runs W over P is the wiring VER_018_order assumes and does not yet state (open item, carried there), so the 'pipeline continues' parts of this block reach runPipeline only through that wiring.
- The third quoted sentence is line 11: the search runs on every sat candidate, and a run it reports ends the phase before seRefine is consulted (VER_018_forbids_noWitness).
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 1. The fifth is line 2: the run a search reports is a shortest one; how the search finds it (the runtimes' breadth-first search over markings and unspent counts, which the Witness paragraph names as motivation), the order among runs of one length (flat order in the runtimes) and the deduplication by marking and unspent counts are not pinned. The sixth is line 3. The seventh is line 4: 'still run' is that a run found without injection is found with it, which a search that skips injected nets breaks (VER_018_forbids_searchSkipsInj). The eighth is line 5: the node budget is a parameter of S, and the line states that some budget suffices, as the runtimes' breadth-first search over (marking, unspent counts) does once the budget exceeds those finitely many nodes; the reference search needs no budget. At the shipped budget (the twenty-first quoted sentence) nothing requires the search to report a run that exists, so AC3 holds within the node budget. A run the search misses leaves the candidate to refinement, and no false Proven follows: the run's last marking is reachable, so it satisfies the equation and every trap and inductive refinement (VER_018_refinements_hold), and it stays a solution of every later query while the relative refinements hold.
- The ninth quoted sentence is line 6 ('places of the flat net' is that every place of Q lies below w) and the tenth is line 7. They state what a trap is and that one is found when it exists; which trap the search returns (the runtimes shrink the largest trap inside the empty places to a locally minimal one, the reference returns the first subset in order) changes the refinement text, not a verdict, and is not pinned. That a trap with clearing arcs stays marked on every reachable marking, injection included, is seGTrap_stays_marked; the plain trap of Commoner (input arcs only) does not, and a trap search that ignores reset and consume-all arcs breaks line 6 (VER_018_forbids_trapNoClearing).
- The eleventh quoted sentence is line 8. 'Exact integer arithmetic' is Lean's Int. The reference re-check refSECheckInd is the runtimes' check_inductive_exact (every flat transition that can fire keeps the bound or restores it from its guard, injected places weigh at most 0), and refSECheckInd_sound proves it sound; the Farkas query that proposes the inequality, its multipliers in {0, 1} and the least-magnitude objective are script text (VER-013) and not modelled.
- The twelfth quoted sentence is line 18: X accepts every inequality the reference re-check accepts. 'A flat transition that can fire' is canFire (a transition that inhibits a place it needs never fires); 'the least marking its guard allows' is seLower (each place at its input requirement, at least 1 when it is read, 0 when it is inhibited); the keep test is seKeeps over the coefficients seKeepC and the restore test is seRestores over seRestoreC. Lines 8 and 18 together pin X between the inductive inequalities and the reference: a re-check without the restore test (the textbook Farkas check with the multiplier 1 only) rejects hasdata <= ready0 + ready1 on the join of AC2, so the join would end inconclusive, and breaks line 18 (VER_018_forbids_recheckKeepOnly). Java's BigInteger and TypeScript's bigint are exact; Rust computes in checked 128-bit arithmetic and rejects on an overflow, which needs M0 to hold 2^63 tokens or more in total or weights beyond the weight bound of the twenty-second quoted sentence, and is not modelled.
- The thirteenth quoted sentence is lines 13 and 14 through seRefine, the fixed function the lines name: trap first, then the inductive query, then the relative query; the inductive inequality is kept only when X accepts it and it excludes the candidate, the relative one only when it excludes the candidate. 'Marked inductive' and 'marked relative' are the origins seRefine gives, which the report prints as the refinement's origin (AC2). A phase that skips the trap search, or labels a relative inequality inductive (so that it is used without the equation), breaks line 13 (VER_018_forbids_noTrap, VER_018_forbids_relativeAsInductive). The fourteenth quoted sentence is line 13 itself: P over rs is P over rs with r appended, so the state-equation query is asked again over every refinement. The fifteenth is line 14: a transport failure, unknown, a model that cannot be decoded and a timeout of an invariant query are one answer each in SESynAns.aside, which seRefine turns into the reason synthesisAside.
- The sixteenth quoted sentence is line 12. The order is the runtimes': the witness search runs before the limit is tested, so a candidate at the limit can still be violated, and the query after the last refinement can still prove (the limit is tested after a sat candidate). That the outcome carries at most L refinements is VER_018_limit, from the statement alone. The limit is a parameter of P. The twentieth to twenty-second quoted sentences are configuration (kind N, ruling D45): the refinement limit 32 is the constant ver018_refinementLimit, the node budget 100 000 the constant ver018_nodeBudget (a parameter of S, line 5), and the weight bound max(8, tokens of M0) the function ver018_weightBound, all pinned below. No line of the statement checks the three: L and B are parameters of P and S, and the weight bound limits the invariant queries' search space and is script text (VER-013), so the model's solver answers range over every weight.
- The seventeenth quoted sentence is lines 15 and 16 (ruling D52 (a)): a passed check gives the decision Proven (line 15), and a failed or inconclusive one an aside (line 16), so while the check is enabled a Proven comes from a passed check and from nothing else. 'Neither a counterexample nor counterexampleConfirmed' is the empty trace and the absent flag of line 15, as the result record of VER-003 has them where no replay applies and as VER-019's hand-over has them for its own Proven. The certificate check is not modelled; its answer is an input of W. That a passed check makes the proof sound is VER_018_proven_sound, from the statement alone, under the premise that the check is right (a passed check means the three verification conditions of Novel.Certificate.VCs hold against the raw counter step StepCntRel from (M0, 0) for seCert, the invariant SE(M, n) and the refinements); it rests on vc_sound_state_equation. That a decided Proven comes only from a proof with the check passed or disabled is VER_018_proven_needs_check. The eighteenth quoted sentence is line 15 for the disabled check, with the same empty trace and absent flag; its report line is text (kind Q), the constant ver018_certDisabledLine pinned below; with the check disabled a relative refinement is re-proved by nothing, and the proof rests on the solver alone.
- The nineteenth quoted sentence is line 17 for the transitions: the trace of a decision is the run's transitions by name, as VER-019's pipeline block has it. The markings of the run, which the result also carries as its counterexample trace in replay order (Rust witness_result, smt_verifier.rs), are not a field of the decision PhaseOut, so no line checks them; they are the replay of those transitions (seReplay), whose last marking VER_018_violated_sound gives. That the result carries them is an open item for the result model of VER-019's pipeline block. That a reported run is a run of the abstraction to a violating marking, so a genuine violation is reported only for a replayed run, is VER_018_violated_sound, from the statement alone.
- The body's motivation (the equation ignores firing order; the join's skip transition as the typical spurious candidate; the CAV 2014 and CAV 2003 references; the Farkas dual of the final unsat is not used; that every trap and inductive refinement holds in every reachable marking, which is VER_018_refinements_hold, and a relative one when the solver's answer is right, which is the premise of VER_018_unsat_sound), the 'Where it runs' paragraph and the measurements are not lines of this block. The paragraph is VER_018_order. The equation and the violation of the query are VER-016's rows and VER-001's error rule, inputs here through the solver's answers. 'Unlike VER-015 the query asks for the violation directly, so it covers every property' is the shape of the script (VER-013).
- AC1 (a property the equation excludes is Proven with method state-equation without a fixpoint query, with the PASSED certificate line) is lines 10 and 15: an unsat answer gives the proof, the hand-over returns a decision, which ends the run before the fixpoint query (VER_018_order). The report line is the constant ver018_certPassedLine, pinned below. VER_018_nonvacuous proves the ring t0: p0 to p1, t1: p1 to p0 after one trap refinement.
- AC2 (the join-with-skip net proven with the refinement hasdata <= ready0 + ready1, listed as the result's discovered invariants) is VER_018_join_refinement: the reference re-check accepts that inequality on the join's flat net and it excludes the candidate that skips after the data arrived. The report line and the discovered-invariants list are text (kind Q), the function ver018_refinementLine pinned below; that the solver returns that inequality is not modelled.
- AC3 (a candidate a run within its counts realises is reported violated, with that run confirmed) is lines 5, 11 and 17, within the node budget (see the eighth quoted sentence); VER_018_nonvacuous replays the run produce, produce, produce, cancel on the queue-and-bundle net with cancel.
- AC4 (the phase's Proven is withheld unless the certificate check passes, while the check is enabled; Violated only for a replayed run) is line 16 with VER_018_proven_needs_check, and line 1 with VER_018_violated_sound.
- AC5 (with the phase disabled, verdicts and reports are those of the pipeline without it) is VER_018_order line 4 with VER_018_order_disabled.
- AC6 (LIBPETRI_SMT_DUMP records the scripts under the phases state-equation and invariant) and AC7 (the first query is exposed with the encoded scripts and pinned as a golden of VER-013 AC1) are about script text and its dump names (kind Q), checked by the dump and golden-script tests of VER-013; the phase names are the constants ver018_dumpPhases, pinned below.
- The Implementation notes name the per-language option and modules (kind N). The Naming bullet's SHOULD, that an implementation cross-reference stateEquationPhase and the stateEquation option of VER-016 wherever it documents either, is about documentation text (kind N), and no line checks it. The test derivation is AC2 and AC3 on the join and queue nets under the options it names (the enumeration budget of VER-017 at 0 and assumeAtomicFiring), which the pipeline sets outside the model.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_018_order"></a>
## VER-018: State-Equation Phase with Refinement: its place in the pipeline

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier's pipeline, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 cfe8823cc35862e7 ai** · Statement hash `cfe8823cc35862e7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The pipeline *shall* place the state-equation phase at one point, after the linear bound of [VER-015] and before the fixpoint query.<br><br>*While* the phase is enabled, the pipeline *shall* run it on exactly the queries whose verified net has no match transition and that are not verified under `Ignore` with environment places registered ([VER-006]), unless an earlier step has decided the query or the run has stopped.<br><br>*If* the phase is disabled, *then* the verifier *shall not* run it, and the verdicts and reports *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.<br><br>Every implementation *shall* turn the phase on by default. | 1. In the pipeline's step names, the linear bound comes before the state-equation phase: the list splits so that every linear-bound step is in the first part and every state-equation step in the second, and each part holds one of them.<br>2. In the same sense, the state-equation phase comes before the fixpoint query (the IC3/PDR query).<br>3. The state-equation phase occurs exactly once in the step names.<br>4. The gate seG is true exactly when the verified net has no ν match transition, the policy is not Ignore with environment places declared, and the phase's option is on. | <pre>fun names seG ↦<br>  Verifier.Before names ver018_lbStep ver019_seStep ∧<br>    Verifier.Before names ver019_seStep ver019_fixStep ∧<br>      List.count ver019_seStep names = 1 ∧<br>        ∀ (c : FBCtx), seG c = (!c.nuNet &amp;&amp; !c.ignoreEnv &amp;&amp; c.seOn)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (names, seG). names is the list of the pipeline's step names, in order (the names of the GStep list of Spec/Verifier/Pipeline.lean); runPipeline gives the order its meaning in a run (VER_018_order_runs). seG reads FBCtx, the context of VER-019's pipeline block. The witness is rtStepNames (the runtimes' thirteen step names) and refSeGate.
- That the pipeline's state-equation step is entered under seG and runs the hand-over W of the first block over the phase P is the wiring this block assumes and does not state: in rtPipeline the step is still idle, and the integrator ties it when the phase's slice replaces the idle step (open item). VER_018_order_disabled takes the wiring as a premise.
- The first quoted sentence is lines 1 to 3. 'Place' is the order of the step names (Before); in every run the steps are entered in that order, and the state-equation phase at most once (VER_018_order_runs). The runtimes run the linear bound twice, once before the enumeration route and once on the flat path; both come before the phase, and Before reads every occurrence. That the firing-bound phase comes after this phase is VER-019's order line.
- The second quoted sentence is line 4. 'No match transition' is the nuNet flag of FBCtx; the name-coloured encoding of NU-050 applies only to such nets, so 'not on the name-coloured encoding' is the same condition. 'Not under Ignore with environment places registered' is the ignoreEnv flag, read on the net the dispatcher receives. 'Unless an earlier step has decided the query or the run has stopped' is the pipeline: a decision ends the run, and so does the stop poll before each step, with no decision (runPipeline). With this line, VER-019's pipeline block pins the firing-bound phase's gate to the runtimes' (VER_018_order_fb_gate), which closes the open item recorded there.
- The third quoted sentence is line 4 with the option off: the gate is false, a step whose gate is false is skipped without a poll, and the run, its decision and its trail are those of the step list without the step (VER_018_order_disabled). The reports are not modelled. It is AC5.
- The fourth quoted sentence is configuration (kind N): the constant ver018_defaultOn, pinned above.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✓ **The runtimes satisfy the pipeline block.** In their step list the linear bound comes second and seventh, the state-equation phase eighth and only there, and the IC3/PDR query twelfth; the phase is entered on the flat path with its option on.
  <pre>VER_018_order Verifier.rtStepNames refSeGate</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_gateNoOption` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A phase that runs although it is disabled violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 4).
  <pre>¬VER_018_order Verifier.rtStepNames ver018_gateNoOption</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_gateOnNu` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A phase that runs on a net with match transitions violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 4): the flat encoding is name-blind there, and [VER-012] and [NU-053] are its exact routes.
  <pre>¬VER_018_order Verifier.rtStepNames ver018_gateOnNu</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_gateUnderIgnore` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A phase that runs under `Ignore` with environment places violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 4): [VER-006] refuses every `Proven` there.
  <pre>¬VER_018_order Verifier.rtStepNames ver018_gateUnderIgnore</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_seFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A pipeline that runs the phase before the linear bound violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 1).
  <pre>¬VER_018_order ver018_seFirst refSeGate</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_seLate` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A pipeline that runs the phase after the fixpoint query violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 2): the query would decide first, and the phase could never spare it.
  <pre>¬VER_018_order ver018_seLate refSeGate</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_018_order_forbids_seTwice` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_018): ✗ A pipeline that runs the phase a second time violates VER-018's pipeline block (line 3).
  <pre>¬VER_018_order ver018_seTwice refSeGate</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_019"></a>
## VER-019: Firing-Bound Phase

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_019` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 0417695269924143 ai** · Statement hash `0417695269924143`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the ranking query answers with a weighting `r`, the phase *shall* re-check in exact integer arithmetic that every weight is at least 0 and that `r·C_t ≤ −1` for every flat transition `t` that **Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (C, D, P) of FBRankingCheck, FBDepthLoop and FBPhaseFn. C is the re-check from the number n of flat places, the flat net as deposit rows (Row = transition and deposit, the exact abstract semantics of VER-004: enabledA, fireAD), M0 and the weighting (Weight, an integer per place) to the bound K or none. D is the depth loop from the bound, the depth limit and the solver's answer per depth (some true = sat, some false = unsat, none = no answer). P is the phase from the injection flag, n, the rows, M0, the violation isBad (the property's violation predicate as replay_run reads it), the depth limit L, the ranking query's answer (FBRank) and the bounded model check's answer per depth (Witness.Answer, as for VER-025: sat with the selector values the model defines, unsat, unknown, a transport failure, a spent budget). The witness triple is checkRankingExact, phaseDepths and refFiringBoundPhase.
- The first quoted sentence is line 1. 'Can fire' is canFire (bounded_run.rs can_fire): every inhibited place has pre 0 and is not read; a transition that inhibits a place it needs is enabled at no marking (not_canFire_never_enabled), so its column does not count. 'Exact integer arithmetic' is Lean's Int: the model has no overflow. A port whose i128 re-check overflows refuses the weighting, which is the recheck outcome; z3's weights keep it far from that. A sat reply whose weights do not decode is reported by the ports as a failed re-check; the model's FBRank.ranking carries decoded weights only, and both cases end inconclusive. That a ranking bounds every run by K is a consequence, not a line: VER_019_bound, from line 1 through ranking_bounds_length.
- The second quoted sentence is lines 6 and 7: P ends inconclusive and D is never consulted. 'The pipeline shall continue' is the pipeline around the phase, the second block VER_019_order (line 7): its hand-over turns P's inconclusive and unbounded outcomes into an aside, after which the pipeline enters its next step (VER_019_order_continues).
- The third quoted sentence is line 2 (ver019_schedule, pinned with #guard below: bound 5 gives the depths [5], bound 25 [8, 16, 25], bound 600 at the limit 512 [8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512]). The fourth (the limit 512) is the constant ver019_depthLimit, pinned below; the model is parametric in L, so the statement holds at every limit.
- The fifth quoted sentence is line 2 (unsat at a depth of at least K is proven) with line 8 (P is proven with the bound K, the outcome proven K; VER_019_forbids_neverProves kills a phase that steps aside there). 'Method bounded-model-check' is the verdict's method ver019_method, which the hand-over of VER_019_order (line 8) puts on the Proven it returns, with no counterexample and no counterexampleConfirmed, and the bound reaches the report as the Bound line of AC1. That the proof is sound is VER_019_proven_sound, from the statement alone, under the premises it names: well-formed rows (P1, P2), an integer violation that agrees with isBad (P5), and correct unsat answers (P4: the depth-d script has no model, BmcSat, when the solver says unsat). These premises are about the solver and the encoder, which the statement does not model, so they are hypotheses of the derived theorem, not of the requirement.
- The sixth quoted sentence is line 2 (unsat at the last depth of the schedule, the limit, below K ends the scan with stop) and line 9.
- The seventh and eighth quoted sentences are line 10. The run is read as VER-025 reads it (decodeModel at T = the number of rows, J = 0: a selector in [0, T) is a transition step, anything else ends the run, an undefined selector is idle, a model that defines none of the selectors below a positive depth gives no run, and depth 0 gives the empty run whatever the model, as decode_bounded_run does with seen = depth == 0) and replayed by replays with no injection (replayEnv at [] is replay: replayEnv_nil). So at depth 0, which the schedule asks only when K = 0 (or L = 0), a sat answer is the empty run, reported when isBad a0 holds; the prose after the eighth sentence says so. The run is reported as decoded, untrimmed, as the seventh sentence says (the trim is VER-025's). Each branch of line 10 has its own mutant: VER_019_forbids_silentAsEmpty (a model that defines no selector at a positive depth read as the empty run), VER_019_forbids_neverViolated (a replaying run not reported) and VER_019_forbids_noReplay (a run reported without replay). 'Confirmed' (counterexampleConfirmed true) and the run's transitions as the counterexample are VER_019_order line 9; the result text is outside the model. That a reported run reaches a violating marking is VER_019_violated_sound, from the statement alone. A sat answer comes only at a depth the loop asked (line 2: scan reports sat only where ask answered sat), so the model given is that depth's.
- The ninth quoted sentence is line 4. The second query that names the transitions of a repeatable firing vector is not an input of P: line 4 fixes unbounded for every answer the phase gets after the ranking query's unsat, so whatever the second query answers (a vector, unsat, unknown, a transport failure or a spent budget, as bounded_run.rs reads every reply but a decodable sat as no vector) the outcome is unbounded. Its report line, with the vector or the fallback, is report text (ver019_noBoundLine and ver019_noBoundFallback, pinned below); which transitions z3 names is not modelled. 'Continue to the fixpoint query' is the pipeline, as in the second quoted sentence.
- The tenth quoted sentence names the ranking query and the bounded model checks only; the second query is the ninth sentence's. It is line 5 for the ranking query and lines 2 and 9 for a depth (no answer ends the scan with stop). A transport failure, unknown and a spent phase budget are one answer each in Witness.Answer and one FBRank.aside; the model does not tell them apart, as the outcome does not; only the reason text of the report does, and it is not modelled. The budget, half the timeout rounded down to whole milliseconds and at least 1 ms as the prose says (max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 2)) in smt_verifier.rs, smt-verifier.ts and SmtVerifier.java), is the pure function ver019_budgetMs, pinned below; the wall clock is not modelled.
- The eleventh quoted sentence is line 3. The flag is the declared injection list being non-empty (smt_verifier.rs gates on cx.env_injection before resolution), so a declared environment place no arc touches sets it too. 'Send no query' is not expressible, as for VER-025: the answers are inputs of P; line 3 fixes the outcome for every answer, so it depends on none. Under Ignore the phase is not entered at all (it runs on the queries VER-018 runs on), which is the pipeline's gate (VER_019_order line 6), not this model's.
- The twelfth quoted sentence (on by default, as VER-018) is configuration (N): the constant ver019_defaultOn, pinned below; that the two phases default alike is checked by the verdict-parity fixtures, and the order 'after VER-018 and before the witness phase and the fixpoint query' and 'runs on the queries VER-018 runs on' are VER_019_order lines 1 to 4 and line 6, not this model.
- The sentence on a disabled phase (not run, and the verdicts and reports those of the pipeline without it) is quoted by VER_019_order, line 5, the pipeline's gate: P is the phase when it runs, so a disabled phase is not an input of P and the equality with the pipeline without the phase is a statement about the pipeline (VER_019_order_disabled). The prose 'Disabling the phase leaves the query to the later steps, up to the fixpoint query' is the same gate seen from the pipeline.
- The kept prose that the ranking with the least K is found by one optimisation query names the ranking script's objective, the line (minimize r·M0) that encode_ranking_query writes in every port (bounded_run.rs, bounded-run.ts, BoundedRun.java). The model takes the solver's weighting as an input of P, and every line holds for every weighting, so the statement neither needs nor checks that it is least. Least matters across ports, since K sets the depth schedule and the tooLarge cut, but the least K is one number for a given net and M0, so ports that send the same objective and get a correct optimum agree on it. The objective is pinned by the Rust and Java script tests (bounded_run.rs, BoundedRunTest.java); the cross-language goldens of VER-013 hold the state-equation, horn, certificate and witness scripts, not the ranking script.
- A name-alignment property (NU-055) is refused by the phase before any query and before the injection check (bounded_run.rs and bounded-run.ts return the NU-055 reason first; the prose says so); that refusal is NU-055's line, and isBad here is a violation over counts. The quiescence reading inside isBad (reap-aware unless assumeNoReaping, VER-002) is VER-002's subject: the model takes the violation as given. Reaping.firing_bound_proves_reaped_net is a retrodiction of the phase before the reaping fix and is not evidence here.
- AC1 (the ranking re-checked before its bound is used; the Bound report line) is line 1 and lines 6 to 10 (no bound is used unless C accepts), with VER_019_nonvacuous (the queue-and-bundle ranking budget + s + 2*src accepted with the bound 5) and the report line ver019_boundLine, pinned below.
- AC2 (a violating run replayed and reported violated, confirmed) is line 10 and VER_019_violated_sound; VER_019_nonvacuous replays the run produce, produce, produce, cancel on the cancelled queue.
- AC3 (unsat at depth K is Proven with method bounded-model-check; the certificate line) is lines 2 and 8, with ver019_method and ver019_certLine pinned below. That the certificate check does not apply is the pipeline's: the hand-over of VER_019_order returns a decision, which ends the run before the certificate check step.
- AC4 (a net without a ranking, with the repeatable-vector line or its fallback, then the fixpoint query) is line 4, VER_019_ring_no_ranking (no weighting is accepted on the ring t0, t1, t2) and the report lines pinned below.
- AC5 (with the phase disabled, verdicts and reports are those of the pipeline without it) is VER_019_order line 5 with VER_019_order_disabled: the model here is the phase when it runs.
- The Encoding paragraph (the script's selectors, idle steps, the empty post-caps) is the constraint system BmcModel of Bmc.lean, whose exactness at the bound (bmc_exact_at_bound) VER_019_proven_sound uses; the SMT-LIB text and its goldens are VER-013's (P4). The measurements are not requirements. The test derivation is AC1 to AC4 as above, under the options it names (enumeration budget 0, VER-018 off, assumeAtomicFiring for the queue, the linear bound off for the ring), which the pipeline sets outside the model.
