**Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (A, Θ, W). A reads a TimedCheckInput: the option, the verdict and the route the pipeline reached, the verified timed net (after the rewrites of VER-006, VER-004 and EXEC-042, none of which changes timing or adds a match transition), whether it declares a match transition and the environment places still registered on it. Reference.TimedNet has no match transition and no environment place of its own, so both are fields of the input, as in VER-017. Under the Arrivals mode of VER-006 every runtime closes the net before any route and clears its environment places (with_arrivals in smt_verifier.rs, applyArrivals in SmtVerifier.java and in smt-verifier.ts), so the gate sees none and the check runs on the closed net; the environment places of AC5 are those registered under any other mode. The order of the reference is that of finish (smt_verifier.rs): UNTIMED_NET on an untimed net, TIMED_EXACT when Route B decided, UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION when the option is off or an environment place or a match transition is present, the check otherwise; the first three are VER-003's labels, which W leaves alone because A is false there.
- The statement constrains A, Θ and W one at a time. That the verifier hands W the gate's answer on its own result, and Θ's answer on the timed graph of the verified net, built by the graph layer's loop at the class-key explorer of the timed graph (Scg.scgE, the explorer of VER_023_graph) from the initial class Novel.TimedScg.initCls with the class budget of VER-017 and the stop oracle of VER-013, is the wiring the model assumes and does not state. The labels are (transition name, outcome row) as the timed graph's edges carry them (StateClassEdge); the trace W reports is their names. The flat timed net TNet of the graph is the verified net's image; that image (the Link of the verified net to TNet, with the [VER-001] outcome rows) is not stated here, as the on-time bridge of this wave (premise 9 of Novel/TimedScg/Succ.lean) is not proved. So the shall sentence of line 1, and AC7, speak of the verifier under that wiring: Lean checks A, Θ and W one at a time, not the call site in verify().
- Lines 2 to 6 read Θ over any explorer and any build of the graph layer's loop, the same loop and the same predicate Decide.violatesAt the enumeration route of VER-017 and Route B of VER-012 read ('decide the same property over its classes with the same shared predicate'; the sinks and conditional sinks of VER-014 are inside the property's predicate). Killed: a reading that ignores a stop (VER_023_forbids_readStopped), one that never confirms from a truncated prefix (VER_023_forbids_noPrefixHit), one that never answers SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING (VER_023_forbids_neverSpurious), one that answers SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING from a truncated prefix (VER_023_forbids_prefixSpurious, the markdown's 'SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING needs a closed graph and never comes from a prefix'), one that reports an empty path (VER_023_forbids_emptyPath), one that reports the last violating class instead of the first (VER_023_forbids_lastHit), and one that reports a longer path to the first (VER_023_forbids_longPath). 'Stopped' is the loop's stop flag, which the stop oracle cut sets (the total budget or a cancellation, VER-013) and which the model also sets when its fuel runs out, a bound no runtime has; the shall sentence names the first two.
- Line 6 asks for the first violating class in storage order and a shortest path to it, which the reference meets for every key-equivariant explorer (ver023_verdict_first, Graph.trace_spec); the timed class-key explorer is one (Scg.scgE_equivariant). Every runtime takes the first violating class: (0..view.count()).find in graph_decision.rs, firstWhere in GraphDecision.java and in graph-decision.ts. The markdown's 'the shortest path from the initial class to a violating class', shortest over every violating class, follows from line 6 because the build is breadth-first, so the first violating class stored is a nearest one; the breadth-first argument is proved at the identity explorer only (VER-017's ver017_build_bfs), so the line states the first class and the shortest path to it, not the minimum over every class. That the path is a run of the timed semantics ignoring priority (ruling D67 (a), VD-4) needs the exact half of the timed successor, which Lean does not prove (Novel/TimedScg.lean); it is a later line of this ID, not stated here. That it is an ordered firing sequence of the untimed abstraction, which VER-003's line 5 asks of a confirmed trace, needs the same Link to the verified net and is likewise not stated.
- Lines 7 to 11 are the annotation. 'Why it never changes a verdict' is lines 7 and 8: the verdict is the one the pipeline reached, so a check that turns Violated into Proven or Unknown is killed (VER_023_forbids_verdictChange); VER_023_keeps_timing derives that every result W returns after the gate meets VER-003's timing line. Ruling D20 (VD-5 (6), ver-d#7): the markdown's 'every other field is unchanged' is read as the verdict, the route and the invariants, since TIMED_CONFIRMED replaces the trace and sets counterexampleConfirmed (smt_verifier.rs assigns counterexample_trace, counterexample_transitions and counterexample_confirmed = Some(true)). Killed: a check that annotates when it did not run (VER_023_forbids_annotateOff), one that keeps the untimed trace on TIMED_CONFIRMED (VER_023_forbids_keepTrace), one that drops the untimed trace on SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING (VER_023_forbids_dropTrace), one that leaves a stopped check at UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION (VER_023_forbids_undecidedLabel), one that reports another route (VER_023_forbids_routeChange) and one that drops the P-invariants (VER_023_forbids_dropInvariants). The trace of markings beside the transitions (counterexample_trace in Rust) is the result record's shape, kind N.
- Ruling D22 (a): VER-023 is SHOULD, and its shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the check. 'Off by default' is the Options default (timedCheck := false), kind N. 'The check does not read or write a state-space cache' and 'It runs once, as a wrapper at the end of verify(), after every route has spoken' are the wiring above: W reads the result the pipeline reached, and the check builds its graph afresh rather than through VER-017's cache, whose graphs are untimed; neither is a line. The report text (that the trace came from the timed graph, the class count, the truncation at N classes, which stop ended the build, the plain statement that the counterexample is spurious under timing, and what the timed claim assumes, 'The report MUST also say what that timed claim assumes') is kind Q, as is the byte identity of the report with the option off.
- AC1 (the watchdog net: UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION with the check off, SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING with it on, the class count in the report) is lines 1, 4, 7 and 10 with the graph block; its timed graph is not evaluated in Lean (rational zone arithmetic does not reduce under decide, so no concrete timed graph is computed here), and the class count is report text, kind Q.
- AC2 (the watchdog at delayed(1): TIMED_CONFIRMED with the path start, watchdog) is lines 3, 6 and 9; the graph is not evaluated in Lean, as for AC1.
- AC3 (quiescence on the timed graph) is the graph block, line 1 of VER_023_graph: the class holding S with d at delayed(5) has a successor (VER_023_graph_nonvacuous); the second net (fast and slow on A) is not evaluated in Lean, as for AC1.
- AC4 (a class budget below the graph's size, and a total budget that runs out, give TIMED_UNDECIDED without a hit in the prefix; a hit in the prefix gives TIMED_CONFIRMED) is lines 2, 3 and 5, checked on the producer gen: G -> G, A at a budget of 6 at the identity explorer (VER_023_nonvacuous): placeBound(A, 2) is TIMED_CONFIRMED with the path gen, gen, gen, and deadlock freedom on the same truncated graph is TIMED_UNDECIDED. That the prefix path is gen, gen, gen and not the path to a later violating class (gen five times) is line 6 (VER_023_forbids_lastHit). The report naming the truncation is kind Q.
- AC5 (environment places registered under a mode other than Arrivals, or match transitions: the check does not run and the value is UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION; a Route B verdict on a timed net stays TIMED_EXACT; an untimed net stays UNTIMED_NET) is lines 1 and 7: refTimedGate is false on each (VER_023_nonvacuous), and the value is the one VER-003 gives: line 10 of VER-003 labels a timed Violated TIMED_EXACT when Route B decided it and UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION when another route decided it with the check off (VER_003_forbids_timedExactEnum, VER_003_forbids_routeBAbstraction).
- AC6 (the race t1: p -> a at window(3, 5), t2: p -> b at delayed(10): Violated, SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING, and the report says the timed claim assumes an on-time executor with atomic firings) is the graph block with VER_023_ac6: no run of the timed semantics marks b, while a late executor that reaps t1 does (Novel.TimedScg.reaping_escapes_timed_graph); the report line is kind Q.
- AC7 (no verdict differs between the check on and off) is lines 7 and 8.
- The worked example 'On the [VER-002] AC11 witness the check is TIMED_CONFIRMED with the empty trace' is lines 3 and 6 with the reap-aware predicate, checked on a stand-in graph at the identity explorer (VER_023_ac11: the class that enables only the reapable t rests and is reported with the empty path; with nothing reapable the same closed graph answers SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING); the timed graph of that net is not evaluated, as for AC1.
- The graph is priority-blind ('The graph is priority-blind', and the hi/lo example of TIMED_CONFIRMED): TNet has no priority and the reference successor expands every enabled clock, so a closed graph without a violating class speaks for every prioritized run too, since priority only removes runs.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✓ **The reference check meets VER-023.** Example: on a timed `Violated` decided by the SMT route, with the option on, no environment place and no match transition, the gate lets the check run; the reading answers `TIMED_CONFIRMED` with the shortest path of the built graph to the first violating class, `SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING` when the graph closed without one, and `TIMED_UNDECIDED` when it was truncated without one or stopped; the annotation then writes the label, replaces the trace only for `TIMED_CONFIRMED`, and never touches the verdict.
  <pre>∀ {K S Key : Type} [inst : DecidableEq Key],<br>  VER_023 refTimedGate refTimedOutcome refTimedAnnot</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_forbids_annotateOff` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **A check that does not run changes nothing** (line 7, AC5). Example: with the option off, the watchdog `Violated` keeps `UNTIMED_ABSTRACTION`; this annotation relabels it.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_forbids_dropTrace` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING keeps the untimed trace** (line 10, AC1). Example: the watchdog `Violated` keeps its trace `start, watchdog`, which is still a run of the untimed abstraction.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_forbids_emptyPath` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **The confirmed path leads to a violating class** (line 6).   <pre>¬VER_023 refTimedGate ver023_emptyPath refTimedAnnot</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_forbids_keepTrace` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **TIMED_CONFIRMED replaces the trace** (line 9, AC2). Example: an untimed counterexample `start, watchdog` and a timed graph whose path to the violating class is a different one, here the stand-in path `watchdog` alone; a result that still reports `start, watchdog` reports a path other than the one the timed graph found.
  <pre>¬VER_023 refTimedGate refTimedOutcome ver023_keepTrace</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_forbids_lastHit` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **The reported class is the first violating class** (line 6, AC4). **Assumptions**

- The model is the successor function σ of the timed graph, from the flat timed net (Novel.TimedScg.TNet: transitions with their outcome rows and static intervals) and the emptiness tolerance. The graph is the build loop of the graph layer (Decide.build) at the explorer that keys classes by Scg.idxKey and expands them by σ, from the initial class initCls in the canonical name order (Scg.coByName): the loop and the key are VER-017's and VER-010's subject, fixed here. The timed semantics is Novel.TimedScg.TStep (strong urgency, every firing atomic, the clock rule of TIME-012 by the graph's own survives), and 'an on-time run with atomic firings' is a TStep run; that the reference executor's on-time runs (OnTimeStep RefTStep, ruling D3) are TStep runs of the verified net's flat image is premise 9 of Novel/TimedScg/Succ.lean, the on-time bridge J7 of this wave, not proved here, so these lines are about TStep (design O4).
- The four assumptions the markdown names for SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING ('an on-time executor with atomic firings, one that reaps no transition, fires none after its latest bound, and gives an action no duration') are this TStep reading. Each is needed: a late executor that reaps escapes the graph (Novel.TimedScg.reaping_escapes_timed_graph, VER_023_ac6), and so does an action with a duration (Novel.TimedScg.action_duration_escapes). The pass recheck of EXEC-003 AC3, which takes a clock from a transition a same-pass deposit keeps enabled, is part of 'atomic firings' (ruling D20, ver-d#8).
- Line 1 is 'For the quiescence properties the predicate reads "this class has no successor" as "no transition can ever fire again"' and 'On a timed graph that MUST still hold: a class with an enabled transition has a successor whatever its interval'. It needs an exact emptiness test (Scg.ExactEps: eps = 0, or the Rust EPSILON = 1e-9 below the grid of whole-millisecond bounds, ruling VD-7) and an outcome row per transition (a transition with no output spec has one empty row, VER-001). The shall sentence names the first as its While clause (every finite bound a whole number of milliseconds, the grid of step 1); Lean also covers eps = 0 for any bounds. Well-formed intervals and a row per transition hold of every net a runtime accepts (TIME-001's validity table rejects a latest bound below the earliest), so the sentence does not name them. A graph that drops the successors of a class whose enabled transition has no upper bound reports a timed deadlock the net does not have, and is killed (VER_023_graph_forbids_dropUnbounded, on the net S -> d -> X of AC3).
- Lines 2 and 3 are SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING's meaning ('The property holds under timing', 'SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING there means that no on-time run reaches a violating rest'): with lines 3 to 5 of VER_023, an answer SPURIOUS_UNDER_TIMING comes only from a closed, unstopped graph with no violating class (VER_023_spurious_sound). The quiescence predicate is VER-002's reap-aware one ('on a net with a reapable transition, also treats a class whose enabled transitions are all reapable as resting'), with the reapable set over transition names (TIME-013; empty under assumeNoReaping), and the class test is Decide.quiescentAt, which reads the labels of the class's successors. A graph that stops expanding after the initial class (VER_023_graph_forbids_noSuccessors) and one that adds a step out of a dead class (VER_023_graph_forbids_deadLoop) are killed.
- Out of scope: the exact half of the successor (every class is realised by a timed run), which TIMED_CONFIRMED's 'a run of the timed semantics ignoring priority' needs (ruling D67 (a), a later line of this ID); environment places and match transitions, which the gate of VER_023 excludes (premise 8 of Succ.lean); and fractional millisecond bounds, which TypeScript accepts (ruling D58).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_graph_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✓ **The reference timed graph meets VER-023's graph lines.** Example: on the net `S → d → X` with `d` at `delayed(5)`, the class holding `S` has the successor that fires `d`; on a closed graph without a violating class, every timed run stays in classes of the graph (`Scg.timed_run_stored`), so it never reaches a violating marking, nor a violating rest.
  <pre>VER_023_graph refTimedSucc</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_023_graph_forbids_deadLoop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_023): ✗ **A closed graph holds every resting run** (line 3). Example: on the net with no transition and a token on place 0, the initial marking is dead and strands that token; a graph that lets the dead class step to itself finds no resting class, so it would call deadlock freedom spurious under timing.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_024"></a>
## VER-024: Stubborn-Set Reduction of the Enumeration Route

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_024` · Kind **B** · Scope the enumeration route of VER-017 on a quiescence property, all implementations (SHOULD; the shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the reduction) · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 48e64fd98bd49532 ai** · Statement hash `48e64fd98bd49532`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the route expands a class, it *shall* expand only enabled transitions, each with all of its outcomes.<br><br>*While* the reduction applies, every dead marking reachable from the initial marking *shall* be reachable by a run that fires, at each class, one of the transitions the route expands there.<br><br>*While* the reduction applies, a class *shall* have no reduced successor exactly when no transition is enabled at its marking. | 1. For every net and marking, every transition the selection Sel picks is a transition of the net enabled at the marking.<br>2. For every net whose transitions each have at least one outcome, and all markings a0 and d: if d is reachable from a0 in the net (ReachAD over every outcome of every transition) and no transition is enabled at d, then d is reachable from a0 by reduced steps (StepSel: fire an enabled transition Sel picks at the current marking, with any of its outcomes).<br>3. For every net whose transitions each have at least one outcome, and every marking a: a has no reduced successor iff no transition is enabled at a. | <pre>fun Sel ↦<br>  (∀ (net : Ver024.SNet) (a : AMarking), ∀ i ∈ Sel net a, Ver024.enAt net a i = true) ∧<br>    (∀ (net : Ver024.SNet),<br>        Ver024.Outcomes net →<br>          ∀ (a0 d : AMarking),<br>            Novel.ForwardDeposit.ReachAD (Ver024.rowsOf net) a0 d →<br>              Ver024.DeadT net d → Relation.ReflTransGen (Ver024.StepSel Sel net) a0 d) ∧<br>      ∀ (net : Ver024.SNet),<br>        Ver024.Outcomes net →<br>          ∀ (a : AMarking),<br>            (∀ (b : AMarking), ¬Ver024.StepSel Sel net a b) ↔ Ver024.DeadT net a</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the untimed atomic abstraction of the net the graph is built on (VER-004), as rows of Novel/Stubborn.lean: a transition with all of its outcomes (TEntry), each outcome a deposit list, firing by fireAD and enabling by enabledA. The net is the one after the inert places of VER-001, the in-flight split of VER-004 and the terminal rewrites of EXEC-042; those rewrites are their own requirements. The conditions under which the reduction applies are VER_024_route below; ν-joins, environment places, timing and drained forwards (IO-014) are outside the model, as the first and third of those conditions exclude them. A drained forward's deposit depends on the marking, which a deposit list cannot express.
- With all of its outcomes is the reduced step itself, not a line: StepSel fires a selected transition with each of its outcomes (rowsAt), so a selection names transitions, never single outcomes, and no selection can break that half of the first quoted sentence. The row-level closure of Novel/Stubborn.lean can hold one outcome of an input-less transition without the other (rowLevel_drops_an_outcome in the ver-c check); the transition-level selection here cannot.
- Line 2 starts from any marking a0, which covers the initial marking of the second quoted sentence. A run that fires, at each class, one of the transitions the route expands there is a run of StepSel.
- Classes are markings: the class key of an untimed graph is its marking (VER-017). The lines are stated on the reduced step relation, so they hold for the graph at every class budget. On a closed reduced graph the quiescent classes are exactly the reachable dead markings, so a property read off the quiescent classes is decided exactly (VER_024_exact, from the statement alone). That a violated is a real firing sequence, shortest in the reduced graph, and that a truncated reduced graph is read as in VER-017, are VER-017's lines over the reduced successor function; reduced steps are steps of the net, whatever the selection (VER_024_steps_sound).
- Ruling D22 (a): VER-024 is SHOULD, and its shall sentences bind an implementation that offers the reduction. Transition names are unique (rulings D10 and D23); place ids follow the code-point order of place names (the flattener's order, VER-013); no place carries both an input and a read arc of one transition (ruling D15, EXEC-012).
- AC1 (verdict with and without the reduction equal on the conformance corpus, every violated trace replays) is the corpus test, kind Q; lines 2 and 3 are the reason it holds (VER_024_exact).
- AC2 (k independent cycles of length n: at most 1 + k·n classes reduced, 1 + n^k full, the same verdict) is a corpus test over every k and n, kind Q; it is not proven for all k and n. VER_024_ac2 is one worked instance (k = 2, n = 3: 4 classes reduced, 10 full), and VER_024_nonvacuous the chain variant of the test derivation.
- AC3 (a safety property builds the full graph) and AC4 (partialOrderReduction(false) gives the graph of VER-017) are VER_024_route, line 1.
- AC5 (the same class count in every implementation) is VER_024_select: the selection, with its order, is a function of the net and the marking (VER_024_select_unique_list), so the reduced graph is.
- AC6 (the report line Stubborn-set reduction (VER-024): on) is report text, kind Q. The default (on) is a quoted sentence of VER_024_route, kind N (ver024_defaultOn); the option names of the Implementation notes are kind N.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✓ **The reference selection keeps every dead marking.** Example: on a net that forks one token into two independent subnets, `refSel` expands one subnet at a time, yet every marking where nothing is enabled is still reached: the transitions it picks form a stubborn set (`refStub_family`, through the bridge `closedT_stubborn`), and a stubborn family keeps every reachable dead marking (`stubborn_preserves_dead`) and stops exactly at the dead ones (`reducedQuiescent_iff_dead`).
  <pre>VER_024 Ver024.refSel</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_forbids_noD2` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **Without S-D2 a dead marking is lost** (line 2). Example: from tokens on 0 and 1, `t` is disabled but shares place 0 with `s`. Without S-D2 the closures of `s` and of `u` each hold one enabled transition, the name `s` wins, and `s` fires first, which disables `t` for good. The dead marking with one token on place 4 (`u`, then `t`) is lost. S-D2 puts `u`, which can increase `t`'s missing place 2, into the set of `s`.
  <pre>¬VER_024 ver024_noD2</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_forbids_noOverwrites` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **Without the overwrite clauses a dead marking is lost** (line 2). Example: `t` clears place 2 and `u` fills it; neither tests a place the other writes, so a dependency without the overwrite clauses calls them independent. The name `t` wins the tie and `t` fires first, so the run ends with one token on place 2; the dead marking with place 2 empty (`u`, then `t`) is lost.
  <pre>¬VER_024 ver024_noOverwrites</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_forbids_nothing` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **A class with an enabled transition has a successor** (line 3). Example: `t` has no arcs, so it is enabled at the empty marking; a selection that expands nothing leaves that class without a successor, and the route would report a deadlock that does not exist.
  <pre>¬VER_024 ver024_nothing</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_forbids_seedOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **Expanding only the seed loses a dead marking** (line 2). Example: `a` and `b` compete for one token. Expanding `a` alone reaches only the dead marking with a token on place 1; the dead marking with a token on place 2, which `b` reaches, is lost. S-D1 puts `b` into the set, since the two share their input place.
  <pre>¬VER_024 ver024_seedOnly</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_forbids_withDisabled` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **Only enabled transitions are picked** (line 1). Example: with place 0 empty, `t` is disabled; a selection that also lists it names a transition the route cannot expand. Its steps are the reference's, so only line 1 tells it apart.
  <pre>¬VER_024 ver024_withDisabled</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✓ **The reduction is real and keeps the dead marking.** Example: after `fork`, both `a` and `b` are enabled, but each closure holds one enabled transition, and the name `a` wins the tie, so the reference expands only `a` there. The marking with tokens on 2 and 4, where nothing is enabled, is still reached by the reduced steps: `fork`, then `a`, then `b`.
  <pre>Ver024.Outcomes ver024Chain ∧<br>  Novel.ForwardDeposit.ReachAD (Ver024.rowsOf ver024Chain) (Ver024.mkM [1, 0, 0, 0, 0])<br>      (Ver024.mkM [0, 0, 1, 0, 1]) ∧<br>    Ver024.DeadT ver024Chain (Ver024.mkM [0, 0, 1, 0, 1]) ∧<br>      Ver024.refSel ver024Chain (Ver024.mkM [0, 1, 0, 1, 0]) = [1] ∧<br>        Relation.ReflTransGen (Ver024.StepSel Ver024.refSel ver024Chain)<br>          (Ver024.mkM [1, 0, 0, 0, 0]) (Ver024.mkM [0, 0, 1, 0, 1])</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_024_route"></a>
## VER-024: Stubborn-Set Reduction: when it applies, and the cache key

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_route` · Kind **F** · Scope the enumeration route of VER-017 and its state-space cache, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 60a35bb2a87a4c8b ai** · Statement hash `60a35bb2a87a4c8b`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the enumeration route of [VER-017] runs on a quiescence property (`deadlockFree`, `terminatesAtSink`, `joinedOrDeadLettered` or `quiescentCount`), on a net without a drained forward ([IO-014]), with the reduction enabled, the route *shall* build the reduced graph.<br><br>*If* the property is not a quiescence property, the net has a drained forward or the reduction is disabled, *then* the route *shall* build the full graph of [VER-017].<br><br>Every implementation *shall* turn the reduction on by default.<br><br>The cache of [VER-017] *shall* key a reduced graph apart from the full graph of the same net and initial marking, so that a safety query, and a quiescence query with the reduction off, never read a reduced entry. | 1. For every property, option value and drained-forward flag: U builds the reduced graph iff the property is a quiescence property (DeadlockFree, TerminatesAtSink or QuiescentCount), the option is on and the net has no drained forward.<br>2. For every net, in-flight split, initial marking, property, option value and drained-forward flag, the reduced field of the cache key is the bit U gives. | <pre>fun {K N M} U key ↦<br>  (∀ (φ : VerProp K) (opt dr : Bool),<br>      U φ opt dr = true ↔ quiescenceProp φ = true ∧ opt = true ∧ dr = false) ∧<br>    ∀ (net : N) (split : List String) (m0 : M) (φ : VerProp K) (opt dr : Bool),<br>      (key net split m0 φ opt dr).reduced = U φ opt dr</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Condition 1 (the enumeration route runs: no ν-join, no environment place, untimed, a positive class budget) is VER-017's applicability; the decision U is read only when the route runs.
- JoinedOrDeadLettered (NU-055) is not a VerProp of VER-002, so line 1 does not range over it. The runtimes count it as a quiescence property and reduce for it (stubborn_enumeration, smt_verifier.rs:593-602), and the route meets it on a net without ν-joins (smt_verifier.rs:7265-7343 runs it on such nets with the route turned off explicitly). It reads only the classes without successors, so the reduced graph decides it as it decides the three others (VER_024_exact). That the first two quoted sentences hold for it is a corpus test, kind Q.
- The third quoted sentence (on by default) is configuration, kind N: the constant ver024_defaultOn, pinned below. All four runtimes default to on (smt_verifier.rs:253, SmtVerifier.java:189, smt-verifier.ts:166, Python verify(..., partial_order_reduction=True)); that they default alike is checked by the verdict-parity fixtures. The option names are kind N (Implementation notes).
- The cache is VER-017's sequential state machine (Verifier.Graph.cacheQuery): a query reads and writes only the entry of its own key (cacheQuery_frame). With the reduced bit in the key, a safety query and a quiescence query with the reduction off use keys whose bit is false, so they never read or write an entry whose bit is true (VER_024_route_apart, from the statement alone). Line 2 pins only the reduced field: which other fields the key has (the net or its structural fingerprint, the split, the initial marking) and the reuse rules are VER-017's cache block.
- AC3 (a safety property builds the full graph whatever the setting) and AC4 (with partialOrderReduction(false), VER-017's graph, witness and class count) are line 1 with the property or the option set; that the full graph is VER-017's is VER-017's subject.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-VER_024_select"></a>
## VER-024: Stubborn-Set Reduction: the pinned stubborn set

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select` · Kind **F** · Scope the stubborn set the enumeration route expands at each class, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-13 2b7d225579be0e67 ai** · Statement hash `2b7d225579be0e67`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* the reduction applies, *when* the route expands a class whose marking `M` enables a transition, it *shall* expand exactly the enabled transitions of `S(s)` for the enabled seed `s` whose closure has the fewest enabled transitions, the code-point-smallest seed name breaking ties.<br><br>*When* a transition `t` of `S(s)` is disabled at `M`, the closure *shall* read its first unsatisfied condition over its input and read places in code-point order of place name, then over its inhibitor places in code-point order.<br><br>*While* the reduction applies, the route *shall* expand the transitions it selects at a class in ascending code-point order of transition name. | 1. For every net whose transition names are distinct and every marking: every transition Sel picks is enabled.<br>2. If some transition is enabled, there is an enabled seed s0 such that: Sel picks exactly the enabled transitions i in S(s0) (InClosure: i is in every set that contains s0 and is closed under S-D1 and S-D2, with S-D2 reading the first unsatisfied condition in the pinned order, firstUnsat over conds);<br>3. no enabled seed has fewer enabled transitions in its closure than s0 (enabledCount);<br>4. every enabled seed with as many enabled transitions in its closure as s0 has a name no smaller than s0's (String order, which is code-point order).<br>5. Sel lists the transitions it picks in strictly ascending order of name, the order in which the route expands them. | <pre>fun Sel ↦<br>  ∀ (net : Ver024.SNet) (a : AMarking),<br>    (List.map (fun e ↦ e.1.name) net).Nodup →<br>      (∀ i ∈ Sel net a, Ver024.enAt net a i = true) ∧<br>        ((∃ s, Ver024.enAt net a s = true) →<br>            ∃ s0,<br>              Ver024.enAt net a s0 = true ∧<br>                (∀ (i : ℕ),<br>                    i ∈ Sel net a ↔<br>                      Ver024.enAt net a i = true ∧ Ver024.InClosure net a s0 i) ∧<br>                  (∀ (s : ℕ),<br>                      Ver024.enAt net a s = true →<br>                        Ver024.enabledCount net a s0 ≤ Ver024.enabledCount net a s) ∧<br>                    ∀ (s : ℕ),<br>                      Ver024.enAt net a s = true →<br>                        Ver024.enabledCount net a s = Ver024.enabledCount net a s0 →<br>                          Ver024.nameAt net s0 ≤ Ver024.nameAt net s) ∧<br>          List.Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Ver024.nameAt net i &lt; Ver024.nameAt net j) (Sel net a)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The closure is stated as the spec defines it, the least set containing the seed and closed under the two rules (InClosure over ClosedT); refSel computes it by rounds from the seed (closureWith reqT), and inClosure_iff shows the two agree. Dependency, the increasers and the decreasers are those of the Footprints paragraph over all outcomes of a transition (testsT, writesT, overwritesT, dependentT, increasesT, decreasesT). S-D1 for t = u adds nothing, as t is already in the set, so the closedness rule does not exclude it.
- The order of conditions is a function (conds): input and read places together, sorted by place id, then inhibitor places sorted by place id. Place ids follow the code-point order of place names (the flattener's order, VER-013), so the sort is the code-point order of the spec; that link from names to ids is an assumption about the flattener, not a line, and the runtimes sort by name directly. No place carries both an input and a read of one transition (ruling D15), so the merged order has no tie; two input specs on one place are excluded by the builders. The runtimes build the same list (stubborn_sets.rs:66-88, StubbornSets.java:59-78, stubborn-sets.ts:59-76). Three wrong orders are killed: Novel/Stubborn.lean's firstBlocker order, inputs then reads (VER_024_select_forbids_inputsFirst); the merged list in descending place order (VER_024_select_forbids_descending); inhibitors before inputs and reads (VER_024_select_forbids_inhibitorsFirst).
- Transition names are distinct (rulings D10 and D23), a premise of every line: with two equal names the tie-break does not single out one seed, and the runtimes index transitions by name. The runtimes' early cut (a closure stops counting once it reaches the best count so far) and their stop at a count of 1 change no choice, so they are not in the model.
- Line 5 is the expansion order. A class keeps its enabled transitions in the canonical clock order of VER-010 AC1, ascending by name in code-point order; the breadth-first build iterates that list and the selection only filters it (state_class_graph.rs:193, StateClassGraph.java:580, state-class-graph.ts:166). With lines 2 to 4 it fixes the list of transitions a class expands, so with the order of each transition's outcomes (the net's, VER-021) it fixes the reduced graph, the order in which its classes are found, and which classes a truncated build expands (AC5; the order mutant is killed by VER_024_select_forbids_netOrder).

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✓ **The reference makes the pinned choice.** Example: after `fork` in the chain net, the closures of `a` and of `b` each hold one enabled transition; `refSel` takes the seed `a`, the smaller name, and expands `a` alone. It takes the seed with the least key (count of enabled members, then name) over the enabled transitions (`List.argmin`), and its closure is the least closed set (`inClosure_iff`).
  <pre>VER_024_select Ver024.refSel</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_byIndex` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The smallest name breaks a tie, not the net order** (line 4). Example: `b` and `a` are independent and each closure holds one enabled transition; the route expands `a`, the smaller name, although `b` comes first in the net.
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_byIndex</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_descending` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The merged conditions are read in ascending place order** (line 2, S-D2's order). Example: on the net of the previous example `t` lacks its places 0 and 1 and has place 2. Read from the largest place down, the first missing place is 1, so the closure of `u1` holds one enabled transition and the route would expand `u1` instead of `u0`.
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_descending</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_inhibitorsFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **Inputs and reads come before inhibitors** (line 2, S-D2's order). Example: with tokens on places 0 and 2, `t` lacks its input place 1 and its inhibitor place 0 is marked. Read in the pinned order, the first unsatisfied condition is place 1, which `s` fills, so the closure of `s` holds `s` and `t` and one enabled transition: the route expands `s`. Read inhibitors first, it is place 0, which `d` empties, so the closure of `d` wins instead and the route would expand `d`.
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_inhibitorsFirst</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_inputsFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The first unsatisfied condition merges inputs and reads by place** (line 2, S-D2's order). Example: `t` lacks its read place 0 and its input place 1. In place order the first is place 0, so S-D2 puts `u0` into a closure holding `t`, and the closure of `u0` holds one enabled transition: the route expands `u0`. Reading inputs before reads blames place 1 instead and expands `u1`, a different reduced graph.
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_inputsFirst</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_most` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The fewest enabled members win** (line 3). Example: the closures of `a` and `b` hold both of them, the closure of `c` holds `c` alone; the route expands `c` only, where a choice of the largest closure expands `a` and `b`.
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_most</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_netOrder` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The route expands the picked transitions in order of name** (line 5). Example: `b` and `a` compete for one token, so both are expanded at the first class. In net order the route would fire `b` first and find its successor first; in name order it fires `a` first, so the two builds find their classes in a different order (`VER_024_select_netOrder_graph`).
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_netOrder</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_024_select_forbids_seedOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_024): ✗ **The whole closure is expanded, not the seed alone** (line 2). Example: `a` and `b` compete for one token, so S-D1 puts both into one closure and the route expands both; expanding the seed `a` alone is a different, and unsound, reduced graph (`VER_024_forbids_seedOnly`).
  <pre>¬VER_024_select ver024_seedOnly</pre>

## VER-025: Bounded Witness Phase

`Libpetri.Spec.VER_025` · Kind **B** · Scope the SMT verifier, all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/07-verification.md) · Sign-off **2026-11-10 104625b4eefcf18b** · Statement hash `104625b4eefcf18b`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

| *If* the pipeline reaches the flat fixpoint query, the witness depth `D` is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, *then* the verifier *shall* run the phase directly before the fixpoint script is encoded.<br><br>*While* the fixpoint query takes the name-coloured encoding ([NU-053]), the verifier *shall not* run the phase.<br><br>*If* the net has match transitions and either the property is not a reachability-safety property or no budget place is declared, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase.<br><br>*If* the witness depth is 0, *then* the verifier *shall not* run the phase, and its verdict, route, report and scripts *shall* be those of the pipeline without the phase.<br><br>*When* the verifier does not run the phase, it *shall* send no query for it and print no report line for it.<br><br>*While* environment places are registered under `Ignore`, the phase *shall* run where it runs on any other flat net, with no injection step.<br><br>*While* the counterexample replay of [VER-003] is disabled, the phase *shall* run where it runs with the replay enabled, and a run it reports *shall* still be confirmed.<br><br>*If* the property is a name-alignment property ([NU-055]), *then* the phase *shall* send no query and *shall* end inconclusive with the reason of [NU-055] that the property is decided only by the name-partition state-class graph.<br><br>*When* the phase runs, the verifier *shall* send this script, and every implementation *shall* emit it byte for byte the same for the same net, initial marking, property and options.<br><br>*If* `J` is 0, *then* the script *shall* be byte-identical to the bounded run of [VER-019] at the same depth.<br><br>*When* the solver answers `sat`, the phase *shall* read the run from the model's selectors in step order up to the first idle step, taking a value in `[0, T)` as a transition step, a value in `[T, T + J)` as an injection step, and any other value, or a selector the model leaves undefined, as idle, and *shall* read no run from a model that defines no selector.<br><br>*When* the phase replays a run, it *shall* fire each transition step under the exact abstract semantics with the environment post-caps, take each injection step only while its guard holds, and accept the run only when every step is enabled and the last marking violates the property.<br><br>*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* trim it: it *shall* first cut the run to its violating prefix, then try the steps from the last to the first, replace the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step whenever one exists, and repeat such passes until one changes nothing.<br><br>*When* the phase reports a run, it *shall* report the trimmed run, replayed, with each transition step labelled by its transition's name and each injection step by `inject(&lt;place>)`.<br><br>*When* the phase starts, it *shall* start a wall-clock budget of `max(1, floor(timeout_ms / 8))` milliseconds before it encodes the script, and the query *shall* receive what is left of it.<br><br>*When* the phase runs, the report *shall* carry the line `  Bounded witness phase (VER-025):` followed by exactly one of the status lines below.<br><br>*When* a run replays, the phase *shall* return `Violated` with the trimmed run as the counterexample, `counterexampleConfirmed` `true` and the route of the SMT pipeline ([VER-003]), and the result *shall* continue as the witness result of [VER-018] and [VER-019] does.<br><br>*When* the phase returns `Violated` on a net with match transitions, the result *shall* pass the ν guard of [NU-050] as a name-blind verdict and carry the guard's note that the counterexample may be spurious.<br><br>*When* the phase returns `Violated`, the counterexample-timing step of [VER-023] *shall* apply to the result as to every result of the pipeline.<br><br>*If* the solver answers `unsat`, *then* the phase *shall* report that no run of at most `D` steps reaches a violation, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.<br><br>*If* the query fails in the transport, the solver answers `unknown`, the phase budget is spent or the run does not replay, *then* the phase *shall* report itself inconclusive with its reason, and the pipeline *shall* continue to the fixpoint query.<br><br>The phase *shall not* report `Proven`, and *shall not* read an `unsat` answer as a proof.<br><br>*If* the phase ends without a run, *then* the pipeline *shall* continue as it does without the phase, and the phase *shall* change no verdict except through the time it spends against the total budget of [VER-013].<br><br>The witness depth *shall* default to 8 in every implementation.<br><br>*When* the caller sets the witness depth to a positive `n`, the phase *shall* ask one query at depth `n`.<br><br>*If* the caller sets a negative witness depth, *then* setting it *shall* fail with the argument error `witnessDepth must be non-negative, got &lt;n>`.<br><br>*When* `LIBPETRI_SMT_DUMP` is set, the verifier *shall* keep the phase's script and reply under the phase name `witness` ([VER-013]).<br><br>*When* the scripts are encoded without a solver ([VER-013] AC1), the result *shall* carry as its `witness` member the script `verify()` sends when it reaches the phase, present exactly when the encoding is flat, the witness depth is positive, and the net has no match transitions or the property is a reachability-safety property with a budget place declared, **Assumptions**

- The model is the triple (S, W, P) of ScriptRel, PhaseFn and PipelineFn. S is the script read as a constraint system (P4 of Novel/FiringBound.lean: the SMT-LIB text the ports emit denotes BmcModelEnv, and the solver's sat and unsat are correct). W is the phase from the depth D, the entry gate enter, the name-alignment flag, the flat net as deposit rows (Row = transition and deposit, the exact abstract semantics of VER-004: enabledA, fireAD), the injection list (Inj = flat place index and bound, none under AlwaysAvailable), the seed, the violation isBad and the solver's answer (Witness.Answer: sat with the selector values the model defines, none for a selector it is silent on; unsat; unknown; a transport failure; a spent phase budget). P is the pipeline from the phase outcome, the time spent, the total budget and the fixpoint route as a function of the budget left. The witness triple is ver025_script (BmcModelEnv), witnessPhase and pipeline (Novel/FiringBound/Witness.lean).
- The entry gate of the first three quoted sentences is the input enter: the pipeline reached the flat fixpoint query, the fixpoint query does not take the name-coloured encoding (NU-053), and the net has no match transitions or the property is reachability-safety with a budget place declared. Which nets and properties open it is decided by the pipeline outside the model (VER-001, NU-050), so the sentences are encoded as line 3: the phase runs exactly when enter is true and D is positive. 'Directly before the fixpoint script is encoded' is the order of P: the phase's outcome is decided before the fixpoint route is called (lines 8 to 10).
- The fourth quoted sentence is line 3 at D = 0 and line 10: the phase does not run and the verdict is the fixpoint route's at the whole budget. Its 'route, report and scripts' are not in the model: the route is the fixpoint route's by line 10, the report has no phase line (ver025_report none = [], pinned below), and the scripts of encodeScripts() are outside it.
- The fifth quoted sentence is line 3 and ver025_report none = [] (no report line). 'Send no query' is not expressible: the solver's answer is an input of W, so the model cannot see whether a query was sent; a W that does not run (none) uses no answer. The same holds for 'send no query' in the eighth quoted sentence, whose outcome line 4 fixes for every answer, so the outcome does not depend on one.
- The sixth quoted sentence (Ignore) is the injection list []: under Ignore the verifier builds no injection, and lines 3 to 7 hold at every injection list, [] included, so the phase runs where it runs on any other flat net. At [] the step relation is the firing relation of VER-019 (replayEnv_nil, bmcModelEnv_nil). The Arrivals rewrite produces a closed net, which is again the case injs = [].
- The seventh quoted sentence (the VER-003 replay disabled) is not an input of the model: lines 5 and 6 require the phase's own replay whatever the option, so a run W reports is a replayed one (VER_025_reported_run). counterexampleConfirmed is not in the model; that a run W reports is replayed is VER_025_reported_run.
- The ninth and tenth quoted sentences are about the SMT-LIB text (byte identity across implementations; J = 0 byte-identical to VER-019). The text is not modelled (P4); the scripts are checked by the golden-file parity tests of VER-013. What the model states is the constraint system: lines 1 and 2, and at J = 0 BmcModelEnv is VER-019's BmcModel (bmcModelEnv_nil, cited for VER-025).
- The eleventh quoted sentence (decode) is decodeModel at T + J in lines 5 and 6, and decodeRust in line 2: values in [0, T) are transition steps (rows), values in [T, T + J) injection steps, anything else ends the run, a selector the model leaves undefined (none) is read as idle, and a model that defines none of the selectors below D yields no run, which line 6 makes inconclusive (did not replay), as decode_bounded_run returning None does. Line 2 reads a model of S, which defines every selector (Witness.defined; decodeModel_defined).
- The twelfth quoted sentence (replay) is replays (replayEnv followed by the property) in lines 1, 2, 5 and 6: a transition step fires a row that is enabled (enabledA) and whose successor passes the post-caps (capsOk), an injection step is taken only while its guard holds (injOk: below the bound under Bounded(k), always under AlwaysAvailable) and has no post-cap, and the run is accepted only when every step is taken and the last marking violates (stepIdx, Bmc.lean). That this is the step relation of the HORN rules is stepEnv_injsOf (StepEnv at the verifier's injection list is EnvSemantics.StepAE), cited for VER-025; that a replayed run is a derivation in the strengthened CHC system is witness_horn_derivation.
- The thirteenth quoted sentence (trim) is line 5: the reported run is trim of the decoded run, the reference trim of Witness.lean (violatingPrefix: the shortest prefix that replays to a violating marking, the empty one included; then passes from the last index to the first, each replacing the run by the violating prefix of the run without that step when one exists, repeated until a pass changes nothing). The algorithm is part of the statement, so the run is fixed for a model and a trim in another order is told apart (VER_025_forbids_trimFirst), as is one without the cut (VER_025_forbids_noCut). What follows, from the statement alone (VER_025_reported_run, VER_025_initial_violation): the reported run is a sublist of the decoded run, replays, ends at the first violating marking it reaches, has no single step that can be dropped, and is the empty run when M0 violates. The trimmed run is not claimed to be a shortest run.
- The fourteenth and seventeenth quoted sentences are line 5 (the reported run is the trimmed run, replayed) and line 8 (the result is Violated with that run). The labels (a transition's name, inject(<place>)) are the pure function ver025_stepLabel, pinned below. counterexampleConfirmed true, the route of the SMT pipeline and the result text of VER-018 and VER-019 (RESULT, VIOLATED, the trace, the Firing sequence line, the untimed warning) are outside the model.
- The fifteenth quoted sentence (budget) is the pure function ver025_budgetMs, pinned below. The wall clock, the transport's clamp and 'the query shall receive what is left of it' are not modelled: elapsed is any number the phase spent, line 9 charges it against the total budget, and a spent phase budget is the answer budgetSpent (line 7).
- The sixteenth quoted sentence and the status lines are the pure functions ver025_header, ver025_status and ver025_report, pinned below: ver025_report gives no line when the phase does not run and the header and exactly one status line when it does. The reasons are ver025_reasonText; the transport's failure message (a reply with an (error ...) line included, which is the answer failure) and the NU-055 reason are parameters, since the spec does not fix their text in VER-025.
- The eighteenth quoted sentence (the ν guard of NU-050) and the nineteenth (the counterexample-timing step of VER-023) are steps the result passes through after the pipeline of this model; neither is modelled. The model's Violated is the phase's result before them.
- The twentieth to twenty-third quoted sentences are lines 6, 7, 9 and 10: unsat gives 'no run' and every other ending without a run gives inconclusive with its reason (lines 6, 7), and the pipeline then hands over to the fixpoint route at the total budget minus the time the phase spent (line 9), so the phase changes no verdict except through that time. The pipeline answers Proven only through the fixpoint route (VER_025_never_proven, from lines 8 to 10; Witness.Outcome has no proven outcome at all). 'Shall not read an unsat answer as a proof' is lines 7 and 9 together: unsat gives 'no run', after which the verdict is the fixpoint route's (VER_025_forbids_unsatProven). What 'no run' means is line 1 under P4: no run of at most D steps reaches a violation (VER_025_noRun_exact below, from the statement). It says nothing about D + 1 steps.
- The twenty-fourth and twenty-sixth quoted sentences (default 8, the negative-depth error) are the pure functions ver025_depthDefault and ver025_depthError, pinned below. The twenty-fifth (a positive n asks one query at depth n) is the depth argument D of W, at which lines 5 and 6 decode; that one query is sent is not modelled, as for 'send no query'.
- The twenty-seventh quoted sentence (the dump phase name witness) is the constant ver025_dumpPhase, pinned below; the dump itself is not modelled. The twenty-eighth (encodeScripts' witness member) is about the scripts, which are not modelled (P4).
- AC1 (envBoundedPair: t takes one(e) to p1, e under Bounded(2), empty M0, PlaceBound(p1, 1)) is VER_025_nonvacuous: at depth 8, a padded model's run of 5 steps is trimmed to a run of 4 steps, two inject(e) and two t, that replays and is irredundant, its status line is 'a run of 4 steps reaches a violation (replayed; depth 8)', and the pipeline answers Violated without the fixpoint route (no fixpoint query). 'Confirmed' is outside the model (seventh quoted sentence).
- AC2 (the same net, PlaceBound(p1, 4), shortest run 10 steps) is VER_025_ac2: at depth 10 a model gives a reported run of 10 steps; at depth 8 the answer unsat gives 'no run' (line 7), its status line is pinned, and the pipeline then answers what the fixpoint route answers at the budget left (line 9). That the depth-8 script is in fact unsat is the solver's answer under P4 (line 1 says what it means); it is not re-derived here by enumerating runs.
- AC3 (depth 0 off) is line 3 and line 10, and ver025_report none = []; the encoded scripts and the dump are outside the model.
- AC4 (the name-coloured encoding) and AC5 (the ν gates) are the entry gate enter of line 3, which the pipeline sets outside the model. AC5's ν guard note is the eighteenth quoted sentence, not modelled.
- AC6 (name alignment) is line 4.
- AC7 (the stub replies unsat, unknown, a transport failure, a spent budget, a sat model whose run does not replay: each its own status line, then the fixpoint query, never Proven) is lines 6, 7 and 9, VER_025_never_proven and the status lines pinned below.
- AC8 (selector range: T + j decodes as injection j, T + J or more or a negative selector ends the run) is decodeRust and decodeModel in lines 2, 5 and 6, pinned on examples below (VER_025_ac8), with an undefined selector read as idle and a model with no selector read as no run.
- AC9 (injection replay: an injection at a place holding its bound does not replay, an unbounded one always does, its label is inject(<place>), no post-cap) is the reference replay of lines 5 and 6, pinned on examples below (VER_025_ac9), and ver025_stepLabel.
- AC10 (trim: a padded model is reported as a run of 4 steps; dropping any single step of a reported run makes it fail to replay) is line 5 with VER_025_reported_run, and VER_025_nonvacuous.
- AC11 (M0 violates: a run of 0 steps) is VER_025_initial_violation (from the statement: a reported run is [] whenever M0 violates, whatever model the solver returned) and VER_025_ac11: an all-idle model, and a model on the ring t1: p0 to p1, t2: p1 to p0 that leaves M0 and comes back to a violating marking, are both reported as the run []; a run that passes a violating marking and goes on is reported cut there; its status line is 'a run of 0 steps'. The enumeration route and VER-018/019 being off is the entry gate.
- AC12 (the replay option off) is the seventh quoted sentence: lines 5 and 6 hold whatever the option.
- AC13 (Ignore) is the sixth quoted sentence: the injection list is [].
- AC14 (scripts: J = 0 byte-identical to VER-019, golden witness.smt2, dump file names) is about the SMT-LIB text and the dump, outside the model (P4); at the constraint level, J = 0 is bmcModelEnv_nil.
- AC15 (default 8, one query at a positive n, the error for -1) is ver025_depthDefault and ver025_depthError, pinned below, and the depth argument of W.
- The test derivation (the envBoundedPair fixtures at depths 8 and 10, one test per gate and outcome, the depth-0 opt-out of tests that pin the fixpoint query) is AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7, as above.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): The reference triple satisfies VER-025: the script is exact (`bmcEnv_complete`), a model's decoded run replays (`bmcEnv_sat_replays`), a reported run is the trim of a `sat` model's decoded run (`witnessPhase_violated_sound`), the outcomes are those of `witnessPhase`'s cases, and the pipeline hands every outcome but a run to the fixpoint route at the total budget minus the time the phase spent (`pipeline_some_eq`).
  <pre>VER_025 ver025_script Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_alwaysSat` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A script that is always satisfiable violates VER-025 (line 1): on the empty net with a violation no marking satisfies, it has a model although no run reaches a violation.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_alwaysSat Novel.FiringBound.witnessPhase Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_depth0Runs` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that still runs at depth 0 violates VER-025 (line 3): at depth 0 with the gate open it reports 'no run' on `unsat` instead of not running.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_depth0Runs Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_dropLast` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim that drops a needed step violates VER-025 (line 5): the run `inject(e) inject(e) t t` is reported without its last `t`, which is not the trimmed run.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_dropLast Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_emptyModelRun` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that reads a run from a model with no selector violates VER-025 (line 6): when `M0` violates, it reports the run of 0 steps from a model that defines nothing.
  <pre>¬VER_025 ver025_script ver025_emptyModelRun Novel.FiringBound.pipeline</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noBound` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ An injection step that ignores its bound violates VER-025 (line 6): three injections into `e` under `Bounded(2)` are reported as a run to `e = 3`, which the exact step relation refuses at the third injection.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noCut` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim without the cut to the violating prefix violates VER-025 (line 5): on the ring with `M0` violating, the model `t1, t2` comes back to a violating marking, no single step of it can be dropped, and it is reported as a run of 2 steps instead of the run of 0 steps.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noDeduct` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A pipeline that ignores the time the phase spent violates VER-025 (line 9): the phase's time counts against the total budget.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_noReplay` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A phase that does not replay violates VER-025 (line 6): a model selecting `t` first on `envBoundedPair` decodes to the run `t`, which is not a run (`e` is empty), and the phase reports it.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_starve` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A pipeline that starves the fixpoint route violates VER-025 (line 9): 'no run' after 1 ms of an 8 ms budget turns a fixpoint `Proven` at the 7 ms left into `Unknown`. A statement that only bounds the budget left by the total would accept it.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.VER_025_forbids_trimFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.VER_025): ✗ A trim in another order violates VER-025 (line 5), although its run replays, ends at its first violating marking and is irredundant: from the model `inject(0) inject(1)` it reports `inject(1)`, where the reference cuts the run to `inject(0)`.
